# Lane coordination register

> **The single place to answer *"what am I waiting on?"*** — created 2026-08-01 on the product owner's direction, before a fourth lane makes the question expensive.
>
> **Why now rather than later.** With two or three lanes, coordination happens in conversation and in commit messages. With five or six it does not: a question raised inside an implementation report is invisible to everybody who did not read that report, and the lane that could answer it in thirty seconds never learns it was asked. This is the smallest artifact that fixes that, and it is deliberately not a workflow.

## What this is, and what it is not

| It is | It is not |
|---|---|
| A register of **decisions one lane needs from somewhere else** before it can safely continue | **A bug tracker** — that is [`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md). A defect has an owner and a fix; a coordination item has a *question* and an answer |
| A place to record **contracts being negotiated between lanes** | **A roadmap** — that is `IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` and `PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md`. Nothing here schedules anything |
| The record of **why a lane stopped** | A design document. The design lives in the module's own doc; this holds the question and the answer |

**A coordination item exists because implementation cannot safely continue without an answer.** If work can proceed under a stated assumption, it is a finding for the module's design document, not an item here.

## How it works

**Any lane may open an item.** The **named owner** answers it. The **requesting lane** moves it to `IMPLEMENTING` and then `CLOSED`, because only the requester knows whether the answer was sufficient.

**An answer is not a conversation — it is a decision with a home.** Every `ANSWERED` item names the commit, ADR or document that carries it, so the answer outlives the exchange that produced it.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `OPEN` | Raised. The owner has not yet seen it |
| `WAITING` | The owner has it, and the requesting lane is blocked |
| `ANSWERED` | Decided, with the commit or ADR named. Implementation may begin |
| `IMPLEMENTING` | The requesting lane is building against the answer |
| `CLOSED` | Built and merged, or withdrawn with a reason |

**Ids are `C-nnn`, allocated sequentially and never reused.**

**A lane reads this before starting a slice**, alongside [`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md) and [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md).


> **Two lanes allocated `C-001`…`C-009` independently on 2026-08-02**, while the repository ran on two baselines. The items promoted to `main` keep their numbers; **QE renumbered the later set** — `lane-qe`'s C-001 → [C-010](#c-010--no-lane-is-assignable-to-apps-or-signora_platform-and-a-defect-is-sitting-in-one), C-003 → C-011, C-004 → C-012, C-005 → C-013, C-007 → C-014, C-008 → C-015, C-009 → C-016.
>
> **Two were dropped rather than renumbered, because they had already been answered:** *the target-account list gives Provider Platform the subject it has never had* is [C-001](#c-001--the-target-account-contract), answered by [ADR-0036](architecture/adr/0036-target-account-contract.md); and *ICP is named in five documents and owned by no milestone* was answered by M12.5 shipping it. **An id, once promoted, is never reused for a different question.**

## Dependency Health Review — 2026-08-03, against `d39b136`

> **Every open item re-challenged against the repository, not against its own description.** Is it still real · still blocking · narrowable · splittable · **already answered by shipped code, an ADR, or a repository rule**.

#### C-210 — will Signora hold personal data? ⛔ **CONTESTED IDENTIFIER**

> ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-08-12 — this is now the ONLY `C-210` and it is Lane B's.** **Lane A's item moved to [C-1500](#c-1500--task-1476backlogmd--does-signora-store-what-a-rep-writes-or-only-observe-eight-of-account-360s-sections-turn-on-it)** on the product owner's allocation of `C-1500`+ to Lane A.
>
> ⛔ **This question is `OPEN` and unruled.** ⚠️ **The 2026-08-12 Notes-and-Tasks ruling was for `C-1500`, never for this** — 📁 **a reader who followed `C-210` before today landed here and could reasonably have believed otherwise.** 📁 [B-263](BUGS.md).

> ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Keep grouped with future People Intelligence work"*, alongside [C-203](#c-203) and the narrowed [C-221](#c-221).

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · owner: product owner · 🔴 architectural**

**The problem.** Sales Engagement Intelligence was assigned to answer *"who should I contact?"*, and **the platform has no people**. `EntityKind` is `COMPANY | TECHNOLOGY`, and the exclusion is deliberate and documented twice: *"claims carry role changes but no person identifier, so there is no identity to resolve"*, and *"naming an individual would put **personal data in a module with no lawful basis declared for holding it**."*

**Affected modules.** Knowledge Graph (a `PERSON` kind and identity resolution for people) · Provider Normalization (person fields in the canonical vocabulary) · Provider Platform (contact providers, on a dispatch path already blocked by [C-021](#c-021)) · AI Platform, Timeline and every export surface (PII reaching prompts, evidence and records).

**Alternatives.** **(a)** Declare a lawful basis, retention, erasure and subject access, then build people across four modules. **(b)** Defer people and build the role-level capability, which needs none of it. **(c)** Abandon the person-level ambition permanently.

**Recommendation: (b) now, (a) later if a customer asks for names.** [50-sales-engagement.md](architecture/50-sales-engagement.md) §2 shows **eight of the eleven questions in the assignment are answerable without a person**, including the one nothing currently reads — *which role has to agree*.

**Trade-offs.** (b) delivers most of the value in weeks and leaves the last mile — the individual's name — undone. (a) is a legal commitment before it is an engineering one, and it touches the whole pipeline. Deferring costs nothing that taking it now would save.

**Implementation impact.** (b) blocks nothing that is currently buildable. (a) blocks itself until the decision exists.

### C-211 — where does an approach brief live?

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — 🔴 **architectural, and the most architectural of the unrouted set**: an approach brief reads six subjects and **no existing module may read all six.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the item carried none, so no instrument could route it** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *structured state is canonical*). |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — 🔴 **a new bounded context or a widened contract; both are the product owner's.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the owner was declared inline beside `Opened` and no instrument reads prose** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). |

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · owner: product owner · 🔴 architectural**

**The problem.** An approach brief reads the buying committee, signals, business events, validation, narration and the opportunity. **No existing module may read all six**, and the Opportunity Engine's import contract forbids reaching the Signal Engine at all.

**Alternatives.** **(a)** A new `sales_engagement` module. **(b)** Extend the Opportunity Engine — refused by its own ownership contract ([49](architecture/49-lead-ownership.md) §19). **(c)** A read-model composition in the API layer. **(d)** Extend AI Reasoning Engine — refused, because the ranking is deterministic and *"if the system already knows something deterministically, never ask a model to invent it again"*.

**Recommendation: (a), with an ADR before any code.** **The composition is the product**, and a product capability living in a composition root has no owner, no tests of its own and no boundary.

**Trade-offs.** (a) adds a node to the dependency graph reading six modules — honest, and the largest change. (c) is smallest and hides commercial reasoning where nothing reviews it.

**Implementation impact.** Blocks SE-01 onward. **Nothing in Sales Engagement can begin until it is settled.**

### C-212 — which product is an opportunity about?

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — 🟠 **the buying committee is declared per product and an opportunity has no product**, so *"which committee applies?"* is unanswerable and role ranking cannot start. ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the item carried none, so no instrument could route it** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *structured state is canonical*). |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — 🟠 **it decides what an opportunity is *about*, which is product modelling.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the owner was declared inline beside `Opened` and no instrument reads prose** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). |

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · owner: product owner · 🟠**

**The problem.** The buying committee is declared **per product**. An opportunity has no product. So *"which committee applies to this account?"* is unanswerable, and role ranking cannot start.

**Alternatives.** **(a)** Ask the seller once, at the moment they take the account on — one field on a decision they are already making. **(b)** Infer it from the leading hypothesis and the ICP. **(c)** Show every product's committee and let the reader choose.

**Recommendation: (a).** It is a fact the seller knows and Signora does not, which is the definition of something to ask rather than infer. **(b)** would be the platform guessing at a commercial decision.

**Implementation impact.** Blocks SE-04. SE-03 can ship without it by showing the committee per product, which is how it is declared.

### C-213 — the Buying Committee is not exported from `commercial_profile.public`

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · current module assignee: Lane B (`commercial_profile`) · 🟠 — `CLOSED` 2026-08-04**

> ✅ **Closed by the consolidation, not by an answer** ([D-058](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). **This item existed because the export and its only consumer sat in two different lanes.** `commercial_profile` and `sales_engagement` are both Lane B's from 2026-08-04, so **there is no cross-lane contract left to agree** — the export is an ordinary change inside one module, and [TASK-205](BACKLOG.md) is `READY`. **Three assignees in two days is the record worth keeping**: Lane B, then Lane A by rule, then Lane B by consolidation. **The item never moved and the answer never changed** — only who could act, which is exactly what [428](architecture/428-lane-coordination-model.md) proposes to stop storing by hand.

> ⚠️ **Reassigned 2026-08-04, by rule rather than by ruling** ([C-414](#c-414--c-213-is-unfixable-by-anyone-and-that-is-why-the-lanes-stopped)). This row read *"owner: Lane B"*, which was correct when `commercial_profile` was Lane B's. **`CLAUDE.md` §20e — *module assignment is authoritative*: responsibility follows the module.** Lane A holds `commercial_profile` and therefore holds this.

**The problem.** `commercial_profile.public` exports `TargetAccountReader`, `TargetAccountView` and `TargetAccountListView` — and **nothing about the Buying Committee**. Sales Engagement's whole capability is the join between a declared committee role and an observed appointment at a Target Account, and it cannot read the declaration.

**What Lane A has done in the meantime.** SE-02's reasoning core is built against **its own port** (`CommitteeReader`), which is correct architecture regardless — *a port belongs to the module that owns the language it represents* (`CLAUDE.md` §6). The deterministic graph, its thirty tests and its type checking are complete and reviewable now. **Only the adapter is blocked.**

**What is needed.** A read contract on `commercial_profile.public` exposing, for a workspace and a product, the declared roles as `(title, part)`. **Read-only, no ranking, no evaluation** — Commercial Profile's structural boundary test refuses an influence model and Sales Engagement must not import one.

**Recommendation.** Lane B exports a `BuyingCommitteeReader` shaped like the existing `TargetAccountReader`. Sales Engagement writes the adapter mapping it onto its own port, which is where the anti-corruption boundary belongs.

**Trade-offs.** Without it, SE-03 cannot put the committee on a screen — which would be the first time the customer's declaration reached one. **The declaration's own docstring says *"nothing downstream reads it yet"***; this is the change that ends that.

**Implementation impact.** Blocks SE-03 onward. Blocks nothing in SE-02.

> **Still open, and it now blocks an approved slice — Lane A, 2026-08-04.** [TASK-205](BACKLOG.md) — 417 §4's **A-ii**, the Sales Engagement interface layer — was approved by the product owner and **cannot be built while this is open.**
>
> **417 §2c rated A-ii *"built, tested, unreachable"* with the reuse column reading *"25+ exported types, unchanged."* That is true of the contract and not of the module.** `AssembleApproach` requires three ports — `CommitteeReader`, `EvidenceReader`, `PortfolioReader` — and **not one has an implementation anywhere in the repository.** So the module is not merely unreachable; the half that would reach outward was deliberately never written, and `application/ports.py` says so in its own docstring: *"the adapter that satisfies it is a separate, small change **once the export exists**."*
>
> **Two of the three are blocked by this item.** `commercial_profile.public` today exports `TargetAccountReader`, `TargetAccountView`, `TargetAccountListView` and — since Epic D — `DeclaredCompetitorReader` and its two views. **Nothing about the Buying Committee, and nothing about the product portfolio.**
>
> **Lane A is not proceeding**, and the reason is the rule rather than the difficulty: *a lane may proceed past an open item only where proceeding encodes no assumption about the answer* (§20e). Writing the adapter now would mean inventing the shape of an export Lane B has not written, inside a module Lane A may not touch — **which is how two lanes ship incompatible halves of one contract.** The recommendation above is unchanged and is still Lane B's to take.

### C-214 — `Evaluation` assumes one rendering protocol, and a second now exists

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **owner: whoever is assigned `ai_platform`.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the item carried none, so no instrument could route it** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *structured state is canonical*). |
| **Owner** | **The current module assignee for `ai_platform`** — joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), never stored here ([C-213](#c-213--task-205-names-an-assignee-that-moved)). ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the owner was declared inline beside `Opened` and no instrument reads prose** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). |

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · owner: whoever is assigned `ai_platform` · 🟡**

**The problem.** `Evaluation.rendering_protocol_version` records *which protocol produced the text the model actually read*, and `Evaluation.earns_release` compares it against `PROMPT_RENDERING_PROTOCOL_VERSION` — the AI Platform's **evidence** rendering protocol. That was correct while every prompt in the repository was shown an `EvidenceSet`.

**SE-09c introduces a prompt that is never shown one.** A commercial synthesis is shown a *reasoning graph*, rendered by the **Commercial Context Protocol** (`sales_engagement/domain/context.py`), and that is the condition its measurements are bound to. Calling `earns_release` on a Sales Engagement measurement compares this module's protocol version against an unrelated module's constant — meaningless whatever it returns.

**What Lane A has done in the meantime.** Sales Engagement **reuses the record and derives its own eligibility** (`sales_engagement/domain/release.py`). `Evaluation` states facts rather than verdicts and says so in its own docstring, so reusing it is correct; only the derivation is this module's.

**The two protocols share an integer namespace and nothing coordinates them, which is the sharp edge here.** Lane A initially recorded that the divergence *failed closed*. It does not: that held only while the constants differed, and bumping the Commercial Context Protocol to 2 during SE-09c made them equal — at which point `PromptVersion.is_released` began returning the right answer for the wrong reason. **Neither state is a guarantee**, because the comparison is meaningless whichever way it lands. A test now pins the coincidence, so the next move of either constant fails and surfaces this item rather than leaving the coupling invisible.

**Two smaller consequences, recorded here rather than separately.**

- **A commercial synthesis writes no `ai_inference` record.** `Infer` owns that path and is shaped around an `EvidenceSet`. Every failure is carried on `PassResult` with its detail, so nothing is silent — but it is not yet durable, and *observability is a product capability* (`CLAUDE.md` §2).
- **`evaluation/release.py` duplicates the platform's manifest recorder** (~45 lines), because the parameter type is the platform's `EvaluationReport` and this module's report counts refusals, carries stability, and applies a different coverage floor.
- **Stability is measured but not durable.** `Evaluation` has no field for it, so agreement across repeated runs is computed, rendered on the report, and then lost — it cannot be read back from the manifest, and a regression in stability between two releases is therefore invisible. **This is the dimension the architecture guarantees most cheaply and the one it currently forgets fastest**, which is the sharpest argument for reconciling the record type.

**Recommendation.** Parameterise the platform's release derivation on *which* protocol a measurement was taken under, rather than hard-coding one constant — the same shape `for_model` already uses to avoid naming a vendor. A shared manifest recorder and an `Infer` path that accepts a second input kind both fall out of that change rather than preceding it.

**Trade-offs.** Doing nothing costs a duplicated recorder and a synthesis that is observable only to its caller. Doing it early, before a third input protocol exists, risks generalising from two instances — which is why this is raised rather than built.

**Implementation impact.** Blocks nothing. SE-09c ships complete under the divergence above.

### C-215 — the Timeline feed is per-account, and the workspace needs it per-seller

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`OPEN` — answered by Lane B, 2026-08-07**, as `timeline`'s current assignee ([`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), `current_owner = "Lane B"`). **The recommendation is accepted and every technical claim in it was verified against the tree rather than taken on trust** — see *Lane B's answer* below. ⛔ **Not `READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION`**: that state is the product owner's on a ruling, and **the work is [TASK-435](BACKLOG.md), which is `SEQUENCED` and only Lane C may release.** **The requesting lane closes** (§20e). **Was:** **`OPEN`** — ⚠️ **assigned 2026-08-04 by the consolidation ([D-058](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) and *still not answered*.** **Whoever builds [TASK-902](BACKLOG.md) inherits it with the module.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the item carried none, so no instrument could route it** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *structured state is canonical*). |
| **Owner** | **The current module assignee for `timeline`** — assigned 2026-08-04 by the consolidation ([D-058](DECISION_REGISTER.md)); **joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), never stored here.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the owner was declared inline beside `Opened` and no instrument reads prose** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). |

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · current module assignee: Lane B (`timeline`) · 🟠**

> **Assigned 2026-08-04 by the consolidation** ([D-058](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). `timeline` was unassigned; **every implementation module is Lane B's**, so this item has a current assignee for the first time since it was opened. **It is still not answered** — whoever builds [TASK-902](BACKLOG.md) inherits it with the module, exactly as the correction below required.

> ⚠️ **Corrected 2026-08-04** ([C-414](#c-414--c-213-is-unfixable-by-anyone-and-that-is-why-the-lanes-stopped)). This read *"owner: Lane B"*; **`timeline` is assigned to no lane today.** Under `CLAUDE.md` §20e — *module assignment is authoritative* — **whichever lane claims [TASK-902](BACKLOG.md) inherits this item with the module.** Naming a lane that does not hold it is the same defect C-213 carried.

**The problem.** `GET /workspaces/{id}/accounts/{account_id}/timeline` is the only timeline endpoint, and the repository query underneath it is hard-scoped: `WHERE workspace_id = … AND entity_id = …`, ordered off a `(workspace, entity, occurred_at, id)` index.

**The Sales Workspace's highest-value capability is workspace-scoped.** *"Three Target Accounts became significantly more active since you last looked"* is a query across everything a seller holds, and there is no way to ask it. The alternative — one request per account from the browser — is the N+1 pattern `CLAUDE.md` §14 names as *a defect at write time, not a future task*.

**What is needed.** A feed for a workspace rather than an entity: same entry shape, same cursor, same ordering, filtered by `workspace_id` alone and optionally by a set of entity ids and an `occurred_at` lower bound. **It needs a second index** — `(workspace_id, occurred_at, id)` — because the existing one is entity-leading and cannot serve it.

**Why this is not Lane A's to build.** It is production code, a public contract and a migration inside `timeline`, which Lane B built (M7 S01–S04a, [B-301](BUGS.md)). *A lane never changes a module it is not assigned* (`CLAUDE.md` §20e); this is a finding to raise.

**Recommendation.** Lane B adds `feed_for_workspace(workspace_id, *, entity_ids=None, since=None, after, limit)` beside the existing `feed`, exposed as `GET /workspaces/{id}/timeline`. **Read-only, no new judgement** — Timeline ranks nothing and explains nothing, and this must not become the place that starts.

**On `since`, and why it is a parameter rather than stored state.** *What changed since you last looked* also appears as [TASK-016](BACKLOG.md), `BLOCKED` on per-user read state that does not exist. **It does not need to exist for this contract**: `since` is a declared input, and who supplies it is a separate question — a client-held timestamp works today, and a server-side read state later changes no contract. **That keeps storage out of the design until something earns it**, which is the product owner's standing instruction.

**Trade-offs.** Without it the workspace can say what each account's score did, but not *what happened*. Score movement is a number; a leadership appointment is the sentence a seller acts on.

**Implementation impact.** Blocks SW-02 and SW-06. **Blocks nothing else** — SW-03, SW-04 and SW-05 are composition over `GET /accounts`, which is already workspace-scoped, and Lane A has taken SW-03 instead.


### ✅ Lane B's answer — accepted, and checked rather than accepted

**Three claims, all verified in the tree on 2026-08-07 at `f3ec15f2`:**

| Claim | Verified |
|---|---|
| *"the repository query underneath it is hard-scoped"* | ✅ `repository.py:60-61` — `workspace_id == …` **and** `entity_id == …`, with no variant that omits the second |
| *"ordered off a `(workspace, entity, occurred_at, id)` index"* | ✅ `0026_timeline_entry.py:85-89` — `ix_timeline_entry_feed` is exactly those four columns, in that order |
| *"it needs a second index"* | ✅ **Confirmed, and the reason is the column order rather than the column set.** The existing index is **entity-leading after `workspace_id`**, so a workspace-wide scan ordered by `occurred_at` cannot use it — every `entity_id` group would have to be read and re-sorted |

**The contract is accepted as recommended**: `feed_for_workspace(workspace_id, *, entity_ids=None, since=None, after, limit)` beside `feed`, at `GET /workspaces/{id}/timeline`, with `(workspace_id, occurred_at, id)` added. ✅ **And `since` as a declared input rather than stored state is right** — §6, *build for the requirement in front of you*. **A server-side read state later changes no contract**, which is what makes deferring it free.

### ⚠️ One correction, and it is about the sentence the item is built on

> **[C-215] *"Three Target Accounts became **significantly more active** since you last looked."***

⛔ **That sentence contains a judgement, and `timeline` must not be the module that makes it.** **Timeline returns what happened, in order.** *Significant*, *more active* and *three* are a ranking over those entries — **and the item's own guard says so**: *"Timeline ranks nothing and explains nothing, and this must not become the place that starts."*

⚡ **Both halves are true and they point at different modules.** The feed is Timeline's; **deciding which accounts moved and by how much is `buying_score_engine`'s**, which already owns movement, or the consumer's composition. **Named here because a motivating example is what an implementer builds toward**, and this one would walk `feed_for_workspace` into a `significance` parameter one release later.

### ⛔ Two things the implementing slice must not assume

**① `entity_ids` and `occurred_at` ordering do not share an index.** Filtering by a set of entities *and* ordering by time is served well by neither the existing index nor the proposed one. **It is fine — the set is small and bounded by what a seller holds — but it should be a deliberate choice rather than a discovery**, and the slice should say which access path it expects.

**② `timeline/public/__init__.py` is 0 bytes**, and that is **not** a blocker here. ✅ **This contract is consumed over HTTP** — `GET /workspaces/{id}/timeline` — so no consumer needs the Python contract, and **nothing should be parked waiting for it.** ⚠️ **It is the second empty `public/` Lane C's new check found** (the other was `people`, now filled); recorded so the emptiness is understood as *no consumer yet* rather than as a gap under this item.

### What this unblocks, and what it does not

**[TASK-435](BACKLOG.md) is the row that carries this work and it is `SEQUENCED` on *"SW-02 is scheduled"*.** ⛔ **This lane has not claimed it and has written no code** — `READY` is Lane C's to set on fitness (§20e), and **the specification being finished is what makes it a new row rather than a live one**, exactly as [TASK-902](BACKLOG.md)'s disposal recorded.

**So the answer this item was waiting for exists as of today. Whether TASK-435 is scheduled is a sequencing decision and remains Lane C's and the product owner's.**

### C-216 — the setup scripts do not load `.env.local`, and fall back silently

**Opened 2026-08-03 · Lane A · owner: QE ([`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) is QE's) · 🟠**

**The problem.** `npm run auth:migrate` and `npm run demo:users` run under `tsx`, not Next.js. **Next.js loads `.env.local`; a standalone `tsx` script does not.** Both read `process.env` through `lib/auth/config.ts`, whose `required()` helper supplies a **default** when the variable is absent:

```ts
databaseUrl: required(
  'SIGNORA_AUTH_DATABASE_URL',
  'postgresql://signora_auth:…@localhost:5432/signora',   // ← the review database
),
```

**Observed, on this lane, today.** `frontend/.env.local` correctly named `signora_lane_a`. Both scripts ignored it, took the default, and **created four sign-in accounts in `signora` — the human-review database** — while reporting success. `make demo-seed` then found no users in the lane's database and printed *"members — none, no accounts exist yet"*, which reads as a seeding bug rather than as a configuration one.

**Why this matters beyond one lane.** [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane) tells every lane to set its own database and ports, and its *"three things per lane"* section does not mention that the `tsx` scripts bypass `.env.local`. **Every lane setting up its own environment will hit this**, and the failure is silent in the direction that matters: it writes to somebody else's database rather than failing.

> **The default is the defect, not the missing loader.** `required(name, fallback)` is a fallback wearing the name *required*. A variable with a default is not required, and a setup script that silently targets the review database when misconfigured is the *"hidden inputs are architecture defects"* rule (`CLAUDE.md` §2) in its most expensive form.

**Recommendation, in the order the product owner stated it.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Deterministic loading** | The `tsx` scripts load `.env.local` explicitly, so a script and the dev server read the same file |
| **Lane-aware configuration** | One documented way to point a whole lane — API, web, scripts, seeder — at its own database |
| **No silent fallback** | A setup script with no `SIGNORA_AUTH_DATABASE_URL` **fails and says so.** A runtime default that happens to be another environment's database is worse than a crash |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **owner: QE** ([`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) is theirs). **The default is the defect, not the missing loader.** ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the item carried none, so no instrument could route it** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *structured state is canonical*). |
| **Owner** | **QE** — [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) is theirs, and *"QE removes its own blockers"* (§20e). ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the owner was declared inline beside `Opened` and no instrument reads prose** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). |

**Trade-offs.** Removing the default would fail any environment that relied on it; that is the point, and it fails loudly at setup rather than quietly at seed time. Loading `.env.local` in the scripts alone fixes the symptom and leaves the fallback in place for the next caller.

**Implementation impact.** Blocks nothing. **It has already cost one lane an hour and wrote to a database that lane does not own** — recorded because a lane touching another environment's data must say so, and because the next lane deserves the sentence `RUNNING.md` is missing.

> ⚠️ **[C-024](#c-024--timeline-has-a-surface-and-nowhere-to-mount-it) is QE's error, recorded rather than quietly corrected.** It was escalated in **two consecutive cycle reports** as the sharpest blocker in the repository — *"ten lines of routing separate a working capability from a customer"* — **when Lane A had already mounted it and said so in its handoff.** QE was reading the register instead of the repository, which is precisely the failure [L-2 *Evidence before assumption*](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md) exists to prevent. **Written by QE, violated by QE, in the same week.**
>
> **The durable lesson is not *be more careful*.** It is that **an item's own description is not evidence of its status**, and this review's method — verify every item against shipped code — is now what happens every Closeout.

### Resolved by delegated ruling — 2026-08-03, [ADR-0100](architecture/adr/0100-delegated-dependency-rulings.md)

**The product owner delegated dependency resolution to QE on 2026-08-03.** Ten rulings, four deliberate deferrals. **Every ruling names whether it rests on evidence or judgement**, so the judgement ones are cheap to reverse.

| Item | Ruling | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **C-012 · C-013 · C-021 · C-207** | **`ANSWERED` — R-1.** One platform amendment, one RFC, four capabilities. **Seven independently certifiable rewiring slices** | **Evidence** — 7 of 9 modules unwired since M3A; `type: ignore` 8 → 13 |
| **C-020** | **`ANSWERED` — R-2 + R-3.** [ADR-0038](architecture/adr/0038-timeline.md) **ratified**, all three ❓ answered. **M7 may proceed** | **Evidence** |
| **C-023** | **`CLOSED` — R-2.** It asked whether M13 was executable; **Lane B executed three slices of it** | **Evidence** |
| **C-200** | **`ANSWERED` — R-2.** A roadmap row is not claimable until it names its bounded context. M14b's first task is a discovery slice | **Evidence** — three lanes, same friction |
| **C-010** | **`ANSWERED` — R-4.** QE owns it; **a rotating lane verifies QE's fixes**, starting with Lane B | **Evidence** — 8 defects landed here |
| **C-004** | **`ANSWERED` — R-4.** **QE may correct factual drift in `01`–`21`** — recording what was built, never changing a decision | **Evidence** |
| **C-014** | **`ANSWERED` — R-4.** A milestone slot **after M14**. Not urgent: §20c already treats accessibility as a defect class | **Judgement** |
| **C-008** | **`ANSWERED` — R-5.** **Yes, read-only for `member`, beside the account brief**, not under `/settings` | **Evidence** on *whether*; **judgement** on *where* |
| **C-011** | **`ANSWERED` — R-6.** Posture reaches the row; **a contraction risk is never confusable with an opportunity.** Treatment is the lane's | **Evidence** |
| **C-017** | **`ANSWERED` — R-9.** Ratified as `D39` | **Zero-cost. It should not have waited five cycles** |
| **C-206** | **`ANSWERED` — R-7.** **Signora owns the invitation**; the plugin is not adopted. **v1 delivery is a shareable link, not email** | **Evidence** on the plugin; **judgement** on delivery |
| **C-205** | **`ANSWERED` — R-8.** **Desktop-first, usable to tablet. Phone is out of scope for v1.** [B-019](BUGS.md)'s hidden aside is correct behaviour | **Judgement — the thinnest here** |
| **C-002 · C-018 · C-204** | **STAY OPEN — R-10, the product owner's own ruling.** ADR-0041 models customer *intent*; these are its *interpretation*. **Complementary, not one decision** | **QE's Pack C grouping withdrawn** |

**Deliberately not ruled, and each says why:** C-002/C-018/C-204 need product intent · **C-203** is product semantics touching AI attribution, audit and notifications at once · **C-003, C-005, C-007, C-009, C-025** are **not yet re-validated against current code** · **C-302** is **tenancy, which is never decided inside a session**.

> **Ten rulings, four deferrals, and the deferrals are the honest part.** A delegation returning *"all resolved"* would mean the hard ones had been decided by somebody without the information to decide them.

> **[C-024](#c-024--timeline-has-a-surface-and-nowhere-to-mount-it) was the recommendation here and no longer needs answering** — Lane A mounted the timeline in `CX-03` while this classification was being written, which is the outcome the item wanted. **Closed 2026-08-03 by Lane B**, the requesting lane, after verifying the whole chain: route, component, hook, endpoint.

### Re-validation, round two — 2026-08-03, at `de3491e`

**The five items [ADR-0100](architecture/adr/0100-delegated-dependency-rulings.md) deliberately would not rule on, now read against current code.** Ruling on them without this was the register-not-repository error; this is that read.

| Item | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **C-025** | **`CLOSED` — answered by implementation** | **The OAuth flow is fully built in the Next.js tier**: `frontend/app/api/integrations/[slug]/start` and `/callback`, with state issuance and **a separate OAuth client from Better Auth's**. The question *"which tier may run an integration OAuth flow"* was answered by [`18-authentication.md`](architecture/18-authentication.md) **before the item was raised** — the implementation followed the architecture and the register never caught up |
| **C-007** | **STILL OPEN — and it now blocks, where it did not** | Its own text: *"blocks nothing until M12.5 slice 5 is done."* **Slice 5 is done** — all five Commercial Profile slices are promoted. **The condition it named has been met, so the block is live.** The only item in two rounds of re-validation to get *more* blocking rather than less |
| **C-009** | **`CLOSED` — it was never a decision.** Refiled as [B-103](BUGS.md) | **Verified, and the premise was wrong.** It sat five cycles as a frozen-platform change under §20a needing an RFC. **`opportunity_engine/interface/errors.py` documents the mechanism in its own comment** — *"handler lookup walks the exception's MRO"* — so a module can already map an invariant separately from a refusal. **A second exception class and one row, inside the module. No platform change, no RFC, no ruling.** The defect is real and confirmed in two modules; **the blocker was not** |
| **C-003** | **STILL OPEN — but its urgency was a forecast that did not happen** | It said *"slice 5 makes it four."* **Slice 5 deliberately added none** — `commercial_focus` carries the comment *"No `*_unknown_product` here — a watch list cites no product."* Still three codes, and a neutral `unknown_product` now exists beside them. **Stable debt, not compounding — priority should fall, not rise** |
| **C-005** | **STILL OPEN — correctly deferred, blocking nothing** | It blocks *"the first customer-editable relevance profile."* **No write surface exists** — `signal_profile` appears in no interface layer and no frontend route. Unchanged and correctly parked |

> **The symmetry with [C-013](#c-013--publishableevent-cannot-be-satisfied-by-a-frozen-dataclass) is the useful part.** C-013 forecast that a workaround would spread, and it spread — 8 files to 13 — so its priority **rose**. C-003 forecast the same shape and **the lane held the line**, so its priority **falls**. *"Is the workaround compounding?"* is doing real discriminating work, not just sounding rigorous.
>
> **Across two rounds: 9 items closed on evidence, 2 narrowed, 1 escalated, 3 confirmed open.** The register has never once been wrong in the direction of *understating* what was blocked — every correction so far has been the repository moving ahead of its own paperwork.

**On the product owner's direction: every blocked item re-checked against the repository *as it exists now*, not as it existed when the item was raised.** Months of implementation have landed since most were written.

| Item | Was | Is, measured today | Action |

| **[C-023](#c-023--m13-is-ratified-architecture-not-an-executable-milestone)** | *"M13 is ratified architecture, not an **executable** milestone"* | **It executed.** `44-integrations.md` written, the module built, **S01, S02 and S09 promoted** | **CLOSE.** The question was empirical and implementation answered it. Which lane holds M13 is scheduling, and Lane B holds it |
| **[C-013](#c-013--publishableevent-cannot-be-satisfied-by-a-frozen-dataclass)** | *"eight publishing modules carry a `# type: ignore`"* | **13+ files carry one.** The item predicted *"a `type: ignore` in eight places trains people to add a ninth"* | **STILL OPEN, and worse.** Its own forecast came true. **Priority raised** |
| **[C-203](#c-203--nothing-in-the-product-can-render-a-persons-name)** | *"nothing can render a **person's** name"* | `entity-name.tsx` exists — **and renders a *company***. Its own docstring says so | **STILL OPEN.** Nearly closed in error; the component's name suggested otherwise and the code did not |

> **Two of the four moved, and two did not — which is the useful shape.** A re-validation that closed everything would mean the register had been wrong; one that closed nothing would mean the exercise was theatre. **[C-203](#c-203--nothing-in-the-product-can-render-a-persons-name) is the one to learn from**: `entity-name.tsx` looked like the answer by its filename, and reading it showed it renders companies. **A component's name is not evidence of what it does** ([L-2](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md)).

**Not yet re-validated**, and stated rather than implied: C-003, C-005, C-007, C-009, C-011, C-018, C-021, C-025, C-200, C-204, C-205, C-206, C-207 and the platform items. Each needs a code read of the kind above; **guessing at them would produce exactly the register-not-repository error this exercise exists to correct.**

## C-113 · `/settings/connections` is the one shipped screen with no row to implement its finalized design

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **QE**, 2026-08-21, during the full UI conformance audit on `1db9f5e7` |
| **Owner** | **Lane C · Product Office** — backlog coverage, not a defect |
| **Status** | `READY FOR LANE C` |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing today.** ⛔ **Raised so a gap in coverage is visible before somebody plans around it**, not because a lane is stopped |

**The measurement.** Seven shipped screens were compared against their own design documents by extracting each design's visible strings and testing them against the rendered page. **Every screen has a row that owns implementing its finalized design — except one.**

| Screen | Route | Design strings present | Row that owns the design |
|---|---|---|---|
| Security Center | `/profile/security` | 13/60 | [TASK-1414](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md) |
| User Profile | `/profile` | 10/55 | [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md) |
| Reports | `/reports` | 4/40 | [TASK-1417](BACKLOG.md) |
| Settings | `/settings` | 4/54 | [TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md) |
| Team Management | `/settings/team` | 2/60 | [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) |
| Help Center | `/help` | 1/60 | [TASK-1420](BACKLOG.md) |
| 🔴 **CRM Integrations** | **`/settings/connections`** | **3/57** | 🔴 **none** |

⚠️ **The percentages are NOT the point and must not be read as a defect count.** 📁 **[478](architecture/478-design-conformance-audit.md) §4 already established that no UI in this repository is derived from the finalized design**, and many of the absent strings are the design documents' own annotation chrome (*"Platform foundation · Module 9"*, *"Design system v2.0 · help & support"*). ⚡ **They are a coverage measurement, and every one of them is already somebody's row — except the last.**

**What `/settings/connections` does have.** 📁 **[TASK-407](BACKLOG.md) — *"a connection says whether it actually works"* — is `PROMOTED`, and its row names *CRM Integrations* as its approved screen.** ✅ **It delivered a genuine slice of that design: the health check.**

⛔ **What no row owns** is the rest of the screen the design draws: **Objects & sync status · field mappings · the write contract · held writes · run diagnostics · sync now · per-object direction and record counts.**

### The question for Product Office

> **Is `/settings/connections` deliberately scoped to the connection-health slice, or is its design-implementation row simply missing?**

⚡ **Both answers are fine and they lead to different places.** **If deliberate**, ⛔ nothing needs building and this item closes with the reason recorded — **so the next audit does not re-raise it**. **If missing**, it is a row Lane A can take, and it is the only screen of the seven that has nowhere to start.

⚠️ **QE is not proposing scope and does not own priority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). **The measurement is the contribution; the ruling is the product owner's.**

## C-1526 · Two documents in one snapshot disagree about how many columns may pin, and the design's own example does not exist

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-17, finishing Companies against the design |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — 📁 [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes [`docs/design-snapshot/`](design-snapshot/MANIFEST.md) the implementation authority, ⛔ **and a lane may not decide which of two of its documents wins** |
| **Type** | **A conflict between two ratified design documents** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚡ **Companies ships with one pinned column and the design's gradient treatment** — this asks whether a second is wanted, not whether the screen can go out |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### ⚡ ① The two sentences

📁 **`Fortune Signora Design System v2.dc.html`, *Pinned identity*:**

> ✅ ***"**The first column** pins with a 24px gradient fade instead of a border, so horizontal scroll never produces a hard seam."***

📁 **`Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html`, the Column configuration panel:**

> ⚡ ***"**Two columns** may be pinned left; pinning is per view, not per user, so a shared view looks the same for everyone."***

⚠️ **Both are in the same snapshot and neither is wrong on its own.** ⛔ **They cannot both be implemented by one primitive**: `components/ui/table.tsx` pins with `sticky left-0`, which is correct for exactly one column, and its own docstring records the Design System's wording — *"⛔ At most one per row."*

### ⛔ ② The design's second pinned column does not exist

📁 **Companies names which two:** *"**Company and score** pin left behind a soft gradient rather than a hard rule."*

🔴 **There is no Signora score on this screen and no source anywhere produces one** — ⚡ **already recorded**, and it is the one column of the design's nine with nothing behind it. **So the design's own example cannot be built even if the rule is adopted.** ⛔ **The second pin would be whichever column a customer chose**, which is a different feature from the one the sentence illustrates.

### ⚡ ③ What the second pin costs, measured rather than estimated

**Four pieces, and the first is the one that leaves Companies:**

**① The shared primitive.** ⛔ **A second sticky column needs `left: <width of the first>`, and nothing knows that width** — the table sizes its columns automatically and the design's fixed `232px` template was never adopted. ✅ **Either measure the first pinned cell at runtime and publish it as a CSS variable, or fix the identity column's width.** 📁 **Both change `components/ui/table.tsx`, which every table in the product renders** ([§20c](../CLAUDE.md): permitted under the UI Migration Program, ⚠️ **but it is a change to a shared contract rather than to Companies**).

**② View state.** **`ColumnSpec.pinned` is a literal `true` today.** It becomes a per-view value, in the saved view and in the URL, exactly as sort and group already are.

**③ A control.** 📁 The design puts a pin marker beside each column in its configuration panel; ⚡ **the screen's equivalent is the Columns pill.**

**④ The refusal.** ⛔ **A third pin must not silently replace the second** ([B-255](BUGS.md)), so the control has to say what it did.

### ✅ ④ What is shipped, and why it is not a partial implementation

✅ **Company pins, with the design's 24px gradient fade rather than a border** — 📁 **the Design System's rule, implemented exactly**, and the shared table already carried it.

⛔ **The half-measure was deliberately NOT built.** ⚠️ **A pin control that can only ever pin the column that is already pinned is a control that does nothing**, which is the defect this repository names most often.

### 🔴 ⑤ What is being asked

**One of three, and the third is a real answer:**

**①** **Design System v2 wins** — one pinned column, and Companies' sentence is corrected in the next snapshot.
**②** **Companies wins** — two, and ① above becomes a Design System slice before Companies can consume it.
**③** **Neither yet** — ⚡ **the second pin waits for a column worth pinning.** **The design's example is the score, and until something produces one, a customer pinning a second column is choosing between Segment, Renewal, Owner and Tags — none of which the design says needs it.**

⚡ **Lane A's recommendation is ③**, on 📁 [§6](../CLAUDE.md): *do not add generalization for cases that do not exist yet*. ⛔ **It is a recommendation and not a decision** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *proposing a direction is expected; proceeding on it is not*.

## C-1533 · Home state 14's entry condition and its copy describe different cards

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-19, implementing Home's fourteen states |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — **one approved document contradicts itself, and the fix is a sentence a customer reads** |
| **Type** | **An internal contradiction in one design document** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **State 14 only.** ✅ **Every other Home state is implemented.** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### The contradiction, at its smallest

📁 **State 14's entry condition**: *"Fully activated for blocking cards, but a
**non-blocking** card was skipped and its 30 days have elapsed."*

📁 **`HM-COPY-12`, the sentence it renders**: *"**Calls** are still not connected.
Signora is scoring on CRM fields alone."*

⛔ **Under Home's own model those cannot both be true.** 📁 The document states
three times that **calls is BLOCKING**: `P-06` — *"Calls is blocking; invite is
not"*; the dismissibility rule — *"blocking cards — CRM and calls — cannot be
dismissed"*; and the priority table. ⚡ **So the only skippable card is invite**,
and if the blocking set is complete then calls **is** connected — which makes the
sentence false exactly when the state fires.

### ⛔ The corpus was searched and it does not resolve this

| Document | What it says | Does it resolve it? |
|---|---|---|
| **Home** | Calls is blocking, three times. Invite is the only optional card | ⛔ **It is the document that contradicts itself** |
| **System States** | Draws its own activation sequence — CRM, **invite**, then calls — and calls ***"Optional"*** | ⚠️ **This is `U-01`**, and Home's own interim already rules: *"implement from this document; leave System States untouched"* |
| **Onboarding · Settings · CRM Integrations** | Connection steps, no skip semantics | ⛔ No |
| **`policy.csv` · permissions** | Nothing about activation | ⛔ No |
| **`0050_invite_skipped_at`** | Implements the 30-day skip for **invite alone** | ⚡ **Corroborates Home's model** |

✅ **`U-01` decides which DOCUMENT wins. It does not decide which SENTENCE to
show**, and 📁 **contract item 18 forbids composing one**: *"every string is used
verbatim from the copy table. **No message is assembled from fragments at
runtime.**"*

### The smallest decision that unblocks it

> ## **Either: one sentence for the state that CAN occur — blocking complete, invite skipped, 30 days elapsed.**
>
> ## **Or: a ruling that calls is NON-blocking after all**, which would also make states 02 and 03 reachable and would resolve `U-01` in System States' favour.

⚠️ **The second is the larger answer.** ⛔ It changes which composition a workspace
resolves to: **calls cannot be connected by anybody today** — every calendar entry
in the catalog is `connectable=False` — **so making it blocking-and-uncompletable
is what currently makes states 02, 03 and 04 unreachable.**

### ✅ Shipped meanwhile — nothing else waits on this

**Thirteen of Home's fourteen states are implemented and browser-verified.** ⛔
**`HM_COPY_12` stays in the copy table, unrendered**, exactly as `HM_COPY_10` does
for state 11 — 📁 the string is ready the day a producer or a ruling exists, and a
copy table holding a sentence nothing renders is honest in a way a fabricated
substitute would not be.

## C-1536 · The People Intelligence screen is drawn entirely in named people, and the domain is anonymous by specification

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-19, on picking up its own claimed [TASK-430](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — 📁 **[D-074](DECISION_REGISTER.md) is already the ruling on this exact question** |
| **Type** | 🔴 **Architectural blocker** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a dependency on a decision nobody has made is architectural however small the code would be* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **TASK-430's *"People Intelligence screen"*.** ✅ **Nothing else** — its second deliverable, *Global Search's people group*, **is already built and correct** |
| **Status** | 🔴 **`OPEN`** |

### ✅ The half that is already delivered, measured before anything was claimed about the other

📁 **TASK-430 `Delivers`: *"The People Intelligence screen · Global Search's people group."*** ⚡ **The second is DONE:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Backend** | `SEARCH_COVERAGE[EntityKind.PERSON] = NOT_APPLICABLE`, with the reason in place — *"search matches a legal name; a `Person` in this repository has none by specification"* |
| **Frontend** | `account-search.tsx` renders the group and its sentence — ***"Signora does not search people by name."*** ⚡ **Reachable since [B-288](BUGS.md)**, which fixed the mirrored union that crashed the whole search box |

⛔ **So this item is about the screen alone**, and the row does not need re-scoping — it needs the screen's premise ruled on.

### 🔴 The problem, stated as the gap between two documents

| 📁 The design draws | 📁 The domain publishes |
|---|---|
| *"Jonas Hald · VP Operations · advocated in 6 of 8 calls, replies within a day"* | ⛔ **`PersonView`: an `id` and a `workspace_id`. That is all** |
| *"Peter Sørensen · Blocker · two objections on record · 3 touches · 24 days"* | ⛔ **`AffiliationView`: `title`, `seniority`, `started_on`, `ended_on`** |
| *"Mette Bruun · Signer · never emailed, never met, not on any call"* | ⛔ **No engagement record of any kind exists in this repository** |
| *"Committee · 6 · All · 24 · Changed · 2 · Gaps · 1"* | ⛔ **`BuyingCommittee` records SEATS, not people** — its own header: *"No person is named here"* |

⚡ **Every row of the screen is a person's name, their stance, and how often we
have spoken to them.** ⛔ **The product holds none of the three**, and
`modules/people/` opens by saying so: ***"No name. No email. No phone. No
provider identifier"*** — 📁 **[C-221](#c-221) *"is not a constraint on this
module — it is its specification"*.**

⚠️ **And `people/` has no `interface/` layer at all**, so there is no read
surface either. **That half is ordinary work; the premise is not.**

### 🔴 The ruling that already exists, and why it is the blocker rather than the answer

📁 **[D-074](DECISION_REGISTER.md), product owner:**

> *"I approve moving the **People domain** implementation earlier in the
> roadmap. **I am not approving the full People Intelligence feature set.**"*

⛔ **TASK-430 is the full feature set as drawn.** ⚡ **Its own `Position` cell
says *"the anonymous surface is buildable from S3"*** — **and there is no design
for an anonymous surface.** 📁 [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot
the implementation authority, and the snapshot draws the named one.

### ⚖️ The alternatives, with what each costs

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | **Build the screen as drawn** | ⛔ **Not available.** It needs names (📁 [C-203](#c-203), `DEFERRED`), per-person engagement (**no producer**), and a lawful basis 📁 `committee.py` says has never been declared. ⚡ **And D-074 declined it** |
| **②** | **Build an anonymous surface** — seats, appointments, departures, tenure, gaps | ⚠️ **Buildable from what `people` publishes today** — ⛔ **but no design draws it**, so the lane would be designing a screen, which [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) forbids |
| **③** | **Commission the anonymous design**, then build ② | ✅ **The only path that breaks nothing.** ⛔ **Commissioning a design document is the product owner's** — 📁 [C-1405](#c-1405--the-entry-coverage-review-recommends-four-documents-and-three-of-them-block-work-already-released) established exactly that |
| **④** | **Rule on C-203 and build ①** | 🔴 **The largest of the four.** 📁 C-203 decides Timeline, comments, audit history, AI attribution and mentions **at the same time**, which is why it has stayed open |

### ✅ Recommendation, offered as input and not as authority

**③.** ⚡ **The domain shipped early on D-074's own instruction, and it is
sound** — six modules run role changes through production without a name. ⛔ **What
is missing is a drawn surface for the intelligence the product actually holds**,
and that is a smaller commission than either ① or ④.

⚠️ **Recommending is not deciding** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a lane's
recommendation is architectural input and never implementation authority.*

### ⚡ Implementation impact

⛔ **Nothing is half-built and nothing is reverted.** ✅ **TASK-430's search half
is on `main` and correct.** ⚠️ **The row stays `CLAIMED` rather than moving to
`IN VALIDATION`** — 📁 marking it delivered would say a screen exists that does
not, which is the class [§2](../CLAUDE.md) exists to prevent. ✅ **The lane moved
to the next eligible row rather than idling or inventing an anonymous design.**

## C-112 · After a host reboot every lane's stack stays down silently while prod-local's services return and crash-loop

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **QE**, 2026-08-20, jointly with Lane A after both lanes hit the same signature and mistook it for each other's doing |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner.** **A policy that resurrects three containers per lane on every boot is a decision about developer machines, not a defect fix** — and 📁 [`QUALITY_ENGINEERING.md` §0f](QUALITY_ENGINEERING.md) classes a change to what a repository-level workflow MEANS as ⑤: stop and escalate |
| **Type** | **Decision** — ⚡ **the engineering is three lines; what needs a ruling is whether we want them** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **It cost two lanes an afternoon of mutual suspicion** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** |

### The asymmetry, measured on both compose files and confirmed live

| | |
|---|---|
| 📁 `infra/docker-compose.yml` — **every lane's stack** | ⛔ **`postgres`, `redis`, `minio` declare NO `restart:` at all.** Live: `signora-lane-qe-postgres-1` → **`restart=no`** |
| 📁 `infra/docker-compose.prod.yml` — **prod-local** | **three services carry `restart: unless-stopped`.** Live: `signora-prod-relay-1` → **`restart=unless-stopped`** |

⚡ **So a host reboot leaves every lane's data services down — silently — while prod-local's relay, worker and API return and crash-loop against a database that is not there.**

### ⚠️ What it cost, which is the argument for deciding rather than shrugging

**Lane A saw its stack `Exited (0)` and prod-local `Up 5 seconds`, and reasonably suspected QE's `make down --remove-orphans`.** **QE saw the same shape and offered its own 12 busy loops as a likelier cause.** ⛔ **Both were wrong; neither could have known.** ✅ **Lane A dated the boot from `who -b` — `2026-08-20 17:47:12`, landing between their last successful `docker exec` and the `ConnectionRefusedError` that started the thread — which is what settled it.**

📁 **[B-1034](BUGS.md) already records this shape once**: *"it exited on the host restart ten hours before this cycle."* ⚡ **Twice now.**

### ⛔ Why neither lane is taking it

**`infra/` is `platform_foundation`, which [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) joins to Lane A — so it is theirs to change and they declined**, on the grounds that it is a choice about developer machines rather than a repair. ✅ **QE agrees and is routing it rather than filing it as a defect.** 📁 **Lane A's own words: *"if you would rather it went to the product owner as an infra choice, that is the more honest route and I would lean that way."***

### The QE-side consequence, so the decision has both halves

⚠️ **A cold start after a reboot means the first `make certify` of a session can fail on a stack that is not there** — an **abort**, not a verdict, and 📁 [`QUALITY_ENGINEERING.md`](QUALITY_ENGINEERING.md) already requires QE to tell those apart. ⛔ **And prod-local's crash-looping relay and worker are noise beside anything QE certifies.** ⚡ **Neither is severe; both are avoidable.**

### ⚠️ One thing deliberately left unexplained

**Lane A's containers reported *"Exited (0) 9 hours ago"*, which does not fit a 17:47 stop, and they restarted them so `FinishedAt` is gone.** ✅ **QE's `signora-lane-qe-postgres-1` is self-consistent — stopped 08:32:59, never restarted, `restart=no`.** ⛔ **Lane A declined to invent a staleness theory to make the number fit, and this item does not either.** **The boot explains the observation; the reported exit age remains odd and is recorded as odd.**

## C-111 · Two gates assert a property they do not measure, and fixing that changes what a gate's environment is

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **QE**, 2026-08-20, after holding [B-1039](BUGS.md) and [B-1040](BUGS.md) across three cycles on the same reasoning |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner.** **The fix changes `infra/docker-compose.prod.yml`, which decides what `make smoke` and `make dr` MEAN** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md) puts the compose files among the things that decide whether a gate passes) |
| **Type** | **Decision** — ⚡ **the engineering is understood and small; what needs a ruling is whether QE may change a gate's environment** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚠️ **It costs 162 seconds of every browser gate and leaves four of five populated queues undrained** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** |

> ## 🔴 MEASURED 2026-08-20, cycle 256 — **and it is worse than [B-1039](BUGS.md) states**
>
> **Taken after a full product exercise: 423 browser tests against a freshly seeded production stack, with the stack still up.**
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | `outbox_event` published | **808** |
> | `outbox_event` relayed | **808** — ✅ **the relay is doing its job perfectly, and this is why both gates pass** |
> | `processed_event` | 🔴 **0** |
> | `dead_letter_event` | **0** |
>
> ⛔ **`processed_event` is the idempotency ledger and `claim()` inserts into it before every handler runs** (`event_bus/idempotency.py:37`). ⚡ **Zero rows means NOT ONE event was consumed by ANY consumer.**
>
> ### ⚠️ Not *"four of five pools undrained"* — nothing was consumed at all
>
> | Redis queue | Pending |
> |---|---|
> | `signora:events:read_model` | **139** |
> | `signora:events:intelligence` | **29** |
> | `signora:events:ai_research` | **1** |
> | `signora:events:default` | ⛔ **the key does not exist** |
>
> ✅ **The worker is healthy and behaving exactly as configured** — `"pool":"default"`, `"queue":"signora:events:default"`, `"subscriptions":8`, **zero errors in its log.** ⛔ **`signora:events:default` was never created, so nothing was ever routed to the only pool being drained.** ⚡ **169 events sit pending across three queues nothing is bound to.**
>
> ### 🔴 And both gates reported success against that
>
> **`smoke` printed *"workers consuming without error"*. `make dr` printed *"workers resumed consuming"*.** ⛔ **Neither is false — and neither measured a consumer.** 📁 **That is [B-1040](BUGS.md), demonstrated rather than argued.**
>
> ### ✅ The five questions, answered
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | **What each gate CLAIMS** | that workers are consuming |
> | **What it MEASURES** | `smoke`: the absence of `ERROR` in the worker log · `dr`: `outbox_event.relayed_at`, **which the relay writes** |
> | **What the correct assertion is** | **`processed_event` gained rows** — written by a consumer, so a row proves consumption. **Bounded-deadline poll, exactly the pattern the relay half already uses well** |
> | **Does correcting it change runtime?** | ⛔ **The assertion itself is one query.** ⚡ **Fixing what it exposes removes `notification-arrival`'s 162s.** ✅ **Adding workers costs ~5 containers on `make up`** |
> | **Can it expose a product defect?** | 🔴 **It exposes this one immediately** — **the corrected assertion FAILS on today's stack**, and that is the point |
>
> ⛔ **QE has changed nothing.** ⚠️ **The corrected gate would turn `smoke` and `dr` red until a worker exists per pool**, so the two changes are one change and neither is QE's to take alone.

### The measured position

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pools carrying subscriptions** | `DEFAULT` 8 · `INTELLIGENCE` 2 · `graph` 2 · `READ_MODEL` 1 · `ai_research` 2 — **five** |
| **Pools the local production stack drains** | 🔴 **one** — `docker-compose.prod.yml:143` starts a single worker and sets no `SIGNORA_WORKER_POOL` |
| **What that costs the browser gate** | ⚡ **`notification-arrival` waits out 162s** — **14% of the suite**, and the single largest remaining item in it |
| **What notices** | ⛔ **Nothing.** `smoke.sh` prints *"workers consuming without error"* and tests only the *without error* half; `disaster-recovery.sh:203` prints *"workers resumed consuming"* and measures `relayed_at`, **which is the relay** |

### ⛔ Why QE has not simply done it

📁 **QE has held this three times with the same sentence — *"not while a candidate is mid-cycle"*.** ⚠️ **No candidate is mid-cycle now, so that reason has lapsed, and a reason that keeps lapsing and keeps being reused is an excuse.** ⚡ **The honest blocker is different and it is real:**

> **Adding a worker per pool changes what `make smoke` and `make dr` are run against.** ⛔ **QE's authority is to make a documented gate runnable, never to change what it means** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

⚠️ **And the change would strengthen rather than weaken**: it makes two assertions capable of failing, and it may **surface** tests that currently pass because nothing was consumed. ⚡ **That is the desired direction and it is still a change to the certification boundary**, which is the product owner's to approve.

### What a ruling would authorise

**① One worker service per pool that carries subscriptions**, each with its own `SIGNORA_WORKER_POOL` — 📁 the shape [B-1039](BUGS.md) names, and the one Lane A already built by hand on its own stack. ⛔ **Cost: five more containers on every `make up`.**

**② Then `smoke.sh` stage 12 and `disaster-recovery.sh:203` assert CONSUMPTION** rather than silence — a processed-event row or a handler's visible trace, checked with the bounded-deadline pattern the relay half already uses well.

⚡ **Expected effect: `notification-arrival` passes, 162s leaves the browser gate, and two gates begin measuring what their names claim.** ⛔ **No threshold moves, no test is removed, nothing is skipped.**

### ⚠️ If the answer is *not yet*

✅ **That is a complete answer and QE will record it as one.** **The rows stay open, the 162s stays measured, and nothing is quietly done anyway.**

## C-1535 · The first journey that needs the background tier, and no environment starts one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-19, writing the journey [§19](../CLAUDE.md) requires of [TASK-495](BACKLOG.md) ⓑ |
| **Owner** | **QE** — 📁 [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) is QE's file and *"development environments"* is its one responsibility |
| **Type** | **Environment** — ⛔ **not a defect in the product and not a defect in the gate** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **One spec.** ✅ **Nothing else in the suite reaches a worker**, which is exactly why nobody has met this |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### What the journey needs, measured rather than assumed

📁 **[TASK-495](BACKLOG.md)'s own testing metadata**: *"**Playwright** — an event
occurs and the customer sees it without reloading."* ⚡ **The event is a research
run finishing**, and the chain it travels is:

```
  click  ─▶  API  ─▶  outbox  ─▶  relay  ─▶  arq (ai_research pool)  ─▶  run
                                                                          │
   bell ◀── feed ◀── notification row ◀── workspace_tenancy consumer ◀────┘
```

⛔ **Two processes in that chain are started by nothing in this repository:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The relay** | `python -m apps.worker.relay_main`, and it needs **`SIGNORA_RELAY_DATABASE_URL`** — 📁 the `signora_relay` identity, because [§8](../CLAUDE.md) gives `signora_app` no read grant on `outbox_event`. ⚠️ **Without it the relay retries a `ProgrammingError` forever and says nothing about which credential is missing** |
| **A worker per pool** | `arq apps.worker.main.WorkerSettings` with **`SIGNORA_WORKER_POOL`**. ⚠️ **The default pool is not enough** — 📁 `apps/worker/pools.py` partitions by cost, and research runs in **`ai_research`**. ⛔ **A default-pool worker starts cleanly, logs *"worker started"*, and consumes nothing**, which is the most expensive way this can fail |

**Measured on 2026-08-19**: `grep -rn "relay_main\|WorkerSettings" infra/ review/` returns
**nothing**, and `make review` starts *"both tiers"* — the API and the web app.
✅ **`infra/docker-compose.prod.yml` has both services and is the shape to copy.**

> ## ⚠️ Corrected by measurement — QE, 2026-08-19, cycle 253. **Half of the paragraph above is wrong, and the wrong half is the headline.**
>
> ⛔ **Both processes ARE started.** 📁 `infra/docker-compose.prod.yml:164` runs `python -m apps.worker.relay_main` with `SIGNORA_RELAY_DATABASE_URL` under `signora_relay`; `:143` runs `arq apps.worker.main.WorkerSettings`. **`signora-prod-relay-1` and `signora-prod-worker-1` were both running when this was measured**, and **the browser suite runs against that stack** (3100/8100).
>
> ✅ **This item's own text already said so** — *"`infra/docker-compose.prod.yml` has both services and is the shape to copy"* — **so its two halves disagreed, and the louder one was believed.** ⚠️ **The `grep` above scoped `infra/` and `review/` and reported nothing; `infra/docker-compose.prod.yml` contains both strings.**
>
> ### ⚡ What is actually missing is ONE environment variable, and this item predicted it
>
> 📁 **This item's own second row is exactly right**: *"The default pool is not enough — `apps/worker/pools.py` partitions by cost, and research runs in `ai_research`. A default-pool worker starts cleanly, logs *worker started*, and consumes nothing, which is the most expensive way this can fail."*
>
> **That is precisely what is happening.** `docker-compose.prod.yml:143` sets **no `SIGNORA_WORKER_POOL`**, so the worker binds the `default` queue, while `relay.py:142` enqueues to `queue_name_for(subscription.pool)` — **one queue per pool.**
>
> | Subscriptions registered | |
> |---|---|
> | `DEFAULT` **8** · `INTELLIGENCE` **2** · `graph` **2** · `READ_MODEL` **1** · `ai_research` **2** | ⛔ **Five pools carry work. The stack drains one** |
>
> ### ⛔ Still `OPEN`, and deliberately not closed
>
> **The journey remains blocked** — ⚡ **for a smaller and more fixable reason than this item recorded.** **Filed as [B-1039](BUGS.md)**, because a compose file starting one of five workers the design requires is *something behaving wrongly today* rather than something unbuilt. ✅ **The fix stays QE's and stays out of a mid-certification candidate**: `docker-compose.prod.yml` decides what `make smoke` and `make dr` mean.
>
> ⚠️ **Nothing in this correction criticises the row.** **It named the exact mechanism before anybody had measured it**, and the half that was wrong cost nothing because the half that was right is the one that matters.

### ⚠️ What this lane did instead of waiting

⛔ **It did not weaken the journey**, and the two alternatives were both worse:
**stubbing the arrival** would have removed the only test in the repository that
crosses the whole mechanism, and **asserting the row directly** would have tested
the database rather than the customer's screen.

✅ **The journey's failure message names both processes and both variables**, so a
150-second timeout reads as *"the background tier is not running"* rather than as
a product defect. ⚡ **That is a legible failure, not a fix** — and the fix is a
line in [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) and the review launcher, both QE's.

### ⛔ Why it is not filed as a defect

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md)**: *a defect is something behaving wrongly today; a
dependency is something not yet built or agreed.* ⚡ **Nothing is behaving
wrongly** — **the suite has simply never needed the background tier before**, and
the first row that does is this one.

says so explicitly.

| Kept | Its current authority |
|---|---|
| `GET /workspaces/{id}/accounts` (`opportunity_engine.attention_list`) | ⚡ **A shared capability with two live consumers** — Account 360's *next in sequence*, and onboarding's completion step |
| `components/intelligence/attention.tsx` (6 exports) | **Account 360 renders all six** |
| `components/home/attention-card.tsx` | 📁 Home's `card.attention`, *"Needs you today"* — **a card, not a route** |
| `backend/tests/opportunity_engine/test_attention_list.py` | **Domain ordering of the shared list** |

⚡ **The e2e journeys that used the screen were never ABOUT it** — they entered
through a list and opened a brief. **`AttentionPage` became `AccountsPage` at
`/accounts`**, so nine specs keep their subject and enter through an approved
surface.

### ⚠️ ⑧ Two consequences, stated so neither is rediscovered as a defect

🔴 **One capability leaves the product with the screen.** 📁 **C-204/TASK-456**
put the signal catalog's `why_it_matters` on screen — *"a seller can learn what
the two-word label means"* — **and the Attention row was its only renderer.**
⛔ **Home's attention card and the Signals queue both refuse it deliberately**,
in comments, because it describes the TYPE rather than the instance; **and no
design document in the snapshot asks for it.** ✅ **So it is removed rather than
re-homed — but it was a real capability and this is where that is written down.**

✅ **The empty-workspace question in ⑤ is answered by the shell.** 📁
`composition.ts` returns `activation` for a workspace with no connection, so
Home shows connection steps — **and `Accounts` is one of the nine rail
destinations**, so the book of accounts is reachable without Attention.

### ✅ ① What changed, and it was not optional

📁 **The Authenticated Entry document:** *"Every authenticated person lands on `/w/:workspace/home`"*, and *"**entry resolution belongs to the shell, exclusively**, and a module that wants to influence it registers a rule rather than performing a redirect."*

⚠️ **`/` rendered the Attention screen**, so 🔴 **the twenty-four-rule engine had one production caller — onboarding's exit — and never ran for anybody arriving at `/`.** ⛔ **That is the most travelled path in the product**, and rules 11–14 decide which workspace a person with several memberships enters and whether they see the chooser at all.

✅ **`/` calls `resolveEntry` now.** ⚡ **`replace`, never `push`** — 📁 *"pressing back from Home after login exits to the sign-in page, not into a loop through the resolver."* **Verified in a browser: back from Home leaves the app rather than re-entering the resolver.**

### ⚠️ ② The screen that moved has no design document

**Measured across all 34 documents in `docs/design-snapshot/screens/`: none names an *Attention* screen**, and 📁 **the App Shell's rail vocabulary is Home · Accounts · Pipeline · Deals · Reports · Signals** — **Attention is not among them.**

⚡ **It predates the design corpus.** 📁 [D38](../docs/architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) created it by retiring an Overview page — *"a seller's first screen should be their morning's work"* — **and the Home design now answers exactly that question, from the design's own contract, with the Signal Center owning the queue.**

### ⛔ ③ Moved rather than deleted, deliberately

**Retiring a shipped surface is a product decision, not an implementation one.** ✅ **It kept its content, its filters and its tests at `/attention`**, reached from an account brief's *"All accounts"*. ⚠️ **No rail item was invented for it** — **inventing product navigation to satisfy a reachability check would be worse than the orphan.**

### ⚡ ④ Three ways to close it

**①** **Retire it.** Home is the answer, Signals is the queue, Accounts is the book. ⛔ **Place its orphans first** — see ⑤.
**②** **Keep it and give it an entrance** — a rail item, which 📁 D38 removed screens by name to avoid.
**③** **Keep it unlisted**, reachable from the account brief only, as today.

⚡ **Lane A's recommendation is ①, after the five component families in ⑤ are placed.** ⛔ **It is a recommendation and not a decision** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

### ⚠️ ⑤ It is five component families, not three — and three state responsibilities

🔴 **This row said *"`NeedsIdentity`, `DecidedAccounts` and the stage view"* and that undercounted by two.** ⚡ **Raised by Lane C, then measured independently here across every consumer in `frontend/`:**

| Family | Consumers |
|---|---|
| `NeedsIdentity` · `DecidedAccounts` · `STAGE_MARK` · `TriageStrip`/`NothingRaises` · `AttentionScore` | ⛔ **the Attention screen, and nothing else** |
| `EntityName` | ✅ **4** — both Accounts screens too |
| `ActivationChecklist` | ✅ **also `lib/entry/observed.ts`** |
| `NoWorkspace` | ✅ **10** |

✅ **So retirement orphans five families and not eight** — **the last three survive on their own consumers.** ⛔ **Each of the five needs a named destination BEFORE retirement, not after**: **five single-consumer components are the exact shape that disappears without anybody deciding it should.**

⛔ **This row briefly claimed it also *"redistributes three state responsibilities that currently sit together"* — `ActivationChecklist`, `NoWorkspace` and `StatedAbsence`. ⚠️ That was wrong and is withdrawn.** ✅ **Measured: `NoWorkspace` has nine other consumers and `StatedAbsence` is in THIRTY files.** ⚡ **They are standard page furniture on nearly every screen, not responsibilities this screen holds.** **Only `ActivationChecklist` is near-exclusive, and its other consumer is `lib/entry/observed.ts`** — already named above.

🔴 **The error was method, not arithmetic, and it is worth naming because it repeats**: the first measurement checked the five candidates that turned out to be orphans and **did not check the ones that might not have been**. ⛔ **Every result confirmed the hypothesis because nothing that could refute it was looked at.** ✅ **Nine were measured the second time, and three of them refuted it.**

⚠️ **Its close relative, recorded because the pair travels together**: the withdrawn *"eleven"* came from a `grep` ending in `head -12`, **and the bound was read as the count.** ⛔ **A bound is a display choice; a count is a claim about the repository.** ⚡ **Both failures produce a confident number that agrees with itself** — **one measures too few candidates, the other reads too few results** — **and truncated output looks complete, which is why neither is caught while it is being written.** ✅ **Every number in this section was produced unbounded (`wc -l`, no `head`).**

🔴 **What survives, and it is the half worth ruling on**: 📁 `lib/home/composition.ts` returns `activation` for an empty workspace, **so a workspace with no CRM connected sees connection steps and no account list at all.** ⛔ **Any option that assumes Home covers Attention's job has to say what that workspace sees.** ⚡ **Observed in the Playground, not reasoned about** — ⚠️ **and it is true of Home TODAY, not a consequence of retiring anything.**
