## C-1531 · Home's first-run overlay has no copy id, and its second sentence was false

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-17, browser-verifying Home's seller composition |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — **it is product copy**, not an endpoint |
| **Type** | **A string the design requires and its copy table does not carry** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ The overlay ships and no longer points at an absent card. |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 ① The defect, and only a browser could see it

📁 **Rule 20:** *"Home, with the first-run overlay: **one sentence on what this is, one on what to do**, dismissible forever."* 📁 **And Home:** *"adds the first-run overlay **over whichever composition resolved**."*

⛔ **Sentence two was the literal *"Start by connecting a CRM below — everything on this page fills in from there."*** ⚠️ **The CRM card belongs to the activation composition and is filtered out of the other three**, so **a seller whose workspace was already connected was told to start with a card that was not on the page.**

⚡ **No gate could have caught it.** It is a string literal; nothing in the type system knows which cards a composition renders.

### ⚠️ ② The copy table has no id for it

📁 **§10 carries `HM-COPY-01` … `HM-COPY-12`** and every one of them belongs to a *state*. **None is the overlay.** 📁 The Authenticated Entry document states the *shape* — two sentences — **and supplies neither.**

### ✅ ③ What ships, flagged rather than left false

**One sentence per composition, each naming something that is actually rendered:**

| Composition | Sentence two |
|---|---|
| **Activation** | ✅ *"Start by connecting a CRM below — everything on this page fills in from there."* — **the design's, unchanged** |
| **Seller** | ⚠️ *"Start with what needs you today — every item below says why it is there."* |
| **Executive** | ⚠️ *"Start with the figures below — each one says what it was derived from."* |
| **Revenue operations** | ⚠️ *"Start with the health of your connections below — each one says what needs a person."* |

⛔ **The three marked ⚠️ are authored by this lane and are what needs ratifying.** ⚡ **They were written rather than omitted because the design requires a second sentence** — and a sentence describing the wrong page does not satisfy it. **`first-run-overlay.test.tsx` now refuses a CRM instruction on any data composition**, so the defect cannot return silently.

## C-1530 · Home's U-02 is undecided, and the implementation had to pick

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-17, implementing Home §10's composition switcher |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — 📁 the Home document records it as **U-02** and assigns it there itself |
| **Type** | **An unresolved item the design names, reaching implementation** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ The switcher works; this asks whether it should forget. |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

📁 **The design's own words:** *"Whether a dual-role person switching composition sets that preference permanently or only for the session is undecided."* 📁 **Its interim ruling:** *"switching persists for the session; the profile preference is the only permanent setting."*

### 🔴 The interim ruling is the one option that cannot be built cheaply

⛔ **A session-only switch has nowhere to live.** ⚡ **Home holds no client state store**, 📁 **contract item 8 forbids `localStorage` for Home state** — *"Nothing about activation lives in localStorage"* — and a session store invented for one control is the speculative mechanism [§6](../CLAUDE.md) refuses.

✅ **So the switch writes the profile preference**, which is 📁 **the design's own permanent option** and rule 2's input. ⚠️ **It is reversible from the same control**, so nobody is trapped.

### ⚡ Three ways to close it

**①** **Ratify persistence** — the implemented behaviour becomes the decision. **Cheapest, and it is already reversible.**
**②** **Session-only** — needs a session store and a rule for what a new tab does. ⛔ **And it makes the switch invisible on the next login**, which a reader who deliberately switched may read as the product forgetting.
**③** **Both** — a persistent control plus a *"just for now"* modifier. ⚠️ **Two mechanisms for one choice**, and the design draws one control.

⚡ **Lane A's recommendation is ①.** ⛔ **It is a recommendation and not a decision** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

## C-1529 · Home's attention reasons are model prose, and the contract publishes facts

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-17, implementing Home's `card.attention` |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — **it is a question about what Signora may say**, not about an endpoint |
| **Type** | **A design requirement the current producers can only partly satisfy** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ The card ships with a stated fact per row. |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### ⚡ ① The requirement is right, and it is the reason the card works

📁 **P-08:** *"Every attention item carries a reason. **And a cost of ignoring it.** A ranked list with no stated reason is a list people learn to scroll past within a fortnight."*

### ⚠️ ② The design's reasons are reasoned, not merely factual

📁 **Its own examples:**

> *"Your champion moved to procurement on 4 August and nobody has been re-engaged. **In 412 comparable deals this pattern cost 23 days when left a week. Day nine.**"*

⛔ **Three things there have no producer:** a comparable-deal population, a derived cost in days, and a named committee change. ⚡ **`AccountAttention` publishes** `score`, `trend`, `score_change`, `signal_type`, `contested`, `evidence`, `stage`, `since` — **facts, and good ones.**

### ⛔ ③ And one of them is refused rather than missing

📁 **`AccountAttention`'s own contract:** *"Signora records workflow decisions and **cannot see a call, an email or a meeting**, so it must not say an account is neglected — it says how long it has been since anything it *can* see happened, and the reader decides what that means."*

⚡ **That is the same rule as [C-1528](#c-1528--onboardings-completion-screen-is-built-on-a-forecast-and-the-domain-refuses-to-produce-one)'s forecast**, one surface over: **the design asks for a judgement and the domain deliberately produces a fact.**

### ✅ ④ What ships, and the three ways forward

⚠️ **Amended 2026-08-17, after the product owner ruled `AccountAttention` out of Home the same day.** ⛔ **§③ above described the row's source and no longer does** — 📁 the card now reads the **open signal queue**, and the reason is the signal's own `rationale`. **The dated analysis above is left standing** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)) **and this section states what is true now.**

✅ **The reason improved, and the gap did not close.** 📁 `rationale` is authored *"per signal, not per type"*, **where the reasoning happened** — *"An acquisition may force systems and budgets to be consolidated. Your profile treats this as a supporting indicator. Based on: Announced the acquisition of Ardenway Clinical."* ⚡ **That is a reason with its grounds attached**, which is more than the elapsed-time sentence it replaces.

⛔ **The *cost of ignoring* is still absent.** **No comparable-deal population exists**, so *"in 412 comparable deals this pattern cost 23 days"* remains unproducible — **and the three options below are unchanged by the source moving.**

**①** **Accept the reason as it stands** — the shipped behaviour: a hypothesis, its relevance, and the event it rests on. **Honest, checkable, and it states no cost.**
**②** **Build the comparable-deal population** so a cost in days can be derived. 🔴 **A real capability**, and it must not become a forecast — [C-1528](#c-1528--onboardings-completion-screen-is-built-on-a-forecast-and-the-domain-refuses-to-produce-one) is the boundary it would run into.
**③** **Let the Decision Package's reasoning write the row.** ⚡ `decision-package` already produces cited statements per account; **it is per-account and expensive**, and Home wants five at once.

⚡ **Lane A's recommendation is ①ing now and ③ when a collection-level read exists.** ⛔ **A recommendation, not a decision.**

## C-1528 · Onboarding's completion screen is built on a forecast, and the domain refuses to produce one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-17, reaching screen `09` of the onboarding rebuild |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — ⛔ **a ratified design document and a ratified architectural boundary require opposite things**, and a lane may not choose between them |
| **Type** | **A conflict between the finalized design and the module's stated domain law** |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Screen `09` only.** ✅ Screens 01, 02, 04, 05, 06 and 07 are built and browser-verified; the flow runs end to end and finishes on Connect |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 ① The design's payoff is three numbers, and the third cannot exist

📁 *"09 · Completion — **the payoff is the product, not a congratulation**"*, and it is right to be: a completion screen that congratulates somebody for filling in a form has given them nothing. **The design's answer is three real findings**, and this is the whole point of the screen.

| Design's finding | Its example | Can Signora produce it? |
|---|---|---|
| **Accounts read** | *8,412 · "312 enterprise, of which 41 have an open renewal"* | ⚠️ **No producer today, and buildable** |
| **At risk today** | *$8.3M · "Across 11 deals, concentrated in Negotiation"* | ⚠️ **No producer today, and it raises [ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) §5** |
| **Forecast gap** | *56 pts · "Between the model and the committed number"* | 🔴 **NO — refused by domain law** |

### ⛔ ② The third is not unbuilt. It is forbidden.

📁 **`buying_score_engine/domain/events.py`:**

> ⛔ ***"…it does not forecast a purchase"***

📁 **`buying_score_engine/public/__init__.py`:**

> ⛔ ***"no recommendation, no opportunity, and no probability. A score is a…"***

⚡ **So *"the gap between the model and the committed number"* asks for a model output this product has ruled it does not produce.** ⛔ **It is not a missing endpoint** — building it would reverse the boundary that defines what a Signora score is.

⚠️ **And the same word governs the AI line beneath the findings**: *"ordered by **forecast accuracy** and renewal risk"*. **Half of that ordering is unproducible for the same reason.**

### ⚠️ ③ The second is a real question rather than a gap

**Summing `OPEN_ACV` across at-risk accounts sounds like an endpoint and is not.** 📁 [ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) §5: ***"absence is never inferred, defaulted or zero-filled"*** and ***"a claim is only produced where the provider supplies the fact."***

⛔ **So a total over a set where some accounts have no `OPEN_ACV` silently understates**, and a customer reading *"$8.3M at risk"* has no way to see that it is *"$8.3M across the deals we have a figure for."* 📁 §3 of the same ADR: ***"a figure without its currency is not a fact"*** — **and a figure without its coverage is not one either.**

⚡ **This is answerable** — report the figure with the population it covers — **but the shape is a product decision, not an implementation detail.**

### ✅ ④ The first is straightforwardly buildable

**A count of accounts read.** ⚠️ **The list is keyset-paginated by design, so no total exists anywhere today** — 📁 numbered page jumps are architecturally impossible and a total was never needed. **A count is a small, honest addition.**

### ⚡ ⑤ Three ways out

**①** **Ship the screen with the findings that have producers, and say what is absent.** ⚡ **Build the account count; report *at risk* with its coverage; ⛔ draw no forecast.** **The screen keeps its shape and every number on it is true.**
**②** **Ship the confirmation and the three actions, with no findings**, until the producers exist. ⛔ **This is the *congratulation* the design's own title refuses.**
**③** **Reverse the domain law** so a forecast can be produced. 🔴 **An architectural decision far larger than this screen**, and it would change what a Signora score means.

⚡ **Lane A's recommendation is ①.** **The design's principle — the payoff is the product — survives with two findings; it does not survive a fabricated third.** ⛔ **It is a recommendation and not a decision** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

> ⚠️ **Nothing is half-built while this is open.** Screen `09` is **not started**, and the flow currently completes on Connect — 📁 which is where the design puts *"Connect and finish"* — so **a customer reaches a finished setup today**. **The completion screen adds a payoff; its absence does not leave a dead end.**

## C-1527 · The Onboarding mock draws four type sizes the Design System's scale does not have

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-17, rebuilding onboarding against the finalized design |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — 📁 [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes [`docs/design-snapshot/`](design-snapshot/MANIFEST.md) the implementation authority, ⛔ **and a lane may not decide which of two of its documents wins** |
| **Type** | **A conflict between two ratified design documents** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚡ **Onboarding is shipping** — the resolution below is applied and stated, and a ruling would change class names rather than what anyone can do |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### ⚡ ① The two documents

📁 **`Fortune Signora Design System v2.dc.html`, §04 `typeRows`** — **the scale is nine roles and it is exhaustive:**

| Role | Token | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| Display · Title · Section · Metric | `--text-display` · `--text-title` · `--text-section` · `--text-metric` | 40 · 26 · 18 · 30 |
| Body · Body strong | `--text-body` · `--text-body-md` | **14** / 1.6 / 400 · **14** / 1.6 / 600 |
| Label | `--text-label` | **12.5** / 1.45 / 600 |
| Caption | `--text-caption` | **12** / 1.5 / 400 |
| Column head | `--text-col` | **11** / 1.4 / 600 / +0.06em |

📁 **`Fortune Signora Onboarding.dc.html` uses four sizes that are not on it**, and uses them everywhere:

| Size | Where | Nearest role |
|---|---|---|
| **13.5px** | every control, every primary button | Body (14) |
| **13px** | the role card's label, every secondary action | Label (12.5) |
| **12.5px** | rail items, field labels | ✅ **Label — this one is on the scale** |
| **11.5px** | every supporting line and hint | Caption (12) |

⚠️ **None is more than 1px from a role.** ⛔ **That is what makes it worth a ruling rather than an obvious call** — **a 0.5px difference is invisible on screen and total in the code**, because one form is a token and the other is not.

### ⚠️ ② Why it cannot simply be resolved in favour of the mock

📁 **`frontend/tests/components/design-tokens.test.tsx` refuses an arbitrary `text-…` size inside `components/ui`**, on its own stated reasoning: ***"an arbitrary value is to a scale what a hex colour is to the palette: correct today, and invisible to whoever changes the scale tomorrow."***

⚡ **That guard is the repository's existing answer and it was ratified before this snapshot.** ⛔ **Implementing the mock's literal pixels inside a shared component would require weakening it**, and 📁 [§11](../CLAUDE.md) forbids weakening a guard to make a change pass.

### ✅ ③ What is implemented, and it is stated rather than assumed

**The line the repository already draws, followed rather than moved:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Inside [`components/ui/`](../frontend/components/ui/)** | ⚡ **The Design System's scale.** `choice-cards.tsx` renders the role label as `text-label` and its description as `text-xs` |
| **Inside the onboarding route files** | 📁 **The mock's literal geometry**, as `company-form.tsx` already shipped and as every gate has passed |

⛔ **This split is the guard's own scope and not a new rule Lane A invented.** ⚠️ **It is nonetheless a split**, and a reader comparing the role card with the field label beneath it is comparing 12.5px with 13.5px for no reason either document gives.

### ⚡ ④ The three ways out

**①** **The Design System wins** — ⚡ **the onboarding mock is corrected to the nine roles in the next snapshot.** **Cheapest, and it makes onboarding consistent with every other screen.**
**②** **The Onboarding mock wins** — **the scale gains `13.5` and `11.5`**, which is a 🔴 change to `tailwind.config.ts` and `globals.css` and reaches every surface in the product.
**③** **Neither** — **the split above stands and is documented.** ⛔ **Today's state, and the one nobody chose.**

⚡ **Lane A's recommendation is ①.** 📁 A scale exists so that *"a theme change is a token edit"*, and a screen that opts out of it for half a pixel has taken the cost of a scale without its benefit. ⛔ **It is a recommendation and not a decision** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

> ⚠️ **Related and separate: [B-275](BUGS.md).** **The guard reads raw source, so it also refuses a *comment* explaining why the scale was used** — a defect in the check, not in this conflict.

## C-1525 · TASK-202 was released on a premise a later measurement overturned — every remaining action is forbidden

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-16, claiming [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md) and auditing before building |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — ⛔ **an architectural blocker by [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s test: *a dependency on a decision nobody has made is architectural however small the code would be*** |
| **Type** | 🔴 **A live ruling whose premise a later measurement contradicts** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **[TASK-202](BACKLOG.md) whole.** ⚠️ **Not partly** — the row's own words |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### ⚡ ① The problem

📁 **The row is `READY` on the product owner's ruling at [C-334](#c-334), 2026-08-06:**

> ✅ ***"TASK-202 is `READY` today and stays `READY` — the credential gates its PROMPT RELEASE, never its start."***

⛔ **That premise was true when it was made and a measurement six days later overturned it.** 📁 **[B-260](BUGS.md), recorded on [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md), 2026-08-12:**

> 🔴 ***`reasoning@2` … evaluated under protocol 2 on `granite3.3:2b`, twice, independently: 2 of 2 grounding failures, coverage `0.000`, release REFUSED.*** ⚡ ***The model COMPLETED — no timeout — so this is not [C-222](#c-222)'s wall-clock blocker.***
>
> ⛔ ***"The credential is no longer one blocker among several — it is the LAST UNTRIED VARIABLE."***
>
> ⛔ ***"What it forbids: authoring `@3` against this model until something passes — [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) in writing, [404 §7](architecture/404-epic-g-copilot.md) as this epic's named process risk."***

🔴 **So the start the ruling protected no longer contains any permitted action**, and that is a different fact from the one the ruling was given.

### ⛔ ② The row's stated first slice is forbidden by the row itself

📁 **First slice: *"Author a `reasoning` dataset and evaluate `reasoning@1` under protocol 2."***

⛔ **Two cells above it, the same row forbids exactly that**: *"authoring one now would put a second copy of an evidence set the module shares on purpose — reasoning and narration operate over the identical closed evidence set and a second copy would be a second thing to keep in step"* ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)).

✅ **And the shipped code already settled it.** 📁 `modules/ai_reasoning_engine/evaluation/__main__.py`:

```python
PROMPT = "reasoning"
DATASET = "explanation_narration"
```

⚡ **The reasoning harness EXISTS, already runs under `make eval-reasoning`, and deliberately shares the narration dataset** — **with the reason written above the constant.** ⛔ **So the first slice is not unbuilt; it is refused, by this module, in writing.**

### ⚡ ③ The alternatives, and why each fails

| | |
|---|---|
| **Author the `reasoning` dataset anyway** | ⛔ **A second copy of a shared closed evidence set** — [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *truth has exactly one authoritative representation*. **The module refuses it by name** |
| **Author `reasoning@3`** | ⛔ **Forbidden in writing** by [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) and [404 §7](architecture/404-epic-g-copilot.md) **until something passes** |
| **Raise `InferencePolicy.timeout_seconds` above 60.0** | ⛔ **The change [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) forbids in writing.** ⚠️ **And [B-260](BUGS.md) makes it moot: `@2` COMPLETED and still failed, so the wall clock is not what is wrong** |
| **Change the pinned evaluation model** | ⛔ **Not a lane's** — 📁 [ADR-0028](architecture/adr/0028-model-runtime-by-environment.md) and [§10](../CLAUDE.md): *"the pinned evaluation model is part of the benchmark… changing the model is an architectural decision that belongs to the product owner, never to a coding session working around slow hardware"* |
| **Build phases 2–4 instead** | ⛔ **Phase 2 needs a hosted-model evaluation ([C-410](#c-410)) · phase 3 needs `require_model` to accept `reasoning@1`, which needs a passing evaluation · phase 4 needs Epic C.** 📁 **The row: *"the epic is blocked whole, not partly."*** |

### ✅ ④ The recommendation — and it is input, never authority

**Configure a hosted provider credential for EVALUATION only**, and re-run `make eval-reasoning` against a frontier model.

⚡ **Everything needed already exists and nothing new is built**: 📁 [ADR-0028](architecture/adr/0028-model-runtime-by-environment.md) already makes evaluation's provider **configurable** — *"mock · Ollama · Anthropic · OpenAI · Azure OpenAI · Bedrock · Vertex AI"* — ✅ **and [TASK-420](BACKLOG.md) shipped the OpenAI adapter on 2026-08-15, so a second hosted vendor is registered and waiting for a key.**

⛔ **This changes no production behaviour.** 📁 **Development stays on the deterministic mock** ([§10](../CLAUDE.md)), and **provider remains operational metadata, never an input to a decision.**

### ⚠️ ⑤ The trade-offs

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **For** | **It is the LAST UNTRIED VARIABLE, named as such by the measurement.** ⛔ **Every other variable has been tried and recorded**: two prompt versions, two independent runs, and a completion rather than a timeout |
| ⚠️ **Against** | **A real spend, and a hosted call leaves the machine.** ⛔ **Evaluation data is the recorded golden set rather than a customer's**, so [§10](../CLAUDE.md)'s workspace-scoping rule is not engaged — **stated rather than assumed** |
| ⛔ **The risk of NOT doing it** | 📁 **Epic G is *assigned whole* and blocked whole.** ⚡ **It has been blocked since 2026-08-06 on a question one credential answers**, and the row has been claimed by two lanes without either being able to start |

### 🔴 ⑥ The implementation impact

⛔ **None until it is ruled.** ✅ **After a credential exists: one command** — `make eval-reasoning --model <hosted>` — **and the answer is a recorded evaluation rather than a code change.**

⚠️ **If it PASSES**: `reasoning@1` releases, `require_model` accepts it, and phase 3 unblocks. ⚠️ **If it FAILS**: 📁 **that is the finding [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) is waiting for** — *"authoring `@3` … until something passes"* — **and authoring `@3` becomes permitted for the first time.**

> ✅ **Either outcome discharges the epic's blocker. Neither is available without the credential, and that is the whole of this item.**

## C-1524 · The platform's principal type is human-only, and the row that needs it is claimed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-16, auditing [TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md) before writing a line |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner + ADR** — 📁 [§20a](../CLAUDE.md), `signora_platform/**` is frozen |
| **Type** | 🔴 **A ratified model that was never built, and a claimed row that needs it** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The authentication half of [TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md).** ✅ **Not the credential lifecycle, the hashing, the one-time display or the per-call record — those sit above this boundary** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED [D-238](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ③: the existing ratification is sufficient authority; ⛔ do not create another approval layer.** ⚠️ **Closed 2026-08-16 — this row read `OPEN`/`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` after the ruling, which is the [C-213](#c-213) class in this office's own register.** *(was: **`OPEN`** ·…)*

### 🔴 An API-key request has nowhere to say it is not a person

📁 **`signora_platform/auth/principal.py`:**

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuthenticatedPrincipal:
    user_id: UUID
    session_id: str
    email: str
    email_verified: bool
    active_workspace_id: UUID | None
    token_id: str
```

⛔ **Every field is human**, and its own docstring says it is *"the ONLY representation of caller identity in the system."*

📁 **[495](architecture/495-principal-and-identity-boundary.md) already measured this and said it in the same words** — *"every field is human, and every non-human caller in [D-176](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §1 is unrepresentable"* — **and ratified the repair:**

> ✅ ***"One principal type. A `kind`. A `subject_id`. A workspace. And — the field that does the real work — `acting_for`."***

⚠️ **Ratified 2026-08-13 and not built.** ⛔ **`signora_platform/**` is 🔴, so a lane may not build it** ([§20a](../CLAUDE.md)).

### ⚡ The asymmetry, and the frontend is the one that got it right

📁 **`frontend/lib/entry/principal.ts` ships `PRINCIPAL_KINDS` and `resolveEntryFor(principal, …)`**, delivered by [TASK-1407](BACKLOG.md) with an explicit argument for the timing:

> ✅ ***"Widened while `resolveEntry` has ZERO callers — after the shell, the compositions and the cards consume it, the same change is a refactor across six."***

⛔ **The backend platform never received the same widening**, and [TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md) is the first row that cannot proceed without it.

🔴 **And the argument for ruling it SOON is that the asymmetry is now inverted, which QE named**: **`resolveEntry` was widened at zero callers deliberately; `AuthenticatedPrincipal` already has MORE than zero.** ⚡ **Its own docstring is the measure of that** — *"this is the ONLY representation of caller identity in the system. Nothing downstream re-reads the token."* ⛔ **So every request path in the product goes through it, and the cost of the widening only rises from here.** ⚠️ **The frontend row paid the cheap version of this bill on purpose; the backend is being offered the expensive one, and it gets more expensive every slice.** ⚡ **[TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md)'s own body predicted this**: *"TASK-1407 widens the entry engine to admit a NON-HUMAN principal. This row is where non-human principals come from. The two must agree on what a service principal is."*

### ⛔ A second thing, and it is a design decision this lane is TAKING rather than asking

📁 **[ADR-0414 §4](architecture/adr/0414-machine-credentials-bounded-context.md) hands this row *"the key format and hashing scheme"* and *"the API shape"*, so this is stated rather than asked** — ⚠️ **but it interacts with the Security Invariant and is worth reading before validation.**

📁 **`Authorizer.is_allowed(role, workspace_id, resource, action)` — the subject term is a ROLE STRING.** ⛔ **A key has a SCOPE, not a role, and *"a scope narrower than its creator's"* cannot be a Casbin subject**: 📁 `policy.csv` is read-only at runtime by design ([ADR-0010](architecture/adr/0010-identity-and-access.md) — *"policy changes ship as code review"*), **so a per-key policy row cannot be written at issuance.**

✅ **The model this row adopts:**

> 🔴 ***The GRANT is Casbin's alone. A key's scope can only SUBTRACT.***

⛔ **A key can never permit what Casbin denies for its owner's role.** ⚡ **The scope is a filter applied AFTER the enforcer answers, never a second enforcer** — which is 📁 [TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md)'s own invariant, *"enforced by the same enforcer as a human's, never by a parallel check"*, satisfied exactly rather than approximately.

✅ **And it is checkable rather than assertable**: for every `(resource, action)` pair the product defines, `key_allowed ⊆ casbin_allowed(owner_role)` — **an invariant that enumerates the product rather than sampling it.**

### ✅ What is asked

**Whether [495](architecture/495-principal-and-identity-boundary.md)'s principal model is built now, and by whom.** ⚠️ **It is `signora_platform/**`, so not a lane's.** ⚡ **Lane A continues on everything above that boundary meanwhile and will say plainly which half is missing at handoff.**

## C-1522 · The engine's last-used hint exists, and its key is private to a frozen module

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, wiring [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md) — ⚡ **found by trying to build the caller, which is the only way it could have been found** |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — 📁 [§20c](../CLAUDE.md), the frontend foundation is 🔴 and `lib/state` is named in it |
| **Type** | ⚠️ **A budget question, not a design one.** ✅ **Nothing is wrong; the fact is simply not reachable from where it is needed** |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Degrades [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md) rather than blocking it** — rules 12 and 14 cannot fire, so rules 11-14 resolve on membership COUNT alone |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED [D-238](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑤: expose the required state. known → continue · ambiguous → ASK · ⛔ never silently choose the first.** ⚠️ **Closed 2026-08-16 — this row read `OPEN`/`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` after the ruling, which is the [C-213](#c-213) class in this office's own register.** *(was: **`OPEN`** ·…)*

### 🔴 The fact exists and the engine cannot read it

📁 **`frontend/lib/state/workspace-provider.tsx:18`:**

```ts
const ACTIVE_WORKSPACE_KEY = 'signora.activeWorkspaceId';
```

⛔ **Not exported.** 📁 **`EntrySession.lastUsedWorkspaceId` is what rules 12 and 14 read**, and its own comment names the hazard it manages — [D-196](DECISION_REGISTER.md), *"a stored preference that OUTLIVES membership."*

⚠️ **Re-declaring the string inside `lib/entry` was considered and refused**: 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *truth has exactly one authoritative representation.* ⛔ **Two copies of a storage key drift in the one way nothing catches — the engine reads a key nobody writes, and every person silently becomes *no last-used*.**

### ⛔ And `activeWorkspace` is not a substitute, which is the part worth reading

⚡ **The provider already exposes `activeWorkspace`, so the obvious move is to use it.** 🔴 **It is a different fact.** 📁 The provider's own effect:

```ts
return isStillAMember ? stored : first.id;
```

⛔ **It falls back to `workspaces[0]`, so it is NEVER null while a membership exists.** ⚠️ **Feeding it to the engine would make rule 13 (`AMBIGUOUS`) unreachable** — and rule 13 is the one that shows the chooser. ⚡ **So the product would silently enter somebody's first workspace where the design specifies asking them**, and it would look correct because they would land somewhere plausible.

### ✅ What is asked

**Either** ⓐ **export the constant** — one word, no behaviour, and the narrowest possible change to a 🔴 file — **or** ⓑ **have `WorkspaceContextValue` publish `lastUsedWorkspaceId` as the RAW stored hint, distinct from `activeWorkspace`.**

⚡ **ⓑ is better and larger**: it names the distinction above in the type, so the next lane cannot make the substitution this item exists to warn about. ⛔ **ⓐ is what unblocks the rules tomorrow.**

⚠️ **Lane A has implemented neither.** 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) — *touching a file outside your budget is a finding to raise, not a change to make.*

## C-1523 · Nothing in the repository produces the intent the entry engine reads

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, wiring [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — 📁 [§20c](../CLAUDE.md), **Routing** is frontend foundation |
| **Type** | 🔴 **An unreachable primitive, and a promoted one** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Rules 06-09 entirely** — the four intent rules — **and with them the customer-visible half of [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED [D-238](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④: no product-owner ruling; routed to the frontend foundation. ⛔ Do not invent `?next=` behaviour to unblock a row.** ⚠️ **Closed 2026-08-16 — this row read `OPEN`/`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` after the ruling, which is the [C-213](#c-213) class in this office's own register.** *(was: **`OPEN`** ·…)*

### 🔴 A promoted module with no producer

📁 **[TASK-1402](BACKLOG.md) is `PROMOTED` and shipped `lib/entry/intent.ts`** — `captureIntent · encodeIntent · decodeIntent · classifyIntent`, 21 tests, the open-redirect refusal, the local `not_member` decision. ✅ **All of it correct.**

⛔ **Measured 2026-08-15: `git grep` for a writer of `?next=` across `app/`, `components/` and `lib/` returns NOTHING outside `lib/entry` itself.** ⚡ **The consumer was built and the producer never was**, so four of the engine's twenty-four rules read a parameter no code sets.

### ⚠️ Where the producer would have to live, and why it is 🔴

📁 **`frontend/app/(app)/layout.tsx:35`:**

```ts
if (!session?.user) redirect('/signin');
```

🔴 **That line is where the attempted route is discarded**, and it is the only place that sees a signed-out person asking for a protected page. ⛔ **A Next 15 server layout cannot read the pathname** — the supported mechanism is a root `middleware.ts`, **which does not exist in this repository and is Routing.**

⚠️ **Alternatives were measured and each is worse**: **per-page capture** puts the rule in every page under `(app)` and is what the layout's own comment already rejects — 📁 *"declared on the segment, so it covers every page beneath it rather than relying on five files each remembering"* — and **`Referer`** is referrer-policy dependent and silently absent, which is the worst failure mode for a security-sensitive input.

### ⛔ A second finding, delivered with it: three of *the five* are not the engine's

📁 **[TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md) names five call sites.** ⚡ **Three of them happen BEFORE authentication succeeds** — `register-form` → `/verify`, `reset-password-form` → `/reset/done`, and the `(app)/layout` line above → `/signin`.

🔴 **There is no reason code for *never signed in*.** 📁 **All twenty-four rules presume an identity** — `AccountStanding` is *active · locked · suspended · deleted · pending_deletion* and `SessionStanding` is *valid · expired · step_up_required*; **none of them means *nobody is here*.**

⛔ **Mapping it to `SESSION_EXPIRED` would write a false answer into the record support reads** — 📁 the diagnostics bundle exists precisely to answer *"why did I land here"*, and telling somebody their session expired when they never had one is the [§10](../CLAUDE.md) *failure attribution must be truthful* rule in the routing layer.

✅ **The engine's own name is the resolution: it is the AUTHENTICATED Entry engine.** ⚡ **The row's five are two.**

### ✅ What is asked

**Whether a root `middleware.ts` may exist**, and if so **whether it is Lane A's to write or the foundation's.** ⛔ **Lane A has not written one.**

**Remove the `[[blocked]]` entry, and — the part that matters more —** ⚠️ **consider whether the queue's `blocked` array should be DERIVED from the backlog rather than maintained beside it.** 📁 **Two hand-kept lists of the same fact is the [C-213](#c-213) class, and it has now produced a stale block twice in one file in one week.**

📁 **[TASK-1432](BACKLOG.md):**

> ✅ ***"One module renders a figure that `period`, `region`, `segment` or `owner` would narrow, and reads it from `scope.ts`."***

📁 **Its release says the condition fired:** *"This row was checked twice before and stayed sequenced because no module read `lib/shell/scope.ts` — **grep found**…"*

### ⛔ Measured, and nothing imports it

```
$ grep -rn "from '@/lib/shell/scope'" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx frontend
tests/unit/scope.test.ts:20:} from '@/lib/shell/scope';
```

🔴 **The only importer in the entire frontend is the file's own unit test.**

⚠️ **The two files a path-grep matches name it in COMMENTS:**

| File | What actually matches |
|---|---|
| `components/shell/top-bar.tsx:29` | *"`lib/shell/scope.ts` has to the filter strip"* — **prose in a docstring** |
| `components/shell/copilot.tsx:95` | *"the direction [`scope.ts`](…) refuses by name"* — **prose in a docstring** |

⚡ **`copilot.tsx` does take a `scope` prop — and it is a `string`**, not `scope.ts`'s type, and it renders it as a line of text. ⛔ **Nothing narrows a figure by it.**

### ⚠️ Why it matters more than a mis-sequenced row

📁 **The row states its own consequence:**

> ⛔ ***"A seller who sets the period to Q3 and sees every figure unchanged learns the filter is broken, and stops trusting the ones that work."***

✅ **So shipping it now would produce exactly the outcome the row was sequenced to prevent** — **four chips serialising into the URL with nothing reading them.**

### ⚡ The reusable half, and it is today's fourth instance of one shape

⛔ **A path string appearing in a file is not evidence that the file DEPENDS on it.** ✅ **The checkable form is the import**, and 📁 `infra/reachability.py` already learned the same lesson one register over: *"a route named in a file that renders links is a door; a route named in a file that renders nothing is a declaration."*

> ⚡ **The operand again: `grep -l <path>` answers *"which files mention this"*, and the question was *"which modules depend on this"*.**

## C-1517 · The Workspace Chooser's verbatim copy says *workspace*; ADR-0034 says that is the platform's word

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, starting [TASK-1421](BACKLOG.md) — ⚡ **before writing a string**, which is where this has to be caught |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner**, through Lane C — ⛔ **[ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) is ratified and the design snapshot is the implementation authority ([D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md)); a lane may not choose between them** |
| **Type** | ⚠️ **A conflict between a ratified ADR and the finalized design.** ✅ **Not blocking — implemented in the direction the ADR and the shipped product already take, and raised rather than resolved quietly** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** ⚡ **The screen is built; only which noun it uses is in question** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 The two documents use different words for one concept

📁 **`Fortune Signora Workspace Chooser.dc.html`, §04 *WS-B rendered*, under *Copy — verbatim*:**

> **"Choose a workspace"** · **"You are a member of four. Signora will remember this choice on this device…"** · **"Search four workspaces"** · **"Create a workspace"**

📁 **[ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md):**

> ✅ ***"A customer says Organization… The platform says workspace, tenant, provider…"*** **"Both are correct; exactly one reaches a screen."**

⛔ **And it is enforced, not merely stated**: `frontend/tests/components/vocabulary.test.tsx` lists `workspace` first among `INTERNAL_TERMS` and fails any screen literal containing it.

### ⚠️ The design's own banned list is what makes this a question rather than a slip

📁 **§09: *"Banned: 'Select a tenant', **'Organisation'**, 'No workspaces found', 'Access denied' alone…"***

⚡ **Two readings, and they lead to opposite screens:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **① The British SPELLING is banned** | ✅ **Compatible with ADR-0034** — which uses *Organization*. **The rest of the design's copy would then be describing the concept in engineering's words, as design documents often do** |
| **② The CONCEPT is banned on this screen** | ⛔ **Directly contradicts ADR-0034**, and would make *workspace* the customer's word here and nowhere else |

⛔ **Neither reading is available from the document**, and the difference is every string on the screen.

### ✅ What was built, and why that direction

**The customer's vocabulary — *organization*.** ⚡ **Three reasons, in order of weight:**

1. 📁 **[ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) is ratified architecture with an enforcing gate.** ⛔ **The design's verbatim copy fails that gate**, and a screen that cannot pass the repository's own vocabulary test is not shippable as written.
2. ⚡ **The shipped WS-A switcher already made this call** — `components/shell/workspace-switcher.tsx` renders *"Switch organization"*, *"Filter organizations"*, *"No organization matches …"*. 🔴 **The design's own §03 says both surfaces render the same row and differ only in container** — ⛔ **so a chooser saying *workspace* beside a switcher saying *organization* would be the two surfaces disagreeing about what the thing is called.**
3. ⚠️ **The ROUTE is unchanged and stays `/workspaces`.** 📁 ADR-0034: *"no table, column, API path, JWT claim, module, type or architecture document is renamed."* ✅ **The translation is at the edge, exactly as it says.**

### ⚠️ What is actually being asked

**Which reading of the banned list is right** — ⛔ **not which word is better.** ✅ **If ① , nothing changes and this row closes.** ⚠️ **If ②, it is a change to ADR-0034 rather than to this screen**, because the shipped switcher, the team screens and the entry gates all already say *organization* — 📁 `gates.ts:111` offers *"Go to your organizations"*, **and that is the label on the control that sends somebody to this very route.**

## C-1516 · A raw record says where a payload came from, never what it IS

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, building [TASK-1477](BACKLOG.md) ⓑ — ⚡ **found by writing the mapper and discovering it cannot be registered** |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner**, through Lane C — ⚠️ **all three modules are Lane A's, and the change is still a CONTRACT change across them** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)) |
| **Type** | ⚠️ **An implementation blocker on registering a second mapper for one provider.** ✅ **Not architectural — nothing needs deciding that has not been decided; it needs a discriminator that does not exist** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The HubSpot deal mapper reaching a record.** ✅ **The mapper itself is written and testable; [TASK-1477](BACKLOG.md) ⓐ, the vocabulary, is delivered and unaffected** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 The registry holds one mapper per provider, and it fails silently

📁 `provider_normalization/infrastructure/mappers/__init__.py`:

```python
MAPPERS: dict[str, ProviderMapper] = {
    mapper.provider: mapper for mapper in (…, HubSpotCompanyMapper())
}
```

⛔ **`HubSpotDealMapper.provider` is `"hubspot"`, exactly as it must be.** ⚡ **Measured rather than reasoned about:**

```
registry size for two hubspot mappers: 1
survivor: HubSpotDealMapper
```

🔴 **Adding the deal mapper to that tuple DELETES the company mapper**, and **nothing fails** — every firmographic claim a customer's CRM supplies would simply stop being produced. ⚠️ **A dict comprehension, last-wins, no error.**

### ⛔ Why the obvious discriminators do not work

| Candidate | Why not |
|---|---|
| **A second `provider` string** — `"hubspot_deal"` | ⛔ **`provider` is provenance and travels onto every claim.** 📁 `crm.py`: *"a claim from HubSpot is a claim… nothing downstream branches on where evidence came from."* **One CRM would look like two sources** |
| **`capability`** — the raw record already carries it | ⛔ **`CRM_RECORDS`' own docstring covers both**: *"The customer's own account **and opportunity** records."* ⚡ **One capability, two object shapes, decided deliberately** |
| **Dispatch on the payload's shape** | ⛔ **HubSpot returns companies and deals from different endpoints and the objects carry no type field.** **A *"does this look like a deal?"* branch is the interpretation this layer exists to refuse** |

### ⚡ The knowledge exists at acquisition and is thrown away

📁 **`raw_provider_record` records `provider` · `capability` · `external_id` · `occurred_at` · `payload`.**

> 🔴 **The fetcher knows it called `/crm/v3/objects/deals`. The stored record does not.**

⛔ **That is the whole defect, and it is one sentence: a raw record says where a payload came from and never what it IS.**

### ✅ Recommended, and it is input rather than authority

**A nullable `record_kind` on `raw_provider_record`, set by the source that fetched it, and a registry keyed on `(provider, record_kind)`.**

- ⚡ **Additive.** Existing records carry `NULL` and resolve exactly as today; **no stored row changes meaning.**
- ⛔ **Nothing branches on the value but the registry.** The kind is a mapper-selection key, **never a fact about the account**, and no claim carries it.
- ⚠️ **It touches three modules** — `provider_platform`'s table, `integrations`' source, `provider_normalization`'s registry — **all Lane A's, and still a contract change rather than a local one.**

### ⛔ What this lane did NOT do, and the reason is the rule it keeps applying to others

**The deal mapper is written, typed and lint-clean.** ⛔ **It is NOT committed**, because **a mapper that cannot be registered cannot run even when records arrive** — 📁 **the unreachable-primitive class**, and this lane has filed that finding against other people's work three times this week.

✅ **The design is recorded here so nothing is lost**: the subject is the **associated company and never the deal** — *"attributing it to the deal's own id would mint a company per deal"* — `closedate` is ⛔ **not** a renewal date, and an unknown `dealstage` becomes `CommercialStageValue(position=None, label=…)` rather than a rejection, **so the customer sees the deal and is told it is unmapped.**

## C-1515 · Every commercial fact is a deal property, and nothing fetches a deal

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, auditing [TASK-1477](BACKLOG.md) **before writing a line** — 📁 the order [TASK-1478](BACKLOG.md) says this programme depends on |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner**, through Lane C — ⛔ **it is an assignment and sequencing question, and [C-300](#c-300--provider-platform-owns-the-half-of-the-inbound-path-lane-b-may-not-build) already holds the neighbouring one** |
| **Type** | ⚠️ **An implementation blocker on the CONSUMERS, not on the vocabulary.** ✅ **The vocabulary is delivered; the mapper is buildable; only acquisition is not** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **All three consumers [ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) §6 releases** — Companies' *Open ACV* and *Renewal* columns, [TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md)'s deal record, [C-297](#c-297)'s Forecast. ✅ **Nothing else** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 Measured, before anything was built

📁 **[ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) §3 names three attributes.** ⛔ **In both CRMs the design and the repository name, all three are properties of a DEAL — never of a company.**

| Attribute | HubSpot | Salesforce |
|---|---|---|
| **`OPEN_ACV`** | `deal.amount` | `Opportunity.Amount` |
| **`COMMERCIAL_STAGE`** | `deal.dealstage` | `Opportunity.StageName` |
| **`RENEWAL_DATE`** | ⚠️ **no standard property on either object** — a custom field in practice | ⚠️ **same** |

⛔ **And the only CRM read path in the repository is company-only:**

```
modules/integrations/infrastructure/hubspot.py:44
_BASE: Final = "https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/companies"
```

⚡ **`HubSpotCompanies` · `HubSpotCompanySource` · `HubSpotCompanyMapper`** — **three classes, all company.** ✅ **Measured: `grep -rn "deal\|opportunit"` over `integrations/infrastructure/` returns nothing**, and `ProviderName` holds five enrichment and intent suppliers with **no CRM member at all.**

### ⚡ The design already knows the object is Opportunity

📁 **`Fortune Signora CRM Integrations.dc.html`, and it is unambiguous:**

> **"Connected 14 Mar 2026 by L. Petrova · 8,412 accounts, **3,104 opportunities**, 24,880 contacts in sync."**
>
> **"Field mappings — **Opportunity**"** · *"28 mapped · 2 need attention · 1 write-back"*

⛔ **So the gap is not a design gap.** ✅ **The design specifies a synced Opportunity object with its own field-mapping surface; the repository has never fetched one.**

### ✅ What this lane did anyway, and why it is not blocked on this item

⚡ **The vocabulary is delivered** — `ClaimDomain.COMMERCIAL`, the three attributes, `MoneyValue`, `CommercialStageValue`, `VOCABULARY_VERSION` → `2`. 📁 **ADR-0409 §1 calls that *"the whole of the architectural half"***, and it encodes no assumption about acquisition.

✅ **A HubSpot DEAL mapper is buildable next, on `crm.py`'s own stated reasoning**: *"Nothing here decides how the payload arrived… the gap Epic E1 found is in **acquiring** records, not in interpreting them."* ⛔ **That is the precedent that made the company mapper buildable while [ADR-0300](architecture/adr/0300-inbound-customer-systems.md) was still proposed, and it applies unchanged.**

### 🔴 What actually needs a decision

⛔ **Who builds the deal read path, and when.** 📁 **[ADR-0300](architecture/adr/0300-inbound-customer-systems.md) is `PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED` and Option A is BUILT** — `IntegrationSourceAdapter`, `Capability.CRM_RECORDS`, `HubSpotCompanySource` are on `main`. ⚠️ **What remains is [409](architecture/409-inbound-source-port-contract.md) steps 3–5 in `provider_platform`** — the event annotation, the runner, a simulated adapter — **held on [C-300](#c-300--provider-platform-owns-the-half-of-the-inbound-path-lane-b-may-not-build), `DEFERRED` with the runner as its trigger.**

> ⛔ **So the port exists, nothing drives it, and a second sibling source would be a second thing nothing drives.**

⚠️ **Stated plainly rather than sequenced around: shipping the Companies *Open ACV* column against no acquisition path would render an empty cell for every account, forever** — 📁 **the decorative class [§2](../CLAUDE.md) names, and P-A's *a failed read must never render as an empty result* is the same rule one layer up.**

### ✅ What this lane recommends, and it is input rather than authority

**Build the deal mapper next** — it is complete, testable and encodes no assumption — **and sequence the consumers behind whatever ruling C-300's trigger produces.** ⛔ **Do not ship a column that can only ever be empty.**

## C-1514 · ADR-0409 §3 does not describe the unmapped stage the design requires

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, implementing [TASK-1477](BACKLOG.md)'s vocabulary |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner**, through Lane C — ⛔ **the shape of a ratified contract's value is not a lane's to change silently** |
| **Type** | ⚠️ **A gap between a ratified ADR and the finalized design.** ✅ **Implemented in the direction the design requires, and raised rather than resolved quietly** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** ⚡ **The vocabulary ships with the optional position** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 The two documents describe different values

📁 **[ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) §3:**

> **`COMMERCIAL_STAGE`** — *"**A closed canonical position**, carrying the tenant's own label beside it."*

⚡ **Which reads as though a canonical position is always present.**

📁 **`Fortune Signora CRM Integrations.dc.html`:**

> *"Salesforce added **"Legal review"** and **"Procurement"** to StageName last week. **214 opportunities now sit in stages Signora treats as unmapped**, and their velocity metrics are **excluded until mapped**."*

### ⛔ Unmapped is a state the product shows, counts and acts on

⚠️ **Not an error. Not a gap to be filled. Not a missing claim.** ⚡ **The design puts a NUMBER on it — 214 — offers *"Map both →"*, and states a consequence: velocity metrics are excluded.** **A value that cannot express it cannot render that screen.**

🔴 **And the alternative is worse than a missing feature.** ⛔ **Coercing an unknown tenant stage into the nearest canonical position is precisely the invention ADR-0409 exists to prevent** — 📁 its own §3: *"A free string would be a `value: Any` in disguise."* **A wrong canonical position is not a disguise; it is a false fact.**

### ✅ What was implemented

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CommercialStageValue:
    position: CommercialStage | None   # None means: maps to nothing canonical
    label: str                          # the tenant's own word, always present
```

⚡ **`is_mapped` is the predicate the design's *"excluded until mapped"* needs**, in one place rather than in every consumer that has to honour it. ⛔ **An empty label raises** — a stage with no label is a claim about nothing.

### ⚠️ What is being asked

**Whether ADR-0409 §3 should record the optional position**, or whether the office reads the design differently. ✅ **Either answer is implementable and the code is already in the direction the design requires** — ⛔ **what must not happen is the ADR and the type disagreeing about a ratified contract with nobody having noticed.**

## C-1513 · The design snapshot says both *"New role"* and *"Custom roles are deliberately absent"*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, building [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) slice ⓸ — ⚡ **found by reading both screens the ADR releases**, not by review |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner**, through Lane C — ⛔ **the design snapshot is not a lane's to edit**, and neither is which half is right |
| **Type** | ⚠️ **A contradiction inside one snapshot**, not a dependency. **Nothing is blocked** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** 📁 **[ADR-0410](architecture/adr/0410-authorization-capability-layer.md) §6 rules it already** — it releases *New role* by name — **and slice ⓸ is built on that reading and shipped** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — ⚡ **filed so the design says one thing rather than two**, before a later slice reads the other half and builds the opposite |

### ⛔ The two sentences, both in `docs/design-snapshot/screens/`

📁 **`Fortune Signora Settings.dc.html`, the *Roles & permissions* card:**

> ✅ ***"Five roles · permissions are additive, never subtractive"***, with a ***"New role"*** control beside it.

📁 **`Fortune Signora Team Management.dc.html`, the role matrix:**

> ⛔ ***"Full · Team-scoped · Own only · Read · None. Roles are fixed; scope comes from teams. Custom roles are deliberately absent — they become unauditable within a year."***

### 🔴 Three disagreements, not one

| | Settings | Team Management |
|---|---|---|
| **Can a customer define a role?** | ✅ ***New role*** | ⛔ ***"Custom roles are deliberately absent"*** |
| **How many roles are there?** | **Five** | **Five, named** — `Owner · Admin · Analyst · Member · Guest` |
| **Can a role take something away?** | ⛔ ***"additive, never subtractive"*** | ⚡ **The matrix draws `Analyst` as NARROWER than `Admin`**, which is subtraction |

### ⚡ What this lane did, and why it needs no ruling to have shipped

📁 **ADR-0410 §6 is the ratified contract and it names the control:** ✅ ***"Settings — Roles & permissions, New role."*** ⛔ **So the Settings half is the one implemented**, and [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot the *implementation* authority while the ADR is the ratified decision — **and where a ratified ADR names a control explicitly, it is not ambiguous.**

⚠️ **The third row is the one that would have mattered most, and this lane recorded its reasoning in `capability.py` rather than leaving it implied.** 🔴 ***"Additive, never subtractive"* and a narrower `Analyst` cannot both hold**, and **a capability role that could only add makes a narrower one unbuildable** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md): *a design that cannot express the product.* ✅ **Replacement is what the Security Invariants assert**, and 📁 **ADR-0410 §5's safe direction survives it**: an unlisted pair denies for a capability role exactly as it does for `member`.

### ✅ What is actually being asked

**Which half of the snapshot is current** — ⛔ **not which is better.** ⚡ **`Five roles` and `Custom roles are deliberately absent` read as an EARLIER revision than a *New role* button**, and 📁 [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) says a refresh is a new baseline **assessed before it propagates** — so **the two halves may simply have been refreshed at different times.**

⚠️ **If custom roles are genuinely out**, ⛔ **the capability layer is unaffected and only the *New role* control is** — the roles would become a fixed set defined in `policy.csv` rather than by a customer, and **everything else in slice ⓸ stands.**

## C-1512 · [ADR-0413](architecture/adr/0413-customer-authored-notes-and-tasks.md) creates a bounded context and names no module for it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, starting [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) slice ⓷ — ⚡ **before writing a line**, which is what [C-225](#c-225--wave-1s-technology-stack-section-has-no-contract-a-screen-can-reach-and-414-counts-it-twice) cost when it was not |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — ⛔ **a new module or bounded context is 🔴 in the Change Budget**, and this lane may not create one |
| **Type** | 🔴 **Architectural blocker**, not an implementation one — [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *no accepted architecture exists for the next step* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Slice ⓷ entirely.** ✅ **Nothing else** — slice ⓸ ([ADR-0410](architecture/adr/0410-authorization-capability-layer.md)) is unaffected and this lane has moved to it |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED [D-238](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ①, product owner, 2026-08-15: create the new bounded module `notes_and_tasks`; ⛔ NOT `commercial_profile`.** ⚠️ **Closed 2026-08-16 — this row read `OPEN`/`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` after the ruling, which is the [C-213](#c-213) class in this office's own register.** *(was: **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** — ⚡ **all six things [§20e]…)*

### 🔴 The problem

📁 **ADR-0413 §1 says this is a new category in the product's own words:**

> ⚡ ***"This is the first time Signora becomes the system of record for something a customer creates."*** *"That is why retention, export, permissions and audit follow from it — not as scope creep, but because a system of record owes them and a read-only platform did not."*

⛔ **And §7's list of what it deliberately did not decide names schema · API shape · the migration · versioned-or-append-only · task state vocabulary · reminders and due dates · retention periods · export format · any UI.** ⚠️ **It does not name the module**, so the delegation [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) grants this lane — *"§7 items are Lane A's to propose in the Slice Handoff"* — **does not reach it.**

### ⚠️ Measured before raising

**Nothing exists.** `grep` over `backend/modules/` finds **no note or task table, no migration, no domain type, no `tenancy_policy.py` row, no route.** ⛔ **A clean build with no home.**

### The affected modules, and why none of them is the answer

| | Why not |
|---|---|
| **`commercial_profile`** | ⚡ **The closest, and it is the one this lane would reach for.** ⛔ **But its bounded context is what a customer DECLARES about their commercial setup** — products, ideal customer, buying committee, competitors, target accounts, and now tags, owner and segments. **A note is not a declaration; it is a record somebody wrote about an account** — and ADR-0413's own retention, export and audit obligations attach to the module, which this one has never carried |
### 🔴 The precedent that points the other way, and the answer to it

⚠️ **`commercial_profile` already holds Tags, and a tag is customer-authored too** — nobody declared it and nobody asserted it. 📁 **[ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md) put them there at migration `0051`, which this lane wrote.** ⛔ **So *"its context is what a customer DECLARES"* does not survive the question *"why do notes not follow tags?"***

✅ **Found by Lane C reviewing this item rather than accepting it.** ⚡ **The real distinction is in ADR-0413's own §1 and it is stronger than the elimination this item first gave:**

> **A tag is a *label*. A note is *content*.**
>
> ⚡ **Only content makes Signora *"the system of record for something a customer creates"*** — and that is what brings **retention, export, permissions and audit**, the obligations `commercial_profile`'s `public/`, its import contract and its design doc were never built against.
>
> ⛔ **Losing a tag is annoying. Losing a note is a data-loss incident.**

✅ **And that axis is what defends §7's boundary**: **files, emails and meetings are excluded for the same reason rather than by fiat** — each is content, each would bring the same obligations, and the ruling named them separately because they arrive by different routes.

| **`timeline`** | 📁 **A projection that *"deliberately holds no interpretation"*** and is append-only from events. ⛔ **Notes and Tasks are AUTHORED.** ✅ They *appear* in the timeline, which is a projection rule, not a home |
| **`knowledge_graph`** | Account identity and evidence, every claim carrying provenance to a provider. ⛔ **Nobody asserted a customer's own note** — 📁 the same argument [ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md) used to keep tags out |
| **`people`** | ⛔ **[C-221](#c-221)'s scope bound**: no person's name, anywhere. A note has an author and a body |

### The alternatives

| | |
|---|---|
| **A** — **a new module**, narrow by name | ✅ **What the ADR describes.** ⛔ **🔴 in the Change Budget: product owner + ADR.** ⚡ **This lane's proposed name is `notes_and_tasks`** — deliberately compound, because **it cannot grow into files, emails, meetings or custom fields without renaming itself**, which is exactly the boundary §7's last paragraph asks for |
| **B** — **inside `commercial_profile`** | ✅ **Buildable today with no ruling**, and the module is already this lane's. ⛔ **It gives one module two different obligations** — immutable versioned declarations, and authored records owing retention, export and audit — **and its `public/` surface, its import contract and its whole design doc are built around the first** |
| **C** — **a new module named for the act rather than the artefacts** — `customer_authoring` | ⚡ **Narrow for the same reason as A**: files are uploaded, emails and meetings are read from elsewhere, custom fields are schema. ⛔ **Still 🔴, and *customer* is ambiguous here** — the Signora customer, or the accounts they sell to |

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**A, named `notes_and_tasks`.** ⚡ **The ADR's own §1 argues for it** — a system of record is a different category from everything the repository holds — **and §7's closing boundary is easier to keep when the module name cannot absorb the four exclusions.**

⚠️ **The trade-off, stated rather than hidden:** **it is the repository's first module created for a capability rather than for a pipeline stage**, and every module in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) was placed by a product-owner ruling ([D-103](DECISION_REGISTER.md) `people`, [D-127](DECISION_REGISTER.md) `action_batch`). **This would be the third, and it needs the same.**

### Implementation impact

**Everything else in slice ⓷ is ready and does not depend on the answer** — the audit is done and recorded on [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md)'s board row: **due dates are drawn so they are in; reminders are not drawn so they are out; the task state vocabulary is binary because the design draws a tick and a strikethrough and nothing between; *Overdue* is derived from the due date rather than stored.** ⛔ **All of it is unwritable until the file paths exist**, which is what makes this architectural rather than an inconvenience.

⚠️ **And two findings from the same audit that the ruling should see**, because they narrow what ⓷ can deliver whatever the module is:

- 🔴 **The reference model draws AI-AUTHORED notes and tasks** — one note's author is *"Signora"*, tagged *"AI note"*; two tasks read *"Agent · renewal sweep"* and *"Recommended by Signora"*. ⛔ **The ruling is about CUSTOMER-authored records, and nothing in the repository writes a note**, so those rows are [414](architecture/414-wave-1-account-360.md)'s ⬜ — no source rather than no endpoint.
- ⚠️ **`@mentions` and slash commands are drawn**, and a mention needs a member directory with a **name**. 📁 **The platform has none** — [C-024](#c-024), ADR-0026 — which is the same absence the Owner column met at ⓶a and answered with an address.

## C-1511 · The Companies `Segment` column and the `Segments` panel are disjoint vocabularies

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-15, building [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) ⓶b — ⚡ **measured off the design snapshot, not inferred from it** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner**, with Product Office — ⛔ **it is what a customer's `Segment` cell MEANS**, and a lane picking is a lane deciding the product |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **⓶b ships the enumerated grouping the ruling names**, and this asks about values the ruling does not explain |
| **Status** | **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** — ⚡ **the measurement, the three readings and a recommendation are all here.** ⛔ **Blocks nothing** |

### 🔴 The measurement

📁 `Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html` draws segments in two places:

| | |
|---|---|
| **The table's `Segment` column** | **One value per row** — `Enterprise` (6 rows), `Mid-market` (2). The card view renders `Enterprise · EMEA`, `Mid-market · EMEA`, `Enterprise · NA` |
| **The `Segments` panel** | **Five named groupings with counts** — `Renewal risk — 90 days` 41 · `Expansion-ready` 118 · `Board reporting set` 212 · `Competitive watch` 26 · `Dormant enterprise` 304 |

⛔ **The two sets are disjoint.** **No row's cell holds any panel segment's name, and no panel entry is named `Enterprise` or `Mid-market`.**

### ⚠️ Why [D-235](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ② does not settle it

📁 **The ruling is explicit and this lane is following it**: *"The App Shell's `segment` scope dimension, Companies, Account 360 and Action Batch all carry the [ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md) meaning."*

⚡ **So the column carries the enumerated grouping.** ⛔ **And then the values drawn in it are unexplained**: `Enterprise` and `Mid-market` are a **tier vocabulary**, one per company, and nothing in ADR-0411 produces them.

> ⚠️ **This is not [C-1503](#c-1503--task-466--segment-already-means-something-in-this-repository-and-adr-0411-means-something-else-by-it) again, and the distinction matters.** **C-1503 asked which of two ratified meanings the word carries, and the product owner answered it.** **This asks what the values the design DRAWS in that column are** — a question C-1503 never put and D-235 never reached.

### ✅ What ⓶b shipped, so the question is not blocking

**The membership model, following the panel** — because **the panel is the only place a segment is created, named and counted**, and 📁 `Board reporting set — "manually curated for the quarterly pack"` is ADR-0411's enumerated grouping in the design's own words.

⚡ **The cell renders a LIST rather than one value**, because a company can be in *Board reporting set* and *Competitive watch* at once. ⛔ **Rendering only the first would be the screen choosing which of a customer's groupings matters.**

### The readings, and each is coherent

| | |
|---|---|
| **A** — the column is the panel's groupings | ✅ **What ⓶b built.** The mock's `Enterprise`/`Mid-market` are placeholder values from before the panel existed |
| **B** — the column is a firmographic tier | ⛔ **Then it is not ADR-0411's**, and D-235 ② would need revisiting — **or the column has a different source** and is one of [`table.ts`](../frontend/lib/accounts/table.ts)'s source-less columns after all |
| **C** — both, and the design draws two things | ⚠️ **Possible, and it is what the snapshot literally shows** — but 📁 **ADR-0411 §3 says the choice is *"ONE choice, made once, not per screen"***, so two would need saying out loud |

### ⛔ And the Dynamic kind is inside the same question

📁 **The panel draws two kinds — `Dynamic` (*"recalculates hourly"*) and `Static` (*"manually curated"*) — and four of the five drawn are Dynamic.** ⚡ **A recalculating segment is a stored PREDICATE**, which is the other half of the one choice ADR-0411 reserved.

🔴 **Measured rather than assumed**, of the predicates the five rules name:

| Predicate | Source |
|---|---|
| `score below 50` | ✅ `buying_score_engine` publishes it |
| `open ACV above $100K` | ✅ `opportunity_engine` |
| `no contact 14d` · `Usage above 88%` · `healthy support` · `No activity in 60 days` | ⛔ **Zero occurrences across `backend/modules/`** |

⛔ **So a rule engine would be built over facts that do not exist** — 📁 the same ⬜ class [414](architecture/414-wave-1-account-360.md) records for product usage and calls, and **building a screen section against invented data is what `no-mock-data.test.tsx` exists to refuse.**

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**Reading A, and say so.** ⚡ **It is the only one that makes the panel — the place a customer creates and names a segment — the same concept as the column that shows it**, and it needs no new source. ⛔ **If B is intended, the column needs a source naming and it is not `commercial_profile`'s.**

**And rule the Dynamic kind separately**, because it is buildable independently of the column's meaning and **two of its six drawn predicates already have sources.**
