## C-1510 · What may *take it back* do when the previous owner has left?

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-14, building [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) slice ⓶ — ⚡ **on QE's hypothesis, tested and found to be a different class from the three defects beside it** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **the question is what the button means, not how it is implemented** |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing.** ⚠️ **But the shipped path has ALREADY CHOSEN**, which is why this is an item rather than a note |
| **Status** | **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** — ⚡ **both options argued, and a third this lane would propose.** ⛔ **Blocks nothing; the shipped behaviour is an encoded assumption, documented** |

### 🔴 Why this is a `C-` and not a `B-`

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"A defect is not a dependency. Something behaving wrongly today is a `B-` row; something not yet built or agreed is a `C-` row."*** ⛔ **Nothing behaves wrongly against an agreed definition, because the definition is the open question.**

⚡ **And it clears the register's own bar by that test rather than by importance**: *"if you can proceed without encoding an assumption about the answer, you do not need an item."* 🔴 **This lane has encoded one** — the shipped reversal picks *restore faithfully* out of two live options. **Documented rather than silent, which is the difference between a recorded assumption and a hidden one. It is still an assumption.**

### ⚠️ The situation, in one sentence

**A bulk assignment moved an account from Priya to Sam. Priya has since left the workspace. The customer presses *take it back*.**

### The two options, and the argument on each

| | |
|---|---|
| **A — restore faithfully** *(what is shipped)* | ⚡ **The batch's own change is undone exactly.** 📁 [ADR-0405](architecture/adr/0405-an-action-is-approved-before-it-is-effective.md) puts the inverse with the domain that performed the operation, and **the inverse of *"set Sam"* is *"set Priya"*** — she was a member when it happened. ⛔ **The cost, and it is QE's counter and it is strong: an account silently owned by somebody who cannot open it is worse than an account with no owner, because THE EMPTY STATE IS VISIBLE AND THE INVALID ONE IS NOT.** ⚠️ **A seller reading the Companies column cannot tell a valid owner from a departed one** |
| **B — decline that account and say so** | ✅ **Nothing invalid is ever written**, and the customer is told which accounts could not be returned. ⛔ **The cost: *take it back* no longer means what it says.** **A reversal that partly reverses is one the customer has to reconcile by hand**, and they pressed one button expecting one outcome |

⚡ **A third shape exists and is the one this lane would propose if asked**: **restore faithfully AND report the accounts whose holder is no longer eligible**, so the write is complete and the screen can say *"3 of 40 returned to somebody who has since left."* 📁 **It is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md)'s shape applied to a write**: the outcome must not be indistinguishable from an unqualified success.

### ⛔ What this is NOT

**Not the three defects fixed in `935cbbd5`.** Those were cases where the reversal touched **state that was never its own** — an assignment made since, a second reversal, an account the batch no longer held. ⚡ **Every one is now conditional on the batch's own value still being in place.** **A departed prior holder is different in kind: it IS the batch's own change to undo, and replaying it is faithful.**

### 📁 Where the code says so

**`ReverseAssignment`'s docstring carries the reasoning** — ⛔ **but a decision recorded only in a docstring is one nobody will find when they need to rule on it**, which is what this register exists to prevent.

## C-1509 · [TASK-429](BACKLOG.md) — four of the six relationship facts cannot come from a contact provider

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, building the second half of [TASK-429](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner**, with **Lane C** — ⚡ **the mock contract is Lane C's, handed over rather than left to be invented, and this is a second gap in it** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The relationship half of [TASK-429](BACKLOG.md), and therefore the org chart and relationship views of [TASK-430](BACKLOG.md).** ✅ **The identity half shipped and is not affected; `reports_to` is being built now because it does not depend on the answer** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 The contract, and who could actually author each field

📁 **[TASK-429](BACKLOG.md)'s required mock contract puts all six on `Apollo`**: *"Per relationship the design draws: `committee_role` · `stance` with a citable source per stance · `engagement_last_90d` as a weekly series · `risk` with a severity · `reports_to` · `relationship_strength`."*

⚡ **[§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s decision rule is *every field has the least powerful author capable of producing it correctly*, and applying it splits the six:**

| Field | Author | |
|---|---|---|
| `person_id` · `full_name` · `title` · `seniority` · `email` · `first_seen` · `last_seen` | **Apollo** | ✅ **Shipped.** A contact provider's own product |
| **`reports_to`** *(`confirmed` \| `inferred`)* | **Apollo** | ✅ **Being built.** ⚡ **An org chart is what a contact vendor sells, and `inferred` is the vendor's own hedge about its own data** |
| **`engagement_last_90d`** | ⛔ **Not Apollo** | 🔴 **Meetings and emails between the CUSTOMER and this person.** **Signora's vendor has never seen them.** 📁 This is the customer's own CRM — the shape [`mappers/crm.py`](../backend/modules/provider_normalization/infrastructure/mappers/crm.py) already exists for: *"a system the customer owns and holds the credential for"* |
| **`stance`** *(with a citable source)* | ⛔ **Not Apollo** | 🔴 **A judgement about a deal, and the citation makes it worse rather than better** — a vendor supplying *evidence* for a stance is a vendor deciding a customer's buying committee |
| **`relationship_strength`** *(`strong` \| `damaged` \| `none`)* | ⛔ **Not Apollo** | 🔴 **The customer's own history**, and plausibly **derived** from engagement rather than supplied at all |
| **`committee_role`** | ⛔ **Nobody yet** | 🔴 **Which seat a title fills is unowned.** 📁 `people/public/` states it: *"which seat does 'Head of Clinical Informatics' fill?"* is **[C-018](#c-018--nobody-owns-the-customer-facing-name-of-an-attribute)'s question with a different noun, and it belongs to whoever owns that mapping"* — **and no module has claimed it** |

### ⛔ Why this is not a shape quibble

⚡ **The fixture teaches the contract.** 📁 [`generators/base.py`](../backend/signora_platform/simulation/generators/base.py): *"replacing a fixture with a real payload is a **one-file change**"* — **which only holds while the fixture's shape is one a real payload could have.**

🔴 **A real Apollo response does not contain a stance.** **So a fixture that emits one is not a development fixture; it is a design for a provider that does not exist**, and whoever swaps it discovers that four fields have no source — after everything downstream has been built on them.

⚠️ **And it collides with what this lane wrote into the vocabulary one commit ago**, on the neighbouring committee model's own warning: ⛔ ***"No stance, no influence, no seat, no rank"*** on `PersonIdentityValue`, because 📁 `commercial_profile/domain/committee.py` records that *"a person is one plausible field away from becoming an influence model."*

### ✅ What Lane A is doing meanwhile, so nothing waits

**Building `reports_to` on Apollo**, which is unambiguous and which [TASK-430](BACKLOG.md)'s org chart needs. ⛔ **Not building the other four**, and not inventing a home for them.

### 🔴 The options

| | |
|---|---|
| **A** *(recommended)* | ⚡ **Split the contract by source.** **Apollo supplies identity + `reports_to`.** **A CRM fixture supplies `engagement_last_90d`** — `mappers/crm.py` and its provider already exist. **`stance` and `relationship_strength` are DERIVED from engagement**, in a module that owns judgement, never supplied. **`committee_role` waits on the seat mapping.** ⛔ **Cost: [TASK-430](BACKLOG.md)'s stance and committee views need the CRM slice first** |
| **B** | **Emit all six from Apollo as the row specifies**, and accept that four fields have no real source. ⛔ **Cost: the one-file-change property is gone, and the four are discovered at vendor-swap time by somebody who did not choose this** |
| **C** | **Emit all six, but from a fixture that is honestly named as a composite** — not `apollo`, a Signora-internal *"customer engagement"* source. ⚠️ **Honest about provenance and still invents a provider**, and 📁 [ADR-0300](architecture/adr/0300-inbound-customer-systems.md) is the proposed ADR that would name the real one |

⚡ **A is the only option under which each field's author is one that could produce it.** **B and C both ship a screen whose data has nowhere to come from.**

## C-1508 · Is `20-provider-simulation.md` a module design doc or system architecture?

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, updating it for [TASK-429](BACKLOG.md) and noticing which band it sits in |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **the Change Budget is [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md)'s, and only the product owner amends it** |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing.** ⚡ **Raised because a lane touched a 🔴 path, not because a lane is waiting** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |

### ⚠️ The conflict, and it is between two rules that both bind

📁 **The Change Budget puts `docs/architecture/01`–`21` in 🔴 — *product owner + ADR*.** **`20-provider-simulation.md` is inside that band by its number.**

📁 **[§12](../CLAUDE.md) requires the opposite of leaving it alone**: *"any change that affects module boundaries, event contracts, database schema, or a principle's application must update the corresponding document in the same change — not as a follow-up, not 'later'"*, and **§19 lists documentation as one of the three things a slice needs to be complete.**

⚡ **The Provider Simulation Framework is a module Lane A is assigned** ([`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), `platform_foundation`, `backend/signora_platform/`). **So its design doc is 🟢 by ownership and 🔴 by filename.**

### 📁 What the repository already does — evidence, not authority

**Three of the last commits to that file are feature-lane commits**: `TASK-436`, `M12.3`, `M12.1.5`. **The `playground@1` and `playground@2` lineage sections were both written by the lane that built the dataset.**

⚡ **This is the shape [§20a](../CLAUDE.md)'s `Resource` ruling settled one file over** — *"the practice was already this; the rule now says so."* ⛔ **But practice is not permission, which is why this is an item rather than a decision.**

### ✅ What Lane A did, stated plainly rather than buried

⚠️ **The edit was made and is in the TASK-429 commit**, announced there as a 🔴 touch. **The reasoning, and it is a choice between two failures:** ⛔ **reverting it leaves `20-provider-simulation.md` denying the existence of two datasets that are on `main` and in the seeder** — 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md) calls a document asserting something untrue *more damaging than the absent version, because it is trusted.*** ⚡ **A truthful document written slightly outside a budget is the smaller error, and it is the reversible one.**

⛔ **The section added is dataset lineage only** — `playground@3` and `playground@4` — **no principle, no contract, no stage, no decision.**

### 🔴 The options

| | |
|---|---|
| **A** | **The band is right and the practice is wrong.** Lanes stop editing it; **Lane C or the product owner maintains dataset lineage.** ⚠️ **Cost: the doc drifts by one cycle every time a lane ships a dataset, which is how `playground@3` came to have no section at all** |
| **B** *(recommended)* | ⚡ **A module's design doc follows its module, whatever its number.** **`20` is `platform_foundation`'s design doc the way `23` is `observation_engine`'s** — 🟢 for the assigned lane, unchanged for everyone else |
| **C** | **Split it.** Framework architecture stays 🔴; **dataset lineage moves to a document in the `30`+ records band**, where a dated record already belongs |

⚡ **B costs one sentence in the Change Budget and matches what four commits already did.** ⛔ **C is tidier and moves a file, which the governance freeze asks for evidence before doing.**

## C-1507 · [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) — a batch can be proposed and approved, and no screen approves one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, writing the Playwright journey — ⚡ **the journey found it, not the suite** |
| **Owner** | **Design Authority** — ⛔ **the approved design draws no approvals surface, and inventing one is a customer journey a lane made up** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The second half of [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md)'s journey.** ✅ **Propose ships and is proven headed; approve, apply and reverse are proven at the API** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 What exists now, and what does not

✅ **The lifecycle is complete at the API** — [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) added `approve` and `reverse` this cycle, because 📁 the module published *"two endpoints of seven"* and a proposed batch could not be accepted at all.

⛔ **No screen calls any of them.** 📁 `Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html` draws the bulk bar and **no approvals inbox**, no pending-batch list, and no *"3 waiting for you"* affordance anywhere in the shell.

⚡ **So a seller can propose *"Tag 41 companies"* and nobody can accept it from the product.**

### ⚠️ Why this lane did not build one

📁 [D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑥: ⛔ ***"do not invent alternative user experiences."*** ⚡ **An approvals surface is a screen with a list, a decision, a history and a permission model** — **it is a design, not a control**, and guessing it is how a product grows a second inbox nobody asked for.

⛔ **And the alternative — approving silently on the seller's behalf — is worse.** 📁 [ADR-0405](architecture/adr/0405-an-action-is-approved-before-it-is-effective.md): *intelligence suggests; humans commit.* **A propose that auto-approves is not an approval workflow; it is a write with extra steps**, and it would make the whole context decorative.

### ✅ What ships meanwhile, and it is declared rather than implied

**The journey covers what a customer can actually drive**: select companies · name a label · propose it · **be told plainly that nothing has happened yet.** ⚡ **Six assertions, run headed.**

📁 **The approve → apply → reverse half is proven at the API and in the handlers** — `test_api_action_batch.py` and `test_tag_batch_handlers.py` — ⛔ **and the spec's own header says so, so a green run cannot be read as more than it checked.**

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**Two candidates, and the first is much smaller:**

**① The proposer approves their own batch, from the bulk bar.** ⚡ **The confirm dialog already exists and already names the count** — one more control on it, and the seller who selected the companies is the person deciding. ⛔ **It is not an approvals *workflow*** and does not pretend to be; it makes the batch mechanism reachable while the real question waits.

**② A proper approvals surface**, which is a design and belongs upstream.

⚠️ **① changes what `Add tag` does and is therefore not a lane's call**, which is why it is raised rather than built.

## C-1506 · [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) — the reversible window for a bulk tag is the design's number for a different act

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, on reaching `reversible_for` and finding no citation for it |
| **Owner** | **Design Authority** — ⚡ **a customer-visible promise about how long an undo lasts** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **A window is declared and the batch is reversible; this asks whether the NUMBER is right** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |

### ⚠️ What the design states, and what it does not

📁 **`Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html` states exactly one batch window**, and it states it for imports:

> ***"Nothing is written until the preview is approved, and every import is reversible for 24 hours as a single named batch."***

⛔ **A bulk *Add tag* is not an import**, and the document says nothing about how long one stays reversible. ⚠️ **It also draws a second, much shorter window for a different mechanism** — *"optimistic commit, undo in the toast for 10 seconds"* — **which is an inline edit rather than a batch**, and is not this.

### ✅ What this lane did, and why it is an inference rather than a guess

🔴 **`None` was the alternative and it is worse.** 📁 `reversible_for=None` means ***reversal was never offered***, and [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) says in terms: *"a batch that applies but cannot be reversed in the window is a defect, not a limitation."*

✅ **So `REVERSIBLE_FOR = timedelta(hours=24)` is a named constant** in [`tag_use_cases.py`](../backend/modules/commercial_profile/application/tag_use_cases.py), **carrying this item's number in its own comment** — ⚡ **a ruling is one edit and one test line.**

⚠️ **Stated as an inference in the code rather than passed off as a citation**, because the document's sentence is about imports and somebody reading the constant later would otherwise believe it was specified.

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**24 hours, on consistency.** ⚡ **Both are bulk mutations applied as one named thing a person approved**, and a customer who learns *"a batch is reversible for a day"* has learned one rule rather than two. ⛔ **A shorter window for tagging would need a reason**, and the obvious one — *tagging is less consequential* — argues for the same window rather than a tighter one.

⚠️ **If the answer is *"it depends on the operation"*, that is a real product position** and the constant moves to the operation that declares it, which is where `ProposeBatch.reversible_for` already puts it.

## C-1505 · [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) — *"Select all 312"* names a number no endpoint publishes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, on `tsc` refusing `pages[0].total` — ⚡ **the type found it, not a reading of the design** |
| **Owner** | **Design Authority**, with an architecture question underneath it |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **One control on the Companies bulk bar.** ✅ **Selection, the header checkbox and Export all ship** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 The gap, measured

📁 **`Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html` draws two counts**: *"8,412 total · 312 in view"* and, in the bulk bar, ***"41 selected of 312 in view · Select all 312"***.

⛔ **`CursorPage` publishes `items`, `next_cursor` and `has_more`. There is no total, anywhere** — and it is deliberate rather than an omission. 📁 The accounts read's own words:

> *"The graph is written continuously: a resolution binds a new provider identity and an account appears, so an offset page would skip or repeat rows between two requests and a customer paging the list would silently miss accounts."*

⚡ **Keyset pagination and a live total are in tension by construction.** A count over a set that changes between two requests is wrong by the time it renders.

### ⛔ Why this lane did not approximate it

⚠️ **The loaded count was available and using it would have been the same word in two meanings**: the customer reads *"Select all 312"* and gets the 50 in hand. 📁 [`table.ts`](../../frontend/lib/accounts/table.ts) already names that class in its own comment — *"an export named 'all companies' that contained 50 would be the worst kind of wrong: **silently plausible**."*

✅ **So the control is absent rather than approximate**, and the header checkbox still selects everything on screen.

### ⚠️ And the control needs more than a number

🔴 **Even with a total, *"Select all 312"* selects a set the client cannot enumerate** — which is why [`selection.ts`](../../frontend/lib/accounts/selection.ts) returns `null` for its ids rather than the rows in hand. ⛔ **Every action on it needs a server-side counterpart that takes the FILTER rather than a list**: export, tag, assign. **None exists.**

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**Two questions, and the first is cheap:**

**① Does the design need an exact total, or a bounded one?** ⚡ *"312 in view"* beside a keyset list could honestly be *"312+"* or *"about 312"*, and 📁 the design's own header already says *"8,412 total"* — **a workspace-level count that changes far more slowly than a filtered one.**

**② If *Select all matching* is genuinely wanted, it is a filter-taking API on every action**, not a count. ⛔ **That is architecture rather than a screen**, and it is why this is raised rather than sized.

⛔ **Not decided here**, and ⚠️ **nothing about the bar's other controls waits on it.**

## C-1504 · [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) — the Action Batch publishes no way to PROPOSE one, and its first consumer has to

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, reaching the wiring rather than predicting it — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"ownership becomes obvious when implementation reaches a module"* |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **a new cross-module dependency is 🔴 in the Change Budget**, and this lane will not take one inside a feature slice |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The *propose* step only.** ✅ **Everything else in the batch path proceeds** — see below, and nothing about it encodes an assumption |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13, on [D-235](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ① reaching `integration`.** ⚡ **Option ① approved, narrow, and the ruling is tighter than the raise**: `propose` creates the batch and its payload **atomically** · ⛔ does NOT approve · ⛔ does NOT apply · ⛔ **no batch-without-payload state representable** · ⛔ no event alternative · ⛔ no further writes without an explicit later requirement. 📁 **Human approval stays a product boundary, not a call in a stack.** ⚠️ **Closed only after `86f0133a` was an ancestor of `origin/integration`** — [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s five states: *ruled* and *actionable* are different days, and this lane held the row open through both. |

### 🔴 The gap, measured

📁 **`action_batch/public/` publishes `ActionBatchReader`, `ActionBatchView` and `ApprovalState`** — and the port says why, in terms:

> ⛔ ***"Read-only, and deliberately. Proposing, approving and reversing are slice 4's application layer; a port that could write before the domain exists would let a consumer commit to a lifecycle nobody has built."***

⚡ **That reasoning was right when it was written and its premise has expired**: 📁 slices 4 and 5 shipped, [TASK-465](BACKLOG.md) is `PROMOTED`, **the domain exists.** ⚠️ **The docstring still says *"Nothing implements this yet, and that is the slice"*, which is stale** — recorded here rather than edited, because whether the port gains a write is the question rather than the answer.

⛔ **So `commercial_profile` — [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md)'s first consumer, by the row's own title — cannot propose a batch through `public/`**, and 📁 [§5](../CLAUDE.md) forbids reaching deeper.

### ✅ What is NOT blocked, and why it is not an assumption

🔴 **A consumer must hold its own payload, and that is forced rather than chosen.** 📁 `ActionBatchView` publishes ***"`item_count` and not the items… what each item *means* belongs to the domain that proposed it"***. ⚡ **So `commercial_profile` stores which tag and which accounts, keyed by `batch_id`, however the batch comes to exist.**

✅ **And the event route needs no dependency at all** — measured, not assumed: 📁 `apps/worker/subscriptions.py` hands every handler a generic **`EventEnvelope`**, so a consumer reads `payload` and imports nothing from the producer. **`ActionBatchApplied` and `ActionBatchReversed` are published whichever way the batch was proposed.**

⚡ **Both halves are answer-independent, so this lane is building them** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a lane may proceed past an open item only where proceeding encodes no assumption about the answer*).

### ⚠️ The options, with the trade-off each buys

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **① Publish a write port on `action_batch/public/`** | ✅ **One transaction**: the batch row and its payload commit together | ⛔ **A new cross-module edge**, `commercial_profile → action_batch.public`. 🔴 in the budget. ⚠️ Not forbidden by any import contract — `modules.action_batch` is absent from `commercial_profile`'s forbidden list, and the reverse edge stays forbidden, which is the direction that matters |
| **② The client calls both endpoints** | ✅ **No new edge** | 🔴 **A batch with no payload becomes representable** — the first call succeeds, the second fails, and an `APPROVED` batch applies nothing. ⛔ **That is [ADR-0405](architecture/adr/0405-an-action-is-approved-before-it-is-effective.md)'s *no partial state* broken by construction** |
| **③ Propose by event** | ✅ **No synchronous edge** | ⛔ **The caller gets no `batch_id` back**, so the confirmation cannot name what it created, and *"applied"* has nothing to poll |

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**① — and the narrow version of it: `propose` alone, not approve or apply.** ⚡ **Approval is a human decision and belongs on a screen, not in a module's call stack**; what a consumer needs is the ability to *ask*. 📁 The port's own sentence permits exactly this reading — the objection was *"before the domain exists"*, and it now does.

⛔ **Not decided here.** 📁 [§5](../CLAUDE.md) says a new cross-module dependency is *"proposed and approved as a graph change first"*, and ⚠️ **this lane owns both modules, which makes taking it quietly easy and is precisely why it is being raised instead.**

## C-1503 · [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) — *Segment* already means something in this repository, and [ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md) means something else by it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, measuring the module before writing into it — ⛔ **not after** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **two ratified ADRs use one word for two concepts, and neither may be reinterpreted by a lane** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The *Segment* third of [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) only.** ✅ **Tags are built and Owner/CSM is next — neither collides with anything** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13, on [D-235](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ②.** ⚡ **Option C, and it is a better answer than either this lane proposed.** ⛔ **Nothing is renamed and there is no terminology rewrite** — 📁 [ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md)'s existing distinction already carried it: **a customer says *ICP* for [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md)'s aggregate and *Segment* for [ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md)'s enumerated grouping**, and only the internal table name overlapped. ✅ **`icp_segment` stays internal; Companies, Account 360, the App Shell's `segment` scope and the Action Batch all carry the ADR-0411 meaning — so *"Add to segment"* is buildable as drawn.** ⚠️ **This lane framed it as *rename one of them* and both options were worse.** |

### 🔴 Both sides, quoted

📁 **[ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md) §3** — the ruling this row was released on:

> **Segments** — ***"A named, saved grouping of accounts."*** *"Whether a segment is a stored list or a stored predicate is an implementation choice and is Lane A's — **but it is ONE choice, made once, not per screen**."*

📁 **[ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md), shipped, and `commercial_profile` already implements it** — tables `icp_segment`, `icp_segment_version`, `icp_segment_product`, `icp_segment_state`, all four registered in `tenancy_policy.py`:

> ***"An ICP as a thing a customer can name, open, copy and retire."*** *"Mid-market fintech in the US, 100–1000 employees" is a complete description of a segment without naming anything sold.*

⚡ **So the choice ADR-0411 says is Lane A's has already been made, by a ratified ADR: a segment is a stored PREDICATE.** ⛔ **And that makes the design's control unbuildable as drawn** — 📁 `Fortune Signora Companies` puts ***"Add to segment"*** in the bulk bar, **and you cannot add an account to a predicate.** You can only match it.

### ⚠️ Why this is not a naming tidy-up

🔴 **The two are different in the one way that matters: who decides membership.**

| | **ADR-0041's segment** *(shipped)* | **ADR-0411's segment** *(ruled)* |
|---|---|---|
| **Membership** | ⚡ **Derived** — an account is in it because it matches criteria | ⚡ **Enumerated** — an account is in it because somebody put it there |
| **Reversal** | ⛔ **Nothing to reverse** — change the criteria and the set changes | ✅ **A batch that added forty-one accounts can take them back** |
| **What a bulk *Add to segment* means** | ⛔ **Nothing coherent** | ✅ **Exactly what the design draws** |

⛔ **Building the second alongside the first is what [ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md) §2 forbids in terms** — *"if two screens model them separately they will disagree within a release"* — ⚠️ **and it is [§4](../CLAUDE.md)'s *never introduce a second definition of a concept a module already owns*, in a module this lane is inside.**

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**Rename the customer-facing half rather than the shipped aggregate.** ⚡ **`icp_segment` is cited by opportunities and carries four tables of versioned history**, so moving it is expensive and reaches surfaces this row does not touch. 📁 **The design's own bulk bar says *"Add to segment"* and its column header says *Segment*, showing `Enterprise` and `Mid-market`** — ⚠️ **which read as ICP names, not as saved lists**, so it is genuinely possible the design means the shipped concept and the bulk action is *"apply this ICP's criteria"*.

⛔ **Not decided here, and the reason is that both readings are coherent**: one makes the design's control buildable and the other makes it a no-op. ⚡ **A lane picking between them would be choosing what a customer's *Segment* column means.**

### ✅ What proceeds meanwhile, so this blocks one third rather than a row

📁 **Tags are shipped in this slice** — no prior concept exists anywhere in `backend/modules/`, measured. ✅ **Account Owner/CSM is next and collides with nothing**; `opportunity_engine`'s `owner_id` is *who owns this deal*, a different subject on a different aggregate, and it is named here so nobody merges them later.

## C-1502 · [TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md) — WL-08 renders a soft-delete window that no approved document says exists, and the design says so itself

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, ⚠️ **correcting its own row from the day before** — [TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md) declared WL-08 *"waiting on four facts `Membership` does not carry"* and **that was the wrong reason**, reached by reading the screen and not the document's §07 |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Two owners, and the design names both** — **Architecture** for U-02, **Legal + Product** for U-01 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **WL-08 only — one of [TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md)'s eleven.** ✅ **Six are delivered; two more wait on [C-1501](#c-1501--task-1423--the-entry-engine-sends-a-suspended-workspace-to-a-page-and-the-design-gives-it-a-banner)** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-13, on [D-235](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ③, and closed as ALREADY OWNED rather than as answered.** ⛔ **WL-08 stays blocked; the rest of [TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md) does not.** ⛔ **No 30-day window · no Restore · no `deleted_at` to satisfy a mock · no purge job · no scheduled deletion.** 🔴 **The substantive finding is not this lane's**: the question was already owned as 📁 [R-04](architecture/16-architecture-risks.md) and named unowned in terms by `ADR-0041:523` — *"workspace-level erasure remains the repository's unowned capability"* — **and [TASK-426](BACKLOG.md) already exists for it.** ⚠️ **This raise rediscovered something the repository had recorded nine documents away from the screen being built**, which is a finding about the register's reachability. ⛔ **And TASK-426's own trigger (c) — *migration 0050* — had fired unnoticed.** |

### 🔴 This is not a gap this lane found — it is a gap the design DECLARED, and the lane missed it

📁 **`Fortune Signora Workspace Lifecycle.dc.html` §07 `Unresolved decisions`**, whose own heading reads ***"Five items. Three are capabilities this document deliberately did not invent."*** ⚠️ **Two of the five are WL-08's, quoted verbatim:**

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **U-01** | **Retention window length** · *Legal + Product* | 📁 ***"This document uses 30 days for DELETING → PURGED, which the shipped documents assert nowhere. It is the single most consequential number here and it is not a design decision."*** |
| **U-02** | **Whether restore-from-deleting exists at all** · *Architecture* | 📁 ***"The brief warns against inventing recovery. No approved document establishes that a soft-delete window exists. WL-08 and transition 11 assume it; if the backend hard-deletes, both must be removed and the confirmation copy rewritten to say so."*** |

⛔ **U-02's interim is an instruction to this lane and it is unambiguous**: 📁 ***"do not build WL-08's Restore action until the backend model is confirmed."***

### ⚠️ What the code measurement adds, which the design could not know

🔴 **`workspace_tenancy` has no deletion lifecycle of any kind.** ⚡ **Measured, not inferred** — [`WorkspaceModel`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/models.py) is `id`, `name`, and the timestamp and audit mixins: **no standing, no `deleted_at`, no `deleted_by`, no retention column**, and `application/use_cases/` holds **no delete-workspace case at all**.

⛔ **So the correction to yesterday's row is not a nuance.** ⚡ **Adding four facts to `Membership` would have meant inventing the soft-delete window U-02 says nobody has approved** — **a schedule-deletion operation, a retention policy, a restore route and a purge job**, ⛔ **the last of which destroys customer data on a timer.** 📁 [D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑦ and [§21](../CLAUDE.md) both put that with an authority rather than a lane, **and I would have shipped it as a slice.**

### ✅ What is already built and does NOT wait on this

📁 [`lib/entry/gates.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/gates.ts)'s `ScheduledDeletion` **already satisfies U-01's interim in its stronger half**: it carries **an instant and has no field a caller could pass a duration through**, which is 📁 *"render the resulting date rather than the duration"* made unrepresentable rather than merely tested. ⚡ **Whatever number Legal rules, this contract renders it correctly**, so **U-01 alone would not block the screen.**

🔴 **U-02 is the one that blocks it**, because it decides whether the state WL-08 describes **exists**.

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**Take U-02 first and U-01 second, because U-01 is only meaningful if U-02 is yes.** ⚡ **If the backend hard-deletes, WL-08 is not deferred — it is deleted**, along with transition 11 and the confirmation copy that promises recovery, 📁 exactly as the document says.

⚠️ **Not decided here.** ⛔ **A retention window is a number a customer's data disappears on, and this lane inventing it is [§20c](../CLAUDE.md)'s worst case rather than a fixture gap** — 📁 and [D-233](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s *fixture gap, not a blocker* does not reach it, **because the missing thing is a capability and not a fixture.**

## C-1501 · [TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md) — the entry engine sends a suspended workspace to a PAGE and the design gives it a BANNER

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-13, reading `Workspace Lifecycle` against `lib/entry/rules.ts` before building |
| **Owner** | **Design Authority** — ⚡ **a contradiction between two authorities, not a gap** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Two of [TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md)'s eleven screens — rules 15 and 16 ONLY.** ✅ **The other nine are unaffected and this lane is building them** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |

### 🔴 The contradiction, both sides quoted

📁 **[`lib/entry/rules.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts) rules 15 and 16** route to **dedicated destinations**:

```
15  WS_SUSPENDED   route: (s, i) => `/w/${…}/suspended`
16  WS_ARCHIVED    route: (s, i) => `/w/${…}/archived`
```

📁 **`Fortune Signora Workspace Lifecycle.dc.html` gives both a BANNER over the working product**, and says so in the same row that grants access:

| State | Access | Banner |
|---|---|---|
| **`SUSPENDED`** | ⚡ **Read-only** — *"read everything, export everything. No writes, no sends, no agent runs."* | **"Persistent, no dismiss"** |
| **`ARCHIVED`** | ⚡ **Read-only** — *"identical mechanic to SUSPENDED, different cause and different resolver."* | **"Persistent, no dismiss"** |

⛔ **And the document distinguishes the two shapes explicitly elsewhere in the same table** — `PROVISIONING` is *"WL-02 page"* and `DELETING` is *"WL-08 page"*. ⚡ **So *page* and *banner* are terms it uses deliberately, and it chose banner for these two.**

### ⚠️ Why it matters more than a layout choice

🔴 **A page REMOVES the capability the design grants.** 📁 SUSPENDED says *"read everything, export everything"* — ⛔ **and a redirect to `/w/{id}/suspended` means a customer whose payment failed cannot reach their data at all**, which is the opposite of what the state is for. ⚡ **The worst moment to lock somebody out of their own records is the moment they are being asked to pay.**

### ✅ Recommended, and stated as input rather than authority

**The design.** 📁 [D-154](DECISION_REGISTER.md) — *begin from the design rather than iterate from it* — **and `rules.ts` predates this document**: [C-1405](#c-1405) commissioned it precisely because it did not exist when the engine was written.

⚠️ **Not decided here**, because it changes an engine contract eleven rules share and 📁 [§21](../CLAUDE.md) says an ambiguous design is a ruling rather than an interpretation.

## C-1500 · [TASK-1476](BACKLOG.md) — does Signora STORE what a rep writes, or only observe? Eight of Account 360's sections turn on it

> ✅ **RENUMBERED FROM `C-210` — product owner, 2026-08-12, allocating `C-1500`+ to Lane A.** ⛔ **`C-210` remains Lane B's canonical item** — *"will Signora hold personal data?"*, line 48, `OPEN` and unruled.
>
> ⚡ **The ruling recorded here was always for THIS question and is unchanged.** 📁 **Traceable from the old location, which now points here** — [B-263](BUGS.md) has the collision in full.
>
> ⚠️ **39 references to `C-210` exist across the registers, the design doc and implementation comments, and MANY of them mean this item.** ⛔ **Not swept from here: [B-259](BUGS.md) is what a per-file replace costs, and repointing content this office does not own is that defect again.** ✅ **Lane A repoints its own, as it did for `C-209`.**

> ⚠️ **Lane A's own contested-identifier note, superseded by the renumber and kept because it is the record of what was believed before the ruling:**
>
> 🔴 **⛔ CONTESTED IDENTIFIER — [B-263](BUGS.md). This item shares `C-210` with Lane B's *"will Signora hold personal data?"*, which holds the index row and this anchor.** ⚡ **Two sessions have already reported opposite states of *"C-210"* within an hour and both were reading correctly** — one meant this question, one meant Lane B's. ⛔ **Cite this item by its TITLE until it is renumbered**, and 🔴 **it cannot be renumbered until Lane A is given a `C-` block: all 100 of `C-200`–`C-299` are defined.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **WHICH QUESTION WAS RULED** | 🔴 **`C-210` IS ALLOCATED TWICE AND THE RULING BELOW APPLIES TO *THIS* ROW ONLY** — *does Signora STORE what a rep writes?* ⚠️ **Line 48 carries a different `C-210`, Lane B's *"will Signora hold personal data?"*, which owns the anchor and is `OPEN`.** ⛔ **THAT QUESTION IS NOT RULED AND NOTHING BELOW ANSWERS IT.** 📁 **Recorded 2026-08-12 on Lane A's [B-263](BUGS.md).** ⚡ **This office ruled one question and QE read the other, within the hour, and neither reading was wrong — the identifier was.** ⛔ **Not renumbered here: the id is Lane A's to move and they have stopped allocating until a block is stated** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-12: option A.** ⚡ **Signora owns customer-authored NOTES and TASKS.** ⛔ **NOT files · NOT emails · NOT meetings · NOT arbitrary custom fields** — 📁 *emails and meetings remain integration/read-domain concerns.* ⚠️ **Field-level permissions are ALSO NOT implicitly approved** — a separate authorization question, and it sits in [ADR-0410](architecture/adr/0410-authorization-capability-layer.md). **Contract: [ADR-0413](architecture/adr/0413-customer-authored-notes-and-tasks.md).** ⛔ **RECORDED LATE, 2026-08-12, and that is this office's defect: the ruling was made with six others and this row was not updated with them.** 📁 **Found by QE reading both refs rather than taking a status line** — a ruling that exists only in a report is a ruling nobody can act on |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, auditing the design against the shipped page **before claiming** — 📁 **Lane C asked for exactly this**: *"if you hit a third thing the design draws and the platform cannot express, raise it before claiming — the way [C-209](#c-209) worked and [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) did not."* |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Not the package.** ⚡ **Nineteen of the design's twenty-seven sections are unaffected**, and TASK-1476 stays claimable — this names the boundary so the remainder is not discovered mid-implementation |

### ① The question, in one line

📁 **The design's own subtitle: *"Flagship record page — everything a rep needs without opening the CRM."***

> 🔴 **Does Signora hold records a rep AUTHORS — notes, tasks, files, emails, meetings, custom fields — or does it observe, reason and explain over records that live elsewhere?**

### ② Measured, not assumed

⛔ **Thirty-five write endpoints across every module, and not one accepts customer-authored record content.**

```
accounts · action-batches · buying-committee · competitors · connections · focus
icp · invitations · members · membership · onboarding · opportunities
ownership · preferences · products · saved-views · signals · target-accounts
```

⚡ **Every one is configuration, membership, or a workflow decision.** ⛔ **No note, no task, no file, no email, no meeting, no custom field** — and **no domain model for any of them** in any module.

### ③ The eight sections that turn on it

| Section | Why it turns on this |
|---|---|
| **Notes** | 📁 *"rich text, @mentions, slash commands"* — **authored content with a store** |
| **Tasks** | 📁 *"＋ Add"*, a tick, a due date — **authored, mutable, assignable** |
| **Files** | 📁 *"Upload"* — **object storage and a per-account binding** |
| **Custom fields** | 📁 *"12 · editable in place · synced both ways"* — ⛔ **plus *"field-level permissions apply; read-only fields show a lock"***, which is a per-field grant Casbin's resource/action model does not express |
| **Emails** | 📁 *"38 threads · 2 unanswered"* — **a mailbox read, and threading** |
| **Meetings** | 📁 *"11 held · 1 upcoming"* — **a calendar read** |
| **Organisation chart** | 📁 *"Inferred from email, calendar and public sources"* — ⚡ **depends on the two above** |
| **Relationship graph** | 📁 *"who knows whom, and how strongly"* — **same dependency** |

### ④ ⚠️ Two of these are a different question from the other six, and conflating them would be a mistake

⛔ **Emails and Meetings are a READ of a customer's own system**, and 📁 **`integrations` already owns that boundary** — the inbound source port exists and `Capability.CRM_RECORDS` is built. ⚡ **They are an integration scope question, not a *does Signora become a record store* question.**

✅ **Notes, Tasks, Files and Custom fields are the real subject**: **Signora would be the system of record for something a customer creates**, with everything that follows — retention, export, permissions, audit, and the [§2](../CLAUDE.md) immutability rules about what may be edited.

### ⑤ Options, and the consequence of each

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Signora observes; it does not host** — the eight sections are permanently out, and Account 360 links to the CRM for them | ✅ **Keeps the product's boundary sharp and matches every module built so far** · ⛔ **contradicts the design's own subtitle**, and a rep does open the CRM |
| **B** ▶ | **Signora hosts what it can reason ABOUT** — notes and tasks, because they are evidence and follow-through; ⛔ **not files, emails or custom fields** | ✅ **The smallest store that makes the page defensible**, and both feed the timeline the product already has · ⛔ **a new bounded context and a real product commitment** |
| **C** | **Signora hosts all of it** — the CRM-replacement reading of the subtitle | ⛔ **A different product**, and it is [§20d](../CLAUDE.md)'s build-ahead in its largest form |

⚡ **Recommendation: B, and it is architectural input rather than authority.** 📁 **A note and a task are already the shape of things this product reasons over** — the timeline projects events, and a follow-through is an event. ⛔ **A file store and a custom-field engine are neither.**

### ⑥ ⛔ What this lane will NOT do meanwhile

**Invent any of it.** 📁 The product owner: *"do not invent unresolved product/domain concepts."* ⚠️ **And a designed empty state is not automatically the answer either** — 📁 [C-297](#c-297) is the worked example: *"honest is not the same as good"*, and eight empty sections on a flagship page is a different judgement from one.

### ⑦ ✅ What is unaffected and claimable today

**Nineteen sections**, and the ones that matter most are among them: **the AI summary, the score and its drivers, customer health, the signals timeline, research, opportunities, contacts, technology stack, competitors, market signals, recent activity, risk indicators, recommendations, the AI reasoning ladder and its evidence** — 📁 **plus the six-state matrix the design applies to every section**, which is the largest single piece of unbuilt, unblocked work in the package.

## C-209 · [TASK-1475](BACKLOG.md)'s row facts have no source, and its pager cannot be built over its own endpoint

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN`** — Lane A, 2026-08-12 |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, under the product owner's **end-to-end module model** ruled today: 📁 *"If you discover a genuine Product/Architecture decision: **STOP THAT SCOPE and raise it.** Do not invent product behaviour to keep moving."* |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** *(the RFC in ②)* · **Lane C** *(the package's scope lines)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing yet — [TASK-1475](BACKLOG.md) is not on `integration`.** ⚡ **Raised BEFORE it lands so the row can be corrected rather than claimed and then narrowed**, which is what happened to [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-1416](BACKLOG.md) |

### ① The package says nothing in scope waits on a contract. Three things do

📁 **[TASK-1475](BACKLOG.md) includes *"the row facts the design draws"*** and records *"capability verified before writing"* for six reads. ✅ **Those six do exist.** ⛔ **The row facts are a different question and five of the design's eight have no source.**

| The design's column | Source |
|---|---|
| **Company** | ✅ `AccountIdentity.name`, on the list contract |
| **Signora score** | ⚠️ **Exists** — `buying_score_engine`, 0–100 — ⛔ **but on `/accounts` (attention), not on `/accounts-list`.** A join, not an absence |
| **Segment** · **Owner** · **Tags** | ⛔ **Excluded already by [C-1425](#c-1425), and the package excludes them** |
| **Open ACV** | 🔴 **No canonical attribute, and extending it needs an RFC** |
| **Renewal** | 🔴 **Same** |

### ② 🔴 ACV and Renewal are not unbuilt — they are refused in writing

📁 **[`provider_normalization/infrastructure/mappers/crm.py`](../backend/modules/provider_normalization/infrastructure/mappers/crm.py):99**

> ***"Nothing commercial.** Is this already a customer, **contract value**, **renewal date**, opportunity stage — the facts that make a CRM worth connecting for Epic D — have **no canonical attribute**, and `ClaimAttribute` says an RFC extends it. Inventing one here would put a vocabulary decision inside a translation file, which is the quietest place in the codebase to make one."*

⚡ **So this is the same shape as [C-297](#c-297)**: 📁 `buying_score_engine` refuses probability *"in writing"* and the product promised Forecast anyway. ⛔ **Here the design draws two commercial columns the canonical language declines to carry**, and **a table is a quieter place to invent a vocabulary than a translation file, not a louder one.**

> 🔴 **This is one decision, not two rows.** **Whether Signora holds commercial facts about an account — value, renewal, stage — is upstream of this table, of [TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md)'s deal record, and of [C-297](#c-297)'s Forecast.** ⚠️ **Three surfaces have now asked for it independently.**

### ③ ⛔ The design's pager and the endpoint's pagination are incompatible

📁 **The design draws** `Rows 1–8 of 312 · Previous · 1 · 2 · 3 · Next` — **numbered pages and a total.**

📁 **[`knowledge_graph`'s endpoint is keyset, deliberately, and says why](../backend/modules/knowledge_graph/interface/router.py):**

> ***"Keyset pagination, never offset.** The graph is written continuously… an offset page would **skip or repeat rows** between two requests and a customer paging the list would silently miss accounts."*

⛔ **A numbered pager needs offset, and a total needs a count the contract does not return.** ⚡ **Building the design's pager over this endpoint means either breaking a rule the endpoint states, or adding a count and an offset mode — a contract change, not a screen.**

✅ **What IS buildable today**: **`Previous` / `Next` over the cursor**, which is honest and is what the contract supports. ⛔ **Numbers and a total are the decision.**

### ④ ✅ What this lane can build the moment the row lands, unchanged

⚡ **Named so the item reads as a narrowing rather than a refusal**: **card view · density · column configuration over the fields that exist · filters over `name`, `source`, `kind` and freshness · `Previous`/`Next` paging · export of what is on screen.** ✅ **None of those waits on anything.**

⛔ **Import is not among them**: it is a write path that creates companies, and **`New company` is excluded by the package itself** — importing them is the same capability with a different door.

### ⑤ ⚠️ Why this is raised now rather than on claiming

📁 **The end-to-end model says *"start implementation as soon as the package reaches your queue and its prerequisites are satisfied."*** ⚡ **These are the prerequisites, and they are checkable today** — **so checking them now is what makes step 6 immediate when it lands**, rather than a claim followed by a narrowing.

⚠️ **[TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-1416](BACKLOG.md) were both claimed-shaped and unstartable, and both were found so after they were `READY`.** ⛔ **This is the same measurement performed one step earlier.**

---

### ⚠️ Renumbered from `C-300`, and the scheme was not at fault

⛔ **`C-300` was already allocated** — 📁 *"Provider Platform owns the half of the inbound path Lane B may not build"* — **and it is in LANE B's block**, not a legacy range. 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): **Lane A allocates from `200`+, Lane B from `300`+.**

🔴 **This lane took the number after the highest it had used**, which is the one method the rule forbids by name: ***"Identifiers are allocated from a block, never from the highest number seen."*** ⚡ **The block was never full** — **209–216 were free the whole time**, and `209` is where this belongs.

⛔ **Nothing detected it**, and `state-check` is right not to: **218 `C-` ids, none duplicated**, because this item was never on `integration` under any id. ⚠️ **The collision was with a row that already existed, not between two live ones.**

✅ **Lane C published links to the wrong item and corrected them at `e1845e9b`; the renumber is this lane's** — 📁 **a lane allocates its own ids, and this one allocated badly.**


## C-299 · Which organization a person lands in, when they have more than one and have chosen none

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-12.** ⚡ **The Workspace Chooser design says so in its own header: *"C-299 folded in"*.** 📁 **The default-selection rule now lives where it belongs — in the chooser's specification, not beside it.** ⚠️ **[B-245](BUGS.md) stays OPEN**: the defect is repairable against the ruled design, and it is a defect rather than a question |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, routing [B-245](BUGS.md) — ⛔ **filed 2026-08-11 and carried to nobody until now.** ⚠️ **See the note at the foot of [C-298](#c-298--which-environments-may-write-a-credential-to-a-log-and-the-auth-tier-and-the-registry-do-not-agree-what-an-environment-is-called): this is the second unrouted decision from this lane in four days, and the pattern is the finding** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **No task row.** ⚡ **It costs the journey suite continuously** — 📁 [B-245](BUGS.md) records six organizations accumulating in one session and the account-backed journeys failing two projects later |

> ⚡ **CLASSIFIED 2026-08-12, Lane C: this is not an independent decision. It is the *default-selection rule* of a screen that has not been drawn** — 📁 **[C-1405](#c-1405) priority ⑤, the Workspace Chooser**, which the Entry Coverage Review calls ***"the single largest hole… no document draws it."***
>
> ⛔ **Ruling this separately would set a default for a chooser whose behaviour is undecided**, and the two would then have to agree by accident. **The default is the chooser's quietest rule, not a rule beside it.**
>
> ⚠️ **But the harm is live now and does not wait for the design** — ⑵ below is a salesperson put into a throwaway organization on every new device. 📁 **[B-245](BUGS.md) is the defect; this row is the missing rule.** ✅ **Both stay open: the defect can be repaired against *any* rule, and repairing it does not decide which rule is right.**
>
> ➡️ **So: linked to [C-1405](#c-1405) ⑤, not escalated separately.** **One fewer independent decision, and the same ruling answers both.**

### ① The mechanism, and all three parts are measured

📁 **The list is newest-first** ([`repositories.py`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/repositories.py):81) · 📁 **the default is `workspaces[0]`** ([`workspace-provider.tsx`](../frontend/lib/state/workspace-provider.tsx)) · ⛔ **nothing deletes an organization** — `useDeleteWorkspace` does not exist and no route offers one.

⇒ **Every organization anybody creates becomes the default for every browser with no stored choice, permanently.**

### ② ⚠️ It is not only a test hazard, and that is why it is here

🔴 **A salesperson who creates a second organization to try something out is put into it on every new device**, ahead of the one holding their book of business. ⛔ **They did not choose it; it was merely the most recent thing they made.**

📁 **The design does not answer this.** §19 ③ says switching *"keeps the equivalent route when it exists, and lands on Home when it does not"* — ⚡ **which is about SWITCHING and not about DEFAULTING.**

### ③ The four candidates, and what each costs

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Newest** *(today)* | ⛔ **The one behaviour nobody chose** — it is an artefact of a keyset order |
| **B** ▶ | **Most recently used**, falling back to oldest | ✅ **Matches what a person means by *my* organization** · ⛔ **needs a per-person last-used record** — 📁 **`last_used_workspace` already exists in `workspace_tenancy`**, so this is cheaper than it sounds |
| **C** | **The one with data** | ⛔ **Signora choosing on the customer's behalf from a heuristic**, and wrong the day somebody starts a real second organization |
| **D** | **Explicit at creation** — *"make this my default?"* | ✅ **Honest** · ⛔ **a question at the worst moment**, and it leaves the no-answer case unresolved anyway |

### ④ ⚡ Recommendation: **B**, and the reason is that the mechanism already exists

📁 **[`last_used_workspace`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/) is built and this lane implemented it.** ⛔ **Nothing consumes it for the DEFAULT**, only for the stored choice — ⚡ **so B is wiring an existing fact to a decision that is currently made by an ordering.**

⚠️ **It does not fix the test hazard on its own.** **A fresh browser context has no last-used record either**, so the fallback still decides — ✅ **and *oldest* is the safe fallback rather than *newest*, because the oldest organization is the one somebody has had longest.**

### ⑤ ⛔ What this lane will not do

**Pick one and ship it.** 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"I could just add it" is how a product decision becomes a line in a feature slice.* ⚡ **The repair is small in every option, which is exactly why it needs saying out loud rather than deciding in passing.**

## C-298 · Which environments may write a credential to a log, and the auth tier and the registry do not agree what an environment is called

> ✅ **RULING: credentials and secrets are NEVER written to logs in production or any customer-facing environment.**
>
> ⛔ ***"The implementation must NOT rely on developers remembering which environment they are in. The environment must be explicit and machine-readable."*** ⚡ **That is [§2](../CLAUDE.md) applied to logging — a guard kept by memory is documentation pretending to be code.**
>
> **`SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` defined consistently across runtime · production enforces redaction · credential values never emitted · diagnostic logging safe by default · frontend and backend semantics consistent.** ⛔ **No second environment taxonomy.**
>
> ➡️ **Contract: [ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md).**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-12.** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, routing [B-223](BUGS.md) — ⛔ **filed 2026-08-09, implementing [TASK-473](BACKLOG.md), and carried to nobody for three days** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **a security decision, not a list a lane extends** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚠️ **It is LATENT**: nothing sets `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` for the frontend, so every clone works — **and it fires the first time anybody configures the variable to the name their own registry gives them** |

### ① The disagreement, and the intersection is empty

```
infra/environments.py  → review · lane-qe · lane-a · lane-b · lane-c · lane-d · lane-e · demo
lib/auth/config.ts     → local · test · development
```

⛔ **Not one of the registry's eight names appears in the auth tier's three, and not one of the three is a registry row.**

⚠️ **So a lane that exports `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT=lane-a` — the name the registry gives it, and what `--exports` emits — is classified deployed**, `resolveEmailTransport()` refuses the console and mailbox transports, **and the auth tier will not start, with a diagnostic calling a developer's laptop a deployed environment.**

### ② 🔴 Why the obvious fix is the wrong one

⚡ **Widening the allowlist to the registry's development names is a weakened guard, however it is dressed.**

📁 **The guard exists because the console transport writes verification and password-reset links to stdout** — *"a credential sitting in a log file"* — **and the mailbox keeps a history of them.** ⛔ **Every name added is an environment in which a credential may be written to a log**, and 🔴 **`review` and `demo` both serve people who are not the person who started the process.**

> **The question is not *which names are missing*. It is *which environments may write a credential to stdout*.** 📁 **[TASK-473](BACKLOG.md)'s own Change Budget says *"no weakened guard"* by name.**

### ③ Two repairs, and the second is the safe direction

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | **Make the registry authoritative for both** — the auth tier asks it rather than keeping a parallel list | ✅ 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *truth has exactly one authoritative representation* · ⛔ **crosses a tier boundary**: a Node process cannot import a Python registry, so it needs a published form — **a design decision** |
| **②** ▶ | **Invert the list** — name the environments where a credential in a log is ACCEPTABLE | ✅ **A NEW environment is then deployed-by-default rather than development-by-default**, which is the direction that fails safe · ⛔ **a behaviour change to a security guard**, which is 🔴 |

### ④ ✅ What is already true, and it is why this is not urgent

📁 **[TASK-473](BACKLOG.md) recorded the wrong behaviour as a PASSING ASSERTION** rather than as a comment:

```ts
expect(withEnvironment('lane-a', authMode)).toBe('production');
```

⚡ **That test is written to FAIL on the day somebody repairs this**, which is the point: **a comment describing a defect is indistinguishable from a comment describing a design**, and this one cannot be mistaken for either.

### ⑤ ⚠️ The ruling buys a second row, and it was not visible when this was raised

🔴 **[B-257](BUGS.md), found the day after this item was written**: 📁 **three defaults in the SAME file point at human review's ports** — `SIGNORA_APP_URL` and `SIGNORA_JWT_ISSUER` at `3000`, `SIGNORA_API_URL` at `8000`.

⛔ **An unset variable does not aim a lane at *a wrong port*. It aims it at the product owner's demo stack** — 📁 [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md):311, *"3000 and 8000 belong to human review on `main`, and to no lane."*

⚡ **The honest repair is the same missing capability this item is about**: **a default for a first clone and an error for a lane** requires the auth tier to know which it is — ⛔ **and `environmentName()` returns `local` for every lane, which is precisely the disagreement above.**

> ✅ **So the ruling here buys both rows.** ⚠️ **Recorded before the decision rather than discovered after it**, so the cost of each option is known to include B-257.

### ⑥ ⚠️ The finding that is worth more than either row

🔴 **This is the second defect this lane has filed, declined to fix for a correct reason, and then failed to route** — 📁 **the first was [B-219](BUGS.md)**, whose own row says it: *"This lane filed the bug on 2026-08-09 and did not file the coordination item, so nothing carried it to anyone who could rule — a defect whose fix a lane may not make, with no `C-` row, can sit indefinitely."*

⛔ **B-223 was filed the same day, for the same reason, and sat for three.** ⚠️ **[B-245](BUGS.md) is a third** — routed as [C-299](#c-299--which-organization-a-person-lands-in-when-they-have-more-than-one-and-have-chosen-none) alongside this.

> ⚡ **Declining to fix something is only half the duty.** **A lane that stops correctly and says why has still dropped it, unless it also hands it to somebody who can act** — and **`BUGS.md` is read by the lane that owns the module, which is precisely the lane that already decided it may not act.**

## C-297 · A customer tells Signora what they came for, and for three of six answers the product has nothing to say

> ✅ **RULING: Forecast is based on COMMERCIAL STAGE, never probability.**
>
> ⛔ ***"The product must NOT fabricate a probability/percentage when the underlying platform does not own that concept."*** ⚡ **Forecast communicates the current stage and its meaning.** ✅ **`buying_score_engine`'s refusal stands and is vindicated rather than overridden.**
>
> 📁 **[ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md) is the source of truth for the vocabulary Forecast consumes.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-12.** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, measuring `opportunity_engine`'s read surface for [TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md) — ⚡ **that row's own *"what can be done now, in parallel"*** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** *(what the step should say)* · **Lane C** *(whether the goal→feature map should shrink)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **[B-256](BUGS.md)'s false statement is already removed** — this is about what replaces it |

### ① What was wrong is fixed; what is left is a decision

📁 **Onboarding screen `06` asked for up to two goals and then said, in the product's own words:** ***"Signora will open on Forecast, the Executive Dashboard."***

⛔ **Neither exists**, and 📁 **`FORECAST_ACCURATELY` is the first of the six options.** ✅ **[B-256](BUGS.md) removed the promise**: only destinations with a route are named, and a goal with none produces no sentence.

### ② ⚠️ Honest is not the same as good, and that is the whole item

🔴 **A customer who picks *"Forecast accurately"* now sees their selection register and nothing else.** ⚡ **They have just told Signora what they came for, and the product says nothing about it** — **which is true, and is a worse experience than the false sentence in one specific way: it gives them no information at all.**

⛔ **This lane will not invent the replacement.** 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"I could just add it" is how a product decision becomes a line in a feature slice.*

### ③ The three options, and the trade of each

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Say what is coming** — *"Forecast is not built yet; you will see it here when it is."* | ⛔ **A roadmap promise in the product**, and 📁 **`forecast` is refused as DOMAIN LAW rather than merely unbuilt** — see ④ |
| **B** ▶ | **Narrow the six goals to what Signora does** — remove or reword `FORECAST_ACCURATELY` | ⛔ **The six are a designed vocabulary** — 📁 *"users can't rank features they haven't used, but they know what is going wrong"* — **and removing the one a seller feels most is a real product loss** |
| **C** | **Keep the goal, drop the *"will open on"* claim entirely** — record the goal, promise no destination | ✅ **Cheapest and already half-shipped** · ⛔ **the step then visibly does nothing, which is the feature menu the design replaced** |

### ④ 🔴 One fact that decides more than it looks

📁 **`forecast` is not an unbuilt screen — it is a capability the owning module DECLINES to have.** [`buying_score_engine/domain/events.py`](../backend/modules/buying_score_engine/domain/events.py):

> ***"No probability, no likelihood, no prediction. A buying score prioritizes commercial attention; it does not forecast a purchase."***

📁 **`opportunity_engine`'s router says it again independently**: *"No forecast, no probability, no deal value. Not an omission."*

⚡ **So option A would promise something two modules have refused in writing**, and **[TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md) — whose whole subject is *AI win probability vs rep forecast* — is asking for the same capability from the same modules.** ⛔ **Whether Signora forecasts at all is one product decision, and it is upstream of both.**

### ⑤ What this lane measured, and it is the answer TASK-1469 was waiting for

📁 **[TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md) says it frees when a Deals destination exists *"and `opportunity_engine`'s read surface has been measured against this screen's needs."*** ✅ **Measured, against the design's four reads:**

| The design needs | `opportunity_engine` publishes |
|---|---|
| **AI win probability** | ⛔ **Nothing — refused by name** |
| **Forecast gap** *(`Commit 90%` vs `34%`, `−23 pts`)* | ⛔ **Nothing. There is no rep forecast anywhere in the repository** |
| **Deal health, five dimensions** | ⛔ **Nothing** |
| **Contribution set** | ⚠️ **`ContributionList` exists and is about the BUYING SCORE on an ACCOUNT** — 📁 **different subject, different aggregate**, exactly as the row warns |

⛔ **So TASK-1469 does NOT free when a Deals route appears.** ⚡ **Its subject has no source and no owner**, and the row's *"⑤ it frees when a Deals destination exists and that measurement is done"* **is now measured and the answer is no.** ✅ **Reported rather than acted on** — 📁 the row's fitness is Lane C's and its priority is the product owner's.

> ⚠️ **The row also says this measurement is *"what Lane B can do NOW"*.** ⛔ **`opportunity_engine` is LANE A's** in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) — **so the sentence names the wrong lane**, which is why nobody had done it.

> 🔴 **CORRECTED 2026-08-12, before the ruling. This row was titled *"Decision brief for C-300"* and every reference in it pointed at `#c-300`.**
>
> ⛔ **`C-300` is already allocated, to *"Provider Platform owns the half of the inbound path Lane B may not build"* at line 6767 — an unrelated item that has been in the register since before this question existed.** ⚡ **There is exactly one `C-300` and it is not the commercial-facts item**, so every link here resolved to the wrong subject and a reader following one would have found a Provider Platform dependency.

> ✅ **So `C-1430` is the item, not a brief attached to one.** ⚠️ **Lane A raised the commercial-facts question as *"C-300"* and it is not on `integration` under any id — the collision is with an existing row rather than between two live ones, which is why nothing flagged it.**
>
> ⛔ **Not renumbered by this office.** **Lane A allocates from its own block and the correction is theirs**; this row is corrected because the wrong link was mine to publish. **Reported to Lane A.**

> ⚡ **So the scheme did not fail and there is no evidence here about it.** **The blocks made a cross-lane collision unrepresentable, and this was a lane stepping outside its own** — by the one method the rule names: 📁 ***"identifiers are allocated from a block, never from the highest number seen."*** **Lane A read its highest used id and added one.** ✅ **`209`–`216` were free throughout, which is why the renumber needed no escalation.**

>
> ⚠️ **AND THE RENUMBER IS NOT ON `integration` YET, so `C-300` is genuinely duplicated there today** — line 516 (Lane A's item) and line 6842 (Provider Platform). 📁 **`state-check` now reports it: *"C- identifiers are allocated twice: C-300."*** ⚡ **It could not see the collision while the number lived on a branch, and it saw it the moment the row landed** — which is the checker working, one step later than anybody would like.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED AND RATIFIED, product owner, 2026-08-12.** ⚡ **Option A: Signora owns commercial account facts — Open ACV, Renewal, commercial/opportunity stage.** **Contract: [ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md), RATIFIED.** ⛔ **Ownership only; it defines no implementation detail.** ⚠️ **This row read `READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` for hours after the ruling — corrected on QE's measurement.** **The ruling was recorded on the ADR and not on the brief that asked for it**, the same defect one artifact along |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** |
| **Relationship** | ⛔ **The item raised by Lane A is now `C-209`, renumbered at `301307e2`. This row is its decision brief** — the preparation §20e asks this office for, never a second decision |
| ✅ **Accepted** | **Product owner, 2026-08-12: this is the correct bounded brief and the evidence is sufficient.** ⛔ **No further investigation is authorised, and this office is not to design the RFC** — **field names, schema, API shape and mechanism are all outside the ruling.** ⚡ **The ruling determines one thing: whether Signora owns the capability. The RFC then proceeds through normal governance** |
| **Consolidates** | ⚡ **`C-209` · [TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md) · [C-297](#c-297).** **One ruling, three surfaces** |

### ① The exact question

> **Does Signora hold commercial facts about an account — *Open ACV*, *Renewal date*, *opportunity / commercial stage* — as first-class canonical attributes?**

⛔ **Not *"how should they be modelled"*.** **Only whether they are in the product's vocabulary at all.**

### ② Design evidence requiring them

📁 **`Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html`** draws **Open ACV** and **Renewal** as account-table columns. 📁 **TASK-1469's deal record** and 📁 **[C-297](#c-297)'s Forecast** each require the same concept independently.

### ③ Existing domain evidence — the platform refuses them, in writing

📁 **[`provider_normalization/infrastructure/mappers/crm.py`](../backend/modules/provider_normalization/infrastructure/mappers/crm.py):100**

> *"**Nothing commercial.** Is this already a customer, **contract value**, **renewal date**, **opportunity stage** — the facts that make a CRM worth connecting for Epic D — have **no canonical attribute**, and `ClaimAttribute` says an RFC extends it. **Inventing one here would put a vocabulary decision inside a translation file, which is the quietest place in the codebase to make one.**"*

⚡ **This is not an omission. It is a refusal with a stated reason and a named route — an RFC extending `ClaimAttribute`.** ✅ **The architecture already says who may answer: not a translation file, not a table, not a lane.**

📁 **[C-297](#c-297) records the same shape one module along** — `buying_score_engine` refuses the probability concept in writing, and the product promised Forecast anyway.

### ④ Consequences

| | **A — Signora owns commercial account facts** | **B — it does not** |
|---|---|---|
| **Route** | **An RFC extending `ClaimAttribute`**, which the refusal names. ⛔ **Not a lane's change** | ⛔ **None needed** |
| **Reaches** | `provider_normalization` · `knowledge_graph` · every CRM adapter · the account table · TASK-1469 · C-297 | — |
| **Product** | ✅ **The account table matches its design. Forecast and the deal record become possible** | ⛔ **Three approved surfaces are permanently narrower than drawn, and the designs need correcting upstream** |
| **Risk** | ⚠️ **A commercial vocabulary is a CRM's hardest surface to normalise** — stage names differ per tenant, ACV is currency-and-period bound | ⚠️ **Signora reads a CRM and cannot say what a deal is worth**, which is the question a seller asks first |

### ⑤ Recommendation — **A**, and the reason is not the design

⚡ **Three independent surfaces asked for the same concept without coordinating.** 📁 **That is the repository's own test for whether something belongs in the vocabulary** — [P-C](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md): *an event exists when a consumer appears*. **Three consumers have appeared.**

⛔ **This office recommends *that* the concept is owned. It does not propose the model** — the refusal names an RFC, and [§21](../CLAUDE.md) forbids inventing architecture in a brief. **Ruling A commissions that RFC; it does not decide its content.**

⚠️ **B is a legitimate answer and would be cheaper today.** **Its cost is that three approved designs must then be corrected upstream** — ⛔ **and leaving them drawn while the platform refuses them is the one option that is not available**, because it is the state that produced C-300 and C-297.

### ⑥ Exact scope affected

**Blocked until ruled:** *Open ACV* and *Renewal* columns in [TASK-1475](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-1469](BACKLOG.md)'s deal record · [C-297](#c-297)'s Forecast.
✅ **Not blocked:** ⚡ **everything else in TASK-1475** — see the row.
