## C-1433 · `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` now names a deployment class, and `environments.py` still reads it to resolve a stack

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-13, on Lane A's report from [C-298](#c-298)'s fix. ⚡ **They named it and explicitly declined to decide it** — *"it needs its own variable, and that is a change with cross-lane reach rather than something to fold into a security slice"* |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **one variable serving two concepts across three lanes' files is an architecture question, and the fix touches [`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) (Lane A), the compose files (QE) and every lane's local setup** |
| **Status** | 🔵 **`OPEN`** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ✅ **[C-298](#c-298)'s fix stands on its own and [TASK-1479](BACKLOG.md) ⓵b proceeds.** ⚠️ **What it risks is a lane setting the documented value and breaking its own stack** |

### 🔴 The conflict, measured

📁 **[ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md) makes `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` a **deployment class** — the ratified vocabulary is `local` · `test` · `demo` · `production-local` · `staging` · `production`**, and `is_development` is an allow-list of `{local, test}`.

📁 **[`infra/environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) reads the same variable to resolve a **stack**:** `:267` — `explicit = os.environ.get("SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT")`, resolving names like `:183` — `Environment("lane-a", 2, "Development — Product Surface", "Lane A", port_slot=3)`.

⛔ **And its own docstring INVITES the value that breaks things:** `:254` — ***"`SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` — explicit, and it wins. A lane driving a stack that is not its own must be able to say so out loud."***

🔴 **So a lane following that instruction sets `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT=lane-a` and gets a value ADR-0412's vocabulary does not contain.** ⚠️ **Lane A measured what that did before the fix: it read as DEPLOYED to both tiers, so the mock provider refused *and* the console email transport threw at startup — breaking development twice at once and explaining neither.**

### ⚡ The shape, and it is the general one

> **One variable carries two concepts: *which stack* — ports, database, Redis index — and *what kind of deployment* — is it safe to serve a stub, or to write a credential to stdout.**
>
> ⛔ **A value that answers one cannot answer the other.**

✅ **[§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s least-powerful-author rule points the same way**: a stack name is developer configuration and a deployment class is a safety property, and **a safety property must not be settable by somebody choosing a port slot.**

### 🔴 The decisive measurement — the two vocabularies share exactly one member, and it is deliberate

**Contributed by QE, whose files two of the three are. ⚠️ Re-measured here against the RATIFIED enum, and it comes out one member different from QE's report.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stack** — [`environments.py`](../infra/environments.py) `BY_NAME` | `demo` · `lane-a` · `lane-b` · `lane-c` · `lane-d` · `lane-e` · `lane-qe` · `review` |
| **Deployment class** — [ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md), ratified | `local` · `test` · **`demo`** · `production-local` · `staging` · `production` |
| ⚡ **Intersection** | **`{demo}` — one member, and Lane A put it there on purpose**: *"the one deliberate overlap, because there the stack and the deployment class genuinely are the same thing."* |

⚠️ **QE reported the intersection as EMPTY and measured against `development · test · production · production-local`** — ⛔ **the PRE-FIX vocabulary. `development` is deliberately absent from the ratified enum and `local` replaces it.** ✅ **Verified against `signora_platform/environment.py` on Lane A's branch: `LOCAL · TEST · DEMO · PRODUCTION_LOCAL · STAGING · PRODUCTION`.**

⚡ **The correction does not weaken the finding — it sharpens what the ruling is choosing between.** **Every stack name except `demo` is invalid for the deployment reader, and every deployment class except `demo` resolves to `BY_NAME.get(...) → None`.** ⛔ **So the overload cannot be resolved by convention, documentation or care: outside one intentional member there is no value that satisfies both readers.**

📁 **A consequence QE owns and reports as not-a-defect-today:** `infra/docker-compose.prod.yml`:41 sets `production-local`, **so inside the prod-local stack, stack resolution returns `None`.** ✅ **Services address each other by compose service name and never ask.** ⚠️ **A future in-container caller of `current_environment()` would get the fallback and be told nothing.**

### The alternatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** ▶ | **A second variable for the stack** — `SIGNORA_STACK` or equivalent — **and `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` keeps ADR-0412's meaning alone** | ✅ **Each variable answers one question.** ⚠️ **Touches every lane's local setup and [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md), which is QE's** |
| **B** | **`environments.py` stops reading `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT`** and resolves the stack from the branch alone | ✅ **Smallest change.** ⛔ **Removes the capability its docstring exists to provide — a lane driving a stack that is not its own** |
| **C** | **Leave it and document the hazard** | ⛔ **ELIMINATED by the measurement above.** **Outside `demo`, no value satisfies both readers — so there is no convention a document could teach.** ⚠️ **A documented trap is still a trap, and this one breaks development in two places while explaining neither** |

### ⚡ FIRST QUESTION — is this already decided? Because if it is, the item collapses

**Raised by QE, 2026-08-13. ✅ Verified verbatim against the ADR rather than accepted, and the citation is exact.**

📁 **[ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md) §6, last clause:** > ⛔ ***"`SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` is no exception, and a second reader of it elsewhere is the second taxonomy this ruling forbids."***

📁 **§2:** ***"`SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT` is the single name"*** · ***"The vocabulary is closed"*** · ***"an unrecognised environment value must be unrepresentable, never silently treated as development."***

⚡ **[`environments.py`](../infra/environments.py):267 is a second reader of that variable resolving a different taxonomy** — the clause's subject, almost word for word. ⛔ **And under a closed vocabulary, `lane-a` — a legitimate, defined stack name — is an *unrepresentable* value by ratified contract**, which is precisely what Lane A observed when the demonstration began raising a Pydantic validation failure rather than `AIRegistrationError`.

**The argument against, which QE stated themselves rather than leaving for somebody to find:** ⚠️ **§6 cites [§20b](../CLAUDE.md), whose subject is *"no **module** calls `os.environ`"*, and `infra/` is tooling rather than a module.** ✅ **But the clause's second half is unqualified — *"a second reader of it **elsewhere**"* — and the harm it names is exactly what the resolver creates.**

### ⛔ THIS OFFICE WILL NOT ADJUDICATE THE REACH OF ITS OWN SENTENCE

🔴 **Lane C drafted [ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md), including that clause.** ⛔ **Reading it as already deciding the thing this office then recommended is the self-serving reading, and it is not one a lane may take on its own behalf** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a lane's recommendation is architectural input and never implementation authority*, and [OPERATING-MODE §1](coordination/lane-c/OPERATING-MODE.md): ⛔ *close a decision because closing it unblocks Lane C.*

**So the question is put rather than answered, and it is one word:**

> **Does ADR-0412 §6 already forbid `environments.py`'s second reading of `SIGNORA_ENVIRONMENT`?**
>
> ✅ **If YES — this is not a new decision. It is ADR-0412 applied, and the only open questions are *which* new variable names the stack and who edits [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) and the compose files.** ⚡ **QE has offered to implement either way, and both files are theirs.**
> ⛔ **If NO — the three alternatives below stand as written.**

📁 **Checked rather than assumed: §7's *deliberately does not decide* list names member names · the logging library · the field-matching strategy · the `Settings` object's owning module · deployment configuration.** ⛔ **A second taxonomy keyed on the same variable is on none of them.**

⚡ **`{demo}` survives either reading** — it is in both vocabularies *on purpose*, so it is one concept two systems agree on rather than a second taxonomy.

### Recommendation — **A**, and it is input rather than authority

⚡ **The variable that means a safety class should be the one that cannot be set for convenience.** ⛔ **Not decided here**: it reaches `infra/` (Lane A), the compose files and [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md) (QE), and every lane's environment, **which is three owners and therefore not one lane's to choose.**

📁 **[ADR-0412](architecture/adr/0412-environment-and-secret-safe-logging.md) §7 already settles what is NOT in question**: the vocabulary itself is Lane A's and *"becomes part of the ratified contract"* on proposal, so ⛔ **this item must not reopen the member names.**

## C-1432 · Three orderings for one worklist — which survives the Attention migration?

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-13, [D-231](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ②.** ⛔ **Do not reopen absent a separate future requirement** |
| ✅ **THE RULING — all three RETIRE** | > **`By urgency` → RETIRE · `By stage` → RETIRE · `All / Mine / Unassigned` → RETIRE**<br><br>✅ **The finalized Home design's canonical worklist model replaces the legacy `/` controls, and the canonical ordering remains *"ranked by what it costs to ignore."***<br><br>⛔ **Do NOT carry the legacy controls into `/w/:workspace/home`.** ⛔ **Do NOT invent replacement controls.** ⛔ **Do NOT create a new design unless a separate future requirement explicitly asks for one** |
| ⚡ **And proceed with Home immediately** | 📁 **The ruling says so in terms: *"this decision applies only to the legacy controls. It does NOT block or change the already-authorized Home implementation."*** ✅ **The legacy `/` surface may be reconciled and removed once the canonical Home migration requirements are satisfied** |
| ⚠️ **It releases no backlog row, and that is measured** | 📁 **`grep -c "C-1432" BACKLOG.md` → **0**.** ✅ **No row was ever blocked on it** — the `Blocks` cell below has said so since the item was raised. ⚡ **What the ruling discharges is the last PRODUCT question in front of the retirement; two ENGINEERING conditions remain and neither is this ruling's:** ⛔ **27 e2e specs and the post-login redirect still point at `/`** · ⛔ **[TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)'s open question — *do `/` and `/business` leave the rail before their design-named successors exist* — is a member-navigation regression this office declined to take and did not manufacture a row for** |
| **Owner** | — *(was: product owner)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The retirement of the legacy `/` Attention surface, and nothing else.** ✅ **Confirmed by inspection 2026-08-12, not asserted: neither [TASK-1424](BACKLOG.md) nor [TASK-1425](BACKLOG.md) mentions `Unassigned`, `By urgency` or `By stage`** — **the separation the product owner asked for already exists by construction and needed no refinement** |
| ⚡ **NOT A HOME BLOCKER** | **Product owner, 2026-08-12: *"C-1432 is a product decision, NOT a blanket Home implementation blocker."*** ✅ **Everything the Home design specifies is implementable now** — the canonical route · the composition and card registry · *ranked by what it costs to ignore* · the card catalogue · the six states · responsive · a11y · activation ordering · **U-04's interim ranking instruction · U-05's *reorder and remove only***. ⛔ **Only the three legacy controls wait on this ruling** |

### The question, and it is three-way rather than two

**The legacy `/` offers two orderings the finalized Home design does not name. The design specifies a third that no code implements.**

| | Where | Today |
|---|---|---|
| **`By urgency`** | ⛔ Legacy `/` only | Client regroup, **deliberately no round trip** — 📁 *"a round trip could return a differently-ordered list mid-triage"* |
| **`By stage`** | ⛔ Legacy `/` only | Same mechanism |
| ⚡ **"what it costs to ignore"** | ✅ **`Fortune Signora Home.dc.html`** | ⛔ **Nothing implements it** |

**Plus `All / Mine / Unassigned`** — ⚡ **server-side narrowing via `?owner=` into `useAccounts`, not a client filter.** ⛔ **No equivalent in the card contract.**

### Measured, not inferred

📁 **Lane A scanned all 106,819 bytes of the Home design:** `"Unassigned"` **0** · `"urgency"` **0** · `"By stage"` **0** · `"All /"` **0** · `"Mine"` **2**, ⚡ **and neither is a control** — one is `activity.mine`, a data dependency of the *Pick up where you left off* card; the other sits inside the design's own open question U-05.

⛔ **So the design does not silently supersede these. It is silent about them, which is different.**

### What is being asked

> **Do `By urgency` and `By stage` survive alongside the design's *"what it costs to ignore"*, or does that ordering replace them?**
> **Does `All / Mine / Unassigned` survive, given it is server-side narrowing the card contract does not express?**

⛔ **No recommendation.** ⚡ **This office ruled on design *conformance* for the pager ([C-1431](#c-1431)) because the design was silent in a way that resolved itself. Here it is silent in a way that does not** — **three orderings is a product choice about how a seller works, and choosing it would be inventing the product** ([§21](../CLAUDE.md)).

### ⚠️ The design carries its own open questions, and says so

📁 **U-04 — *attention ranking model ownership*, owner Architecture:** whether the ranking is computed by the signals service or composed client-side, which ***"determines whether the order is stable across a refresh"***. ✅ **Its interim instruction is explicit and unblocking: assume the service returns a ranked list; if it does not, seed the order deterministically so a refresh does not reshuffle.** ⛔ **Not blocking, and not this item.**
📁 **U-05 — *Customisation scope*.**

⚡ **So the composition authority is authoritative AND incomplete, and it declares both.** **That is a better basis than an authority which is silently incomplete.**

## C-1431 · Pagination — the design does not require numbered pages, and `Previous`/`Next` is design-compatible

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — design-compatible. Product owner, 2026-08-12, accepting the measurement.** ⛔ **Not to be reopened absent new evidence contradicting the four findings below** |
| **Owner** | — |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** **Lane A implements `Previous`/`Next`** |

**Measured in `Fortune Signora Companies.dc.html`:** ⛔ **the word *"pagination"* appears ZERO times.** *"paging"* appears **once**, *"of 312"* **twice**, *"virtualis"* **once**.

⚡ **The numbered pager exists only in the rendered mock** — `Rows 1–8 of 312 · virtualised beyond 100 · Previous · 1 · 2 · 3 · Next` — **beside a rendering technique, never as a stated rule.** 📁 **The design's own stated rules are Grouping · Sorting · Selection · Bulk actions · Tags · Smart filters · Pinned columns · AI in the table. Pagination is not among them.**

📁 **The one normative sentence touching paging is the *Selection* rule:** *"Survives scrolling, filtering and paging: the count is always of records, never of rows on screen."* ✅ **That constrains selection, not the pager's form, and it is satisfiable under `Previous`/`Next`.**

⛔ **Drawn in a mock is not required by the design authority**, and 📁 [`knowledge_graph/interface/router.py`](../backend/modules/knowledge_graph/interface/router.py):114 is keyset **by deliberate choice**: *"an offset page would skip or repeat rows… a customer paging the list would silently miss accounts."*

⚡ **So the two do not actually conflict.** **A numbered pager would require abandoning a guarantee the contract makes on purpose, to satisfy a rule the design never states.**

> ⚠️ **Lane A measured this first and explicitly did not conclude it** — *"whether drawn in the mock rises to required by the design authority is the determination the product owner left with you."* ✅ **That is the right line and this office made the call.**

## C-1429 · The approved designs assume four roles and the domain represents two — found twice, in two workflows, by two capability checks

> ✅ **RULING: a capability/permission layer ABOVE `WorkspaceRole`. ⛔ Do NOT widen the enum.**
>
> 📁 ***"`WorkspaceRole` represents tenancy membership… Admin / Analyst / Effective permissions represent authorization capabilities, which is a different concern."***
>
> **`OWNER` and `MEMBER` stay the membership model.** ⛔ **No UI-only role with no authorization semantics.** ✅ **Casbin remains the implementation authority**, and **migration and backward compatibility must be addressed by the contract.**
>
> ➡️ **Contract: [ADR-0410](architecture/adr/0410-authorization-capability-layer.md). Then Settings and Team Management release to Lane A.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-12, feeding Lane A's pipeline. ⚡ **Not sought — hit twice while running Gate E on unrelated workflows** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **a role model is product scope, and widening one is neither a lane's nor this office's** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-12.** |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Every remaining slice of Settings and Team Management that touches a role.** ⛔ **Nothing currently claimed, and no lane is idle *on this*** |

### The evidence, and it is two lines

📁 **[`workspace_tenancy/domain/entities.py:32`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/domain/entities.py)** — `WorkspaceRole` is a `StrEnum` of exactly **`OWNER`** and **`MEMBER`**.

📁 **`Fortune Signora Team Management.dc.html`** draws **`Admin`**, **`Analyst`**, ***Change to Analyst***, ***Effective permissions*** and ***A Member will be able to***. 📁 **`Fortune Signora Settings.dc.html`** draws ***Roles & permissions*** with ***New role***.

⚡ **So this is not unbuilt UI. It is unrepresentable UI** — and that distinction is the reason no Lane A row was created for either.

### Why it is raised rather than absorbed

⛔ **A frontend task for a role the domain cannot express is a row Lane A cannot finish**, and creating one to move the [D-187](DECISION_REGISTER.md) count toward 20 is precisely what that floor must not be met with.

⚠️ **It is the [C-1425](#c-1425--task-466backlogmd-is-the-action-batchs-first-consumer-and-no-domain-implements-an-operation-for-it-to-apply) shape at the level of a shared primitive rather than one operation** — and unlike C-1425 it gates **two** workflows, which is why it is worth one item instead of two rejections in a checkpoint.

### What is *not* being asked

⛔ **No recommendation on the role model, deliberately.** **The options — widen the enum · add a capability layer beside it · narrow the designs — differ in tenancy, authorization and migration consequences that this office has not assessed**, and a preference stated without that work would be the guess [§21](../CLAUDE.md) forbids.

✅ **What is being asked is only whether the gap is scheduled.** ⚡ **Until it is, both workflows' role slices stay unwritten, and that is the correct state rather than a stalled one.**

## C-1428 · [TASK-1462](BACKLOG.md) §03 needs two facts nothing models, and its §14 half names a surface that does not exist

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN` — Lane A, 2026-08-12, measuring the row's premises before writing code, which the row itself instructs** |

| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Two of the row's three halves.** ✅ **§09 shipped**, and one value the row listed as *verified* was measurably wrong and is fixed |

📁 **The design**: *"The trigger states the workspace, its plan and its region."*
📁 **The row's own instruction**: ⚠️ ***"Verify `plan` and `region` exist on the workspace contract first. If they do not, this half is a dependency on `workspace_tenancy` and is raised as a `C-` item, not invented client-side."***

✅ **Verified, at every layer rather than at the one that was convenient:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Frontend contract** | `Workspace` is **`id` · `name` · `created_at` · `updated_at`** |
| **HTTP contract** | `WorkspaceResponse` is **the same four** |
| **The aggregate itself** | `Workspace` is those four plus `created_by` and `updated_by` |
| ⚠️ **The one near-miss, and it is not the same thing** | `region` appears in [`domain/onboarding.py`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/domain/onboarding.py) as an **`Answer[str]` to an onboarding question** — 📁 **where a customer SELLS**, not where their workspace is hosted. ⛔ **Rendering a commercial answer as a data region would be a wrong fact stated confidently** |

📁 **§12 · the assistant**: ***"a NON-MODAL 420px drawer that PUSHES CONTENT."***
📁 **§14 · the context drawer**: ***"MODAL, right-hand, 480 / 640 / 800px… a header with the object name, a scrolling body, and a pinned footer."***

🔴 **So `480` is not present either**, and **the context drawer does not exist as a surface.** ⚡ **Building it would be a new modal panel with no caller** — 📁 the class named in [C-1427](#c-1427--the-top-two-rows-of-lane-as-queue-each-wait-on-a-capability-nobody-has-scheduled-and-the-pattern-is-worth-more-than-either-row), refused twice already today.

### ③ ⛔ One value the row listed as *verified* was wrong, and it is fixed

📁 **The row's *"must NOT touch"* cell**: *"The rail (232/56), user menu (280), top bar (56) and **copilot (420)** all carry their specified values — **verified**."*

🔴 **Measured in a browser at 1280: the assistant drawer was 1265px.** ⛔ **`copilot.tsx` quoted §12's *"non-modal 420px drawer"* in its own doc comment and passed no width**, and `Drawer` is `w-full` — **so the verification was of the sentence, not of the panel.**

✅ **Fixed, because leaving a measured defect in place on the strength of a cell that says *verified* is the deference [§2](../CLAUDE.md) exists to refuse.** ⚠️ **Recorded here rather than quietly**, since it means the row's *"verified"* list is now known to be unverified and **the other three should be measured before anybody trusts them.**

### ④ What shipped anyway

✅ **§09 is delivered and asserted from geometry**: 📁 *"640px, anchored at 14vh."* ⛔ **It was 576px at 10vh** — `max-w-xl` and `pt-[10vh]`, **two wrong numbers that both looked deliberate**, one because it was a name and one because it was round.

## C-1426 · The Security Center's Security Invariant cannot be met for session revocation, and the honest repair is not to add a challenge

| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN` — Lane A, 2026-08-12, found building [TASK-1414](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Owner** | **QE** *(the invariant is the row's and QE validates it)* · **product owner** *(if the answer is to change what the product offers)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **[TASK-1414](BACKLOG.md) shipped**, with the gap stated in the component and asserted in a test |

### ① The invariant, and the one control it cannot cover

📁 **The row's Testing metadata**: 🔴 ***"every destructive control on this page passes through [TASK-1410](BACKLOG.md)'s challenge — and the challenge is enforced server-side."***

✅ **Two of the three destructive controls meet it, by the framework rather than by a screen:**

| Control | What enforces the fresh factor |
|---|---|
| **Change password** | Better Auth's `changePassword` **takes the current password** |
| **Remove a second factor** | `twoFactor.disable` **takes the password** |
| 🔴 **Revoke a session** | ⛔ **Nothing.** `/revoke-session` uses **`sensitiveSessionMiddleware`**, which requires a **valid** session — **not a fresh one** |

### ② Why a `StepUpDialog` was not simply rendered in front of it

📁 **[TASK-1410](BACKLOG.md)'s own row names this as the failure**: *"a dialog that guards the dialog guards nothing."* ⛔ **A challenge the server does not check is a screen a caller skips**, and shipping one would make the invariant read as met while nothing enforced it — **which is worse than the gap, because it stops anybody looking.**

### ③ Why enforcing it server-side is the WRONG repair, and this is the part worth ruling on

⚠️ **It is buildable**: a `hooks.before` in [`lib/auth/server.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/server.ts) could refuse `/revoke-session` on a stale session, and that file is inside the row's Change Budget. ⛔ **It should not be built.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **There is no re-verification capability** | **Better Auth publishes no *prove it is you again* endpoint.** ⚡ **A person past the 10-minute window could only refresh their freshness by signing in again** |
| ⛔ **An SSO account has no password to re-enter** | **So for those accounts the challenge is unperformable, not merely inconvenient** |
| 🔴 **The design guarantees the opposite** | 📁 §08: ***"Session revocation still works — it is enforced by Signora — and that distinction is stated so you know what you can still do while under attack."*** |

⚡ **The consequence is the whole item**: **the one control that must survive an attack would become the first to fail**, on the page whose stated job is *"let someone who thinks they have been compromised understand what happened and stop it, in under a minute, while frightened."*

### ④ What shipped, and what is asked for

✅ **Revocation ships unchallenged, and [`sessions-panel.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/profile/security/sessions-panel.tsx) states all of the above in the component** — ⛔ **the gap is not hidden in a commit message.**

**One of three, and it is not this lane's to pick:**

1. **Accept it** — record the invariant as *two of three, by the vendor*, and note that revocation is deliberately the unchallenged one.
2. **Narrow the invariant** to controls the framework challenges, and say so in the row.
3. **Add a re-verification capability** — a real one, server-enforced, that an SSO account can also satisfy. ⚠️ **That is a workflow, not a line**, and it would need its own row.

⛔ **This lane recommends ① or ②** and did not act on either, because **changing what a Security Invariant means is not an implementation decision.**

## C-1425 · [TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) is the Action Batch's first consumer, and no domain implements an operation for it to apply

> ✅ **RULING: Signora owns Account Owner/CSM, Tags and Segments as CUSTOMER-ORGANIZED account metadata.**
>
> ⛔ **Explicitly NOT merged with [C-209](#c-209)/[ADR-0409](architecture/adr/0409-commercial-account-facts.md)** — 📁 *"customer-authored organizational concepts, distinct from provider/CRM commercial facts."* ⚡ **The separation this office recommended is the one ruled.**
>
> **One contract, reused by Companies · Account 360 · Action Batch/[TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) · every approved surface.** ⛔ ***"Do NOT build fake Action Batch actions before the underlying capability exists."***
>
> ➡️ **Contract: [ADR-0411](architecture/adr/0411-customer-organized-account-metadata.md).**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-12.** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, measuring the row before claiming it — ⛔ **not after starting it** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **which operation the first consumer performs is product scope, and the row's Change Budget contains no module that could hold one** |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-466](BACKLOG.md) only.** ✅ **Lane A is NOT idle** — [TASK-1414](BACKLOG.md), the next entry in the queue, was claimed in the same turn ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *Continuous execution*) |

> ⚡ **CLASSIFIED 2026-08-12, Lane C: a genuine product decision, and ⛔ it must NOT be merged with [C-1430](#c-1430).**
>
> **They look like one question — *does Signora model account attributes it was not given?* — and they are two, because the least-powerful-author rule ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)) separates them.**
>
> | | **This row: owner · tag · segment** | **[C-1430](#c-1430): Open ACV · Renewal · stage** |
> |---|---|---|
> | **Who authors it** | ✅ **The customer.** Workspace-authored organisation of their own book | ⛔ **The provider.** Facts a CRM already holds |
> | **Route if owned** | **A domain that models them** — the row's Change Budget names none | 📁 **An RFC extending `ClaimAttribute`**, which `crm.py` names |
> | **Failure if wrong** | A customer's own labels are unrepresentable | ⛔ **Signora invents a commercial vocabulary from someone else's data** |
>
> ⚠️ **Merging them would let one ruling settle both, and the cheap answer to one is the expensive answer to the other.** ⛔ **Two rulings, and this office recommends nothing on this one** — *which* operation the Action Batch's first consumer performs is scope, and proposing it would be inventing the product.

### ① What the row asks for, in its own words

📁 **Definition of Done**: ***"A seller selects several companies, sees exactly what will happen, applies it, and is told the truth about when it finished · the confirm states the COUNT and the ACTION in the customer's words · reversal is offered only where the window genuinely allows it."***

⚡ **Two of those four are pure Product Surface and this lane can build them today** — the selection, and the confirm that names a count. ⛔ **The other two name an *operation*: something that is applied, and something that is taken back.**

### ② What exists, measured rather than assumed

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **The lifecycle context is real and complete** | 📁 [`application/batches.py`](../backend/modules/action_batch/application/batches.py) implements **`propose` · `approve` · `reject` · `withdraw` · `request_application` · `apply` · `reverse`** |
| ⛔ **Its HTTP surface publishes exactly two of them** | 📁 [`interface/router.py`](../backend/modules/action_batch/interface/router.py) — **`POST …/action-batches/{id}/apply`** and **`GET …/action-batches/{id}`**. ⚠️ **No propose, no approve, no reverse endpoint exists**, so a screen cannot create a batch, cannot approve one, and cannot take one back |
| 🔴 **The design's bulk bar draws six actions, and NONE of them has an implementation** | 📁 *Assign owner · Add tag · Add to segment · Create tasks · Export 41 · ✦ Draft outreach.* ⛔ **No module models an account owner, an account tag or a segment** — the `tags=` hits across `backend/modules/**/router.py` are **FastAPI route metadata**, and `owner_id` belongs to **an opportunity**, never to a company |
| ⛔ **The contract the screen already reads publishes two fields** | 📁 `ListedAccount` is **`account: AccountIdentity`** and **`kind`**. **Nothing mutable is on it** |

### ③ Why this is not a gap this lane may close inside the row

📁 **The context's own public contract states the boundary, and [ADR-0405](architecture/adr/0405-an-action-is-approved-before-it-is-effective.md) ratifies it**:

> ***"This context owns lifecycle. The consuming domain owns interpreting the action, performing the operation, validating business rules, executing the change, and implementing the inverse."***

⛔ **So `action_batch` may not perform any of the six**, and 📁 **the row's Change Budget is 🟢 `frontend/app/(app)/**` · `modules/action_batch/**` · 🟠 a shared data table · 🔴 *nothing*** — **it names no business module at all.** ⚡ **The row was sized as though the operation existed**; it is the one input the six-slice chain never had, and **[455 §5](architecture/455-context-definitions-r02-r03.md) says so itself** — *"the module that owns an operation is the only thing that knows how to perform or undo it."*

### ④ Why the shared data table is NOT shipped as a down-payment

⚠️ **The obvious salvage is the half with no backend dependency** — 📁 the row's own *"the SAME data table [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) needs, and whichever lands first owns it"*, which **workflows 14, 20, 21 and 22 all inherit.**

⛔ **Refused, and for the reason this lane has refused three times already**: a bulk bar whose six buttons cannot do anything is **the false-affordance class** — a customer selects eleven companies, presses *Add tag*, and learns the product is unreliable rather than unfinished ([§20c](../CLAUDE.md), and the same argument [`copilot.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/copilot.tsx) makes about an input box that accepts a question nothing will answer).

### ⑤ Input, never authority — and the cheapest unblock is probably not Companies

⚡ **The first consumer does not have to be this screen, and one candidate already has both halves the Companies bulk bar lacks:**

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **The operation exists and is reachable** | 📁 **`POST /workspaces/{id}/signals/{signal_id}/resolution`** — *"Record what you decided about this signal"* |
| ✅ **Its inverse is already designed, in the endpoint's own words** | 📁 ***"Changing your mind creates another one naming the one it replaces; nothing is deleted: every resolution is auditable"*** — ⚡ **which is precisely a reversal within a window, expressed as an append** |
| ✅ **The list already renders with bulk selection** | 📁 **[TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md) shipped the Signal Center's selection and count**, so the surface half is built and would not be built twice |

⛔ **This lane is not proposing a re-scope and has not acted on it** — **where TASK-466 sits and what it covers is the product owner's** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *fitness only, never priority*). ⚠️ **It is recorded because the alternative is a row that waits on a business capability nobody has scheduled**, and **naming a cheaper first consumer is worth more than reporting the blocker alone.**

### ⑥ What would close this item

1. **A ruling on which operation the first consumer performs** — one of the design's six, or the signal resolution above.
2. **That operation existing in the module that owns it**, with its inverse — ⛔ **not in `action_batch`, and not in the Product Surface.**
3. **`propose`, `approve` and `reverse` reaching the HTTP surface.** ✅ **That third one IS inside this row's budget and is this lane's to build** — it is held only because an endpoint with no operation behind it is the same defect one layer down.

## C-1424 · [B-253](BUGS.md) — an unresolved read renders as a denied permission, and which wrong state is less harmful is a product decision

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — RULED, product owner, 2026-08-13** ([D-234](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). ⛔ **No new authorization semantics, no new permission model, no navigation redesign.** ✅ **Three states, distinguished: `unresolved/loading` · `resolved with permission` · `resolved without permission`** — ⛔ **and an unresolved role must NOT render as an explicit denial.** ⚡ **[B-253](BUGS.md) is released to Lane A** |
| ✅ **AND THE DESIGN ALREADY SPECIFIES ALL THREE — no product behaviour is invented** | 📁 **App Shell §16, Cold boot: *"Chrome paints from cached shell state; only the content region skeletons. **Workspace name and rail appear before data resolves**"*** and ***"the frame is never blank."*** ⛔ **So the rail renders as an ordinary rail while the role is unresolved — it does NOT skeleton and it does NOT lock.** 📁 **Rail States: *"Restricted destinations stay visible at 45% with a lock and explain on click"*** — ✅ **that is the `resolved without permission` appearance, and it is the ONLY state that shows a lock.**<br><br>⚡ **This retires the choice this office prepared.** ⛔ **Option A — a resolving state on the rail — is refused by the design, which says the rail appears before data resolves.** ✅ **The recommended B is what the design specifies, so it was never a preference** |
| ✅ **The residual question I flagged is answered, and it is smaller than I thought** | ⚠️ **I wrote that B was only cheap *"if the refusal a member lands on is designed."*** ✅ **A restricted destination is not navigable in the design — it is a lock that explains on click, not a link** — **so the optimistic render applies only inside the unresolved window, and the server remains the enforcement.** ⛔ **NO unresolved design question remains**, and none is manufactured |
| **Raised by** | **QE**, from Lane A's handover of [TASK-1471](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** |
| **Blocks** | **[B-253](BUGS.md) only.** ⚡ **No task row is waiting on it and no lane is idle** — this is 🟠 REVIEW SOON, not 🔴 |

### ① The defect, in one line

📁 [`authenticated-shell.tsx`](../frontend/app/\(app\)/authenticated-shell.tsx) passes `role={resolved ? role : null}`, and `null` means both *"has no role"* and *"has not arrived yet."* ⛔ **The rail can only read it as the first**, so `navigation.tsx:537` computes `restricted` and renders a locked `<button>` — **on every cold boot an owner is briefly told they need somebody else's permission to open their own product.**

### ② Why it is not Lane A's to settle, and Lane A was right to stop

✅ **Lane A fixed the identical conflation for the *workspace* in TASK-1471 and deliberately left the role half**, saying so rather than picking one quietly. ⚡ **That is [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s architectural-blocker test applied correctly: the repair is small, and nobody has decided which wrong state is less harmful.** *"I could just add it"* is how a product decision becomes a line in a feature slice.

### ③ The two repairs

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Pending, like Home** — guarded rows render in a resolving state until the role lands | ⛔ **Several rail rows visibly settle on every cold boot**, on the most-looked-at surface in the product |
| **B** ▶ | **Optimistic** — render as an ordinary link until the role is known | ⛔ **A member briefly sees a destination that will refuse them** |

### ④ Recommendation: **B**, and it is not a preference

📁 **[§20c](../CLAUDE.md) already rules on what this control is**: *"Keep client-side permission checks presentational. Casbin on the server is the authorization decision; hiding a control the caller cannot use is a courtesy, never enforcement, and must never be the only check."*

⚡ **A courtesy that fires on data it does not have is not a courtesy — it is a false claim about entitlement**, and B is the option that stops the product asserting one. ⛔ **A is the safer-looking option and asserts nothing false either**, which is why this is a decision rather than a correction: **it costs motion on the rail on every single boot to avoid a state that is already survivable.**

⚡ **This is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) one level up** — *a failed read must never render as an empty result* becomes **an unresolved read must never render as a denied permission.** QE named that generalisation and it is the right one.

### ⚠️ One check decides B's cost, and it is not yet made

⛔ **B is only cheap if the refusal a member lands on is designed.** 📁 **[D-205](DECISION_REGISTER.md) records eleven terminal reason codes rendering nothing**, and if a guarded route is among them, B trades a false lock for a blank screen — **which is the [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) defect it is meant to avoid.**

✅ **This office will verify it before the row is released to Lane A, whichever way the ruling goes.** ⛔ **It is named here rather than assumed, because assuming it is what would make B the wrong recommendation quietly.**

## Answer to [C-1428](#c-1428--task-1462backlogmd-03-needs-two-facts-nothing-models-and-its-14-half-names-a-surface-that-does-not-exist) — QE, 2026-08-12: the other three values are applied, and one nearly read as false

> ⚠️ **This heading read `## C-1428 — ANSWERED by QE`, and that made the id appear twice.** ⛔ **It was never a second allocation** — it is C-1428's *answer*, and only the heading shape made every parser count it as an item, `state-check` flagging it three ways. ✅ **Retitled 2026-08-12 by Lane C, on QE's report: mechanical, non-semantic, no content moved and no id renumbered.** ⚡ **The two headings also differed by their separator — `·` against `—` — which is why this office's own sweeps saw one row where there were two.**

> **Lane A asked QE to measure the three values [TASK-1462](BACKLOG.md)'s row calls *"must NOT touch — verified"*, after finding the fourth was not.** ⚡ **That is the right ask and it is QE's remit: a list known to contain one false claim has no authority for the rest of it.**

**Measured on `f58768e5`, at the source and in the compiled output — never from a doc comment.**

| Value | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **rail 232 / 56** | ✅ **applied** | `RAIL_WIDTH` is **consumed**, not merely exported — `app-shell.tsx:242` sets `style={{ width: … }}` from it |
| **user menu 280** | ✅ **applied** | `w-[280px]` on the menu's own element, `account-menu.tsx:153` |
| **top bar 56** | ✅ **applied** | `--topbar-height: 3.5rem` → `h-topbar`, and `height: var(--topbar-height)` appears in the **built** CSS |

> ⚠️ **The top bar nearly read as a second false claim, and the reason is worth keeping.** ⛔ **`h-14`, `h-[56px]`, `height: 56` and `TOP_BAR_HEIGHT` all return nothing** — the value is a **design token**, so every numeric search misses it.
>
> ⚡ **The copilot's `420` was found because it was quoted and unused. The top bar's `56` would have been reported the same way by the same method, and would have been wrong.** **A search for a literal cannot distinguish *"the number is absent"* from *"the number is named"*** — which is [B-187](BUGS.md)'s shape in a different register, and the reason this answer measures the compiled CSS rather than the source alone.

✅ **So the copilot's `420` was the only unverified value, and Lane A found and fixed it themselves.** ⛔ **The row's list is now measured rather than asserted, and C-1428 closes.**

## C-109 · The browser suite cannot exercise the auth journeys against a production rate limit from one host

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **QE**, 2026-08-19, attributing [B-1030](BUGS.md) to a cause the row had recorded as *disconfirmed* |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — 🔴 **it is a security control's configuration**, and 📁 `frontend/lib/auth/server.ts` is not QE's to change |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** **QE will implement the half that is unambiguously its own** — the suite honouring the limiter it is being refused by — **and that may be sufficient.** ⚡ **Raised now precisely because nothing is waiting on it** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** |

**The product is behaving correctly. `frontend/lib/auth/server.ts:147` sets `rateLimit: { enabled: true }`, and Better Auth's defaults are:**

| Paths | Limit |
|---|---|
| `/sign-in` · `/sign-up` · `/change-password` · `/change-email` | **3 per 10 seconds** |
| `/forget-password` · `/request-password-reset` · `/send-verification-email` | **3 per 60 seconds** |

**Measured against the running stack, twelve POSTs to `/api/auth/sign-in/email`:**

```
401 401 401 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429 429
```

⚡ **The browser suite signs in far more than three times in ten seconds** — 📁 **`auth.setup.ts` alone signs in THREE times back to back**, which is the limit exactly, before a single journey has run.

### ⛔ The tension is between two correct things, which is why it is not QE's to settle

| | |
|---|---|
| **The limit** | **A real security control**, and ⛔ **weakening it to make a suite green is exactly what this repository forbids** |
| **The suite** | **Cannot avoid signing in** — the journeys that trip it are the ones whose subject IS signing in |

### The options, and QE's recommendation

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Recommended — ① the suite honours the limiter** | **The sign-in helper detects the product's own `429`/`Retry-After` and waits for the window it is told about.** ⚡ **Responding to the product's real signal, not sleeping blindly**, and it weakens nothing: a test whose subject IS rate limiting still asserts it. ⛔ **QE's own fixture, so QE can do this without a ruling** — and it may be the whole answer |
| ⚠️ **② configure the limit per environment** | **A typed setting, strict by default, looser only in `.env.prod-local`** — 📁 the same shape as [B-1026](BUGS.md)'s mailbox fix, and what §20b requires of configuration anyway. ⛔ **Cost: the local gate stops proving the production limit works**, so it would need a test that asserts the limiter deliberately. **Product code — Lane A's, not QE's** |
| ⛔ **③ disable it locally** | **Refused.** A control that is off wherever it is tested is a control nobody tests |

**QE proceeds with ① and reports what it recovers. ② is only worth deciding if ① is not enough.**

### 🔴 The general property this exposes, which outlives the instance

> ⛔ **A product-owner ruling that exists only in a planning artifact, and is never written into the canonical document the lanes consume, can later be silently reversed** — **by somebody reading the canonical document correctly.**

⚠️ **It has now happened twice in four days from one ruling.** 📁 **D-230 ② moved four Lane B rows to Lane A on 2026-08-12; on 2026-08-16 three still named Lane B** ([TASK-300](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-406](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-205](BACKLOG.md)) — **found only because the Lane B retirement made QE look.** ⚡ **Same mechanism, different artifact: the ruling was real and the document lanes read never learned of it.**

### ✅ What must happen once ownership is settled — and it is NOT QE's to do

📁 **Product owner, 2026-08-16: *"Do not make that amendment as an implicit QE decision."***

**Whichever way it resolves, the canonical source must be made consistent so this cannot recur:**

📁 **And [§2](../CLAUDE.md) is the sharper objection**: ***"when something a module needs starts accumulating in the substrate every module already imports, the substrate has stopped being a substrate."*** ⚠️ **The reasoning in that docstring is good and the conclusion may still be right** — **a customer-visible delivery state genuinely does need RLS.** ⛔ **What it cannot be is decided inside a feature slice.**

## C-107 · The 🔴 promotion block reads a row's status, and the defect it names is already fixed in the candidate

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **QE**, 2026-08-12 |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — 📁 this is a reading of [§20e](../CLAUDE.md), and **the party a permissive reading releases is QE** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** ⛔ **This read *"Every promotion to `main`"* and is no longer true — promotion occurred at `0dfc07f4`.** ⚠️ **The stale row also sat orphaned below the prose after this office's own edit, where a reader scanning for the blocker would meet it *after* the conclusion voiding it. Flagged by QE, corrected here** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RESOLVED` — no product decision required. Lane C, 2026-08-12, on measurement.** ⛔ **The premise is void: B-183 is `CLOSED`, promoted at `0dfc07f4`, which is an ancestor of `main` (`95c0e12f`). Promotion occurred.** ⚡ **And the general question is answered below rather than left implied** |

### ⚡ What the promotion mechanism actually inspects — measured, not read from the rule

📁 **`infra/certification-guard.py:202` `_promote()` runs exactly two gates:** ① **is this exact commit certified**, and ② **no `VERIFIED` state is undone** ([B-168](BUGS.md)).

⛔ **It never opens [`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md). It never reads a severity.** **There is no executable 🔴 promotion block** — [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s *"`integration` never fast-forwards to `main` with an open 🔴"* is **prose applied by QE**, and [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py) reports it **advisory**, never failing.

### ⛔ The circularity was real, and it was not in §20e

⚡ **§20e says an open 🔴 blocks promotion. It says nothing about when a row closes.** **The loop came from one row's own close condition** — B-183 was written *"closes when the fix is promoted"*, so the row blocked the promotion that would close it.

✅ **The counter-example is in the same register and was written for the same defect.** [B-243](BUGS.md) closed on **the fix** (`ee4e34c3`) and never self-blocked. **Two rows, one defect, two close conditions — and only the promotion-conditioned one was circular.** ⚠️ **QE observed exactly this and reported it without arming this item with it.**

**Classification: neither a governance defect nor an implementation defect. A defect in one bug row's close condition, and it has cleared** — B-183 closed on 2026-08-12 *"the row's own close condition, met literally"*.

⚡ **The transferable rule, and it needs no ruling because [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already carries it:** **a defect closes when it is fixed and QE verifies it — never when it is promoted.** **A row conditioned on promotion makes itself the obstacle to its own closure.**

⚠️ **Independence, stated because this office is an affected party.** ⛔ **This conclusion does not reinterpret §20e and does not widen what may be promoted.** **It rests on two facts that would read the same either way: `_promote` does not consult severity, and `0dfc07f4` is already on `main`.**

⚠️ **What this does NOT reduce — QE's caveat, 2026-08-12, and it is right.** ⛔ **Resolving the *mechanism* leaves the *judgement* with the product owner, per defect.** ⚡ **For B-183 that was moot because the row closed. For B-428's second criterion it is the whole question, and [C-106](#c-106--b-428bugsmds-second-criterion-is--and-only-the-product-owner-may-move-it) is where it lands.** **C-107 closing sharpens C-106 rather than easing it — there is now no code to defer to.**

### The question, in one line

> **Does *"`integration` never fast-forwards to `main` with an open 🔴 bug"* evaluate the defect's presence in the candidate tree, or the row's status in [`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md)?**

### Why it is not academic

**[B-183](BUGS.md) is the worked example, and QE built the trap itself.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The defect** | `backend/.env.example` shipped a `BYPASSRLS` superuser as the development runtime identity |
| **On `main` (`4f680315`)** | ⛔ **`:35` carries it.** The defect is live in the promoted tree |
| **On the candidate** | ✅ **`:31` names `signora_app`.** The defect is **absent** |
| **The row** | 🔴 `OPEN` — because **QE wrote *"closes when the fix is promoted"***, on the product owner's own instruction that `FIXED` ≠ `PROMOTED` |

⛔ **So the fix cannot ship, and the row cannot close, and each is the other's reason.**

> ⚠️ **QE states plainly that it created this.** The *"`OPEN` until promoted"* wording was correct about **not claiming credit for an unshipped fix** and did not consider that the same words would **hold the fix hostage.** ⛔ **A rule that prevents a security fix from reaching `main` is not the rule working.**

### The two readings, and what each costs

| | **① The candidate tree** | **② The row's status** |
|---|---|---|
| **The gate asks** | *Is the 🔴 defect present in the commit being promoted?* | *Is any 🔴 row `OPEN` in the register?* |
| **B-183 today** | ✅ **Absent — promote.** The tenancy fix ships | ⛔ **`OPEN` — blocked.** The fix stays off `main` |
| **What it protects** | **Ships fixes.** The gate measures the artifact, which is what `main` actually receives | **Ships nothing unreviewed.** The register is a human judgement the tree cannot express |
| **What it costs** | 🔴 **A 🔴 whose defect is not *in a file* — a missing capability, a wrong behaviour — becomes invisible to the gate.** [B-428](BUGS.md) is exactly that shape | 🔴 **Any 🔴 written as *"closes on promotion"* is unclosable by construction**, and QE has now written one |
| **Who it releases** | ⚠️ **QE** — QE decides what "present in the tree" means, per defect | **Nobody** — the register is the check |

### What QE recommends, and it is deliberately the narrow one

✅ **Neither reading as a general rule. A ruling on B-183 alone**, and a follow-up that makes the trap unrepresentable rather than adjudicated case by case:

> **A 🔴 row may not use *"closes when promoted"* as its close condition.** ⚡ **Split it the way [B-428](BUGS.md) was split** — one criterion for *the fix is correct and merged*, a second for *it reached `main`* — **and let the promotion gate read the first.**

⛔ **QE will not adopt that itself.** 📁 It changes what a gate means, and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) puts that with the product owner.

> ⚡ **One precedent, reported rather than relied on:** [B-428](BUGS.md)'s own row records that **cycles 201, 202 and 203 promoted while it was `OPEN`**, and `state-check.py` said so on every one. ⛔ **That is not authority for reading ①** — it is QE having read past an advisory three times, and it is why this item exists instead of a fourth.

## C-105 · [D-200](DECISION_REGISTER.md) gives Lane A and Lane C each a half, and QE cannot write either

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **QE**, 2026-08-09, on the product owner's ruling |
| **Owner** | **Lane A** for §2 · **Lane C** for §5 |
| **Status** | ✅ **§2 ADOPTED — Lane A, 2026-08-09, on the poll that found this item.** ⛔ **§5 is still Lane C's and this lane does not speak for it**, so the item stays `OPEN` until both halves land |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚡ **QE certifies exactly as before until [427](architecture/427-impact-based-validation.md) steps 3–5 land** |

**[D-200](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2 asks every Lane A submission to carry an impact summary** — changed areas, potential impact, unaffected areas — **as the starting point QE validates and extends.**

✅ **The vehicle already exists: the Slice Handoff**, which carries `Reuse`, `Preserved`, `Reachable`, `Rollback` and `Budget`. ⚡ **An `Impact:` field is the same shape and travels the same way** — in the commit message, greppable, immutable, attached to the change forever.

**[D-200](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §5 asks Product Office to state expected impact areas when it creates a task**, giving QE a scope before implementation starts.

> ⛔ **Neither is QE's to write.** **[`ENGINEERING_LAWS.md`](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md) is Lane C's; the Slice Handoff's fields are §20e's; and a lane's obligations reaching it through a QE poll narrative is exactly what [B-153](BUGS.md) cost an hour ago** — **a row held where the other lane could not see it, and a duplicate identifier as the result.**

### ✅ Lane A's half, done — the first submission carrying it is [TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md)

**QE named the vehicle correctly and this lane took it as named**: an `Impact:` field **inside the `Slice-Handoff` block**, beside `Reuse`, `Preserved`, `Reachable`, `Rollback` and `Budget` — ⛔ **not a new file and not a new convention.** ⚡ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already argues the whole case**: *"a shared queue file would conflict between lanes, and a commit message travels with the change forever and is greppable."*

**Four parts, because [D-200](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2 asks for three and the fourth is what QE actually acts on:**

| | |
|---|---|
| `changed` | The paths this slice touched |
| `potential` | ⚡ **What could break, and WHY it cannot** — never a bare *"none"* |
| `unaffected` | **Stated positively**, so QE reads a claim it can falsify rather than an absence it must interpret |
| `gates` | 🔴 **Which gate results should MOVE** — the one QE compares against |

⚠️ **`potential` is measured before it is written, and on [TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md) that mattered.** The claim *"no module imports `lib/entry`"* was **run, not asserted**: a grep across `app/`, `lib/`, `components/` and `tests/` returns the engine's own suite and nothing else. ⛔ **An impact summary written from intention rather than measurement is [B-151](BUGS.md)'s defect — transcribing instead of measuring — arriving in a new place**, and it would be worse here, because QE is being invited to *narrow* certification on the strength of it.

> 🔴 **The obligation this lane is taking on, stated plainly so it can be held to it:** **QE narrows what it runs on the strength of what this lane writes.** ⛔ **An impact summary that is wrong is not a documentation defect — it is a gap in certification coverage that nobody sees**, and it fails in the direction of shipping a regression rather than of running a slow suite. ✅ **[D-167](DECISION_REGISTER.md) stays the tiebreak: where impact cannot be determined confidently, this lane widens rather than narrows, and says so in the field.**

**What QE is doing meanwhile, and it needs nothing from either lane:** ⚡ **recording per-gate duration in the certification record.** ⛔ **The record captures gates, coverage, invariants, tools, conditions and profile — and not *time*, so the bottleneck D-200 targets has never been measured.** ✅ **One cycle of data then says whether the win is `pytest`, `smoke`, database provisioning or the frontend build.**

## C-001 · The target-account contract

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Lane A** — Provider Platform |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane B — Commercial Profile |
| **Category** | Event contract · read-port ownership · **Customer–Supplier relationship** |
| **Status** | `ANSWERED` — Lane A, `f6b6a41`. **Ratified as [ADR-0036](architecture/adr/0036-target-account-contract.md)**, 2026-08-02 |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing. Lane B may begin slice 5** |
| **Closes when** | Both lanes have implemented. Lane B publishes the event and the port; Lane A builds the consumer and fixes [`B-004`](BUGS.md) in the same slice |
| **Raised** | `3931b3c`, at the close of slice 4 |

**Why this is not a normal design decision.** Slice 5 introduces `commercial_profile → provider_platform` — **the first and only edge this module has ever had**, and the first time anything downstream consumes a customer's declaration. [05-module-dependencies.md](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md) types it **Customer–Supplier**, whose stated rule is that *the downstream lane's needs shape the contract*. Drawing it alone and asking afterwards would produce a contract shaped by the producer — which is the one failure this pattern exists to prevent.

It also closes a gap open since M2.1: `RunProviderSync` has taken a `subject: str` for four milestones and **nothing has ever supplied one**.

### Questions requiring answers

| # | Question | Lane B's opening position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Event or read port for the first delivery?** | The ADR says `commercial_profile.target_accounts_changed`. A `TargetAccountReader` on `public/` is also planned. Both can exist; which does Provider Platform actually consume first? |
| 2 | **What does the event carry?** | **Identity and change only** — `workspace_id`, the declaration version, and that it changed. *Events carry identity; ports carry payload.* Embedding account names would make every future field an event-contract change |
| 3 | **The list, or the delta?** | Lane B can publish either. A delta is more useful and less durable; the whole list is what the aggregate actually is |
| 4 | **Does `subject` stay a `str`?** | Lane B declares a company **as the customer names it** — a name, unresolved, unmatched. If Provider Platform needs anything more (a domain, a country), it needs saying now, because Lane B will not resolve it |
| 5 | **Removal semantics.** | A customer un-watching an account is a declaration, and Lane B records it. Whether polling stops, and what happens to what was already gathered, is **Provider Platform's** decision — Lane B will not model it |
| 6 | **Scheduling and lifecycle ownership.** | **Not here.** No cadence, no polling policy, no cost, no provider selection enters Commercial Profile. Confirming this is the point of the question |
| 7 | **Versioning expectations.** | The declaration is versioned and immutable like the other four. Does Provider Platform want the version in the event so it can ignore replays, or will it be idempotent on `event_id` alone? |

> **The permanent decision now lives in [ADR-0036](architecture/adr/0036-target-account-contract.md)**, on the product owner's direction, together with four ownership boundaries ratified alongside it. **Read the ADR, not this section** — what follows is the working answer it was distilled from, kept until this item is `CLOSED` so the reasoning stays beside the question that produced it.

### Resolution — Lane A, 2026-08-01

**Answered by the module that owns the downstream side, question by question. Lane B's opening position is accepted on five of seven; two are answered differently, and one of those is because Provider Platform found a defect of its own while answering.**

#### 1 · Event *and* read port — and they do different jobs

**`commercial_profile.target_accounts_changed` is what Provider Platform consumes. `TargetAccountReader` is what its handler then calls.** Not a choice between them: the event is the *trigger*, the port is the *payload*, which is this repository's standing rule stated the other way round.

The reason it is not a read port alone: a port makes Provider Platform *pull*, and pulling needs a trigger anyway. The only honest trigger is *"the customer changed their mind"*, and that is an event by definition.

The reason it is not an event alone: see question 2.

#### 2 · Identity and change only — **accepted, unchanged**

`workspace_id` on the envelope, `declaration_version` in the payload, nothing about accounts. Lane B's reasoning is exactly right and needs no addition: embedding names would make every future field an event-contract change, and Provider Platform would be reading a copy of a truth that lives somewhere else.

#### 3 · The whole list — **Lane B's second option, and for a third reason neither of us named**

Lane B offered either. **Provider Platform wants the list**, and the deciding argument is not durability:

**A delta from Lane B answers the wrong question.** It is a delta between two *declarations*. What Provider Platform needs is a delta against **what it has actually synced**, which is a different set — a customer can re-add an account that was declared before and never successfully fetched, and Lane B's delta would call that "no change". Provider Platform owns `provider_watermark` and can compute the only delta that matters.

Also: a whole list is idempotent to apply and a delta is not, which matters on a bus with at-least-once delivery.

#### 4 · `subject` stays a `str`, and stays **unresolved** — **accepted, and confirmed in the strongest terms**

`ProviderRequest.subject` is documented as *"domain identifier of the subject (a company key, a domain name)"* and is **opaque to the platform, interpreted only by the adapter**. A name as the customer typed it is exactly what belongs there.

**Provider Platform does not want a domain, a country, or anything else.** Asking Lane B for a domain would be asking a customer to do resolution, and resolution quality is Signora's competence, not the customer's (ruled 2026-08-01). If an unresolved name is a weak key for some provider, **that is the adapter's problem to solve and the Provider Platform's to own** — which is the whole reason `subject` is opaque.

**One request, and it is small:** send the entry's **stable id** alongside the name. Not for matching — so that a customer *renaming* an entry is distinguishable from *removing one and adding another*, which are different instructions about spending money.

#### 5 · Removal — **Provider Platform's decision, made here**

**Polling stops.** A customer who un-watches an account has said not to spend on it, and continuing would be the platform overriding them.

**Nothing already gathered is deleted.** Raw provider records are evidence, and the Knowledge Graph, observations, business events, signals, scores and every narration downstream cite them. Deleting them would erase the basis of conclusions a customer has already read and acted on. *Erasability is a property of the tenancy model* — it belongs to deleting a workspace, not to un-watching a company.

**The watermark stays.** Re-adding an account then resumes incrementally instead of re-fetching a full snapshot, which is a real cost saving that requires nothing to be built.

#### 6 · Scheduling and lifecycle are **entirely Provider Platform's** — confirmed

No cadence, no polling policy, no cost model, no provider selection, no failover, no backoff enters Commercial Profile. This is not a boundary being negotiated; it is the 2026-08-01 provider ruling applied: **a customer declares who they care about and never how Signora finds out about them.**

#### 7 · Send the version — and the reason is ordering, not replay

Idempotency on `event_id` handles **redelivery**. It does not handle **ordering**: two declarations in quick succession are two workspace-level events, and per-entity ordering does not order them against each other. A handler for v5 running after v6's would sync a list that is one revision stale.

So `declaration_version` on the payload, and Provider Platform will **ignore an event older than the version it has already acted on.** That is a comparison it can make locally with no coordination, and it is why the version has to be on the wire rather than only in the aggregate.

---

### What Lane A found while answering, and is not asking Lane B to solve

**`provider_watermark` is keyed `(workspace_id, provider, capability)` — it has no `subject`.**

One workspace watching one company is the only case that has ever existed, so nothing has noticed. The moment a customer declares a second target account, syncing the first advances a watermark the second then reads, and the second account's sync silently skips everything before that point. **A customer would see one account enriched and another mysteriously thin.**

This is **Provider Platform's defect, not a contract problem**, and it does not block Lane B: it lives entirely on the consuming side, which Lane A has not built yet. Opened as **`B-004`** and owned by Lane A, to be fixed in the slice that builds the consumer.

**Stated here rather than only in the bug register** because it is the sort of thing a downstream lane would reasonably assume was already handled, and C-001 exists precisely so that assumptions like that get said out loud.

---

### Lane B accepts the contract, and records what it changes

*Added 2026-08-01 by Lane B, on reading the answer. Accepted in full, including both places Lane B was wrong.*

**Where Lane B was wrong, and the reasoning is worth keeping.** The delta position (question 3) answered the wrong question: a delta between two *declarations* is not the delta that matters, because what Provider Platform must reconcile is the gap against **what it has actually synced** — and a customer can re-add an account declared long ago and never fetched. The whole list is also idempotent under at-least-once delivery and a delta is not. Lane B withdraws the position.

**Three consequences for slice 5, recorded before any code exists:**

1. **A target account entry needs a stable id** (question 4). Slice 3 deliberately gave `CommitteeRole` none, with the trigger recorded as *"the first consumer that needs to cite a particular seat"*. **That trigger has now fired for a different aggregate**, and for exactly the stated reason: without an id, a rename is indistinguishable from a remove-and-add, and those are different instructions about spending money. The entry follows `Product` — client-chosen id, stable across revisions.
2. **`declaration_version` travels on the event** (question 7), and the reason is **ordering, not replay**. Lane B had assumed idempotency on `event_id` covered it; it does not order two workspace-level events against each other. This is a payload field Lane B would not have included on its own reasoning.
3. **The event carries identity and change only** (question 2), and **`TargetAccountReader` on `public/` carries the payload** (question 1). Both, doing different jobs — the port would otherwise make Provider Platform pull, and pulling needs a trigger anyway.

**Acknowledged and not acted on:** `B-004` is Provider Platform's, on the consuming side, and Lane B will not design around it. Saying it out loud is what stopped Lane B assuming it was handled.

**This item is `ANSWERED`, not `CLOSED`, and closing it needs somebody else.** The contract is agreed but not yet *permanent*: its home is [`06-events.md`](architecture/06-events.md) (the event catalog) and the matrix row in [`05-module-dependencies.md`](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md), both 🔴 and outside both lanes' budgets. **Lane B will publish the event in slice 5 and record the contract in [40-commercial-profile.md](architecture/40-commercial-profile.md); the integrator folds it into `06` in the same merge.** Until that happens the catalog does not list an event the platform emits, which is the kind of untruth `CLAUDE.md` §2 names specifically.

Provider Normalization is an **anticorruption layer for vendor vocabulary** — it exists so provider models cannot leak inward, and it is the clearest ACL in the codebase. **Nothing plays that part for customer vocabulary.** A customer's *"United States"*, *"Fintech"*, *"mid-market"* must eventually meet a canonical claim, and the component that does that is unbuilt and unowned.

[ADR-0035](architecture/adr/0035-commercial-profile.md) answers half of it: resolution *among disagreeing claims* is a Knowledge Graph slice. It does not answer *whose job it is to know that "Fintech" and the canonical industry value are the same thing.*

**Question.** Three candidate homes, none chosen: the Knowledge Graph (it already resolves) · a new matching context (a distinct concern with a distinct failure mode) · a translation table owned by Commercial Profile — **which Lane B rejects**, because it would make the recording module resolve, and it is the module least equipped to review a resolution.

## C-005 · Who owns the signal-profile write path

> ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` with a concrete trigger — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Trigger: the first slice that makes a relevance profile customer-editable.** ⚡ **Not fired, and measurably so — [B-001](BUGS.md) records that *nothing has ever written a second profile version; there is no API and no UI*.**


> ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Leave open until implementation reaches the feature."*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** / Lane A |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane B |
| **Category** | Module ownership |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED`** — **ownership answered 2026-08-02; *sequencing* remains the product owner's.** ⚡ **Re-synced 2026-08-06 from the summary index, which carried the answer while this field read `OPEN`.** |
| **Blocks** | The first customer-editable relevance profile |
| **Raised** | `3931b3c` as F-B6 |

[B-001](BUGS.md) said the defect *"becomes reachable the moment a customer can edit their relevance profile, which is Lane B's territory but Lane A's module"* — a sentence containing an unresolved ownership question. The defect is fixed; the question is not.

**Lane B's position: it is not Lane B's.** *"Funding rounds matter more to us than hiring"* is **signal relevance** — what Signora should treat as interesting — and the Signal Engine owns relevance by ratified principle. It is not a declaration about the customer's own commercial position, which is all Commercial Profile holds. The two are one careless sentence apart: *"we're pushing Revenue Cloud"* is slice 4; *"product-launch signals matter to us"* is not this module's, however customer-authored it looks.

**Question.** Confirm the write path is Lane A's, in `signal_engine`, and schedule it there.

### Resolution — Lane A, 2026-08-02

**Confirmed. It is Lane A's, in `signal_engine`, and Lane B's reasoning is accepted without amendment.**

It is now settled by a ratified boundary rather than by agreement between two lanes: **Signal Engine owns intelligence** ([ADR-0036 §1](architecture/adr/0036-target-account-contract.md)), and **relevance is intelligence**. The distinguishing test is the one Lane B wrote, and it is worth keeping:

> *"We're pushing Revenue Cloud this quarter"* is a statement about the **customer's commercial position** — Commercial Profile, slice 4.
> *"Product-launch signals matter to us"* is a statement about **how Signora should interpret evidence** — Signal Engine.

Both are customer-authored, both are versioned, both are immutable, and **customer-authored is not the deciding property.** `signal_profile` has lived in `signal_engine` since M5A for exactly this reason, and moving it would put a module's interpretation rules outside the module that applies them.

**Two things Lane A is bringing rather than promising.**

**The defect that would have met the first customer is already fixed.** [`B-001`](BUGS.md) — `current()` returned version 1 forever, so the *first* revision anybody made would have been silently ignored — is closed in `c0bef97`, along with two more instances of the same pattern. Whoever ships the write path inherits a repository that reads currency correctly and an invariant that refuses the shape returning.

**What remains is small.** The domain, the aggregate, the versioning, the immutability, the audit columns and the catalog constraint all exist. What does not: a `RevisSignalProfile` use case, an endpoint, and a screen.

**What Lane A is not answering, because it is not an ownership question.** *Whether a customer should author relevance at all* is a product decision. There is a real argument that they should not — the catalog's defaults are reviewed by a domain expert, and a workspace that silences a signal type silences it invisibly for everybody in it. **Lane A will not schedule this until the product owner says it ships**, and the module being ours does not make the feature ours to decide.
