Qualified, not renamed | **Nothing.** ⚡ `matching.py` → `evaluation.py` is Lane B's 🟢 |

### What the audit is asserting, precisely

**That each item is blocked on a *decision nobody has made*, not on work nobody has done.** That is the `CLAUDE.md` §20e test for an architectural blocker, and it is why none of these resumes automatically: there is no dependency to satisfy, only a ruling to make.

**Each unblock condition is one explicit sentence**, and they are deliberately short:

| Item | The sentence that unblocks it |
|---|---|
| **C-021** | *"Dispatch works like route A"* — or B |
| **C-024** | *"Identity resolution lives here, scoped like this"* |
| **C-025** | *"The catalog carries names and nothing else"* — or *"no prose that duplicates the validation surface"* |
| **C-026** | *"The supported viewport is X"* |
| **C-008** | *"Sellers see the commercial profile"* — or not — *"and it lives here"* |

**Four of the five are one sentence away from executable work that is already designed**, and two of them (C-025, C-008) have implementations either written or scoped. **The cost of leaving them open is not idle capacity — Lane A has moved on — it is that the work stays undone while the reasoning behind it is still fresh.**

### Owners re-confirmed

**Checked rather than assumed**, because an item routed to the wrong owner waits exactly as long as one nobody read.

| Item | Owner | Correct because |
|---|---|---|
| **C-021** | Product owner | `apps/worker/` has no assignable lane ([C-010](#c-010--no-lane-is-assignable-to-apps-or-signora_platform-and-a-defect-is-sitting-in-one)), and route B needs `06-events.md` — 🔴 |
| **C-024** | Product owner | A new cross-tier surface with a privacy property. **Not QE's**: nothing is wrong, something is absent |
| **C-025** | Product owner, with `signal_engine`'s assignee | A public API response shape whose omission is documented as deliberate. `signal_engine` questions already route this way ([C-005](#c-005--who-owns-the-signal-profile-write-path)) |
| **C-026** | Product owner | Product scope. **No engineering answer exists** — which devices a seller uses is a customer fact |
| **C-008** | Product owner + QE | The decision is the product owner's; the frozen file (§20c) is QE's to change once a direction exists. **Lane B raised it and Lane B is not the owner** |

### One finding the audit produced, which is not a coordination item

**Three collisions, not two — `C-024`, `C-025` and `B-019`.** Lane B's `C-024`/`C-025` are *Timeline has a surface and nowhere to mount it* and *M13 is not a module*; Lane A's are the two above. **And [`BUGS.md`](BUGS.md) now holds two `B-019`s** — *the constitution's branch table says two different things about `integration`* and Lane A's *below 768px the product has no navigation at all*, found while writing [43-customer-experience.md](architecture/43-customer-experience.md). **This is the same defect `B-024` exposed**, and QE's identifier-block rule (`CLAUDE.md`, 2026-08-02) now prevents it for future allocations — Lane A allocates from `200+` from here on, starting with [C-200](#c-200--m14b-is-three-concerns-in-one-roadmap-row-and-none-of-them-has-a-module) and `B-200`.

**It is deliberately not raised as an item.** Nothing is blocked by it, and renumbering an existing identifier is **QE's at merge, only to break a tie, decided by author timestamp** — exactly as the rule states. **Recorded here so QE finds it rather than discovers it**, and so a reader who meets two `C-024`s in the register knows why.

**A gap the block rule does not cover, stated once and not acted on:** the rule enumerates `B-`, `C-`, `TASK-` and ADR numbers. **Numbered architecture documents are allocated the same way by the same actors** — `40` came from Lane B, `41` and `42` from Lane A — and two lanes writing a module design doc in the same week would collide identically, with git merging both happily. **Not opened as an item**, because nothing is blocked and governance evolves on evidence rather than on possibility (`CLAUDE.md` §20e); recorded for whoever next touches the rule.

## C-200 · M14b is three concerns in one roadmap row, and none of them has a module

> ✅ **`CLOSED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Previous deferral confirmed."* [D-029](DECISION_REGISTER.md) stands; [TASK-906](BACKLOG.md) stays `WAITING` on *implementation naturally reaching M14b*.

> **First identifier from Lane A's allocated block (`200+`), per `CLAUDE.md`'s identifier-block rule ratified 2026-08-02.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — a new bounded context is 🔴 and needs an ADR |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Bounded context · module boundary · milestone scope |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner |
| **Kind** | **Architectural blocker** (`CLAUDE.md` §20e). No accepted architecture exists for the next step |
| **Blocks** | **The whole of M14b.** Every candidate first slice decides the boundary by implementing it |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, at the close of the M14b domain discovery — [42-billing-and-entitlements.md](architecture/42-billing-and-entitlements.md) |

### The problem

**M14b is *"Billing, analytics, feature flags"*, `~3–4 ew`, position 19 — two table rows in [IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md](../IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md) and nothing else.** No scope section, no demo scenario, no acceptance criteria, no task ids, no entry condition. Every other milestone in that document has all of them.

**And the roadmap's own justification for splitting M14 asserts something [04-modules.md](architecture/04-modules.md) does not contain:** *"each has its own bounded context, so splitting is more honest than a combined milestone."* **There is no such module.** Thirteen core modules plus Workspace & Tenancy, and none of them owns a plan, an entitlement, a limit or a price.

**Meanwhile [04-modules.md](architecture/04-modules.md) tells Workspace & Tenancy it does *not* own billing state**, while [ADR-0016](architecture/adr/0016-billing.md) says it *"tracks subscription/plan state as a reference to Stripe's subscription object."* **Both readings are defensible. Nobody has chosen.**

### Affected modules

| | How |
|---|---|
| **Workspace & Tenancy** | The candidate home under one reading, and explicitly excluded under another. **Its `Workspace` has no lifecycle, no settings and no state today** — only `create` — so there is nothing to hang a plan on either way |
| **AI Platform** | Owns `ai_inference`, which is **already half of usage-based billing**: per-workspace tokens, latency, retries and outcome on every call since M8, with **no currency column by design** (AC-72). Billing would read it through a port and must not add money to it |
| **`signora_platform/`** | All three ADRs place their adapter in `backend/platform/bought_infra_adapters/`, **which has never existed** and cannot now be created (§20a). **The third instance** of the pattern §6 records as *learned twice* with the Provider Port and the AI Provider Port |
| **Every module** | If the plan lands on the tenancy root, **every module that imports the substrate inherits commercial vocabulary** |

### Alternatives

| | What it is | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A — a new bounded context** *(recommended)* | One module owning plan, entitlement, allowance, limit and the Stripe adapter. Flags and analytics stay **bought infrastructure at the edge**, not module members | ✅ Passes every bounded-context test: its own invariants, its own language, an independent lifecycle. ✅ Keeps commercial vocabulary out of the substrate. ❌ **A fifteenth module and a dependency-graph edge — 🔴, needs an ADR** |
| **B — Workspace & Tenancy absorbs it** | Plan becomes workspace state; ADR-0016's *"tracks a reference"* read literally | ✅ No new module. ❌ **Gives the tenancy root a commercial vocabulary that every module imports** — the substrate-erosion failure §2 names by name. ❌ Forces a payment-processor webhook into the same aggregate as adding a colleague. ❌ Contradicts [04-modules.md](architecture/04-modules.md) as written |
| **C — split M14b into three milestones** | Billing (a module), analytics (an edge integration), flags (an edge integration) | ✅ **Most honest about what these actually are** — one is a domain and two are SDKs. ✅ Each ships independently. ❌ A roadmap change, and the estimate was written for one |
| **D — defer M14b entirely** | It is *"not required"* for the simulator and nothing depends on it | ✅ Legitimate: no customer is being billed today. ❌ **[R-01](architecture/16-architecture-risks.md) is High/High and has been waiting for exactly this** — it names a pricing table, a budget owner and an excess policy as its three prerequisites, all three M14b's |

### Recommendation

**A, with C's honesty about the other two.** One module — name is the product owner's — owning **billing and entitlements**. **Flagsmith and PostHog are adopted as bought infrastructure at the edge and are not part of it.**

**The reasoning that decided it, in one line:** *a feature flag answers "is this switched on?", an entitlement answers "is this customer allowed?"* — and **implementing the second as the first would put a customer's commercial rights in a vendor console with no RLS, no `workspace_id` and no audit trail.** That makes *"who changed our plan?"* unanswerable, which is one of the questions the product owner named.

**Full reasoning, the least-powerful-author mapping, the customer-question mapping and the several-years-ahead test are in [42-billing-and-entitlements.md](architecture/42-billing-and-entitlements.md).** Not restated here (§2).

### Trade-offs of the recommendation, stated plainly

| | |
|---|---|
| **Costs a fifteenth module** | The architecture has held at fourteen deliberately. This is a real addition and should be resisted unless the tests pass — **they do**, and they are written out rather than asserted |
| **Costs three new dependencies** | Stripe, PostHog, Flagsmith — all three **already authorised** by accepted ADRs, so this is adoption rather than a new choice |
| **Leaves one thing unabsorbed, deliberately** | **Enterprise contracts, organization-level billing, resellers and partner licensing all need a billing entity *above* the workspace**, which does not exist anywhere in the architecture. Addable later, but a boundary change rather than an absorption. **Said out loud rather than glossed** |
| **Does not settle M15** | M15 already claims *spend governance*. Whether the ceiling is M14b's or M15's needs a sentence either way |

### Implementation impact

| | |
|---|---|
| **Already built and reusable whatever is decided** | `ai_inference` — per-workspace usage, RLS-enforced, no currency, since M8. **The measurement half of usage billing exists and is correct** |
| **If A** | A module, a `plan` table with its `tenancy_policy.py` registration, a Stripe adapter in the owning module, derived entitlements, a plan-change record, and a settings surface. **~3–4 ew is plausible for the plan-and-entitlement half; it does not include analytics or flags** |
| **If B** | Reverses a ratified line in [04-modules.md](architecture/04-modules.md) and reshapes the tenancy root |
| **If C** | The billing half proceeds as A; the two integrations become their own small milestones |
| **If D** | Nothing is built and **R-01 stays unmitigated at High/High**, which should be an explicit acceptance rather than a side effect |
| **Cost of waiting** | **Lane A has moved on and is not idle** — this blocks the milestone, not the lane. What it costs is that the discovery is fresh now and will need re-reading later |

### One decision that is not a lane's and is not asked for here

**What Signora charges for.** The architecture above is deliberately indifferent to it — seats, usage, tiers and hybrids are all the same shape — and this lane has no standing to propose a pricing model.

## C-201 · Identifier allocation is still only *unlikely* to collide

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). The prefixed strategy is adopted.** ***"Repository growth should remove collision risk completely rather than reducing it probabilistically."*** **Future allocations follow `B-A12` · `C-B03` · `TASK-A07`.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **QE** (the rules and the tooling) + **product owner** (ratification) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Repository governance · identifier allocation |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). **The prefixed strategy is adopted.** ⚡ **Corrected 2026-08-06: this row still read as pending while the ruling above had been taken.** **`decision-queue.py --check` would have escalated a settled question — the failure its own docstring calls *the most misleading*, because it costs the product owner attention on something already decided.** |
| **Blocks** | Nothing being implemented. **It blocks the repository from scaling past three actors without manual reconciliation** |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, after the third collision |

**The product owner's bar, verbatim:** *"If two lanes work completely offline for a week, they should still be unable to produce conflicting identifiers."* **Not unlikely. Unable.**

### Three collisions, and the third was found by accident

| # | Ids | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `C-001`…`C-009` | Two lanes on separate baselines, reconciled by QE at merge |
| 2 | `B-024` | Two lanes, seven minutes apart. **Neither push conflicted** — different regions of one file, git merged them happily |
| 3 | **`C-024` · `C-025` · `B-019`** | Lane A and Lane B, independently. **Found while writing an unrelated document**, which is the part that matters: nothing reported it |

**Nothing was careless in any of the three.** Every lane read the register, saw the highest number, and took the next one. **The allocation model is the defect**, which QE already concluded — and the block rule that followed is a real improvement that does not yet reach the stated bar.

### Where blocks still leave a collision possible

**Not hypothetical objections — each is reachable from today's rules as written.**

| # | Hole | Why it is open |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Numbered architecture documents are not covered** | The rule enumerates `B-`, `C-`, `TASK-` and ADR. **`40` came from Lane B; `41`, `42`, `43` from Lane A.** Two lanes writing a module design doc in one week produce two different filenames — **git merges both without a word**, which is defect #2 exactly |
| **2** | **A block is finite** | 100 ids per actor. Small, and *"impossible"* does not admit a bound |
| **3** | **A sixth actor has no block** | The table stops at Lane E. A new lane needs a governance edit before it may open a bug — **which reintroduces the coordination bottleneck blocks were adopted to remove** |
| **4** | **Nothing prevents; one thing detects** | `state-check.py` finds duplicates **at Closeout**, after both lanes have written, pushed and been merged. **Detection is not prevention**, and detection *after* merge is reconciliation work for QE |
| **5** | **The block must be looked up** | *"Which block am I?"* is human memory consulting a table in a 1,100-line file. **The rule replaces one act of memory with another** |

### The property that would actually close it

> **Two actors that cannot communicate can only produce disjoint identifier sets if each set is determined by something only that actor has. Offline, the one thing an actor has is its own identity.**
>
> **Therefore: every shared identifier must contain its allocator's identity. Everything else is coordination wearing a different hat.**

**Blocks satisfy this weakly** — identity is encoded *implicitly*, as a numeric range, which is why it is finite, needs a lookup, and needs a governance edit to extend. **Making the identity explicit removes all three at once.**

### Recommendation — two mechanisms, chosen by what the number is *for*

**The classes are not alike, and one rule for all of them is what produced holes 1 and 2.**

#### A · Where the number is a shared counter → **prefix it with the allocator**

`B-A12` · `C-B03` · `TASK-A07` · `ADR-A041`. Read *"bug 12, from Lane A."*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Collision** | **Impossible.** Two allocators cannot share a prefix, and **one lane is one session at a time** — an invariant `CLAUDE.md` §20e already enforces, so each namespace has exactly one writer |
| **Offline for a week** | Safe, indefinitely. Nothing is shared |
| **A new actor** | Needs **nothing**. Its letter is already allocated by [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane)'s environment table — one row, one lane, already unique |
| **Lookup** | **None.** You know which lane you are; that is the whole input |
| **Readability** | **Better than today.** `B-A12` says who found it. `B-217` says so too, but only to somebody holding the table |
| **Ordering** | Chronology was never in the number, and QE already said so: *"every row carries `Found`, and `git log` carries the rest"* |

#### B · Where the number carries no meaning → **delete it, and let the path be the identity**

**Documents `30`+ are numbered by arrival order and nothing else.** `43-customer-experience.md` is not *"after"* `42` in any sense a reader uses. **The number is a shared counter bought at the price of a collision class — and it buys nothing.**

**Drop it for that family** — `customer-experience.md`, `product-surface.md` — and **git enforces uniqueness for free**: two lanes creating one path is an add/add conflict git **cannot** auto-merge. It is the only mechanism in this list that needs no rule at all.

> **This is the repository's own proven pattern, and [ADR-0039](architecture/adr/0039-release-engineering-model.md) RC-4 already names it:** *"`docs/architecture/adr/` is one file per record, written by every lane, and has produced zero merge conflicts and zero structural corruption in 39 records."*

**`01`–`29` keep their numbers.** There the number *is* meaning — `01`–`21` is the architecture in reading order, `22`–`29` is one per module — and that family is closed rather than growing.

#### C · Migrations stay exempt, and gain a check

Alembic's `down_revision` is a linear chain: **a gap is a broken graph, not an oddity.** Renumber-on-rebase is correct and stays. **What is missing is that it is remembered rather than enforced** — three collisions, three manual renumbers, and the third was caught because `alembic upgrade head` refused.

**A check that refuses two revisions sharing a `down_revision` turns a late failure into an immediate one.** Cheap, and it is the one class where prevention genuinely cannot work.

#### D · Detection stays, as a backstop and not as the mechanism

`state-check.py` keeps its duplicate check and gains the classes it misses. **Add one assertion it cannot make today: that every id's prefix matches an actor in the registry** — which catches a typo inside a namespace, the only failure A leaves.

### Trade-offs, stated rather than glossed

| | |
|---|---|
| **A rename touches every reference** | ~19 `TASK-`, ~30 `C-`, ~30 `B-`, 39 ADRs, and hundreds of links. **The real cost, and it grows every day this waits** |
| **`ADR-A041` breaks a near-universal convention** | ADR numbering is a recognised idiom. **A block may genuinely be the better answer for ADRs alone** — they are rare, and QE could hold the only pen |
| **Existing ids should not be rewritten** | They are cited in commit messages, which are immutable. **Prefix new ids; leave promoted ones alone** — the register carries both forms, which is ugly and honest |
| **B changes filenames referenced by ~848 links** | [`REPOSITORY_ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md`](REPOSITORY_ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSAL.md) measured them, and its finding #1 is that **nothing verifies a link resolves.** B should not ship before that check does |

### Implementation impact

| | |
|---|---|
| **Governance** | `CLAUDE.md`'s identifier section is replaced. **QE's and the product owner's** — this lane does not edit it ([C-022](#c-022--governance-belongs-to-qe-and-the-product-owner--and-this-branch-carries-governance-edits)), which is why this is a proposal with the reasoning attached rather than a diff |
| **Tooling** | `state-check.py` — three checks: duplicate ids per class · prefix resolves to a known actor · no two migrations share a `down_revision`. **QE's file** |
| **Migration** | Prefix new ids from ratification. **Do not rewrite history** |
| **Cost of waiting** | Every cycle, QE reconciles by hand. **Three collisions in two days with three actors**; the rate is quadratic in actors, and lanes C, D and E are already reserved |

### What this confirms rather than discovers

**[ADR-0039](architecture/adr/0039-release-engineering-model.md) RC-4 already diagnosed this**, and listed *"id collisions requiring QE to renumber `B-` and `C-` rows at merge"* as one of three symptoms of one cause. **That ADR is deliberately `Proposed` and waiting on an evidence bar:** an *observed*, *repeated* bottleneck.

> **Three collisions in two days, the third found only by accident, is that bar being met.** The first question `CLAUDE.md` §20e asks is whether the north star already contains the answer **before a new one is invented** — and for the register's structure it does. **This item adds the half ADR-0039 does not solve:** one file per record removes structural corruption and rebase loss, and **leaves id collision exactly where it was**, because two differently-named files never conflict.

## C-206 · Is an invitation Better Auth's or Signora's?

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"**Invitation lifecycle belongs to Signora.** Authentication proves identity. **Workspace membership, invitations and tenancy belong to Signora.**"* **[TASK-904](BACKLOG.md) is unblocked.** §13 stands — auth is bought; **tenancy is not auth.**

> **Was `C-202b` for part of one cycle.** QE renumbered Lane A's earlier items to `C-203`–`C-205` at merge while this was being written, so it takes the next free number in Lane A's block. **Cited nowhere else at the time of renaming.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — a new vendor capability, and an amendment to [ADR-0010](architecture/adr/0010-identity-and-access.md) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Build vs buy · cross-tier boundary · authentication |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner |
| **Kind** | **Architectural blocker.** No accepted architecture exists for the next step |
| **Blocks** | **Inviting anybody.** Not the members list, which [46-team-management.md](architecture/46-team-management.md) §7 shows is now unblocked |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, at the close of Team Management discovery |

**An organization cannot grow.** `POST /members` takes a `user_id: UUID`, nothing resolves an email to a user, and every workspace is permanently whoever created it.

**Better Auth's `organization` plugin is installed and unused**, and it ships the whole domain — invitations, expiry, limits, membership. **`CLAUDE.md` §13 says auth is bought and never built**, so using it is the default answer and needs saying out loud rather than assumed.

### Why it is not simply "use the plugin"

| | |
|---|---|
| Migration `0005` revokes `signora_app` from the `auth` schema | **Membership in the plugin's tables is membership the Python tier cannot read** |
| §13 requires membership re-verified server-side on every request | **That check reads `membership`.** Moving it out of reach breaks the tenancy model at its root |
| RLS enforces tenancy on application tables | A vendor's organization table cannot participate |

### The options, and the recommendation

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Enable the plugin and own membership there | ❌ **Rejected on evidence.** Breaks server-side verification and the RLS root — a tenancy-model change, not a build-vs-buy trade |
| **B** | Build invitations in `workspace_tenancy` | Keeps one owner for membership, no cross-tier work. ⚠️ **An invitation is addressed to an email that may not be a user, which is identity**, and §13 forbids building that |
| **C** | **Split at acceptance — recommended.** Better Auth owns the invitation; Signora owns the membership it creates when somebody accepts | **The boundary the repository already draws.** Signora writes no token minting, no expiry, no email-ownership proof and no delivery — the four security-sensitive, entirely commodity parts |

**Costs of C, stated:** enabling a plugin is a **new vendor capability** needing an ADR amendment, and acceptance becomes a two-tier operation whose failure modes must be designed rather than discovered.

### Implementation impact

| | |
|---|---|
| **Unblocked either way** | **The members list.** It needs nothing from this item — see the C-024 narrowing below |
| **If C** | Enable the plugin, design acceptance, add a membership write path from it |
| **If B** | An `invitation` table with its `tenancy_policy.py` registration, expiry, revocation, delivery, and an email-ownership proof Signora would be writing itself |
| **Cost of waiting** | **Every workspace stays a single person.** [J10](architecture/43-customer-experience.md) cannot open |

### Narrowed sharply — 2026-08-02, and the recommendation above is withdrawn

**Challenged on the product owner's direction, and option C was inconsistent with this item's own reasoning.** §6 rejected option A because the `auth` schema is unreadable by `signora_app` — *the Python tier cannot verify what it cannot read* — and then recommended putting the **invitation** there, which is equally workspace-scoped, equally audit-relevant and equally in need of RLS.

**An invitation is two facts with two owners:**

| The fact | Owner |
|---|---|
| *"This address belongs to the person holding it"* | **Better Auth** — and it already does this |
| *"Ana invited this address into this workspace, as a member, on this date"* | **Signora.** Workspace-scoped business intent, and the row that supplies the address [C-203](#c-203--nothing-in-the-product-can-render-a-persons-name)'s narrowing needs |

**And the proof already arrives in the token. Measured:**

| | |
|---|---|
| `frontend/lib/auth/jwt.ts` | Every access token carries **`email`** and **`email_verified`** |
| `backend/signora_platform/auth/jwt_verifier.py:36-37` | Both are **required claims**; `email_verified` is type-checked |
| `frontend/lib/auth/server.ts:58` | **`requireEmailVerification: true`** |

> **The Python tier already knows, on every request, a verified address the caller has proved they own.** Accepting an invitation is matching a pending row against a claim the token already carries — **no plugin, no invitation token, no expiry in a link, no cross-tier call.**

**So the earlier recommendation is withdrawn.** Enabling the `organization` plugin would add a dependency, a schema, an ADR amendment and a two-tier acceptance path to obtain a proof the repository already has.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What remains of this item** | **Who sends one email.** The Python tier has no transport; [`lib/auth/email.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/email.ts) has one, with a two-value `purpose` union and a comment describing itself as a port *"without anticipating"* a third. **Is a third value this tier's, or is invitation delivery M14a's?** |
| **What is now unblocked** | **Everything else.** The invitation table, its lifecycle, acceptance, and — through it — the members list |
| **Severity** | Was *"inviting anybody"*. Is now **one delivery decision**, and even that has an obvious answer if M14a is far off |

**Full analysis, including the six other self-challenges, is [46-team-management.md](architecture/46-team-management.md) §11.**

**Full discovery — thirty customer questions, the stress test against the roadmap, and the two weak points — is [46-team-management.md](architecture/46-team-management.md).** Not restated here (§2).

## C-207 · Casbin cannot express an action on yourself

> ✅ **`CLOSED` by [ADR-0404](architecture/adr/0404-platform-composition.md) — product owner, 2026-08-05.** **Four items, one approval.** [435](architecture/435-platform-composition-rfc.md) was ratified whole: all four capabilities approved, **the single handler shape adopted** — *"we should not support two implementation patterns permanently"* — and the sole-owner question ruled. **[TASK-901](BACKLOG.md)'s seven slices are released.** *Nothing is implemented by the ADR; it authorises the contract.*

> ✅ **Answered by [435 · Platform composition](architecture/435-platform-composition-rfc.md)**, [TASK-900](BACKLOG.md), Lane C 2026-08-05 — **awaiting product owner approval.** **Four items, one RFC**, because deciding them separately is how the substrate drifts.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — `signora_platform/authorization/` is frozen (§20a) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Authorization model · platform freeze |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED`** — 2026-08-05, ADR-0404 |
| **Kind** | **Architectural blocker** |
| **Blocks** | **Leaving an organization**, and every self-directed operation Signora will ever have |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, implementing the first Team Management slice |

**`policies/model.conf` defines the request tuple as `(sub, dom, obj, act)`, and `sub` is *the caller's role*.** The caller's **identity is not in the tuple**.

> **So the model can say *"an owner may remove a member"* and cannot say *"anybody may remove themselves"*.**

**Found trying to build the one Team Management slice that needs neither names nor a ruling.** Leaving an organization needs no identity resolution and no invitation — and it cannot be authorized.

### Why each way round is worse than raising it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Add `Action.LEAVE`** | `Action` is in `signora_platform/authorization/enforcer.py` — **frozen.** A platform change needs an RFC, which is this item |
| **Grant `p, member, *, member, remove` and restrict to self in the handler** | **The policy would then assert that members may remove members, which is false.** The repository already carries one grant it cannot honour — `member:remove` with no endpoint — and adding a second that *overstates* is worse: the first is a missing capability, this would be a **false statement about who may do what**, in the file an auditor reads first |
| **Skip the check for this endpoint** | §7 admits no carve-out, and rightly. **The first endpoint without a policy check is the one nobody notices later** |

### It is small, structural, and will recur

**Every self-directed operation meets it:** leave an organization · change your own notification preferences (M14a) · delete your own account · manage your own connected systems. **None is buildable today**, and each will look like a five-line endpoint to whoever tries next.

### Options, with a recommendation

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Add `Action.LEAVE`**, granted to both roles | Smallest and most literal. ❌ **One new verb per self-directed operation**, and the enum grows with the product |
| **B** | **A `self` subject the enforcer resolves** — the caller's role *or* the literal `self` when the target is the caller | Expresses the concept once. ❌ **Changes the request tuple**, so every call site and the model file move together |
| **C** — *recommended* | **Rule it out of Casbin entirely.** Acting on yourself is not an authorization question: **it is a consequence of membership**, which `CurrentWorkspace` already verifies before any handler runs. Record the rule in §7 — *"an operation whose only subject is the caller requires membership and no policy tuple"* — so the absence is a stated decision rather than a gap | ✅ Adds nothing to the platform, and it is **true**: nobody needs permission to stop being somewhere. ❌ It is a **governance change to §7**, which is the product owner's |

**Lane A recommends C**, and notes it costs no code at all — it makes an existing verified fact sufficient, and says so where an auditor will look.

### Stress-tested on the product owner's direction — 2026-08-02. **It survives, with one counterexample that sharpens it**

| Operation | Self? | Where it belongs |
|---|---|---|
| **Leave a workspace** | ✅ | Membership + the last-owner invariant. **Not Casbin** |
| **Password · MFA · avatar · email · delete account** | ✅ | **Better Auth's entirely** — these never reach the Python tier |
| **Notification preferences** *(M14a)* | ✅ | Self, per workspace. **Not Casbin** |
| **API tokens** | ✅ | Self. **Not Casbin** |
| **Disconnect "my" connected system** | ❌ **The counterexample** | **It is not yours.** A connection belongs to the *organization* — `integration:update` is owner-only, and whoever connected HubSpot is not thereby entitled to disconnect it. **Casbin, correctly** |

> **The refinement it forces:** a self-operation is one whose **only subject and only object are the caller**. Connecting a system fails the second half — the object is the workspace's.
>
> **Stated as a rule:** *an operation requires no policy tuple only when the thing it changes would cease to exist if the caller did.* A membership would. A CRM connection would not.

**Worth generalising rather than solving for Team Management alone**, as the product owner proposed: it removes a Casbin entry from four future features, and the counterexample prevents the *"my"* mistake — treating something a person created as something they own.

### Implementation impact

| | |
|---|---|
| **If C** | One paragraph in §7, then the leave endpoint is ordinary work. **No migration, no platform change, no new grant** |
| **If A** | A frozen-platform change plus a `policy.csv` line, then the same endpoint |
| **If B** | A frozen-platform change touching the model file and every `authorize` call |
| **Cost of waiting** | **A person cannot leave an organization.** Small today — every workspace has one member — and permanent for every self-directed feature after it |

## C-208 · A tenant-scoped row whose only legitimate reader is outside the tenant

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Introduce an explicit **authenticated-but-not-member** state. **Do not weaken general RLS.** Provide only the **minimum read path** required for invitation acceptance."* ⚠️ `signora_platform/db/` is frozen (§20a): a named single-purpose path, never a policy change.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — it is a tenancy-model question, and `signora_platform/db/` is frozen (§20a) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Tenancy · Row-Level Security |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner |
| **Kind** | **Architectural blocker** |
| **Blocks** | **Accepting an invitation.** Nothing else in Team Management |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, planning TM-03's acceptance endpoint |

**An invitation is workspace-owned data, and the person it is addressed to is — by definition — not in the workspace yet.**

| | |
|---|---|
| `CurrentWorkspace` verifies membership before any handler runs | **It refuses the accepter, correctly.** They are not a member |
| Every RLS policy is `workspace_id = current_setting('app.workspace_id')` | [`session.py:32`](../backend/signora_platform/db/session.py) sets **one** variable, and there is **no user-scoped session setting** |

> **So the row addressed to somebody is invisible to them**, because reading it needs a workspace context that membership grants and they do not have.

**This is a new shape rather than a variant of [C-207](#c-207--casbin-cannot-express-an-action-on-yourself).** That one is about *authorizing* an action on yourself. This is about **tenant-scoped data whose legitimate reader is outside the tenant** — the first time the tenancy model has met it, and it will recur for anything a person receives before they belong.

### Options

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **A second session setting** — `app.user_email` — and an RLS policy of `workspace_id = …` **OR** `invited_email = …` | Keeps everything in Postgres, where the tenancy model is authoritative. ❌ **Changes `signora_platform/db/session.py`**, frozen, and a second variable is a second thing every unit of work must set correctly |
| **B** | **A workspace-less read path** for invitations only, executed under a role that is not `signora_app` | ❌ **A role that bypasses RLS is exactly what §8 forbids**, and the exemption would be permanent |
| **C** — *recommended* | **Acceptance never reads across tenants.** The customer names the organization they are accepting — the invitation email links to `/join/{workspace_id}` — so the workspace is supplied by the request and `app.workspace_id` can be set before the read, **exactly as it is for every other endpoint.** The row is then found by `(workspace_id, invited_email = the verified claim)` | ✅ **No platform change, no new setting, no RLS exemption, no cross-tenant read.** ⚠️ It means *"show me every invitation waiting for me"* is not offered — a customer accepts the one they were sent rather than browsing a list |

**Lane A recommends C**, and the trade-off is worth stating plainly: **the missing feature is a cross-workspace inbox**, which nothing has asked for and which would be the one screen in Signora that reads outside a tenant. **Every invitation arrives with a link; the link carries the workspace; the tenancy model never bends.**

**If C is accepted this item closes with no code beyond the endpoint**, and the recommendation is a design constraint rather than a change.

### Stress-tested, and smaller than this item claimed — 2026-08-02

**Nine acceptance scenarios, all preserving one tenant at a time:** from another logged-in workspace · logged out · logged into a different account · after switching organizations · after expiry · after revocation · after workspace deletion · after rename · after the inviter left. **All nine hold, and none reads outside a tenant.** Detail in [46-team-management.md](architecture/46-team-management.md) §15 Challenge D.

**And it needs no platform change.** `set_workspace_context` is **already a public function** in [`signora_platform/db/session.py`](../backend/signora_platform/db/session.py):69. The acceptance endpoint needs a dependency that verifies the token and sets context from the path **without requiring membership** — a new dependency **in this module's interface layer, composed from platform functions that already exist.** *Using* the platform, not changing it.

> **So what remains is one sentence, not an architecture:** *may a request establish workspace context from a path parameter when the caller is not yet a member?* Everything else follows, and option A's frozen-file change is no longer on the table.

### Implementation impact

| | |
|---|---|
| **Unblocked regardless** | **The invitation aggregate, its lifecycle, the partial unique index, inviting, listing and revoking** — all workspace-scoped, and **needing no new authorization**: inviting *is* `member:add`, revoking *is* `member:remove`, listing *is* `member:read`, and all three grants exist |
| **If C** | The accept endpoint takes the workspace in its path. **Ordinary work** |
| **If A** | A frozen-platform change to session handling, plus a second RLS clause on one table |
| **Cost of waiting** | **An invitation can be sent and not accepted.** TM-03 ships its administrator half and stops at the customer half |

## C-202 · Four shared documents disagree, and one disagrees with itself

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **QE** — every document below is QE's to write |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Shared-document governance · dashboard consistency |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED`** — 2026-08-03, by QE, re-measured rather than assumed |
| **Blocks** | Nothing being implemented. **It blocks a cold session from trusting any status in the repository** |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, during the cross-check the product owner asked for |

**The stated requirement:** *"The same work item should never appear with different states in different documents. The repository should have exactly one truth for every status."*

### Measured, at `origin/integration` — five disagreements

| # | Fact | `PROJECT_STATUS.md` says | The authoritative record says |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Lane B's assignment** | *"Lane B — `AVAILABLE`"* | [`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md): **two rows** — M7 Timeline `IN VALIDATION`, M13 Integrations `CHANGES REQUESTED` |
| **2** | **Whether anything is blocked** | *"**Nothing is blocked.**"* | The board carries **three `BLOCKED` rows** and one `CHANGES REQUESTED` |
| **3** | **Lane A's batch** | §1c: *"PS-01, PS-02, PP-01, PP-02 — **four** slices"* | §1b of the **same file**: *"Lane A's batch is now **eight** slices"* — **and then lists nine** |
| **4** | **M10** | §2: **✅ Complete 2026-07-31** | §6 of the **same file**: AI Research Engine *"🔵 **In progress** — M10"* |
| **5** | **Lane A's branch contents** | *"sits ahead with **four** finished slices"* | The branch holds **fifteen** |

**Two of the five are a document contradicting itself in the same session.** That is the strongest available evidence that the cause is structural rather than anybody's care.

### The cause, and it is one line of that file's own prose

`PROJECT_STATUS.md` §1c says it plainly:

> *"Authoritative record: `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` — the execution board. **Summarised here** because a dashboard that cannot say who is working is not a dashboard."*

**A summary of another document is a stored copy of a derivable fact**, and `CLAUDE.md` §2 already rules on those: *"truth has exactly one authoritative representation; everything else derives from it… a stored copy of a derivable fact is a defect waiting for the two to disagree."*

**It has waited two days.** [ADR-0039](architecture/adr/0039-release-engineering-model.md) RC-7 names this exactly — *"the dashboard is a stored copy of a derivable fact"* — so this is a second confirmation of the same north star from a different direction.

**And #5 is a different defect worth separating.** `PROJECT_STATUS` is *"always representing `main`"*, measured at Closeout — correct and deliberate. **But a lane branch is not `main`, and moves on a different clock.** A dashboard that describes `lane-a-product-surface` has taken on a fact it structurally cannot keep true. **The fix is not a better number; it is not carrying that fact.**

### What each shared document should state about itself

**The product owner asked for ownership, timing, section ownership, what is generated and what needs review. None of the eight shared documents states any of it today**, and a reader cannot tell a hand-maintained section from a measured one — which is exactly how #3 and #4 survive review.

**Recommendation: a five-line header on each, and nothing more elaborate.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Who writes it** | One actor. Where two do, name the sections |
| **When** | The trigger, not a cadence — *"at Closeout"*, *"when a lane claims"* |
| **Which sections are measured** | **Read from the repository, never typed.** Test counts, coverage, `HEAD`, migration head |
| **Which sections are judgement** | Written by hand and reviewed by a person |
| **What it must never contain** | **The one that would have prevented all five:** a fact whose authoritative home is another document |

### Recommendation on the specific five

| | |
|---|---|
| **§1c *Active work*** | **Delete the table; keep the link.** It restates the board and can only ever lag it. *"Who is working"* is one `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` away, and a dashboard that links is not a dashboard that cannot answer |
| **§1b *Recommended next work*** | Stop naming slice counts. **They are a lane's fact, on a lane's clock** |
| **§6 *Current AI architecture*** | Derive milestone state from §2 or drop the column. **Two states for M10 in one file is the whole finding** |
| **Branch descriptions** | **Remove.** `PROJECT_STATUS` describes `main`; a branch is not `main` |
| ***"Nothing is blocked"*** | Derive from the board, or say nothing. **A blanket claim about a multi-writer record is a claim that will be wrong within a day** |

> **Every one of the five recommendations deletes something.** That is deliberate, and it is the shape the answer takes: **the dashboard is not wrong because it is under-maintained — it is wrong because it stores facts it does not own.** A rule requiring more diligence would fail the same way in a week.

### Implementation impact

| | |
|---|---|
| **Whose** | **QE's, entirely.** All eight shared documents are QE's or the product owner's to write |
| **Cost** | Five deletions and eight five-line headers. **Smaller than one Closeout** |
| **Risk of not doing it** | A cold session reads `PROJECT_STATUS` first, and it is currently wrong about who is working, whether anything is blocked, and how much is waiting |
| **Not proposed** | A tool that generates the dashboard. **That is [ADR-0039](architecture/adr/0039-release-engineering-model.md)'s territory**, it is a much larger change, and the five deletions above are worth having whether or not it ever happens |

## C-027 · M14a Notifications — what was bought is not what must be built

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision required** | Whether Notifications is a bounded context · what Day One is · one boundary Lane B must not draw alone |
| **Participating modules** | none yet — **that is the finding** · `signora_platform` (frozen) · Revenue Intelligence Platform (not started) |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **Product owner** |
| **Blocking** | **M14a's shape.** Not its start — a first slice exists and is named below |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, by Lane B, assigned M14a. **Before any code**, as with M7 and M13 |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED`** — **four decisions taken 2026-08-02; [ADR-0040](architecture/adr/0040-notifications.md) proposed.** ⏸️ **Ratification deferred by [D-027](DECISION_REGISTER.md), and it needs a `04-modules.md` entry — see [B-401](BUGS.md), which measured that the stated count is stale.** ⛔ **Corrected 2026-08-06 — this office wrote `OPEN` here hours earlier by defaulting rather than reading.** **The summary index carried the resolution and the body did not, so a `Status` field added *safely* overwrote a real answer.** ⚡ **The safe default is only safe when the other record is also empty**, and this one was not. |

**M14a was reviewed the way M7 and M13 were. It is in a third condition, different from both.** M7 had no design. M13 had a ratified architecture that described something other than a module. **M14a has a ratified *purchase decision* that has been read as an architecture, and it is not one.**

### 1 · What exists today: nothing, and precisely nothing

`grep -ri notification` across `backend/` returns **two** hits, and neither is a notification: a comment in the outbox relay about PostgreSQL `LISTEN/NOTIFY`, and `aria-label="Dismiss notification"` on the frontend toast. There is **no module, no table, no event, no port, no type, no route and no screen.**

That is the correct starting point and it is stated so nobody assumes otherwise. What exists is a set of *assumptions*, and they are load-bearing:

| Source | What it says | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-0017](architecture/adr/0017-notifications.md) | **Novu**, for cross-channel delivery orchestration | **Accepted** |
| [02-principles.md](architecture/02-principles.md) §15 · [09-build-vs-buy.md](architecture/09-build-vs-buy.md) | Notifications are commodity. **Bought, not built** | Ratified |
| [15-project-structure.md](architecture/15-project-structure.md):39 | The Novu adapter lives in `platform/bought_infra_adapters/` | **A directory that has never existed** |
| [13-integrations.md](architecture/13-integrations.md):107 | Slack and Teams are **Novu delivery channels**, distinct from and downstream of their use as data sources | Ratified |
| [04-modules.md](architecture/04-modules.md) | Fourteen modules. **Notifications is not one of them**, and the word does not appear in the file | Ratified |

### 2 · The finding that decides the module question

> **ADR-0017 bought *delivery*. It did not decide *notification*, and the two are different concerns.**

Read what the ADR actually chose: *"templating, channel fallback, user preference management, delivery tracking."* Every one of those is **how a message reaches a person.** None of them answers:

- **should this produce a notification at all?**
- **who should be told?**
- **how urgent is it, next to the other eleven?**
- **has somebody already dealt with it?**

Those are product decisions with a customer-facing vocabulary, and no vendor can take them. **Buying a courier is not the same as deciding what to send.**

So the answer to *"module, platform capability, or part of another module?"* is **all three, split along that line** — and the split is the same shape the repository already uses twice, for providers and for AI:

```
  what happened            →  Timeline           entity-addressed, immutable, exists
  what to do about it      →  Recommendation     content, not started
  who should be told, and
  have they dealt with it  →  Notifications      person-addressed, mutable  ← M14a
  how it reaches them      →  Novu               bought, behind a port
```

**Why it is not part of Timeline**, which is the strongest rival and worth answering directly. Timeline is *immutable by design* — no `UPDATE` grant, a correction is a new entry — and **a notification is mutable by definition**: read, dismissed, snoozed. Folding one into the other destroys the defining property of the one that already ships. They are genuinely projections of the same events; they project to **different addressees with different lifecycles**, and sharing the projection would couple two things that must not be coupled.

**Why it is not part of Recommendation Engine**, which ADR-0017 names as the primary producer: a recommendation is *content*; a notification is *that somebody should be told about it*. The same distinction as delivery, one level up. Also — Recommendation Engine **is not started**, so building M14a inside it is not available in any case.

**Why the adapter does not go where 15-project-structure.md puts it.** `platform/bought_infra_adapters/` has never been built, and `CLAUDE.md` §6 already records this exact mistake happening twice: *"15-project-structure.md placed both the Provider Port and the AI Provider Port in platform packages that were never built, and the implementation put each in its owning module both times."* **This would be the third.** The port belongs to the module that owns the language; `signora_platform/` is frozen (§20a) and a notification port is not platform vocabulary.

### 3 · The design rule this produced, and it is the valuable one

> **"Needs attention" is derived. "Something happened, and have you seen it" is stored. Conflating them is the error M14a is most likely to make**, because a product surface shows them in the same place.

They are two of the repository's already-ratified data categories, and the boundary is exactly where it always is:

| | Derived intelligence | Workflow state |
|---|---|---|
| **Example** | *"This credential expires in two days"* · *"this score is contested"* · *"this opportunity has not moved in three weeks"* | *"Your credential expired — seen · dismissed · snoozed"* |
| **Rebuildable?** | Yes, from current state | **No.** Nothing reproduces whether a person looked at something |
| **Stored?** | **Never.** A stored copy is stale the moment the world moves | Always |

**A concrete rule follows, and it prevents the commonest failure in the stress list:** *a notification is generated from an **event**, never from a **state**.* Generating one by scanning state produces it again tomorrow, and again the day after — and **the need for "duplicate suppression" is the symptom, not the requirement.** Idempotency on `event_id` handles genuine redelivery; needing *semantic* deduplication means it was modelled from state. This is the least-powerful-author rule reaching notifications: the attention list is computed, and only the *fact that a person was told* is written down.

**A second rule from the same place: a notification holds a reference, never a copy.** *"Your HubSpot credential expired"* must read as resolved once it has been reconnected. A notification carrying a snapshot of the thing it is about becomes a lie the moment the thing changes — and *"notification expiration"* in the stress list is that problem wearing a different name.

### 4 · The stress test, and what it moves out of scope

Run against the scenarios the product owner named. **Most of them belong to the vendor, and saying so is the point of buying one:**

| Ours | Novu's |
|---|---|
| Whether a notification exists · who receives it · urgency · read, dismissed, snoozed · what it references | Retries · delivery failure · delayed delivery · quiet hours · digest and batch scheduling · multi-channel fan-out · templating · channel fallback |

**Preferences are split, and the split is not obvious.** *"Which kinds of thing do I want to hear about"* is product vocabulary and ours; *"by which channel, at which times"* is delivery and Novu's. A design that put both in one place would either duplicate Novu's preference model or make our own depend on it.

**Thousands of notifications** is the one scale question with a real answer needed on day one: **one row per recipient, not one row plus N read-states.** Preferences and channels differ per person, and a shared row with a read-state table is the same thing with worse queries and a harder tenancy story. A workspace-wide event across fifty members is fifty rows, which is what every product of this kind does.

**Escalation and audit** are out of Day One and named so they are not rediscovered: escalation needs an ownership model the repository does not have, and delivery attempts are operational history under [ADR-0029](architecture/adr/0029-operational-history-durability.md) rather than a new category.

### 5 · The one thing that constrains the build, and it is not a blocker

**M14a is by construction an event consumer** — it has no other input. So [C-012](#c-012--eventhandler-receives-no-session-so-no-module-handler-is-registered) is directly in its path, and it has been `WAITING` since M3A.

**It does not stop M14a, and Lane B will not report it as though it does.** The deployed worker registers exactly one subscription — `ai_research.requested`, AI Research Engine consuming its own event — and it works by holding a session factory on the worker runtime rather than by taking the dispatcher's session. **A notification handler can be built the same way and made idempotent on `event_id` by construction**, deriving its own identity from the envelope exactly as Timeline's projection does with `uuid5`, so it never needs the dispatcher's ledger.

What C-012 genuinely costs is **the shape of the handler, not its existence** — and that is worth stating rather than treating as a reason to wait.

### 6 · The boundary Lane B must not draw alone

**[37-product-surface.md](architecture/37-product-surface.md):224 puts the attention list — journey J1, *"which accounts deserve my attention today?"* — inside Revenue Intelligence Platform**, and records a live defect in it: the list names accounts by truncated identifier because no module in the ratified graph reaches both workflow and entity names.

**That is the derived half of §3, and it already has an owner.** Lane B will not claim it. But the question has to be answered before either module builds it, because two lanes independently deriving *"what needs attention"* is precisely the duplicated truth the register exists to prevent:

> **Does the attention list belong to Revenue Intelligence Platform, or is it Notifications' derived half with RIP as a consumer?**

Lane B has no position it would defend. RIP's claim is older and J1 is written against it; Notifications' claim is that *"what needs attention"* and *"what have you been told about"* are one customer question answered in two halves, and splitting them across modules means the screen assembles from two sources with two vocabularies.

### 7 · What Lane B recommends

| # | Decision | Why it cannot be a lane's |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Is Notifications a bounded context?** Lane B's position: **yes**, on §2 — and `04-modules.md` gains a fifteenth entry, which is a 🔴 architecture change | It adds a bounded context. RFC territory |
| 2 | **Does Day One include a delivered channel, or only in-app?** Lane B's position: **in-app only** | Sequencing, and it decides whether M14.5 is a prerequisite |
| 3 | **Is Novu still the right purchase for a Day One that delivers nothing?** | Reversing or deferring a ratified ADR |
| 4 | **Who owns the attention list** — RIP or Notifications? (§6) | A module boundary between two modules, one unbuilt |

**On decision 2, the argument in full, because it decides the milestone's size.** **In-app is the only channel that needs nothing bought.** It is our database, our API and our UI; it requires no Novu instance, no SMTP, no deliverability, no vendor account, and no cloud infrastructure — which matters because [ADR-0027](architecture/adr/0027-local-first-development.md) means every gate is local and M14.5 is three milestones away. **Every other channel needs infrastructure that does not exist yet**, and building against it would repeat exactly the position M13 has just paused in: a capability that cannot be exercised, waiting on an environment.

It is also the honest one. A product that shows *"3 things need your attention"* in the application, and says nothing about email until email actually sends, is telling the truth about what it can do — which is the rule the Connection Center already follows with `connectable: false`.

**The first slice, if decisions 1 and 2 go that way**, is demonstrable to a non-engineer without naming a module: *a seller opens Signora and sees that their CRM connection expired, marks it as dealt with, and it stops asking.* No vendor, no new dependency, no infrastructure, and a real customer capability.

**Lane B has written no M14a code and has created no `modules/notifications/`.**


### Resolution — product owner, 2026-08-02. All four answered, and the fourth was the important one.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Is Notifications a bounded context?** | **Yes.** Proposed as [ADR-0040](architecture/adr/0040-notifications.md) with the `04-modules.md` entry drafted ready to ratify — that entry is 🔴 and remains the product owner's to make |
| 2 | **Day One scope** | **In-app only.** Unread/read · acknowledge/dismiss · event-driven · idempotent · workspace- and user-scoped · history · preferences only where immediately required. **No email, SMS, push, Slack or Teams** |
| 3 | **Is Novu still right?** | **Not reversed, and unused on Day One.** *"Build an excellent notification center before introducing delivery channels. Channels plug into a mature notification domain rather than define it"* |
| 4 | **Who owns the attention list?** | **Revenue Intelligence Platform keeps it, and the two are different products.** *"Attention answers 'what currently requires my attention?'. Notifications answer 'what changed since I last looked?' Do not let them converge"* |

**Decision 4 settles the boundary Lane B declined to draw**, and it does more than assign a module: it names the *reason* they are different, which is what makes the separation enforceable rather than remembered. Recorded as a permanent principle in ADR-0040 §2, along with the two rules that follow from it — **a notification is generated from an event, never from a state**, and **it records a fact in the past tense while referencing its subject live.**

**The stress test the product owner asked for ran against all nineteen scenarios before any code.** Four changed the design and are recorded in ADR-0040 rather than here:

| Scenario | What it changed |
|---|---|
| **Imported historical data** | The rule in §6 — *nothing is notified about a moment the recipient could not have acted on*. Without it a provider backfill notifies every member about a year of history at once. **Derived at generation time, never a flag a producer must remember**, because a producer-set flag is a hidden input and the module doing the backfill is the one that forgets it |
| **Deleted source objects** | Corrected Lane B's own earlier phrasing. *"Reference, never copy"* was too strong: it makes a notification about a deleted object unreadable. The rule is **store the fact, resolve the subject** — the fact is past tense and never goes stale, the affordance exists only while the subject does |
| **Priority vs severity** | They are different and only one belongs here. **Severity is a property of the event; priority is a property of the recipient's situation** and is Attention's. A module permitted to rank becomes a second scoring engine |
| **Snoozing** | Needs no scheduler at all. `snoozed_until` evaluated at read time, because an in-app center is pull-based — **a benefit of the Day One scope rather than a constraint of it** |

Two scenarios were **excluded on principle rather than on effort**, and the reasons are in ADR-0040: **reminders** (*"you still haven't dealt with this"* is generated from a state, which the ratified rule forbids — and what a reminder reaches for is the Attention surface, which answers it correctly by construction) and **reassignment** (assigning a notification to somebody else is a work-assignment concept and no module owns one; a notification is **addressed**, not owned).

**Status: `ANSWERED`. What remains before implementation is one 🔴 ratification** — the fifteenth entry in [04-modules.md](architecture/04-modules.md), drafted in ADR-0040 §10 and a paste away. **Lane B will not add it**; a lane writing itself a new bounded context is the one change ⚫ forbids outright.

## C-104 · May a request handler call a vendor synchronously, when the answer *is* the request?

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). Option (a): repair by *reference*.** *"The repository should have one authoritative principle. Other documents should reference it instead of restating it."* **`CLAUDE.md` §7 now cites [02-principles.md §13](architecture/02-principles.md) and carries the four cumulative conditions. Applied.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — an architectural interpretation, not a defect |
| **Requesting lane** | **QE**, validating TASK-407 |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this field was not.** **Twelve items carried the same defect**, and every one would have been escalated as an open question. |
| **State** | ~~`OPEN`~~ — **superseded by `Status` above.** ⚠️ **This field name is why the item drifted; see the note at the end** |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-04 |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing today.** TASK-407 passes every gate and was promoted. **This asks whether it should become precedent** |

### The question

`POST /workspaces/{id}/connections/{id}/check` makes a **real HubSpot call inside the request handler** and returns what came back.

**`CLAUDE.md` §7 names that shape explicitly:**

> *"Endpoints that would trigger pipeline processing (**provider calls**, AI reasoning, etc.) synchronously are not permitted — that work is dispatched to background workers."*

**Lane B anticipated the objection and answered it in the route's own docstring**, which is why this is a question rather than a bug row:

> *"Nothing about the customer's data moves. No record is read into the pipeline, nothing is stored about their companies, and no synchronization starts. **This asks whether the door opens and closes it again.**"*

### Why QE is asking rather than ruling

| | |
|---|---|
| **No gate fails** | 3344 backend, 382 invariants, coverage above floor, contracts kept, migration reversible. **QE's authority is to run the gates faithfully and act on the result, not to judge whether the result matters** |
| **The call is bounded** | It reuses `HubSpotCompanies` and its `READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. **There is no unbounded-request defect here**, which is the concrete risk §7 exists to prevent |
| **The abstraction holds** | `HubSpotReachability` implements a module-owned port. No vendor SDK reaches domain or application code |
| **It is genuinely arguable** | §7's stated subject is *pipeline processing*. A liveness probe ingests nothing, starts nothing and stores nothing about the customer's records |

---

### ⚡ Lane C's analysis — 2026-08-06. The two texts disagree, and the principle is narrower than the constitution that cites it

**Read at the source rather than in the paraphrase.** **[02-principles.md §13](architecture/02-principles.md), verbatim:**

> ***"Work that is **not required to complete within the request/response cycle** (provider **polling**, normalization, observation/event/signal/opportunity pipeline processing, AI reasoning calls, recommendation generation) is performed by background workers."***

**`CLAUDE.md` §7, restating it:**

> *"Endpoints that would trigger pipeline processing (**provider calls**, AI reasoning, etc.) synchronously are not permitted."*

| | |
|---|---|
| ⚡ **The qualifying clause** | **Principle 13 governs work *not required to complete within the request/response cycle*.** **A liveness probe's answer *is* the response** — it is required to complete within the cycle **by definition**, so the principle's own precondition is not met |
| ⚡ **The enumerated list** | **Every item is a pipeline stage**: polling, normalization, the observation→signal→opportunity chain, AI reasoning, recommendations. ⛔ **A probe is not among them, and it is not one of them** |
| ⚠️ **The paraphrase widened it** | **`polling` became `calls`.** **Polling is repeated, unbounded and customer-data-bearing; a call is neither** |
| **The rationale confirms the subject** | *"The core pipeline is inherently asynchronous and often I/O- and LLM-latency-bound"* — **latency the customer is not waiting on.** Here the customer is waiting on exactly this |

> ## **So `CLAUDE.md` §7 forbids something [02-principles.md](architecture/02-principles.md) §13 does not, and §20e already predicted how**: ***"a rule written in two places is a rule that will eventually contradict itself, and the copy nobody is maintaining is the one somebody will read."***

#### Evidence First — measured, not assumed

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Is `/check` the only one?** | ⚡ **Yes.** **No other module's `interface/` layer makes a synchronous outbound vendor call** — grepped across all sixteen. **So this is a precedent being set, not one being discovered** |
| ✅ **Is the abstraction intact?** | **Yes.** `HubSpotReachability` implements a module-owned port; no vendor SDK reaches domain or application code |
| ✅ **Is it bounded?** | **Yes** — it reuses `HubSpotCompanies` and its `READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` |

#### The recommendation, which is input and not authority

> ✅ **Permit it, and bound the precedent by a stated test rather than by case-by-case judgement.**

**The four conditions, all of which `/check` meets and none of which a pipeline stage could:**

**① The call's result *is* the response** — not a side effect of producing it · **② nothing about the customer's data is read into the pipeline, stored, or normalized** · **③ it is bounded by an explicit timeout** · **④ it reaches the vendor only through a module-owned port.**

⛔ **What this must not become:** *"synchronous vendor calls are fine if they are quick."* **①+② are the load-bearing pair** — a stage that ingests a single record fails ② however fast it is, and that is the line §7 exists to hold.

🔴 **And the second half is the product owner's alone: `CLAUDE.md` §7's wording.** **If the ruling is *permit*, §7 says something the architecture does not** — the honest repair is to narrow *"provider calls"* to *"provider polling"* and cite Principle 13. ⛔ **Lane C drafts `CLAUDE.md` amendments only on instruction and never on its own initiative** (§20e).

#### ⚠️ Why this item drifted for two days, and it is this office's finding rather than QE's

**QE reported it as *"on the list of items with no `Status` row, which is part of why it has been easy to leave."*** **That inference was reasonable and the premise was wrong** — **this item declares `State`, not `Status`, and [`state-check`](../infra/state-check.py) knew only the second name.**

> ⚡ **Second instance of one defect in one file, on consecutive days.** **The ownership sweep knew one field name and reported twelve owned items as unowned; the state check knew one field name and reported two stated items as stateless.** **Corrected: both now read every form.** **14 items are genuinely stateless, not 16.**
>
> ⛔ **And the real reason this item drifted is not the field name.** **`OPEN` means *raised, nobody has looked* — and somebody had.** **QE's analysis was complete on 2026-08-04; the item simply never moved to a state that says a decision is available.** **That transition is Lane C's under §20e, and this office did not make it for two days.**

---

### ✅ Accepted in principle — [D-103](DECISION_REGISTER.md). Draft text, ready to paste

> ***"Proceed with preparing the documentation changes required to align the repository with the canonical interpretation. However: do not broaden the exception… The exception should remain intentionally difficult to misuse."***

⛔ **`CLAUDE.md` is the product owner's and Lane C drafts only on instruction** (§20e). **This is the instruction; below is the text and nothing is applied.**

#### The shape of the fix, and it is not a new sentence

⚡ **§7's defect is that it *restated* Principle 13 rather than citing it.** **So the repair is subtraction, not addition** — [§0-iii](PRODUCT_OFFICE.md) applied to the item that produced it. **A second paraphrase, however careful, is the same defect one generation later.**

#### Draft — `CLAUDE.md` §7, replacing the existing bullet

```markdown
- Endpoints must not perform work that belongs in the background. The rule and
  its subject are **[02-principles.md §13](docs/architecture/02-principles.md)**,
  which is authoritative and is deliberately not restated here: it governs
  *work not required to complete within the request/response cycle* — provider
  polling, normalization, the observation/event/signal/opportunity pipeline, AI
  reasoning, recommendation generation. That work is dispatched to background
  workers, and a handler responds once the request is durably accepted.

  **A synchronous outbound call is permitted only where all four hold**, and
  they are cumulative rather than indicative:

  ① the call's result **is** the response — not a side effect of producing it;
  ② nothing about the customer's data is read into the pipeline, stored,
     normalized, or made visible to any other module;
  ③ the call is bounded by an explicit timeout owned by the calling module;
  ④ the vendor is reached only through a port that module owns.

  **`POST /workspaces/{id}/connections/{id}/check` is the worked example and
  currently the only one** ([C-104](docs/LANE_COORDINATION.md)). It asks
  whether a door opens and closes it again.

  ⛔ **This is not a latency exemption.** *Quick* is not one of the four, and a
  stage that ingests a single record fails ② however fast it is.
```

#### Why this is hard to misuse, stated as the test it must pass

| | |
|---|---|
| ⚡ **① and ② together exclude every pipeline stage** | **A stage exists *to* produce a side effect and *to* bring data in.** **It fails both, not one** |
| **③ and ④ are not the bar** | **They are hygiene every outbound call already owes.** **A proposal satisfying only ③ and ④ has satisfied nothing** |
| **The named example bounds it** | **One endpoint, named.** ⛔ **A second one is a coordination item, not a precedent already granted** |
| ⚠️ **What was deliberately *not* written** | **No *"health and liveness"* category.** **A named category invites membership claims** — *"this is a liveness check for the CRM's record count"* — **and the four conditions refuse that without needing to argue about the word** |

#### What still needs deciding, and it is one line

**Whether §7 is repaired by *reference* as drafted, or by narrowing *"provider calls"* to *"provider polling"* in place.** ✅ **Lane C recommends the first** — **the second leaves a paraphrase, and a paraphrase is what produced this item.**

> **The reason to ask is precedent, not this slice.** *"Architecture is agreed explicitly or it is inferred, and inferred architecture is two lanes shipping incompatible halves of one contract"* (§20e). **The next lane that wants a synchronous vendor call will cite this endpoint**, and it should be citing a ruling instead.

### The alternatives, so a ruling needs no second round-trip

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **§7 means pipeline processing; a bounded liveness probe is outside it** | The product stays as built. Worth writing the boundary into §7 explicitly, so the next lane reads a rule rather than an endpoint |
| **B** | **§7 means every provider call** | The check dispatches to a worker and the screen polls. **A worse product for the customer**, who clicked *Check* and wants an answer, and considerably more machinery |
| **C** | **A named exception, bounded by conditions** | e.g. *user-initiated · bounded timeout · ingests nothing · writes only its own result.* Keeps the rule strict and makes this case legible |

**QE recommends C**, and notes it is a recommendation rather than a position: it is the option that leaves §7 as strong as it is today while making the one legitimate case checkable rather than argued afresh each time. **The choice is the product owner's.**


## C-103 · Two lanes wrote the same file, from the same bug row, within hours
