```
  lane-b-commercial-profile 128 lines
```

**Both lanes created the same path, independently, in response to the same row.** [B-109](BUGS.md) listed `modules/integrations/public/__init__.py` among five files at 0%; each lane read it and each wrote a test.

### Neither lane did anything wrong, and their reasoning differs interestingly

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lane A** | *"A `public/` module is the one file whose **absences** are load-bearing."* Asserts what the contract refuses to expose |
| **Lane B** | *"Nothing in the repository imports it… the contract has been correct and unused since it was written."* Explains **why** it was uncovered, and names [ADR-0300](architecture/adr/0300-inbound-customer-systems.md) as what decides its consumer |

**Both are good, and they are not the same test.** Whoever merges second will conflict on the whole file, and the resolution is a judgement about which assertions matter — not something QE may make.

### Why this is Lane C's rather than a bug

**Nothing is broken.** This is **duplicate engineering**, which the Product Office charter names directly: *"Prevent duplicate engineering. Continuously ask: do we already have this capability?"*

**The mechanism that produced it is worth more than the instance.** A QE bug row naming five uncovered files is, in effect, **a work item visible to every lane with no owner attached**. Two lanes claimed the same one without either knowing.

> **`integrations` has no current assignee** — it appears in Lane B's assignments and in Lane A's B-109 fix. **A file at 0% in an unassigned module is work anybody may take, and therefore work two lanes may take.**

### What QE will do meanwhile

**Nothing to the file.** QE reports the collision, and whichever candidate certifies first is promoted unchanged. **The second lane resolves the conflict at its own rebase**, which is where a code conflict belongs.

**QE will not choose between two lanes' tests**, and will say so again if asked — the same line drawn when Lane A's rebase conflicted in `test_api_accounts.py`.

---

### ⚡ Second instance — 2026-08-06, and it names this office

**QE reported at cycle 74: *"Lane B had nothing new after all. Their `B-328` commit dropped entirely as a duplicate on rebase — the `READY`-count fix they wrote is the same one Lane C landed in cycle 73."***

> ## **Two lanes independently fixed the `54 READY` miscount within hours of each other. One of them was this office.**

**The mechanism is identical to the first instance and the source is one step earlier:**

| | First instance, 2026-08-04 | ⚡ This one, 2026-08-06 |
|---|---|---|
| **The shared work item** | **[B-109](BUGS.md)** — a bug row naming five uncovered files | **`state-check`'s own output** — *"Backlog: 54 task(s), 54 READY"*, printed on every run |
| **Who could see it** | **Every lane** | ⚡ **Every lane, every time anybody ran the checker** |
| **Who owned it** | ⛔ **Nobody** — `integrations` had no current assignee | ⛔ **Nobody.** `infra/` is Lane C's, **but the defect was visible to all three lanes and claimed by none** |
| **Cost** | One rebase | **One rebase** |

⚠️ **And this instance is worse in one specific way: the first was a *file* two lanes created, so git surfaced it as a conflict. This was a *defect two lanes diagnosed*, and the duplicate work was already finished before either knew.** **No conflict arises when both fixes are correct and one is simply redundant** — **B-328 vanished on rebase, which is the quiet version of the same waste.**

> ⛔ **What this does not license.** **The answer is not a claim protocol for defects** — [B-109](BUGS.md) and this both show the cost is *one rebase*, and §20e's freeze wants proportionate responses to observed problems. **Two instances, both cheap, is evidence of a pattern and not yet evidence for a mechanism.**

✅ **What is worth doing, and it is small:** **a defect visible in a tool's output is a work item with no row.** **When Product Office finds one and intends to fix it, the fix is announced where lanes look** — a `B-` row before the commit, not after. **This office did not do that on 2026-08-06**, and Lane B paid the rebase.

**Recorded as the second instance rather than acted on further.** ⚡ **The third is the trigger** — and if it comes, the pattern will be *three lanes reading one instrument's output as unclaimed work*, which is a different finding from the one this item opened with.


## C-102 · A lane cannot see the defect report that blocks it

> ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-124](DECISION_REGISTER.md), and built rather than recommended.** ⚡ **QE's own closing line is the answer — *"the cheapest possible answer may be the right one"* — and half of it has since become a rule**: **§19 already requires the lane to run its own gates before handover, and [D-114](DECISION_REGISTER.md) added *the lane runs the affected journeys*, with `certification-guard.py --plan` computing which.** **What remained was the *reporting reach*: a lane cannot read a row that is on a ref it has not pulled.** ✅ **[`state-check`](../infra/state-check.py) now reports when the current branch is behind `integration` *and that ref carries register rows this branch has never seen* — bug rows for [C-102](#c-102--a-lane-cannot-see-the-defect-report-that-blocks-it), coordination items for [C-103](#c-103--two-lanes-wrote-the-same-file-from-the-same-bug-row-within-hours).** ⛔ **No notification, no scheduler, no CI — §20c-2.** **It is the check a lane already runs, telling it locally that the ref it consumes has moved and carries something it must see.** ⚡ **Verified against today's repository: Lane B is 9 commits behind and has never seen `B-207`, `C-228` or `C-229`.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — Product Office. *Governance workflow* |
| **Requesting lane** | **QE**, from a measurement rather than an inconvenience |
| **Category** | Governance workflow · defect communication |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-124](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **The answer is recorded above; the requesting lane closes** |
| **Blocks** | Nothing being implemented. **It blocks two lanes from learning that their branch cannot certify** |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-04, after both lanes continued building for hours past a blocking defect |

**Measured, not inferred:**

```
lane-a-product-surface  B-107 rows visible on its own branch:  0
lane-b-commercial-profile  B-108 rows visible on its own branch:  0
origin/integration        rows present:  2
```

**QE reports a defect by writing to `docs/BUGS.md` and pushing to `integration`. A lane sees it only after rebasing.** Neither lane has, so neither knows.

### What each lane did while unable to see its report

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lane A** | Six hours idle, then **23 executable files** in one push. B-107 untouched |
| **Lane B** | **Five pushes**, branch now 41 commits deep. B-108 untouched |

**Neither is misbehaving.** *Continuous execution* (`CLAUDE.md` §20e) explicitly tells a lane not to idle waiting for validation, and Startup — which includes *pull `integration`* and *read every `OPEN` row* — happens at a **slice boundary**. A lane mid-area may legitimately go hours without one.

> **The mechanism is documented and correct. It is simply not exercised on the timescale a blocking defect needs**, and the result is two lanes building on bases that cannot produce a certifiable commit.

### Why QE raises it rather than solving it

**QE cannot make a lane rebase, and should not try.** The options all touch how lanes are told things — a push notification, a defect surfaced at claim time, a rule that a returned task forces a Startup, or nothing at all because the cost is acceptable. **Every one of those is a governance decision about how lanes work**, which is Lane C's to prepare and the product owner's to rule.

**What QE will keep doing meanwhile:** reporting the defect with its mechanism and its fix, and re-checking on every push. **It is the reporting *reaching* the lane that is in question, never the reporting itself.**

> **The cheapest possible answer may be the right one:** both defects are in gates the lanes own and run in under two minutes. If a lane ran `npx tsc --noEmit` or a production build before pushing, it would not need QE's report at all. **That is not QE's rule to make.**

**`CLAUDE.md` §9 requires a new event to be added to [`06-events.md`](architecture/06-events.md) *in the same change that introduces it*. `06-events.md` is 🔴 — product owner and ADR only. A lane that emits an event therefore cannot comply with §9, and the rule is unsatisfiable by the only person in a position to satisfy it.**

### This is a workflow gap, not a discipline problem — and the number matters

**Measured before raising it**, because the difference changes what should be built:

```
declared in code   25
in the catalog     24
missing             1     commercial_profile.target_accounts_changed
```

> **Twenty-four of twenty-five is a healthy repository.** Every reader of the one finding should understand that the catalog has been maintained well **by everyone who was allowed to maintain it**. C-004 exposed the boundary; it did not expose neglect.

**The one gap has a specific cause.** Lane B shipped `target_accounts_changed` in slice 5, could not edit the catalog, and raised [C-004](#c-004--shared-documents-lag-commercial-profile) with the exact table row written out ready to paste. **That was the correct behaviour under the rules as written**, and the row has been waiting ever since.

### What Lane C is being asked to design

**Not the missing row.** That is a product-owner edit, tracked in C-004. This item asks for the *process* that stops the next one happening:

1. **How does an authoritative 🔴 document stay synchronized when the lane that must change it may not write it?** Options exist and QE deliberately does not choose between them — a batched QE-applied edit, a lane-writable appendix the 🔴 document includes, a narrower Change Budget for the catalog specifically, or a ratification step attached to the Slice Handoff.
2. **Does the same gap exist for other 🔴 documents a lane's work can invalidate?** `04-modules.md` (a module's endpoints and tables) and `05-module-dependencies.md` (a new read port) have the same shape, and C-004 lists pending edits to both.
3. **What closes this item?** A ruled process, and §9 becoming satisfiable by whoever incurs it.

### Why QE raises it rather than solving it

**QE validates; Lane C prepares governance; the product owner decides.** A workflow that lets implementation and documentation stay synchronized is governance design, and QE choosing one would be the drift Lane C was created to end — the same drift that left [C-004](#c-004--shared-documents-lag-commercial-profile) and [C-201](#c-201--identifier-allocation-is-still-only-unlikely-to-collide) filed under QE while both waited on a ruling.

**What QE did build** is the detection: `make event-catalog` (Repository Health · *Documentation Synchronization*) enumerates every declared `event_type` and compares it against the catalog. **Advisory, deliberately** — its one finding today can only be cleared by editing a 🔴 file, and a gate that fails on something its owner cannot fix teaches people to ignore gates. **It becomes gateable the day this item is resolved**, which is the clearest statement of what "resolved" means.

---

## C-301 · Nothing asserts what the deployed worker consumes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **QE** — **repository-wide automated tests.** ⚠️ **Owner cell added 2026-08-08 — the item stated its owner inside `Status` prose, where no instrument can read it and no reader can find it.** ⛔ **That is [C-213](#c-213)'s class: an owner that is *derivable* rather than *visible*, and derivable is not visible.** |
| **Decision required** | Whether a repository-wide assertion of the deployed subscription set is built, and by whom |
| **Participating modules** | `apps/worker/` — a composition root no module's suite covers · every module that will ever add a consumer |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **QE** — repository-wide automated tests are QE's; lanes own the tests specific to their slices (`CLAUDE.md` §20e) |
| **Blocking** | **Nothing today.** [B-301](BUGS.md) is fixed and Timeline consumes correctly |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, by Lane B, having just shipped the defect it describes |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — **owner: QE**, repository-wide automated tests. ✅ **Blocking nothing today**: [B-301](BUGS.md) is fixed and Timeline consumes correctly. ⚡ **Field added 2026-08-06 — the item carried none, so no instrument could route it** ([D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *structured state is canonical*). |

**The specific defect is fixed; the class that produced it is not.** [B-301](BUGS.md) — Timeline promoted to `main` with a projection handler the deployed worker never registered — got through **2518 passing tests, a coverage gate, MyPy strict, import-linter, `make smoke` and a full certification cycle.**

**Why none of them could see it.** `apps/worker/subscriptions.py` is a composition root, and **a composition root is the one file no module's own suite covers**: each module tests its own half and assumes the wiring. Timeline's unit tests drive `ProjectEvent` directly and its integration tests drive the handler directly, so both halves were proven and the join was not.

**Lane B has written Timeline's half** — `backend/tests/integration/test_worker_subscriptions.py` asserts that every event Timeline projects has a consumer, that it subscribes to nothing it cannot project, and that every subscription routes to a declared pool.

**What Lane B has deliberately not written is the general one**, and the boundary is the reason:

> **A per-module assertion catches the module that remembered to write it.** The defect is a module *forgetting*, and a test written by the forgetting lane is exactly the one that will be absent.

**What a repository-wide version would assert**, offered as input rather than as a design:

- **Every module with an `interface/handlers.py` has at least one subscription**, or is on a stated list of modules that deliberately consume nothing (Commercial Profile is the head of the pipeline and consumes nothing; that is a fact worth asserting, not an omission).
- **Every event type in `06-events.md`'s catalog with a declared consumer has a matching subscription** — the catalog names consumers today and nothing checks that they exist.
- **Every subscription routes to a pool a process actually runs.**

**The second one is the valuable one and the most work**, because `06-events.md` is prose. It is also the only one that would have caught this before Timeline was written rather than after.

### Concrete validation rules, as QE would implement them

**Offered as a specification rather than a design.** Each is stated as a property with the failure it catches, because a rule whose failure mode is unstated is a rule nobody can judge.

| # | Assertion | The defect it catches | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V1** | **Every subscription routes to a pool a process runs.** `registry.pools()` ⊆ `POOLS` | An event relayed, queued, and never picked up. Silent — the outbox marks it relayed | Trivial. **Already written** in `test_worker_subscriptions.py`, and QE may lift it |
| **V2** | **Every module with an `interface/handlers.py` has at least one subscription**, or appears on an explicit `CONSUMES_NOTHING` list | **Exactly B-301.** A handler written, tested and never registered | Small. The list is the interesting part — it makes *"Commercial Profile consumes nothing"* an asserted fact rather than an omission |
| **V3** | **Every consumer named in `06-events.md`'s catalog has a matching subscription** | The catalog says Timeline consumes `observation.recorded`; nothing checked that it did. **This would have failed the day the catalog named Timeline** — before the module existed | **The most work and the most valuable.** `06-events.md` is a prose table; either it grows a machine-readable form, or the check parses it |
| **V4** | **Every subscribed event type is one some module publishes** | A subscription to a renamed or removed event — a worker waking for something that will never arrive | Small, and it is V3 read backwards |

**V2 is the one that would have caught B-301**, and V3 is the one that would have caught it *earliest*. **V1 is free today.**

**A deliberate non-recommendation:** *"every published event has a consumer"* must **not** be asserted. Publishing before anyone consumes is how this pipeline was built, `for_event_type` documents an empty list as a normal outcome, and a check demanding consumers would push lanes into writing empty handlers to satisfy it.

### Ownership, reconciled

**QE's `e7ec943` and this item disagreed and both were partly right.** QE recorded the durable fix as belonging to *"whoever owns `apps/`"* — [C-010](#c-010--no-lane-is-assignable-to-apps-or-signora_platform-and-a-defect-is-sitting-in-one)'s unassigned gap, its seventh defect. This item assigned it to QE. **The split is:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The assertion** — a repository-wide test | **QE.** §20e: *"QE creates, maintains, extends and retires repository-wide automated tests"* |
| **Any production change in `apps/`** that a failing assertion demands | **Unassigned — [C-010](#c-010--no-lane-is-assignable-to-apps-or-signora_platform-and-a-defect-is-sitting-in-one).** A failing check with nobody able to fix what it reports is a check that will be skipped |

**Both are needed, and V1–V4 need only the first.** They assert wiring that lanes write; a lane adding a subscription is already permitted to (§20a).

**Not blocking.** Recorded so the class does not survive on the memory of the lane that hit it.

## C-302 · A notification is per-person, and workspace RLS is not enough

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision required** | Whether a tenant-owned table may carry a **second** RLS predicate scoping rows to `app.user_id` within the workspace |
| **Participating modules** | `notifications` (proposed) · the Tenant Isolation Policy · [11-tenancy.md](architecture/11-tenancy.md) 🔴 |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **Product owner** — `11-tenancy.md` and `docs/architecture/01`–`21` are 🔴 |
| **Blocking** | **N-01's migration**, and nothing before it |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, by Lane B, stress-testing [ADR-0040](architecture/adr/0040-notifications.md) against membership changes |
| **Status** | ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` — [D-139](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑤: *"Continue holding this until ADR-0040. No further Product Owner time required until then."*** ⚡ **Trigger: [ADR-0040](architecture/adr/0040-notifications.md) reaching ratification.** **Trigger steward: Lane C.** |

**Every workspace-owned table in this repository is workspace-scoped and workspace-*shared*.** RLS answers *"may this organization see this row?"*, and within a workspace every member sees everything. That has been correct for every table so far, because every one holds facts about the *organization*.

**A notification holds a fact about a *person***: what they have been told, and whether they have read, dismissed or snoozed it. **Under a workspace-only policy, any member could read any colleague's notifications and their read state** — which is not a tenancy breach between customers, and is still wrong.

**The mechanism already exists and needs no platform change.** `tenant_scoped_session` sets `app.user_id` transaction-locally alongside `app.workspace_id`, and **user-scoped RLS is established precedent**: `workspace` and `membership` have been membership-scoped on `app.user_id` since migration `0001`. So the policy is ordinary:

```sql
USING (
  workspace_id  = NULLIF(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid
  AND recipient_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id',   true), '')::uuid
)
```

**Why it is a question rather than a decision Lane B takes.** It is *stricter* than the Tenant Isolation Policy and satisfies every check in `tenancy_policy.py` — which asserts *which commands* have policies, never their predicates. But **[11-tenancy.md](architecture/11-tenancy.md) describes a one-key model**, it is 🔴, and *"a lane invented a second tenancy dimension inside a slice"* is precisely the drift the Change Budget exists to stop.

**Two consequences worth deciding with it, because they are the same decision:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **A removed member's notifications** | Lane B's position: **rows are retained and become unreadable**, since the policy already denies them and the workspace's own record of what was sent is operational history. **Deleting them would be a lane deciding a data-retention question that [README](../README.md) lists as unowned** — *"data export and account deletion (no owner)"* |
| **The unread count is per workspace** | Not a product choice. **A cross-workspace aggregate would have to read outside the active workspace context**, which RLS forbids — and a count mixing three organizations is a number nobody can act on. Recorded in ADR-0040 §9 |

### The alternatives, and what each one costs

**Four ways to make a per-person row safe. Only one is recommended, and the other three are recorded because rejecting them silently would leave the ruling looking narrower than it is.**

| | Approach | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A** ✅ | **Second RLS predicate on `app.user_id`** | **Enforced by the database, which is the only place tenancy is ever enforced here.** A forgotten `WHERE recipient_id = …` in a repository method is refused rather than shipped. Costs: `11-tenancy.md` describes a one-key model and must say so, and the Tenant Isolation Policy gains a second dimension to reason about. **Uses only existing primitives** — no platform change, no new grant, no migration pattern that does not already exist in `0001` |
| **B** | **Application-level filtering only** — RLS stays workspace-scoped, every query adds `recipient_id` | **Rejected.** §8 is explicit that application filtering is *defence in depth beside* RLS, never instead of it. One missed `WHERE` exposes a colleague's read state, and nothing structural refuses it. This is the option that looks cheapest and is the one the repository has spent four milestones designing against |
| **C** | **A separate `notification_recipient` table** carrying read state, workspace-scoped, with per-user rows | **Does not solve it.** The read-state rows are still workspace-scoped, so the same exposure exists one table further away — and it costs the join and the *"one row per recipient"* simplification (ADR-0040 §5) for nothing |
| **D** | **Per-user database roles or a session-scoped view** | **Rejected as disproportionate.** It would make tenancy depend on connection identity rather than transaction context, which contradicts the pooling model the whole application is built on, and `signora_platform/` is frozen |

**The rule that decides it:** *types should make incorrect architecture impossible*, applied to data. **B and C leave a violation as ordinary code that happens to be wrong; A makes it unrepresentable.**

**What "no ruling" costs, stated plainly.** N-01 cannot ship a table. There is no partial version — a notification table without the right policy is one that would have to be migrated later under real customer data, and a migration that tightens RLS on a populated table is exactly the change nobody wants to make in production.

**Lane B recommends A**, and will not write the migration until it is ruled on. **N-01 has no other blocker of its own** — it waits on the `04-modules.md` entry (C-027) regardless, and both can be answered in one pass.

## C-303 · An ICP is not an addressable thing, and every verb the brief asks for needs one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision required** | **One aggregate decision**, and **one product question** underneath it that changes what an ICP *is* |
| **Participating modules** | `commercial_profile` — currently **unassigned**; Lane B built it in M12.5 |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **Product owner** — the structural decision was reserved explicitly |
| **Blocking** | **All ICP Management implementation.** Discovery, audit and design continue |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, by Lane B, assigned ICP Management, **after the reuse audit and before any code** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED`** — **2026-08-02: the ICP stays in Commercial Profile, and the aggregate is [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md).** ⚠️ **The structural decision the body describes was reserved to the product owner and the *ownership* question is settled.** ⛔ **Corrected 2026-08-06 — this office wrote `OPEN` here hours earlier by defaulting rather than reading.** **The summary index carried the resolution and the body did not, so a `Status` field added *safely* overwrote a real answer.** ⚡ **The safe default is only safe when the other record is also empty**, and this one was not. |

### 1 · The reuse audit — what already exists, and it is more than expected

**Substantial ICP implementation already ships, and none of it should be replaced.** Delivered as M12.5 slice 2 and reviewed since.

| Layer | Artifact | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Domain** | `IcpDeclaration`, `ProductIcp`, `EmployeeRange`, `IcpError` | **Reuse.** The validation rules, the customer's-words principle and the *"describes, never matches"* boundary are all correct and stay |
| **Application** | `DeclareIcp`, `DeclareIcpInput`, `IcpVersionConflictError` | **Extend.** Optimistic concurrency on `expected_version` is right and generalises |
| **Infrastructure** | `icp_declaration` (migration `0020`, JSONB `profiles`), versioned repository on the shared `DeclarationModel` | **Extend.** RLS forced, no `UPDATE` grant, `uq_(workspace_id, version)` as the concurrency control |
| **Interface** | `GET`/`PUT /workspaces/{id}/icp`, purpose-built schemas, `ERROR_MAPPING` | **Evolve, not replace** — see §4 |
| **Frontend** | `IcpEditor`, `useDeclareIcp`, `queryKeys.icp`, `IcpDeclaration`/`ProductIcp` types | **Reuse the editor's field design; extend around it** |
| **Tests** | **32** domain · **19** API · **18** component | **Keep every one.** They encode decisions, not implementation |
| **Docs** | [40-commercial-profile.md](architecture/40-commercial-profile.md) slice 2 · [ADR-0035](architecture/adr/0035-commercial-profile.md) | **Current and accurate** |

**Nothing downstream consumes an ICP.** `commercial_profile/public/` publishes only `TargetAccountReader`; no module imports `IcpDeclaration`. **That makes evolving the model unusually cheap**, and it is the single most useful fact the audit produced: there are no consumers to migrate, no event contract to version, and no coupling to unwind.

### 2 · The finding: the model has no place to put an ICP

**Today an ICP is not a thing. It is a slice of a document.**

```
IcpDeclaration          ← one per workspace, versioned, immutable
└── profiles: tuple[ProductIcp, ...]
    └── ProductIcp(product_id, industries, countries, employees, notes)
                   ↑ no id, no name, no state, and one per product — enforced
```

`IcpDeclaration.__post_init__` refuses *"one product is described twice"*. A `ProductIcp` has **no identity of its own**: it is addressed by `product_id`, it has no name, and it has no lifecycle.

**Every verb in the brief presupposes an identity and a lifecycle that do not exist:**

| Asked for | Why it cannot be expressed today |
|---|---|
| Create · duplicate · **multiple ICPs** | The uniqueness rule forbids a second one for a product |
| Archive · restore · activate · deactivate · **draft** | There is no state on a `ProductIcp`, and the document is immutable — states would be a second mutable truth beside it |
| **Default** | Nothing to point at; there is no id |
| Search · filter · sort · bulk operations | Nothing to enumerate — `profiles` is a JSONB array inside one row |
| Compare · version history *per ICP* | Versions exist **for the whole workspace**. *"Version 7 of the EMEA ICP"* has no referent |
| Usage indicators · health · effectiveness | Nothing to attach them to |

**This is not a defect and the existing design was not wrong.** [40-commercial-profile.md](architecture/40-commercial-profile.md) records the alternative being considered and rejected, with a trigger: *"Rejected: one aggregate per product… **Trigger to revisit: a customer with enough products that two people edit different profiles concurrently and collide.**"*

> **The brief is a stronger trigger than the one recorded.** Not concurrency — **an ICP becoming a thing a customer names, opens, copies, retires and compares.** The recorded trigger anticipated pressure from *scale*; this is pressure from *identity*.

### 3 · The product question underneath it, and it is the real decision

**Before the aggregate can be shaped, one sentence has to be settled**, because today's model answers it one way and the brief implies the other.

> **Is an ICP *"the kind of company that buys **this product**"*, or *"a named segment we sell into"*?**

Today it is strictly the first — `ProductIcp` names a product, exactly one per product, and the module's own docstring is *"an ICP is 'the kind of company that buys **this**'"*.

**The customer sentence that breaks it:** *"We sell Revenue Cloud to mid-market fintech in the US, and separately to enterprise insurers in the UK."* **Two ICPs, one product.** Structurally impossible today. The brief's territories, markets, business units and product lines are all this sentence.

| | Shape | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Keep product-keyed.** *"Multiple"* means multiple products | **Does not satisfy the brief.** Recorded only so the option is visibly rejected rather than skipped |
| **B** ✅ | **`Icp` names exactly one product, plus a customer-given name.** Several per product | Keeps *"who buys **this**"* intact and unambiguous for every future consumer. Every verb in the brief works. Costs: *"EMEA Enterprise"* for two products is two ICPs, which is mild duplication a customer would probably expect |
| **C** | **`Icp` is a named segment; product is one criterion among many** (0..n products) | More expressive and avoids that duplication. **Costs the sentence that makes an ICP meaningful** — an ICP naming no product is *"companies we like"*, which is vaguer for a customer to reason about and much vaguer for a consumer to act on |
| **D** | **B with the product optional** | Rejected: two meanings for one type, and a downstream consumer would have to branch on which kind it received |

**Lane B recommends B**, on the evidence that the module's whole value is being *citable* — every downstream use of an ICP will ask *"who buys what?"*, and C makes half the answer optional.

### 4 · What Lane B is **not** proposing

**Not a new module.** A bounded-context analysis was run and the evidence points the other way: the ubiquitous language is identical (a customer *declares* their commercial reality), the invariant is identical (*"it records; it computes nothing, resolves nothing, matches nothing"*, guarded by `tests/commercial_profile/test_boundary.py` reading the domain as a syntax tree), the lifecycle is identical (versioned, immutable, superseded), and an ICP references a **product from this module's own catalog** — so extracting it would create a cross-module dependency for no gain.

> **This is an aggregate change, not a context change** — and [40-commercial-profile.md](architecture/40-commercial-profile.md)'s own opening already says the module holds *"several small aggregates, each versioned independently — never one profile object."* Promoting ICP to its own aggregate makes the module **more** consistent with its stated design, not less.

**Not a replacement of the API.** `GET`/`PUT /workspaces/{id}/icp` continues to answer *"what is our ICP?"* — it becomes a collection resource alongside per-ICP resources, and existing clients are not broken by adding siblings.

**Not a rewrite of the editor.** The field design, the free-text principle, the immediate-save behaviour and the dropped-product handling ([B-005](BUGS.md)) are all correct and stay; the work is the surface *around* them — a list, a lifecycle, a default.

### 5 · What unblocks this

**Two answers, in one pass:**

1. **The product question in §3** — B, C, or something the brief means that Lane B has not seen.
2. **Confirmation that ICP stays inside Commercial Profile** as a first-class aggregate rather than becoming a fifteenth bounded context.

**And one assignment matter:** `commercial_profile` currently has **no assignee**. Lane B built it and is recording the claim on the board with this item; if that is wrong, it is a board correction rather than an architectural one.

**Independent work that continues meanwhile:** the customer journey and UI/UX design (Phases 3 and 4), the stress test (Phase 2), and the QE impact statement — **none of which encodes an assumption about the answer**, because all of them describe what a customer does rather than how it is stored. **Nothing is implemented.**


### 6 · The customer journey, designed while the structural question is open

**None of this encodes an assumption about the answer**, because it describes what a customer does rather than how it is stored. Recorded now so that the decision in §3 arrives at a journey rather than at a blank page.

| | The customer's question | What the product does |
|---|---|---|
| **JI1** | *"Who do we sell to?"* | The list, and **it is the screen that does not exist today.** Today an ICP is only reachable through a per-product editor, so *"show me everything we've said about who buys from us"* has no page |
| **JI2** | *"We sell this to two very different kinds of company."* | A second ICP for the same product. **The sentence today's model refuses** |
| **JI3** | *"Which one is Signora actually using?"* | A stated default, visible on the list rather than inferred |
| **JI4** | *"Start from the EMEA one and change the country."* | Duplicate. The most common way a real second ICP gets written |
| **JI5** | *"We don't sell into that market any more."* | Archive — **not delete.** Everything Signora found under that ICP was found *because of it*, and deleting the reason leaves the evidence unexplainable |
| **JI6** | *"Is this too broad?"* | The hardest question on the page, and the one with no honest answer yet — see §7 |
| **JI7** | *"What changed, and who changed it?"* | Already answered by the existing model: every declaration is versioned, immutable, and names its author |

**JI5 is the one with an architectural consequence.** *Delete* and *archive* are different promises, and the repository already has the vocabulary: a declaration is immutable and superseded. **An archived ICP is a state, not a deletion** — and a deleted one, if it is ever offered, must state what happens to what it produced.

**JI6 is deliberately unanswered.** *"Too broad"* means *"this would match too many companies"*, and **matching does not exist** — it needs resolved attribute values from the Knowledge Graph, which is [C-002](#c-002--customer-language-has-no-anticorruption-layer)'s open anticorruption question. **Offering a health indicator before matching exists would be the product asserting something it cannot compute**, which is the rule the Connection Center already follows with `connectable: false`. It is recorded as the first thing to build once C-002 is answered, and is not in Day One.

### 7 · The stress test, run against the brief's own scenarios

**Four moved the design. The rest were absorbed.**

| Scenario | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Hundreds of ICPs** | The list is a **cursor-paginated collection**, not a JSONB array in one row. Today's `profiles` array is read whole on every request and rewritten whole on every save — **fine for a handful, wrong for hundreds**, and it is the clearest technical argument for the aggregate change in §2 independent of the product argument in §3 |
| **Multiple products × territories × business units** | **The multiplication is the point of §3.** Under B it is *n* ICPs and the customer names them; under C it is fewer ICPs with more criteria each. **This is the scenario the product owner should picture when choosing** |
| **Archived and draft ICPs** | A lifecycle state on an aggregate whose *content* is immutable and versioned. **The two must not be confused**: content is superseded, state is updated. That is the same split ADR-0040 draws for notifications, and the same `UPDATE`-grant-on-named-columns-only treatment applies |
| **ICP effectiveness · performance analytics** | **Does not belong here, and the boundary test would refuse it.** `tests/commercial_profile/test_boundary.py` reads the domain as a syntax tree and rejects any identifier naming a judgement — `score`, `rank`, `fit`, `weight`. **Effectiveness is a judgement.** It belongs to whoever owns measurement, reading ICPs through a port; recording it here would put a verdict in the module whose whole guarantee is that it holds none |
| **Templates · AI-assisted creation** | Both are *sources* of an ICP's content, not new concepts. An ICP written by a template and one typed by a seller are the same aggregate with different provenance. **Provenance is a field; neither is a new lifecycle** — and AI-authored content would need [ADR-0031](architecture/adr/0031-evidence-citation-protocol.md)'s citation discipline before it ships |
| **Import / export · bulk editing** | Absorbed. Bulk edit is *n* revisions, each versioned; the optimistic-concurrency rule already in `DeclareIcp` is what makes that safe rather than last-write-wins |
| **Historical comparison** | Already possible — declarations are immutable and superseded. **Per-ICP history needs the aggregate change; workspace-wide history exists today** |
| **Shared ICPs across teams** | **Out of scope, and it is a tenancy question rather than an ICP one.** The repository has no team-below-workspace concept. Recorded rather than designed around |

### 8 · QE impact, stated ahead of implementation

**So automation evolves alongside rather than behind.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **New APIs** | A collection and per-ICP resources alongside the existing `GET`/`PUT /workspaces/{id}/icp`, which keeps working |
| **Migration** | A new table, and a **data migration from `icp_declaration.profiles`** — the first in this repository that moves customer data rather than adding to it. **Reversibility needs stating explicitly** |
| **Regression areas** | `test_api_icp.py` (19), `test_icp.py` (32), `icp.test.tsx` (18), `your-business.test.tsx`, `test_boundary.py`, `tenancy_policy.py` registration |
| **Seed data** | Through the existing declaration path, never by inserting rows |
| **Demo scenario** | *"We sell Revenue Cloud to two different kinds of company, and Signora knows which one is which"* |
| **Performance** | The first list in this module that can be long. Cursor pagination, no `COUNT` |


### Resolution — product owner 2026-08-02, and a reversal Lane B made against itself

**The product owner answered the boundary question and asked one more:** *is Product the strongest aggregate root for ICP ownership?* — with the instruction to **challenge Lane B's own recommendation** rather than defend it.

**It did not survive.** The reversal, the evidence and the answer are in **[ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md)**, proposed. In short:

| | |
|---|---|
| **The boundary** | **ICP stays inside Commercial Profile.** Ruled by the product owner on the evidence in §4 |
| **Product as anchor** | **Confirmed**, and for a reason the challenge sharpened: Product is the only one of *product · offering · bundle · family · motion* that already exists as a reviewed, identified thing. **The correction is to cardinality, not to ownership** |
| **The recommendation** | **Reversed from B to E** — an ICP names **one or more** products, never zero |

**Where §3's reasoning broke, stated plainly rather than quietly corrected.** Option C was written as *"product is one criterion among many (**0..n**)"* and rejected because *"an ICP naming no product is 'companies we like'"*. **That rejects the `0` and was applied to the `n`.** Nothing about letting an ICP name three products requires letting it name none.

**The product owner's own example is B's strongest counter-example.** Revenue Cloud + CPQ + Billing sold as one offering to one segment is **three identical ICPs under B**, maintained by hand, and **they drift the first time somebody edits one.** Duplicated truth is this repository's most-cited failure mode, and B does not merely permit it — it makes it the only way to express a common commercial arrangement.

**E is a strict superset of B with no added optionality**, and **the migration is identical under both** — each existing `ProductIcp` becomes one `Icp` naming one product, 1:1. So the choice costs nothing to get right and a live data migration to get wrong.

**One requirement is challenged rather than designed:** **`default` may have no job in a multi-ICP world.** If Signora acts on every `active` ICP, *"which is default"* never needs answering and the field is a leftover from the model being replaced. **Not implemented in Day One unless a customer question is named that `active` cannot answer** — ADR-0041 §3.

**This item is `ANSWERED`. Implementation begins on ADR-0041's ratification**, which is the one thing outstanding.


### 7 · The ICP customer experience, designed before any code

**Designed for fifty, so one does not need redesigning into fifty.** [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md) holds the architecture; this holds what a customer does. Neither encodes an assumption the ADR has not settled.

#### The screen that does not exist today

**There is no ICP list.** Today an ICP is reachable only through a per-product editor inside *Settings → Products*, so *"show me everything we've said about who buys from us"* has no page. **That page is slice 1**, and it is the whole reason this feels like a capability rather than a form.

| State | What the customer sees |
|---|---|
| **None yet** | *"You haven't described who buys from you yet."* One action. **Not an apology for empty data** — a statement about what to do next |
| **One** | The list still, never a special case. **A one-item list that becomes a different screen at two items is a redesign the customer performs on our behalf** |
| **Fifty** | Search, filter by product and state, sort by name or last change. **Cursor-paginated — no `COUNT`, no offset** |
| **Loading · failing** | The foundation's states, unmodified (§20c) |

#### The journeys, in the customer's words

| | Question | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **JI1** | *"Who do we sell to?"* | The list. Product chips, state, when it last changed |
| **JI2** | *"We sell this to two very different kinds of company."* | A second ICP for the same product — **the sentence today's model refuses** |
| **JI3** | *"Start from EMEA and change the country."* | **Duplicate.** How a real second ICP actually gets written, and it opens as a **draft** |
| **JI4** | *"We don't sell into that market any more."* | **Archive, never delete.** Everything Signora found under it was found *because of* it; deleting the reason leaves the evidence unexplainable |
| **JI5** | *"Bring it back."* | Restore. Archiving is reversible or it is deletion with a nicer word |
| **JI6** | *"What changed, and who?"* | Version history — **already true today** and inherited unchanged |
| **JI7** | *"Is this too broad?"* | **Deliberately unanswered.** It needs matching, matching needs [C-002](#c-002--customer-language-has-no-anticorruption-layer), and answering it before then would be the product asserting what it cannot compute — the Connection Center's `connectable: false` rule |

#### Decisions the design takes now, so slices do not re-take them

**Editing is an editor, not a wizard.** A wizard suits a thing done once; an ICP is revisited. **Duplicate-then-edit is the shape of the second one**, which is why JI3 exists rather than a template gallery.

**A draft is where an ICP is incomplete** — and it is what lets [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md)'s `≥1 product` rule bind at publication instead of blocking the first keystroke.

**Save behaviour changes, and the reason is recorded.** The current editor saves every change immediately, correctly, because the whole workspace declaration is one version. **Under a per-ICP aggregate a draft has an obvious boundary**, so editing a draft is buffered and publishing is the commit — while **editing a published ICP still writes a version per change**, because that is a statement already made.

**Bulk operations are archive and restore only.** No bulk delete: a destructive action across an unseen selection is the one place a confirmation genuinely cannot inform.

**Compare is deferred, and named.** *"How do these two differ?"* is real, and it is a reading of two versions rather than a new concept. It waits until customers have enough ICPs to need it.

**AI assistance is a source, never a state** — an ICP drafted by a model is an ordinary draft with provenance, and it never publishes itself.

**Accessibility, per §20c:** the list is a list; every row action is reachable and labelled **per ICP** — *"Archive Mid-market Fintech"*, not *"Archive"* — because fifty identical labels are unusable to a screen reader. Nothing depends on hover. Design tokens only.

#### QE impact — stated before implementation

| | |
|---|---|
| **New APIs** | An ICP collection, per-ICP resources, publish/archive/restore. **`GET`/`PUT /workspaces/{id}/icp` keeps working** |
| **Migration** | **The module's first move of customer data.** Reversibility ends at the first multi-product ICP or second ICP for one product — [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md), *Migration reversibility* |
| **Regression** | `test_api_icp.py` (19) · `test_icp.py` (32) · `icp.test.tsx` (18) · `your-business.test.tsx` · `test_boundary.py` · `tenancy_policy.py` |
| **E2E** | Create → publish → duplicate → archive → restore, and *"two ICPs for one product"* |
| **Seed data** | Through the declaration path. **Never inserted rows** |
| **Visual regression** | Three new states — empty, one, many |
| **Performance** | The module's first list that can be long. Cursor pagination, no `COUNT` |
| **Demo** | *"We sell Revenue Cloud to two different kinds of company, and Signora knows which is which."* |

## C-304 · A standing review question that has already paid for itself

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — **it asks a question about `CLAUDE.md`, which is theirs.** ⚡ **A standing review question, not a blocker and not closeable.** ⚠️ **Owner cell added 2026-08-08 — the item stated its owner inside `Status` prose, where no instrument can read it and no reader can find it.** ⛔ **That is [C-213](#c-213)'s class: an owner that is *derivable* rather than *visible*, and derivable is not visible.** |
| **Decision required** | Where a repository-wide review question belongs, and whether it is adopted |
| **Participating modules** | none — review practice |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **Product owner** — `CLAUDE.md` is theirs, and a review practice is governance |
| **Blocking** | **Nothing** |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, by Lane B, at the product owner's suggestion after it caught a real error |
| **Status** | 🟣 **`OPEN` — PARKED, CORRECTLY. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** ✅ **Strategic, and its own trigger is named.** ⛔ **Out of the active product owner queue and not raised again until its trigger fires** |

**The question, ready to adopt:**

> **When rejecting a design option, ask whether the stated reason rejects the entire option or only one characteristic of it.**

**It has already paid for itself once, in the cycle that produced it.** [C-303](#c-303--an-icp-is-not-an-addressable-thing-and-every-verb-the-brief-asks-for-needs-one) §3 rejected an option described as *"product is one criterion among many (**0..n**)"* because *"an ICP naming no product is 'companies we like'"*. **That reason rejects the `0` and says nothing about the `n`** — and the conflation carried a recommendation for six hours that would have forced every customer with a bundled offering to maintain three copies of one description ([ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md) §2).

**Why it is worth a rule rather than a habit.** The failure is invisible from inside: the reasoning is *locally valid* at every step, and the rejected option is never revisited because it has been dealt with. **Nothing in a review naturally re-opens a closed option** — which is why it took an explicit instruction to argue against a recorded recommendation to find it.

**Lane B has not added it to `CLAUDE.md`.** Governance is the product owner's, and §20e is explicit that a repository-wide rule belongs there rather than in the document that happened to prompt it. **This is the same shape as [C-017](#c-017--the-onboarding-honesty-principle-has-no-permanent-home)** — ratifiable text, awaiting placement.


### Challenged, on the product owner's direction — it produces noise, and the noise is nameable

**Asked to find where the question costs more than it returns, before proposing it as a permanent rule. It does, in one identifiable case, and the fix sharpens the rule rather than weakening it.**

**Where it is noise: an option rejected on a *whole-option* property.**

> *"Rejected: a second datastore for the read model."* · *"Rejected: a new dependency."* · *"Rejected: it modifies frozen platform internals."*

**Nothing here has characteristics to separate.** Asking *"does the reason reject the whole option or one characteristic?"* returns *"the whole option"* every time, and the cost is a paragraph in every ADR proving a negative. **A review question that fires on every rejection and finds something in one of twenty is a check people learn to skip** — which is worse than not having it, because the twentieth is the one that mattered.

**Where it earns its cost, and the trigger is textual:**

> **Apply it when the rejected option's own description contains a quantifier, an optionality, or a compound** — `0..n` · *optional* · *several* · *up to* · *either…or* · *and/or*.

**Those are exactly the descriptions where a reason can attach to one end and be read as attaching to both**, and the failure it caught is the archetype: Option C was written *"product is one criterion among many (**0..n**)"* and rejected because *"an ICP naming no product is 'companies we like'"* — **a reason about the `0`, applied to the `n`.**

**A second property worth stating:** the question is only worth asking about an option that was **described by the person rejecting it**. When an option arrives already worded by somebody else, the wording is evidence rather than a summary, and re-parsing it is second-guessing rather than review.

> **Sharpened rule, and Lane B's recommendation for adoption:**
>
> **When you reject an option you yourself described, and your description contains a quantifier or an optionality, check which part of it your reason actually rejects.**

**That fires rarely, and every time it fires the failure is possible.** It survives the challenge in this form and does not survive in the general one.

**Still the product owner's to place.** `CLAUDE.md` is governance.

## C-305 · Two principles that outgrew the ADR that found them

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — **two principles that outgrew their ADR, and `CLAUDE.md` is theirs.** ⚠️ **Owner cell added 2026-08-08 — the item stated its owner inside `Status` prose, where no instrument can read it and no reader can find it.** ⛔ **That is [C-213](#c-213)'s class: an owner that is *derivable* rather than *visible*, and derivable is not visible.** |
| **Decision required** | Whether two rules discovered in [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md) become repository principles, and where they live |
| **Participating modules** | `commercial_profile` · `ai_platform` · `opportunity_engine` · `notifications` *(proposed)* — **each already exhibits one or both** |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **Product owner** — `CLAUDE.md` §2 is governance |
| **Blocking** | **Nothing.** Both are being applied; this decides whether they are named |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-02, by Lane B, at the product owner's direction |
| **Status** | 🟣 **`OPEN` — PARKED, CORRECTLY. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** ✅ **Strategic, and its own trigger is named.** ⛔ **Out of the active product owner queue and not raised again until its trigger fires** |

**Neither was invented. Both were *found* — each already enforced in a module that had never described it as a rule**, which is the evidence that they are repository principles rather than ICP details.

### 1 · Immutable versions record decisions, not editing

> **A version is something the customer intentionally published. Not something they typed.**
>
> Editing produces a draft. **Publishing produces a version.** A discarded draft leaves no trace, because nothing was ever said.

**Already true in the AI Platform**, which nobody wrote down: a prompt version is immutable and a released one may never be edited — *"a change is a new version, never an edit, because editing one silently invalidates every result that claims it."* **The same sentence describes an ICP.**

**What it buys, and it is more than tidiness:** AI-assisted generation, collaborative editing, approvals, comments and review workflows all become **operations on drafts**, and none of them pollutes published history. **A model that treats every keystroke as a version cannot support any of them without a cleanup process** — and a cleanup process over an immutable chain is a contradiction.

**Where it will recur:** Prompt Registry (already) · signal definitions · buying committee definitions · playbooks · email and notification templates · automation rules · AI agents.

### 2 · Execution invariants are enforced at publication, not at creation

> **An object may exist in an editable state without satisfying the invariants that make it executable. Those invariants are checked when it is published.**

**Two independent instances, and neither knew about the other:**

| | Freely created | Gate at publication | Why the gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prompt Registry** | any version | evaluated against every supported `(model, dataset)` | the platform cannot demonstrate it works |
| **ICP** | a draft | **≥ 1 product** | the platform cannot act on it |

**The third column is the part that matters most.** In both cases the gate asks *"can the platform execute against this?"* and **never *"is this good?"*** — which is what stops it becoming a validation rule that judges the customer's business. `REFUSED` is a legitimate prompt-evaluation outcome; **a broad ICP is never refused.**

**The corollary is a product rule as much as an engineering one:** *a draft exists for a human; a published artefact exists for the platform.* Friction at creation is a cost paid at the worst possible moment — first use — and moving it to publication costs nothing, because publication is when the customer has decided.

**Where it will recur:** billing plans · feature flag rules · notification rules · automation and workflow definitions · AI playbooks.

### What Lane B is asking for

**Placement, not agreement** — both are already applied in the code. If they belong in `CLAUDE.md` §2, the text above is ready. If they belong in a module document each, that is equally fine and this item closes.

**What Lane B will not do is add them itself.** A repository-wide rule belongs in the governance document rather than in whichever ADR happened to find it — §20e is explicit, and **a principle discovered inside an ICP ADR that lives only there will be rediscovered by the next module that needs it.**


### Closed — Lane B, 2026-08-03, by verification rather than by ruling

**Lane A mounted it in `CX-03` (`e70dd60`) and this register did not notice.** The account brief carries a *What has happened* section rendering `AccountHistory`; the chain is complete end to end — route → component → `useAccountTimeline` → `GET /workspaces/{id}/accounts/{id}/timeline`.

**Verified before closing rather than inferred from the commit message**, which is what the register's *"the requesting lane closes"* rule is for.

**The finding worth keeping is the lag, not the fix.** The item sat `OPEN` — and was classified hours ago as *"the highest-value item on this page, the only one standing between a fully built capability and a customer using it"* — while the capability was already reachable. **A register that describes a gap somebody has closed is worse than one that never recorded it**, because it sends the product owner to answer a question that no longer exists. Both halves are ordinary: Lane A had no reason to edit an item it did not raise, and Lane B was not looking at Timeline that day. **The mechanism that would catch it is a lane re-verifying its own open items before reporting them**, which is what found this one.

## C-1423 · ADR-0408 §1 states something untrue of the repository, and its §20a exemption may have no subject

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-11, verifying [C-287](#c-287)'s premise on Lane A's measurement (`096b9a1c`, their branch) |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — ⛔ **an accepted ADR carries a false factual premise, and a [§20a](../CLAUDE.md) exemption was granted on it. Neither is a lane's to correct** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED **A**, product owner, 2026-08-13** ([D-234](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). ✅ **[ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) §1 corrected in place, the conclusion preserved, the mechanism constrained to the tier that serves the route.** ⛔ **Explicitly NOT a platform-wide rate-limiting programme: no unrelated authentication redesigned, no route moved to satisfy the ADR, no speculative custom policy without an explicit requirement.** ⚡ **The remaining scope is `"memory"` → shared storage, plus per-route policy where a requirement calls for one** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **[TASK-1430](BACKLOG.md) is already `BLOCKED` on [C-287](#c-287) and stays there.** ⚠️ **Lane A spent no implementation time — this was the verification the directive gated on** |

### ✅ Verified independently by this office, not relayed

📁 **Every claim below was re-measured on `lane-c-sync` before being brought here.**

| | Claim | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ | **The installed Better Auth is not the declared one** | `package.json` declares **`^1.1.0`**; `node_modules/better-auth/package.json` reports **`1.6.25`**. ⚡ **This is why the first search found nothing — it read the 1.1-era layout** |
| ✅ | **Better Auth ships a rate limiter** | **`dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs` exists** |
| ✅ | **It is already enabled in this product** | 📁 **`frontend/lib/auth/server.ts`:147 — `rateLimit: { enabled: true }`**, set deliberately because the vendor defaults it to production-only |
| ✅ | **And its refusal already renders** | `app/(auth)/signin/throttled.tsx`, built against a real `429` |
| 🔴 | **Storage resolves to in-process memory** | 📁 **`create-context.mjs`:174 — `storage: options.rateLimit?.storage \|\| (options.secondaryStorage ? "secondary-storage" : "memory")`.** ✅ **`server.ts` configures NEITHER — `grep` returns 0 for `storage:`, `secondaryStorage` and `customRules`** |

### 🔴 So [ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) §1 is false

📁 **It reads: *"nothing stands between a credential-stuffing script and Better Auth."*** ⛔ **Something does, in every mode, and this product already renders its refusal.**

⚠️ **[§2](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit that the repository must not assert something untrue of itself, and an ADR is the strongest place that rule binds** — the ADR is the reason the [§20a](../CLAUDE.md) platform-freeze exemption was granted.

### ⚡ The real gap is smaller than the ADR describes, and it is configuration

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **In-process counters** | **`"memory"` gives an attacker *n* × the budget across *n* replicas and loosens silently as you scale** — ⛔ **precisely what [ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) §9 rejects** |
| ⚠️ **No `customRules`** | **Password-reset request and verification-resend get the DEFAULT policy**, not the tighter one the ADR itself calls *"arguably worse"* — **they make Signora send mail on an attacker's command, needing no credential** |

### The options

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** ✅ **RECOMMENDED** | **Correct §1, keep the ADR, re-scope its subject** | ⚡ **The ADR's *conclusion* survives — Signora needs a Redis-backed limiter with per-route policy.** ⛔ **Its *mechanism* does not: an ASGI middleware in `signora_platform/api/` can never see `/signin` or `/register`, which live in Next.js permanently** ([§13](../CLAUDE.md), [ADR-0026](architecture/adr/0026-jwt-boundary-architecture.md)). ✅ **Two policies, as [C-287](#c-287) recommends: the vendor's facility configured with `secondaryStorage` + `customRules` for authentication, and a re-scoped Python middleware whose row says *the business API*.** ⚡ **[§9 and §13](../CLAUDE.md): authentication is bought, never built** |
| **B** | **Correct §1 and withdraw the §20a exemption entirely** | ⛔ **Leaves the business API unguarded and discards a conclusion that is still right** |
| **C** | **Build the ASGI middleware as written** | 🔴 **The outcome Lane A refused, and correctly.** ⚡ **It would guard sixteen routers that already require a verified JWT, satisfy the ADR and the exemption, and flip `production-readiness.py` to ✅ while `/signin` still had memory-backed counters.** ⛔ **The gap plus a green light — strictly worse than the gap** |

### ⚠️ A second finding, and it is about the probe rather than the product

📁 **[D-213](DECISION_REGISTER.md) records `production-readiness.py` matching `rate.?limit\|throttl` and reporting green on **38 outbound files** — vendor calls, the opposite concern.** ⛔ **The correction to inbound-only then searched `backend/`.** 🔴 **Authentication does not live in `backend/` and permanently cannot** ([§13](../CLAUDE.md)). ⚡ **Wrong direction, then wrong tier, both times confidently green.** ✅ **Whoever fixes the probe should assert against `frontend/lib/auth/`, and the assertion that discriminates is `storage`, not `enabled`**

### ⛔ The minimum decision

> **Correct ADR-0408 §1, and rule whether its §20a exemption re-scopes to the business API (A) or is withdrawn (B).**

⚡ **Nothing is blocked either way.** ✅ **Under A the configuration half needs no new dependency — `redis>=5.2` is already present, `require_redis_url()` exists, and Better Auth's `secondaryStorage` is the vendor's own seam**

### 1 · The audit's first finding: it is already built, and reachable

**The brief describes a capability to build. The repository already has most of it, and every part of it is reachable** — which is the opposite of what the last three assignments found, and it changes what this initiative is.

| Customer question | Where it is answered today |
|---|---|
| *"What should I work on?"* | **`/`** — the attention list. Score, movement, hypothesis, contested mark, evidence health, ownership |
| *"Why this account?"* | **`/accounts/{id}`** — the brief: workflow stage, momentum, contributions, *what it cannot tell you* |
| *"Prove it."* | The **evidence drawer**, opened from a citation |
| *"What did we observe?"* | **`ValidationBlock`** — signals as the evidence layer under a score |
| *"What happened?"* | **`AccountHistory`** — the timeline, mounted by Lane A in `CX-03` |
| *"Go find out more."* | **`ResearchPanel`** — AI research, on the brief |
| *"I'm working this."* | **`WorkflowActions`** and `DecisionHistory` |

**Every backend endpoint has a frontend caller and every hook is used.** Checked rather than assumed: `useAccounts`, `useDecidedAccounts`, `useAccountScore`, `useAccountValidation`, `useSignalCatalog`, `useAccountNarration`, `useAccountResearch`, `useAccountTimeline` — all consumed by a rendered screen. **There is no unreachable capability in this area**, which was the defect class the last three audits kept finding.

**One item closed as a result:** [C-024](#c-024--timeline-has-a-surface-and-nowhere-to-mount-it), which this register still described as *"the highest-value item on this page — no customer can open it"*. Lane A mounted it. **Verified end to end and closed by Lane B**, the requesting lane.

### 2 · So the work is not building it — it is the open findings against it

[39-product-review-findings.md](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) already holds the audit somebody would otherwise redo. **Fourteen open findings sit in this capability**, including four 🔴:

| | |
|---|---|
| **R1-01** 🔴 | *"Why now"* says the same thing eleven times. `ScoreTrigger` answers *why the score was recomputed* — a pipeline event — where a seller asks *why this company matters today* |
| **R1-02** 🔴 | Trigger and evidence state contradict each other on the same row. Both correct, both read as a defect — *"one of these is wrong and I don't know which, so I don't trust either"* |
| **R10-01** 🔴 | There is exactly one exit from the brief, and it is backwards |
| **R11-01** 🔴 | Nine of twenty lifecycle stages implemented; five more built and unreachable |

> **Rebuilding this experience would discard fourteen findings from real product review and replace a working surface with an unreviewed one.** The reuse policy's strongest form applies: **the experience evolves, and the findings are the backlog.**

### 3 · The ownership conflict, stated precisely

**[`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`](ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md) records Product Surface as *"Lane A — assigned, and not released"***, with `PS-01…08` and `CX-01…03` built. **That is where this experience's frontend lives**: `app/(app)/page.tsx`, `app/(app)/accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx`, and all fourteen `components/intelligence/*`.

**`CLAUDE.md` §20e's hardest invariant is one assignee per module at a time**, and it is the one that makes a claim refusable. **Lane B will not edit Lane A's module**, and raising it is what §20e requires rather than a manufactured pause — it is exactly *"repository ownership prevents implementation"*, one of the five conditions the product owner named.

**The split is clean, which is what makes this answerable rather than awkward:**

| Half | Module | Assignee | Lane B can start? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The intelligence** — what a row *says*, and why | `buying_score_engine` · `signal_engine` · `opportunity_engine` | **Unassigned** | **Yes, now** |
| **The surface** — how it reads, navigates and flows | Product Surface | **Lane A** | **No** |

**R1-01 is the worked example.** Its root cause is a **backend** read model: the row's most valuable line carries `ScoreTrigger`, which cannot discriminate between two accounts because it describes a pipeline event. **Making it carry something commercially meaningful — the strongest contributing signal — is a change in modules nobody holds.** Rendering it is Lane A's. One finding, two lanes, and the ordering is obvious: the field has to exist before a row can show it.

### 4 · What Lane B proposes, and what it will do meanwhile

| 1 | **Does Lane B take the three engines** and leave Product Surface with Lane A — the two-lane build [C-007](#c-007--the-guided-first-run-is-a-two-lane-build) already established as a pattern? |

**Lane B's recommendation is 1**, on the evidence that the surface is Lane A's most recent work — `CX-01…03` shipped days ago — and reassigning a module somebody is mid-context on costs more than it saves.

**Meanwhile, and without waiting:** Lane B begins **R1-01** in the engines, because it is 🔴, its root cause is unambiguously backend, and its fix is a prerequisite for the row change rather than a duplicate of it. **No frontend file is touched until this item is answered.**

## C-308 · Browser→API is in no gate, and that is how the product shipped without one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-03, End-to-End Product Validation |
| **Owner** | **QE** — every gate named here is QE's |
| **Status** | `OPEN` |
| **Blocks** | Nothing today. **The next defect of this class**, which will look exactly like the last four |

**The question.** *Which gate would have caught [B-303](BUGS.md)?* The answer is none, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight.

| Layer | Proven by | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| the API | ~2000 backend tests | the endpoint is correct |
| the components | Vitest, with mocked hooks | the component renders what it is given |
| the token exchange | `make smoke`, minting through the real path | the cross-tier JWT contract holds |
| **the browser reaching the API** | **nothing** | — |

`make smoke` mints a real token through the real frontend issuance path and then calls **the API directly**. That is a genuine and valuable check of the JWT boundary, and it steps over the one hop a customer's browser actually makes. `/api/proxy` therefore 404'd from `ad52e66` (M1.2) to today with every gate green.

**What Lane B has built, and what it does not settle.** `frontend/tests/e2e/` now signs in and drives the real browser against the real API, so the hop is exercised. **Whether that suite becomes a gate is QE's decision, not a lane's** — it needs a running application and a seeded organization, which is a prerequisite `make smoke` does not currently establish.

**The recommendation, offered as input.** `npm run test:e2e:smoke` is eight tests and about forty seconds, and it is the shortest thing that would have failed on all three of B-303, B-304 and B-305. Where it belongs — a new gate, a stage of `make smoke`, or QE's validation runbook — is QE's to decide.

**Extended 2026-08-03, with a second finding of the same class — and this one was Lane B's own.** `playwright.config.ts` defaulted `SIGNORA_APP_URL` to `http://localhost:3000`, **Human Review's stack**. Harmless while the suite only read; **not harmless once it began writing** products, watched companies and permanent attributed decisions. **This is the cycle-25 pattern exactly** — one operation mutating an environment another owns — and it is fixed the way [`RELEASE_ENGINEERING.md`](RELEASE_ENGINEERING.md) §7 concluded that class should be: **prevention, not detection.** The suite now refuses to start without an explicit URL and refuses ports 3000/8000 outright, and `make e2e` / `make product-demo` run inside `infra/environment-lease.py` **unchanged**.

> **Nothing new was built for isolation, and QE should know that no second environment model exists.** A lane's row in [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md#running-a-lane) already *is* the isolation; RE-05 stays deprioritised; RE-03 stays unbuilt. The one new decision is that **`make e2e` re-seeds before running**, because the workflow journeys record real decisions and a suite whose result depends on how many times it has been run is not a suite.

**One documentation debt this raises, and it is not Lane B's to pay.** The four fixes land in files [`37-product-surface.md`](architecture/37-product-surface.md) describes — the shell, the auth client, the browser's API client — and **that design doc has no account of how the browser reaches the API**, which is precisely the gap that let the hop go unbuilt. Under rotation the next lane assigned Product Surface inherits that document and nothing else (§12). **Lane B has not edited it**: a design doc is 🟢 for the module's *assignee*, and Lane B is not it. The sentence it needs is *"the browser never calls the API directly; `lib/api/client.ts` routes through `app/api/proxy/[...path]`, which forwards the caller's own token and decides nothing"* — offered here so the current assignee can add it.

**The pattern this is the fourth instance of.** [B-024](BUGS.md) · [B-301](BUGS.md) · [B-302](BUGS.md) · [B-303](BUGS.md). **Every component proven; the composition between them never exercised.** [C-301](#c-301--nothing-asserts-what-the-deployed-worker-consumes) asks for the assertion at the worker boundary; this asks the same question at the browser boundary. **They may well be one item, and QE is the one lane that can see both.**
