## C-307 · Signora cannot say who anybody is

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — **it is a product-capability question** (*"the product cannot tell me who my colleagues are"*), **grouped with People Intelligence beside [C-203](#c-203--nothing-in-the-product-can-render-a-persons-name) and [C-210](#c-210--will-signora-hold-personal-data).** ⚠️ **Owner cell added 2026-08-08 — the item stated its owner inside `Status` prose, where no instrument can read it and no reader can find it.** ⛔ **That is [C-213](#c-213)'s class: an owner that is *derivable* rather than *visible*, and derivable is not visible.** |
| **Decision required** | Where a person's **display identity** lives, given that Better Auth owns the account and the Python tier only verifies tokens |
| **Participating modules** | `signora_platform/auth` (frozen 🔴, verification only) · `workspace_tenancy` (**Lane A — Team Management**) · Product Surface (**Lane A**) · a new home, unowned |
| **Current assignee(s)** | **Product owner** — a recommendation is stated below and **Lane B is proceeding on it rather than waiting** |
| **Blocking** | **Nothing Lane B intends to build.** Named because the answer changes where one table goes |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-03, by Lane B, assigned User Profile, **after the reuse audit and before any code** |
| **Status** | 🟣 **`OPEN` — PARKED, CORRECTLY. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** ✅ **Strategic, and its own trigger is named.** ⛔ **Out of the active product owner queue and not raised again until its trigger fires** |

### 1 · The audit's finding, and it is not "there is no profile screen"

**Nothing in this repository can turn a user id into a human being.** Verified rather than assumed — `grep` finds no name resolution of any kind in `lib/` or `components/`.

| Where a person appears | What a customer sees |
|---|---|
| Who owns an account (`Ownership`) | **`Yours`** or **`Taken`** — the product compares to the viewer because it cannot name the other person |
| Who moved a stage (`DecisionHistory`) | a UUID |
| Who published an ICP, who last changed a segment | a UUID — **including in Lane B's own ICP-01 work** |
| Who is in this organization (`MembershipResponse`) | `user_id`, and nothing else |

> **The customer problem is not *"I want to edit my name."* It is *"the product cannot tell me who my colleague is."*** Every collaborative feature already shipped is degraded by it, and every one planned — mentions, assignment, approvals, comments, presence — is blocked by it.

**`Taken` is the sharpest evidence.** It is a well-written fallback for a fact the platform does not have, and it will keep being written until the fact exists.

### 2 · What already exists, and must not be duplicated

| | |
|---|---|
| **Better Auth** | Owns the account: `name` is collected at sign-up, plus email, verification, sessions, linked accounts, password. **[ADR-0026](architecture/adr/0026-jwt-boundary-architecture.md) makes it the sole Authentication Authority** |
| **The JWT** | Carries `sub`, `sid`, `email`, `email_verified`, `active_workspace_id`. **It does not carry `name`** |
| **`AuthenticatedPrincipal`** | The Python tier's whole knowledge of a caller — and `signora_platform/auth` is **frozen** (§20a) |
| **`membership`** | `user_id` + role. Deliberately no user model: [ADR-0010](architecture/adr/0010-identity-and-access.md) — *"Signora does not own the user identity model"* |

**So the account is Better Auth's, and nothing is Signora's.** That is correct and is not the question.

### 3 · The question, stated exactly

> **A display identity is not authentication.** *"What should we call you, and what should your colleagues see?"* is a product fact about a person; *"are you who you say you are"* is Better Auth's. **Signora needs the first and must not own the second.**

| | Option | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Add `name` to the JWT** | Cheapest. **But a token is a snapshot** — a rename shows nowhere until re-issue, it cannot answer *"who is user X?"* for a colleague you have no token for, and it widens a frozen boundary for a non-security fact |
| **B** ✅ | **Signora owns a `user_profile`**, keyed by the Better Auth user id, holding display identity only | Answers *"who is X?"* for anybody. Renames are immediate. **Better Auth stays the sole Authentication Authority**; this owns no credential, no verification, no session |
| **C** | **Query Better Auth from Python** | A synchronous cross-tier read on every screen that shows a person, and it makes the Python tier depend on the auth tier's storage — which [ADR-0026](architecture/adr/0026-jwt-boundary-architecture.md) exists to prevent |

**Lane B recommends B**, and the boundary that keeps it honest: **the profile holds what a colleague may see, and never what proves who you are.** Email stays the JWT's, password and sessions stay Better Auth's, and the profile is a display fact — the same split ADR-0034 draws between the customer's words and the platform's.

**Where it lives** is the part genuinely open: a new bounded context, or `workspace_tenancy` — which already answers *"who is in this organization?"* and is **Lane A's Team Management capability**. Lane B's position: **a profile is not workspace-scoped** — one person, many organizations, one name — so putting it in a workspace-scoped module would be the first row there with no `workspace_id`, which is a strong signal it does not belong.

### 4 · What Lane B is building meanwhile, and why it is not blocked

**The first slice touches no file either Lane A or the platform owns:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **New** | A profile aggregate and its table · `GET`/`PUT /me/profile` · **`/settings/profile`, a route that does not exist** |
| **Customer value** | *"I can tell Signora what to call me, and see it."* Demoable on its own |
| **Not touched** | `signora_platform/auth` (frozen) · `membership` and its schemas (Lane A) · `Ownership`, `DecisionHistory`, the attention row (Lane A) |

**Rendering a colleague's name on an existing surface is the second slice and is Lane A's**, exactly as [C-306](#c-306--the-opportunities-and-signals-experience-already-exists-and-lane-a-owns-half-of-it) splits. **The fact has to exist before a screen can show it**, which is the same ordering R1-01 has.

**Answer needed only for:** whether the table lives in a new context or in `workspace_tenancy`. **Lane B proceeds on B with a new context**, and will move it if ruled otherwise — a table with no consumers is cheap to relocate, and waiting is not.


### 5 · Implementation reached a tenancy question, and it is [C-302](#c-302--a-notification-is-per-person-and-workspace-rls-is-not-enough)'s twin

**Lane B began building and stopped at the first table, for a reason that is one of the product owner's five named stop conditions.**

**Every workspace-owned table in this repository is scoped by `workspace_id`.** A profile is not: **one person, many organizations, one name.** It has no `workspace_id`, so it satisfies neither classification the Tenant Isolation Policy offers — it is not tenant-owned (no tenant identifier) and it is certainly not platform infrastructure.

**The precedent that nearly solves it, and does not.** `workspace` and `membership` have been RLS-scoped on `app.user_id` since migration `0001`, so **user-scoped RLS is proven here**. But `workspace` qualifies as tenant-owned because **it is the tenancy root — its own `id` is the tenant identifier.** A profile has no such claim. **It is the first table that is genuinely user-scoped rather than workspace-scoped**, and that is a tenancy-model question rather than a module one.

**The policy itself is ordinary and reuses a shape already in the repository** — *you may read a profile belonging to anybody you share a workspace with*, which is `workspace_select`'s membership `EXISTS` inverted:

```sql
USING (
  user_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid
  OR user_id IN (
    SELECT m.user_id FROM membership m
     WHERE m.workspace_id IN (
       SELECT workspace_id FROM membership
        WHERE user_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid)
  )
)
```

### The alternative that avoids the ruling, and why Lane B rejected it

**A workspace-scoped *membership* profile** — *"what this person is called in this organization"* — fits the existing model exactly, needs no ruling, and ships today. Some products do it (Slack). **Lane B is not building it.**

> **A person in three organizations would have three names that drift.** That is duplicated truth **forced by the model**, which is precisely the failure [ADR-0041](architecture/adr/0041-icp-aggregate.md) §2 reversed a recommendation to avoid six hours after making it. Choosing it here to dodge a decision would repeat, deliberately, the mistake that review caught.

### Why this is worth answering once rather than twice

**[C-302](#c-302--a-notification-is-per-person-and-workspace-rls-is-not-enough) asked the same question for notifications**: a notification is a fact about a *person*, and workspace RLS lets any member read a colleague's read state. **Two capabilities are now blocked on one missing decision**, which is better evidence than either alone — the repository has reached the point where *per-person data* is a category, not an exception.

**Lane B recommends ruling once, on the general shape:** *a table may carry a second RLS predicate scoping rows to `app.user_id`, and a table whose subject is a person rather than an organization is classified user-owned.* That answers notifications, profiles, and everything that follows them.

**What is not blocked:** nothing in User Profile. The profile table is the foundation and every slice needs it. **Lane B is not building a screen over a table shape it expects to migrate.**


### Evidence from the end-to-end journey review — Lane B, 2026-08-03

*Appended by Lane B, not the item's owner. **Nothing here changes C-012, its owner or its status** — the decision remains the product owner's RFC. What is new is the cost, measured for the first time by walking the product as a customer rather than by reading the item.*

**Seven of nine pipeline consumers are unregistered in the deployed worker.** Verified twice from `apps/worker/subscriptions.py`: only `timeline.project` and `ai_research_engine.run_requested` are registered, and the second is a self-loop. `provider_platform.sync_declared_targets`, `knowledge_graph.resolve_identity`, `observation_engine.observe_changes`, `business_event_engine.detect`, `signal_engine.generate`, `buying_score_engine.compute` and `opportunity_engine.qualify` are **written, tested and never registered.** `backend/tests/pipeline.py` is the only composition root that wires them.

**What that costs, stated as a customer journey rather than as a gap:**

> **A customer can sign up, create an organization, invite their team, declare what they sell, describe who buys it, name the buying committee, state their focus, and name the companies they want watched — and nothing will ever happen.**

**`commercial_profile.target_accounts_changed` is published into the outbox, the relay delivers it, and no consumer exists.** The first hand-off in the product is also the last, and **sixteen built, reviewed screens are correct and permanently empty** because the pipeline that fills them never runs.

**Timeline made it visible rather than fixing it.** Since [B-301](BUGS.md), Timeline projects nine event types faithfully — and **six have no producer in a deployed environment**, so an account's history will show the declaration and nothing after it.

**This does not change what C-012 asks.** A handler still needs a defined relationship to the dispatcher's transaction, and that is still an RFC. **Two consumers now work around it in different ways** — AI Research holds a session factory on the runtime, Timeline is idempotent by derived identity and needs no transaction share — and **neither pattern has been ratified**, which is exactly what the item exists to prevent becoming permanent by accident.

**Recorded in full in [48-customer-journey-review.md](architecture/48-customer-journey-review.md) §1**, with the stage-by-stage journey behind it.


### A second consideration for C-308, from Lane B — 2026-08-03

*Appended by the raising lane. **Nothing here changes C-308, its owner or its status.*** What is new is a constraint on the answer, found by running the suite from a clean terminal.

**If `test:e2e:smoke` becomes a gate, it must be runnable by somebody who has read nothing.** [B-311](BUGS.md): the suite depended on an exported `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` that lived in one terminal and in no document, so the same commit passed 119/119 in one shell and failed 128/128 in another — **`browserType.launch` on every test, which reads as a catastrophically broken product rather than as a missing variable.**

That is fixed at the root (`browserEnvironment()` in `tests/e2e/fixtures/environment.ts`), and the general point survives the fix: **a browser gate has a system-library surface that no other gate in this repository has.** WebKit still needs forty packages and `sudo`. Whatever QE decides C-308's answer is, *"the gate cannot start"* and *"the product is broken"* must not look the same from the outside — which argues for the gate to fail loudly on a launch failure with its own message, rather than reporting N red tests.

## C-320 · No environment can complete a sign-up, so nobody has reviewed the first hour

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Three explicit execution modes.** ***"During development, do not allow missing infrastructure to unnecessarily block UI implementation. However, do not introduce shortcuts that misrepresent production behavior."*** ⚡ **The item asked two questions and the ruling answers the second, which is the one that was blocking**: *"until then, how does anybody experience a customer's first hour?"* — **by the front door, in Development Mode, with the real link.** ⛔ **The first — *where and when does Signora get an email transport* — stays a vendor decision with deployment, and no longer blocks review.** **[ADR-0406](architecture/adr/0406-authentication-execution-modes.md) drafted; [TASK-455](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-473](BACKLOG.md) implement it.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-03, Product Experience Review 3 |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — it is a deployment decision, not an implementation one |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field written in the same change as the ruling, per [D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md)**: *"a decision recorded only in prose is effectively invisible to the repository."* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md). **Three explicit execution modes.** ⚡ **The item asked two questions and the ruling answers the one that was blocking**: *"until then, how does anybody experience a customer's first hour?"* — **by the front door, in Development Mode, with the real link.** ⛔ **The first — *where and when does Signora get an email transport* — stays a vendor decision with deployment.** **[ADR-0406](architecture/adr/0406-authentication-execution-modes.md) approved at [D-134](DECISION_REGISTER.md); [TASK-455](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-473](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-474](BACKLOG.md) implement it.** ⚠️ **Restored 2026-08-06 after a rebase reverted it.** |
| **Blocks** | **Reviewing the most commercially important hour in the product.** Blocks no implementation |

**The question.** *Where, and when, does Signora get an email transport — and until then, how does anybody experience a customer's first hour?*

**What is true today, and none of it is a defect.** `createEmailTransport` returns a console transport; `loadAuthConfig` **refuses to start in production with it**, deliberately, so a misconfigured deployment stops rather than silently emailing nobody. The `.example` addresses can never resolve, deliberately, so no build can email a real person by accident. **Every one of those decisions is correct.**

**The consequence nobody has stated.** Sign-up requires email verification (`requireEmailVerification: true`, and rightly — it is what makes the `email_verified` claim mean anything). The link goes to a terminal. **So in every environment this team possesses, including Human Review, a new customer's first hour ends at *"check your email"*.**

**And therefore:** every account that has ever existed in Signora was created by `demo-users.ts`, which mints a verification token and redeems it through `auth.api.verifyEmail`. **The front door is fully implemented and has never been walked.**

> **This is the pattern that produced [B-303](BUGS.md), [B-301](BUGS.md), [B-302](BUGS.md) and [B-024](BUGS.md)** — *every component proven, the composition never exercised.* It is the fifth instance, and the first one where the unexercised composition is **the customer's path into the product**.

**What Lane B is not asking for.** Not a vendor, not an ADR, not an implementation. **A decision on sequencing**: whether a transport belongs to M14.5 with the rest of deployment, or earlier because it gates the review of onboarding — which is now a named priority for this lane. **Proceeding needs no answer**; reviewing the first hour properly does.

## C-321 · What should Signora do with a company it cannot name?

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Adopt Lane B's proposed behaviour. Proceed."* All six sub-answers stand: appear **yes** · working list **no** · score **yes** · opportunity **no** · workable **never** · **`Needs identity`, its own queue.** **[TASK-400](BACKLOG.md)'s A6 half is unblocked.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-03, Product Experience Reviews 1–3 |
| **Owner** | **Product owner**, with `knowledge_graph` and `opportunity_engine` |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner |
| **Blocks** | **Epic A's A6**, which is this item under a slice's name *(raised from* nothing today, *2026-08-03)*. Also [PX-301](PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md) and [PX-316](PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md) |

**The question**, and it is a product-philosophy one rather than a screen fix: **identity and significance are different axes, and the attention list currently multiplies them into one number.**

A record can be highly significant and unidentifiable — `70b04700` has four weeks of elevated research on Design Systems, peaking at 87, and no name. **That combination is genuinely interesting and genuinely not actionable**, and today the product offers *"I'm working this"* on it.

**Six sub-questions, with Lane B's recommendation as input rather than authority:**

| | Recommended |
|---|---|
| Should an unnamed company appear at all? | **Yes** — hiding it discards real intelligence |
| On the working list? | **No** — that list answers *"who should I call?"* |
| Contribute to a score? | **Yes** — the score measures evidence, and the evidence is real |
| Become an opportunity? | **No** — an opportunity is something a person can pursue |
| Be workable? | **Never.** Today it is |
| What is it, then? | **`Needs identity` — a queue with its own workflow**, not a filter |

**Why it is a coordination item rather than a bug.** Whichever answer is taken changes `knowledge_graph`'s output contract, `opportunity_engine`'s qualification rule, and a Product Surface screen. **Two lanes would otherwise encode contradictory halves of it**, which is precisely what this register exists to prevent.

> ### Sharpened 2026-08-03 by Epic A's A6 reuse audit — and it now blocks a scheduled slice
>
> **`Blocks` above said *nothing today*. It now blocks A6**, which is this item wearing a slice's name: *"`Needs identity` — unnamed records leave the working list"* is the recommendation in the last row of the table above.
>
> **Two things the audit settled, so the ruling does not have to.**
>
> **1 · No new workflow state is warranted.** The proposed lifecycle *Unknown → Needs Identity → Named → Qualified → Opportunity* is two existing lifecycles glued together: the first three are **derived** from `NameAgreement` and `IdentityState` on every request, and the last two **are** `opportunity_engine`'s `Stage`, already stored, append-only and audited. A single stored enum would be a third representation of facts two modules own (§2). **The decision is about behaviour, not about a state machine.**
>
> **2 · *"Needs identity"* is two situations, and the ruling should say which one it means — or rule on both.**
>
> | | **An ambiguous binding** | **An account nobody has named** |
> |---|---|---|
> | Does an account exist? | **No** — `entity_id` is `None` by design; binding one would be the merge the graph refuses | **Yes**, and it is on the attention list today |
> | Read over | bindings | entities |
> | The customer's action | *"which company is this?"* | *"what is this company called?"* |
> | Evidenced | Not yet observed in the Playground | **Yes** — [PX-301](PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md), `70b04700`, peaking at 87 with no name |
>
> **The six sub-questions above are all about the second.** The first has no screen anywhere and, unlike the second, is not currently offering a customer a button that cannot work.
>
> **Lane B has built nothing against this and is not proceeding on an assumption.** The derivable read is three lines on top of `identities()` and is worthless without knowing what the queue *does*, so it is recorded rather than built.

## C-322 · Is an ICP a description, or a filter?

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** > ## **An ICP is a declarative filter evaluated against observed customer attributes.** **The repository had already taken this direction through implementation, and the documentation now describes reality rather than an open question.** **[C-332](#c-332--the-predicate-landed-and-task-406-still-cannot-call-it--nothing-builds-its-input-and-the-module-that-measures-may-not-reach-one) completes it**


> ⏸️ ~~**`DEFERRED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Keep grouped with [C-002](#c-002). Do not split. **Review when Epic B1 begins.**"*~~
>
> ## ⚡ **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` — 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md). The trigger fired early, and not because Epic B1 began.**
>
> **[TASK-434](BACKLOG.md) shipped `evaluate(icp, observed)` and it is `PROMOTED`** — **a predicate that measures an account against a declaration is the *filter* reading, built.** **[D-077](DECISION_REGISTER.md) sequenced it deliberately, ahead of its first consumer.** ⛔ **So the repository has already taken half of position B while this item records the question as open** — and [C-332](#c-332--the-predicate-landed-and-task-406-still-cannot-call-it--nothing-builds-its-input-and-the-module-that-measures-may-not-reach-one) is the other half asking to be finished.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-03, Product Capability Audit ([481](architecture/481-product-capability-audit.md) §2.4, §4b) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner**, with `commercial_profile` and `buying_score_engine` |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this field was not.** **Twelve items carried the same defect**, and every one would have been escalated as an open question. |
| **Blocks** | **Epic B1.** And it is why the product currently contradicts itself on screen |

**The contradiction, measured.** *Your business* says Signora needs the catalogue *"before it can tell you anything useful about anyone else's company"*. A freshly seeded organization has **no products and twelve scored accounts** ([PX-314](PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md)). **One of those two screens is wrong**, and which one is a product decision.

**The two positions, and each is coherent.**

| | **A description** *(today)* | **A filter** *(the vision document)* |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | The customer's words, versioned, ungraded — *"Signora records what you say here; it does not grade anyone against it"* ([40-commercial-profile.md](architecture/40-commercial-profile.md)) | A query: `size > 500 AND uses AWS AND hiring "AI Engineer"`, with a live preview |
| Scoring | Runs regardless. **Relevance is judged against the signal catalog, not the customer's ICP** | Relevance is measured against the declaration; an account outside it scores lower or not at all |
| Strength | Nothing to get wrong; no false precision | The catalogue becomes load-bearing, and *Your business* becomes true |
| Cost | **The declaration is decorative** — it changes nothing a customer can observe | Somebody must express an ICP in structured terms, which is harder than describing one |

**Lane B's input, not authority.** **The claim model already supports the filter reading** — `claim(attribute, value, observed_at)` is the shape a query needs, and no new storage is required. **And a hybrid is available**: keep the prose declaration as the customer-facing artifact, derive a structured predicate from it, and let scoring consume the predicate. That preserves *"in your words, not ours"* while making the words consequential.

**Why it is a coordination item.** Whichever answer is taken changes `buying_score_engine`'s relevance rule and `commercial_profile`'s public contract. **Two lanes would otherwise encode contradictory halves**, and one of them is already shipped.

## C-323 · Epic A was assigned to Lane B, and Lane A is already building it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-03, on being assigned Epic A — **found by reading Lane A's branch before writing a line, not by reading this register** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED` 2026-08-03** — the product owner ruled on the day it was raised |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing.** It blocked A4, A1 and two renders for the length of one review |

> ### Ruled — option A, and wider than option A
>
> **Lane B owns Epic A end to end**: backend, read models, public contracts, API composition, Knowledge Graph, Provider Platform, Product Surface, routing, UI, UX, navigation, workflows, tests and documentation. **Lane A keeps Sales Workspace** and its roadmap.
>
> **Module boundaries are unchanged and bind exactly as before.** What moved is implementation ownership, not architecture: a slice crossing two modules is still two proper extensions through two `public/` contracts, and *"Epic A needs it"* is not a licence to shortcut one.
>
> **A2 and B2 stay struck.** Lane A's implementations stand; [51](architecture/51-implementation-specifications.md) records where each lives and what the original proposal got wrong. **The *Questions instead of Filters* finding is promoted to product philosophy** rather than left in a struck slice.
>
> **What the ruling rejected, and it is the part worth recording:** splitting Epic A by layer. *"Surface what already exists"* is not backend work with a frontend attached — it is one capability per slice, and **a split would have made every slice a coordination item.** This lane proposed the split; the product owner was right that it optimises the wrong thing.

**The problem.** The product owner assigned Lane B as implementation owner for Epic A, and instructed in the same message: *"continue respecting ownership boundaries · do not quietly bypass module boundaries."* **Those two instructions are in direct conflict, because every slice in Epic A lands in a module Lane A holds and has not released.**

**The evidence, measured on `origin/lane-a-product-surface` at `db373db`.** 128 files, ~19,000 lines ahead of `integration`.

| Epic A slice | What Lane B was asked to build | What is already there |
|---|---|---|
| **A2** — *"if a seller owns 2,000 accounts, how do they progressively narrow the space until only today's work remains?"* | The accounts workspace | **`SW-01`…`SW-04`, this week.** `TriageStrip`, `lib/state/triage.ts`, URL-driven narrowing, `triage-strip.test.tsx`, `triage.test.ts`. SW-04's own handoff: *"Two more questions appear above the account list … and each narrows the list"* |
| **B2** — the first-run path | The empty-state journey | **Built.** `first-run.test.tsx`, against D36 |
| **A4** · **A1** · **A5** · **A6** | Freshness · search · company history · needs identity | **Not built** — but each needs `provider_platform`'s `public/`, Product Surface, or both |

**Had Lane B followed the instruction literally, it would have re-implemented A2 and B2 in parallel with the lane that was shipping them.** That is the exact failure the Task Claim Protocol exists to prevent, occurring one level up: **the protocol arbitrates tasks, and nothing arbitrates epics.**

**Affected modules.** `provider_platform` (Lane A, `BLOCKED`/Implementation Waiting) · Product Surface (Lane A, `ACTIVE`) · `knowledge_graph` (**unassigned**) · `opportunity_engine` (Lane B).

**The alternatives.**

| | What it means | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Reassign Product Surface and `provider_platform` to Lane B** | The board changes; Lane A moves off | **Lane A is 128 files into an initiative.** Reassigning mid-flight discards the most expensive thing the lane model has — accumulated engineering context — and the Sales Workspace is not at a slice boundary |
| **B · Epic A goes to Lane A; Lane B keeps the specification role** | Lane A implements what Lane B specified | Honest and cheap. **But it makes Lane B a document-producing lane**, which the product owner has twice said is not what they want |
| **C · Split by layer — Lane B builds backend, Lane A renders** | Lane B: the `knowledge_graph` reads, `opportunity_engine` composition, the freshness derivation. Lane A: every screen | **Works today for A5 and A6.** Fails for A4, whose port is in Lane A's `provider_platform`, and for A1, whose endpoint has no owning module at all |
| **D · Split by module, and move `provider_platform`'s Epic-A port only** | Lane B takes `knowledge_graph` outright, plus a single named port in `provider_platform` | Narrow, auditable, and does not touch the surface Lane A is live in. **Needs Lane A to agree to one file** |

**Lane B's recommendation — D, then C.** Take `knowledge_graph` now and build A5 and A6's backends, which collide with nobody and are the two slices whose *data* work is the real content. Ask Lane A for the one `provider_platform` port A4 needs. **Leave every screen with Lane A while the Sales Workspace is in flight**, and revisit when it reaches a slice boundary.

**The trade-off this accepts.** **Epic A stops being one lane's epic**, and the product owner's stated goal — one owner converting hidden capability into visible product — is not achieved by any of these four. **A is the only option that achieves it, and it is the most expensive.** That choice is the product owner's, not a lane's, which is why this is here rather than decided.

**Implementation impact.** Until this is answered: A4 and A1 cannot start · A5 and A6 build backend-only and wait for a render · A2 and B2 should be **struck from Epic A** rather than built, and [51-implementation-specifications.md](architecture/51-implementation-specifications.md) has been corrected to say so.

> **This is the second time in three days.** [C-306](#c-306--the-opportunities-and-signals-experience-already-exists-and-lane-a-owns-half-of-it) found the same shape in Opportunities & Signals. **The pattern is not bad luck: Lane B keeps being assigned initiatives whose customer surface is Product Surface, and Product Surface has one permanent-feeling assignee.** Whatever is decided for Epic A, the third occurrence is already scheduled unless the allocation model changes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **The C-323 ruling** | Lane B owns Epic A **end to end** — *"backend implementation, read models, public contracts, API composition, Knowledge Graph, Provider Platform, Product Surface implementation, frontend implementation, routing, UI, UX, navigation, interaction model, visual hierarchy, customer workflows"* |
| **The later clarification** | Lane B owns Epic A *"except for **Product Surface rendering that belongs to Lane A**"* — and the list of owned responsibilities that follows it is entirely backend |

**They cannot both be applied to the same slice, and the same message resolved A1 in favour of the first**: the shell mount was approved, the component tests were requested, and the push was authorised without further approval. **A1 shipped on that reading.**

**Why it needs answering before A5 rather than now.** A4 was one line on an existing page. A1 was one control. **A5 is a screen** — *"how do we let a customer understand years of company evolution in seconds?"*, which the product owner has already said is *"a place where visual design becomes more important than engineering"*. **A6 introduces a workflow**, not just a view. On the second reading almost none of either is Lane B's, and on the first, all of it is.

**Lane B's reading, offered as input and not as authority.** The distinction that actually held in A1 is the one the product owner drew when approving the shell change — **the shell owns *placement*, the feature owns *behaviour*.** Generalised: **Lane A owns the surfaces it is actively building (Sales Workspace, the attention list, the brief's hierarchy); Lane B owns the surfaces Epic A brings into existence.** That is a boundary about *which screens*, not about *which layer*, and it is the one that does not split a slice in half.

**What Lane B is doing meanwhile.** Continuing on work inside its boundaries on **either** reading — A5's backend is a `knowledge_graph` read over `claim.observed_at` and is unambiguously Lane B's. **The screen is not started until this is answered.**

> **A layer boundary makes every Epic A slice a coordination item**, which is the exact cost the product owner rejected when ruling on C-323. That reasoning has not changed; only its application to the frontend is unclear.

## C-325 · B-400's renumber cannot be performed by either lane on its own branch

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-04, on being assigned [B-400](BUGS.md) as priority 1 |
| **Owner** | **QE** — the merge order is the integration authority's, and it is the only input the fix is missing |
| **Status** | `OPEN` — **blocking [B-400](BUGS.md), which blocks promotion for every lane** |
| **Blocks** | Nothing this lane is implementing. **Epic E1 proceeds** |

**[B-400](BUGS.md) is real, and this lane measured it rather than reading it.** With both branches' migration files in one tree:

```
UserWarning: Revision 0031 is present more than once
alembic heads    →  0031, 0035 (two heads)
alembic history  →  FAILED: Requested revision 0035 overlaps with other requested revisions 0031
alembic upgrade head
                 →  FAILED: Multiple head revisions are present for given argument 'head'
```

**Three corrections to the row, all measured.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The target has moved** | B-400 says *"the cheaper renumber is Lane B's single file to `0035`"*. **Lane A took `0035` after that row was written** — `0035_watermark_attempted_at.py`, A7, commit `d8f5832`. The correct target today is **`0036`**, and it will move again the next time either lane adds a migration. **A renumber target computed against a branch you cannot see has a shelf life** |
| **The failure is not a load error** | The row says *"every `alembic` command fails to build the revision map — a hard load error"*. It is a **`UserWarning`**, and the map builds with one of the two `0031` files silently dropped. Commands that name `head` then fail on multiple heads. **The distinction matters**: the first thing a reader tries is `alembic heads`, which *succeeds* and prints two lines |
| **Neither lane can fix it alone** | Measured both ways, below |

### The fix is verified, and it is one file

Renumbering `0031_commercial_profile_segment.py` to `0036` with `down_revision = "0035"`, **in a tree containing Lane A's chain**, gives a single head and a linear graph:

```
0030 -> 0031 invitation -> 0032 -> 0033 -> 0034 -> 0035 watermark -> 0036 segment (head)
```

### And it cannot be applied here

The same file on `lane-b-commercial-profile` alone:

```
KeyError: '0035'
```

**`down_revision` must name a revision that exists in the tree, and Lane A's chain exists only on Lane A's branch.** The symmetry is exact: Lane A cannot renumber its five files onto Lane B's `0031` either, for the same reason.

> **B-400 is not a code defect with an owner. It is a merge-order decision with a consequence**, and the consequence lands on whichever lane rebases second — which is precisely what `CLAUDE.md` §20e already says: *"a lane that finds its number taken renumbers on rebase and says so in the commit message."* **Assigning it to a named lane in advance made it look like an actionable 🔴 when the missing input is a sequencing decision.**

### What QE is being asked for

**One choice, and either resolves it.**

| Order | Who renumbers | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Lane A first, then Lane B** | **Lane B**, one file to `0036` | **Verified above.** Minutes, at this lane's next rebase |
| **Lane B first, then Lane A** | **Lane A**, five files to `0032`–`0036` | Larger, and not this lane's to estimate |

**B-400 named the first, on cost, and that reasoning still holds.** This lane is ready either way: `lane-b-commercial-profile` is rebased onto `1252d02` with its gates green, and the renumber is pre-verified.

**What this lane is doing meanwhile.** **Epic E1**, which touches no migration yet. **If E1 adds one, this lane will number it after whatever head exists at that rebase and say so** — which is the same rule, applied at the only moment it can be applied correctly.

## C-338 · TASK-003 would put customer labels in the file that builds the evidence digest

**Opened 2026-08-07 · Lane B · 🟠 · owner: product owner** *(architectural — the ruling and the code disagree about one file)*

> **Raised rather than worked around.** [C-018](#c-018--nobody-owns-the-customer-facing-name-of-an-attribute) is `RULED` and this lane holds [TASK-003](BACKLOG.md), so the obvious move was to implement it. **Implementing it as written would change evidence identity**, and that is not a thing to discover afterwards.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED **A**, product owner, 2026-08-13, [D-231](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ①.** ⛔ **Do not reopen absent new contradictory evidence** |
| ✅ **THE RULING** | > ⛔ **No label catalog. No rename of canonical attribute names in `explanation.py`. No change to evidence identity or digest construction.**<br><br>📁 **[C-018](#c-018--nobody-owns-the-customer-facing-name-of-an-attribute)'s boundary stands unchanged**: customer-facing terminology belongs in the composed presentation layer · **the canonical representation and evidence identity must remain unchanged** · ⛔ ***"until R11-06 receives real reviewer evidence, do not introduce a terminology transformation merely for readability."***<br><br>⛔ **No new terminology architecture is to be created** |
| **Owner** | — *(was: the product owner)* |
| ⚠️ **What this does NOT do** | ⛔ **It does not make [TASK-003](BACKLOG.md) claimable.** ⚡ **That row's work IS the terminology transformation the ruling forbids**, so releasing it to `READY` would hand a lane exactly what ① prohibits. ✅ **It moves `BLOCKED` → `WAITING` on the trigger the ruling itself names** — 📁 **real reviewer evidence against [R11-06](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md)** — **which is Option A's own stated consequence, written into it before the ruling: *"TASK-003 returns to `WAITING` on that trigger."*** |
| ⚠️ **The three browser translations stay** | 📁 **`employee count` · `Employee count` · `employee_count`, catalogued by [C-018](#c-018--nobody-owns-the-customer-facing-name-of-an-attribute) and still inconsistent.** ⛔ **Not converged here and no row created for it** — **the ruling forbids introducing a transformation for readability, and no task is manufactured to work around that** |
| **Blocked** | **[TASK-003](BACKLOG.md)** — ⛔ **no code was ever written for it, which is why the ruling costs nothing to apply** |

### ① The problem, measured

**[C-018](#c-018--nobody-owns-the-customer-facing-name-of-an-attribute) ruled: *"Customer-facing terminology belongs in `explanation.py`."*** **There is exactly one `explanation.py` in the repository** — `modules/ai_platform/infrastructure/explanation.py` — **and it is the file that assembles the `EvidenceSet`**, not a file that renders wording:

```
assemble(explanation: OpportunityExplanation, *, assembled_at: datetime) -> EvidenceSet
    ... attributes={...}          # three call sites
```

**Those attribute names reach the digest.** `evidence.py:169` renders each fact as `f"{name}={_canonical(value)}"`, and `digest()` hashes exactly that:

```
rendered = "|".join(f"{name}={_canonical(value)}" for name, value in self.attributes)
return hashlib.sha256(f"{self.workspace_id}\x1d{canonical}".encode()).hexdigest()
```

> ⛔ **So renaming `employee_count` to *headcount* in the file the ruling names does not relabel a display. It changes the identity of every piece of evidence that carries the attribute** — and **every stored artifact citing that identity stops matching**, which is the one thing [ADR-0031](architecture/adr/0031-evidence-citation-protocol.md) and the never-repairing validator exist to make impossible.

### ② The affected modules

**`ai_platform`** — `domain/evidence.py`, `domain/rendering.py`, `infrastructure/explanation.py` · **`knowledge_graph`** — where the attribute names originate · **Product Surface** — the three browser translations C-018 already catalogued, which are Lane A's and must not be converged until this is answered.

### ③ The alternatives

| | What it means | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **A · The trigger has not fired** | **[R11-06](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) is *"recorded as a deliberate trade-off, not as debt"*, priority **Low**, milestone ***"on evidence from a real reviewer"*** — and C-018 itself records that **no reviewer evidence exists.** TASK-003 returns to `WAITING` on that trigger | **Nothing.** The three inconsistent browser translations stay, and stay recorded |
| **B · A label catalog, applied strictly at display** | A reviewed catalog of attribute labels, consumed **downstream of `canonical_form()`** — composed wording only, **never the evidence drawer, never the digest** | A new artifact with an owner, a version and a review process. ⚠️ **And the drawer keeps engineering's words**, which is most of what a seller actually reads |
| **C · A label catalog applied in `explanation.py` as ruled** | The literal reading of C-018 | ⛔ **Breaks evidence identity.** **Not recommended, and named only so the ruling's literal reading is on the record as having been considered** |

### ④ Recommendation

> ## **A — the trigger has not fired, and R11-06 says so in its own words.**

**C-018 asked three questions and the ruling answered the second.** Question 1 was *"does an attribute get a customer-facing name **at all**, or is R11-06's *the verbatim-ness is the value* still the ruling?"* — and the ruling named **where** terminology lives without saying **that** it is now wanted. **R11-06's milestone is unmet and its reasoning is still true**: *"prettifying `false` into 'No' would show the reader something different from what was cited."*

**If the answer is B**, this lane will build it — **and the boundary must be written into the row**: the catalog reaches composed wording only, and **the evidence drawer keeps the verbatim names**, because that view exists to show what was cited.

### ⑤ The trade-offs

**Choosing A** leaves a seller reading `contested false · delta 0 · ceiling 120`, which is genuinely poor, and leaves three disagreeing browser translations (`employee count` · `Employee count` · `employee_count`). **Choosing B** buys readable composed sentences and **does not fix the drawer**, which is where the unfriendly text mostly appears — so it may buy less than it looks. **Choosing C** buys the same as B and silently invalidates stored evidence.

### ⑥ Implementation impact

**None until this is answered.** ⛔ **This lane has written no code for TASK-003** and will not, because every implementation encodes an answer to question 1. **Lane A must also not converge the three browser translations meanwhile** — C-018 already says converging them *"would encode the answer to this item"*, and that is still true.

## C-337 · SSH to GitHub is intercepted on this workstation, and the obvious fix is the dangerous one

**Opened 2026-08-07 · Lane B · 🟠 · owner: product owner** *(operational — not a repository defect)*

> **Recorded because the remediation every lane will reach for is `ssh-keygen -R github.com`, and running it is what turns a caught interception into a successful one.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7. ⚙️ OPERATIONAL, never a product decision.** 📁 **Its own status: *the remote is HTTPS and pushes cleanly*.** ⛔ **A workstation condition carried in the product owner's queue for days** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C / the implementing lane** — ⚡ **reassigned 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7: operational or sequencing, never a product decision** *(was: product owner)* |
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-07, on `git fetch` failing mid-slice with `REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED` |
| ✅ **Corroborated independently** | **Lane C, 2026-08-07**, which hit the same failure in the same window and measured before reading this row: **`ssh-keyscan` returns a single 2048-bit RSA key, `SHA256:7zYnlSpxx6z0t477lR5vNYfelxewzWwu8N1X6v+wsZA`, and offers no ed25519 or ecdsa at all**, while `known_hosts` holds GitHub's three published fingerprints. ⚡ **Two lanes, two measurements, one answer — so it is not a transient.** ⛔ **Lane C did not run `ssh-keygen -R`**, for the reason this row exists |

### The measurement, because the conclusion depends on it

| | Key size | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub's official RSA**, from `api.github.com/meta` **over HTTPS** | **3072-bit** | `uNiVztksCsDhcc0u9e8BujQXVUpKZIDTMczCvj3tD2s` |
| **What answers `github.com:22`** | **2048-bit** | `7zYnlSpxx6z0t477lR5vNYfelxewzWwu8N1X6v+wsZA` |
| **What answers `ssh.github.com:443`** | **2048-bit** | **the same impostor key** |

⚡ **Two different ports, one key, and only RSA offered** — GitHub serves ed25519, ECDSA **and** RSA. **A key rotation would not lose two key types or change the key size**, and it would be published. **`known_hosts` holds all three genuine keys and SSH refused correctly.**

### Why HTTPS is trustworthy when SSH is not

**Separate transport, separate validation, and the two disagree in the direction that settles it.** TLS to `github.com` verifies against **Sectigo** — GitHub's genuine public issuer, not a local or enterprise CA — and **that same HTTPS path returned the real fingerprints, which contradict the key SSH is being offered.** ⛔ **Anything able to forge both would have made them agree.**

### ⛔ What no lane should do

**Do not run `ssh-keygen -R github.com`.** It is the first result for this error message and it **deletes the evidence that caught the problem**, after which SSH silently trusts whatever answers. **Use the HTTPS remote**, which is what this clone now does.

### What is actually being asked

**Nothing from any lane.** **The product owner decides whether this is a corporate or ISP middlebox to accept or to escalate** — DNS resolves `github.com` to `20.207.73.82`, which is inside GitHub's own Azure range, so **the interception is on the path rather than at the destination.** **Close this when the network is understood**, or leave it open as the standing reason SSH is not used here.

## C-334 · Four rows wait on one credential, and it has no row of its own

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** *"I will provide the hosted evaluation credential."* ⚡ **Release is automatic on configuration and needs no further instruction**: [TASK-003](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md)'s prompt-evaluation work · [C-222](#c-222--reasoning1-earns-a-release-under-protocol-2-on-a-model-this-workstation-cannot-measure-in-time) · [C-331](#c-331--task-003-changes-what-the-model-is-shown-which-un-releases-the-narration-prompt). ⚠️ **[TASK-202](BACKLOG.md) is `READY` today and stays `READY`** — the credential gates its *prompt release*, never its start


**Opened 2026-08-06 · Lane B · owner: product owner · 🟠**

> **Every task assigned to Lane B is blocked. They trace to three roots, and this is the one that is not a decision.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-06, on being asked to document its blockers and finding this one is recorded **only as a sub-clause of two other items** |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it is a resourcing act, not a ruling. Nothing here needs to be decided, only provided |
| **Status** | ⚙️ **`OPERATIONAL` — reclassified 2026-08-06, [D-139](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ②.** ⛔ ***"This is no longer a Product Owner decision. It is an operational environment dependency."*** **Tracked, and removed from decision discussions unless a new architectural issue appears.** ⚡ **Release remains automatic on configuration; nothing waits on further instruction.** |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-003](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md) · [C-222](#c-222--reasoning1-earns-a-release-under-protocol-2-on-a-model-this-workstation-cannot-measure-in-time) · [C-331](#c-331--task-003-changes-what-the-model-is-shown-which-un-releases-the-narration-prompt).** **Two of those four are the only `READY` rows in the entire backlog** |

### Why it needs a row when two items already mention it

**[C-331](#c-331--task-003-changes-what-the-model-is-shown-which-un-releases-the-narration-prompt) says it best and says it in passing**: *"a single hosted evaluation credential converts two of the six into executable work, and it is the only one of the blockers that is not a decision about the product."*

> **That sentence is the most actionable thing in the register and it is buried inside an item about a prompt.** **C-222 mentions it too, from the other end.** So the one blocker nobody has to think about is the one nobody has a row for — and a dependency that appears only as a clause inside two others is one that gets read as somebody else's problem twice.

### What is actually being asked for, concretely

**One API key, in `.env`, for any hosted provider the AI Platform already adapts.** The mechanism is built and needs no engineering:

```bash
# backend/.env
SIGNORA_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
```

`AISettings` reads it under the `SIGNORA_` prefix; `build_provider_registry` registers the adapter **only when the key is present**; the evaluation harness names a *model* and the registry resolves who serves it. **No code changes, no configuration design, no new dependency.**

> ⚠️ **`anthropic` is named as the adapter that exists, not as a preference.** The product owner's direction stands — *"continue treating this as a provider-independent evaluation process; do not optimise for any specific LLM vendor"* — and **any hosted adapter satisfies this item.** `ollama.py`, `anthropic.py` and `mock.py` are what is built today; a second hosted vendor is [TASK-420](BACKLOG.md).

### ⛔ Necessary, and **not** sufficient — measured before asking

**This is the finding that stops the credential being reported as an unblocking**, and it was measured from the committed manifest rather than predicted ([29](architecture/29-ai-reasoning-engine.md)):

| Model | Protocol | Grounding failures | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `granite3.3:2b` | 1 | 0 | 0.833 ✅ |
| **`granite3.3:2b`** | **2** | **2 of 2** | **0.0** |

**Same model, same dataset, same prompt.** With `MINIMUM_COVERAGE = 0.66`, **`reasoning@1` has no passing protocol-2 evaluation and cannot earn one as written** — so TASK-202's first slice fails *whatever* provider serves it. **A prompt revision is needed as well as a credential**, and the shape is known: `research_synthesis@2` fixed the same class by replacing a transformation instruction with *"copy the reference character for character"* plus a worked example. **`reasoning@1` has no example at all.**

**Stated here so the credential arrives with the right expectation.** It converts TASK-003 and C-331 into executable work immediately; it converts TASK-202 into *authorable* work, which is the next step rather than the last.

## C-333 · Lane B has no claimable work, and the file whose job is to say so reports no shortfall

> ⛔ **Two items now hold this id, and QE renumbers at merge** (§20e — *"renumbering an existing identifier is QE's, at merge, and only to break a tie… the later claim moves, decided by author timestamp"*). **This one is the earlier**, raised 2026-08-05 and promoted to `main` inside `a6eee5d3`; **[the other](#c-333--the-queue-was-documentation-and-it-is-now-validated) is Lane C's, on the same subject.** **`B-327` collided the same way and on the same day.**
>
> **Not a lane's to fix and deliberately not fixed here.** Lane C's note records that the product owner named both ids and that they were *"verified absent from every register and from `origin/integration` before use"* — **which was true when it was checked and had stopped being true by the time it was written**: these two were on `origin/integration` at `24349948`. **Nobody was careless; that is the whole argument for allocation blocks** (§20e — *"a block makes it unrepresentable"*), **and both ids came from Lane B's `300+` block rather than Lane C's `400+`.**
>
> **`state-check.py` catches it, which is the system working**: *"`B-` identifiers are allocated twice: B-327. `C-` identifiers are allocated twice: C-333."*


**Opened 2026-08-05 · Lane B · owner: Lane C — queue health, backlog health and execution flow are its standing responsibilities under the governance freeze**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-05, on setting [TASK-438](BACKLOG.md) to `IN VALIDATION` and returning to the queue for the next row |
| **Owner** | **Lane C.** ⛔ **Not the product owner** — nothing here needs a ruling. Every input already exists; what is missing is the routing |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RESOLVED` — 2026-08-06.** **Eight validations in [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py), and [D-099](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the duty standing rather than closing it** |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing now.** It blocked *every future Lane B slice*; what replaced it is a check that runs on every invocation |

### The state, measured rather than described

> ⚠️ **The first command below is wrong, and it is corrected rather than deleted** (2026-08-06, Lane B, its own error). **It returned nothing because the rows are `✅ READY`, not `` `READY` `` — the emoji defeats the pattern.** **The right answer is two: [TASK-201](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md)**, which are the same two rows the queue names below, and **both are blocked by the dependencies named beside them.**
>
> **The item's conclusion is unchanged and was never resting on that line** — point ② below is exactly this fact stated correctly, and it is the point Lane C's fix has still not addressed. **What changes is that *"zero `READY` rows"* was the wrong sentence for it**, and this lane said so in four reports before checking.
>
> ⚡ **And the gate had the same bug in the opposite direction** — `state-check.py` reports **54 `READY`** by counting task *headings* ([B-328](BUGS.md)). **Two independent readers got one field wrong on one day**, which is the argument for parsing a status once rather than matching it wherever it is wanted.

```bash
# READY rows in the whole backlog — ⚠️ this pattern misses `✅ READY`; see above
awk '/^### TASK-/{t=$0} /^\| \*\*Status\*\* \| \*\*`READY`/{print t}' docs/BACKLOG.md
→ (nothing)   # ⛔ actually two: TASK-201 and TASK-202, both blocked

grep -E '^(current|next|future|eligible_count|shortfall|depth_target)' \
    docs/coordination/queues/lane-b.toml
→ depth_target   = 5
  current        = "TASK-202"     # blocked — hosted evaluation credential
  next           = "TASK-201"     # blocked — ADR-0400 / B-205
  future         = []
  eligible_count = 2
  shortfall      = 0
```

### Three things are wrong with those six lines, and they compound

| | |
|---|---|
| ① **`shortfall = 0` against `depth_target = 5` and `eligible_count = 2`** | **Wrong on the file's own arithmetic** before anything else is considered. 5 − 2 = 3 |
| ② **Neither "eligible" task is startable** | **[TASK-202](BACKLOG.md)** waits on the hosted evaluation credential; **[TASK-201](BACKLOG.md)** waits on ADR-0400 and [B-205](BUGS.md). **So the true `eligible_count` is 0 and the true shortfall is 5** |
| ③ **[TASK-438](BACKLOG.md) was never in this file at all** | It was `READY`, in `opportunity_engine`, which [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) assigns to Lane B. **This lane found it by reading `BACKLOG.md` directly**, which §20e permits — *"the backlog wins on state, the queue wins on ownership, and the disagreement is reported"* — **and this is that report** |

> **This is [C-329](#c-329--lane-b-has-nothing-claimable-and-the-row-that-says-otherwise-names-two-tasks-it-cannot-take)'s shape again, inverted, and that is why it is worth a row rather than a message.** C-329 was *a lane reporting an empty queue while the file named a current task* — **the lane had not read its own queue.** This is *the file naming two current tasks while the lane has nothing to take* — **and this time the lane did read it.** The register's own note above [`queues/lane-b.toml`](coordination/queues/lane-b.toml) says the fix was step 3 of the Task Claim Protocol; **step 3 was followed and still produced nothing**, because the file's contents are stale rather than its position in the procedure.

### Why `shortfall = 0` is the field that matters

**It is the instrument.** §20e makes running dry *"a finding, and it is Lane C's to investigate"*, and the **Bottleneck Dashboard** is meant to surface it. **A queue that is dry and reports no shortfall is invisible to the one mechanism designed to catch it** — which is how a lane goes idle without anybody's dashboard turning a colour.

### What would resolve it — and none of these needs a ruling

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Recompute the file against reality** | `eligible_count = 0`, `shortfall = 5`, both blocked rows moved to `[[blocked]]` with their named blockers. **Ten minutes, and it makes the condition visible** |
| **B** | **Place [TASK-427](BACKLOG.md)** | Its own `[[blocked]]` entry says *"NOT blocked on a decision — D-074 ruled the direction and 441 is the plan… What remains is one act, and it is a priority act."* ⚠️ **That act is the product owner's, and Lane C may not perform it — but Lane C can ask for it**, which is the routing this item is about |
| **C** | **Approve preparation Lane B authors for its own modules** | Under *Distributed Product Development* the owning lane prepares and Lane C sets `READY`. **Lane B has four modules and can write rows for them** — see below |

### What Lane B will do meanwhile, so this is not a lane waiting to be fed

**Nothing is invented and nothing is claimed.** §20e is explicit: *"a lane never begins work when no `READY` task exists"*, and *"`AVAILABLE` with an empty queue is a correct repository state, not a stalled one."*

**What this lane can do without a ruling is prepare**, which the product owner has already directed as the operating model — *"continue preparing everything that does not require executing"*. **Preparation for every blocked row is already complete and on `main`**: [27](architecture/27-opportunity-engine.md) for TASK-406, [40](architecture/40-commercial-profile.md) for Epic C, [29](architecture/29-ai-reasoning-engine.md) for Epic G. **There is no fourth thing to prepare** — which is precisely why this item exists rather than a fourth preparation commit.

### Implementation impact

**None. No code, no contract, no schema.** This is a routing and bookkeeping item, and it is filed here rather than raised in a report because **a dependency stated in a report reaches one reader, and a dependency stated in the register reaches whoever is on Lane C next week** (§20e — the register exists so no dependency disappears because the lane that found it could not fix it).

## ✅ Resolution — 2026-08-06 · the queue was documentation, and it is now validated

**Ruled by the product owner the same day it was raised:** ***"The queue must always represent the actual executable state of the repository… The queue should be considered an executable planning artifact rather than documentation."***

⚠️ **The id falls in Lane B's allocation block (`300+`), not Lane C's (`400+`).** **The product owner named it explicitly.** **Recorded here so QE renumbers rather than discovers it.**

### The eight validations, in [`infra/state-check.py`](../infra/state-check.py)

**① `eligible_count` against the sequence beside it · ② `shortfall` against `depth_target` · ③ actual claimability · ④ dependency satisfaction · ⑤ queue freshness against `BACKLOG.md`'s last commit · ⑥ `READY` rows in no queue · ⑦ departed rows still sequenced · ⑧ the `held` and `in_validation` arrays.**

> ⚡ **Seven were specified; the eighth was found by the first seven passing a queue that was wrong.** **Checks ①–⑦ all read the *executable* fields and none read the arrays describing what a lane is **not** doing** — so a shipped task could sit in `held` indefinitely and every check agreed. **Check ⑧ then found five drifts, two of them in a file this office had corrected that morning.**

### ⚡ Four drifts on the first run, and two were in queues this office wrote

| | |
|---|---|
| **`lane-a`** | Queued **TASK-437** as executable; its row says `IN VALIDATION`. **Lane A had shipped the leave endpoint** |
| **`lane-b`** | Declared `shortfall = 0` against **2 of 5** |
| **`lane-c`** | Queued **TASK-418** as executable; it is with QE |
| **`TASK-901`** | ⚡ **`READY` in the backlog and in nobody's queue** — and the finding was the *backlog*, not the queue. **Both lane queues already listed it as blocked on TASK-418; the backlog was the optimistic one.** Corrected to `BLOCKED` on [C-417](#c-417--adr-0404-approved-three-platform-capabilities-whose-owner-may-not-finish-two-of-them) |

### ⚠️ And the check found a defect in its own wiring

**It was appended *after* `if not findings: return 0`.** **Every queue validation would have been skipped on exactly the day the rest of the repository agreed with itself** — **the one day a silent queue drift goes unseen.** **Moved above the early return, and the reason is recorded in the code.**

### What [D-099](DECISION_REGISTER.md) changed, and it is why this item closes rather than ends

> ***"C-333 now becomes a standing operational responsibility. Implementation lanes should not reach a genuine zero-READY state without Product Office immediately investigating why."***

**So the deliverable was never the eight checks.** **It is the obligation they make cheap**: a dry queue is now a finding the instrument raises, and **[§5f](PRODUCT_OFFICE.md) carries the six causes that must be ruled out before a lane is reported as correctly waiting.** **The checks detect; the protocol decides what the detection means.**

## C-332 · The predicate landed and TASK-406 still cannot call it — nothing builds its input, and the module that measures may not reach one

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md). [462](architecture/462-observed-attributes-proposal.md) approved exactly as proposed.** **`AccountAttributesReader` published by `knowledge_graph/public/` · `opportunity_engine` consuming the public contract only · [ADR-0403](architecture/adr/0403-signal-engine-reads-a-declaration.md)'s precedent followed exactly.** *"No alternative architecture is required."* **[TASK-446](BACKLOG.md) implements it**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-05, on resuming [TASK-406](BACKLOG.md) after [TASK-434](BACKLOG.md) was promoted — reading the two contracts before writing, exactly as [C-328](#c-328--task-406-asks-commercial_profile-to-read-the-pipeline-which-a-contract-forbids-by-design) and [C-330](#c-330--task-406-measures-icp-fit-against-outcomes-and-nothing-can-say-which-accounts-are-in-the-icp) were raised |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it needs a dependency edge that the ratified graph does not contain, which is 🔴 and never a lane's |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — 2026-08-06, by the requesting lane, which is the rule.** **[TASK-446](BACKLOG.md) is promoted at `a1945436`**: `AccountAttributesReader` publishes a resolved value per attribute with its provenance, and **the edge is narrowed to the inner-layer form** so `opportunity_engine` may read `knowledge_graph.public`. **Both halves of what this item named are answered** — something constructs the predicate's input, and the module ruled to measure can reach it. **[462](architecture/462-observed-attributes-proposal.md) was approved exactly as written** ([D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), and TASK-406 resumes. **Originally: `OPEN` — TASK-406 returns to `BLOCKED` and no code is written.** ⚠️ **This is not a re-raise of C-330.** That item asked for the predicate; the predicate exists and is on `main`. **This is about the two things either side of it** |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-406](BACKLOG.md) whole — both halves, not only the backtest.** The row's *"the per-criterion lift half is unaffected and needs nothing new"* is **measurably wrong**, and that is the most useful thing in this item |

### The problem, in one line

> **`evaluate(icp, observed)` shipped and is correct. Nothing in the repository constructs an `ObservedAttributes`, and the module ruled to do the measuring is forbidden from every module that could.**

### What was verified, out of the code rather than recalled

| | |
|---|---|
| **The predicate is real and promoted** | `commercial_profile/domain/matching.py` at `fec8b5b2`. It takes `ProductIcp` and `ObservedAttributes` and **is pure by design** — *"the facts are handed to it"* |
| **Nothing hands them to it** | `ObservedAttributes(industry, country, employees)` has **no producer anywhere in `backend/modules/`.** The claims exist — `ClaimAttribute.INDUSTRY`, `COUNTRY`, `EMPLOYEE_COUNT` — but **a claim set is not a value**, and choosing among disagreeing providers is a projection with a rule, not a lookup |
| **Only one module can make that projection** | `ClaimReader.for_subjects` keys on **`SubjectRef`** — a *provider* identity. **The `entity_id → SubjectRef[]` binding lives only in `knowledge_graph`** (`identity_binding`, `_subjects()` in its `application/queries.py`) |
| ⛔ **And `opportunity_engine` may not reach it** | `pyproject.toml` forbids `modules.opportunity_engine` → **`modules.knowledge_graph` in full**, not merely its inner layers. [05](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md) agrees and is narrower still: **its only upstream edge is Buying Score Engine** |
| ⛔ **And the score carries nothing** | `buying_score_engine/domain/score.py`, verbatim: *"no name, no domain, no industry"* — **deliberately**, so a score row never becomes an account record |
| ⛔ **And the other direction is already ruled shut** | [C-328](#c-328--task-406-asks-commercial_profile-to-read-the-pipeline-which-a-contract-forbids-by-design): `commercial_profile` may not read the pipeline. **That ruling is correct and is not being reopened** |

**So the ruled design — `opportunity_engine` measures, reading the ICP through `commercial_profile/public/` — is available for the *criteria* and closed for the *facts*.** A description crosses the boundary; the values to compare it against cannot.

### Why the lift half is blocked too, which the backlog row denies

**[C-330](#c-330--task-406-measures-icp-fit-against-outcomes-and-nothing-can-say-which-accounts-are-in-the-icp) already stated it and the amendment overlooked it:**

> *"Lift is `P(win | matches criterion) ÷ P(win)`. **Every term** needs *"does this account match this criterion?"*"*

**Both of TASK-406's halves are the same question asked twice** — per criterion, and rolled up per cohort. **Neither is buildable without a producer of observed attributes.** A lane taking the row at its word would build the arithmetic, discover the input on the last day, and either stop or invent one.

### The alternatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **`knowledge_graph` publishes the projection**, and `opportunity_engine` gains an edge to its `public/` | The projection genuinely belongs there — **`select_name` is the exact precedent**, resolving one attribute with its rule stated, reporting `NameAgreement`, and refusing provider precedence because *"provider precedence is a customer policy."* ⛔ **But it needs a new ratified edge**, and the contract forbidding it carries reasoning |
| **B** | **`opportunity_engine` declares an `AccountAttributeReader` port in its own vocabulary**, satisfied by an adapter wired at the composition root | **No module-to-module import is added** — the port is `opportunity_engine`'s language (§6, *a port belongs to the module that owns the language*) and the adapter lives outside both. **The `ExplanationSource` precedent is exact.** Still introduces a runtime edge absent from [05](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md), so **still 🔴** |
| **C** | **An event-carried projection** — `knowledge_graph` publishes attributes, `opportunity_engine` keeps a local copy | ⛔ **Two representations of one fact** (§2). Adds a table and a staleness window to answer a question that is already answerable live |
| **D** | **Narrow TASK-406 to the cohort-wide backtest** — win rate and median cycle over all decided accounts, no ICP split | **Computable today from `DecidedAccount` alone, with no new edge.** ⛔ **Does not satisfy the row** — *"the backtest reports both cohorts, never in-ICP alone"* — and the product owner has already bounded it: *"reasonable if it is clearly labelled as 'overall cohort performance' rather than ICP lift, but do not spend time implementing that unless it already fits the roadmap"* |

### The recommendation, which is input and not authority

> **B, and A as the thing B is wired to.**

**The projection belongs in `knowledge_graph`** — it owns identity, it owns claim selection, and it has already solved this shape once for the name. **The edge belongs to a port rather than an import**, because that is the only option that lets `opportunity_engine` state what it needs in its own words without learning that a Knowledge Graph exists.

**Two design questions come with A and neither is a lane's to settle**, both recorded in [27](architecture/27-opportunity-engine.md) during preparation:

1. **When two providers disagree — `Fintech` against `Banking` — is the account measured or `UNMEASURED`?** Both are defensible and they are not equivalent. Deciding is decisive on contested evidence; abstaining is honest and will mark more accounts unknown than a seller expects.
2. **`select_name` refuses provider precedence as *"a customer policy."*** If that holds here, the projection needs the same refusal, and the tie-break must be stated where a customer can read it.

### The trade-offs

**B costs one port, one adapter and a ratified edge before TASK-406 can start** — and the edge is the part that is not a lane's. **A without B would put `modules.knowledge_graph` in `opportunity_engine`'s imports**, which is the line C-328's reasoning was written to hold. **D lands a real number this week and is not the number the approved screen shows.** **Doing nothing leaves the ICP Builder's headline figure with no path to itself for a third consecutive item.**

### Implementation impact

**No code was written and no dependency added.** **TASK-434 is unaffected and stays correct** — a pure predicate with no producer is not a defect, it is a foundation with its next milestone unbuilt, and 443 §7 sequenced it that way deliberately. **What this item asks for is 443's missing rung**: M2 shipped, M4 is TASK-406, and **the step that turns claims into the values M2 compares was folded into M1 and deferred behind a trigger that TASK-406 does not satisfy** — *"when exact agreement is measurably losing accounts."* **That trigger is about synonyms. This is about there being no value to synonymise.**
