> ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` on a ruled dependency — [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Trigger: the hosted evaluation credential, ruled and being provided at [C-334](#c-334--four-rows-wait-on-one-credential-and-it-has-no-row-of-its-own).** ⛔ **No longer an open question — it is a queued consequence**, and [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md) already directs its automatic release.


| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-05, on claiming TASK-003 and tracing the change through before writing |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — it needs an evaluation run this workstation cannot perform, which is a resourcing question |
| **Status** | ⏸️ **`REVIEW LATER` — Lane C, 2026-08-11.** ⛔ **NOT a product decision, and this row's own banner has said so since [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md)**: *"no longer an open question — it is a queued consequence, and [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md) already directs its automatic release."* ⚠️ **The banner read `DEFERRED` and this field read `OPEN`; the field is what a sweep reads, which is why this item kept returning to the product owner's queue.** ✅ **Its trigger is [C-334](#c-334)'s credential — `RULED` 2026-08-06, *"release is automatic on configuration and needs no further instruction"*.** ⚡ **Nothing here needs deciding; it needs configuring** |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Three rows, not one — consolidated 2026-08-05 rather than raised three times.** **[TASK-003](BACKLOG.md)** needs a re-evaluation to keep `explanation_narration` released · **[TASK-202](BACKLOG.md)** — Epic G — has *"author a `reasoning` dataset and evaluate `reasoning@1` under protocol 2"* as its **first slice** · **[C-222](#c-222--reasoning1-earns-a-release-under-protocol-2-on-a-model-this-workstation-cannot-measure-in-time)** has been open since 2026-08-04 on the same measurement. **One missing input gates all three** |

> **This is why it is worth a decision rather than a workaround.** Lane B's queue currently holds **TASK-408** (needs a product ruling), **TASK-406** (`BLOCKED`, [C-330](#c-330--task-406-measures-icp-fit-against-outcomes-and-nothing-can-say-which-accounts-are-in-the-icp)), **TASK-201/427** (need ADR-0400 ratified), **TASK-902** (`WAITING`), and **TASK-003 and TASK-202 — both of which this item gates.** **A single hosted evaluation credential converts two of the six into executable work**, and it is the only one of the blockers that is not a decision about the product.

### The task is one file. Its consequence is a release cycle.

**[C-018](#c-018) ruled the *where* and it is correct**: *"customer-facing terminology belongs in `explanation.py`; business language should never leak inward."* That is the only place it can go, and [R11-06](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) says why in its own words:

> *"These are **verbatim what the model was shown**, and the digest covers their textual form. Prettifying `false` into 'No' would show the reader something different from what was cited — a second vocabulary, and the one place where a second vocabulary would defeat the panel's entire purpose. **The verbatim-ness is the value.**"*

**So the fix is not a label map over the output. It is a change to the evidence the model reads** — and that is exactly what makes it correct, because the seller and the model then read one vocabulary rather than two.

### What follows, traced rather than assumed

| # | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | `assemble()` emits different attribute text | `contested` · `delta` · `ceiling` · `value` · `contested_at_creation` all change |
| **2** | **The golden dataset stops describing what the pipeline emits** | `datasets/explanation_narration@1.json` **pins those exact keys and values** and is `seeded_from` assembly. Leaving it would leave a benchmark measuring a shape the product no longer produces — **a stale benchmark is worse than an absent one**, because it keeps passing |
| **3** | **A re-seeded dataset is a new version** | `dataset_version` is on every `Evaluation`, and AC-73: *"a result that cannot name the expectations it was measured against is not evidence of anything"* |
| **4** | ⚠️ **The prompt's only releases are against dataset v1** | `manifest.json`: `explanation_narration@1` holds **two evaluations, both `(explanation_narration, v1, llama3.1:8b)`**. A v2 dataset is a pairing absent from that record |
| **5** | **`require_model` then refuses it at runtime** | §10: *"a prompt may never be used with a pairing absent from that record."* **Shipping steps 1–3 without step 6 breaks narration in the product** |
| **6** | **So the slice needs a real-model evaluation to complete** | And §10 again: *"a quality measurement taken against a fake measures the fake"* — the deterministic mock cannot earn this release |

### Why this is a resourcing question rather than an architectural one

**Nothing here is undecided.** [C-222](#c-222--reasoning1-earns-a-release-under-protocol-2-on-a-model-this-workstation-cannot-measure-in-time) was ruled 2026-08-04 — **the evaluation provider is configurable** — and [TASK-416](BACKLOG.md) now records which provider served a run, so a hosted evaluation is both permitted and attributable. **The architecture for doing this correctly exists and was built by this lane.**

**What is missing is a provider that can complete the run here.** C-222 measured the pinned local model **`UNMEASURABLE` on this workstation** — 2 of 2 cases never reached a verdict against a 60s policy — and **the pinned evaluation model is part of the benchmark and is not a lane's to change** (§10, ADR-0028).

### The alternatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Provide a hosted evaluation credential and complete the slice** | The vocabulary change, a re-seeded `explanation_narration@2`, and one recorded evaluation earning the release. **The whole task, done properly, in one slice** |
| **B** | **Build steps 1–3 and hold the push until a release exists** | The code is ready and nothing ships un-released. **Costs a held branch and gains nothing over A unless the credential is weeks away** |
| **C** | **Ship the vocabulary change without re-evaluating** | ⛔ **Not proposed.** It breaks narration at runtime, and it is the precise failure §10's release rule exists to prevent |

### Recommendation

**A.** The credential is the only missing input, every other part is decided, and **the capability that makes a hosted evaluation attributable shipped in this lane's last slice.**

**If no credential is available, B** — and TASK-003 is then reported as *implementation complete, release pending*, which is a true statement rather than a finished one.

### Implementation impact

**No code written.** The change is understood and small: one function's attribute vocabulary, a re-seeded dataset, one evaluation. **The cost is the release cycle, not the edit**, and that is the thing the row does not currently say.

## C-330 · TASK-406 measures ICP fit against outcomes, and nothing can say which accounts are in the ICP

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-05, on claiming TASK-406 and reading the two modules before writing |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — it needs a capability nobody owns, which is an assignment question rather than a defect |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED` — 2026-08-05, product owner — and broadened rather than merely answered.** **TASK-406 stays `BLOCKED` exactly as raised.** **Product Office is asked to plan a reusable matching capability as foundational work, and TASK-406 is sequenced after it exists** |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Not TASK-406 alone. The ruling widened this.** *"The ability to determine whether an account satisfies an ICP criterion is a **foundational platform capability** that multiple future product areas will depend upon"* |

### The ruling, 2026-08-05 — and the correction in it is the valuable half

> **"Do not solve this inside TASK-406. Do not create temporary matching logic. Do not duplicate matching inside `commercial_profile`."**
>
> **"No workaround should become permanent architecture."**

**This lane raised it as a TASK-406 dependency and the product owner declined that framing.** Named as depending on it: **ICP Builder · ICP validation · account fit scoring · opportunity prioritization · AI reasoning · buying score · recommendations · backtesting · analytics · executive dashboards · future AI agents.**

**Recommendation A is accepted in substance and reassigned in form.** This lane proposed *"build matching as its own slice, in the module that owns resolution"* and offered to take it since `knowledge_graph` is Lane B's. **The ruling makes it foundational rather than a slice, and gives the planning to Product Office** — which is the difference between a capability designed once for eleven consumers and a capability shaped by the first one that needed it.

**Alternative B is permitted and deliberately not taken.** The product owner: *"a cohort-wide backtest is reasonable **if it is clearly labelled 'overall cohort performance' rather than ICP lift**, but do not spend time implementing that unless it already fits the roadmap."* **It does not — no row asks for it — so this lane built nothing.** The permission is recorded so a future lane knows the shape was allowed and the labelling was the condition.

**This item stays open until the capability exists.** Closing it now would report a dependency as resolved when what happened is that it was correctly reassigned.

### The problem, in one line

> **Lift is `P(win | matches criterion) ÷ P(win)`. Every term needs *"does this account match this criterion?"*, and no component in the repository can answer it.**

**[C-328](#c-328--task-406-asks-commercial_profile-to-read-the-pipeline-which-a-contract-forbids-by-design) verified the import direction and was ruled. This is a second verification and it fails on data rather than on dependencies.** The ruled direction — `opportunity_engine` reads `commercial_profile/public/` — is available and correct. **What travels across it is a description, and a description is not a membership test.**

### Why it cannot be answered today, read out of the modules rather than recalled

| | |
|---|---|
| **An ICP is free text, deliberately** | `domain/icp.py`: *"`industries` and `countries` are free text… a seller says 'mid-market fintech in the US and UK', and recording that faithfully is what a module whose job is recording should do"* |
| **A segment is still a description** | `domain/segment.py`: *"'Mid-market fintech in the US, 100–1000 employees' is a complete description of a segment"* — an ICP has an **identity**, never a **membership list** |
| **The Knowledge Graph publishes no resolved value** | `knowledge_graph/public/`: *"What they get is **identity and evidence, never a resolved value**"* — so an account's current industry or employee count is not readable across the boundary |
| **Matching is named, unbuilt and unowned** | `domain/icp.py`, verbatim: *"**Reconciling the two is what matching does**, and matching is not built, is not this module's, and has no owner today. That is recorded as a finding rather than pre-solved here"* |

**The gap is not a missing query. It is a missing capability two modules have each explicitly declined** — and the ICP module recorded the decline as a finding rather than leaving it to be discovered, which is precisely what has now happened.

### The alternatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Build matching as its own slice, in the module that owns resolution** | Reconciles a free-text criterion against canonical claim vocabulary and publishes a membership answer. **A real capability with real design questions** — fuzzy industry matching, a missing employee count, an account with no claims — deserving its own row and its own review |
| **B** | **Narrow TASK-406 to what needs no matching** | The aggregate backtest **without** the in-ICP split: win rate and median cycle across decided accounts, which `opportunity_engine` can compute today from `DecidedAccount` alone. **Honest and much smaller — and not what the row asks for**, because every comparison the approved screen shows is *in-ICP versus outside* |
| **C** | **Match inside this slice** | ⛔ **Not proposed.** It would put resolution in the module that measures, invent a vocabulary reconciliation nobody reviewed, and make one lane's slice the authority on a capability two modules deliberately left open |

### Recommendation

**A, as a separate row, with TASK-406 sequenced behind it.** Matching is the thing of value here; lift is a small calculation on top of it. **Building the calculation first would mean inventing its input**, and the input is the part carrying the design questions.

**If a partial answer is wanted sooner, B is safe** — and must be labelled as what it is, a cohort-wide backtest with no ICP comparison, rather than shipped under a heading the screen would read as ICP fit.

### Trade-offs

**A costs a slice before TASK-406 can start**, and it needs an owner: resolution is the Knowledge Graph's by the ICP module's own reasoning, and `knowledge_graph` is this lane's, **so Lane B can build it if the product owner wants it built.** **B is cheap and lands a real number**, at the cost of the row's central comparison. **Doing nothing leaves an approved screen with no path to its own headline figure.**

### Implementation impact

**No code was written and no dependency added.** The edge verified at C-328 stays correct and unused. **TASK-406's `Non-goals` already exclude fitted weights and drift** — this item concerns the *input* to the measurement rather than its sophistication, and neither option changes the ruled dependency direction.

> ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md). Moot by events.** **It said *"Lane B has been `AVAILABLE` with nothing verifiable to claim since cycle 54."* Lane B now holds four eligible rows.** ⚡ **And the class is guarded rather than merely resolved: [C-333](#c-333--lane-b-has-no-claimable-work-and-the-file-whose-job-is-to-say-so-reports-no-shortfall)'s eight checks report a dry queue on every `state-check` run.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-05, on being asked whether it had documented what it was waiting on. **It had not, and that is the finding** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — synchronization priority is theirs (§20e) · **Lane C** for the register correction, which is their row |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED`** — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this field was not.** **Twelve items carried the same defect**, and every one would have been escalated as an open question. |
| **Blocks** | **Every Lane B slice.** The lane has been `AVAILABLE` with nothing verifiable to claim since cycle 54 |

### Two facts, both measured from `origin/integration` today

**1 · The prepared work is on a branch and has never reached `integration`.**

```
origin/lane-c-product-office   5ecd2da   57 commits ahead of origin/integration
origin/integration             fa26a8e
```

ADR-0300's Option A ruling, [409](architecture/409-inbound-source-port-contract.md)'s contract and every task row drafted alongside them exist **only there**. `CLAUDE.md` §20e is unambiguous about what that means:

> *"Executable work comes from `integration`, and from nowhere else… Product Office branches are planning artifacts, not execution contracts. A lane does not monitor one, does not wait on one, and does not treat work found on one as claimable."*

**The Task Claim Protocol reads `integration`**, so none of it is claimable however complete it is. [422](architecture/422-synchronization-plan.md) is the plan to collapse the 57 into six and is itself on that branch.

**2 · [C-412](#c-412--three-backlog-rows-say-ready-and-are-not-claimable) is the row a reader would consult to answer *"does Lane B have work?"*, and its answer is stale.**

It names **TASK-003 and TASK-904** as Lane B's remaining claimable rows. Both fail, for different reasons:

| Row | C-412 says | Is |
|---|---|---|
| **TASK-003** — R11-06 attribute vocabulary | Claimable, Lane B | ⚠️ **Its own backlog note says *"Not claimable as written — [C-018](#c-018) opened"***, and C-018 is still `OPEN`. **One file, two answers** — the exact defect C-412 was written to name |
| **TASK-904** — an organization can grow | Claimable, Lane B | ⚠️ **`workspace_tenancy`, and [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) records `current_owner = "Lane A"`.** One lane per module |

**So Lane B's claimable count from that row is zero, not two.** This is not a criticism of C-412 — it was correct when written and `modules.toml` became authoritative afterwards ([D-061](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). **It is the failure mode C-213 cost two days to teach**: a row naming an assignee that has moved *looks answered*.

### Why this is a coordination item rather than a line in a lane report

**§20e already rules the condition, and names who reports it:**

> *"Whenever an implementation lane has been idle for more than one reporting cycle because `READY` work exists only outside `integration`, synchronizing that work becomes the highest repository priority"* — and **"Lane C reports this condition itself and does not wait to be told."**

**It has been true for several cycles and recorded in no document a lane reads.** That is precisely [C-411](#c-411--three-findings-reported-but-recorded-nowhere-a-lane-would-look)'s finding class — *a finding that exists only in a commit message has not been reported* — committed here by the lane that raised nothing about its own idleness while raising items about everything else.

### What closes it

**Either** the Product Office set reaches `origin/integration` **or** one `READY` row exists there for a module `modules.toml` records as Lane B's. **Either is sufficient; neither is this lane's to perform.**

### What this row deliberately does not do

**It does not claim from the branch**, does not propose a module transfer, and **does not amend C-412** — that row is Lane C's, and a lane correcting another lane's register entry is how two records start disagreeing. The correction is named here for its owner to apply.

## C-328 · TASK-406 asks `commercial_profile` to read the pipeline, which a contract forbids by design

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"**Do not introduce the forbidden dependency.** `commercial_profile` declares. `opportunity_engine` measures. Maintain the existing dependency direction."* **Lane B stopped at the boundary and was right to.** [TASK-406](BACKLOG.md) is unblocked at changed scope.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-05, on claiming [TASK-406](BACKLOG.md) and running the verification its own row demands **before writing a line** |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it decides which module owns a measurement, which is a bounded-context question |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner |
| **Blocks** | **A-iv only.** Every other slice in `commercial_profile` is unaffected |

### The problem, in one line

> **The ICP is declarable today and nothing tells a customer whether it is any good** — and measuring that requires outcomes the declaring module is architecturally forbidden to see.

**[TASK-406](BACKLOG.md)'s row anticipated this exactly**: *"a read of `opportunity_engine`'s `public/` — **verify the edge exists in [05](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md) before writing it; if it does not, that is a `C-` item, not a new import.**"* **It does not exist. It is refused on purpose**, and the refusal carries its reasoning in `pyproject.toml`:

> *"`commercial_profile` records what a customer declares. **If it could read a signal, a score or an opportunity, "declaration" would quietly become "declaration informed by our own conclusions"** — the module would start computing, and the one boundary it has would be gone."*

**`modules.opportunity_engine` is on that contract's forbidden list in full** — not merely its inner layers — so this is not a `public/` question that a well-behaved import would satisfy.

### The affected modules

| | |
|---|---|
| **`commercial_profile`** | Owns the ICP declaration, its versioning and `GET /icp-segments`. **Forbidden from reading eleven pipeline modules**, `opportunity_engine` among them |
| **`opportunity_engine`** | Owns the outcomes. Publishes `OpportunityQueries`, `Stage`, `TERMINAL_STAGES`, `Qualification` and `TrackedOpportunity`. **Already permitted to read `commercial_profile.public`** — the reverse contract forbids only that module's inner layers |

**The asymmetry is the whole finding: the direction A-iv needs is closed, and the opposite direction is already open.**

### The alternatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **`commercial_profile` reads `opportunity_engine.public`** | ⛔ **Breaks the contract and the principle behind it.** Would require deleting a line whose comment explains why it exists. **Not recommended, and recorded so the option is visibly rejected rather than silently unavailable** |
| **B** | **The measurement lives in `opportunity_engine`**, reading the ICP through `commercial_profile.public` | ✅ **Uses an edge that already exists**, in the direction already permitted. The module that owns outcomes measures against them; the module that records a declaration goes on only recording it |
| **C** | **A third module or read model** joining both through their contracts | Architecturally clean and **the largest.** A new bounded context is 🔴, and nothing else yet needs it — the speculative structure §6 refuses |

### The recommendation, which is input and not authority

> **B.** It is the only one that adds no edge, moves no boundary and needs no ADR — **the measurement is a fact about opportunities, and `opportunity_engine` already owns those.** Reading the ICP to score it against outcomes is exactly what its existing permission to read `commercial_profile.public` was written for.

**The trade-off is a real one and is stated rather than buried:** the customer-facing surface is the **ICP Builder**, which is `commercial_profile`'s screen, so under B the value a seller reads is computed by a module they never see named. **That is already true of every derived fact in the product**, and the alternative is worse — a declaring module that grades its own input.

**Implementation impact under B:** no migration, no new table, **no new dependency edge** · lift stays derived rather than stored (§2) · the endpoint's owning module changes, which is the part that is not a lane's to decide.

### What Lane B did instead

**Marked [TASK-406](BACKLOG.md) `BLOCKED`, wrote no code, and claimed the next `READY` row.** §20e: *"a dependency on a decision nobody has made is architectural however small the code would be"* — and *"I could just add it"* is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision inside a feature slice.

## C-326 · Epic E1 has no path for a customer's own system to reach the pipeline

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-04, on claiming [TASK-402](BACKLOG.md) and auditing the existing foundation before writing code |
| **Owner** | **The product owner.** Three of the four decisions are 🔴 and one is environmental; none is a lane's |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED` — the product owner ruled it 2026-08-04: [ADR-0300](architecture/adr/0300-inbound-customer-systems.md) **Option A**, the sibling source port.** Closed by the requesting lane, as the register requires. ⚠️ **The ruling is awaiting integration synchronization** — Product Office's document set has not reached `origin/integration`, so a reader there still sees ADR-0300 as `Proposed`. **The decision is authoritative; the repository is not yet converged** ([`PRODUCT_OFFICE.md`](PRODUCT_OFFICE.md) §11c). **Steps 1, 2 and 6 of [409](architecture/409-inbound-source-port-contract.md) are built and held on `lane-b-commercial-profile`** — the port, `Capability.CRM_RECORDS`, and `HubSpotCompanySource` — **on the product owner's explicit standing instruction that a ruling authorizes implementation while synchronization authorizes convergence.** **Steps 3, 4 and 5 are `provider_platform`'s and were not touched**; see [C-300](#c-300--provider-platform-owns-the-half-of-the-inbound-path-lane-b-may-not-build) |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing now.** It blocked the read path only — records arriving — and through it D3, D1's two missing risk families, and E2 |

### What has been built since, and the correction it forces

**This row said implementation had stopped. It had not, and the product owner should rule with that in front of them.** On the product owner's direction — *a blocker blocks only the implementation that truly depends on it* — Epic E1 continued, and the following reached `main` on 2026-08-04:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Interpretation** | `HubSpotCompanyMapper` — a customer's CRM as a firmographic source. **Six of the seven firmographic attributes needed no vocabulary extension** |
| **Acquisition** | `POST /connections` · the RFC 6749 §4.1.3 code exchange · the hand-off. **Complete**; what remains is a developer application, not engineering |
| **Grant lifecycle** | Revocation · renewal (§6) · refresh-on-use. **Complete** |
| **The vendor read** | `HubSpotCompanies` — paged, incremental, every failure typed. **Complete** |

**What this row still blocks is exactly one thing: how a fetched record reaches `raw_provider_record`.** The source port, the runner, and the fixture and merge test that need records to arrive. `HubSpotCompanies` sits provisionally in `integrations/infrastructure/` and **the ruling moves a file and rewrites a wrapper — no behaviour moves with it.**

> **Four times in this epic, work was filed here that depended on the ruling only for its *placement*.** The pattern is worth naming in the row the ruling will be read from: *"blocked on C-326"* was absorbing code whose behaviour is identical under all three options. What is genuinely gated is where the *signature* of the thing is what is being decided.

**The full analysis is [ADR-0300](architecture/adr/0300-inbound-customer-systems.md).** This item carries the six things a blocker must state so a ruling needs no second round trip.

### 1 · The problem

**Epic E1 was sized on the belief that *"what remains is the read, not the plumbing"*. The plumbing is what is missing.** Measured against the code:

| | |
|---|---|
| **`ProviderName` is a closed `StrEnum`** | Five ratified suppliers. `ProviderRecord.provider` and `ProviderRegistry` are typed by it, so **a CRM slug is unconstructable** — the type system doing exactly what §2 asks |
| **`ProviderRequest` carries no connection** | A provider adapter holds *Signora's* credential from the composition root. **A customer's credential is per workspace, per connection, and expires**, and there is nowhere to put it |
| **`ProviderRequest.subject` is required** | Providers are asked *about one company*. **A CRM is asked for the customer's accounts** — an enumeration with no subject, and `provider_watermark`'s fourth column has nothing truthful to hold |
| **`ClaimAttribute` has no CRM concept** | Nothing for *is already a customer*, *contract value*, *renewal date*, *opportunity stage*. The file says **RFC required to extend** |
| **No HubSpot developer application exists** | Environmental, named in E1's own specification as *"a product-owner action"* and again in [44-integrations.md](architecture/44-integrations.md) §9 |

**One thing is not a problem, and it is the good news.** `NormalizeRawRecord` keys mappers by `provider: str` and `raw_provider_record.provider` is `String(64)`. **The canonical shape is already open**, so no second normalization path is needed — the constraint TASK-402 named first is satisfied by what exists. **The gap is entirely in acquiring records and not at all in interpreting them.**

### 2 · The affected modules

`integrations` **(Lane B)** — owns the connection, the credential and `ExecutionContext`, which already exists, is tested, and is deliberately unwired · `provider_platform` **(Lane A, itself in Implementation Waiting on [C-021](#c-021--the-dispatch-direction))** — owns synchronization, watermarks, raw records and `provider.record.received` · `provider_normalization` — owns the canonical vocabulary, and is the one module that needs no structural change.

### 3 · The alternatives

**Four, with the reasoning in the ADR.** A sibling port owned by Integrations · extending the Provider Port · a second ingestion path owned entirely by Integrations · deferring until the developer application exists.

### 4 · The recommendation

> **A customer-held system is a *source*, not a *provider*.** A sibling port — `IntegrationSourceAdapter` — defined in `integrations/domain/` because **a port belongs to the module that owns its language** (§6), taking the `ExecutionContext` that already exists. **Provider Platform drives it and writes the raw records and the event it already writes**, so nothing downstream of `raw_provider_record` changes at all.

### 5 · The trade-offs

**Gained:** one ingestion path · raw records, watermarks, pacing, sync history, failure classification and the entire downstream pipeline reused unchanged · `ProviderName` stays closed and keeps meaning what it says · a customer's credential never leaves `integrations`.

**Given up:** a second port to maintain, deliberately parallel to the Provider Port and free to drift · Provider Platform learns that customer systems exist · **E1 needs two rulings rather than one**, because the vocabulary extension is separated deliberately.

**And the reversal is cheap, which is the argument for deciding now:** the port would have one implementation and one caller, `raw_provider_record.provider` is already a string, and every row written stays valid. **No data migration, no re-normalization, no claim rewritten** — and that stays true only until the first customer connects.

### 6 · The implementation impact

| # | Work | Budget | Whose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The port and its types in `integrations` | 🟠 | **Lane B — ready now** |
| 2 | The use case in `provider_platform`, and a watermark keyed on a connection | 🔴 | **This ruling**, then that module's assignee |
| 3 | New `ClaimAttribute` members and probably a new `ClaimDomain` | 🔴 | **A separate ruling.** Deliberately not bundled |
| 4 | A HubSpot adapter and a mapper registered under `"hubspot"` | 🟢 / 🟠 | Lane B |
| 5 | **The HubSpot developer application** | environmental | **The product owner.** Nothing can be demonstrated without it |

> **This lane has built nothing against any option, and will not.** *"I could just add it"* is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision inside a feature slice, and the change that follows is always small — which is exactly why nobody notices it was a decision.

**What Lane B is doing meanwhile — and the sentence that was here on 2026-08-04 was wrong.**

It read *"the smaller slice inside it does not exist."* **It did.** That claim came from asking what a CRM *could* contribute, and the right question was what the canonical vocabulary *already accepts*. The answer is **six of the seven firmographic attributes** — legal name, employee count, revenue band, industry, country, founded year — all of which a HubSpot company record carries and none of which needs an RFC.

**`HubSpotCompanyMapper` is therefore built, registered and tested**, and it encodes nothing about the ruling above: a mapper receives a stored record and translates it, and has never been able to ask who fetched it or how. **The gap this item describes is in acquiring records, not in interpreting them**, and that is what makes the interpretation half safe to finish first.

**What remains genuinely gated on this ruling** is everything that would put a record in front of that mapper — and it is now the *only* thing standing between a customer's CRM and the whole pipeline behind it.

**Everything else was built and promoted.** Acquisition, the grant lifecycle and the vendor read are on `main`; the inventory was closed once on the product owner's direction rather than re-swept. **This lane holds Epic E1 and waits on this ruling alone.**

## C-327 · Withdrawn — the OAuth client credential question was not a decision pack

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane B, 2026-08-04 |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED` — withdrawn the same day, on the product owner's direction.** The id is retired and never reused |

**Lane B opened this asking where Signora's own OAuth client credentials should live, on the reading that credential ownership is an architectural boundary. The product owner ruled otherwise: it is an implementation detail, to be isolated behind an interface and built.**

> **Lanes do not create Product Office decisions.** When implementation reaches a governance or architecture question, the lane documents the implementation boundary, isolates it behind an interface, and continues. Creation and maintenance of decision packs is the Product Office's.

**It was implemented rather than escalated.** `ClientCredentialsStore` is the interface; `IntegrationSettings` is the implementation, which is where §6 already puts a module's configuration — *a typed Settings object owned by the module whose behaviour it governs*. **Absent credentials produce `NoTokenRefresher`**, the same honest shape `NoRevoker` held, so a deployment that has not configured them refuses rather than pretending.

**Nothing depends on this row.** It is left in place rather than deleted because a register that quietly loses a row is worse than one that records a withdrawal — but no implementation, document or task references it.

| **Class** | **Dependency Resolution** ([`PRODUCT_OFFICE.md`](PRODUCT_OFFICE.md) §1) |

## C-415 · Lane B is thin because its modules drifted, not because work ran out

> ✅ **ANSWERED 2026-08-04.** `commercial_profile` and `knowledge_graph` are **Lane A's**; **Lane B's implementation ownership becomes `integrations`, `provider_normalization`, CRM integrations, provider connectors, ingestion, normalization and future adapters.** **Dual ownership of an implementation module is no longer permitted.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | Lane C, 2026-08-04 |

## C-416 · `signora_platform/` had no assignable owner, and seven slices sat behind it

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Assign `backend/signora_platform/` to **Lane C (Platform Foundation)** as the permanent governance and architectural owner… `signora_platform` is shared infrastructure, not a bounded context… **Platform ownership must remain stable and independent of feature ownership.**"*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-05, on the product owner's instruction: *"If no coordination item exists for this ownership, create one so the decision becomes permanently traceable instead of remaining implicit inside [TASK-418](BACKLOG.md)."* |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ruled |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, the requesting lane.** ⚡ **Ruled and closed the day it was opened; it has sat `RULED` since 2026-08-05 because nobody performed the close.** ⛔ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *the requesting lane closes* — and the requesting lane was this office** *(was: **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, and **closed on the same day it was opened.** Recorded for traceability, not for deliberation)* |
| **Blocks** | ~~**[TASK-418](BACKLOG.md)**, and **[TASK-901](BACKLOG.md)'s seven independently certifiable slices behind it**~~ — **released by this ruling** |

### Why it existed

**[C-010](#c-010) asked about `apps/` *and* `signora_platform/`. The 2026-08-05 ruling named `apps/`.** [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) allocated only `backend/signora_platform/simulation/` to Platform Foundation — **so the event bus and the authorization engine belonged to nobody**, and **three of [ADR-0404](architecture/adr/0404-platform-composition.md)'s four capabilities live there.**

> **It had no item of its own, which is why it stopped surfacing.** It lived inside a task row, and a blocker recorded only in the thing it blocks is invisible to every register that lists blockers. **That is [C-411](#c-411)'s class** — *a finding that exists only where nobody looks has not been reported.*

### What the ruling changes, and what it does not

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Changes** | `signora_platform/` has a permanent architectural owner. **[TASK-418](BACKLOG.md) is buildable and [TASK-901](BACKLOG.md) is released** |
| ⛔ **Does not change** | **§20a still freezes the tree.** Ownership is not a licence — every change still needs an approved RFC, and [ADR-0404](architecture/adr/0404-platform-composition.md) is what makes TASK-418 buildable, **not this row** |
| ⛔ **Does not change** | **Feature lanes still consume the platform without a handoff.** §20a: adding a subscription, an event type or a worker pool is *a use of the platform, not a change to it* |
| ⛔ **Does not change** | **Lane C may still never write production code inside a product module** (§20e). `signora_platform/` is not one |

### ⚠️ Correction, 2026-08-05 — this row's own claimable split named the wrong lane twice

**Found by Lane B at [C-329](#c-329), reading this row against [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) and declining to amend it** because it is Lane C's row. **It was right to report and right not to fix.** Lane B named `TASK-904`; **checking the other pair found the same defect mirrored**, which a single-row report would not have surfaced.

| Row | This item said | [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) says | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TASK-903** | Lane A | `commercial_profile` → **Lane B** | ❌ |
| **TASK-904** | Lane B | `workspace_tenancy` → **Lane A** | ❌ |
| **TASK-905** | Lane A | Product Surface · `buying_score_engine` → **Lane A** | ✅ |
| **TASK-003** | Lane B | `knowledge_graph` → **Lane B** | ✅ — but **not claimable**: [C-018](#c-018) is `OPEN` and its own `Blocks` field names this task |

**Corrected split, joined from the registry rather than restated:** **Lane A** — TASK-904, TASK-905, TASK-417 · **Lane B** — TASK-408, TASK-903, TASK-203, TASK-415, TASK-416.

**The cause is exactly [C-213](#c-213)'s, committed by the office that closed it.** This row **stored an assignee beside a task** on 2026-08-04. `modules.toml` became authoritative on 2026-08-05, ownership moved, and **the stored copy went on reading as an answer.** A derived field written down once is a stale field with no expiry.

> **So the rule C-213 established applies to prose and not only to tables:** **never write a lane's name next to a task.** Name the module. **The registry is the only place a lane's name is allowed to be the answer**, and anywhere else it is a cache nobody invalidates.

**Also corrected: TASK-003 is not claimable and this row implied it was.** [C-018](#c-018) — *"nobody owns the customer-facing name of an attribute"* — is `OPEN`, is the product owner's, and its `Blocks` field says TASK-003 *"cannot be implemented without the answer."* **Lane C's execution queue listed it as Lane B's `next` on the reasoning that the labelling half was separable. That was Lane C's judgement placed above the register's own statement, and the register wins.** Removed from the queue; **the split above is the corrected one.**

> **The general finding, and it is worth more than the three rows:** **`READY` is a status a row carries; *claimable* is a fact about a particular lane on a particular day.** One-lane-per-module means a pooled count is always wrong, and **a status that its own file contradicts is worse than an absent one** — a lane reads it, plans around it, and discovers the truth after claiming.

## C-218 · A lane can report AVAILABLE, and the office that assigns cannot see it

> ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-125](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **It asked for a path by which *"a lane reports `AVAILABLE`"* reaches the office that assigns.** ⚡ **That path was built and it runs the other way, which is better**: **the office writes the queue continuously ([D-070](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) and the lane reads it — so nothing has to be *reported* for work to be waiting.** ✅ **And the reverse direction — *is a lane about to run dry?* — is now measured rather than reported**: **[C-333](#c-333--lane-b-has-no-claimable-work-and-the-file-whose-job-is-to-say-so-reports-no-shortfall)'s eight queue checks fire on every `state-check` run**, and [D-100](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes investigating a dry queue a standing Product Office duty **before the lane reports it**. ⚠️ **The item's own framing was right and its remedy was upside down: the fix was not a better signal from the lane, it was removing the need for one.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Lane C** (the model) · **QE** (the mechanism) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Coordination model |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-125](DECISION_REGISTER.md)** |
| **Blocks** | **Every implementation lane's idle time, structurally.** Not one assignment — the signal that triggers all of them |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-03, immediately after [C-217](#c-217--lane-a-is-available-and-requests-its-next-product-surface-epic) was pushed and turned out to be invisible |

**The product owner's instruction is that a lane reports `AVAILABLE` and Lane C assigns. There is no path by which the report reaches Lane C.**

### Measured, not inferred

| | |
|---|---|
| **`C-217` on `origin/integration`** | **Absent.** It is on `lane-a-product-surface` only |
| **Lane A's rows on `origin/integration`'s board** | **Four, and every one is stale** — Product Surface `ACTIVE`, `provider_platform` `BLOCKED`, Team Management `ACTIVE`, M14b `BLOCKED`. Dated `08226e5` |
| **What Lane C therefore believes** | **Lane A is busy on four things.** Nothing from this session — LO, SE, SW, PS-09, CX-05 — is visible to it |

**So the lane is idle and the board says it is working.** Proactive assignment does not fix this: Lane C has no reason to prepare an epic for a lane its board shows as `ACTIVE` four times over.

### Why it happens, precisely

**The repository already solved this once, for claims, and the fix does not generalise.**

> *"`integration` is the one ref every lane pulls. A claim pushed only to `lane-a-product-surface` is invisible to every other lane, so the queue still reads as unclaimed and the race the protocol exists to prevent is still open."* — `CLAUDE.md` §20e, corrected 2026-08-02 **after watching it fail.**

**That correction is narrow by construction, and correctly so.** `infra/certification-guard.py` recognises a claim as *a commit whose subject begins with `Claim TASK-`, touching `docs/ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` and `docs/BACKLOG.md` and nothing else.* **An availability report is not a claim** — it names no task, because not having one is the point — so it has no path to `integration` and waits for QE to fast-forward the lane branch.

**Which inverts the intended order.** The signal that is supposed to *start* the next assignment arrives **after** validation and certification of the previous slice — a full QE cycle later. **The pull model made the claim fast because a claim is a race. The assign model made availability the trigger and left it on the slow path.**

### Three ways out, and the choice is not this lane's

| | Change | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Widen the exception to a status commit.** Subject `Status <LANE> AVAILABLE`, same two files, same audit. **Smallest change, and it reuses a mechanism already proven** | The exception stops being one line and becomes a category. `--audit-claims` needs a second recognised subject |
| **B** | **Lane C reads lane branches rather than `integration`.** The information exists — it is on `lane-a-product-surface` right now | **Makes an unvalidated branch load-bearing for scheduling**, and Lane C would be reading state QE has not seen |
| **C** | **QE fast-forwards on availability rather than only on validation.** No rule changes | **Reintroduces the bottleneck the pull model removed** — every lane's next assignment waits on QE's cycle, which is the arithmetic that moved scheduling out of QE on 2026-08-02 |

**Lane A recommends A**, and holds it lightly: it is the one that keeps `integration` authoritative, keeps QE out of the scheduling path, and stays inside the enforcement that already exists. **B and C both trade away something the repository has already paid for.**

### What Lane A is not doing

**Not pushing this to `integration`.** It is not a claim, and the exception is bounded to claims for a reason. **Not self-assigning while it waits** — the product owner was explicit that a coordination breakdown is a coordination issue rather than a licence to pick up work. **Not editing another lane's rows** to make the board describe reality.

**Lane A is idle, correctly, and this item is the reason.**

## C-219 · TASK-400's two halves are not equally buildable

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"No Product Owner decision required. Proceed exactly as documented."* A7 proceeds; A6 is unblocked by [C-321](#c-321); **the render still waits on the join proposal Lane A owes Lane C.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** (A6, via [C-321](#c-321--what-should-signora-do-with-a-company-it-cannot-name)) · **Lane C** (A7's join, and the assignment) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, no decision required |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-03, on claiming [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md) and reading the specification it cites |

**Lane A claimed TASK-400 and is implementing A7. A6 is held, and this says why rather than quietly doing half an epic.**

### A6 is blocked on a decision, by its own specification

**`51-implementation-specifications.md` §A6 states it twice, in its own words:** *"Backend — **depends entirely on the [C-321] ruling**"* and *"Dependencies — **C-321 must be answered first. This is the clearest case in the roadmap of a decision blocking a build.**"*

**[C-321](#c-321--what-should-signora-do-with-a-company-it-cannot-name) is `OPEN`, owned by the product owner, and asks six unanswered sub-questions** — should an unnamed company appear at all, on the working list, contribute to a score, become an opportunity, be workable, and what is it instead.

**TASK-400 narrows A6 to *the render*, and that does not escape the block.** *What to render* **is** the ruling: whether an unnamed record leaves the working list, whether it keeps its score, whether it is offered a workflow action. **Building the render picks an answer by implementation**, which is precisely what the register exists to prevent — and exactly the reasoning Lane A applied to [C-008](#c-008--sellers-cannot-see-what-their-company-sells), where the obvious repair would have chosen option B or C silently.

**Lane A is not asking for a different task.** A7 is real, is Lane A's, and is being built. **This asks the product owner to rule on C-321**, after which A6 is a normal slice.

### A7's open question, narrowed by reading the code

**The specification calls the `subject` ↔ entity join *"the design decision the slice turns on"*. It is smaller than that, and the domain has already made half the decision.**

> `targets.py`: ***"`already_read` is what has a position**, not what has a watermark row. A watermark that exists with no position records an attempt that stored nothing."*

**So *ever attempted* is already distinguishable from *never attempted* today** — acceptance ② is partly modelled. What is genuinely missing is **when we last tried**, because `position` advances only when records arrive (`run_sync.py:137`), so a repeat successful-but-empty read leaves the row untouched.

**Lane A is therefore building the half that needs no ruling** — `attempted_at` on `provider_watermark`, written on every completed run, inside `provider_platform`, which is Lane A's. **The render waits on the join**, and Lane A will bring Lane C a proposal rather than assume one.

**The word *checked* does not ship until it is true.** A4 refuses it and `freshness.test.tsx` asserts the refusal; that test is updated by the render slice, never worked around.

---

### The join proposal Lane A owes — brought 2026-08-05, four polls late

**This is the proposal C-219 records as owed, and its lateness is this lane's finding rather than Lane C's.** The item has read *"Lane A will bring Lane C a proposal"* since 2026-08-03, and the queue's `[[held]]` entry has said *"no proposal has been brought"* on every poll since. **Lane C was never the one holding this.**

#### What the repository actually contains, read rather than recalled

| Where | What it knows | What it does **not** |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_watermark` | `(workspace, provider, capability, **subject**, position, attempted_at)`. **The only place `attempted_at` lives** | Any entity id |
| `provider_sync` | provider · capability · status · timings · counts | **No subject at all** — the sentence A4 already relies on, now confirmed against the columns |
| `raw_provider_record` | `external_id` — the **provider's** id for the record — and `sync_id` | **Which subject was requested.** The request's input is not stored on its output |
| `knowledge_graph` | Entities bound by **`(provider, provider_external_id)`** (`repository.entities_for_subjects`) | Any typed subject string |

> **The two identifier spaces never meet.** The watermark holds a string the customer typed; the entity holds an identifier the provider issued; **nothing records that a request for *"Datadog"* returned external id `co_9f3`.** The join does not exist to be found — it would have to be created.

#### Three ways to create it, and one of them is refused outright

**① Match the entity's claimed names against `watermark.subject`.** ❌ **Refused, and not on cost.** *"Datadog, Inc."* is not *"Datadog"*; an entity found under a former name matches nothing; casing and punctuation decide correctness. **The failure is silent and confident** — it renders *"checked 2 hours ago"* against the wrong company, or *"never checked"* against one that was. That is precisely what A7's own risk line forbids — *ship the word `checked` only once it is true* — and it re-performs resolution in a second place by a **weaker method than the resolver's**, which inverts §2's least-powerful-author rule: a string comparison guessing what the resolver already computed.

**② Record the binding where it is known.** A sync for subject *S* holds *S* in hand and receives records carrying external ids. **Persist `(workspace, provider, subject, provider_external_id)` as an output of the sync**, and the path becomes entity → identity binding → subject → watermark. ✅ **Deterministic, replayable, and authored by the component that actually has the fact.** ❌ A new table, a migration and a write on the ingest path — 🟠, and `provider_platform`'s, so Lane A's to build. ⚠️ It is **many-to-many**: one subject yields many external ids, and two spellings of one company reach one entity, so an entity's *last checked* is *the most recent `attempted_at` across the subjects that produced it*. Well-defined, and worth stating before anybody assumes a single row.

**③ Surface the fact against the declaration instead of the entity** — **C-219's own second alternative**, *"a decision to surface the fact per target account rather than per account entity."* ✅ **No join, no schema change, no migration, buildable today**: the declared-target list is keyed by subject, which is the watermark's key. ✅ **Truthful by construction** — the customer asked Signora to watch *"Datadog"*, and the product says when it last tried to read *"Datadog"*. ❌ It does not put the fact on the brief, which is where §A7 put it.

#### Recommendation — ③ now; ② only when a screen demands it. ① never

**The fact `attempted_at` records is *"when did we last try to read this subject"*, and a subject is a declaration rather than an entity.** Rendering it against the declaration is not a workaround — **it is the fact in its own vocabulary**, and it needs no identifier that does not already exist.

**The asymmetry that decides it**: an entity can exist having never been a target — it arrived through another capability — and *last checked* is **meaningless** for that entity, not merely unknown. **The subject is the thing that gets checked; the entity is what was learned from it.** A brief-level rendering would therefore have to say *nothing to report* for a whole class of accounts and could never explain why.

**② is the right answer if and when the product genuinely needs entity-level freshness** — and building it before a screen asks is speculative architecture for a question nobody has posed (§6). **The trigger to reconsider is explicit: a screen that must state freshness for an account reached through something other than a target declaration.**

**What Lane A asks of Lane C:** ratify ③ as A7's render target, or name the screen that requires ②. **Either answer unblocks the render; this lane is not waiting on which.**

---

### ✅ Lane C's review — 2026-08-06 · **③ ratified.** The render is unblocked

**Reviewed under [D-100](DECISION_REGISTER.md), which makes a Product Office-owned dependency blocking a lane the highest operational priority.** ⚠️ **This item had been answerable since 2026-08-05 and sat because [this office's own queue named Lane A as the holder](coordination/queues/lane-c.toml).**

#### ⚡ The specification already contains ③, which decides who may ratify it

**[51 §A7](architecture/51-implementation-specifications.md), *The hard part, and it is not the column*, verbatim:**

> *"Joining the two needs either a resolved-subject link the Knowledge Graph can follow, **or the answer surfaced per *target account* rather than per account entity**. **This is the design decision the slice turns on.**"*

> ## **③ is not a deviation from approved scope. It is the specification's own second branch, and the specification explicitly delegated the choice.**
>
> **So this is Lane C's to ratify and needs no ruling** — §6a's test is *would this, as submitted, breach a rule the repository can name?*, and the answer is no.

#### And the code makes ③ stronger than *"cheapest"* — it is the only coherent option

**Measured, not recalled:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **`TargetAccount`** | **`(id: UUID, name: str)`** — and **nothing else.** `target_accounts.py`: *"It names companies; it finds none… It does not resolve the name"* |
| ⚡ **The key identity** | **`TargetAccount.name` is what becomes `RunProviderSync(subject=…)`** — *"`RunProviderSync` has taken a `subject: str` since M2.1 and nothing has ever supplied one. This is it."* **The two keys are the same string from the same source** |
| ⚡ **And the entry has a stable client-chosen id** | **So the render keys on an id rather than on a name** — ①'s failure mode is not merely avoided, it is unreachable |

> ## **③ performs no join because there is nothing to join. `subject` *is* the target account's name, by construction.**

⛔ **And ② is not merely deferred — it is the only route to the brief, and the brief is closed.** **`TargetAccount` carries no entity id *deliberately*, and [ADR-0036](architecture/adr/0036-target-account-contract.md) makes that boundary permanent.** **Rendering `attempted_at` on the brief requires the subject↔entity binding, which is exactly what ② would have to create.**

#### ⚠️ The one consequence Lane A understated, and it is this review's own finding

**§A7's UX row says *"the same line A4 owns, extended"* — which is the brief. ③ does not render there.** **The specification therefore disagrees with itself**: its *hard part* row offers ③, and its *UX* row assumes ②.

> **Resolved in ③'s favour, and the acceptance criteria already permit it:** **③ *"The existing A4 sentence is unchanged when this fact is absent"*** — **so a brief with no target declaration behind it stays exactly as it is today, which is what acceptance asked for.**
>
> ⚡ **And Lane A's asymmetry is the reason this is right rather than merely allowed:** **an entity that was never a target has no *last checked* — the fact is *meaningless* for it, not unknown.** **Rendering it on the brief would require saying *nothing to report* for a whole class of accounts with no way to explain why**, which is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md): an absence that cannot distinguish itself from a failure.

**[51 §A7](architecture/51-implementation-specifications.md)'s UX row is amended to name the target-account surface.** **It is Lane C's document and this is the branch it delegated** — recorded rather than edited silently.

#### The ruling

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Ratified** | **③ — freshness renders per target account.** **A7's render is unblocked and needs nothing from anybody** |
| ⛔ **Refused** | **① name matching.** Lane A's refusal is correct and its reasoning is the repository's: **a second resolver by a weaker method than the resolver's.** [462 §1](architecture/462-observed-attributes-proposal.md) refused the identical shape for `ClaimSet` four documents ago |
| ⏸ **Sequenced, trigger stated** | **②, and the trigger is exactly Lane A's**: *a screen that must state freshness for an account reached through something other than a target declaration.* **Not fired. No screen asks** |
| 🔴 **What would reopen it** | **A product owner decision that freshness must appear on the brief.** **That is ②, it costs a table, a migration and a write on the ingest path, and it is the only thing in this item that is not Lane C's** |

⛔ **No code written · no table created · no migration · no UI changed · no backlog row.** **Lane A builds the render; this office ratified which fact it renders.**

### ✅ Closed — Lane A, 2026-08-06. The render is built, and ③ cost less than the item did

**Closed by the requesting lane, which is the rule** (§20e — *the requesting lane closes*). **Both halves of [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md) are delivered** and the task is `IN VALIDATION`.

**What shipped**: **`GET /workspaces/{id}/target-account-coverage`** — `provider_platform`'s **first HTTP surface** — answering, per declared company, *when did anybody last look* and *did anything come back*. The watch list renders it; **the brief is untouched**, so acceptance ③ holds by construction rather than by care.

> ⚡ **The ratification's central finding held up against the code, and it made the slice smaller than either lane expected.** **③ performs no join because there is nothing to join.** `TargetAccount.name` is the `subject` a sync is given, so the two keys are one string from one source — **no resolution, no binding, no matching, and the entry's stable client-chosen id means the render keys on an id rather than on a name.**

**One thing this lane owes the record, because the item was opened on the opposite belief.** **C-219 was raised as *"the render waits on the join"*, and there was never a join.** The specification's *hard part* row said the choice was ②-or-③ and this lane read that as *a join must be designed*; **③ was the branch that required no design at all.** Four polls were spent before the proposal was brought, and the proposal, once brought, took Lane C one sitting to ratify. **The cost was not the ruling — it was the framing.**

⚠️ **And this lane understated one consequence, which Lane C caught rather than this one**: [51 §A7](architecture/51-implementation-specifications.md)'s **UX row assumed ②** while its *hard part* row offered ③ — **the specification disagreed with itself**, and the proposal did not say so. It is amended in place now, with the reason recorded rather than the sentence quietly replaced.

**The two refusals stand and are recorded as commitments, not preferences.** ⛔ **① name matching** — a second resolver by a weaker method than the resolver's, and its failure is silent and confident. ⛔ **② the binding table** — sequenced behind Lane C's stated trigger, *a screen that must state freshness for an account reached through something other than a target declaration*. **Not fired; nothing in this slice brings it closer.**

**And the standing contract was kept in the direction that costs something.** *"Only ship the word checked once it is true."* **`Freshness`'s refusal is not lifted** — it still may not say *checked* on the brief, and `freshness.test.tsx` still asserts it. **`LastChecked` is a second export beside it**, which is what that component's own docstring predicted the second kind would be, so the honest sentence and the dishonest one are not one boolean apart inside one component.

## C-221 · Epic C's first open question is answered, and the answer blocks the epic

> ✅ **`RULED WITH MODIFICATION` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"**Do NOT expand the architecture around people until we have a reliable provider capability.** Epic C should initially focus on **role-based and organization-level intelligence**. Treat named-person intelligence as a future enhancement. **Avoid speculative architecture.**"* ⛔ **No `people` bounded context is created.** **[TASK-201](BACKLOG.md) is unblocked at narrowed scope** — and **Lane C's specification half is answered by the narrowing itself**, so nothing is owed here.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** (the epic) · **Lane C** (the specification) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Product scope · provider contract |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner, at narrowed scope |
| **Blocks** | **All of Epic C's Phases 1–3.** Phase 4 was already conditional |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-04, doing exactly what [ADR-0400](architecture/adr/0400-person-as-an-entity.md) instructs before any code |

**ADR-0400 marks ❓1 *"Check this before writing any code."*** It was checked before any was written. **The answer is no**, and the ADR had already named the consequence.

### The trace, end to end

| Where | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `provider_normalization/.../mappers/enrichment.py` | Reads `title`, `type`, `seniority`, `occurred_on` from `employee_changes`. **No name is read** |
| `RoleChangeValue` (`domain/vocabulary.py:144`) | `title` · `seniority` · `direction`. **No name field exists to carry one** |
| `simulation/generators/enrichment.py:149` | Emits exactly those four keys. **The simulator models no name** |
| **Every dataset and scenario in the repository** | **2 real `employee_change` records**, in `playground@2.json`, keys `occurred_on · seniority · title · type` |
| Repository-wide search | **No `person_name`, `contact_name`, `full_name` or `first_name` anywhere outside tests** |

> **No person's name enters the platform at any point.** Not from the provider contract, not from the simulator, not from any recorded data.

### Why that blocks the epic rather than merely shrinking it

**ADR-0400's aggregate root is an identity**: *"`Person` — identity · **names as claims** · provider identities · resolution state."* **There are no name claims to make, and no field that could carry one.**

**This is precisely the condition `knowledge_graph` wrote down as the reason people were excluded** — *"claims carry role changes but no person **identifier**, so there is no identity to resolve"* (`domain/identity.py:32`). **The ADR's case was that Epic C supplies that identifier. Nothing in the repository does.**

**Building `Person` and `Affiliation` now would be an identity model with nothing to identify** — speculative structure for an input that does not exist (§6, *do not add abstractions for requirements that do not yet exist*), and it would introduce **personal-data storage with no personal data and no lawful basis declared** (❓2).

### What the ADR itself says happens now

> *"If the answer is no, Phase 2 of the strategy degrades to **'a VP of Engineering left'** — **today's behaviour** — and ❓2's route B becomes the only path to a named person."*

**Route B is [E1](BACKLOG.md) — read contacts from the customer's own CRM, under the customer's own lawful basis.** It is **Lane B's, and unbuilt.** Lane C recommended it on its own merits and it is already `READY` in the queue.

### Three ways forward, and none is Lane A's to choose

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Answer the provider-contract question** — does the *production* provider return a name? | **Nothing in this repository can.** It needs the vendor contract, which is a product-owner input |
| **B** | **Sequence [E1](BACKLOG.md) first**, then Epic C reads people from the customer's CRM | **Lane C's recommendation in ❓2, for independent reasons.** It is Lane B's epic |
| **C** | **Build the context now against no input** | **Lane A recommends against.** It is structure for a capability with no data, in the module class with the heaviest compliance obligation |

**Lane A is not asking for a different assignment and has not started one.** [TASK-201](BACKLOG.md) is claimed and recorded blocked. **This is the epic's own gate returning *stop*, checked in the order the ADR set.**

### One governance note, separate from the above

**[ADR-0400](architecture/adr/0400-person-as-an-entity.md) is `PROPOSED`, not ratified**, and says so in its own status block: *"Not ratified, and nothing is implemented."* **A new bounded context is 🔴** (product owner + ADR). The assignment is the epic approval; **the ratification stamp is a separate act and only the product owner can apply it.** Recorded rather than assumed, because the ADR is explicit that the two are separate.

---

### Investigation continued — every ADR-0400 repository claim validated, 2026-08-04

**On the product owner's direction: the epic is not handed back, and one blocked phase does not stop the rest.** Every claim ADR-0400 makes about this repository was checked against source.

| ADR-0400 claim | Verified |
|---|---|
| `identity.py:32` — *"Person is deliberately absent… no person identifier, so there is no identity to resolve"* | ✅ **Exact, at that line.** `EntityKind` holds `COMPANY` and `TECHNOLOGY` |
| `committee.py:116` — no stable role id; *"trigger: the first consumer that needs to cite a particular seat"* | ✅ **Exact.** And the asymmetry with `Product` is argued in place |
| `LEADERSHIP_APPOINTED` / `LEADERSHIP_DEPARTED` exist | ✅ `taxonomy.py:71–72`, with detection rules at `rules/point.py:186,192` |
| `new_decision_maker` / `decision_maker_departed` exist | ✅ `signal_engine/domain/catalog.py:57–58` |
| *"The buying score consumes both"* | ✅ **True, and better than stated** — see below |
| *"`make runtime-composition` reports 2 of 9 consumers wired"* | ✅ **2 of 9**, and *unexpected missing wiring* is **0** |

**Two findings that change the epic's shape.**

#### 1 · The score is signal-type-agnostic, so a person costs it nothing

`scoring.py:78` weights a signal by `model.weight_for(signal.signal_type)` — **generic over the catalog, with no branch per type.** The ADR says the score *consumes* both signals; the stronger fact is that **it would consume a person-subjected signal with no change at all.** **Epic C adds no scoring work**, which removes a phase most people would have planned.

#### 2 · An interval cannot close without an identity — and that is *why* `Person` is the root

**Worth stating because the obvious workaround does not survive contact.** `Affiliation` is the ADR's *"where the intelligence lives"*, and it is tempting to read it as buildable without ❓1: the platform has `title`, `direction` and `occurred_on`, so *"a VP of Engineering joined Acme in July"* is already expressible.

**It is not, beyond one end.** Pairing an appointment with a departure requires knowing they concern **the same person**, and with no identifier two VPs of Engineering appointed and one departing is unresolvable. **A single-ended interval is exactly today's behaviour** — which is the degradation the ADR predicted, reached from the other direction.

> **So the epic does not split into a blocked half and an executable half.** `Person` is the root because the interval depends on it, and the ADR was right to make it so. **Recorded because the split is the first thing a reader will reach for**, and it costs a week to discover it does not work.

#### What is executable today, and by whom

| | Owner | Depends on ❓1 |
|---|---|---|
| **A stable role id on `commercial_profile`'s committee** | **Lane B** — the module's own recorded trigger has fired | **No.** Small, independent, and useful to Epic C whichever route wins |
| **`EntityKind.PERSON` in the graph** | `knowledge_graph`, **unassigned** | **Yes** — the docstring's own condition is the identifier |
| **Person storage, repository, API, UI, events** | Lane A | **Yes** — all of it is structure around an identity |
| **Scoring changes** | — | **None needed.** Finding 1 |

**Everything Lane A owns in this epic sits behind ❓1.** That is not a scoping accident: ADR-0400 made identity the root deliberately, and finding 2 is why the shortcut around it does not exist.

### Investigation closed — 2026-08-04

**The product owner accepted the findings and moved Lane A off Epic C.** Recorded rather than left implied, because the next reader needs to know this item is *finished as an investigation* and not *abandoned mid-way*.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What was achieved** | Repository reuse verified · every ADR-0400 assumption verified against source · implementation dependencies identified · risks documented |
| **What is preserved** | Everything above. **No further repository investigation is required for Epic C unless requested** |
| **Why Lane A stopped** | **Not a blocker it could engineer around.** Epic C waits on product direction, an architectural decision, and [E1](BACKLOG.md)'s progression — none of which an implementation lane supplies |
| **Ownership** | **Historical ownership of the investigation stays with Lane A.** Implementation ownership is no longer its active priority, by the product owner's ruling |

> **Whoever picks Epic C up inherits a validated starting point rather than a re-run.** The two findings that matter are above: **the buying score needs no change at all**, and **an interval cannot close without an identity** — which is why the tempting split into a blocked half and an executable half does not exist.

## C-222 · `reasoning@1` earns a release under protocol 2, on a model this workstation cannot measure in time

> ### Re-read 2026-08-04 under the AI Execution Modes directive — [431 §5](architecture/431-ai-execution-modes.md)
>
> **This item is not a fact about `reasoning@1`. It is a fact about `llama3.1:8b` on this workstation.**
>
> **The prompt passes protocol 2 on quality** — 0 grounding failures, 0 schema failures, `EARNED`. **It fails only on wall-clock**, against a local runtime **the product will never use in production** ([ADR-0028](architecture/adr/0028-model-runtime-by-environment.md): *"Ollama is a development dependency, never a production one"*).
>
> **Under Evaluation Mode with a configurable provider, `reasoning@1` can be evaluated against a hosted model.** The Anthropic adapter **already exists and is already registered when credentials are present.** **No timeout is tuned, no prompt is re-authored, no rule is bent** — the *pairing* changes, and a pairing is what an evaluation record names.
>
> ✅ **Ruled 2026-08-04.** The evaluation provider is configurable; **the deterministic mock is the local default**; another provider may be chosen explicitly where credentials exist. **`reasoning@1` is re-evaluated under a chosen provider, and the record names it** — provider · model · version · execution mode · prompt version · protocol version. **No timeout was tuned and no prompt re-authored**, which is what [TASK-013](BACKLOG.md)'s prohibition was protecting.
>
> **The original note is kept as the dated record of why it was not inferred.** `CLAUDE.md` §10: *"the pinned evaluation model is part of the benchmark… changing the model is an architectural decision that belongs to the product owner, never to a coding session working around slow hardware."* **The directive is that decision at policy level; C-222 needs it at the level of this pairing.**
>
> **What closing it releases:** Epic G's runtime refusal. `require_model` refuses `reasoning@1` until a protocol-2 release exists, and **that has been true since 2026-08-04.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product owner** (recording the measurement) · **QE** (whether the manifest may hold it) |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Release rule · evaluation policy |
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION`** — **ruled by the product owner 2026-08-04.** *"Reasoning evaluations shall no longer depend on a local Ollama runtime. The evaluation provider is now configurable."* **Not `CLOSED`**: the dependency is resolved and **the re-evaluation has not been run**, so closing it would report work that has not happened |
| **Blocks** | **Only a live G1 inference.** `require_model` refuses `reasoning@1` at runtime until a protocol-2 release exists |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-04, running the re-run [29-ai-reasoning-engine.md](architecture/29-ai-reasoning-engine.md) asked for |

### The measurement

**`reasoning@1` on `llama3.1:8b`, rendering protocol 2: 0 grounding failures, 0 schema failures, coverage 0.667 — `EARNED`.** Same prompt fingerprint, same dataset, same rubric, same schema. **One variable differed: the client timeout.**

**It took 172.8 s for two cases — ~86 s each.** `InferencePolicy.timeout_seconds` is **60**. Under the committed policy the identical pairing reports **UNMEASURABLE**.

### Why this is a decision and not an engineering choice

**[TASK-013](BACKLOG.md) forbids it in writing** — *"Do not tune the prompt, delimiter, schema or timeout to make it pass."* **A timeout was changed and it passed.** That the change cannot affect the numbers — a call either completes and is scored, or does not complete and is scored by nobody — is an argument, and **an argument is exactly what that prohibition exists to refuse from a lane.**

**The manifest carries no timeout field.** A recorded row would therefore be indistinguishable from one measured under the committed policy, and **this repository could not re-measure it.** Recording it also *derives a release*, which changes what `Prompt.is_released_for` answers at runtime. **Both are above a lane's authority.** Nothing was recorded.

### The state this leaves `reasoning@1` in

| | |
|---|---|
| **`granite3.3:2b`** | Certified under protocol **1**; under protocol **2** it scores **0.0 with 2 grounding failures** |
| **`llama3.1:8b`** | Passes protocol **2**; needs **~86 s** where policy allows **60 s** |
| **Runtime today** | **Refused** — `_refuse_stale_protocol`, and its message is *"Re-evaluate under the current protocol — do not re-author the prompt"* |

> **The model that fits in 4 GiB of VRAM no longer satisfies protocol 2. The model that satisfies protocol 2 does not fit.** Every locally-runnable model is on one side or the other of that line, so **no local re-measurement closes this**.

### What would close it, in order of cost

- **A hosted-model evaluation.** [ADR-0028](architecture/adr/0028-model-runtime-by-environment.md) says production runs hosted models regardless, `--model claude-sonnet-4-5` already works as configuration, and a hosted model returns well inside 60 s. **This is [C-410](#c-410)'s question arriving with a concrete first caller** — and it settles the release honestly rather than by exception.
- **Accept the measurement above with the timeout stated on the row.** Needs a manifest field that does not exist, and QE should rule on whether a release may cite a policy the default cannot reproduce.
- **Re-measure on hardware that fits the model.** Changes nothing about the benchmark; needs a machine with ≥ 6 GiB of VRAM.

**Lane A recommends the first**, and is not blocked meanwhile: everything in G1 except a live inference is buildable, and the refusal path is testable precisely because the refusal is real.
## C-223 · `competitor_entry` cannot be implemented across the current dependency graph

> ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` with a concrete trigger — [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Trigger: Epic D phase 1's *detection* half entering implementation.** **The declaration, its API and its screen are shipped; only detection waits.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **Product office** — the boundary question. **Product owner** — the ruling |
| **Requesting lane** | Lane A |
| **Category** | Module dependency · architecture boundary |
| **Status** | `OPEN` — **[TASK-203](BACKLOG.md) implementation-complete to this boundary** |
| **Blocks** | **Only the detection half of Epic D phase 1.** The declaration, its API and its screen are shipped |
| **Raised** | 2026-08-04, after the declaration was complete and the consumer could not be written |

> **This item states facts and stops.** Lane A's responsibility ends at identifying the boundary; **how it is crossed is Product Office's**, and nothing below proposes a direction, a mechanism or a contract.

### Which module owns the declaration today

**`commercial_profile`.** Aggregate `DeclaredCompetitors`, table `declared_competitors`, migration `0036`, endpoints `GET`/`PUT /workspaces/{id}/competitors`. Shipped and gated.

### Which module needs to consume it

**`signal_engine`.** The `competitor_entry` signal is its catalog row, its detection rule and its scoring weight.

### The minimal data that must become visible

**Per workspace: the set of declared competitor names, and each entry's stable id.**

Nothing else in the aggregate is needed by the consumer — not the version, not `created_by`, not `created_at`, not `supersedes`. Volume is bounded at `MAX_COMPETITORS = 200`.

### The current dependency path

**There is none.** `signal_engine` reads nothing from `commercial_profile` today, in either direction.

The only `Commercial Profile` edge in [05-module-dependencies.md](architecture/05-module-dependencies.md) is **`Commercial Profile → Provider Platform`**, for the target account list.

### The dependency that is missing

**Any path by which `signal_engine` can observe `commercial_profile`'s competitor declaration.**

### Why the current graph prevents implementation

Two enforcements, either of which is sufficient on its own:

- **`pyproject.toml`** — the contract *"signal_engine reaches upstream modules only through `public/`"* lists the modules it may reach, and `commercial_profile` is not among them. `lint-imports` fails on the attempt.
- **§5 and the Change Budget** — a cross-module dependency may be added only where it *"matches an edge already present in the dependency graph, or is proposed and approved as a graph change first."* No such edge is present, and **a new cross-module dependency is 🔴 — product owner and ADR.**

**The change would be small, which is why it is raised rather than made.** *"I could just add it"* is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision inside a feature slice.

### What is waiting behind the boundary

| | |
|---|---|
| **The catalog row** | `competitor_entry` in `signal_engine/catalog/signals@1.json` — contractionary, and **no detection strategy currently expresses *"only when the adopted technology is one the customer declared"***; the catalog has `single_event` and `composite` |
| **The scoring weight** | `competitor_entry` in `scoring/scoring_model@1.json` |
| **The detection rule** | The join between `TECHNOLOGY_ADOPTED` and the declared set |

**Nothing else.** Everything in Epic D phase 1 that does not cross this boundary is built, tested and pushed — the declaration, its persistence, its tenancy, its API and its screen.
