## C-300 · Provider Platform owns the half of the inbound path Lane B may not build

> ⏸️ **`DEFERRED` with a concrete trigger — [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Trigger: [409](architecture/409-inbound-source-port-contract.md) step 4 — the runner — entering implementation.** ⚡ **The same trigger `LIVE_CAPABILITIES` already names for `CRM_RECORDS`**: *"it joins this set when the runner lands, and not before."* **One trigger, two consumers, and it is already written in code.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane B**, 2026-08-04, on building the Integrations half of [409](architecture/409-inbound-source-port-contract.md) after [C-326](#c-326--epic-e1-has-no-path-for-a-customers-own-system-to-reach-the-pipeline) was ruled |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it is an assignment question, and step 4 is 🔴 |
| **State** | `OPEN` — **and Lane B is holding**, on the ruling of 2026-08-04: *"do not begin steps 3–5 until ownership has been established through the normal Product Office assignment process."* |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing today.** Both halves are specified and one is built. **This asks who builds the other** |

### The situation, in one line

> **The port exists and nothing drives it.** `IntegrationSourceAdapter` is published from `integrations/public/`, `HubSpotCompanySource` implements it, and **`provider_platform` is where a runner would live.**

**Lane B built steps 1, 2 and 6 and stopped exactly at the module boundary**, which is what §20e requires: *"if a lane needs a change inside a module it is not assigned, that is a finding to raise, never a change to make."*

| Step | What | Module | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| **3** | Widen `provider: ProviderName` → `str` on the four sync events. **No payload changes** — `to_payload()` already emits `self.provider.value` | `provider_platform` | 🟢 |
| **4** | `RunIntegrationSync`, writing the same `raw_provider_record` and publishing the same `provider.record.received`. **The watermark's `subject` widens from *"the company this position is about"* to *"the scope this position is for"*, and holds the `connected_account_id`** | `provider_platform` | 🔴 |
| **5** | A **simulated** source adapter, driving port → runner → watermark → raw record → event → mapper → claims **with no vendor and no credential** | `provider_platform` | 🟠 |

### Why the ordering matters more than the assignment

**Step 5 is the one to insist on.** It proves the whole contract before anything external is involved. **A lane that merges 5 and 7 debugs OAuth and the ingestion path at once**, and the second failure always looks like the first.

**Step 7 — the live run — needs the HubSpot developer application**, which is environmental and already recorded. **Steps 3, 4 and 5 need nothing from anybody.**

### What Lane B is not doing, and why it is saying so

**Not building it.** `provider_platform` is Lane A's and is in Implementation Waiting on [C-021](#c-021). **Not proposing to take the module either** — that is an ownership transfer, and those need their own ruling rather than arriving inside a slice.

> **The contract is complete either way.** [409](architecture/409-inbound-source-port-contract.md) specifies all seven steps; **who executes steps 3–5 is the product owner's, and until it is answered the customer's CRM has a door and nobody to open it.**

## C-224 · A new write surface needs an authorization `Resource`, and two governance rules disagree about who may add one

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05.** *"Adding a new `Resource` enum member is a **declarative registration**, not an authorization grant. Authorization is granted only through `policy.csv`. A `Resource` entry without policy grants provides no runtime capability."* **So the procedural conflict is removed without weakening anything**: the declaration is architectural, the grant is the policy file, and the two authorities stop contradicting each other because they were never governing the same thing. **[TASK-405](BACKLOG.md)'s remaining route is unblocked**, and *"future lanes do not reopen this question"* — recorded in `CLAUDE.md` §20a.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-05, implementing [TASK-405](BACKLOG.md) — reached at the route, after the domain, persistence, use case and read surface were complete and green |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it is an authorization permission and a Change Budget question, and both are explicitly the product owner's |
| **Status** | **`RULED`** — 2026-08-05, product owner |
| **Blocks** | **One route.** `POST` a resolution. The read surface, the persistence, the use case and the audit trail are all delivered and tested |

### The problem, in one line

**Every write surface in this repository authorizes against its own `Resource`, there is no `signal` one, and the two files needed to add it have two different owners.**

### What was reached

`TASK-405` records a decision about a signal — actioned, assigned, snoozed, dismissed. The handler must call `context.authorize(Resource.?, Action.?)`. The twelve existing resources are `workspace`, `member`, `opportunity`, `account`, `product`, `icp`, `research`, `buying_committee`, `commercial_focus`, `target_account`, `timeline`, `integration`, `competitor`. **None of them is this.**

### Why no existing tuple was reused

| Candidate | Why not |
|---|---|
| `account:read` | **A write authorized as a read is a security defect**, not a shortcut |
| `account:update` | Granted to **no role** in `policy.csv`, so every caller would 403 — and it is far broader than triage, authorizing whatever "editing an account" comes to mean later |
| `opportunity:update` | **A signal is not an opportunity.** `Resource.ACCOUNT`'s own comment records that identities exist for accounts with no opportunity at all; triage would silently fail on exactly those |

### The two rules, and where they disagree

| | Authority | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `signora_platform/authorization/enforcer.py` — the `Resource` enum | **🔴 Product owner + ADR** | `CLAUDE.md` §20e, the Change Budget: *"`signora_platform/**`"* |
| `signora_platform/authorization/policies/policy.csv` | **Any lane — append-only** | `CLAUDE.md` §20e, *Shared files*: *"Registries every lane extends"* |

**They are one registration in two files.** A policy row naming a resource with no enum member is unreachable; an enum member with no policy row denies everyone. Neither half is useful alone, and the two halves carry opposite authorities.

**§20a does not settle it either.** Its carve-out names *"a new subscription, registering a new event type, adding a worker pool, or extending the Security Invariants suite"* — **not an authorization resource**, and authorization is listed among the frozen substrate in the same section.

### What the repository has actually done, twelve times

Every resource after `workspace` and `member` was added by a feature lane, and three carry an inline justification written by whoever added them — *"a **use** of the platform rather than a change to it (§20a): a new member, no interface reshaped, no existing caller affected — the same category as registering a new event type."*

**That reasoning is sound and it is also a lane's own.** Either it was approved each time and the Change Budget's 🔴 row is understated, or twelve slices took a 🔴 change without an ADR. **Lane A is not going to be the thirteenth on its own authority**, and is not proposing that the earlier twelve were wrong.

### What is asked

**One ruling, and any of the three closes it:**

1. **Registering an authorization `Resource` is a registry extension** — add it to §20a's carve-out list and to the Shared-files row beside `policy.csv`, which is where a lane would look. Lane A adds `SIGNAL` and four policy rows and finishes the route.
2. **It is 🔴 and stays 🔴** — the product owner approves this instance, and the twelve precedents are recorded as historic rather than as a rule.
3. **Triage authorizes under an existing resource** the product owner names, accepting the breadth.

### The proposed registration, if (1) or (2)

```
    #: Registered by TASK-405 — a hypothesis a person triages. Distinct from
    #: `account` because signals exist for accounts nobody has qualified, and
    #: triaging one is not editing the company it is about.
    SIGNAL = "signal"
```

```csv
p, owner, *, signal, read
p, member, *, signal, read
p, owner, *, signal, update
p, member, *, signal, update
```

**`update` rather than `add`**, and granted to `member` as well as `owner`: deciding a signal is ordinary selling work, on the same terms as `opportunity:update`, which both roles hold. A queue only an owner could clear is not a queue.

### The request body Lane A would then define

Four named bodies behind one discriminated union on `outcome`, so `{"outcome": "dismissed"}` **with no reason is refused by the schema** rather than by a check somebody remembered to write — the same reason `Dismissed` carries no default in the domain. `actioned` carries nothing; `assigned` carries `to`; `snoozed` carries `until`; `dismissed` carries `reason`.

**They are deliberately not in the code today.** A schema no route can reach is a contract nobody agreed to.

## C-225 · Wave 1's technology stack section has no contract a screen can reach, and 414 counts it twice

> ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md). Answered by delivery.** **Wave 1 shipped ten sections, not eleven — [414](architecture/414-wave-1-account-360.md) was corrected before anything was built.** **The product owner's half — *does wave 1 ship the subset or wait* — is answered by the subset having shipped.**


| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-05, on claiming [TASK-417](BACKLOG.md) and checking each of the twelve sections against the routes that actually ship — **before writing a line** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** (the [414](architecture/414-wave-1-account-360.md) correction) · **Lane B** (`knowledge_graph`, if an endpoint is wanted) · **the product owner** (whether wave 1 ships eleven sections or waits) |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED`** — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-116](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this field was not.** **Twelve items carried the same defect**, and every one would have been escalated as an open question. |
| **Blocks** | **One section of one screen** |

### The finding, in one line

**`USES_TECHNOLOGY` is derived, stored and exported through `public/` — and no HTTP route returns it, so the frontend cannot reach it.**

### What exists and what does not

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| `application/relationships.py` | ✅ `TECHNOLOGY_DETECTED` opens a `USES_TECHNOLOGY` edge, `TECHNOLOGY_REMOVED` ends it |
| `GraphQueries.relationships(workspace_id, entity_id, kind=...)` | ✅ exists, and `GraphQueries` **is** in `knowledge_graph/public/` |
| `knowledge_graph/interface/router.py` | ❌ serves `account-identities` and `account-search`, **and nothing else** |

**So this is not missing capability. It is a capability with no customer-facing edge** — which is precisely wave 1's premise (*"twelve sections already served by shipped contracts"*) failing for one row.

### 414 already says eleven in one place and twelve in another

[414 §1](architecture/414-wave-1-account-360.md)'s table carries **twelve 🟩 rows**; its own summary line reads **"Eleven 🟩 · two 🟠 · two ➡️ · seven ⬜"**, and [§2](architecture/414-wave-1-account-360.md) says wave 1 delivers *"the eleven 🟩 sections, and nothing else."* **The off-by-one is this row.** The count was taken against the module, and the module is genuinely capable; the check that would have caught it is *"which route returns this?"*

**[TASK-417](BACKLOG.md)'s own row says twelve**, so the discrepancy reaches the task definition too.

### What Lane A is doing meanwhile

**Building the eleven.** The row's escalate clause is explicit — *"a section needs a contract that does not exist. **That is a finding, not an endpoint to add**"* — so no endpoint was added, and `knowledge_graph` is Lane B's in any case.

**Business events with evidence was checked and is *not* a second instance.** Only `GET /business-events/{event_id}` ships, with no per-account list — but `timeline` projects `business_event_detected` carrying `source_ref`, and the shipped evidence drawer already fetches one event on demand when a citation is opened. **The list comes from the timeline and the evidence comes on click**, which is the pattern already on the page. No new contract, and no N+1 on first paint.

### What is asked

1. **Correct 414 and the TASK-417 row to eleven**, so the next reader is not counting a section that cannot be rendered — Lane C.
2. **Decide whether an account's technology stack is worth an endpoint at all**, and if so whose wave it belongs to. It is a normal `interface/` addition in `knowledge_graph` — a route over a query that already exists and is already public. **Lane A is not proposing to add it**: the module is Lane B's, and finding a defect outside your assignment is not permission to fix it (§20e).

## C-226 · Six sections on one page have rendered a failed read as an empty account, and each was fixed alone

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-05, auditing the account brief's sections against [410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md)'s *"27 sections, each in six states"* while building [TASK-417](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — it is a repository-wide frontend invariant, and whether one exists is an architecture question rather than a render slice's |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [467 §3](architecture/467-system-states-traceability-audit.md).** ⚡ **The invariant it asks for already exists: it is [P-A / R-15](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md), ratified 2026-08-05 — the day before this item was raised.** **One thing remains and it is the product owner's: R-15's *owner*** |
| **Blocks** | Nothing |

> ## ⚡ **Answered 2026-08-06 — and the answer was written the day before the question.**
>
> **[P-A · Stated absence](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md), ratified 2026-08-05:** ***"A result says what it could not evaluate… absence can never distinguish itself from failure."***
>
> **This item, raised independently the same day:** ***"`undefined` then means both 'the API said there is none' and 'the request failed', and the section's empty branch states the first as a fact."***
>
> **Two documents, one sentence, neither citing the other** — and **this office wrote both.**
>
> ⚡ **The register even predicted the trigger**: R-15 stood at **8 instances, 0 implementations, 🔴 highest and unowned**, annotated **🟠 *"Name before the ninth."*** **C-226 is the ninth, and it arrived as six at once on the first screen anybody built.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Is it a repository invariant?** | **Yes. It already was.** The question narrows from *should this be one* to *who implements the one it has* |
| ✅ **Lane A's recommendation is endorsed** | **A page-level test, not a per-component prop.** Build it when convenient — 🟢, one screen, its own harness, **no ruling needed** |
| ⚡ **And Lane A's *refusal* is the better half** | *"A naive guard would be wrong"* — **`EntityName` falls back to the real identifier and makes no false claim under any error.** **A guard that flagged it would teach lanes to add a prop to silence it**: Decorative Logic (§2), predicted before it was written |
| 🔴 **What is left, and it is the only ruling** | **R-15's owner.** **Twenty-six consumers, no module, and nine instances already decided by whoever met one** — [D-090](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s *"ownership should be an architectural decision rather than an implementation accident"* |

### The finding

**One defect has now been found and fixed six times on one screen, by four different slices, and each fix was correct and local.**

| Section | What a failed read rendered | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|
| Detected signals | *"nothing to check"* — an outage as a quiet account | An earlier slice, in `ValidationBlock` |
| The account summary | absence — *"nothing has been written"* | `B-010` / `TASK-004`, via a `404` split |
| Timeline | absence | `C-024`'s mount, via `isError` |
| **Observations** | *"Nothing recorded yet"* | **This slice** |
| **Research** | *"…usually takes a minute or two"* — **and an enabled button offering to spend a worker minute and a model call on a run that may already be in flight** | **This slice** |
| **Opportunities** | nothing at all — the workflow controls vanish, and an account somebody is working reads as one nobody has touched | **This slice** |

**The shape is identical every time**: a page-level hook is destructured for `data` alone, `undefined` then means both *"the API said there is none"* and *"the request failed"*, and the section's empty branch states the first as a fact.

**Three of the six needed a `404` split, not a boolean** — narration, research and opportunities each have a legitimate *"none exists"* that arrives as an error. So the rule is not *"pass `isError` everywhere"*; it is *"absence and failure are different, and the section must be told which."*

### Why this is raised rather than guarded

**A repository-wide invariant is the obvious answer and is not a render slice's to write.** `no-mock-data.test.tsx` and the design-token check are exactly this shape and both are foundation-level. Asserting a new one from inside TASK-417 would bind every lane that touches an account section, on a rule no one has agreed, which is the *"architecture arriving in a feature"* §20e forbids.

**And a naive guard would be wrong.** *"Every section takes `isError`"* would fail `EntityName`, which is correct as written — it falls back to **the real account identifier, never a placeholder**, so it makes no false claim under any error. A guard that flagged it would teach lanes to add a prop to silence it.

### What is asked

**One decision: is *"a section must distinguish absence from failure"* a repository invariant, and if so who writes it?**

Lane A's recommendation, offered rather than taken: **a page-level test rather than a per-component one.** Render the account brief with every hook erroring and assert the page says so — one test, no new prop on any component, and it cannot be silenced by adding a field. `brief.test.tsx` already has the harness. **Lane A will build it on request**; it is not being built unasked because the assertion would reach sections other lanes own.

**Six occurrences of one defect is not six mistakes.** Each lane read the component in front of it, saw an empty state, and shipped correctly. The register is where a repeated shape stops being individually correct.

| **What** | ⚡ **Two binding authorities give different answers about the words on a screen.** **[D-138](../CLAUDE.md) makes the design snapshot the implementation authority**; **[ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) and [§4](../CLAUDE.md) forbid `workspace` in any sentence a customer reads**, and `frontend/tests/components/vocabulary.test.tsx` enforces it executably |
| **Where** | `docs/design-snapshot/screens/Workspace Setup.dc.html` — *"Workspace setup"*, *"Workspace name"*, *"Workspace URL"*, *"Create a workspace"*, *"This is your only workspace"*. ⚡ **Measured, not sampled: `workspace` appears in the visible copy of six of its ten sections** |
| **Asked of Lane C** | **Confirm the reading below, or rule otherwise** — ⛔ **and say it once for every design screen rather than per row**, because four more are queued behind this one |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** **[TASK-468](BACKLOG.md) proceeds** — see below |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-07 |

### Why this is not a blocker, and why it is still worth a row

⚡ **There is only one shippable option today, so proceeding encodes no assumption.** **A screen rendering *"Workspace name"* fails `vocabulary.test.tsx` and cannot reach QE at all** — so the constraint decides it, not this lane's preference. **[TASK-468](BACKLOG.md) is being built with the design's structure and behaviour, rendered in the customer's vocabulary**: *Organization setup*, *Organization name*, *Organization URL*.

⛔ **What is genuinely open is whether that reading is the intended one**, and it is worth one answer rather than five: **[TASK-469](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-467](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) are all design screens** and every one of them will meet the same word.

### The reading this lane is proceeding on

> **[D-138](../CLAUDE.md) governs *what the screen is*. [ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) governs *what it says*.**

⚡ **ADR-0034 already states the mechanism**: *"the translation lives at the frontend edge and never travels inward."* **A design authored upstream is upstream of that edge**, so it naming the platform's term is expected rather than contradictory — the same way `POST /workspaces` keeps its path while the screen above it says *organization*. ⛔ **The alternative reading — that a design's copy overrides the ADR — would make `vocabulary.test.tsx` a test the approved designs are expected to fail**, and a test nobody can satisfy is one somebody eventually deletes.

⚠️ **Stated rather than assumed, because the cost of being wrong is small and visible**: if Lane C rules the other way, the change is string constants and one test, in one commit.

## C-238 · `AffiliationReader` has a Protocol and no implementation, so the composition root has nothing to inject

**Opened 2026-08-07 · Lane A · owner: Lane B · 🟠 · ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-07 by Lane A, the lane that raised it**

> ✅ **Closed by the check it was raised about, applied to its own resolution.** ⛔ **Not by reading that Lane B shipped something** — by opening `backend/modules/people/infrastructure/affiliation_reader.py` on `integration` and `main` and reading what `at_company` does.
>
> ⚡ **`SqlAffiliationReader.at_company` has no `ended_on` predicate at all**, and its docstring names the reason this item gave: *"this one must include closed ones, because 'who left, and when' is the question `decision_maker_departed` exists to answer."* **Ordered `started_on, id` so two consumers get the same answer.** ✅ **And `build_affiliation_reader(session)` exists in `people/infrastructure/composition.py`** — which is the half that was actually missing, because a Protocol with an implementation nobody can construct would have left `GenerateSignals` exactly as unwireable as before.

> ⚡ **Three questions, asked in order, and the fifth instance is what asking only the first two would have produced**: does the type exist · does something implement it · **can the composition root obtain one**. **All three answer yes.**
>
> ⛔ **What this does not do is make [TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) `READY`.** **That state is Lane C's** (§20e). **This lane set the row `BLOCKED` and can say the blocker has cleared; it cannot set the row claimable.** **Recorded on the row so the transition is not waiting on somebody noticing.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **What** | ⛔ **`modules.people.public.AffiliationReader` is a `Protocol` with no class satisfying it anywhere in the repository.** ⚡ **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) can consume the *type* and cannot be *wired*** — `GenerateSignals` takes the port by injection ([ADR-0403](architecture/adr/0403-signal-engine-reads-a-declaration.md)), and the application composition root has nothing to pass |
| **Where** | **Every ref, measured — not one of them carries an adapter.** `git grep -lE 'class Sql.*Affiliation\|def at_company' <ref> -- backend/modules/people` returns **`public/__init__.py` and nothing else** on `origin/integration`, `origin/main`, `origin/lane-b-commercial-profile` and `origin/lane-c-sync` |
| **Asked of Lane B** | **Publish the adapter behind its own Protocol** — the shape `commercial_profile` already ships as `SqlDeclaredCompetitorReader`, which is what `apps/worker/subscriptions.py` injects for the competitor half of the identical pattern |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md)**, at the composition root only. **The consumer half is buildable and is not built** — see below |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-07** *(the requesting lane closes — §20e)*. ⚠️ **Body synced by Lane C 2026-08-07: the index read `CLOSED` and this line still read `OPEN`, and `decision-queue.py --check` reported the disagreement.** ⚡ **The index was right** — **Lane A closed it by opening `affiliation_reader.py` rather than by reading that Lane B had shipped something.** **Answered by Lane B, 2026-08-07.** **The adapter exists**: `people/infrastructure/affiliation_reader.py` publishes `SqlAffiliationReader`, and `people/infrastructure/composition.py` publishes **`build_affiliation_reader(session)`** for the composition root to call — the exact shape `commercial_profile` ships as `SqlDeclaredCompetitorReader` / `build_declared_competitor_reader`, which is what this item asked for. **The requesting lane closes** (§20e). **Was:** **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-07, measured before raising |

### What exists, and what does not

**`people/infrastructure/repository.py` has `open_at_company`** — `ended_on IS NULL`, open intervals only. ⛔ **That is not `at_company`**, whose contract is *"everyone recorded in a role at this company, **open and closed**"*, and the closed interval is the whole reason the port was shaped this way: **`decision_maker_departed` is answerable from nothing else.** **The two methods differ in exactly the half that matters.**

⛔ **`SqlPeopleRepository` therefore does not satisfy `AffiliationReader`**, and no other class attempts to.

| **[C-237](#c-237)** | The types were **published** | **Nothing could read them** |

⚡ **C-237's own closing paragraph named this class and this lane still walked into it**: *"none of them asked whether it was usable by the lane being asked to use it."* ⛔ **I verified the contract was consumable as a type and did not verify it was injectable as an object** — **one step later than the check should have run, again.** **The general form, recorded because the specific fix will not prevent the fifth: *a contract is usable when something implements it*, and every proxy short of constructing one has now failed in turn.**

### ⛔ What Lane A is deliberately not building meanwhile

**Not the domain half on its own.** ⚡ **A `Seat` value and a selection rule that nothing constructs is the speculative abstraction [§6](../CLAUDE.md) forbids** — **and it is precisely the reasoning Lane B applied when it declined to publish this port before a consumer existed.** ⛔ **Taking the opposite side of an argument this lane accepted three days ago would be worth less than the wait.**

⚠️ **Nothing is lost by waiting.** **The design is settled and recorded on the port itself**: `at_company(workspace_id, company_id)` scoped to the entity being generated for, the seat matched on the folded `title` fact the `leadership_*` rules already emit, and **`match_departure`'s refusal reproduced as a read — one candidate names the seat, more than one names none.** **The period is the deliverable; no name is wanted** ([C-221](#c-221)).

## C-237 · TASK-458 has types to read and no way to read them, and `people/public/` says so itself

**Opened 2026-08-07 · Lane A · owner: Lane B · 🟠 · ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-07 by Lane A, the lane that raised it**

> ✅ **Lane B published it, and it is the shape this item asked for.** `people/public/__init__.py` on `integration` is **6,899 bytes** and exports **`AffiliationReader`** alongside the two views — *"where another module asks who has held a role at a company"*, with `at_company(...)` returning **"everyone recorded in a role at this company, open and closed."*
>
> ⚡ **Open *and* closed is the load-bearing half.** A reader that returned only current affiliations could serve `new_decision_maker` and **never** `decision_maker_departed` — the row's second signal type is precisely the closed interval, and a port that dropped it would have looked correct until the first departure.
>
> ⛔ **The port is published by the owning module**, which is [ADR-0403](architecture/adr/0403-signal-engine-reads-a-declaration.md)'s shape and the reason this was raised rather than worked around. **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) is unblocked.**

> ✅ **Answered — Lane B, 2026-08-07. The reader is published.** **`AffiliationReader` — `at_company` and `for_person`, both read-only** — is on `lane-b-commercial-profile` awaiting QE, alongside [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md)'s use case.
>
> ⚡ **Shaped by this item rather than guessed at, which is why the wait was worth something.** **`at_company` returns open *and* closed intervals**, because *"who left, and when"* is what `decision_maker_departed` exists to answer; **the answer carries the interval and never a current employer**, on the reason stated here — `ended_on = None` means *no departure has been observed*; and **the read is scoped to one company**, because a workspace-wide one would invite matching on title alone.
>
> ⛔ **No write on the port at any point.** A judging module must never be able to author the history it reads.
>
> ⚠️ **Two things Lane A should know before building against it.** **Nothing populates `people` yet** — `RecordRoleChange` exists and is unwired, so the reader will answer empty until the wiring slice. And **`for_person` returns one affiliation in almost every case**, because this module mints a new subject per arrival and holds no identifier to match one against ([C-221](#c-221), ❓1 of ADR-0400, gated on [TASK-429](BACKLOG.md)). **Neither is a defect to report back; both are stated on the port itself.**
>
> ⛔ **Left open for the requesting lane to close** — §20e: the requesting lane closes, and this one is Lane A's.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What** | **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) is the *consumer* half — `signal_engine` reads the People contract.** ⛔ **`people/public/` publishes `PersonView` and `AffiliationView` and no reader port**, so there is no published way to obtain either |
| **Where** | `origin/integration`, `backend/modules/people/public/__init__.py` — 4,259 bytes, two frozen dataclasses, no `Protocol` |
| **Asked of Lane B** | **Publish the reader.** `people` is Lane B's ([`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml)); `signal_engine` is Lane A's |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-07**, the lane that raised it, having verified the reader on `integration` at 6,899 bytes. ⚠️ **This field read `OPEN — awaiting integration` until the promotion landed and is corrected rather than left**: a state field is a claim about the present, and one contradicting its own header is the defect §2 exists to prevent. **The dated note below stands as written** |

### The contract states the omission, and states it as correct

> ⛔ **"No reader port**, because no consumer has been written yet and a port shaped for an imagined caller is the speculative abstraction §6 forbids."

**That reasoning was right when it was written and TASK-458 is the event that ends it.** The consumer now exists, is claimed, and knows what it needs — so the port is no longer shaped for an imagined caller. ⚡ **This item is not a criticism of that decision; it is the trigger the decision was waiting for.**

### Why Lane A cannot simply add it

⛔ **`people` is Lane B's module.** [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *a change inside a module this lane is not assigned is a finding to report.* **And the shape is not a matter of taste** — [ADR-0403](architecture/adr/0403-signal-engine-reads-a-declaration.md) is the precedent this row cites, and in it the **owning** module publishes the port: `signal_engine` imports `DeclaredCompetitorReader` from `commercial_profile.public`, and the implementation and its injection stay behind that boundary. **A port declared by the consumer would invert exactly the edge the ADR exists to fix.**

### What this lane needs, stated so it is not shaped by guesswork

**The two signal types this serves are already in the catalog** — `new_decision_maker` from `leadership_appointed`, and `decision_maker_departed` from `leadership_departed`. **What a signal cannot say today is *which seat*.** So the read is *affiliations at a company*, and the answer has to carry the interval rather than a current employer, because `ended_on = None` means **no departure has been observed** and not *"they still work there"* — the contract's own distinction, and the one a signal would otherwise flatten.

⛔ **No name is wanted and none should be published.** [C-221](#c-221) is the specification, and this consumer needs a subject, a role and a period — none of which is a name.

### The third instance in three days, and that is the finding worth keeping

**[C-235](#c-235)**: TASK-458 released while its predecessor's `public/` was an empty blob. **[C-336](#c-336)**: Lane B could not claim TASK-428 because its `Module` spanned a lane boundary. **This**: the same row released again, on a contract that exists but cannot be consumed.

> ⚡ **All three passed a check that asked whether something was *present*.** ⛔ **None of them asked whether it was *usable by the lane being asked to use it*** — and that is a different question, which is why presence keeps returning a green answer to it.

**Opened 2026-08-06 · Lane A · owner: Lane C · 🟡 · ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-07 by Lane A, the lane that raised it**

### What is built, and what one field is missing

**The quote that decided the first version of this item was [ADR-0404](architecture/adr/0404-platform-composition.md)'s**: *"a typed `Settings` choosing which adapters exist belongs to the module that owns the behaviour — that is `provider_platform`, **Lane A's**. **Only the `WorkerRuntime` field is `apps/`, which is Lane C's.**"*

⛔ **That sentence is limiting, and this lane read it as assigning.** ***"Only the `WorkerRuntime` field"*** says what belongs to `apps/` — **one field** — and by saying *only*, it says the rest does not.

|---|---|

### Why this lane did not simply do it

⚠️ **The argument for doing it is real and is recorded rather than hidden**: [§20a](../CLAUDE.md) lists *"adding a new subscription"* among the things the platform freeze **does not** prohibit, and this lane has composed its own module in `apps/` before — `apps/api/composition/coverage.py`, shipped and promoted at [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md).

⛔ **The argument against is the one that decides it**: **a row exists, it names this exact change, and it is assigned to another lane.** *"Finding a defect outside your assignment is an obligation to report it, never permission to fix it"* — and the same holds for finding work. **Doing it here would be Lane A implementing a `READY` row belonging to Lane C**, which is worse than waiting.

> ⚡ **Two lanes could close this in one commit each, and either is fine.** **Lane C claims [TASK-419](BACKLOG.md)** and the subscriptions come with it. **Or Lane C says the subscriptions are Lane A's to add**, and this lane adds them the same hour — the code below them is finished and tested.

### ⚠️ Lane B reported a recurrence on 2026-08-07. Measured: it had already been fixed — and the argument under it was still right

**Lane B's claim**: *"TASK-458's release note now claims 'what `people` publishes is published'."*

⛔ **Measured false at the time of reporting.** **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) reads `SEQUENCED` behind [TASK-479](BACKLOG.md) on `lane-c-sync`, and `origin/coordination` — the ref Lane B polls — carried `state = "SEQUENCED"`, `depends_on = ["TASK-479"]` when the report was written.** ⚡ **Lane B read a stale copy.**

⚡ **Correct, and acted on.** ⛔ **`_delivered` asks whether a predecessor was *handed over* — a fact about process. It never asks whether the thing exists.** ✅ **`state-check` now checks the property directly: every `backend/modules/*/public/__init__.py` on `integration`, and it reports any that is empty.**

⚠️ **It found two, not one.** **`people` — 0 bytes on `main` and on `integration`** — **and `timeline`, also 0.** ⛔ **`timeline` has no consumer yet, so it is a latent gap rather than a live blocker, and no row is created for it** (§6 — *build for the requirement in front of you*). **The check will report it every run until it is filled.**

### ✅ [C-336](BACKLOG.md) — approved as recommended, verified first

**Lane B recommended narrowing [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md) from four modules to `timeline` · `commercial_profile` · `people`, removing `signal_engine`.** ✅ **Approved, and checked rather than accepted**: **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) is titled *Signal Engine reads the People contract*, its Module cell is `signal_engine` — Lane A, and its own row says *"it is the *consumer* half, and separating it is what keeps the boundary inside one lane each."*** ⚡ **So `signal_engine` in [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md) was pre-split scope that survived the decomposition, and all three remaining modules are Lane B's — the row is now cleanly one lane's.**

⚠️ **This office wrote the four-module cell, and noted the problem in this very item without acting on it** — *"recorded so it is decomposed before it is released again."* ⛔ **Lane B did the analysis this office had already agreed was needed.**

✅ **Its second correction is confirmed independently**: the row cited `runtime-composition` at **2 of 9**; **re-running the instrument here reports `Runtime wired 4` with `✓ timeline` named.** ⚡ **Not taken at face value — [D-130](DECISION_REGISTER.md), and the instrument was run rather than the report believed.**

### What the row claims, and what is actually there

TASK-458's released row states its evidence explicitly, and **states it as structural precisely so that it would not be a status-string reading**:

> *"Verified structurally, not by reading a status string: **TASK-457** has 6 commits on `main` and `origin/lane-b-commercial-profile` carries nothing for it that `origin/integration` lacks — **what `people` publishes is published**."*

**Both halves of that are true. The conclusion does not follow.**

```
$ git ls-tree -r --long origin/integration backend/modules/people/public/
100644 blob e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391       0    …/people/public/__init__.py
```

⚡ **`e69de29` is git's empty blob, and the size is `0`.** `people/public/` is **one empty file** — on `integration` **and** on `origin/lane-b-commercial-profile`, the same hash on both. **`people` publishes nothing, so there is nothing for `signal_engine` to consume.** Of TASK-457's six commits on `main`, one is `da514e35 Claim TASK-457 — …`, which is a Task Claim Protocol commit and by definition touches only the two registers.

### Why the check passed anyway — and this is the part worth keeping

**The predicate was *"does the module's `public/` exist and is it reachable?"*, and the answer was yes.** ⛔ **The question the release needed answered was *"does it export anything?"*** — **and an empty `__init__.py` is exactly what a module looks like before its contract is written**, because creating the package is the first commit of the work and populating it is the last.

> **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *"a guard that cannot fail is documentation pretending to be code."*** ⚡ **This guard can fail — but not on the case it was built for.** **A `public/` directory is created empty and stays that way until the row completes**, so *"the file is present"* is true from the first commit of the predecessor to the last. **It discriminates nothing across the interval it was asked about.**

**This is [B-101](BUGS.md)'s class — counting by proxy — one register over.** *Reachability* was the proxy for *published*, and nothing asked whether the proxy was sound.

### The other four, checked the same way

**Tested by content, not by reachability**, since that is the correction this item asks for:

| Row | Predecessor | Verified on `integration` | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TASK-444** | TASK-432 | `signal.resolved` present in `signal_engine/domain/events.py` | ✅ **The release is sound** |
| **TASK-450** | TASK-449 | `workspace_tenancy/public/` — four files, `saved_views.py` at 6,535 bytes | ✅ **The release is sound** |
| **TASK-458** | TASK-457 | `people/public/__init__.py` — **empty blob, 0 bytes** | ⛔ **Not released** |
| **TASK-441** | — | `BLOCKED` on [C-229](#c-229--opportunity-intelligence-needs-a-door-and-d38-closed-that-one-deliberately), whose answer is on `lane-c-sync` only | ⚠️ **Blocked on `integration`** |
| **TASK-478** | — | **Row absent from `integration` entirely** | ⚠️ **Cannot be claimed** |

⚡ **So C-427's diagnosis is right, and right about most of it.** **The stall it names is real** — a successor parked behind a predecessor sitting at `IN VALIDATION` because only QE may write `VERIFIED` — and **TASK-432 and TASK-449 are genuinely delivered.** ⛔ **The finding is not that the release was wrong; it is that one row in twenty-two was checked by a predicate that could not answer the question, and twenty-one were checked by the same predicate.**

### Nothing claimed

⛔ **This lane claimed none of the five.** **On `integration` they read `BLOCKED`, `SEQUENCED`, `SEQUENCED`, `SEQUENCED` and absent**, and the releases exist only on a Product Office branch. **`origin/coordination`'s own README settles it** — *"never the tiebreaker… where it disagrees with `BACKLOG.md` on scope, the integration-side source wins and the disagreement is a Product Office defect. Report it."* **Reported.**

⚠️ **And had TASK-458 been claimed, the first hour would have gone into `signal_engine` reading an empty module contract** — which is [TASK-205](BACKLOG.md)'s shape, and the standing instruction on that row is *"do not implement around the missing public contract."*

## C-232 · Companies shows what Signora tracks, and the audit called it what the customer declared

**Opened 2026-08-06 · Lane A · owner: Lane B and the product owner · 🟡**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, holding [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md), from the reuse audit and before writing a line |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-06**, the requesting lane, which is the rule. **[TASK-472](BACKLOG.md) shipped `GET /accounts-list`.** ⚡ **Body re-synced 2026-08-07 from the index, which Lane A had updated** — [D-131](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ①: a close and its field move together, and here the field lagged the close by a day. |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing.** The screen ships over the read that exists and **says on screen which set it is showing** |

### ✅ Closed the same day — Lane B built the read

**[TASK-472](BACKLOG.md) is on `integration`**: `GET /workspaces/{id}/accounts-list` — *"Every account this workspace knows, a page at a time"* — keyset-paged, with a `ListedAccount` row that is deliberately **not** an `AccountMatch` because *"a browse row is in the list because it exists"*.

⚡ **Two lanes reached the same finding from opposite ends within hours**: this item from the screen, and Product Office's [C-422](#c-422--task-440-is-claimed-and-its-central-element-has-no-read--and-product-office-is-why) from the row. **The read that answers it was scoped, built and validated by the lane that owns `knowledge_graph`** — which is the routing the register exists to produce.

> ⚠️ **One consequence for whoever resumes [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md), including this lane.** **The Companies screen this lane built and held was written against `GET /accounts` — the attention list — because that was the only read there was.** ⛔ **It must be re-pointed at `accounts-list` before it ships**, and the subtitle that carefully said *"every company Signora is tracking"* becomes wrong in the other direction once the browse read is behind it. **The held work is a starting point, not a finished screen** — recorded here so it is not shipped as one.

### The premise that did not survive

**[446](architecture/446-companies-traceability-audit.md), verbatim:**

> | **The account table — 8,412 rows** | **Every company this workspace watches** | **Aggregate + read** — `GET /accounts`, cursor-paginated | ✅ **Exists, and correctly** |

⛔ **`GET /accounts` does not return every company this workspace watches.** Its own docstring says what it returns — *"**Open opportunities** for this workspace, ordered by attention"* — and `open_page` filters to `OPEN_STAGES`. **An opportunity is opened when an account crosses the tracking threshold** (`qualify.py`: *"Open an opportunity when an account crosses the tracking threshold"*).

**So there are two sets and the audit conflated them:**

| | Where it lives | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Declared** | `GET /target-accounts` — `commercial_profile` | **What the customer typed.** *"As the customer typed it. Never resolved."* |
| **Tracked** | `GET /accounts` — `opportunity_engine` | **What Signora found enough about to follow** |

**A declared company that Signora has not found enough about is in neither this screen nor any other**, and its absence currently means nothing a customer can read.

### Why this lane did not close it

**There is no join, and building one is not a render slice.** A declared account is `{id, name}` with an id that is *"stable across every revision of the list"* — **a declaration-local id, not a resolved entity** — so nothing connects a declared row to a score, a brief or an account page. **Producing that correspondence is account matching**, which is [443](architecture/443-account-matching-capability.md) and another module's.

### What TASK-440 did instead, so nothing is silently wrong meanwhile

**The subtitle names the set**: *"Every company Signora is tracking for you. A company you have named appears here once Signora has found enough to start following it."* **A test asserts the screen never claims otherwise**, because a subtitle promising the declaration is a sentence a customer cannot check.

⚡ **The related capability already exists and is not consumed**: [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md)'s A7 slice built `GET /target-account-coverage`, which answers *did Signora look at this declared subject, and did it store anything* — **precisely the question a declared-but-untracked company raises.** **Whether Companies should show declared rows with their coverage beside tracked ones is a product decision**, and it is the one being asked here.

## C-231 · The organization history is paged, and its fetch is not yet bounded

**Opened 2026-08-06 · Lane A · owner: Lane A · 🟡 · raised by this lane against its own slice**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, delivering [TASK-443](BACKLOG.md), **before the slice was committed** |
| **Owner** | **Lane A.** `workspace_tenancy` is this lane's; nothing is being asked of anybody |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — recorded so a half-fix is not read as a whole one |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing.** The API contract is correct and bounded; the query cost is not |

### What shipped, and what did not

**`GET /workspaces/{id}/history` is now cursor-paginated** — §7's requirement, and the row's deliverable. **The response is bounded.** ⚠️ **The fetch behind it is not**: the page is taken over the full read, so the query still assembles every entry a workspace has ever produced and then returns fifty of them.

> **Said plainly rather than implied.** It fixes the contract and half the problem, and the docstring in `query_service.py` says so in the same words.

### Why the remaining half is not one more line

**An entry is derived, not stored.** One membership row yields a `joined` and possibly a `removed`, at two different timestamps; one invitation yields up to three. **So *"the newest fifty rows"* is a question no single table can answer**, and `LIMIT 50` on any one of the three sources is wrong.

**The correct shape is six bounded queries, one per kind**, each ordered on its own timestamp and taking `limit + 1`, merged — because the newest `limit + 1` of every kind must contain the newest `limit` overall.

⛔ **Not a `UNION` of the three sources**, and that refusal is older than this slice: the read model records it as *"a UNION would need every column to line up — which would make adding a field to one of them a change to all three."* **A union of three narrow projections `(occurred_at, source_id, kind)` would sidestep that**, at the cost of a second hydration pass — which is the design worth weighing when this is taken up.

### Why it was not done here

**The row's deliverable is *"one workspace-scoped, cursor-paginated history read"*, and that is delivered.** Six queries and a hydration pass is a different slice with a different risk profile, and bundling it would have made a bounded, testable change into an unbounded one.

⚡ **And the urgency is genuinely low**: the sources are memberships, invitations and role changes — **a workspace's people**, not its pipeline. A thousand-entry history is a large organisation over a long time, not a busy afternoon.

### One thing this slice found and fixed on the way

⚠️ **The endpoint had no test of any kind.** It has existed since Team Management, and **its response shape was changed from a bare list to a paged envelope without a single assertion noticing.** **`test_api_organization_history.py` now covers it** — what it records, ordering, the cursor walking without repeating or dropping, who may read it, and that one organisation never appears in another's. **A read nobody tests is a read whose contract is whatever the last edit left behind.**

## C-229 · Opportunity Intelligence needs a door, and D38 closed that one deliberately

**Opened 2026-08-06 · Lane A · owner: the product owner · 🟡**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, holding [TASK-441](BACKLOG.md), after the reuse audit and before writing a line |
| **Owner** | **The product owner.** ⛔ **Not Lane C** — [D38](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) is a ratified product decision about information architecture, and the row that removed *Opportunities* says in its own words that **adding one back is a claim that needs defending** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — 2026-08-07, [D-141](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ①.** ⛔ **Not a ruling: the finalized design already contains the answer, and this item should not have remained open once the design became readable.** |
| **Blocks** | **The *entrance* of the three screens [D38](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) removed by name, and nothing else.** ⚠️ **Not the screens** — see *what this is not* below |
| ⚡ **Evidence, 2026-08-06 — and it is now a failing gate rather than a question** | **[TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) built Companies at `/accounts`, complete and green on every other gate, and `make reachability` fails on it:** *"**NO ENTRANCE — built, and no screen leads here: `/accounts`**"* · *"every one is a defect"*. ⛔ **So the entrance is not a finishing touch that can follow the screen — the repository refuses to certify a screen without one.** ⚡ **This is exactly what [D-127](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ asked for**: *"bring the recommendation back once implementation and journey validation supply the evidence."* **Implementation is done and both journeys pass against the real product** — a seller narrows to their own book, searches a company by name and opens it. **What is missing is one ruling.** ⛔ **This lane did not declare the route in `ENTERED_FROM_OUTSIDE`**: nothing outside the product sends a customer to `/accounts`, so the declaration would be false and would make the guard unable to fail |
| ⚡ **Lane A's recommendation, offered as input and never as authority** | **Give the three screens an entrance *from the surface that already answers the neighbouring question*, and add no navigation entry.** For Companies: **one link at the foot of the attention list** — *see every company Signora is tracking* — which satisfies the gate, keeps [D38](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md)'s two-entry navigation intact, and puts the door where the question is actually asked. ⛔ **Not implemented.** D38's own words are *"adding one back is a claim that needs defending"*, and **a lane that hangs the door has answered the question by shipping a link**, which is what this item exists to prevent |

### The question, in one sentence

> ## **Does [410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md)'s Opportunity Intelligence get a navigation entry, reversing [D38](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) — or does it reach the customer some other way?**

### D38 removed this exact entry, from first principles, and named the reason

**`components/shell/navigation.tsx`, verbatim:**

> *"It was six: Overview, Companies, Signals, Timeline, **Opportunities**, Settings — four of the thirteen pipeline modules with a menu item each, **which is a data model rendered as navigation**… **None of the six customer journeys is *show me all the signals* or *show me all the companies*.**"*

> *"`Attention` rather than `Opportunities` because ***Opportunity* is Signora's own word for the workflow object a human commits to**, and most rows on this list are not that yet."*

> ⚠️ ***"D38 reduced this to two on purpose, so adding one back is a claim that needs defending."***

**The sidebar is three entries and the third had to earn it** — *Your business*, on a measured fact: a `member` was seeing a navigation of one. **This item is the fourth entry asking the same question**, and this lane will not answer it by shipping a link.

### What the screen would add, stated fairly rather than argued away

**Measured, not recalled** — every one of TASK-441's four deliverables already renders, and here is where:

| Element | Renders today |
|---|---|
| **Contributions** — *why this number* | `ContributionList` · `ScoreArithmetic` — **Account 360** |
| **Score and its expiry** | `AttentionScore` + `EvidenceHealth` — **the homepage list *and* Account 360** |
| **Stage and its history** | `OpportunityMomentum` · `AccountHistory` — **Account 360** |
| **Competitors** | `CompetitorContext` — **Account 360** |

> ⚡ **But that does not make the screen redundant, and this lane will not claim it does.** The existing surfaces answer **"this account"** and **"who do I call today"** *(attention, score-ranked)*. **Opportunity Intelligence asks a third question nothing answers: *where does everything stand*** — pursuits grouped by stage, across the workspace. **That is genuinely new**, and it is why the row is worth building.
>
> **What is not new is the components.** They are reused whole; nothing here proposes a second `ContributionList`.

### Three ways it could reach a customer

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A — a fourth navigation entry** | Reverses D38 for this screen | **The product owner's, explicitly.** ⚠️ **And D38's argument still partly holds**: *Opportunity* is the committed-workflow word, and this list would include rows that are not that yet |
| ✅ **B — a view of the surface that already exists** | **Recommended.** The homepage list is *already* this data, ranked by attention. **Add a stage-grouped view of it**, reached from the list's own header, travelling in the URL beside `owner` | **No new entry, no D38 reversal, no second copy of the list.** ⚡ **The precedent is on the page already**: `owner=all\|mine\|unassigned` is a scope that travels in the URL, and `triage.tsx` filters the same list without re-ranking it |
| **C — per-account only** | Drop the workspace-level view; the four elements are already on Account 360 | ⛔ **This is the one that makes the row redundant**, and it answers none of the third question |

### Why B is recommended

**It delivers what the screen is *for* without spending the decision D38 protected.** *Where does everything stand* is a **way of reading the attention list**, not a second list — and the repository already treats scope-and-grouping as URL state over one ranked set rather than as separate pages. **A seller gets the cockpit; the sidebar stays three entries; nothing is duplicated.**

⚠️ **And it is honest about what it is not**: 410 names Opportunity Intelligence as its own screen, so **B delivers the capability and not the screen as drawn.** That is the trade-off, and it is the product owner's to accept or refuse.

### What this is not

⛔ **Not a refusal, and not a second blocked row.** **[TASK-441](BACKLOG.md) stays `CLAIMED` and this lane is holding it.** The reads are verified and shipped, the components exist, the stage vocabulary exists in `opportunity.tsx` and will be reused rather than restated (§4). **Under B this lane can start immediately; under A it can start as soon as the entry is approved.**

⛔ **And not a complaint about the audit.** [453](architecture/453-opportunity-intelligence-traceability-audit.md) traced the screen to its *domain* and did that well — every element it marked ✅ genuinely is built. **It did not ask how a seller arrives**, which is the same shape as [C-228](#c-228--the-signal-center-has-no-workspace-wide-queue-to-render-and-no-way-to-leave-it): **a traceability audit checks that the facts exist and not that a customer can reach them.** ⚡ **Two screens, two audits, two different missing halves — and both halves are *reachability*.**

### Implementation impact

**None yet. Nothing has been written.** No route, no component, no navigation edit, no test. **The audit ran first, which is what found this.**
