## C-228 · The Signal Center has no workspace-wide queue to render, and no way to leave it

> ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06.** **[TASK-439](BACKLOG.md)'s Change Budget is widened to 🟠 and now covers the workspace-wide triage read, the resolve route and `Resource.SIGNAL`.** ⚠️ **This item was `READY FOR LANE C` and waited while Lane A could not act on the row it holds — the delay is this office's, not the finding's.**


**Opened 2026-08-06 · Lane A · owner: Lane C — [TASK-439](BACKLOG.md)'s scope and Change Budget are Product Office's · 🟠**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, on claiming [TASK-439](BACKLOG.md) and running the reuse audit **before writing a line** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C.** ⛔ **Not a defect and not a ruling** — the row says what to do with it in its own words: *"if a section turns out to need one, that is a finding to raise, not a change to make"* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-124](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **The answer is recorded above; the requesting lane closes** |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-439](BACKLOG.md) whole.** Not partially: without a workspace-wide read there is no list, and without a write surface nothing leaves it |

### The row's sequencing line does not survive checking, and neither does the audit's scope

**[TASK-439](BACKLOG.md) says: *"After [TASK-405](BACKLOG.md) promotes (it adds `Resource.SIGNAL`, and a write surface without it is unauthorized)."*** **TASK-405 promoted, and it did not add it** — measured against `origin/main` rather than inferred from a row:

```bash
git show origin/main:backend/signora_platform/authorization/enforcer.py | grep -c SIGNAL
→ 0
git show origin/main:backend/signora_platform/authorization/policies/policy.csv | grep -ci signal
→ 0
git show origin/main:backend/modules/signal_engine/interface/router.py | grep -c '@router.post\|@router.put'
→ 0
```

**TASK-405 withheld the route deliberately and said so**, in its own row and in [25-signal-engine.md](architecture/25-signal-engine.md): the `Resource` was 🔴 at the time and [C-224](#c-224--a-new-write-surface-needs-an-authorization-resource-and-two-governance-rules-disagree-about-who-may-add-one) was unruled. **C-224 is now `RULED` and nobody has built it since.** ⚠️ **[447 §Permissions](architecture/447-signal-center-traceability-audit.md) agrees with this lane and not with the backlog row** — it assigns `Resource.SIGNAL` to **[R-13](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md)**, never to TASK-405. **Two documents name two different owners for one missing member.**

### And the larger gap is one neither document looked for

**447 traced ten elements — domain, events, permissions, projections — and every one of them is about *what a decision is*.** **None asks whether the queue can be listed.**

```bash
grep -n "async def queue" -A 3 backend/modules/signal_engine/application/triage.py
→     async def queue(
→         self,
→         workspace_id: UUID,
→         entity_id: UUID,          ← required, not optional
```

> ## **`TriageQueries.queue` answers *"what is outstanding on this account"*. The Signal Center asks *"what is outstanding"*.**
>
> **There is no workspace-wide read at any layer** — not the repository (`for_entity`), not the application layer, not a route. The four shipped `GET`s are per account, per signal, or the catalog.

**So the approved screen — *"a triage queue, not a notification list"* — has no list to render.** A seller cannot open the Signal Center and see what is waiting, because nothing can answer that question for a workspace.

### This is [B-327](BUGS.md)'s class, third instance in three days

| | |
|---|---|
| **[C-332](#c-332--the-predicate-landed-and-task-406-still-cannot-call-it--nothing-builds-its-input-and-the-module-that-measures-may-not-reach-one)** | `evaluate(icp, observed)` is promoted and correct, and **nothing constructs an `ObservedAttributes`** |
| **[C-417](#c-417--adr-0404-approved-three-platform-capabilities-whose-owner-may-not-finish-two-of-them)** | A contract approved whose owner may not finish two of its capabilities |
| **C-228 — this one** | **Four outcome types, a `Resolution` aggregate, a queue predicate and an event, all built and all correct — and no way for a customer to reach any of them** |

**[D-093](DECISION_REGISTER.md) named the fix the same week and it was not applied here**: *"every Context Definition now carries one more line: who constructs each input, and may they reach it."* **A traceability audit is where that line belongs too.** 447 counted a domain element as ✅ because it exists in `domain/`; **existing and being reachable are different facts**, which is exactly what B-327 corrected four documents ago.

### What would resolve it — three, and the recommendation is the first

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ **A — widen TASK-439's budget to include what it needs** | **The two endpoints and the `Resource` registration.** A workspace-wide `queue`, the resolve route, `Resource.SIGNAL` plus its `policy.csv` rows | **Recommended.** ⚡ **Both modules are already Lane A's and the row says so**, so nothing crosses a lane. **C-224 ruled the enum member is a *declaration* a lane may perform**, and the grants go in the any-lane registry. **The work is ordinary**: one repository query without an `entity_id` filter, one route beside four that already exist, and one use case that is already written and already tested |
| **B — sequence it as its own row first** | A row for the write surface and the workspace read; TASK-439 then becomes a true render | **Honest, and slower.** It splits one screen across two claims for a boundary that is bookkeeping rather than architecture |
| ⛔ **C — narrow TASK-439 to what is reachable today** | A per-account triage panel on the account brief | **Refused, and named so it is not chosen by accident.** That is not the approved screen — it answers *"what is outstanding here"* and the Signal Center's whole premise is the queue across the workspace |

### The trade-off, stated rather than buried

**A changes the row from 🟢 to 🟠**, and a Change Budget is Product Office's to set. **This lane will not widen its own budget**, which is the whole reason this item exists rather than a commit — *"if a section turns out to need one, that is a finding to raise, not a change to make"*, in the row's own words.

### Implementation impact

**No code, no schema, no contract.** **Nothing has been written for TASK-439** — the audit ran first, which is what found this. **The task stays `CLAIMED` by Lane A and is not started**; it does not return to `READY`, because the work is real and this lane is holding it pending a scope answer.

⚠️ **And Lane A is otherwise idle from here.** [TASK-432](BACKLOG.md) is `IN VALIDATION` and [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md) promoted this cycle. The queue's `future` names [TASK-441](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) — **this lane will take the next eligible row rather than wait**, and says so here so an idle-looking lane is not mistaken for a blocked one.

## C-227 · `/join/{workspace_id}` has no in-product entrance by design, and the declaration is QE's

> ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-05, having raised it.** **The premise in this item's own title was wrong, and QE said so.**
>
> **[B-123](BUGS.md), QE, 2026-08-05:** *"Whether the route needs an exemption or the check needs widening is **the implementing lane's call**. QE will not decide which."*
>
> **Lane A argued the declaration was QE's on the strength of one comment** — *"a judgement, maintained by QE"* — and that reading was too literal. **The comment governs the standard the list is held to, not who may write a line in it**, and its actual warning is the opposite of how this lane used it: *"a list that grows without argument is how a check stops meaning anything."* **The argument was already written, in this item, four polls ago.** What was missing was not QE's judgement; it was this lane acting on its own.
>
> **The overrule is right, and the general form is worth keeping**: **the lane that knows why a route has no entrance is the lane that built it.** A second lane can only re-derive that reason or take it on trust, and both are worse than the author stating it.
>
> **Declared, not widened** — `/join/[workspaceId]` joins `/verify-email` and `/reset-password`, which are the same class and sit directly above it. **Widening the check would have weakened the guard to fit one route**, on a check that earned its keep by catching the Connection Center.
>
> **Cost of the delay: four polls, and a red test QE had to find by hand** because [B-123](BUGS.md) shows no gate runs the frontend suite. **This lane's finding against itself.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-05, building [TASK-904](BACKLOG.md)'s acceptance page |
| **Owner** | ~~QE~~ → **Lane A.** [`infra/reachability.py`](../infra/reachability.py) says *"a judgement, maintained by QE"*, and **this lane read that as *written* by QE, which it does not say** |
| **Status** | **`CLOSED`** — 2026-08-05. **Lane A declared the route**, on QE's explicit delegation. `reachability.test.tsx` is green |
| **Blocks** | Certification of the branch, and nothing else |

### What is asked

One entry in `ENTERED_FROM_OUTSIDE`:

```python
    "/join/*": "reached from the invitation link, by design",
```

### Why the route has no entrance, and must not be given one

**Nobody navigates to *"join an organization"* from inside the product.** The page is reached from the link `ConsoleInvitationDelivery` sends, exactly as `/verify-email` and `/reset-password` are reached from their emails — the two entries directly above where this one belongs.

**And an in-product entrance is not available even in principle.** It would have to list the invitations addressed to the reader, across workspaces they are not in — the cross-workspace inbox [C-208](#c-208--a-tenant-scoped-row-whose-only-legitimate-reader-is-outside-the-tenant) refused, and the one screen in Signora that would read outside a tenant.

### Why Lane A did not add the line

**The list's own comment says it is QE's judgement**, and every entry is *"a claim that something outside the product sends a customer here."* Asserting that claim on QE's behalf is the thing the comment exists to prevent — *"a list that grows without argument is how a check stops meaning anything."*

The argument is above. **The check is working**: it caught a genuinely unreachable route within a minute of the route existing, which is what it is for.

## C-417 · ADR-0404 approved three platform capabilities whose owner may not finish two of them

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md). Option A, bounded.** **The slice may delete only the five `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments the capability requires** — ⛔ **no functional change, no architectural change, no opportunistic cleanup, no unrelated edit.** *"This exception exists solely to unblock ADR-0404."* **Releases [TASK-418](BACKLOG.md) ① and ②, and [TASK-901](BACKLOG.md)'s dependent slices**


**Opened 2026-08-05 · Lane C · current module assignee: Lane C (`signora_platform/`) · 🔴**

> **Found by running [ADR-0404](architecture/adr/0404-platform-composition.md) §Validation before the first slice, which is what that section exists for.** **The ADR is Lane C's own** — [435](architecture/435-platform-composition-rfc.md) became it — **so this is this office's error surfacing at the moment the ADR designed to catch it.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, claiming [TASK-418](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it is a Change Budget question, and the Change Budget is theirs |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-418](BACKLOG.md) capabilities ① and ②.** **④ is unaffected and ships now** |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED — Lane C, 2026-08-11, on the PO-queue triage.** ⚡ **It blocks [TASK-418](BACKLOG.md) capabilities ① and ②, and TASK-418 is `IN VALIDATION`** — ⛔ **the work it was holding has been built and handed to QE.** ✅ **A blocker whose target has shipped is a closed item, not an open decision.** *(Was:✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-111](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this field was not.** **Twelve items carried the same defect**, and every one would have been escalated as an open question. |)* |

### The problem, in one line

> **The platform edit is Lane C's. The proof that it worked is inside five files in `backend/modules/`, and `CLAUDE.md` §20e forbids Lane C from touching that tree — ⚫ *refactor a module you are not assigned*.**

### Why the two halves cannot be separated

**`[tool.mypy] strict = true`, which implies `warn_unused_ignores`.**

**Capability ② makes `PublishableEvent`'s six members read-only properties.** The moment it lands, the five `# type: ignore[arg-type]` at the publish sites become **unused**, and **`mypy --strict` fails the gate.** **So the platform change and the five one-line deletions are one atomic change, whether or not anybody wants them to be.**

**Capability ① has the same shape**: `EventHandler` is `Callable[[EventEnvelope], Awaitable[None]]` in `signora_platform/event_bus/subscriptions.py`, and **the two implementations are `modules/provider_platform/interface/handlers.py` and `modules/ai_research_engine/interface/handlers.py`.** Changing the alias breaks both in the same commit.

### ⚠️ Two corrections to ADR-0404, found by the same validation

| | |
|---|---|
| **The count is wrong** | **The ADR says *"all eight `# type: ignore[arg-type]` at publish sites are removable."* There are **five**** — `observation_engine/application/record.py:124` · `signal_engine/application/generate.py:158` · `business_event_engine/application/detect.py:129` · `knowledge_graph/application/resolve.py:329` · `knowledge_graph/application/relationships.py:240`. **The other three are `provider_normalization` (×2) and `ai_research_engine`, and none is at a publish site** |
| **The ownership question was never asked** | **§Validation ③ checks that `apps/worker/` has an owner. It does not check that the *modules* the change reaches have one** — and that is the check that would have caught this at ratification rather than at implementation |

### What the modules already said

**`observation_engine/application/record.py:120`, in the code, before this item existed:**

> *"the platform's `PublishableEvent` Protocol declares settable members, which frozen domain events cannot satisfy. **Raised as a finding, not fixed here.**"*

**Three modules carry that comment.** **They raised it correctly and declined to cross the boundary, which is the rule working.** **ADR-0404 is the fix they were waiting for, and it cannot land without re-crossing the boundary they refused to cross.**

### Alternatives

| | | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **A bounded, named exception.** Lane C's slice deletes **exactly those five `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments and nothing else** — no logic, no behaviour, no signature, announced in the commit message and reviewed by QE like any other slice | **Smallest possible change, and it is still a rule bent.** A comment deletion is not a refactor, but the rule says *"a lane never changes a module it is not assigned"* without qualification |
| **B** | **A coordinated three-lane slice.** Lane C changes the platform; Lane A and Lane B each remove their own module's ignores in the same integration window | **Purest, and it needs three lanes to land inside one gate run.** §20e's *one slice under construction* and the `--ff-only` model both make this expensive |
| **C** | **Move capability ② out of TASK-418** and let each module lane adopt the read-only Protocol when it next touches its own publish site | **Zero rule bent, and the capability arrives never** — the modules have carried that comment for weeks precisely because no slice makes them touch it |
| **D** | **Leave the ignores in place** and land the Protocol change alone | ⛔ **Not available.** `warn_unused_ignores` fails the gate. Recorded so nobody re-proposes it |

### Recommendation

> ✅ **A, bounded in writing.** **The change is five deleted comment lines**, it is provably behaviour-free, and **the alternative that bends no rule (C) delivers the capability never.**
>
> **The bound that makes it safe is that it is checkable**: *the slice may delete `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments at publish sites and may change no other line in `backend/modules/`* — **a reviewer can verify that from the diff alone**, which is the standard §20a's carve-out already uses for a `Resource` member.

### Implementation impact

**Capability ④ — `Action.LEAVE` and two policy lines — is entirely inside `signora_platform/authorization/` and is unaffected. Lane C ships it now.** **Capabilities ① and ② wait on this ruling**, and **[TASK-901](BACKLOG.md)'s seven slices wait on them.**

## C-418 · Does Signora forecast revenue? The Executive Dashboard says yes and a ratified principle says no

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). Option B.** ***"Current Signora reports pipeline health. It does not forecast revenue."*** **Revenue forecasting becomes future scope behind Epic E1.** ⛔ *"Do not promise predictive capability before the underlying inputs exist."*


**Opened 2026-08-05 · Lane C · current module assignee: `opportunity_engine` (Lane B) · `buying_score_engine` (Lane A) · 🔴**

> **Found by [444](architecture/444-executive-dashboard-domain-assessment.md), assessing one approved screen to its domain.** **Not by implementation reaching it** — which is the point of the method.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, Product-Led Domain Discovery |
| **Owner** | **The product owner.** It is a product decision with a ratified engineering principle on one side of it |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing today.** **[TASK-438](BACKLOG.md) delivers five of the screen's sections without it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, the requesting lane.** ⚡ **Ruled by the product owner on 2026-08-06 ([D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) and blocking nothing since.** ✅ **The question — does Signora forecast revenue — was answered; leaving it open advertised a decision nobody was waiting for** *(was: ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this fiel)* |

### The conflict, in two quotations

> **[410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md) describes the screen as *"CEO/CRO homepage — **forecast**, risk, ageing, movements."***
>
> **`buying_score_engine/domain/events.py`: *"**No probability, no likelihood, no prediction.** A buying score prioritizes commercial attention; **it does not forecast a purchase**."*** **`domain/score.py` repeats it: *"They do not estimate probability."***

**The approved UI's first word contradicts a ratified principle, in the module a forecast would naturally come from, and nothing in the repository says which wins.**

### Four absences, and they are one question

| | Measured across every `domain/` layer |
|---|---|
| **A deal has no value** | `Opportunity` carries eleven fields and **no amount, no currency, no expected close date** |
| **There is no plan** | **`quota`, `target_amount`, `forecast` return nothing.** *"Projection against a plan"* needs a plan |
| **There is no period** | **`fiscal` returns zero.** A quarter is a workspace declaration and nothing declares one |
| **There is no team** | **No `Team`, no `manager_id`, no `reports_to`.** [MC-6](PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md) said it first: *"the buyer is a CRO and there is no screen addressed to one"* |

> **Answer the question and all four follow, or none do.** **That is why this is one item and not four**, and why answering it early is cheap.

### The two answers, and what each commits to

| | | Consequences |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Yes — Signora forecasts** | **A deal needs a value and a close date; a workspace needs a fiscal calendar; somebody needs a plan; and the probability principle must be amended or the model must live somewhere that is not `buying_score_engine`.** ⚠️ **And the value must come from the customer's CRM, not a text box** — [ADR-0036](architecture/adr/0036-target-account-contract.md)'s standard: *"asking them… would be asking a customer to do resolution, and resolution quality is Signora's competence, not theirs."* **A number typed into Signora is a second copy of one that already exists, and the two will disagree.** **So A sequences behind Epic E1** ([TASK-402](BACKLOG.md), `IN VALIDATION`) — **a forecast built before E1 lands is a forecast over numbers nobody entered** |
| **B** | **No — it reports pipeline health** | **Nothing is built and nothing is renamed except the screen's own description.** **Conversion, ageing, movement, roll-up and ICP coverage are all buildable today** and are what a CRO actually acts on. **The ratified principle stands untouched** |

### Recommendation

> ✅ **B for now, and A only behind Epic E1 — stated as a sequence rather than as a refusal.**
>
> **The evidence is that five of the screen's sections are buildable today and none of them is a forecast.** **[417](architecture/417-executable-slice-audit.md) reached the same split independently** — *"coverage, conversion, ageing and movement are arithmetic over stages and dates; **the AI projection is BLOCKED BY PRODUCT**."*
>
> **A forecast is the one thing on this screen that Signora would be worse at than the CRM the customer already owns**, until E1 gives it the numbers. **Building it first inverts that.**

### The consequence nobody has hit yet

**Every authorization grant today is workspace-wide — `p, member, *, opportunity, read`.** **A roll-up by owner is, by construction, everybody's performance on one page**, and **this is the first approved screen whose data is sensitive *between colleagues* rather than between tenants.** **No `Resource` exists for a plan, a target or a forecast.**

**Recorded rather than proposed** — it becomes real only on answer **A**. **Coverage and ageing are facts about accounts, not about people.**

## C-419 · The six verbs have no representation, and *17 surfaces, one contract* is undecided

> ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **The six verbs belong to `ai_reasoning_engine`** — *"the engine owns the language. Screens consume that language."* ⛔ **Do not duplicate the taxonomy in frontend code.** **Published through the engine's `public/`.** **[TASK-453](BACKLOG.md) implements it.**


**Opened 2026-08-05 · Lane C · current module assignee: `ai_reasoning_engine` (Lane B) · 🟠**

> **Found by [445](architecture/445-ai-copilot-traceability-audit.md), the first Screen-by-Screen Domain Traceability Audit ([D-078](DECISION_REGISTER.md)).** **AI Copilot is wave 2 — the next screen implementation reaches.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, auditing the screen before implementation reached it |
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it decides a module's published language and a platform boundary |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing today.** [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md) is blocked on [C-222](#c-222--reasoning1-earns-a-release-under-protocol-2-on-a-model-this-workstation-cannot-measure-in-time) for unrelated reasons |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, the requesting lane.** ⚡ **Ruled by the product owner on 2026-08-06 ([D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md)).** ⛔ **Its own `Blocks` field has read *nothing today* since then** *(was: ✅ **`RULED`** — product owner, 2026-08-06, [D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md). ⚡ **Field re-synced 2026-08-06 — the ruling above was recorded and this fiel)* |

### Two halves, and the second cannot be answered without the first

**[410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md) asserts *"**six verbs and no others** — Explain · Summarize · Predict · Recommend · Generate · Reason"* and *"17 surfaces, one contract."***

| | |
|---|---|
| **① The verbs have no representation** | ⛔ **No verb, intent or capability taxonomy exists in any `domain/` layer.** **Six named values the design calls closed, and nothing closes them** |
| **② One route or seventeen** | **The contract is five guarantees** — inherits scope, cites what it read, states confidence with its basis, proposes rather than commits, is attributable and reversible. **Seventeen endpoints is seventeen chances for one of them to differ, and no way to check that it did not** |

### ✅ What already argues for one side

**The guarantees are *already* one implementation.** `GroundedOutput`, `EvidenceRef`, `SupportBasis` and the never-repairing validator are single and shared. **The contract is a platform capability in substance today** — what is undecided is whether the *surface* is a parameter of one route or a convention across seventeen.

### Recommendation

> ✅ **The verb taxonomy and the surface identifier belong to `ai_reasoning_engine`'s `public/`, and the 17 surfaces are consumers rather than variants.**
>
> **The reason is §6's rule, not preference:** *"a port belongs to the module that owns the language it represents."* ***Explain · Summarize · Predict · Recommend · Generate · Reason* is that module's language.** Put it in the frontend and **the closed set stops being closed the first time a screen needs a seventh.**

**Trade-off, stated:** one route with a verb parameter is **less obvious to read** than seventeen named endpoints. **The repository has already taken that trade once and recorded why** — the AI provider registry *"exposes `for_model(model)` and no vendor-keyed lookup, so business code that cannot name a vendor cannot branch on one."* **A surface that cannot name itself cannot diverge from the contract.**

### The permission finding, which is separate and cheaper

⚠️ **There is no `Resource` for reasoning.** **`Resource.RESEARCH` exists precisely because *"reading an account is free and asking for research spends a model call, and one resource could not express both without making every reader a spender."***

> **AI Copilot is 17 surfaces on pages every member already reads.** **Mounted without the same separation, it grants every member the ability to spend a model call, on every page.** **One `Resource` and two policy lines** — the [C-224](#c-224--a-new-write-surface-needs-an-authorization-resource-and-two-governance-rules-disagree-about-who-may-add-one) ruling already makes that a declarative registration a lane may perform.

| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-07, ⚡ **on trying to implement [TASK-474](BACKLOG.md) and confirming the Change Budget first, which is what found it** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *any future ownership transfer requires its own explicit decision, raised as a coordination item, ruled by the product owner*.** **This office may not assign a path to itself** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07, on [D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ①.** ⚡ **Ruled: `frontend/` is Lane A's** — *"Lane A owns the application UI composition, the Design System implementation, page composition and customer-facing experiences. Authentication journeys ultimately become customer journeys, which belong with the application layer rather than Product Office."* ✅ **Closed only after the registry was made consistent, which is what the ruling asked**: [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) grants `frontend/` to `product_surface`, and `git grep frontend` against it now returns matches where it returned nothing. ✅ **[TASK-473](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-474](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md) moved to Lane A and released to `READY`; [TASK-475](BACKLOG.md) was already Lane A's and unblocks behind TASK-474.** ⚡ **Lane C keeps planning, decomposition, readiness assessment and journey sequencing** — the ruling moved implementation, not preparation |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-473](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-474](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚠️ **widened 2026-08-07, see *The scope was measured too narrowly* below.** ⚡ **[ADR-0406 §6](architecture/adr/0406-authentication-execution-modes.md) says ten of the fourteen authentication journey gaps close behind `TASK-474` alone** |
| ⚡ **And a second lane behind it, added 2026-08-07 by Lane A** | **[TASK-475](BACKLOG.md) — Lane A, `product_surface`** — *the seventeen authentication journeys run as one suite* — **is `BLOCKED` on [TASK-474](BACKLOG.md), which is `BLOCKED` on this item.** ⛔ **So the chain is two hops and its far end is a product decision, not a queue position.** ⚠️ **Lane A's row named only its immediate predecessor, which reads as ordinary sequencing** — §20e: *an implementation blocker resumes automatically the moment the dependency is satisfied; an architectural one waits for the product owner*, and **a chain that ends in an unruled ownership question is the second kind however sequential it looks from the near end.** **Recorded here so the ruling's cost is visible as two lanes rather than one** |

### The question, at its smallest

> ## **Which lane owns `frontend/lib/auth/`?**

⛔ **That is the whole of it.** **Not how the mailbox works, not what the transport should be** — **who may write the file.**

### Measured, not assumed

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **[`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) grants Lane C** | `platform_foundation` → `infra/`, `Makefile`, `backend/signora_platform/` · `apps` → `backend/apps/` |
| ⛔ **`frontend/lib/auth/` is in neither** | **And `product_surface` — Lane A's — declares no paths at all** |
| ⛔ **No lane branch has ever touched it** | **`lane-a-product-surface` 0 commits · `lane-b-commercial-profile` 0 · `lane-qe` 0.** ⚡ **Its history is entirely pre-lane** — `M12.3`, `B-104`, the first-run work |

### ⚠️ This office wrote the row that claims it

**[TASK-474](BACKLOG.md)'s Module cell reads *"`infra/` + `frontend/lib/auth/` — Lane C"*.** ⛔ **The registry does not support the second half, and this office wrote it.** ⚡ **[C-213](#c-213--task-205-names-an-assignee-that-moved)'s class exactly: an assignee stored beside a row instead of joined from the registry** — **and the check that catches a *stale* assignee does not catch an *invented* one.**

### What [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already says about this exact case

> *"When ownership is genuinely unclear, leave it unassigned and mark it **review at first implementation**. **Ownership becomes obvious when implementation reaches a module**; predicting it earlier buys nothing and can be wrong."*

⚡ **Implementation reached it today.** **The three candidates, stated without a recommendation this office is not entitled to make:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lane A** | ⚡ **It owns `product_surface` and every screen that signs a customer in.** ⛔ **But it has never touched this directory, and it is the busiest lane** |
| **Lane C** | ⚡ **The row is Platform Foundation work and the rest of it is `infra/`.** ⛔ **But `frontend/` is named in §20e as what this lane *does not* build**, and taking it would widen the office that is meant to prepare rather than implement |
| ⚪ **Split** | **The mailbox lives in `infra/`; the transport member is one line in `frontend/lib/auth/config.ts`.** ⚠️ **A two-lane slice for one line is the coordination cost §20e warns about** |

⛔ **No recommendation offered on purpose.** ⚡ **[D-139](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *bring me only the decision, not the investigation* — and the decision here is one word, while a recommendation from the lane that would benefit is not worth much.**

### ⚠️ The scope was measured too narrowly — amended 2026-08-07, Lane C

> ## **It is not `frontend/lib/auth/`. `git grep frontend docs/coordination/modules.toml` returns nothing at all.**

⛔ **No module in the registry declares a single `frontend/` path.** **`platform_foundation` is `["infra/", "Makefile", "backend/signora_platform/"]`; `apps` is `["backend/apps/"]`; `product_surface` declares no `paths` key.** ⚡ **The entire frontend is unattributable by machine** — **the original row measured one directory and reported one directory, and the same query run against the whole tree answers the same way everywhere.**

⚠️ **This was found the way the first half was: by trying to implement and confirming the budget.** ⛔ **Lane C wrote production code into `frontend/lib/auth/config.ts` and `frontend/lib/auth/health.ts` for [TASK-473](BACKLOG.md) before reading this register, and reverted it on reading this row.** ⚡ **Recorded rather than quietly dropped** — **the office that raised C-430 then walked into it, which is evidence about how visible the row is, not only about the ownership gap.**

**Three rows this office wrote now claim a `frontend/` path the registry does not support:**

| Row | The Module cell says | The registry says |
|---|---|---|
| **[TASK-473](BACKLOG.md)** | *"`infra/` + the frontend edge — Lane C"* | ⛔ **`frontend/lib/auth/` is in no module** |
| **[TASK-474](BACKLOG.md)** | *"`infra/` + `frontend/lib/auth/` — Lane C"* | ⛔ **as above — the original finding** |
| **[TASK-476](BACKLOG.md)** | *"`frontend/playwright.config.ts` + the `Makefile` e2e targets — Lane C"* | ⚠️ **the `Makefile` half is Lane C's; the config is in no module** |

> ⛔ **Both of Lane C's claimable rows are behind this one word.** **The queue reports `claimable = 2` — `TASK-473` as `current` and `TASK-476` as `next` — and neither is buildable.** ⚡ **That is an *architectural* blocker by §20e's test: *a dependency on a decision nobody has made is architectural however small the code would be.***

⚠️ **`TASK-476` may be the easier half and it is still not this office's to answer.** **A launcher configuration reads like *environment profiles and launchers*, which [D-022](DECISION_REGISTER.md) grants Lane C** — ⛔ **but `frontend/playwright.config.ts` is not `infra/`, and *"it reads like"* is exactly the reasoning that produced the three invented Module cells above.** ⚡ **The registry is the authority and it is silent; the fix is a ruling, not a better reading.**

⛔ **Still no recommendation, and now for a second reason:** **the answer may not be one lane.** **Product screens, the authentication tier and the test launcher are three different questions that happen to share a directory**, and this office is not entitled to decide they share an answer.

## C-429 · Four live claims have no row on the execution board, and the check that should have said so was broken in both directions

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-07, ⚡ **after repairing the check — the gaps were invisible until it worked** |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **The claiming lanes.** **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): the board row is written by the claiming lane, at once.** **Lane C may not write another lane's row** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-07 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚠️ **[B-404](BUGS.md) is what it costs when it is left** |

### The four

| Row | Claimed by | Board row under `## Current` |
|---|---|---|
| **[TASK-440](BACKLOG.md)** | **Lane A** | ⛔ absent |
| **[TASK-453](BACKLOG.md)** | **Lane B** | ⛔ absent |
| **[TASK-457](BACKLOG.md)** | **Lane B** | ⛔ absent |
| **[TASK-462](BACKLOG.md)** | **Lane B** | ⛔ absent |

✅ **[TASK-478](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-450](BACKLOG.md) are *not* on this list** — **Lane A wrote board rows for both**, so this is four older gaps rather than a lane ignoring the rule.

### ⛔ Why nobody saw it: the check was wrong in both directions at once

**`_backlog_claims` searched for the lane as `**Lane A**`, a standalone bold span.** ⚡ **Every row actually writes `**\`CLAIMED\` — Lane A**` — the lane sits *inside* the same bold span as the state.**

> ## **So it matched no correctly formatted claim at all, and the only finding it ever produced was a false one.**

⚠️ **That false positive was [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md)**, `IN VALIDATION` since 2026-08-06 with **34 commits on `main` and nothing outstanding** — **whose narrative happens to contain a standalone `**Lane A**`.** ⛔ **It was reported every cycle for days and routed to Lane A each time, against a row nobody could claim.**

**A second defect in the same function**: it substring-matched *any* state token in the cell, and **a backlog row narrates its own history there** — *"Previously **`CHANGES REQUESTED`** — …"*. ⚡ **[B-101](BUGS.md)'s class, and the same defect [`registers.py`](../infra/registers.py) exists to fix on the bug side.**

### ⚠️ And the repair went wrong before it went right

**The first attempt delegated to `_backlog_states` and reported *nothing at all***, missing all six live claims. ⛔ **Over-reporting became a guard that cannot fail, which is strictly worse**, and it was caught only by testing against real rows rather than synthetic ones. **The synthetic cases passed while the repository's own formatting did not.**

✅ **Now verified in both directions against the live backlog**: six claims found — [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-450](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-453](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-457](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-462](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-478](BACKLOG.md) — **and [TASK-400](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-419](BACKLOG.md) correctly absent.**

## C-428 · Releasing a row deleted the evidence that the release was wrong

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | ⚡ **Lane A**, 2026-08-07 — *"[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) still lands as `READY` against an empty `public/` when that branch finally certifies"* |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Lane C.** **This office released the row, on reasoning it had already condemned in [C-427](#c-427--a-sequenced-row-is-never-re-asked-and-that-is-why-two-lanes-were-idle-with-93-tasks-on-the-board)** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07.** **Row corrected, predicate corrected, and the gap that hid it now has a check** |
| ✅ **RE-CHECKED 2026-08-10 — the standing advisory is clear, and this records that so nobody re-investigates** | ⚠️ **`state-check` has reported *one module publishes an empty `public/` contract on `integration` — timeline* on every run this cycle.** ✅ **Investigated: NOTHING is exposed.** 📁 **`git cat-file -s origin/integration:backend/modules/timeline/public/__init__.py` = 0 bytes, confirmed.** ⛔ **But no module imports `timeline.public`, and NO row is `READY` against it.** **The three rows that name timeline are all `SEQUENCED` on unrelated triggers** — [TASK-435](BACKLOG.md) on SW-02's scheduling, [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md) after [TASK-1448](BACKLOG.md) under [D-219](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6, [TASK-1415](BACKLOG.md) behind two unbuilt rows. ⚡ **So this is the check doing its job PREVENTIVELY rather than a repeat of the `people` instance**: the advisory is a standing risk report, and the risk has not been realised. ⛔ **The moment a row is released against it, the same check will say so — which is why it stays noisy rather than being silenced**
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **It would have blocked Lane A on its first claim after integration** |

### What Lane A did that no instrument did

> ## **It opened the file.** **`backend/modules/people/public/__init__.py` on `integration` is zero lines.**

⛔ **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) consumes what `people` publishes, and `people` publishes nothing.** ⚡ **[TASK-457](BACKLOG.md) reads `CLAIMED` — Lane B is holding it, not finished with it.**

### How this office released it

⛔ **On *"6 commits on `main`, nothing outstanding"*** — **a count of commits that *mention* an identifier.** ⚠️ **[C-427](#c-427--a-sequenced-row-is-never-re-asked-and-that-is-why-two-lanes-were-idle-with-93-tasks-on-the-board) records that exact reasoning as [B-101](BUGS.md)'s class and says so in its own last paragraph.** ⚡ **The predicate was corrected in the same commit that made the manual releases — and the releases were never re-checked against it.**

### ⚡ The structural defect, which is worse than the row

> ## **Rewriting `SEQUENCED — predecessor [TASK-457]` into `READY` deleted the only record of what the row was waiting for.**

⛔ **`depends_on` became empty, so `stale_sequencing` could not see it** — that check reads rows still `SEQUENCED`, **and a row released in error leaves its scope at the moment the error is made.** ⚡ **The act of releasing a row destroyed the evidence that the release was wrong.**

### Three fixes, and the second one is the general lesson

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **The row** | **[TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) is `SEQUENCED` again**, carrying what was measured rather than what was assumed |
| ✅ **A release keeps its edge** | **`released from `SEQUENCED` after [TASK-nnn]`** is now parsed, so `depends_on` survives the release. ⚡ **A planning edit must never remove the thing that makes it checkable** |
| ✅ **`premature_releases()`** | **The mirror of `stale_sequencing`** — rows this office set `READY` behind a predecessor that is *not* handed over. ⛔ **Proven to fire on `TASK-458`'s exact shape and stay silent on `TASK-444`'s**, because a guard that always fires is as useless as one that cannot |

### ⚠️ And a second defect found while checking

**`_delivered`'s branch test was lane-scoped**: *"that lane's branch carries nothing `integration` lacks."* ⛔ **So a lane starting any new work made every finished row it owned read as undelivered.** **[TASK-427](BACKLOG.md) flipped to *not delivered* because Lane B pushed [TASK-462](BACKLOG.md), which has nothing to do with it** — and [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md) would have been reverted for no reason. ✅ **Now row-scoped.**

⚡ **That fix is a `--grep`, deliberately.** **[B-101](BUGS.md) bites when a grep is asked *"was this delivered?"* — it matches every mention.** **Asked *"is there outstanding work for this?"* a spurious match reads as *not delivered*, which is the safe direction.** ⛔ **The same tool; the safety is entirely in which way a false match falls.**

## C-427 · A `SEQUENCED` row is never re-asked, and that is why two lanes were idle with 93 tasks on the board

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | ⚡ **The product owner**, 2026-08-07 — *"they are still sitting idle when we have so many tasks to complete… we can't afford to lose velocity just because of lack of coordination"* |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Lane C.** **Every row named below was written by this office and released by this office. No lane could have moved one** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07.** **Seven rows released, one decomposed, and the predicate that would have caught it now runs every cycle** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing now.** ⚠️ **It blocked both implementation lanes for two days** |

### The mechanism, in one paragraph

**A row reads `SEQUENCED — after [TASK-nnn]`. It was correct when written.** ⛔ **The predecessor ships. Its row goes to `IN VALIDATION`, and stops there — because the next state is `VERIFIED`, which is [QE's exclusively](../CLAUDE.md) ([D-123](DECISION_REGISTER.md)).** ⚡ **So the successor is parked behind a state that will never change without a Closeout, nobody re-asks the question, and the row sits.**

> ## **Every root of the wall was a predecessor already on `main`.**

| Root | On `main` | Outstanding on its lane branch | Rows it was holding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[TASK-432](BACKLOG.md)** | 15 commits | ⛔ **0** | [TASK-444](BACKLOG.md) |
| **[TASK-449](BACKLOG.md)** | 11 | ⛔ **0** | [TASK-450](BACKLOG.md) → 451 → 452 |
| **[TASK-457](BACKLOG.md)** | 6 | ⛔ **0** | [TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) |
| **[TASK-461](BACKLOG.md)** | 12 | ⛔ **0** | [TASK-462](BACKLOG.md) → 463 → 464 → 465 → 466 |
| **[TASK-427](BACKLOG.md)** | 23 | ⛔ **0** | [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md) — ⚠️ **the same trigger released [TASK-457](BACKLOG.md) on 2026-08-06 and this row was not re-asked** |
| **[C-229](#c-229--opportunity-intelligence-needs-a-door-and-d38-closed-that-one-deliberately)** | **closed 2026-08-07** | — | [TASK-441](BACKLOG.md), ⛔ **still `BLOCKED` a day after its blocker closed** |
| **[TASK-448](BACKLOG.md)** slice 3 | — | — | [TASK-467](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-468](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) → 469, 470 |

### The result

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Lane A claimable** | 🔴 **0** | ✅ **5** — [TASK-441](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-444](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-450](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-458](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-478](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Lane B claimable** | 🔴 **1**, and that one blocked on a credential | ✅ **3** — [TASK-202](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-428](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-462](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Rows parked behind a delivered predecessor** | 🔴 **22** | ✅ **0** |

⛔ **No scope was invented and no priority was changed.** **Every release is `READY` set on fitness** (§20e — *"`READY` states that a package is fit to implement; position in the queue states what it is worth, and that remains the product owner's"*), **and each row carries the structural evidence that released it.**

### [TASK-478](BACKLOG.md) — the one decomposition

⛔ **[TASK-448](BACKLOG.md) carried two states in one row**: `IN VALIDATION` for slices 1 and 2, `BLOCKED` for slice 3. **Its state is Lane A's to move, not this office's**, so **the slice is decomposed out rather than the row rewritten.**

⚡ **And slice 3's blocker was this office's fabrication.** **The row cited *"eighteen canonical components"* and nothing enumerated which eighteen** — because **the word *eighteen* appears nowhere in the design.** **[410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md) was corrected on 2026-08-06 and [TASK-448](BACKLOG.md) was not**, so the blocker outlived the belief that created it by a day.

### What now runs every cycle

✅ **`infra/coordination.py` exposes `stale_sequencing()`, and `state-check` reports it.** **A row is flagged when every predecessor has been *handed over*** — **declares `IN VALIDATION`/`VERIFIED`/`CERTIFIED` *and* that lane's branch carries nothing `integration` lacks.**

⛔ **It reports and never reclassifies.** **A `SEQUENCED` row is a fitness judgement**; a generator that silently promoted one would be editing the projection, **which makes it wrong rather than true.**

> ⚠️ **The first version of the predicate asked `git log origin/main --grep=TASK-nnn` and was wrong.** **A grep matches every commit that *mentions* an id — including the commit that wrote the row — so every task ever discussed on `main` read as delivered**, and it reported six rows unblocked that were not. ⛔ **[B-101](BUGS.md)'s class, inside the function written to end it.** ✅ **Caught before publishing, by running it and reading all six.**

## C-426 · Eighteen of Lane A's rows read `IN VALIDATION` and its branch has nothing on it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-07, ⚡ **found by the coordination generator reporting `lane_utilization = 3.6` for a lane that had just reported itself completely idle** |
| **Owner** | ⚡ **QE.** ⛔ **`VERIFIED` · `CERTIFIED` · `PROMOTED` · `DONE` are QE's exclusively** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), [D-123](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) — **neither the lane nor this office may advance one of these rows** |
| **Status** | **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-07 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **No engineering.** ⚠️ **It corrupts every capacity measurement the repository takes**, which is how it stayed invisible |

### The measurement

| | Lane A | Lane B | Lane C |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rows reading `IN VALIDATION`** | **16** *(+1 `IN PROGRESS`, +1 `CLAIMED`)* | 14 | — |
| ⚡ **Commits its branch has that `integration` does not** | ⛔ **0** | **8** | **12** |
| **`lane_utilization` before this was measured** | 🔴 **3.6** | 3.6 | 1.0 |
| ✅ **After** | ⚡ **0.0** | **3.6** | **1.0** |

> ## **A lane with zero commits ahead of `integration` has handed everything over. There is nothing there for QE to validate.**

⛔ **So Lane A's eighteen rows are not with QE. They are waiting for a state transition that nobody has written**, and **the lane cannot write it, and neither can this office.**

### What was verified, and how far

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Structural, exhaustive** | **`git rev-list --count origin/integration..origin/lane-a-product-surface` → 0.** ⚡ **This is not a proxy and not a count of anything textual** |
| ⚠️ **Sampled, not exhaustive** | **5 rows checked individually** — [TASK-200](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-405](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-417](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-432](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-437](BACKLOG.md) — **each has commits on `main` carrying its id, and each still reads `IN VALIDATION`, dated 2026-08-05.** ⛔ **The other eleven are inferred from the branch state, not individually checked** |

⚡ **[TASK-417](BACKLOG.md) is the clearest**: **its `Status` field is byte-identical on `lane-c-sync` and on `integration`**, says `IN VALIDATION — Lane A, 2026-08-05`, and **21 commits naming it are on `main`.**

### Why it matters even though it blocks nothing

⚠️ **`lane_utilization` read `3.6` for a lane that had just reported *"nothing requires Lane A action"* across three consecutive polls.** ⛔ **A metric that says *heavily loaded* about an idle lane is worse than no metric** — **it is the reason starvation was reported by the lane rather than detected by the instrument built to detect it.**

✅ **Fixed in the generator the same day**: **`awaiting_qe_transition` is now emitted per lane and excluded from utilization.** ⚡ **This is [D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) working exactly as instructed** — *"refine it based on real repository behavior rather than continuing to redesign it theoretically."* **v1 was live for one poll and the first thing it got wrong was found by a lane using it.**

### What QE is being asked for

**Nothing urgent, and no gate is involved.** ⚡ **Reconcile the rows against `main` at the next Closeout** — [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) activity 3 already requires exactly this: *"promoted claims marked `COMPLETE` and then removed."* ⛔ **This item exists so the backlog stops asserting a state the repository is not in** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)), **not to add work.**


### ⚡ Measured on the 2026-08-08 project audit — it is 63, not 18, and five days deep

**This item was raised at eighteen rows. The audit counted the register.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Rows reading `IN VALIDATION` on `integration`** | **63 of 115** |
| **Oldest** | **2026-08-03 — five days** |
| **By day** | `08-03` 2 · `08-04` 6 · `08-05` 13 · `08-06` 17 · `08-07` 17 · `08-08` 8 |

⛔ **And they are not with QE.** ✅ **Seven rows whose code is provably on `main` were tested by content — the design tokens (`--color-accent: 19 78 118`), the `(auth)` routes, four `on_main` journeys.** 🔴 **Five of the seven still read `IN VALIDATION`**: [TASK-467](BACKLOG.md), [485](BACKLOG.md), [487](BACKLOG.md), [490](BACKLOG.md), [491](BACKLOG.md). **Only [TASK-486](BACKLOG.md) and [494](BACKLOG.md) carry `PROMOTED`.**

> ## ⛔ **So `BACKLOG.md` cannot answer *what has shipped*.** ⚡ **A reader would conclude 63 slices are outstanding when most are live. Only [`workflows.toml`](coordination/workflows.toml) and git tell the truth, and nothing warns a reader of that.**

⚠️ **This is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s defect in its purest form** — *the repository asserting something untrue of itself* — **and it is the one class this repository treats as worse than an absent record, because it is trusted.**

⛔ **Lane C cannot repair a single row.** 📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md): `VERIFIED`, `CERTIFIED`, `PROMOTED` and `DONE` are QE's exclusively, *always, including on Lane C's own rows*** ([D-123](DECISION_REGISTER.md)). ✅ **The measurement is offered as input to the lane that can.**

⚡ **A mechanical suggestion, offered and not prescribed**: **QE already knows the certified SHA at each promotion, and a row's slice is greppable from its commit.** ⛔ **Sixty-three rows is a Closeout-sized job by hand and a small one by script — and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s Closeout step 13 already asks QE to reconcile the *board*; this is the same reconciliation one register over.**

## C-425 · The coordination ref asserts an authority that is not in the authoritative state

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | ⚡ **Lane A**, 2026-08-07, **on the first poll of `origin/coordination`** — and it found the defect from the outside within one fetch |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **this is a Product Office defect, not a question for the product owner.** **Architecture governance is Lane C's, and the ruling below needs no ratification** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07.** **Ruled in [479](architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md) §11 on the day it was raised; ⚡ the *condition* was met three days later and this row is closed on the fact rather than on the ruling.** ✅ **Measured, not asserted**: `CLAUDE.md` on `origin/integration` matches `origin/coordination` twice, [479](architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md) is present, and `infra/coordination.py` is present. ⚡ **The ref is binding. The README's *"not yet"* block is removed rather than left to age** — **a warning that outlives its condition is the same defect as one that arrives late** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚡ **Both sources agree today, and Lane A said so before asking** |

### What Lane A saw

> **"`origin/coordination` instructs lanes to stop reading `integration` for sequence, but its authority ([479](architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md)) is not on `integration`. Both sources currently say the same thing, so nothing is blocked. ⚡ The moment they disagree I need a ruling on which wins."**

✅ **Verified, all three parts:** **`docs/architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md` — absent from `origin/integration`** · **`infra/coordination.py` — absent** · **`CLAUDE.md` on `origin/integration` — zero matches for `origin/coordination`.**

⚠️ **And Lane A's second observation is the one that matters more:** **the ref's own `[lane.Lane_A]` block and `integration`'s queue give the same answer** — `claimable = 0`. ⚡ **It checked the two sources against each other before reporting a conflict it had not measured.**

### The ruling

> ## **The coordination source is never the tiebreaker. Its value is latency, not authority.**

**Every disagreement resolves toward the integration-side source, and the disagreement is a Product Office defect rather than a competing truth. The full table is [479](architecture/479-coordination-architecture.md) §11.**

✅ **Lane A's behaviour was correct and does not change today**: **poll as currently governed; read the ref as well if useful; ⛔ never act on it against `integration`.**

### Why this office did not see it

⚠️ **The ref is published by Lane C directly; the rule that makes it binding travels through QE like every other governance change.** ⛔ **Between those two moments the ref exists and the rule does not** — **and the repository said nothing about which state a lane was in**, so Lane A had to derive it from an absence.

✅ **Now measured rather than derived:** **`infra/state-check.py` reports the condition on every run**, naming this item.

⚡ **This is [B-101](BUGS.md)'s class one level up** — **the subsystem was verified by fetching the ref back and reading it, which proves the file exists and says nothing about whether a lane may obey it.** ⛔ **Verifying an artifact is not the same as verifying its standing** — **[D-130](DECISION_REGISTER.md), and this office wrote that sentence down four days ago.**

## C-424 · The finalized rail links four screens the design set does not contain

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-06, under [D-140](DECISION_REGISTER.md) — **after exhausting the design set, the Design System, the related screens, the ADRs and the implementation** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **this is missing *design intent*, not a missing decision about architecture** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-07, [D-141](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ③.** ⛔ **Resolved by measurement, not by ruling. No screen is missing.** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** **Every screen currently in flight is one the design set contains** |

### The question, at its smallest

> ## **`Fortune Signora App Shell.dc.html` specifies a navigation rail with eight primary entries. Four of them — `Forecast`, `Pipeline`, `Deals`, `Conversations` — link to screens no design in the set defines.**

**Is each of those four:** **① a screen whose design exists and I have not found · ② deliberately out of scope for this wave · or ③ a screen still to be designed?**

⛔ **That is the whole question.** ⚡ **[D-140](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *"Bring only the smallest unresolved question"*** — **this is not asking how navigation works, or what those screens do. It asks which of three states each of four names is in, and any of the three can be answered by pointing.**

### What was exhausted first

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| **The 26 design documents** | ⛔ **No `Forecast`, `Pipeline`, `Deals` or `Conversations` design.** Verified by filename and by reading the App Shell's `navItems` definition |
| **The App Shell design itself** | ✅ **It names them and gives each an icon and a count field. It does not describe their contents** |
| **Related screens** | ⚡ **`Deals` is confirmed as a real parent — the Opportunity Intelligence design's breadcrumb reads `Deals / EMEA enterprise / Vantage renewal — Q4 FY26`.** ⛔ **The other three appear nowhere else** |
| **The implementation** | ⛔ **No route exists for any of the four in `frontend/app/`** |
| **The ADRs and [D38](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md)** | **[D38](architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) removed *Opportunities* from navigation; the finalized design reinstates a richer rail. [D-128](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the design the authority, so D38 does not answer this** |

### ⚠️ Why it matters even though it blocks nothing

**Four rail entries with no design is either four missing screens or four items that should not be built.** ⛔ **A lane implementing the App Shell has to render the rail, and will otherwise either invent four destinations or silently drop them** — **which is exactly the drift [D-140](DECISION_REGISTER.md) exists to prevent.**

⚡ **`Accounts` is the worked example of why guessing is dangerous**: it carries `8,412`, the exact row count [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) cites, so it maps to **Companies** — **a mapping no filename would have suggested.** **Three of the remaining four may map similarly, and one guess in four is a screen nobody designed.**


### ✅ Closed 2026-08-07 — all four exist, and none of them is a screen

**[D-141](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ③: *"Compare every referenced rail entry directly against the locally copied canonical design documents… the screen exists → correct the references and close; the screen genuinely does not exist → update the architecture and close."*** ⚡ **Measured across all 26 designs. The answer is a third thing the item did not anticipate: each of the four resolves to a *section* or an *entity type*, not to a screen of its own.**

| Rail entry | What it actually is | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **`Home`** | ✅ **The Executive Dashboard** | **That design's own header reads `Home`**, and it carries `Executive summary`, `Revenue forecast`, `Pipeline health`, `Top risks`, `Signals feed`, `Recommended actions` |
| **`Forecast`** | ✅ **A section of the Executive Dashboard — `Revenue forecast`** | ⚡ **And a capability toggle**: Onboarding says *"Signora will switch on Forecast, Signal Center and Renewal risk"*, and Settings carries a `Forecast scenarios` flag at `on: false` |
| **`Pipeline`** | ✅ **A section of the Executive Dashboard — `Pipeline health`** | **`Open funnel` sits beneath it.** System States renders its failure as *"Pipeline trend could not load"* |
| **`Deals`** | ✅ **An entity type, and Opportunity Intelligence's parent** | **Global Search declares `entityPages: Account · Deal · Person · Conversation` and renders `Deals · 286 · complete`** |
| **`Conversations`** | ✅ **An entity type, and an Account 360 tab** | **The same `entityPages` list; Account 360 carries `['Conversations', '96']`; Global Search renders `Conversations · unavailable` with a retry** |

> ## **The rail links four *destinations that already have designs* — one dashboard and three entity lists the design defines through Global Search's entity model.**

⛔ **So nothing is missing and no architecture update is required.** ⚡ **What was wrong was this office's assumption that a rail entry implies a screen document.** **The design's structure is a rail of destinations, a dashboard that answers three of them, and an entity model that answers the rest.**

### ⚠️ What this changes for implementation

**A lane rendering the rail should not look for four missing designs.** ✅ **`Home`, `Forecast` and `Pipeline` are one screen — [418](architecture/418-platform-foundation-assessment.md)'s Executive Dashboard.** ✅ **`Deals` and `Conversations` are entity lists whose shape Global Search specifies and whose records are Opportunity Intelligence and Account 360.**

⛔ **Lane A's [C-233](#c-233--the-app-shells-22-numbered-specifications-are-not-in-the-repository) is a different finding and is not closed by this** — it is about the App Shell's own 22 numbered specifications, not about the rail's targets.

## C-423 · Architecture document numbers can still collide, and D-112 already solved this one class over

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-06, decomposing [TASK-477](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | 🔵 **Lane C** — ⚡ **reassigned 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7: identifier allocation is this office's mechanism and [TASK-477](BACKLOG.md) proceeds either way** *(was: product owner)* |
| **Status** | **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** — **one question, and [TASK-477](BACKLOG.md) proceeds either way** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** **[TASK-477](BACKLOG.md) fixes today's three collisions regardless; this decides whether a fourth can occur** |

### The question

> ## **Do architecture documents get a prefixed allocation block, the way `B-`, `C-` and `TASK-` ids did — or does the repository keep detecting collisions after they happen?**

### Why it is worth asking rather than assuming

**[D-112](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ruled the prefixed strategy on a stated bar, and the bar is general:**

> ***"Repository growth should remove collision risk completely rather than reducing it probabilistically."***

⚡ **Architecture documents fail that bar today and nothing noticed for three days.** **Six files landed on 2026-08-03, three numbers each naming two documents, and `state-check` has reported it every cycle since** — **detection working exactly as designed, and prevention absent.**

⚠️ **And the allocation table in [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already has a column for ADRs — `0100+` QE, `0200+` Lane A, `0400+` Lane C — but *not* for numbered architecture documents.** ⛔ **That is the gap: the same document set, half of it blocked and half of it free-for-all.**

### What this office is not asking for

⛔ **Not a renumbering of existing documents beyond [TASK-477](BACKLOG.md)'s three.** **`30`+ documents are dated records** (§2), **and retro-fitting a scheme across forty of them would rewrite forty identities to prevent a defect that has occurred once.**

✅ **The cheap answer, if you want one: extend the existing block table to numbered architecture documents, prospectively.** ⚡ **Lane A takes `2xx`, Lane B `3xx`, Lane C `4xx` — which is what already happened by accident**, since every `4xx` document in the tree is this office's.

| | |
|---|---|

**② Lane A raised [C-230](#c-230--lane-as-assignable-work-is-exhausted--every-row-and-its-reason) Finding 2** — *"`READY`, and its central element has no read"* — **and was right.**

## C-421 · A lane must be able to read the design it is implementing against

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-06, on [D-129](DECISION_REGISTER.md) |
| **Owner** | ⚠️ **Product owner — EXTERNAL.** **Access to the design set is not a lane's to arrange, and [D-129](DECISION_REGISTER.md) classifies it exactly**: *"treat that as an environmental issue to be resolved — not as a reason to create another specification"* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-06, [D-137](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2.** ⚡ **The dependency is resolved by direct access, exactly as D-137 requires — no copy, no export, no checklist.** ⛔ **And it was never a permission problem: the design was reachable the whole time and this office had not attempted it.** |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-467](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-468](BACKLOG.md) · [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md)** — every slice whose first act is a gap analysis against the design |

### What is being asked for, concretely

**That Lane A can open the canonical design set** — the location registered in [410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md).

⛔ **Not a copy. Not an export into the repository. Not a derived checklist.** **[D-129](DECISION_REGISTER.md) forbids all three**: *"the only acceptable derived artifacts are implementation tasks, measurable gap analyses, and test cases. The design itself must remain the single source of truth."*

### Why this is a coordination item rather than a note

⚡ **Because the alternative was tried and refused.** **This office proposed extracting the design's stated states into a conformance checklist a row could reference, and the product owner ruled against it** — **an intermediate artifact becomes a second specification, and the second one is the one that drifts.**

> **So the slices are written to reference the design *directly*, and the access question is raised as its own item rather than absorbed as a workaround.** ⚠️ **That is the difference between a dependency and a silent assumption.**

### What is not blocked

✅ **[TASK-469](BACKLOG.md) Onboarding and [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md) User Profile carry backend work that is absent regardless of the design** — onboarding state, step progress, inferred-value marking, the three-way field-ownership model. **Those can be measured and prepared without it.**

✅ **And nothing in the current wave waits on this.** **Lane A holds 11 eligible rows; all five refinement slices are `SEQUENCED` behind [TASK-448](BACKLOG.md).**


### ✅ Resolution — 2026-08-06, and the item was open for two days on an untested assumption

**[D-137](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2 asked three questions. All three are yes, and each was answered by *trying* rather than by reasoning.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Can a lane access the finalized designs?** | ✅ **Yes.** `DesignSync get_project 1d043179-1ee9-4c9f-b59e-592e04297cad` returns **`"Signora design system specification"`, `canEdit: true`** |
| **Can they be opened while implementing?** | ✅ **Yes.** `list_files` returns **26 `.dc.html` screen documents**, and `get_file` returned the Authentication design in full — **73,728 characters** |
| **Can refinement tasks reference them directly?** | ✅ **Yes, by path** — e.g. `Fortune Signora Authentication.dc.html`. **A path is a reference, not a duplicate** |

> ⛔ **Why it stayed open: `list_projects` returns *design-system* projects only, and this one is typed `PROJECT_TYPE_PROJECT`.** **So a listing shows two projects — *Modernist* and *Industry* — and not this one.** ⚠️ **An absence in a listing was read as an absence of access, and nobody called `get_project` with the id [410](architecture/410-approved-ui-specification.md) had already registered.**

⚡ **This is [D-130](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s rule turned on a coordination item rather than an endpoint: *verifying a name is not verifying behaviour*.** **The id was recorded, the tool existed, and the office reasoned about access instead of requesting it.** **[TASK-467](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-468](BACKLOG.md) and [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) were blocked for two days on that.**

**The access route, recorded so no lane repeats the search:** ⚡ **`DesignSync` · `projectId` `1d043179-1ee9-4c9f-b59e-592e04297cad` · `get_file` with the screen's document path.**

## C-420 · Two words carry two concepts each — `Owner` and `Match`

**Opened 2026-08-05 · Lane C · current module assignee: `workspace_tenancy` · `opportunity_engine` · `knowledge_graph` · `commercial_profile` · 🟠**

> **Found by building the Canonical Domain Vocabulary ([D-085](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), and the product owner asked for a recommendation on both.** **Neither blocks anything. Both get more expensive with every screen built.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owner** | **The product owner** — it is a vocabulary ruling across four modules |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-05, [D-087](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** **Both recommendations accepted in substance**: *"Workspace Owner and Account Owner clearly communicate different business meanings while preserving compatibility with existing architecture and APIs… distinguishing Identity Resolution from Criteria Evaluation makes the business intent clearer without reopening settled architectural decisions."* **No shipped API, Casbin subject or ratified invariant is renamed** |
| **Blocks** | **Nothing.** ⚡ **One follow-on is actionable and is Lane B's 🟢**: `commercial_profile/domain/matching.py` reads `evaluation.py`, **and the window closes the first time another module imports the path** |

### ① `Owner` — recommend **qualification**, and the Change Budget decides it

| | |
|---|---|
| **`WorkspaceRole.OWNER`** | **An administrative role**, and **the subject of every row in `policy.csv`** |
| **`opportunity_state.owner_id`** | ***The seller working an account.*** `OwnerScope` is `ALL` · `MINE` · `UNASSIGNED` |
| **Where they collide** | **The authorization model uses the first. Every screen shows the second.** *"Who owns this workspace"* and *"who owns this account"* are different questions with one word |

> ⛔ **Renaming either is ⚫ in the Change Budget.** *"Rename an API"* is **never**, and one of these is a **Casbin subject across thirteen resources** while the other is a **shipped API field**. **So the ruling is not *which to rename* — it is whether qualification suffices.**

> ✅ **Recommendation: qualification, and it costs nothing.** **`Workspace Owner` and `Account Owner` become canonical; bare `Owner` becomes `qualified` and is refused in new work.** **No code changes, no migration, no API touched** — what changes is that **UI copy, API documentation, prompts and every future declaration must say which.**
>
> ⚠️ **And it matters for AI**: a model reasoning over *"the owner"* across both contexts has no way to know which, **which is question ⑥ of the vocabulary gate arriving as a concrete cost rather than a principle.**

### ② `Match` — recommend **distinguishing**, and one rename is already ⛔ and one is 🟢

| | |
|---|---|
| **`MatchStrength`** | **Identity resolution** — *"a property of the rule, not a belief"*. ⛔ **A permanent invariant, ratified 2026-07-29.** **Renaming it reopens a ratified decision and is not a vocabulary matter** |
| **`commercial_profile/domain/matching.py`** | **Criterion evaluation** — shipped by [TASK-434](BACKLOG.md) |

> ⚡ **The good word already won at the call site.** **The shipped function is `evaluate`, not `match`** — `domain/matching.evaluate`, and `IcpCriteriaView` and `validate_criterion_list` carry no *match* anywhere. **Only the filename says matching.**

> ✅ **Recommendation: `Identity Resolution` and `Criteria Evaluation` are canonical; `Match` is `qualified`.** **`MatchStrength` keeps its name — it is ratified, and its own docstring is why.** **And `matching.py` is a module-internal filename, which is 🟢** — the cheapest possible correction, available for as long as nobody outside the module imports it.
>
> ⚠️ **That window is open now and closes the first time another module imports the path.** **Recorded as a trigger rather than a request.**

### What this item is not

⛔ **Not a rename programme.** **Both recommendations avoid touching a shipped API, a Casbin subject or a ratified invariant** — which is the whole reason to rule on vocabulary *before* the next screen rather than after.

⚡ **It also claimed `B-327` and `C-333` were *"both verified absent from every register"*. That was wrong on both counts** — each id already carried a live row raised by Lane B the day before. **`state-check`'s duplicate-identifier check found it; the sentence asserting the verification is exactly what a check exists to disbelieve.**

## C-431 · Three controls on the approved sign-in card have no backing capability

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-07, ⚡ **measuring Workflow 1 against the approved design for [D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) — before Lane A starts, rather than when it reaches the control** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **[D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑦: *"If something in the design is unclear: STOP. Raise a precise Product Office question."* Two of the three are scope; the third is an authentication semantic, which [D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ places here too** |
| **Status** | ✅ **TWO OF THREE ANSWERED — [D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md), 2026-08-07, and neither needed a separate ruling.** ⛔ **The attempt counter is out of Workflow 1** by ⑤'s own parenthetical — ***"lock or rate-limit messaging (where backed by implemented capability)"*** — **and there is none.** ⛔ **`Use single sign-on` is out on ④ rather than on scope**: **domain→IdP routing is an authorization semantic, not an infrastructure boundary, and ④ forbids substituting one** — ***"Never introduce development-only authentication paths, authorization shortcuts, or altered business behaviour."*** ⚠️ **`Keep me signed in for 30 days` remains open and has changed character**: under ① it may be a **real** implementation rather than a simulation, since Better Auth owns session lifetime and `server.ts:86` merely fixes `expiresIn` at seven days. ⛔ **This office could not verify it — Lane C has no `node_modules` and did not open the package** ([D-137](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *accessible is a claim to be tested, never assumed in either direction*). ✅ **Lane A verifies by opening it, then builds or defers** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **It shapes what the human review gate is shown, not what Lane A builds first** — **nine of Workflow 1's ten parts do not touch it** |

**Full measurement: [488 §5](architecture/488-workflow-1-login-gap.md).**

> ⛔ **This is raised under [D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑦ — *"No lane may simplify the design. No lane may reinterpret the design. If something in the design is unclear: STOP"* — and under [D-140](DECISION_REGISTER.md), which requires one precise question rather than one convenient assumption.**

### What the design draws, and what exists behind it

**`Fortune Signora Authentication.dc.html`, screen `02 · Sign in`, at real width. Three of its controls have no capability behind them, measured rather than assumed:**

| Control | The measurement | Why it is not a task |
|---|---|---|
| **`Use single sign-on`** — and `Sign in with SSO` on `01 · Welcome` | ⛔ **[418 §1](architecture/418-platform-foundation-assessment.md) lists *per-workspace SSO enforcement* and *domain→IdP routing* among Authentication's named absences** | **Journey 3 of the design's five is `SSO-enforced`.** ⚡ **A login journey "exactly as designed" has an SSO branch point in it, so omitting the control changes what the review gate reviews** |
| **`Keep me signed in for 30 days`** | ⚠️ **`frontend/lib/auth/server.ts:86` — `expiresIn: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7`. Seven days, fixed, and not electable by the customer** | ⛔ **The one item in Workflow 1 that is an authentication *semantic*.** **[D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④: *"Only the infrastructure boundary may change."* Session lifetime is not the infrastructure boundary** |
| **The attempt counter** — *"You have **3 attempts** left before the account locks for 15 minutes"* | ⛔ **`grep -rn "rateLimit\|lockout\|maxAttempts\|failedAttempts"` across `frontend/lib/auth/` and `backend/` returns **zero**.** ⚠️ **418 does not list it, because 418 audited what the design *shows* and this is what its copy *implies*** | **Screen `03 · Sign in — failed` is a Workflow 1 screen and its entire message is a lockout message.** **Screens `11 · Account locked` and `12 · Too many attempts` are the same absent capability** |

### The question

> ## **Does Workflow 1 deliver these three, defer them behind Login as their own rows, or render them?**

| | Option | This office's reading |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Deliver them inside Workflow 1** | ⛔ **Three backend capabilities with no rows. Workflow 1 stops being a presentation-layer replacement, which is the one thing [D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) says it is** |
| **B** | **Render the controls and route them somewhere** | ⛔ **A control that does not do what it says is worse than an absent one, and `03`'s counter would be a fiction about our own product.** **[D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑤ permits simulating a *provider's response*; it does not permit simulating Signora's behaviour** |
| ✅ **C** | **Workflow 1 delivers every element of `02`, `03` and `15` whose capability exists; these three become rows behind Login** | ⚡ **Recommended. This is not a simplification — it is the distinction [TASK-467](BACKLOG.md) already drew with the product owner's approval when it put magic link, MFA, per-workspace SSO enforcement, domain→IdP routing and session-expiry state out of scope by name** |

⚠️ **Stated plainly because it affects the gate rather than the code: under C the product owner reviews a login screen with no SSO entry point and no *keep me signed in*.** ⛔ **That should be known going in rather than discovered at the review.**

### ⛔ What this does *not* block

**[TASK-467](BACKLOG.md) is scoped and buildable today.** ✅ **The palette, the card geometry, the three responsive layouts, the six field states, the six button states, the failure state's summary and remedy, the authenticating state and the product mark are nine of Workflow 1's ten parts, and none of them touches this question.** ⚡ **[D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ⑦ is the instruction being followed: bring the question, and do not pause the work for it.**
