## C-432 · §20c freezes the frontend foundation, and D-154 mandates changing it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-07, ⚡ **auditing UI standards for [D-154](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ — [489 §5](architecture/489-legacy-ui-standards-audit.md)** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **`CLAUDE.md` is the one file this office may never edit** (§20e, *Shared files have one owner*) |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — 2026-08-07.** **Approved by the product owner ([D-170](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2) and applied the same cycle.** ⚡ **§20c now carries the paragraph: the UI Migration Program is a standing approved architectural change under the fourth exemption, and the freeze continues to bar ad-hoc modification for one page's benefit.** ⚠️ **Applied by this office on explicit instruction — *"Update the wording in `CLAUDE.md` as proposed"* — and it is the one edit Lane C has made to that file.** ⛔ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) is otherwise unchanged; `CLAUDE.md` is the product owner's** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing** |

### The inconsistency, stated exactly

**`CLAUDE.md` §20c — *Frontend Foundation*:**

> **"From M1.5, the frontend foundation is **frozen** on the same terms as the platform (§20a). Business milestones **consume** the Design System, Shared Components, Application Shell, Query Layer, Authentication integration, and Routing; **they do not modify them**."**

**Change is permitted for four reasons only: a production defect · an accessibility issue · a security issue · an explicitly approved architectural change (RFC).**

**[D-154](DECISION_REGISTER.md) requires the opposite, in terms:**

> **"The finalized Signora Design System is the baseline. Legacy UI is not the baseline… If an existing visual implementation differs from the finalized design, the design wins. Always."**

### ✅ Why nothing is blocked

⚡ **[D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) and [D-154](DECISION_REGISTER.md) are §20c's fourth exemption — *an explicitly approved architectural change*, ruled by the product owner, which is exactly the authority §20c names.** ⛔ **[TASK-467](BACKLOG.md)'s Change Budget already records this**, and Lane A may proceed today.

### ⚠️ Why it is still worth one paragraph

⛔ **§20c is in the constitution a cold session reads before it reads anything else.** **A lane arriving next week reads *"the frontend foundation is frozen; they do not modify them"* and then finds a queue asking it to replace `globals.css` wholesale.** ⚡ **It will resolve the contradiction correctly — the rulings are in the register — but it will spend the time, and it may resolve it *conservatively*, which is the expensive direction.**

> ⛔ **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *the repository itself should always tell the truth*, and a governance document that reads as forbidding the program the repository is executing is that defect.** ⚠️ **Equally §2's other half: *governance describes reality; it never quietly changes it* — which is precisely why this office raises the sentence rather than writing it.**

### The recommendation, in one sentence

> **§20c gains a line naming [D-153](DECISION_REGISTER.md) and [D-154](DECISION_REGISTER.md) as the standing approved architectural change for the UI migration, and stating that the freeze protects the foundation *from ad-hoc modification*, never from the approved design.**

⚡ **Offered as wording rather than as a request for a decision — the decision is made, and this is the sentence that records it.** ⛔ **Applied only by the product owner.**

## C-434 · Three of Login's remaining screens need a decision, not a build — and one of them is already shipped

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-07, ⚡ **implementing Workflow 1 milestone 3 and opening `node_modules` rather than reasoning about it** ([D-137](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *accessible is a claim to be tested, never assumed in either direction*) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **all three are authentication semantics or scope, and [D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ places both here** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-07, [D-170](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §3.** **All three recommendations agreed, with one clarification on social sign-in.** ⚡ **① SSO/social: implement Google, Microsoft and every provider the design defines, *exactly as designed*, calling the real Better Auth abstraction.** ⛔ **Where credentials are unavailable, the *configuration* may be truthfully simulated — never the authentication behaviour** — **so enabling production later is configuration rather than UI redevelopment.** ✅ **② the attempt counter is not simulated** — ***"If the backend does not expose that information, the UI must not invent it."*** ✅ **③ rate limiting is enabled in development wherever practical** — ***"Development should behave as close to production as reasonably possible."*** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing built.** ⚠️ **It changes what the Workflow 1 review gate is shown**, which [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability) established should be known going in rather than discovered at the review |

> ⚡ **This is [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability) one step later, from inside the implementation.** That item measured three controls from the outside and [D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md) answered two. **Building the screens produced three further facts, and one of them says a ruled-out control shipped anyway.**

### ① 🔴 `Use single sign-on` was ruled out of Workflow 1, and this lane shipped it

**[D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md) via [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability):** ***"`Use single sign-on` is out on ④ rather than on scope — domain→IdP routing is an authorization semantic."***

⛔ **Milestone 2 put the control on the sign-in card anyway, pointing at `/sso`, which did not exist.** **Every enterprise buyer who followed the one link addressed to them reached the not-found page.** ⚠️ **This lane's defect, and it is named rather than folded into the next change.**

**Milestone 3 gave it an honest destination instead of removing it**, and the reasoning is stated so it can be overruled in one line:

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **What was *not* built** | **No domain→IdP lookup.** No table, no setting, no endpoint. **The field renders through [`LockedField`](../frontend/components/ui/locked.tsx) with its reason and no value**, and there is deliberately **no email input** — a control whose outcome cannot depend on its input is a false affordance |
| ✅ **What is real** | **The configured `socialProviders`** — the same `signIn(provider)` call the sign-in card makes, producing the same session ([ADR-0033](architecture/adr/0033-sign-in-methods.md)). ⛔ **Not an alternate journey**: the existing one, offered from a second place |
| ⚠️ **Why not simply delete the control** | **[D-158](DECISION_REGISTER.md) and [D-162](DECISION_REGISTER.md) both post-date D-156 and both say the finalized design wins.** **Journey 3 of the design's five is `SSO-enforced`** — a Login the product owner reviews with no SSO entry point is a different review |

> ### **Does the reviewed Login keep an SSO entry point that names no provider, or is the control removed until domain→IdP routing exists?**

### ② Account lockout does not exist, and Better Auth will not be made to fake it

**Design `03` — *"You have **3 attempts** left before the account locks for 15 minutes"* — and the whole of `11 · Account locked`.**

✅ **Measured in the vendor rather than inferred:** `better-auth@1.6.25` rate-limits **per `ip + path`**, three attempts per ten seconds on `/sign-in`, answering `429` with `X-Retry-After`. ⛔ **There is no per-account lockout, no attempt counter and no unlock time.**

⚡ **The design's own footnote on `12` says why that is the better control**: *"throttling is per device and IP, not per account, so an attacker cannot lock a colleague out by guessing at their address."* **The two screens contradict each other, and the vendor implements the one the design defends.**

**Built:** `12 · Too many attempts`, with the countdown read off `X-Retry-After`. **Not built:** the attempt counter and `/locked`. ⛔ **A counter would be a fabricated number about a security control; a lockout rule would be a business rule this lane invented.** ✅ **Consistent with D-156's answer to C-431, and recorded because it now covers two more screens than that item measured.**

⚠️ **One line of `12` is also not rendered**: *"doubles with each further attempt."* **Better Auth's window is a fixed rolling ten seconds** — printing it would misstate a security control by a factor of two.

### ③ The throttle is invisible outside production, and the fix is one option

`better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs`:

```js
enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction,
```

⛔ **So the rate limiter — the only real brute-force control the product has — is **off** in development and in every test run.** ⚠️ **A security control that exists only where nobody looks at it is a control no review and no journey has ever seen**, which is the shape [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md) and [§2](../CLAUDE.md) both name.

⚡ **Setting `rateLimit: { enabled: true }` uses the vendor as intended and **strengthens** rather than weakens it — [D-158](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s *"never weaken Better Auth"* points the same way.** ⛔ **This lane did not make the change**: it alters the Authentication Authority's configuration in every environment, and the vendor's `max: 3 / window: 10` on `/sign-in` would apply to the e2e suites of every lane.

> ### **Is the rate limiter enabled in all modes, so the throttled state is reviewable and the control is real outside production?**

### ⛔ And one that is a decision rather than a gap

**Magic link — design `05`.** ✅ **`better-auth/plugins/magic-link` is present in `node_modules`**, so this is not a build problem. ⛔ **It adds an authentication *method*, which is not the customer-visible presentation layer [D-159](DECISION_REGISTER.md) bounds this work to.** **No row exists. Raised so it is scheduled rather than discovered missing at the Workflow 3 gate.**

## C-435 · A planning correction that unblocks an idle lane has no trigger of its own

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-08, ⚡ **on Lane A's 136th consecutive idle cycle** — **and as the first unprompted exercise of [D-171](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7** |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner.** **It proposes changing a rule, and the governance freeze reserves that** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, the requesting lane.** 🔴 **Discharged by implementation, not merely by ruling.** ✅ **[D-181](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6 ruled Option 3; [TASK-497](BACKLOG.md) built it — `BACKLOG.md` now reaches `origin/coordination`, so a lane polls one ref for both order and scope.** ⚡ **[D-227](DECISION_REGISTER.md) then proved the remaining authority half unnecessary and [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md) closed it.** ⛔ **Nothing is left of this item** *(was: ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — ruled 2026-08-08, [D-181](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6: **Option 3**.** ⛔ **Neither of the other two.** ⚡ **The ruling's )* |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing, from 2026-08-08.** ⚡ **Instance 3 cleared when QE integrated `50e81139`.** ⛔ **The class did not clear, which is what Option 3 closes** |

> ## ✅ **RULED — Option 3.** **`BACKLOG.md`'s planning state reaches lanes through `origin/coordination`, the ref Product Office already owns and publishes.** **`ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md` stays exactly where it is.**

### ⚡ Why Option 3 answers the ruling's own constraint better than Option 2 did

**The product owner asked for a capability that is *narrowly scoped, auditable, and can never become a route around QE for executable change*. Option 2 delivers that by *discipline plus a guard*; Option 3 delivers it by *construction*, and the difference is the standard [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) already prefers — *a violation that is unrepresentable over one that is merely discouraged*.**

| | **Option 2 — `BACKLOG.md`-only push to `integration`** | ✅ **Option 3 — planning state on `origin/coordination`** |
|---|---|---|
| **Could it ever carry executable code?** | ⚠️ **Only because `--audit-planning` says no.** **A guard that is edited, skipped or bypassed re-opens it** | ⛔ **No. The ref is an orphan with no `backend/`, no `frontend/`, no migration chain.** ⚡ **There is nothing executable to put there** |
| **Auditable** | **Guard output, per push** | ✅ **The ref's whole history is planning, and [B-410](BUGS.md)'s `--publish` validates every publication before it lands** |
| **Touches `integration`** | **Yes — a second writer on the arbitration ref** | ✅ **Never. QE's authority over `integration` is untouched, and this office asked for none** |
| **Touches `ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.md`** | ⛔ **Excluded by the guard, which is a rule** | ✅ **Excluded by *location*, which is a fact.** ⚡ **The claim protocol's arbitration point is unchanged and unreachable from here** |

⚠️ **And the honest cost, stated rather than discovered: this is a migration, not a flag.** **Two readers change** — [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s Task Claim Protocol step 3b, and every lane's habit of reading `BACKLOG.md` on `integration`. ⛔ **Until both move, `BACKLOG.md` on `integration` stays authoritative and Option 3 is not yet in force.**

### ✅ What is already true, which is most of it

📁 **[D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) built the ref, the poll and the projection a year of this argument ago.** ⚡ **`coordination.toml` already carries `current`, `next`, `depends_on`, `waiting_for` and the metrics — every planning fact a lane needs to *choose*.** **What it does not carry is the row's own scope, which is what step 3b goes to `BACKLOG.md` for.**

> ## ⚡ **So the migration is one question, not many: does the *scope text* travel to the coordination ref, or does a lane keep reading it from `integration` while taking its *order* from the ref?**
>
> ⛔ **That is an architectural question and it is [491](architecture/491-planning-synchronization-architecture.md)'s subject.** ✅ **It is not answered here and it does not block: under [D-180](DECISION_REGISTER.md) it becomes a row, not a document.**

### ⚡ The deadlock, stated as two rules that are each correct

> **① [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"Only executable change opens a cycle; documentation, claims, planning and board maintenance still accumulate until an executable slice reaches `IN VALIDATION`."***
>
> **② [D-136](DECISION_REGISTER.md): a planning correction is *"high-priority synchronization — ahead of ordinary feature work in the integration order."***

⛔ **② orders planning corrections *within* a cycle. ① decides whether a cycle happens at all. Neither can start one.**

> ## ⚡ **So: when a lane is idle, there is by definition no executable change coming — therefore no cycle is warranted — therefore the planning correction that would unblock the lane cannot be integrated.** ⛔ **The condition that makes the correction urgent is the same condition that prevents it landing.**

### The measurement

| | |
|---|---|
| **Lane A** | **136 consecutive idle cycles**, reported by Lane A rather than by this office |
| **The published source right now** | **`current = TASK-485` · `claimable = 1` · `claimable_now = 0`** |
| **`integration`'s backlog** | **`TASK-485` reads `SEQUENCED`** |
| ⚡ **What separates them** | **Three `Planning-Sync: required` commits on `lane-c-sync`** |
| ⛔ **What Product Office can do about it** | **Nothing.** **It cannot push to `integration` and is not asking to** |

⚠️ **[D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) built `origin/coordination` to bypass exactly this, and the bypass is half-built.** **Planning *information* flows through the ref — but claim *eligibility* still flows through QE, because [C-425](#c-425) correctly requires a claim to agree with `BACKLOG.md` on `integration`.** ⚡ **A lane can now *learn* what to build without QE and still cannot *start* it.**

### The three options

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Let Product Office fast-forward `integration` with a backlog-only commit** — the same shape as the claim-commit exception, bounded by `certification-guard.py --audit-claims` extended to a `--audit-planning` mode that refuses anything touching code | ⚡ **Cleanest and fastest.** ⛔ **It grants a second lane write access to `integration`, and [D-142](DECISION_REGISTER.md) declined that twice** |
| **B** | **Make the coordination ref authoritative for claimability** | ⛔ **Contradicts [D-144](DECISION_REGISTER.md) in terms — *\"if the coordination source disagrees with `BACKLOG.md`, the backlog wins\"* — and creates the two-representations defect [§2](../CLAUDE.md) forbids** |
| ✅ **C — recommended** | **`Planning-Sync: required` warrants a cycle on its own when a lane is starved.** **QE runs the short path — integrate, no certification — because nothing executable changed and `--audit-main` already proves that by paths rather than by trust** | ✅ **No authority moves. No new file. No second truth.** ⚡ **It closes the loop by making the *starvation* the trigger, which is the fact that actually matters** |

### ⚠️ What C costs, stated rather than hidden

⛔ **It weakens *\"a cycle is warranted by executable change\"*, and that rule exists for a good reason: [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) says certifying documentation alone *\"is how a team learns to skip cycles.\"*** ✅ **The mitigation is that C is not a full cycle — it is an integration without certification, which the audit already distinguishes by paths.** ⚡ **And the trigger is narrow: a lane at zero `actionable` and zero `claimable_now`, which [B-409](BUGS.md) just made measurable.**

### ⚡ Why this is the challenge worth making

**[490](architecture/490-operating-model-critique.md) argued that [D-171](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §1's planning depth would produce stale plans.** ⛔ **That critique was right and it was not the most important thing.**

> ## **Planning depth has never been the constraint. Lane A idled 136 cycles with prepared, sequenced, owned work waiting — and the thing in the way was an integration step, not an analysis gap.**

⚠️ **Adding more planning depth to a repository whose bottleneck is synchronization makes the bottleneck worse**, because every additional prepared row is another thing waiting on the same step. ✅ **This item is what [D-171](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §11 asks for: an improvement to the operating model, brought forward with evidence rather than waited for.**

## C-240 · Two ruled or designed password controls live in the one file Workflow 2 may not touch

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, ⚡ **implementing [TASK-485](BACKLOG.md) milestone 1 and opening `node_modules` rather than reasoning about it** ([D-137](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *accessible is a claim to be tested, never assumed in either direction*) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **both are authentication semantics, which [D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ places here**, and one of them is **already ruled and simply has no row that may execute it** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — all five ruled.** ⚡ **①②⑤ approved to schedule 2026-08-08, and ⑤'s *direction* — the last open half — ruled at [D-185](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2: **`/` becomes the Signora Welcome experience**.** ✅ **[TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) carries ①②③, [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md) carries the route map.** ⛔ **Nothing in this item is now waiting on anybody** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing is stopped.** ✅ **Screen `06` ships without both**, and each is drawn out rather than faked. ⚠️ **What it changes is what the Workflow 2 review is shown** — the same thing [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability) established should be known going in rather than discovered at the review |

> ⚡ **Neither of these is a build problem, and that is the finding.** **Better Auth 1.6.25 already ships both capabilities**, verified by reading `node_modules` rather than the changelog. **Each is one line of configuration in `lib/auth/server.ts`** — and **[TASK-485](BACKLOG.md) states in terms that nothing in it touches that file**: *"⛔ Nothing in this row touches `lib/auth/server.ts`, RS256 verification, `requireEmailVerification` or any route."*
>
> ⛔ **So this lane did not touch it.** **Finding a change is never permission to make it** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)), and a row that quietly widened its own budget would be a worse precedent than either gap.

### ① 🟡 The design's fourth password rule is real, shipped in the dependency, and not enabled

**The design enumerates four rules on screen `06`** — *At least 12 characters · Upper and lower case · A number or symbol · **Not found in a breach corpus***.

✅ **The first three are answered from the typed string and ship.** ⛔ **The fourth is a server check and is not drawn**, because a row a client could only guess at would be **a rule the product does not check painted as one it does** ([D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④: *a state whose business rule is missing is not built at all*).

| | |
|---|---|
| **It exists** | ✅ **`better-auth/plugins/haveibeenpwned` is present**, read at `frontend/node_modules/better-auth/dist/plugins/haveibeenpwned/index.mjs` |
| **It is privacy-preserving** | ⚡ **k-anonymity**: it SHA-1s the password, sends **the first five hex characters only** to `api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/…` with `Add-Padding: true`, and matches the suffix locally. ⛔ **The password never leaves the process** |
| **Where it hooks** | **`init()` wraps `ctx.password.hash`** and gates on the request path — by default `/sign-up/email`, `/change-password`, `/reset-password` and four more. ⚠️ **So it cannot be a live per-keystroke check**; it answers at submit, which is exactly how the design draws it — **the mock shows a filled password with this one rule unmet** |
| **The cost of enabling it** | ⚠️ **An outbound call to a third-party API on every password set.** ⛔ **That is a data-flow decision and a dependency on an external service's availability, not a lane's judgement** — the plugin raises `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` when the range API cannot be reached, so **an outage becomes an inability to register** |

> ⚠️ **The last row is why this is a ruling rather than a task.** Enabling it is one line; **deciding that Signora will not accept a registration while `api.pwnedpasswords.com` is unreachable is a product decision**, and the failure mode is invisible until the day it happens.

### ② 🟡 [D-170](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §3 ③ is ruled, and no row may execute it

**The ruling is already made** — [C-434](#c-434--three-of-logins-remaining-screens-need-a-decision-not-a-build--and-one-of-them-is-already-shipped) ③, [D-170](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §3: ***"rate limiting is enabled in development wherever practical — development should behave as close to production as reasonably possible."***

⛔ **It is not enabled.** **`lib/auth/server.ts` passes no `rateLimit` option**, and Better Auth's default is `enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction` — **so it is off in development**, which is every mode the product owner reviews in.

⚠️ **The screen that needs it is built and cannot be seen working.** **Workflow 1 milestone 3 shipped `sign-in/throttled.tsx`** against the real `429` and the real `X-Retry-After` header — Better Auth's sign-in rule is **3 attempts per 10 seconds, keyed on `ip + path`** — and **nothing in development can produce that response**, so the state is unreachable at the review.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What it needs** | **`rateLimit: { enabled: true }`** in `lib/auth/server.ts`. ✅ **Nothing else** — the window, the limit and the `/sign-in` special case are Better Auth's own |
| **Why it is not in [TASK-485](BACKLOG.md)** | ⛔ **Same file, same prohibition.** ⚠️ **And it is Workflow 1's state, not Workflow 2's** — [TASK-467](BACKLOG.md) is `IN VALIDATION` and closed to this lane |
| **The smallest fix** | ⚡ **A row that owns `lib/auth/server.ts`**, or **one line added to [TASK-485](BACKLOG.md)'s Change Budget by the product owner.** ⛔ **Not a lane's to widen** |

### ③ ⚠️ The agreement screen `06` asks for cannot be read

**The design's line is *"By continuing you agree to the Terms and Privacy Notice"* with both words linked.** ⛔ **No legal route, page, document or configured URL exists anywhere in this repository**, checked rather than assumed — **and the design's own markup points both at `#legal`**, a placeholder.

✅ **The sentence ships and the words are not links.** **Two dead links is precisely the defect Workflow 1 shipped at `Use single sign-on`** and had to repair in milestone 4; **a person is not sent to a not-found page from the screen where they are agreeing to something.**

⛔ **Writing the documents is not this lane's and not any lane's** — they are legal text, and inventing them would be worse than omitting them ([§21](../CLAUDE.md)). ⚠️ **Recorded because *"agree to terms you cannot read"* is a commercial exposure rather than a cosmetic gap**, and because the destinations are almost certainly a hosted URL rather than a product route.

### ④ ⚠️ The design's self-serve branch has no capability, and the lookup would be a disclosure

**Journey 2 in the design:** ***"A work email on a domain that already has a workspace is offered a request to join instead of a second workspace."*** **[TASK-485](BACKLOG.md) carries it under Features and under Playwright coverage.**

⛔ **Nothing behind it exists**, verified by content:

| | |
|---|---|
| **No domain** | **`Workspace` carries no domain field** — `backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/domain/entities.py` |
| **No route** | ⛔ **None of `workspace_tenancy`'s twenty paths is a request-to-join.** ⚡ **The same absence already stopped the *Request access* control on `/join`** — `tests/components/join.test.tsx` asserts it is never offered, *"because nothing can grant it"* |
| 🔴 **And the lookup itself is the question** | ⚠️ **It must answer an unauthenticated caller** — a person registering has no session. **So *"does this company use Signora?"* becomes answerable by anyone with the sign-up form**, from any email domain, one guess at a time. ⛔ **That is the account-enumeration trade the sign-in screen's wording exists to refuse**, one level up: **not *does this person exist* but *is this company a customer*** |

> ⚡ **This is not a build estimate; it is a disclosure decision.** **The design draws a genuinely better journey** — being offered a request to join beats creating a second workspace for the same company — **and the mechanism it needs publishes the customer list to unauthenticated callers.** ⛔ **A lane should not settle that quietly**, which is [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability)'s own lesson.

### ⑤ 🔴 Workflow 2's journey begins on a screen no anonymous visitor is sent to

**[TASK-485](BACKLOG.md) names this as the one gap it *"must settle before implementation"***, and records it as solved: *"the design's `01 Welcome` needed a public root outside `(app)`* — ✅ *Lane A built it in Workflow 1 milestone 3."*

⚠️ **Half of it is solved.** ✅ **The route exists at `/welcome`, it is reachable, and the product mark on every authentication screen leads to it.** ⛔ **But nothing *sends* anybody there**: `app/(app)/layout.tsx:35` still reads `if (!session?.user) redirect('/sign-in')`, so **an anonymous visitor to `/` lands on the sign-in card and never sees the front door.**

⚡ **It mattered less in Workflow 1 and it matters now.** **Journey 2 in the design is the one this row builds** — *Welcome → Create account → Verify email → Workspace creation* — **and its first step is reachable only by somebody who already knew to look for it.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Why this lane did not change it** | ⛔ **Out of [TASK-485](BACKLOG.md)'s Change Budget**, which names `frontend/app/(auth)/` and `components/ui`. **`app/(app)/layout.tsx` is neither.** ⚠️ **And [D-159](DECISION_REGISTER.md) reuses routing** — *"only the customer-visible presentation layer is being replaced"* — **so redirecting the product's front door is a product decision, not a presentation change** |
| **The decision, in one sentence** | **Does an anonymous visitor to `/` land on `01 Welcome` or on `02 Sign in`?** ⚡ **The design says Welcome; the product has said `/sign-in` since M1** |
| **What it costs either way** | ✅ **One line.** ⚠️ **It changes the first thing every returning customer sees** — a signed-out seller reopening a bookmark meets a marketing card instead of the password field they came for, which is the argument *for* the current behaviour and worth ruling on rather than inheriting |

> ⛔ **Raised in Workflow 1 as a code comment and never as an item, which is the process defect here.** **A decision recorded only where the implementing lane can see it is a decision nobody made** — [§20e](../CLAUDE.md), and the reason [C-421](#c-421--a-lane-must-be-able-to-read-the-design-it-is-implementing-against) exists.

## C-241 · Workflow 3's approved screen needs the one file its row forbids, and this is the third instance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, ⚡ **on claiming [TASK-486](BACKLOG.md) and reading `node_modules` before building** ([D-137](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *accessible is a claim to be tested, never assumed*) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **an authentication semantic, which [D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ places here** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION` — Lane C, 2026-08-08.** ⛔ **It was never waiting on a decision, and this office nearly escalated it as though it were.** ✅ **The design decides the control** — screen `07` **is** the six-digit code, and [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot the authority. ✅ **[C-240](#c-240--two-ruled-or-designed-password-controls-live-in-the-one-file-workflow-2-may-not-touch) is already `RULED`, and its own status says what is missing**: *"the ruling needs either a row that owns `lib/auth/server.ts` … and writing rows is Lane C's."* ⚡ **[TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) is that row, and it carries this item's registration with C-240's three controls** — **one row, one file, three instances closed.** ⚠️ **Recorded plainly because the near-miss is the lesson: this office read *OPEN* and prepared a decision package, when the answer was in the item two screens above it.** *(Was:* **`OPEN`**…*)* |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **The screen's *primary control*, not a detail.** ⛔ **Screen `07` is the six-digit code.** ✅ **Everything else on the row is buildable and is being built** |

> ⚡ **This is [C-240](#c-240--two-ruled-or-designed-password-controls-live-in-the-one-file-workflow-2-may-not-touch)'s exact shape, one workflow later, and that is why it is filed rather than absorbed.** **C-240 ① and ② were configuration in `lib/auth/server.ts` that a row forbade; so is this.** ⛔ **The difference is severity: those were a strength rule and a rate limit. This is the control the screen exists for.**

### ⚠️ `otpLength` is not an unchosen security parameter — the design chose it

**QE's cycle-119 account reads: *"registering it means editing the one file [TASK-486](BACKLOG.md) states in terms it does not touch, plus choosing `otpLength` — a security parameter nobody has chosen."*** ✅ **The first half is exactly right and is why [TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) exists. ⛔ The second half is not.**

> ## 📁 **`Fortune Signora Authentication.dc.html`, screen `07`, verbatim: *"Enter the **6-digit** code we sent to m.reinhardt@northwind.com."*** ✅ **`otpLength = 6`.**

⚡ **[D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot the implementation authority, so a value the design states is *decided*, not open** — **and treating it as open is how a decided thing acquires a second decision-maker** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md): *truth has exactly one authoritative representation*).

⚠️ **Recorded because the framing matters more than the number.** ⛔ **An open security parameter is a product-owner decision and would justify waiting. A value the design already carries is a *read*, and waiting on it is the [B-101](BUGS.md) class** — **and this office was one step from making the same error in the other direction, escalating [C-241](#c-241--workflow-3s-approved-screen-needs-the-one-file-its-row-forbids-and-this-is-the-third-instance) as a fresh decision when [C-240](#c-240--two-ruled-or-designed-password-controls-live-in-the-one-file-workflow-2-may-not-touch) was already ruled.**

✅ **Nothing in QE's finding is diminished by this.** **The three refused false affordances — `/join`'s *Request access*, `/sso`'s domain field, and screen `07`'s boxes — are the lane behaving exactly as [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) requires, and the test asserting the boxes' *absence* is the difference between a declared limitation and a discovered one.**

### The contradiction, stated plainly

| | |
|---|---|
| **The design** | **`07 Verify email` — *"Enter the 6-digit code we sent to…"***, six single-character boxes, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, *"paste the whole code and it fills every box"* |
| **[TASK-486](BACKLOG.md)'s Features** | **Repeats it exactly** — *"six single-character boxes · paste fills every box · resend with the doubling timer · a wrong code shows inline and keeps the digits"* |
| ⛔ **[TASK-486](BACKLOG.md)'s own constraint** | ***"Nothing in this row touches `lib/auth/server.ts`, RS256 verification, `requireEmailVerification` or any route."*** **And** *"✅ Zero backend work"* |
| 🔴 **What is actually deployed** | **A link, not a code.** **`lib/auth/server.ts:73` reads `sendVerificationEmail: async ({ user, url })`** — Better Auth mints a token and builds a **URL**; `lib/auth/email.ts`'s `AuthEmail` carries `url` and nothing else. **There is no code to type and no endpoint that would accept one** |

### ✅ The capability exists and is one registration — measured, not assumed

**`better-auth/plugins/email-otp` is present in `node_modules`**, read directly:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Routes it adds** | **`/email-otp/send-verification-otp`** · **`/email-otp/verify-email`** · **`/email-otp/check-verification-otp`** *(plus password-reset and change-email variants)* |
| **How it is configured** | **`emailOTP({ sendVerificationOTP, otpLength, expiresIn })`** in the server's plugin list |
| ⛔ **Where that goes** | **`lib/auth/server.ts`** — **the file this row states it does not touch.** ⚠️ **This item first said *"`otpLength` is a security parameter nobody has chosen"*. ⛔ That was WRONG** — corrected 2026-08-08 by Lane C and **verified here against the design: *"Enter the 6-digit code"*, and its `otp` array has six members.** **So `otpLength: 6` is a *read*, not a decision** ([D-138](../CLAUDE.md) makes the snapshot the implementation authority). ⚡ **The framing mattered more than the number**: an open security parameter is a product-owner decision and justifies waiting; **a value the design already carries is a read, and waiting on it is the [B-101](BUGS.md) class** — this lane nearly blocked on something already answered. ✅ **What is genuinely unstated is `expiresIn`** — screen `08`'s *"expires in 30 minutes"* is the reset **link**, not this code |
| ⚠️ **And it changes the port** | **`AuthEmail` carries `url`.** **An OTP is not a URL** — the port gains a variant, which is `lib/auth/email.ts`, in budget, **but pointless until the plugin exists** |

### ⛔ What this lane built instead, and why it is not the six boxes

**Six boxes wired to nothing is a false affordance** — the rule this lane already applied twice: **`/join`'s *Request access* is never offered *"because nothing can grant it"***, and **`/sso`'s domain field is locked with its reason given** rather than accepting input it cannot act on. ⚡ **A control whose outcome cannot depend on its input is worse than its absence**, and a customer typing six digits into a screen that cannot check them is the strongest version of that failure: **it looks like it worked right up until it does not.**

✅ **So the screen is rebuilt to the design for the flow that exists** — the link — **and the six boxes are not drawn.** **The resend, its timer, the inline failure and the visual language are all real and all shipped.**

### The decision, in one sentence

> **Does Signora verify email by a link or by a six-digit code?** ⚡ **The design says a code; the platform ships a link; the plugin that closes the gap is installed and unregistered.** ⛔ **Registering it is one line and a chosen `otpLength`, and it needs a row that may touch `lib/auth/server.ts`** — **which is the same row [C-240](#c-240--two-ruled-or-designed-password-controls-live-in-the-one-file-workflow-2-may-not-touch)'s three ruled items have been waiting for.**

## C-251 · The Signal Center's queue rows need five facts and the published contract carries two

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **holding [TASK-439](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **after the L-1 reuse audit and before writing a line**, which is the same point [C-229](#c-229) was raised from |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **the gap is a planning one, not an implementation one.** The row's `Delivers` names fields the contract this office released does not carry, **and the contract is correct for what it was asked to do** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — ⛔ **not a missing capability and not a design question** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-09. [TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md) is the row.** 🔴 **AND THE ANSWER IS SMALLER THAN THE QUESTION: both facts already exist on the domain object.** 📁 **`domain/signal.py:81` carries `rationale: str`, whose own comment is the design's sentence — *"why this matters HERE, and what it rests on… so the interpretation a customer reads and the evidence an auditor checks cannot diverge"* — and `:64` carries `relevance`.** ⛔ **`QueueEntryResponse` publishes neither.** ✅ **It is a two-field contract widening, not a capability** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **[TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md) closes it and is claimable today.** ⚠️ **What it changed is what the finished screen shows** — two of the design's five row fields will be absent, and a reviewer holding the design should see that as reported rather than as an omission |

### The five the design draws, and where each comes from

**§ *the queue* draws every row as** `{{ s.title }}` · `{{ s.type }}` · `{{ s.summary }}` · `{{ s.account }}` · `{{ s.pips }}`.

| Field | Source | |
|---|---|---|
| **title** | ✅ `useSignalCatalog` — `SignalTypeName.title` | **Exactly as the architecture intends**: *"`signal_type` is a catalog key and never a title… the key travels and `useSignalCatalog` supplies the words"* |
| **type** | ✅ `QueueEntry.signal_type` | |
| **account** | ✅ `AccountIdentity.name` from `entity_id` | ⚠️ **Nullable by design** — *"`name` is null when nobody has named the account"* |
| **summary** | ⛔ **Nothing** | The catalog carries `why_it_matters`, and its own comment says that is **a fact about the *type*, true before any account exhibits it.** ⛔ **Rendering it per row would state a general truth as this signal's finding** |
| **confidence** | ⛔ **Nothing** | **The string `confidence` does not appear in `lib/api/types.ts` at all.** ⚡ **`components/ui/confidence.tsx` exists and is imported by nothing** — a primitive built for a fact the platform does not yet publish |

### ⛔ What this lane will not do about it

**It will not render `why_it_matters` as the summary.** ⚠️ **It would look right and be wrong on every row**: the same sentence under fifty different signals of one type, presented where the design puts *"the objection came from the economic buyer…"* — **a per-instance finding.** ⛔ **[§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s class**: a screen that reads as informative while saying nothing specific.

**It will not invent a confidence number.** 📁 The design prints *"6 sources · confidence 4 of 5"*, and **both halves are measurements.** ⛔ **[D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ — *real tokens, real URLs, real expiry* — is the same rule one layer up: a pip count nobody computed is a fabricated measurement**, and it would be read as one the pipeline made.

✅ **So both are absent rather than drawn empty or drawn locked**, which is [C-248](#c-248)'s precedent on screen `01`: *"ships with the fields that are real, and the ones with no source are absent rather than drawn locked."*

### ⚡ What is actually being asked for

**Not an endpoint** — this lane is not specifying one. **The question is which module owns each fact:**

**①** **A per-signal summary** — is that `ai_reasoning_engine`'s (the *Why this matters* prose the design shows below it), or a field the signal itself carries? ⚠️ **The design puts a summary in the ROW and a fuller explanation in the DETAIL, so they may be two different things.**
**②** **Confidence** — the design shows it in two places at once, *"6 sources · confidence 4 of 5"*. **`components/ui/confidence.tsx` already takes exactly `level` and `sources`**, so the shape is settled and only the source is not.

> ⚡ **Neither is urgent and this row says so.** **The queue is useful without them** — a seller sees what is waiting, on which account, and every item leaves by a decision. **These two make it faster to triage, not possible to.**

## C-1422 · The finalized design labels the search field with the combined brand, and the brand rule forbids it there

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-10, completing the App Shell forensic audit (§21 Accessibility) |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner** — ⛔ **two ratified authorities disagree and neither can yield to the other without a ruling** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **DESIGN ↔ GOVERNANCE CONFLICT.** ⛔ **Not an implementation defect** — the implementation follows the design exactly |
| **Status** | ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-11. APPROVED: the brand rule wins — `Search Signora`.** ⚡ **Implementation is [TASK-1466](BACKLOG.md), `READY`.** ⚠️ **The design-copy discrepancy is recorded for the next refresh and is explicitly *not a blocker*** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **No lane is waiting**, and this must not stop shell work |

### The conflict, in two sentences

📁 **The finalized design, App Shell §21 `landmarks`:** *"`search` — The top-bar field, labelled **“Search Fortune Signora”**."*

📁 **[`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md), ratified 2026-08-04:** *"**Wherever the product speaks** — the assistant, notifications, emails, tooltips, help, empty states, system messages, **UI copy** — it is `Signora`, alone."* ⚡ ***"Once the application is open, the experience belongs to Signora."***

⛔ **`top-bar.tsx`:120 renders `aria-label="Search Fortune Signora"`.** **An accessible label inside the authenticated application is the product speaking**, not a branding surface — 🔴 **and a screen-reader user is then the only customer who hears the combined brand in-product**, which is the outcome [ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) exists to prevent.

### ⚠️ A second, separate finding — [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) states something untrue about the repository

📁 **The brand section asserts:** *"The inventory is [421](architecture/421-product-naming-inventory.md), and it is empty: `git grep "Fortune Signora"` returns zero matches."*

⛔ **It returns 79.** ✅ **Measured 2026-08-10 across `frontend/` and `backend/`.**

⚡ **Most are legitimate and the rule permits them** — the sign-in masthead, the welcome title, and the `<title>` of `maintenance.html` and `outage.html` are **branding surfaces by the rule's own list.** ⛔ **But the literal claim is false**, and [§2](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit that the repository must not assert something untrue of itself. **`CLAUDE.md` is the product owner's file and this office does not edit it** — recorded here instead.

### The options

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** ✅ **RECOMMENDED** | **The brand rule wins; the label becomes `Search Signora`** | ⚡ **The rule is newer (2026-08-04) and names *UI copy* explicitly.** 📁 The design predates it, and **[D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot the *implementation* authority — not an authority over governance.** ⛔ **One-word change, one test line** |
| **B** | **The design wins; the label stays** | ⚠️ Requires amending the brand rule to exempt accessible labels — ⛔ **which would mean the only customer hearing the combined brand in-product is a screen-reader user** |
| **C** | **Refresh the design so §21 reads `Search Signora`** | ⛔ **[D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md): a refresh is Product Office retrieving a new upstream package, not an edit.** ⚡ Correct long-term, slower than A, and **A is what the repository would do in the meantime anyway** |

⚡ **A and C are not exclusive** — **A now, C at the next refresh**, and the snapshot stops disagreeing with governance.

### ⛔ What this office did NOT do

⛔ **Did not change the label.** 📁 **[§18 of the audit directive](../CLAUDE.md): *"If the finalized design is ambiguous, report the ambiguity. Do not redesign it."*** ⚡ **This is sharper than ambiguity — it is two ratified authorities disagreeing — and neither is Lane C's to overrule.**

## C-269 · Nine of the rail's eleven entries have no destination, and the file's own history says what that costs

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **on claiming [TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **measured before writing a line, which is what the row's own REBUILD framing invites** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **this is row scope, and only the office that writes rows changes one.** ⚡ **The same boundary [C-259](#c-259) was answered on** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **SEQUENCING.** ⛔ **Not a design defect and not an implementation defect** — the design is right about where the product is going, and the rail is right that it cannot go there yet |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10.** ⚡ **The rail entry belongs to the destination's slice — see the resolution below** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **[TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md) entirely.** ⚡ **Not [TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md)**, whose five slots are controls and panels rather than destinations — 📁 *"opens a 400px panel not a page"* — **so it is claimed and proceeding** |

### 🔴 The measurement

📁 **The design draws thirteen entries** — ten in `navItems` (eight primary, two sub under Accounts) and three in `railUtility`. ⛔ **Two of them have a route that exists.**

| Design entry | Route | Exists? |
|---|---|---|
| **Signals** | `/signals` | ✅ |
| **Settings** | `/settings` | ✅ |
| Home | `/w/:workspace/home` | ⛔ **held on [C-268](#c-268)** |
| Forecast · Pipeline · Deals · Conversations · Reports | — | ⛔ **no route** |
| Accounts | `/accounts` | ⛔ **no index — only `/accounts/[accountId]`** |
| Enterprise · Mid-market | — | ⛔ **no route** |
| Shortcuts · Docs & support | — | ⛔ **no route** |

⚠️ **And the two entries the product ships that DO work — `/` (Attention) and `/business` — appear nowhere in the design.** ⛔ **So a literal rebuild removes two working destinations and adds nine that 404.**

### ⛔ The file already knows what that costs, in its own words

📁 **`navigation.tsx`'s own comment, recording why D38 cut six entries to two:**

> ***"And an entry that leads nowhere advertises absence: three of six said *coming soon* on the screen a customer sees first."***

⚡ **Nine of eleven is not three of six.** 🔴 **The rail D-217 asks for would be the defect D38 removed, at three times the scale, on the first screen a customer sees.**

### ⚠️ What the row measured, and the one thing it did not

✅ **[TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)'s measurement is correct and this item does not dispute it**: the design draws eleven, `navigation.tsx:68–70` ships three, and not one of the three appears in the design. ✅ **[D-128](DECISION_REGISTER.md) is right that historical UI is not the authority.**

⛔ **What is not in the row is whether the destinations exist.** ⚡ **They do not, and that changes what a rebuild can mean** — the row reads as *make the rail match the design*, and the honest options are all narrower than that.

### ✅ RESOLVED — Lane C, 2026-08-10. **The rule is derived, so nobody has to decide it**

> ## **A rail entry exists when its destination exists. Never before, never after.**

⚡ **This is not a new decision. It is [D38](../architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) and [§2](../CLAUDE.md) stated as a standing rule instead of re-argued per entry:** 📁 ***"an entry that leads nowhere advertises absence"*** — and a control that does nothing is the decorative class. ⛔ **Nine 404s would be that defect at three times the scale, on the first screen a customer sees.**

#### ⚡ The mechanism, and it is the whole resolution

> **The rail entry belongs to the slice that builds the destination — not to a navigation task.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Reports lands** | **That slice adds `Reports` to `navItems`.** 📁 Lane A already met this: `reachability.py` refused `/reports` with *"no entrance at all: 1"*, and the entrance shipped with the route |
| ✅ **Companies lands** | That slice adds `Accounts`, and its two sub-entries when the segments exist |
| ⛔ **No slice** | **No entry.** The rail is never *"prepared"* for a destination |

⚡ **So C-269 can never recur.** ⛔ **A rail that is one task's responsibility drifts from the routes every time; a rail each destination extends cannot** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md): behaviour exists exactly once).

#### ⚠️ `Attention` and `Your business` stay, and this is the part that needed stating

📁 **Both work, and neither appears in the design.** ⛔ **[D-128](DECISION_REGISTER.md) is right that historical UI is not the authority — and removing a working destination whose designed replacement does not exist is the D38 defect inverted.** ⚡ **They are retired by the arrival of what supersedes them** — `Attention` by the Executive Dashboard, `Your business` by Companies — **each in that destination's own slice, which is the same rule.**

#### ⛔ What this does NOT license

⛔ **It is not permission to ship a rail entry beside an empty route.** 📁 A destination *exists* when a customer can complete something there — **not when a file returns 200.** ⚡ **[§19](../CLAUDE.md)'s demonstrability test decides it, unchanged.**

#### ✅ Where the remaining eleven actually sit

⚡ **They are not a navigation problem at all — they are the workflow audit's, and each is already tracked**: **Reports** [TASK-1417](BACKLOG.md) *(in flight)* · **Companies/Accounts index** · **Executive Dashboard** · **Deals · Conversations · Forecast · Pipeline** · **Shortcuts** [TASK-1458](BACKLOG.md) · **Docs & support** ✅ *ships today*. ⛔ **No new task is created here** — creating one would make the rail somebody's project again, which is what this rule removes.

| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10.** ⛔ **Answered by the repository** ([D38](../architecture/39-product-review-findings.md) + [§2](../CLAUDE.md)), **not escalated**: the rule was already implied by two rulings and only needed saying once |

### ⏸️ What Lane A recommended *(retained — the resolution above adopts its reasoning)*


⛔ **A recommendation, not a decision** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

**①** ⚡ **Ship the design's STRUCTURE now and its ENTRIES as their destinations arrive** — the hierarchy with indented sub-entries, the pinned utility group behind its rule, the *Ask Signora* row with `⌘K`, the count slot. **All of that is buildable and none of it needs a destination.** **Populate it with the entries that resolve, and let each new screen add its own row.**

**②** ⛔ **Do not render an entry to a route that does not exist**, in any form — not disabled, not *coming soon*, not hidden-but-present. 📁 **[C-248](#c-248)'s precedent and the D38 comment agree.**

**③** ⚠️ **The count slot needs real reads.** 📁 The design shows `8,412`, `312`, `1,140`, `14` — **placeholder data.** ⛔ **[§20c](../CLAUDE.md) forbids mock business data**, so a count renders only where something publishes it, and absent otherwise.

**④** ⚡ **`/accounts` having no index is worth a row of its own** — the design's Accounts entry needs one, and the detail route alone cannot serve a nav destination.

## C-268 · Home's route has no permitted entrance, and three of its four compositions have no data

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **while implementing [TASK-1405](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **both halves found by building, not by planning** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **the row's scope is Product Office's to settle**, and the second half is a contract question for whichever module owns a person's role |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **① is a SEQUENCING collision between two rules that are each correct.** **② is MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The ROUTE half of [TASK-1405](BACKLOG.md).** ✅ **The composition resolver is DELIVERED and green** — it encodes no assumption about either question |

### 🔴 ① The route cannot land, because the row ships a surface the gate forbids

📁 **TASK-1405 delivers *"the single route `/w/:workspace/home`"* and states, in its own Manual review gate cell: ✅ *"n/a — no customer surface. ⛔ Stated rather than skipped."***

⛔ **The repository forbids exactly that.** 📁 `frontend/tests/components/reachability.test.tsx` asserts **`No entrance at all — 0`**, and it is a test rather than an advisory: **creating the route turns that 0 into a 1 and the suite goes red.** ⚡ **Measured**: `python3 infra/reachability.py` → `✗ /w/[workspace]/home`.

**Both rules are right.** ⚡ **A slot with no cards genuinely has no customer surface yet**, and ⛔ **a route nobody can reach genuinely is a defect** — *"every one is a defect"*, in the check's own words.

### ⛔ Three exits were tried and each is barred by a rule this lane must not break

| | |
|---|---|
| **Add `Home` to the navigation rail** | ⚡ **Tried, and reverted.** 🔴 **It does not even work**: the scanner reads literal route strings, and Home's href is `workspaceHome(workspaceId)` — **computed, therefore invisible**, so the gate stayed red. ⛔ **And it broke nine passing tests** by making `MobileNavigation` require a `WorkspaceProvider` it never needed. ⚠️ **It is also [TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)'s**, which rebuilds that list wholesale to the design's eleven entries |
| **Declare it in `ENTERED_FROM_OUTSIDE`** | ⛔ **The list is QE's** — 📁 the file says so: *"a judgement, maintained by QE… a list that grows without argument is how a check stops meaning anything."* ⚡ **And the claim would be false**: Home is reached by an in-product redirect, not from outside the product like a reset link |
| **Wire the entry engine's redirect** | ⛔ **[D-205](DECISION_REGISTER.md): the Entry Engine has zero production callers and twelve destinations 404**, and wiring it was explicitly excluded from [TASK-1408](BACKLOG.md) |

✅ **So the route is HELD rather than shipped red.** ⚡ **What the resolver delivers is real and lands today**; the route lands the moment one of the three above is ruled — **and it is one line of `git` when it is.**

⚡ **Whichever way it is ruled, [C-263](#c-263) closes with it**: [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md)'s front door has been blocked because `/w/:ws/home` does not exist, and this is that route.

### 🔴 ② Three of the four compositions have no data, and the near-miss is worth recording

📁 **The design resolves a composition from *"the person's primary role"*** — **CRO, CEO, VP · AE, AM, CSM · RevOps, admin.**

⛔ **The platform publishes no such thing.** **Measured**: `Membership.role` is `'owner' | 'member'` and nothing else; **no persona, job-title or primary-role field exists on any published contract.**

⚠️ **`CommitteeRole` looks like the answer and is not.** It carries titles like *"VP of Revenue Operations"* — ⛔ **but it is a seat at the *customer's* buying committee, a fact about an account Signora tracks, not about the person signed in.** 🔴 **Resolving somebody's Home from it would be reading the wrong company's org chart**, and it is close enough to the right shape that the next lane will consider it.

✅ **`Activation` resolves and the other three do not**, and that asymmetry is the design's own: 📁 its qualifier is ***"Any role, empty workspace"*** — **emptiness is a fact the platform has; role is not.**

### ✅ What Lane A recommends

**①** ⚡ **Rule where Home's entrance comes from** — the rail ([TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)), the front door ([TASK-499](BACKLOG.md)/[C-263](#c-263)), or the engine. ⛔ **Lane A's view is that TASK-1405 and TASK-1439 are not separable in the order the queue has them**, because the design makes Home the rail's first entry and that is the only honest entrance.

**②** **Decide whether a primary role exists at all**, and if so which module publishes it. ⛔ **Until then the resolver returns `Activation` for an unknown person** — *"How do I begin?"* — **which is the only composition that is honest about knowing nothing**, and never a guess from a population statistic.

⛔ **A lane's recommendation is architectural input and never implementation authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)).

## C-267 · TASK-1427's confidence figure has no honest source, and the domain refuses it by name

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, ⚡ **while implementing [TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md)** — 📁 **the row's own instruction**: *"if its shape does not fit, that is a finding against [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md), not a licence to fork"* |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **the row's `Delivers` is Product Office's to correct**, and the mapping it implies is `buying_score_engine`'s to own |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **PLANNING DEFECT, not a missing capability** — **the field the row asks for cannot be derived correctly by anyone** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The confidence half of [TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md) only.** ✅ **The `rationale` half is DELIVERED** — three component tests, one journey, and the two facts the design draws are now four of five |

### 🔴 The row asks for a number the type exists to refuse

📁 **[TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md)'s `Delivers`**: *"Two fields on `QueueEntryResponse` — `rationale`, **and the confidence figure derived from `relevance`**"*.

⛔ **`Relevance` is a four-value `StrEnum` whose own docstring forbids exactly that**, and it names the reason and the owner:

> 📁 ***"A category, declared per workspace and **never computed** — the same discipline as `MatchStrength`, and for the same reason: **a number invites weighting**, weighting invites thresholds, and a threshold here would be a propensity judgement in the wrong module.***
>
> ***The Buying Score Engine maps these to weights in *its* configuration, which is where 'how much does this matter' belongs."***

⚡ **This is [§2](../CLAUDE.md) stated in a type** — *"types should make incorrect architecture impossible"* — **and the constitution cites its sibling by name**: *"`MatchStrength` refuses numeric conversion"*.

### ⛔ And there is no single mapping to derive from, because it is workspace-configurable

**Measured, not argued.** `Relevance → int` exists **exactly once** in the repository:

| | |
|---|---|
| 📁 `buying_score_engine/domain/scoring_model.py:126` | **`relevance_multipliers: dict[Relevance, int]`** — the shipped taxonomy |
| 📁 `buying_score_engine/domain/workspace_model.py:52` | **`ScoringOverrides.relevance_multipliers`** — ⚡ ***"What a workspace has chosen to change"*** |

🔴 **So the same `relevance` legitimately means different weights in two workspaces.** ⛔ **A figure derived in `signal_engine` would be a second, contradicting representation of one fact** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), *"truth has exactly one authoritative representation… a stored copy of a derivable fact is a defect waiting for the two to disagree"* — **and it would put a propensity judgement in the module whose docstring says it does not belong there.**

⚠️ **`IGNORED` has no multiplier at all**, by a validator that says why: 📁 *"it means the hypothesis is not held here at all, so no signal of that type exists to weigh."* **Any total function `Relevance → 1..5` has to invent a value for it.**

### ⛔ A shipped test already asserts the absence, and it was written for this reason

📁 **`frontend/tests/components/signal-queue.test.tsx`**, under [C-251](#c-251):

> **`it('⛔ prints no confidence, because nothing computes one')`** — *"the design prints `6 sources · confidence 4 of 5` — **both halves are MEASUREMENTS**, and `confidence` appears nowhere in the API contract."*

⚡ **Adding the row's figure would have broken a test this lane wrote to prevent precisely that.** ⛔ **The correct response to that test is not to update it.**

### ⚠️ Third finding: the primitive cannot render absence, which is TASK-1411's own rule

📁 **[TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md) requires**: *"A signal with no confidence renders absence, never `0 of 5` — `0 of 5` reads as **certainly wrong** where the truth is **not known**."*

⛔ **`components/ui/confidence.tsx` cannot express that.** **`level: number` is REQUIRED, and the clamp is `Math.max(0, …)`** — so the absent case renders the literal string **`Confidence 0 of 5`**, which is the one output the row forbids. ✅ **Reported against [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md) rather than forked**, exactly as the row directs.

### ✅ What Lane A recommends

⚡ **Strike the confidence figure from [TASK-1427](BACKLOG.md)** and let the row close on `rationale`, which is delivered and demonstrably per-signal. **Then decide the question where it actually lives**, and it is not a surface question:

**①** **does a customer-facing confidence exist at all**, given `Relevance` is deliberately categorical and the weighting is `buying_score_engine`'s and per-workspace; **②** **if it does, which module publishes it** — ⛔ **not `signal_engine`, whose domain refuses it**; **③** **and [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md) gains `level?: number` with a designed absence state before any caller renders one.**

⛔ **A lane's recommendation is architectural input and never implementation authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)), **so nothing above is built until it is ruled.**

## C-266 · The AI attribution primitive has three designs and no data — the read TASK-1411 asks for, taken

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, ⚡ **BEFORE claiming [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md)** — 📁 the same order [D-216](DECISION_REGISTER.md) upheld for [C-263](#c-263), and the row's own instruction |
| **Owner** | **Lane C**, and then whichever module owns the fact — ⛔ **a confidence and a source list are `ai_platform`'s and `ai_reasoning_engine`'s to publish, not `product_surface`'s to invent** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — **the design is complete; the contract behind it is not** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **The DATA half of [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md).** ✅ **The component's shape is knowable from the three designs and is not blocked** |

### ✅ This is the row's own first slice, performed rather than assumed

📁 **[TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md) says so in terms**: ⚠️ ***"whether `ai_platform.public` exposes confidence and source provenance is UNVERIFIED and the row says so — the first slice is the read, and if the contract is missing it is raised, not invented"*** ([D-167](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4). **Measured on `origin/integration`:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **`ai_platform/public/`** | ⚡ **Exports the inference port and its vocabulary** — `Infer`, `InferenceInput/Output/Policy`, `ExplanationSource`, `EvidenceFact`, `EvidenceRef`, `EvidenceSet`. ⛔ **No confidence value** |
| **`ai_reasoning_engine/public/`** | ⚠️ **Names confidence in PROSE only** — *"its confidence must carry its basis"* — ⛔ **not an export** |
| **Any interface schema** | ⛔ **The only `confidence` on an endpoint is `workspace_tenancy`'s `confidence_floor`** — ⚡ **a THRESHOLD the customer sets, the opposite of a model's confidence** |
| **`frontend/lib/api/types.ts`** | 🔴 **Zero occurrences.** **Nothing crosses to the frontend** |

### ⚡ Sources are further along than confidence, and the difference matters

✅ **`EvidenceRef`, `EvidenceSet` and `ExplanationSource` exist in `ai_platform`'s contract**, so *"6 sources"* and *"open all evidence"* have a vocabulary to be built on. ⛔ **`3 excluded` does not** — 📁 the row requires the excluded state *"from the start rather than being widened later by the third consumer"*, and nothing publishes an exclusion or its reason.

### 🔴 The one thing the component must never do is the thing an absent contract invites

📁 **The row: *"render a confidence the model did not produce… if `ai_platform` publishes no confidence, this component renders its ABSENCE."*** ⚡ **And its component coverage is sharper still**: ⛔ ***"`N of 5` with no confidence renders absence, never `0 of 5` — `0 of 5` reads as certainly wrong where the truth is not known."***

> ⚠️ **So the safe half is buildable today and the unsafe half is not**: **a component that renders absence correctly can ship before the data exists; one that renders a number cannot.**

### ⚠️ And part of it already exists, which the row does not say

📁 **`components/ui/confidence.tsx` ships `N of 5` with an optional source count**, clamped, with *"never invented"* already in its comments. ⛔ **[TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md) reads as though nothing exists** — ⚡ **the same shape as [C-264](#c-264) and the palette**: **a row describing a destination without checking what the repository already holds.** ✅ **This one is benign** — the existing component is a subset and extending it is the row's intent — **but it is the third instance and the pattern is the finding, not the file.**

### ✅ What this lane recommends

**Split [TASK-1411](BACKLOG.md).** ⚡ **The strip, its absence states, the source disclosure and *Show reasoning* are buildable now against the three designs** — **and are strictly better built once than three times, which is the row's whole argument.** ⛔ **The confidence VALUE and the excluded-source reason wait on whichever module publishes them**, and that is a contract question for `ai_platform` and `ai_reasoning_engine` rather than a surface one.

## C-265 · Step-up is built and the only module whose controls require it is not

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **holding [TASK-1410](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **on reaching the row's Definition of Done and measuring what could satisfy it** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **which control requires a fresh factor is a row's scope, and marking one that the design does not mark is inventing a security requirement** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — ⛔ **the design is complete and unambiguous about where step-up applies** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **One sentence of [TASK-1410](BACKLOG.md)'s Definition of Done.** ✅ **The capability is built, tested and green** |

### ✅ What is delivered

**`session.freshAge = 600`** — 📁 the design's *"step-up lasts 10 minutes"*, against Better Auth's 24-hour default — **`CodeInput` in `components/ui`**, and **`StepUpDialog`**, which names what it is about to authorise. 🔴 **The server-side half the row's Security Invariant demands is configured and guarded**: removing `freshAge` fails three tests, widening it to a day fails two.

### ⛔ What cannot be satisfied

📁 **The row: *"a destructive action cannot complete without one."*** ⚡ **Measured across all twenty-eight screens in the snapshot, exactly one module requires a fresh factor:**

> 📁 **Security Center §02** — ***"Every control in THIS MODULE requires a fresh factor before it will act, even inside a valid session."***

⛔ **The Security Center is workflow 23 and is not built.** ⚠️ **No built screen's design marks a control as requiring step-up.**

**The two other mentions in the snapshot are different capabilities and were checked rather than assumed:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Team Management** | *"he accepts within 48 hours, **re-authenticating through SSO**"* — ⛔ **invitation acceptance through an identity provider, not a fresh factor on a destructive control** |
| **Workspace Setup** | *"switching sends you to a different region, so you **re-authenticate**"* — ⛔ **a region boundary, not step-up** |

### ⛔ Why this lane did not wire it to Team Management's *Remove*

⚡ **`useRemoveMember` exists and is destructive, and it would have been one import.** 📁 **The design does not mark it.** ⛔ **Applying the Security Center's rule to a control the design leaves unmarked is inventing a security requirement** — ⚠️ **and a lane inventing one is the same act as a lane relaxing one, which [§13](../CLAUDE.md) forbids.** **The direction does not make it a lane's to decide.**

### ⚠️ And the snapshot already records this as a known gap

📁 **`Entry Coverage Review`, row `05`**: ***"`/auth/step-up` — authentication covers first sign-in. **Step-up mid-session is unspecified.** … the largest true gap in the audit."*** ⚡ **So the absence of a caller is not an oversight in [TASK-1410](BACKLOG.md); it is a design gap the audit already named**, and this item connects the two rather than re-reporting it.

### ✅ What this lane recommends

**Narrow [TASK-1410](BACKLOG.md) to the capability — which is complete — and sequence the first caller behind whichever row builds a control the design marks.** ⚡ **That is [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s remedy, and the capability is deliberately in `components/ui` and `lib/auth/` so the caller takes it rather than building a second.**
