| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, ⚡ **BEFORE claiming [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md)** — 📁 [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s whole finding is that this class is discovered mid-slice, so this one was looked for first |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **the question is which row creates the workspace-scoped route tree**, and only the office that writes rows answers that |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — ⛔ **nothing is asked of Design; the design already answered the destination** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-09, [D-216](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** ✅ **[TASK-1438](BACKLOG.md) creates `/w/:workspace/home` and is `READY`.** ⚡ **This lane's refusal to create the route inside [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md) is upheld in full, and for the reason it gave**: 📁 **the path is inside the 🟢 budget and it is still not that row's, because pointing the product's links at the engine's scheme IS adopting the engine, which [D-205](DECISION_REGISTER.md) forbids until its destinations exist.** ⛔ **Two of the six route changes stay held until [TASK-1438](BACKLOG.md) lands; the other four were never held and this office is not holding them now** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Two of [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md)'s six route changes.** ✅ **The other four are reachable today and this item does not hold them** |

### ✅ [D-212](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7's gate answered the destination, so it is not asked here

⚠️ **The row says *"the authenticated home needs a new path"* and does not name it, and [D-185](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2 names five paths without naming this one.** ⛔ **That looked like a design question and it is not.**

📁 **[`lib/entry/rules.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts):52, from [TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md):**

```ts
/** `/w/:ws/home`, the one authenticated landing route — §04 *Home is a slot*. */
return `/w/${workspaceId}/home`;
```

✅ **The finalized design decided it and the entry engine already implements it.** ⛔ **So a lane inventing `/home` would be creating a SECOND answer to *where is home* on a customer-visible URL** — [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s two-representations defect, in the one place a customer would notice.

### 🔴 And the route does not exist

```
find frontend/app -type d -name w   → nothing
frontend/app/(app)/  →  /  /accounts/[accountId]  /business  /join/[workspaceId]
                        /profile  /settings…  /signals
```

⛔ **There is no `/w/` tree at all**, which is 📁 [C-1405](#c-1405)'s *"twelve of the engine's destinations do not exist"* — **the same finding that has [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md) BLOCKED.**

### ⚠️ So two of the six changes are blocked and four are not

| Change | |
|---|---|
| `sign-in` → **`/signin`** | ✅ **reachable** |
| `sign-up` → **`/register`** | ✅ **reachable** — 📁 and the [ADR-0034](architecture/adr/0034-ubiquitous-language.md) one: a customer *registers* |
| `verify-email` → **`/verify`** | ✅ **reachable** |
| `reset-password` → **`/reset/:token`** | ✅ **reachable**, and it carries the `better-auth` callback change |
| `forgot-password` | ✅ **already agrees** |
| **`(app)/page.tsx` off `/`** | ⛔ **BLOCKED — nowhere to go** |
| **`welcome` → `/`** | ⛔ **BLOCKED — `/` is still the authenticated home** |

### ⛔ Why this lane will not simply create `/w/:ws/home`

⚡ **It is inside the budget** — 🟢 `frontend/app/**` routes — **and it is still not this row's to do**, for two reasons that both point the same way:

**①** 📁 **[D-205](DECISION_REGISTER.md): the Entry Engine has zero production callers and must not be wired.** ⛔ **Creating `/w/:ws/home` and pointing the product's links at it IS adopting the engine's destination scheme**, which is [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md)'s subject and is blocked on [C-1405](#c-1405).

**②** ⚠️ **Every link that says `/` would need a workspace id.** 📁 **`components/shell/navigation.tsx` has `{ href: '/', label: 'Attention' }`** — **workspace-scoping it is a data requirement at every call site**, not a path edit, and doing that inside a rename slice is how a route change becomes an architecture change nobody reviewed.

### ✅ What this lane recommends

**Narrow [TASK-499](BACKLOG.md) to the four auth renames, which are independently valuable and independently verifiable** — 📁 **the four shipped journeys are its verification and they exercise exactly those paths** — ⛔ **and sequence the front-door swap behind whichever row creates the workspace-scoped home.** ⚡ **That is [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s own remedy applied by the lane before the row was claimed rather than after it was half-built.**

## C-262 · The cold-start screen exists and nothing decides that a cold start has no network

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **delivering [TASK-1436](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **where a boot with no service lands is a ROUTING decision**, and this row's budget is `components/feedback/**` and a small `lib/` helper |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — ⛔ **the design is complete and nothing is asked of Design** |
| **Status** | 🟢 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **One sentence of [TASK-1436](BACKLOG.md)'s Definition of Done.** ✅ **The capability is built, tested and green** |

### ✅ What is delivered

**`NoConnection` renders the design's screen** — 📁 *"No connection · Your device reports no network. Signora's own service is reachable from other regions, so this is almost certainly local."* — with **Check again**, **Status page**, and *"Last connected 3 minutes ago · retrying in 8s"*. ⚡ **It is the ladder's `platform` scope finding its first caller.**

### ⛔ What decides to show it

**Nothing.** 📁 **The Definition of Done says *"cold start with no network shows a designed screen naming when it last worked"*, and *cold start* is the half that has no owner.**

⚠️ **The three places it could live are three different decisions:**

| | ⛔ Why it is not this row's |
|---|---|
| **`app/(app)/layout.tsx`** or a route boundary | ⚡ **A route-level decision about what a failed boot renders**, and the budget names `components/feedback/**` |
| **`app/error.tsx`** | ⛔ **Wrong by measurement**: that is `app` scope, `global-error-boundary`, and it fires on a RENDER failure. **A cold start with no network is not a render failure** — the render succeeds and the data never arrives |
| **A `QueryProvider`-level check** | ⚠️ **`lib/query` is 🔴**, and it would mean the query layer deciding what the whole application shows |

### 🔴 And there is a real question underneath, which is why this is not just a wiring note

⛔ **What distinguishes *"a cold start with no network"* from *"one request failed"*?** ⚡ **[TASK-1435](BACKLOG.md)'s pill already covers the second case** — a working session that lost its connection, with edits queued — **and the design is explicit that these are *"different problem, different screen."***

> 📁 **The design's own line is the test**: ***"There is no cached session to fall back on."*** ⚡ **So the condition is *nothing loaded AND nothing cached*, not *a request failed*.** ⛔ **Getting that wrong in either direction is worse than not mounting it**: too eager and a single failed request replaces a working page with a full-screen outage; too shy and the screen never appears.

### ✅ What this lane recommends

**One row, sequenced now, naming the condition rather than the file** — ⚡ **and it is small**: the condition is expressible from what already exists (`onlineManager`, an empty query cache, a failed initial fetch). ⛔ **This lane did not build it because choosing the condition IS the row**, and a lane picking one inside a component slice is [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s *"'I could just add it' is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision."*

## C-261 · TASK-492's producer instruction rests on a premise that measurement contradicts, and either reading ships a defect

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **holding [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md)**, ⚡ **on trying to wire the first producer the row names** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **the row's instruction, and the architecture record it rests on** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **STALE PREMISE** — **the design is not wrong; the fact it was written against has changed** |
| **Status** | ⚡ **`SPLIT INTO TWO` — Lane C, 2026-08-09, [D-216](DECISION_REGISTER.md), because the two halves have different owners and one of them is not this office's.** ✅ **① THE ROLE-CHANGE PRODUCER IS RULED HERE — neither ① nor ②, and the row's instruction is WITHDRAWN.** 🔴 **② The three authentication producers are a 🔴 architectural question and move to [C-1411](#c-1411--an-audit-stream-whose-reliable-shape-needs-the-frozen-platform-and-whose-cheap-shape-is-lossy), for the product owner.** ⛔ **This item stays `OPEN` until [C-1411](#c-1411--an-audit-stream-whose-reliable-shape-needs-the-frozen-platform-and-whose-cheap-shape-is-lossy) is ruled** |
| ✅ **① THE RULING — `membership_role_change` stays, and `security_event` neither duplicates it nor replaces it** | ⛔ **The row's instruction — *"it becomes this stream's first PRODUCER"* — rested on *"nothing reads it"*, and this lane MEASURED that nothing is now true**: `query_service.py:221` selects it and renders it as `ROLE_CHANGED`. ✅ **Verified independently by this office before ruling.** ⚡ **So both readings the lane offered are correctly rejected, and the third is what [§2](../CLAUDE.md) already requires**: ***"truth has exactly one authoritative representation; everything else derives from it."*** 📁 **`membership_role_change` is the authoritative record and it is TYPED — `previous_role` and `new_role` as `workspace_role` enum columns.** ⛔ **① writes the same fact twice, which the row's own sentence forbids. ② moves a typed fact into an opaque `detail` blob and asks a shipped screen to trust it, which is a contract change AND a downgrade.** ✅ **A role change is therefore NOT a `security_event` write. If the security stream must present role changes, it DERIVES them at read time from the typed table** — ⛔ **and that is a later row, not this one.** ⚡ **[TASK-492](BACKLOG.md) ships its three remaining producers and the role-change producer is struck from it** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The role-change producer only.** ✅ **The table, the domain type, the repository and the `public/` contract are built, tested and green** — this item does not hold them |

### 📁 What the row says

> ⚡ ***"`membership_role_change` already records every role transition and NOTHING READS IT ([495 §6](architecture/495-principal-and-identity-boundary.md)). It becomes this stream's first PRODUCER rather than a second table — ⛔ duplicating it would be [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s two-representations defect inside the security layer."***

### 🔴 Something reads it

```
backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/infrastructure/query_service.py:221
  select(MembershipRoleChangeModel, MembershipModel.member_email, actors.member_email)
  …
  kind=HistoryKind.ROLE_CHANGED
```

⚡ **`organization_history` reads `membership_role_change` and renders it as `ROLE_CHANGED`.** ⛔ **495 §6's *nothing reads it* was true when it was measured and is not true now**, and the row's instruction is built on it.

### ⚠️ Both readings of *"becomes its first producer"* ship a defect

| Reading | What it means | The defect |
|---|---|---|
| **① Write BOTH** | `ChangeRole` records a role change *and* a `security_event` | ⛔ **The same fact in two tables with two readers** — 📁 **precisely the two-representations defect the row's own sentence forbids** |
| **② The stream REPLACES it** | `security_event` becomes the record; `membership_role_change` retires | ⛔ **Breaks `organization_history`'s read path**, which is a live contract with a rendered surface behind it |

> 🔴 **Neither is a lane's to choose.** ⚡ **① knowingly introduces the defect the row names in the same sentence that names the work.** ⛔ **② changes what a shipped screen reads, which is a contract change** (§20e) — **and it is not a small one: the two carry different shapes.** 📁 **`membership_role_change` is TYPED — `previous_role` and `new_role` as `workspace_role` enum columns — and a `security_event` carries them as opaque `detail`, so ② moves a typed fact into a JSON blob and asks the history screen to trust it.**

### ✅ What this lane built anyway, and why the item blocks none of it

⛔ **The stream is not held on this question.** ✅ **Delivered and green**: the table (`0046`, append-only, forced RLS, classified in both lists), the `SecurityEvent` domain type, `SqlAlchemySecurityEventLog`, and `SecurityEventWriter` through `public/`. **401 Security Invariants, 29 domain tests, `mypy --strict` clean, 37 import contracts kept.**

⚡ **And the three OTHER producers the row names have a DIFFERENT problem** — 📁 **sign-in, sign-out and password reset are authentication facts that NO existing table records**, which is the gap the row opens with: *"Workflow 1 is producing authentication facts on `main` today and nothing records them."*

> 🔴 **CORRECTION, 2026-08-09, by the lane that wrote the sentence this replaces.** ⛔ **I first recorded these as blocked by BUDGET — *"reaching this stream needs an endpoint and a `Resource`, which is more than this row's 🟠 grant."* That is wrong.** 📁 **The Change Budget grants *a new endpoint* at 🟠 and this module's `interface/` at 🟢**, and the [`queues/lane-a.toml`](coordination/queues/lane-a.toml) banner on [B-214](BUGS.md) already settled the general point: ⚡ ***"a budget line names what the SLICE touches. It does not narrow the tier your module already grants you."*** ✅ **Adding a `Resource` member is a declarative registration and explicitly permitted** ([§20a](../CLAUDE.md), [C-224](#c-224)). **Budget does not block them.**

### 🔴 What actually blocks them, and it is worth more than the budget answer was

📁 **[493](architecture/493-security-platform-architecture.md) names the producer** — *"Workflow 1 (Login) — already producing them"* — ⛔ **and specifies nothing about how a fact born in the Better Auth tier reaches a table Python owns.**

⚠️ **The two available shapes are not equivalent, and the row's own argument rules out the easy one:**

| | How | Why it fails |
|---|---|---|
| **① The client reports it** | Next.js calls a new endpoint after Better Auth mints the token | ⛔ **A best-effort client call is a LOSSY audit path**, and it drops events exactly when something went wrong — ⚡ **which is the population an audit stream exists for.** 📁 **The row's whole argument is *"the record cannot be added retroactively"***; a stream with holes is the same failure arriving quietly |
| **② The server records it** | The API records on first verification of a new session | ✅ **Reliable, and no client can forget.** ⛔ **But telling a NEW session from a continuing one lives in `signora_platform/auth/`, which is 🔴 and frozen** ([§20a](../CLAUDE.md)) |

> ⚡ **So the honest position is not *"nearly done"*.** ⛔ **The reliable shape needs a frozen-platform change and the cheap shape is lossy by construction** — **and a lane choosing between those has made an architectural decision inside a feature slice**, which [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) names by hand: *"'I could just add it' is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision."*

### ✅ What this lane recommends

**Rule ② — the stream replaces it — but as its own row, sequenced, with the typing question answered rather than assumed.** ⚡ **`organization_history` is the only reader and it needs `previous_role` and `new_role`**; ⛔ **if those become `detail` keys, the screen is reading untyped JSON and the enum stops being enforced anywhere.** ✅ **That is worth deciding on purpose, and it is the same shape as [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s finding: a row scoped to the destination rather than to the step.**

⚠️ **Until then [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md) delivers the stream and NOT the role-change producer**, and the row's `Delivers` should say so rather than being quietly under-met.

## C-260 · `make product-demo-record` needs one `HEADLESS=1`, and the `Makefile` is not this lane's

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **implementing [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **the row predicted this item by name and told this lane to raise it rather than take a second claim** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — 📁 **`platform_foundation`, [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml).** ⛔ **The `Makefile` e2e targets are not Lane A's**, and [TASK-476](BACKLOG.md)'s Module row says so: ⚠️ ***"the `Makefile` e2e targets are `platform_foundation`'s and stay Lane C's — one line naming the mode explicitly… Lane C supplies it on request rather than as a second claim."*** ✅ **This is that request** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — **one line, no design, no ruling** |
| **Status** | 🟢 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚡ **[TASK-476](BACKLOG.md) is complete and green without it** — this is a consequence to close, not a dependency to wait on |

### ⚡ The one line

```make
product-demo-record:
	… cd ../frontend && HEADLESS=1 SIGNORA_APP_URL=$(E2E_URL) npx playwright test --project=demo …
```

### ⚠️ What changed under it, measured

📁 **[TASK-476](BACKLOG.md) inverts the Playwright default: headed unless somebody opts out.** ⛔ **`product-demo-record` sets neither flag, so it was headless by accident of the old default and is now headed.**

| Target | Before | After | Correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `make product-demo` | **headed** (`HEADED=1`) | **headed** | ✅ **unchanged, and it sets the flag** |
| `make product-demo-record` | **headless** | ⚠️ **headed** | ⛔ **wants the line above** |
| `make e2e` · `e2e-quick` · `e2e-smoke` | headless | ✅ **headed** | ✅ **the point of the row** |

⚡ **It still records.** **`video: 'on'` and `trace: 'on'` are the `demo` project's, not the mode's**, so the artifact this target exists for is produced either way. ⛔ **What it loses is running unattended** — a recording on a machine with no display cannot launch a window.

### ⛔ Why the config cannot fix it here

**Both targets run `--project=demo`.** ⚡ **A project-level `headless` override would apply to both, so it cannot separate *watch it* from *record it*** — 📁 **and the row already named the distinction: *"which command was run, not where."*** ✅ **Which command was run is knowable only in the `Makefile`.**

```
grep -rl CommandPalette frontend/app frontend/components --include=*.tsx | grep -v tests
→ components/ui/command-palette.tsx        (its own definition, and nothing else)
```

📁 **[D-214](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §8 is right on the fact and right to record it on both candidate callers.** ⛔ **Nothing below disputes the finding.**

frontend/components/intelligence/account-search.tsx:72
  if (event.key.toLowerCase() !== 'k' || !(event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey)) return;

> ⛔ **The clause is not wrong; it is stale.** **[TASK-481](BACKLOG.md) was scoped to a repository that had no shell, and that repository no longer exists.**

## C-258 · Two of `StatedAbsence`'s thirteen callers cannot render at region scope, and the ladder is what is short

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **holding [TASK-1428](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **found by measuring the thirteen call sites before composing, which is what the row asked for** |
| **Owner** | **Design Authority** — ⛔ **the gap is in the ladder, and [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)'s row says so in advance**: *"if its region scope will not carry `StatedAbsence`'s sentence, that is a finding against the ladder, not a licence to keep two."* ✅ **This is that finding, taken at its word** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | 🔴 **INCOMPLETE DESIGN** — **the scope ladder has no page-scope failure state, and no way to say a region failure interrupted something** |
| **Status** | 🔴 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-09 |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Five of thirteen call sites.** ✅ **The other eight compose cleanly and this lane will build them** |

### ✅ Eleven of thirteen are exactly what the ruling describes

**`as='card'` and `as='inline'` with the default polite announcement render a sentence in a region.** ✅ **`SystemState` at `scope="region"` carries all of it** — `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, the sentence as the description. ⛔ **No reword, no signature change, no caller touched.**

### 🔴 ① Four callers use `as="page"`, and page scope has no failure state

**Callers**: [`app/(app)/page.tsx:649`](../frontend/app/(app)/page.tsx) · [`accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx:591`](../frontend/app/(app)/accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx) · [`settings/organization/page.tsx:100`](../frontend/app/(app)/settings/organization/page.tsx) · [`business/page.tsx:119`](../frontend/app/(app)/business/page.tsx).

📁 **The ladder's page scope owns `404 · 403 · feature-not-enabled · permission-required`.** ⛔ **All four are REFUSALS. None of them is *"the query behind this screen failed."*** ⚡ **The design's own page-scope test is *"the primary record or query failed, **or** the person may not see it at all"* — the sentence names both, and only the second half has states.**

⚠️ **Today those four render `EmptyState`** — ⛔ **which is the absence primitive drawing a failure**, and precisely the conflation [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md) was written to end. **The row is right that it must stop; the ladder has nowhere for it to go.**

⛔ **This lane will not invent a page-scope state.** **Adding one to `LEGAL_STATES` is amending the design in code**, and 📁 **shell rule 14's principle applies**: *"every new capability is an amendment to this document, not a local decision."*

### 🔴 ② One caller announces assertively, and scope-derived politeness cannot express it

📁 **[TASK-1428](BACKLOG.md) says *"politeness comes from the scope and never from the caller"*** — ✅ **and `SystemState` already works that way, correctly.** ⛔ **But [`components/commercial/segments.tsx:104`](../frontend/components/commercial/segments.tsx) passes `announce="assertive"`, and [`tests/components/segments.test.tsx:136`](../frontend/tests/components/segments.test.tsx) asserts `getByRole('alert')`.**

🔴 **Composing as instructed makes that test fail, and making it pass by editing the assertion would be the defect.** 📁 **`stated-absence.tsx`'s own comment records why the prop exists**: *"Added because removing it was a regression. `segments.tsx` used `role='alert'` and a test asserted it; folding nine implementations into one would have quietly dropped that, and §20c calls an accessibility loss a defect rather than a trade-off."*

⚡ **Both rules are right and they disagree.** 📁 **The ladder's `4.1.3`**: *"only a state that ends the session announces assertively."* 📁 **`StatedAbsence`'s case**: *"a failure that interrupted something the customer had just done"* — **which is not a session-ending state and is still worth interrupting for.**

### ✅ What this lane proposes, and it is input rather than authority

**①** **A page-scope failure state** — the ladder's page scope gains one member for *"the query behind this screen failed"*, distinct from the four refusals. ⚡ **The design already implies it in its own `when` sentence.**
**②** **Either** the ladder admits *"interrupted the customer's own action"* as a second assertive trigger, **or** [`segments.tsx`](../frontend/components/commercial/segments.tsx) is ruled to have been wrong and its test changes with a stated reason. ⛔ **Not silently, and not by this lane.**

✅ **Meanwhile the eight clean callers get composed and the row moves.**

### 📁 The row promises six regions in a fixed order

> 🔴 **AMENDED 2026-08-09 by the lane that raised it, and the amendment is against this item's own method.** ⛔ **The table above measured the row's SIX REGIONS and stopped there. Shell rule 7 — *"anything clickable is reachable in the palette"* — is also this row's acceptance criteria** ([D-210](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) **and it was not measured, because a palette is an overlay rather than a region.**

### 🔴 Why the last two are different from the first two

⚡ **The banners and the breadcrumb are complete components waiting for content.** **Placing them in the frame costs nothing and they render nothing** — that is 📁 *"delivers the frame, not its contents"* working as intended.

⛔ **The filter strip and the utility panel are not like that.**

**The filter strip** would render four chips that serialise scope into the URL — 📁 *"period, region, segment, owner… serialised in the URL"* — ⛔ **and no module reads scope.** **A visible control that changes a URL nothing consults is a control that does nothing** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)), and it is worse than absent: **a seller who sets the period to Q3 and sees every figure unchanged learns the filter is broken**, which is a harder belief to undo than a missing feature. ⚡ **[`lib/shell/scope.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/scope.ts) ships the narrowing law so the first consuming module inherits it** — **the law is the deliverable here; the strip is not.**

**The utility panel** is 📁 *"300px at 1280, 360px at 1600+… docks right of content and pushes it"* with tabs **Insights · Activity · Notes**. ⛔ **All three are module content and none exists.** **An empty 300px panel does not reserve space for a later row — it takes a third of the content region away from every screen that ships today.**

### ✅ What this lane recommends

**Narrow [TASK-1408](BACKLOG.md) to what a frame row can own**: ✅ **the constitution · the region laws · the rail · the banner and breadcrumb slots**, and ⛔ **move the filter strip and utility panel to rows sequenced behind their first consumer** — **which is the same shape [D-209](DECISION_REGISTER.md) counted six times: *"wait on another TASK, which a lane clears without anybody ruling on anything."***

⚠️ **This is the third row whose `Delivers` exceeds what any row builds** — [C-255](#c-255) on §04, [C-256](#c-256) on the banners, and now this. ⚡ **The pattern is worth a look by the office that writes them**: **each design document is complete and correct, and the rows are scoped to the DOCUMENT rather than to what is reachable from the current repository.** ⛔ **Not a criticism of any single row** — [TASK-1408](BACKLOG.md) is the best-specified row this lane has held — **but three in one workflow is a method signal rather than three coincidences.**

Okafor.** Support session · expires in 42 minutes · every action is logged."* ⚡ **It is drawn at RISK severity and is the one banner the design makes undismissable** — **this lane built that rule and tested it**, because it is the sentence that stops somebody believing they are themselves.

No API publishes it, and `Membership` carries no notion of acting-as.** ⚠️ **A support session that expires, is logged and can be ended is a security capability with an audit trail** — **not a banner** — **and the banner is the only place the product currently admits it exists.**

⛔ **This lane will not infer it.** ⚡ **Guessing the shape of an impersonation capability from the sentence on its banner is inventing a security feature backwards from its warning label**, and [§13](../CLAUDE.md) puts authentication and authorization out of a lane's reach entirely.

## C-255 · TASK-1409's `Delivers` names §04, and §04 needs three capabilities no row owns

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **holding [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **measured against the code before building, and against the backlog before raising** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **a scope and sequencing question.** **A row's `Delivers` names more than any row builds, and only the office that writes rows can resolve that** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING CAPABILITY** — ⛔ **and explicitly NOT a design question** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-09, [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md).** ⚡ **This lane was right on every measurement and right about the addressee.** ✅ **[TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)'s `What it delivers` no longer names §04**, and **the three capabilities are three `READY` rows** — **[TASK-1435](BACKLOG.md)** the offline mutation queue · **[TASK-1436](BACKLOG.md)** last-connected and a re-checking retry · **[TASK-1437](BACKLOG.md)** the static maintenance pages. ⛔ **Nothing is deferred; the work is addressed and none of it is [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)'s.** 🔴 **The defect was this office's row-writing, not this lane's reading — see [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md)** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **§04 only** — three states of [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md). ✅ **§01's ladder, `SystemState` and `CopyableId` are delivered and green** |

### ✅ [D-212](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7's gate was applied BEFORE filing, and it is why this is not a clarification

⛔ **The gate**: *"can this be answered by an existing finalized design document? If yes, implementation proceeds and NOTHING is raised."*

✅ **The design answers it completely, and that is precisely the point.** 📁 **§04 specifies the behaviour**: *"two edits are queued… They are sent in order when the connection returns — **the queue is visible, not implied**"*, *"last connected 3 minutes ago"*, and *"maintenance and platform outage pages are **served from static hosting with no dependency on the application, its API or its session**."*

⚡ **So nothing is being asked of Design.** **What is being reported is that the three capabilities those sentences require are not built and no row builds them.**

⚠️ **This lane raised [C-253](#c-253) the other way round last cycle** — filed first, gated after, and the gate changed the answer. **Applied first this time**, and it changed the *addressee* rather than the answer: **Lane C, not the Design Authority.**

### 🔴 Measured, not assumed

| §04 state | What the design requires | Present on `origin/integration` |
|---|---|---|
| **Offline banner** | **An offline mutation queue** — visible, ordered, replayed on reconnect | ⛔ **Nothing.** No `onlineManager`, no `resumePausedMutations`, no `networkMode`, no query persistence anywhere in `lib/` |
| **No internet · cold start** | **Last successful connection time**, and a retry that **re-checks** rather than reloading | ⛔ **Nothing persists a last-connected time**, and there is no offline detection in the codebase at all |
| **Maintenance · platform** | **Static hosting, no dependency on the app, its API or its session** | ⛔ **There is no `frontend/public/` directory** — no static surface exists to serve it from |

**And the backlog was searched before this was written**: ⛔ **`offline`, `mutation queue`, `static hosting`, `maintenance page` and `no internet` match no row's scope**, and 📁 [`workflows.toml`](coordination/workflows.toml) has no workflow for any of them. **The only hit is [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)'s own `Delivers` line, which is the row promising them.**

### ⛔ What this lane will not do

**Render a queue that does not exist.** 📁 **§04's own rules forbid it** — *"**No fabrication.** Never show stale figures as current, never generate sample data to fill an empty screen, never claim a save that has not completed."* ⚡ **A banner reading *"two edits are queued"* over no queue is the third of those**, and it is the one that would cost a customer real work.

**Ship the banner without the queue and call §04 done.** ⚠️ **A banner that says only *"you are offline"* is a materially weaker screen than the approved one**, and 📁 the design is explicit that the offline state is *"a banner, not takeover"* **because Signora keeps working** — **without the queue there is nothing for it to keep working on.** ⛔ **Changing what an approved screen does is not a lane's call** ([D-158](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7).

**Put the maintenance page inside the Next application.** ⛔ **That violates the one rule that defines the state** — it must survive the application being down.

### ✅ What would resolve it

**Any of these, and the choice is Lane C's:** **①** rows for the offline queue and the static surface, sequenced ahead of §04 · **②** §04 narrowed out of [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md) into its own row behind them · **③** a ruling that the reduced offline banner is acceptable, which is a design change and therefore not Lane C's alone. ⚡ **② is the smallest and this lane recommends it** — **the ladder is what thirteen workflows are waiting for, and it should not wait on an offline queue.**

| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — ⚠️ **filed as MISSING CAPABILITY and corrected.** **The capability is designed; it is not built yet** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — raised 2026-08-09, and NARROWED BY THIS LANE THE SAME DAY.** ⛔ **No ruling is needed; a sequence is** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **The `403` state only**, and it is **sequenced behind the effective-permissions model** rather than waiting on anybody. ✅ **Every other state in the row is unaffected** |

### ⚠️ This item was filed wrong, and [D-212](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7 is what caught it

**The gate**: ⛔ ***"can this be answered by an existing finalized design document? If yes, implementation proceeds and NOTHING is raised."*** ⚡ **This lane filed the item first and applied the gate afterwards, which is the wrong order** — and applying it changed the answer.

🔴 **`Fortune Signora Team Management.dc.html` specifies the model**: 📁 **an *Effective permissions* surface where *"every line names where it comes from"*, each row carrying `level` and `source`** — 📁 *"nobody knows what a role actually permits until something leaks. This module answers each one directly."*

✅ **So the product IS designed to know which role grants what, and where the grant came from.** ⛔ **The measurement in this item stands** — `ApiError` carries no authorization detail today — **but the conclusion drawn from it did not.** ⚠️ **The original framing asked the Design Authority *whether the screen ships without the role name*, which is a question the design had already answered: it ships WITH it, once the model exists.**

**What is actually true:** **workflow 10 is `planned`, [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md) is its `READY` row, and the effective-permissions model is unbuilt.** ⚡ **The `403` therefore consumes [TASK-471](BACKLOG.md)'s output and is sequenced behind it** — **the same shape as the six blocked rows [D-209](DECISION_REGISTER.md) counted that *"wait on another TASK, which a lane clears without anybody ruling on anything."***

⛔ **What this lane still must not do is derive the role from a frontend table.** **That would be the second vocabulary [C-251](#c-251) already refused for signal titles**, and a role map in the client would drift from Casbin the first time a policy row changed. **The source is the model, or it is nothing.**

📁 **The design's `403` body**: *"This report needs the **Revenue Ops** role. Your **Analyst** role covers pipeline and activity, not revenue figures."* 📁 **And its rule**: ***"403 names the missing role, never the data."***

🔴 **Both role names are the sentence's entire content, and the transport carries neither.** **Measured on `origin/integration`**: `ApiError` exposes `status`, `code`, `correlationId` and `details`, and **`details` is `{ field: string; message: string }[]`** — ⛔ **a field-validation shape, not an authorization one.** **Casbin decides the refusal server-side and the envelope reports only that it was refused.**

⛔ **So the screen cannot name the missing role without this lane inventing one**, and a fabricated role name is worse than none: **somebody asks an administrator for a role that does not exist.** ⚠️ **[C-1403](#c-1403) already records that the approver names have no publisher and [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md) already rules the request-access button out** ([D-167](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) — **this is the third fact on the same screen with the same problem, and the row's remaining copy is what is left after removing all three.**

**Three ways forward, and the choice is not this lane's:** **①** the envelope gains an authorization detail shape and the screen is built as drawn · **②** the screen ships naming the *capability* rather than the role — *"this needs a role you do not have"* — which is honest, weaker than the design, and discloses less · **③** the `403` is deferred out of this row. ⚡ **② is what this lane would build if told to proceed**, and ⛔ **it is a change to an approved design, so it is asked rather than assumed.**

## C-252 · Two primitives own the region-scope failed read, and TASK-445 built the other one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **holding [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)** — 🔴 **found by [TASK-445](BACKLOG.md)'s own guard failing, which is the guard working exactly as written** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **it spans two rows this office released and neither can settle it alone** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **CONTRADICTORY DESIGN** — **two published primitives claim one concern, and both are correct in isolation** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-09. [TASK-1428](BACKLOG.md) is the row, and it adopts this lane's recommendation unchanged.** ⚡ **`StatedAbsence` becomes a CALLER of `SystemState` at region scope — neither is deleted, neither wins: one owns the SENTENCE, the other the SCOPE.** ⚠️ **And the correction is this office's**: 📁 [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)'s row asserted a distinction that does not hold against the code, and **this lane read the component instead of the row** |
| **Blocks** | 🔴 **[TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md)'s region boundary — the half the row calls *"what every later workflow consumes."*** ✅ **The ladder, `SystemState` and their 23 tests are delivered and green** |

⚡ **[TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md) anticipated this and got the reason slightly wrong**, which is why it is worth recording rather than quietly resolving. **The row says**: *"[TASK-445](BACKLOG.md) already built stated absence and the two must not fork — absence is 'there is nothing', a system state is 'something failed', and conflating them is how a broken widget renders as an empty one."*

🔴 **But `StatedAbsence`'s actual sentence is *"Signora could not load {subject}"*** — **which is a failure, not an absence.** ⛔ **The row's distinction does not hold against the code**: `stated-absence.test.tsx` asserts *"never blames the account for a failure of ours"*, so the component is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md)'s **failed-read** primitive and always was.

**So both rows built the same thing from opposite ends:**

| | `StatedAbsence` — [TASK-445](BACKLOG.md) | the ladder's `region-error` — [TASK-1409](BACKLOG.md) |
|---|---|---|
| **Owns** | ✅ **the sentence**, in one place, across nine former local copies | ✅ **the scope**, the severity, the retry budget and the identifier |
| **Lacks** | ⛔ retry · attempt count · correlation id | ⛔ the sentence |
| **Guard** | ✅ **fails any `.tsx` under `components/` or `app/(app)/` containing *"could not load"*** | — |

✅ **The guard fired on `region-boundary.tsx` and it was right to.** ⛔ **The boundary was removed rather than reworded** — **rewording to dodge a regex is precisely the fork the guard exists to prevent**, and it would have left two failed-read vocabularies with nothing detecting the second.

**The recommendation, and it is input rather than authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)): ✅ **fold `StatedAbsence` into the ladder as the region-scope failed read.** **It keeps the sentence — that is the thing nine local copies proved valuable — and gains the scope, the three-attempt budget and the copyable id from the ladder.** ⛔ **The alternative, leaving both, means a region failure looks like one thing when a read returns an error and another when a component throws** — **the same inconsistency across four surfaces that [C-254](#c-254) is about, reintroduced inside the primitive meant to end it.**

⚠️ **It touches [TASK-445](BACKLOG.md)'s delivered work, so it is not this lane's to decide** even though this lane holds the row that collides with it.

## C-250 · The Entry Engine's rule table counts twenty-four, the row says twenty-one, and one rule cannot fire

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, **implementing [TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **all three found by building the table, not by reading it** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C (Product Office)** for ① · ⛔ **the product owner** for ③, because it is a behaviour a customer sees |
| **Status** | 🟠 **REVIEW NOTE — not a queue item. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6.** 📁 **Its own `Blocks` cell says nothing is blocked; what changes is what a REVIEWER is shown.** ✅ **Surfaced at the review of the screen it names, and not raised again before then** *(was: **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **and it blocks nothing.** ✅ **The engine shi)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **What it changes is what a reviewer is shown** — three points where the row and the design disagree, and a reader holding both should see them as raised rather than as slips |

### ① The count is 24, and [TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md) says 21 — three times

**The row says *"the 21 reason codes as a closed type"*, repeats it in *Closed, not open*, and again in the Definition of Done.** ⚡ **The design's rule table carries 24 rules and 24 DISTINCT codes** — extracted from the document's own script data and checked for duplicates, of which there are none.

```
rules parsed: 24   ·   distinct reason codes: 24
```

✅ **24 shipped.** [D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot the implementation authority and [§21](../CLAUDE.md) says implement the design rather than redesign it while building. ⛔ **Shipping 21 would leave three rules with no code**, and a rule with no code cannot answer *"why did I land here"* — **which the design states as the entire purpose of the codes.**

### ② A resolution is not a destination — read flat, seven rules are dead

**The design says *"evaluated top to bottom"* and *"first match wins"*.** ⚠️ **Taken literally as one flat list, rules 18–24 can never fire**, because **rules 10–14 partition every membership shape there is**: none · exactly one · several with a healthy last-used · several without · several with an unhealthy one. **Every person matches one of them.**

⛔ **The design forbids that outcome in terms** — 📁 ***"Every rule has a fixture; the twenty-four cases are a test suite, not a diagram."***

✅ **§02 gives the reading that works, and it is the document's own**: 📁 *"each gate depends on the one before it **resolving**, and **a gate that fails** produces a designed screen."* **Two outcomes, not one.** So rules **11, 12 and 14 resolve** the workspace and the walk continues; everything else terminates. ⚡ **This is implemented and every rule but one is now reachable, each with its own case.** **Recorded because it is an interpretation**, and a later reader should find it argued rather than assumed.

### ③ 🔴 Rule 24 `HOME` cannot fire, and the design calls it the most common outcome

**Rule 24's condition is *"Everything healthy, no other rule matched"*.** ⛔ **Gate 3 always produces a reason**, so *no other rule matched* is never true — **and the same document tints rule 24's row and describes it as *"the default and the most common outcome"*.** ⚠️ **Both cannot hold.**

**The question, and it is a product question rather than an engineering one:**

> **When a person lands on Home with nothing remarkable about their entry, should the reason code read `HOME`, or the resolution code that chose the workspace — `SOLE_WORKSPACE`, `LAST_USED` or `FELL_THROUGH`?**

⚡ **It matters because the code is customer-facing infrastructure**, not a log line: the design puts it *"in the support diagnostics bundle"*, and **whichever answer is right, support reads it.**

✅ **Shipped meanwhile: the resolution code wins and rule 24 is kept as the totality guard.** ⛔ **It is not deleted** — it is what makes `resolveEntry` total, and **a router handed `undefined` fails far from the cause.** ⚡ **A test asserts it cannot currently be reached**, so if the answer is `HOME` the change is one rule and the test says so.

### ④ One gap the design does not cover, named rather than invented

**Rule 04 `SESSION_EXPIRED`'s route column reads `(intent preserved)`.** ⚠️ **With no intent there is nothing to preserve, and the document does not say where that lands.** ⛔ **Not invented into a product decision** — it currently falls to `/workspaces`, and **the choice is flagged here rather than buried in a route table.**

## C-249 · Two rows on the AI screen are policies, and neither policy exists

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, building [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md) screen `04` |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **both are statements about what a customer's organization allows**, which is not a lane's to assert |
| **Status** | 🟠 **REVIEW NOTE — not a queue item. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6.** 📁 **Its own `Blocks` cell says nothing is blocked; what changes is what a REVIEWER is shown.** ✅ **Surfaced at the review of the screen it names, and not raised again before then** *(was: **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **and it blocks nothing.** ✅ **The five perso)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **What it changes is what the Workflow 9 review is shown** |

**The design draws seven rows on screen `04`. Five are the person's and ship. Two are not, and neither has anything behind it.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **"Write risk flags to the CRM — *switched off for everyone in this workspace*"** | **A workspace AI policy, and none exists.** ⚠️ **The design's own justification is the problem**: *"Shown so you know it exists and is not silently running."* **A row asserting something is switched off *for everyone* is a claim about a setting nobody can inspect** — and it would be drawn by a screen that cannot read one |
| ⚠️ **The confidence floor's second half** | ✅ **The personal floor ships** — the design's `3 · 4 · 5`. ⛔ **What does not is *"yours can be stricter than the workspace floor of 3, never looser"***: the comparison needs a workspace floor, and there is none. **Stating it would describe a rule nothing enforces** ([D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④) |
| ✅ **What DID ship, and why it could** | **"Used to train a shared model — never"** is a *product* fact rather than a workspace policy, and **the repository backs it**: [10-security.md](architecture/10-security.md) makes no-training/no-retention vendor terms **a condition of use**, re-verified at each contract renewal ([14-ai-architecture.md](architecture/14-ai-architecture.md)). ⚠️ **It is contractual rather than code-enforced**, and the panel says so in a comment so nobody later mistakes it for a technical guarantee |

> ⚡ **The three data-use statements render as facts with a mark, never as disabled toggles.** **A disabled control invites the question of who may enable it**, and for the training row the honest answer is *nobody, ever*.

**The decision, in one sentence:** ⚡ **does a workspace get an AI policy — a floor and a CRM-write switch an owner sets for everyone — in which case these two rows are a dependency Workflow 9 sits behind, or are they per-person after all**, in which case the design's *"for everyone in this workspace"* wording is what changes?

## C-248 · Four profile fields are locked as *"Managed by Northwind IT"* and no directory sync exists

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, **building [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md) screen `01` and grepping for the sync before drawing the lock** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **it is a promise about who owns a customer's identity data**, not a build estimate |
| **Status** | 🟠 **REVIEW NOTE — not a queue item. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6.** 📁 **Its own `Blocks` cell says nothing is blocked; what changes is what a REVIEWER is shown.** ✅ **Surfaced at the review of the screen it names, and not raised again before then** *(was: **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **and it blocks nothing.** ✅ **Screen `01` sh)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **What it changes is how complete screen `01` looks at review** — named here so it reads as a stated absence rather than an omission |

**The design's own headline statistic on this screen is `0` — *"Edits accepted that a sync would undo."*** ⚡ **That is not decoration: it is the invariant the three field kinds exist to keep** — *Yours* · *From directory* · *Workspace policy*.

**Four fields are drawn `From directory`, with the note *"Managed by Northwind IT · request a change"*:** **Full name · Work email · Job title · Department.**

| | |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **Measured** | **No directory integration exists anywhere in the repository** — `scim`, `directory_sync` and `directorysync` return nothing across `backend/` and `frontend/` |
| ✅ **`Work email` is genuinely locked, and ships locked** | **For a real reason that is not the directory**: [§13](../CLAUDE.md) makes Better Auth the sole Authentication Authority, and the design says it itself — *"Changing this creates a new identity — IT must do it."* **The lock is true; only the attribution would be wrong** |
| 🔴 **`Job title` and `Department` have no source at all** | **Nothing in the product knows them.** ⛔ **Not built** — [D-156](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④: *a state whose data is missing is built against seeded data of the production shape; a state whose business rule is missing is not built at all.* **A locked field with no sync behind it is a rule the product does not have, painted as one it does** |
| ⚠️ **`Full name` is the interesting one** | **Better Auth holds it and can change it.** **So it is editable today and the design says it is not** — locking it would refuse an edit nothing would undo, which is the *opposite* of the invariant the `0` protects |

> ⚡ **The design is not wrong; it is drawn for a customer who has a directory.** **Northwind is that customer.** The question is what Signora shows the ones who are not, and that is a product answer rather than an implementation detail.

**The decision, in one sentence:** ⚡ **do these four become editable until a directory integration exists — with the lock arriving alongside the sync that justifies it — or is a directory assumed, in which case the integration is a dependency Workflow 9 sits behind?**

## C-247 · A person in two organizations gets two themes, and TASK-470's row says otherwise

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, **implementing [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md) — the row asked for this answer rather than leaving it assumed** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **it is a product question wearing a tenancy question's clothes**: *does a person have one Signora, or one per organization?* |
| **Status** | 🟠 **REVIEW NOTE — not a queue item. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6.** 📁 **Its own `Blocks` cell says nothing is blocked; what changes is what a REVIEWER is shown.** ✅ **Surfaced at the review of the screen it names, and not raised again before then** *(was: **`OPEN`** — ⛔ **and it blocks nothing.** ✅ **Preferences sh)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **What it changes is a customer's experience of belonging to two organizations**, which nobody has yet |

**[TASK-470](BACKLOG.md)'s row says the preferences are *account*-scoped**: *"Theme, density, locale and AI preference are account-scoped, not workspace-scoped — which makes this the first row in the migration whose data is not workspace-owned."*

**[418](architecture/418-platform-foundation-assessment.md) says otherwise**, and [492 §2](architecture/492-person-scoped-tenancy.md) quotes it: *"A profile preference, a notification matrix and a session belong to a **person within a workspace**."*

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **What shipped, and why** | **Person within a workspace** — migration `0044`, `PRIMARY KEY (workspace_id, user_id)`, registered in `TENANT_OWNED_TABLES`, **with every RLS policy carrying `user_id = current_setting('app.user_id')` on top of the tenant predicate.** ⚡ **[492 §0](architecture/492-person-scoped-tenancy.md)'s *narrowing of tenant-owned, never a parallel to it*** |
| ⛔ **Why not account-global** | **It has no lawful home today.** [§8](../CLAUDE.md) offers two classes: tenant-owned needs a non-nullable `workspace_id`, and platform-infrastructure tables are *"owned exclusively by platform services… a business module must never query one"* — **and a profile panel queries this on every render.** A third class would change what the Security Invariants mean, which is not a feature row's to introduce |
| ⚡ **Why the design does not settle it** | *"Applies to this account on every device you sign in from, **not to this browser**"* contrasts the account with the **browser**, never with the organization. **It settles that preferences are server-persisted — which they are** |
| ⚠️ **What it costs, stated plainly** | **A person in two organizations has two preference rows and could see two themes.** ⛔ **Nobody has two organizations yet**, so this is cheap to change now and expensive later |

**The decision, in one sentence:** ⚡ **confirm that a preference belongs to a person *within* an organization — the architecture's answer, and what ships — or rule that theme, density and locale are one person's everywhere**, in which case a third tenancy class is needed and [492](architecture/492-person-scoped-tenancy.md) has already designed it.

## C-243 · The reset link lives an hour and the design says thirty minutes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, **building [TASK-487](BACKLOG.md) and reading `node_modules` rather than trusting either number** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **a credential's lifetime is a security parameter**, which [D-151](DECISION_REGISTER.md) ④ places here |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — ruled [D-185](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §1, product owner, 2026-08-08: **thirty minutes**.** ⚡ **The reasoning is a standing rule and is quoted rather than paraphrased: *"the framework should implement the product, not define it."*** ⛔ **So `resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn: 1800` moves, and the design does not.** ✅ **[TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) ⑤ carries it, and carries the copy change in the SAME slice** — **the config without the copy understates a credential's life; the copy without the config restores exactly the lie Lane A refused to print** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **Screen `08` ships and states the true number.** ⚠️ **What is open is which number should be true** |

**The design's sentence, verbatim:** *"Enter your work email. If an account exists, you'll get a reset link that works once and **expires in 30 minutes**."*

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **What the platform actually does** | **`better-auth`'s `resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn` defaults to `3600`** — `dist/api/routes/password.mjs` reads `resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn \|\| 3600 * 1` — **and `lib/auth/server.ts` does not configure it.** ⚡ **The link lives one hour** |
| ✅ **What the screen prints** | ***"expires in an hour"*** — **the true number**, in the design's own sentence otherwise unchanged |
| ⛔ **Why not the design's number** | **It would state a false thing about a credential's lifetime.** ⚠️ **A customer returning at forty minutes would believe a working link was dead**, and stop. ⚡ **The reverse error is worse**: a screen promising thirty minutes for a token that lives sixty is telling a security-conscious buyer the window is half what it is |
| **What it would take** | **`resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn: 1800` in `lib/auth/server.ts`** — ⛔ **the file [TASK-487](BACKLOG.md) states it does not touch**, and **[TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) already owns that file** |

> ⚡ **This is the fourth instance of one pattern and the first where the two answers are both defensible.** [C-240](#c-240--two-ruled-or-designed-password-controls-live-in-the-one-file-workflow-2-may-not-touch) ①②, [C-241](#c-241--workflow-3s-approved-screen-needs-the-one-file-its-row-forbids-and-this-is-the-third-instance) and this all need `lib/auth/server.ts`; the first three had a right answer already recorded. **Here the design and the platform simply disagree, and either could be corrected.**
>
> ⛔ **This lane did not pick.** **It printed what is true today** and named the choice, because [D-138](../CLAUDE.md) makes the snapshot the implementation authority for *design* and [§13](../CLAUDE.md) makes Better Auth the authority for *authentication* — **and this is the seam where those two authorities meet.**

**The decision, in one sentence:** ⚡ **shorten the token to thirty minutes and match the design, or amend the design to an hour and match the platform.** ✅ **Either is one line; the screen follows whichever lands.**

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **The first half is false, not merely unsupported** | **`revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` is a Better Auth option and `lib/auth/server.ts` does not set it**, so the default applies and **other sessions survive a reset.** ⛔ **Printing it would tell somebody who has just been compromised that they are safe** — **the most expensive place in the product to be wrong** |
| ⚠️ **The second half has no source** | **Nothing lists sessions and nothing records a device.** ⛔ ***"4"* and *"the iPad last used 3 days ago"* cannot be produced** — a session inventory with user-agent metadata is a capability, not a string |
| ✅ **What ships instead** | **Neither the count nor the promise.** ⚡ **Screen `10` is equally careful**: it does not say other devices were signed out, because they were not |
| **What it would take** | **`revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset: true`** in `lib/auth/server.ts` — ⛔ **the file [TASK-488](BACKLOG.md) states it does not touch**, and **[TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) owns it.** ⚠️ **The count needs more than a flag** |

> ⚡ **This is the fifth instance of one shape** — [C-434](#c-434--three-of-logins-remaining-screens-need-a-decision-not-a-build--and-one-of-them-is-already-shipped) Workflow 1, [C-240](#c-240--two-ruled-or-designed-password-controls-live-in-the-one-file-workflow-2-may-not-touch) Workflow 2, [C-241](#c-241--workflows-3s-approved-screen-needs-the-one-file-its-row-forbids-and-this-is-the-third-instance) Workflow 3, [C-243](#c-243--the-reset-link-lives-an-hour-and-the-design-says-thirty-minutes) Workflow 4, **and this one Workflow 5.** ⛔ **Every authentication workflow has needed something in `lib/auth/server.ts` that its own row forbids.**
>
> ⚠️ **[TASK-498](BACKLOG.md) was written to be that row and it has already shipped** — so the pattern now has a home, and **this item is a request to schedule a second pass rather than to invent a place to put one.**

**The decision, in one sentence:** ⚡ **should a password reset end every other session?** ✅ **If yes it is one line in the row that owns that file, and the screen can then say so truthfully.** ⛔ **The device count and its "iPad" are a separate, larger capability and are not bundled into that answer.**

## C-245 · Screen `13` shows a reader six facts they are not permitted to see

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-08, **implementing [TASK-489](BACKLOG.md) under [D-190](DECISION_REGISTER.md)** — ⚡ **reported and implementation continued on the half that is real**, as [D-190](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §3 directs |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **a disclosure boundary, not a build estimate** |
| **Status** | 🟠 **REVIEW NOTE — not a queue item. Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6.** 📁 **Its own `Blocks` cell says nothing is blocked; what changes is what a REVIEWER is shown.** ✅ **Surfaced at the review of the screen it names, and not raised again before then** *(was: **`OPEN`**)* |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Most of screen `13`, and — measured 2026-08-09 — the *Wrong account* and *Declined* screens too.** ✅ **Screen `14 Invitation expired` SHIPPED 2026-08-09** at `/invite/expired`, unblocked by [B-214](BUGS.md); see *the other two screens* below |

### ⚡ UPDATE 2026-08-09 — the other two screens, and one of them must NOT be built

**[TASK-489](BACKLOG.md) scopes four routes** — the design's map gives `/invite/:token`, `/invite/declined`, `/invite/expired`, `/invite/mismatch`. ✅ **`14 Invitation expired` shipped**, because an expired invitation discloses nothing about the organization. **The other two were measured this poll:**

| Route | | |
|---|---|---|
| **`/invite/declined`** | ⛔ **The capability does not exist** | **Measured across `backend/modules/workspace_tenancy` on `origin/integration`: no decline route, no domain method, no frontend hook — the word appears nowhere.** ⚡ **So the screen has no entrance and no cause**, and `reachability.py` would refuse it. **A row is needed before a screen is** |
| **`/invite/mismatch`** | 🔴 **Buildable only by weakening a deliberate security property** | **See below — and this lane is not asking for permission to do it** |

#### 🔴 *Wrong account* conflicts with a ratified disclosure boundary, and the boundary is right

**`InvitationNotFoundError`'s own docstring states the property in terms:**

> ⛔ ***"One sentence covering every reason, and that is the design rather than laziness: never invited, already accepted, withdrawn. Telling them apart would answer 'has this workspace invited this person?' to anybody who can sign in — a fact about a customer's hiring."***

**The accept path looks up `find_live(workspace_id, normalize_email(signed_in_address))`.** ⚡ **Signed in as the wrong person, there genuinely is no invitation *for you*** — and a *Wrong account* screen must say the opposite: **that one exists here, for somebody else.**

⛔ **That is precisely the sentence the docstring forbids**, and [§20c](../CLAUDE.md)/[D-190](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7 put it out of a lane's reach regardless: ***never weaken authorization or business rules.*** ✅ **So this lane has not built it, has not proposed an error code for it, and is not asking to.**

⚠️ **This is the same flattening [B-214](BUGS.md) fixed, and the difference is what makes it interesting.** **Expiry was safe to separate** — the docstring calls it *"the deliberate exception"* — **because knowing an invitation aged out reveals nothing about who was invited.** ⛔ **Wrong-account is not**, and treating the two as one class would have undone a security property while looking like consistency.

> **The question, and it is the product owner's rather than an engineering one:** **does the design's *Wrong account* screen survive the boundary?** ⚡ **A screen that says *"you are signed in as anna@acme.com — if you were invited on another address, sign in with that one"* discloses nothing and would satisfy the journey.** ⛔ **That is a copy decision, not a lane's to take**, and it is offered as input rather than as authority.

**The design's screen `13`, verbatim:** *"**Northwind Global** · Enterprise workspace · **142 members** · **Anders Hald invited you** · You'll join as an **Analyst**, with access to EMEA accounts"*, above **four named permissions**.

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **Every one of those is inside the tenant the reader has not entered** | **[C-208](#c-208) established this for the *name* and it is broader**: the member count, the inviter, the role and the permission list are all workspace data, and **the reader is definitionally not a member yet** |
| ⛔ **And no endpoint could serve them** | **Measured, not assumed**: `workspace_tenancy` exposes **`/workspaces/{id}/invitations`, `/accept`, `/{id}/resend`, `/{id}/revoke`** — **all scoped to a workspace and all requiring membership or admin.** ⚡ **There is no lookup-by-token and no unauthenticated read of an invitation** |
| 🔴 **Adding one is the decision, and it is not small** | **A token-addressed endpoint returning a workspace's name, size, an employee's name and a role is an unauthenticated disclosure of organizational data**, gated only on possession of a link that arrives by email and lives in inboxes and mail logs. ⛔ **That is a product decision about what an invitation link is worth**, not an implementation detail |
| ✅ **What the platform *does* return** | **`role`, on `accept` — after the membership exists.** ⚡ **Which is exactly what `join.test.tsx` already asserts**: *"names the role only once the membership exists"* |

> ⚡ **This is the same shape as [C-241](#c-241--workflows-3s-approved-screen-needs-the-one-file-its-row-forbids-and-this-is-the-third-instance) and [C-244](#c-244--screen-09-promises-a-password-reset-signs-other-devices-out-and-nothing-does), with one difference that matters**: those needed a *configuration line* in a file the row forbade. ⛔ **This needs a new endpoint and a ruling about what it may disclose** — **the first of the five that is genuinely a capability rather than a switch.**

### ⛔ And the second half of the row has the same problem

**Screen `14` offers *"Request a new invitation"*** — *"one click notifies the original inviter and the workspace admins."* ⛔ **Nothing can grant it**: `tests/components/join.test.tsx` already asserts the control is never offered ***"because nothing can grant it"*** — no endpoint, no table, no row — **and that assertion was written by this lane against the same absence.**

**The decision, in one sentence:** ⚡ **may an invitation link, on its own, reveal a company's name, headcount, an employee's name and a role?** ✅ **If yes, that is an endpoint and an ADR.** ⛔ **If no, screen `13` is a different screen and the design needs amending** — **and until either lands, `/join` shows what a non-member may truthfully be shown.**

## ⚡ Design Clarifications — a class, not a second register ([D-207](DECISION_REGISTER.md))

> **[D-207](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2–§3 separate two questions this office had been answering as one.** **Design COMPLETENESS asks *can it be built without inventing behaviour?* — the Entry Coverage Review answers that.** **Design CORRECTNESS asks *is the behaviour itself logically consistent?* — nobody had been answering it, and this office began to and then resolved its own findings, which is the overreach D-207 corrects.**
>
> ## 🔴 **The gate, before anything below is written — [D-212](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7**
>
> ⛔ **One question first: *can this be answered by an existing finalized design document?*** ✅ **If yes, implementation proceeds and NOTHING is raised.** ⛔ **Only if no does it become a clarification.**
>
> ⚡ **This office has already been caught by the inverse of it**: the [D-210](DECISION_REGISTER.md) audit reported *route transitions* and *split layouts* as absent because a term search found no match — **and both were fully specified**, one as `loadingCases → "Route change · module to module"` and one as the utility panel's *"selecting a table row fills the panel rather than opening a second surface."* ⛔ **Two interruptions that a reader, rather than a grep, would not have produced.**
>
> ⛔ **A Design Clarification is NOT a coordination item this office may close.** ✅ **It is evidence sent to the Design Authority, and the specification is confirmed or amended there.** 📁 **[§21](../CLAUDE.md): implement the design, never redesign it while building.**
>
> ⚠️ **Kept as a `Class` field in THIS register rather than a new file, deliberately.** ⛔ **A second register is a second place to look and a second thing to keep current** — the defect [D-203](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2 spent a cycle removing. ✅ **The class is queryable, `state-check` reads it, and it appears on its own line in the dashboard.**
>
> **Every finding is CLASSIFIED BEFORE any work is created** — [D-207](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6, extended by [D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4:
>
> | Classification | What it means | What it produces |
> |---|---|---|
> | `MISSING IMPLEMENTATION` | **The design is complete and the platform cannot do it** | **An implementation row** |
> | `MISSING DESIGN` | **The document does not answer it at all** | **A clarification, or a commissioned document** |
> | `INCOMPLETE DESIGN` | **It is answered, and not far enough to build from** | **A clarification** |
> | `CONTRADICTORY DESIGN` | **Two things are asserted that cannot both hold** | **A clarification** |
> | `IMPLEMENTATION DEFECT` | **The design is clear and the code disagrees with it** | **A `B-` row** |
> | `GOVERNANCE ISSUE` | **The process, a register or an instrument is wrong** | **This office's own work** |
> | `DEPENDENCY` | **It is correct and waits on something named** | ⛔ **Nothing new** — the dependency is recorded on the existing row |
> | `PRODUCT OWNER DECISION` | **A product question, not a design or engineering one** | **A queue row** |
>
> ⚡ **Naming it first is what stops implementation work compensating for design uncertainty**, and it has already changed answers: **rule 03 `/auth/locked` classified as `MISSING IMPLEMENTATION` rather than missing design — the screen is drawn and [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability) records no lockout capability exists.**

## C-1411 · An audit stream whose reliable shape needs the frozen platform, and whose cheap shape is lossy

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-09, **splitting [C-261](#c-261--task-492s-producer-instruction-rests-on-a-premise-that-measurement-contradicts-and-either-reading-ships-a-defect) under [D-216](DECISION_REGISTER.md)** — ⚡ **the analysis and both options are Lane A's, measured while holding [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md); this office is routing them, not re-deriving them** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C / the implementing lane** — ⚡ **reassigned 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7: operational or sequencing, never a product decision** *(was: product owner)* |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | 🔴 **ARCHITECTURAL BLOCKER** — ⛔ **not a design question and not a missing capability: no accepted architecture exists for how a fact born in the Better Auth tier reaches a table Python owns** |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED — Lane C, 2026-08-11, on the PO-queue triage.** ⚡ **It blocks three of [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md)'s four producers, and TASK-492 is `PROMOTED`.** ⛔ **The decision was overtaken by the implementation.** ⚠️ **If the audit stream's shape is still wrong, that is a defect against the shipped code and belongs in [BUGS.md](BUGS.md), not a pending ruling here.** *(Was:⏸️ **`OPEN` — RECLASSIFIED to SEQUENCING, Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** ⛔ **Not a product decision: it waits on three of [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md)'s four producers.** ✅ **Owner is the implementing lane, not the product owner** |)* |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Three of [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md)'s four producers — sign-in, sign-out, password reset.** ✅ **The table, the domain type, the repository and the `public/` contract are BUILT AND GREEN** — 401 Security Invariants, 29 domain tests, `mypy --strict` clean. ⛔ **Nothing else in the repository waits on this** |

📁 **[493 §](architecture/493-security-platform-architecture.md) names the producer — *"Workflow 1 (Login) — already producing them"* — and specifies nothing about how the fact crosses the tier boundary.** 🔴 **Four authentication journeys are on `main` today and nothing records them.**

| | How | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| ⓐ **The client reports it** | Next.js calls a new endpoint after Better Auth mints the token | ⛔ **A best-effort client call is a LOSSY audit path, and it drops events exactly when something went wrong** — ⚡ **which is the population an audit stream exists for.** 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *the record cannot be added retroactively*** |
| ⓑ **The server records it** | The API records on first verification of a new session | ✅ **Reliable; no client can forget.** ⛔ **Telling a new session from a continuing one lives in `signora_platform/auth/`** — 🔴 **frozen, [§20a](../CLAUDE.md)** |

> ⚡ **This office's read, and it is a recommendation rather than a ruling.** ✅ **ⓑ, under [§20a](../CLAUDE.md)'s FIRST exemption rather than its third.** 📁 **The exemption list opens with *"a tenancy, authentication, authorization, or secrets defect. Fix it, and add a Security Invariant proving it stays fixed."*** ⛔ **An authentication tier that produces no audit record is not the platform being *inconvenient* — which is the case §20a explicitly refuses — it is an authentication gap**, and the exemption's own second clause is exactly what [TASK-492](BACKLOG.md) already built the harness for.
>
> ⚠️ **What this office will not do is decide it.** 🔴 **Reading a gap as a security defect to reach an exemption is precisely the reasoning §20a exists to constrain**, and the office that would benefit from the answer is not the office that should give it.

## C-1408 · Rule precedence and interaction — the table and the gate ladder are two different readings

| **Class** | ⚡ **DESIGN CLARIFICATION** |
| **Classification** ([D-207](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6) | ⚠️ **INCOMPLETE DESIGN** — **the correct reading exists in §02 and the rules table does not carry it** |
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-09, implementing [TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md) · **escalated as a clarification by Lane C** |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Design Authority** |
| **Status** | 🟠 **`OPEN`** |
| **Blocks** | ⏸️ **[TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md)**, ⏸️ **[TASK-1402](BACKLOG.md)**, ⏸️ **[TASK-1407](BACKLOG.md)**, ⏸️ **[TASK-1426](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **frozen under [D-207](DECISION_REGISTER.md)'s *stop creating implementation tasks for routing logic until the design is settled*** |

📁 **The rules table says *"evaluated top to bottom"* and *"first match wins."*** ⛔ **Read as one flat list, rules 18–24 can never fire** — **rules 10–14 partition every membership shape there is** (none · exactly one · several with a healthy last-used · several without · several with an unhealthy one), **so a person always matches one of them.**

✅ **§02 gives a reading that works, and it is the document's own**: 📁 *"each gate depends on the one before it **resolving**, and **a gate that fails** produces a designed screen."* ⚡ **Two outcomes per gate, not one** — so rules 11, 12 and 14 RESOLVE the workspace and evaluation continues.

> ## ⚠️ **Both readings are in the same document and they disagree.** ⛔ **The engine implements §02's, because it is the only one under which the table is not two-thirds dead** — ✅ **and that choice was made by a lane rather than confirmed by Design, which is what this item exists to fix.**

**What is asked:** ⛔ **which reading is authoritative.** ⚠️ **This office offers no answer** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6): **both readings are the document's own, they produce different products, and choosing between them is the Design Authority's.**

### ⚡ Impact assessment ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7)

|---|---|
| **Affected design documents** | **`Fortune Signora Authenticated Entry`** §02 and §03 — ⚠️ **and the *Specified in* column the Coverage Review recommends adding, which assumes the table is read as a table** |
| **Affected workflows** | **29** only. ⛔ **Workflows 1–8 end AT the entry decision and do not evaluate rules** |
| **Affected implementation tasks** | ⏸️ **[TASK-1426](BACKLOG.md)** *(via [C-1410](#c-1410--rule-04s-landing-with-no-intent-is-undefined))*. ✅ **[TASK-1400](BACKLOG.md) SHIPPED under §02's reading, with the rule order asserted against the document** |
| **Can work continue in parallel?** | ✅ **YES — 23 rows, including [TASK-1401](BACKLOG.md)'s destinations, [TASK-1402](BACKLOG.md), [TASK-1407](BACKLOG.md) and every workflow row.** ⚡ **Re-derived under [D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §2: this office had frozen four rows and only one was genuinely dependent** |
| **Architectural impact if it changes** | 🟠 **MODERATE and contained.** ⛔ **`RULES` is a data table walked top to bottom — a precedence change is a reordering plus test fixtures, not a rewrite.** 🔴 **What it would invalidate is every reason code already emitted**, and the code is customer-facing infrastructure that goes in the support bundle |
