## C-1404 · Machine credentials have no module, and the entry engine already admits a non-human principal

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-09, decomposing [workflow 11](coordination/workflows.toml) under [D-204](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §3–§4 |
| **Owner** | **Lane C / the implementing lane** — ⚡ **reassigned 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7: operational or sequencing, never a product decision** *(was: product owner)* |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — RULED **ⓐ NEW BOUNDED CONTEXT**, product owner, 2026-08-13** ([D-237](DECISION_REGISTER.md), contract [ADR-0414](architecture/adr/0414-machine-credentials-bounded-context.md)). ⛔ **Do not reopen unless implementation reveals a concrete contradiction with an approved design or ADR** |
| ✅ **THE RULING** | > **The new bounded context owns the API-key credential lifecycle — issuance · rotation · one-time display · revocation · per-call audit.**<br><br>📁 ***"API-key issuance, rotation, one-time display, revocation and per-call audit/logging constitute a credential lifecycle and should not be placed inside `workspace_tenancy`."***<br><br>✅ **`workspace_tenancy` keeps the ownership relationships — workspace · member · machine-principal ownership — and is NOT redesigned.**<br><br>⛔ **Webhooks are separate: outbound delivery on the existing outbox/relay pattern, and NOT placed in the credential context merely because both appear here.** ⛔ **`integrations`' credential models must NOT be reused for inbound API keys simply because they exist.**<br><br>⛔ **No generalized IAM · no OAuth redesign · no new authentication mechanisms · no additional machine-principal types · no credential sharing · no new webhook product features** |
| 🔴 **CLASSIFICATION CORRECTED** | ⛔ **This row read *"RECLASSIFIED to SEQUENCING… never a product decision"*, citing [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** 🔴 **D-232 does not exist — verified — and must not be treated as authority anywhere it is cited.** ✅ **Recorded as a Product/Architecture decision, which is what [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s Change Budget always made it: a new bounded context is 🔴** |
| ⛔ **Superseded status, kept as history** | ⏸️ **`OPEN` — RECLASSIFIED to SEQUENCING, Lane C, 2026-08-10, [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** ⛔ **Not a product decision: it waits on [TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md), and nothing is being built today** |
| **Blocks** | ⏸️ **[TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md)** — and nothing being built today |

📁 **The Settings design specifies API keys and webhooks: *"Scoped, rotatable, and logged per call"*, *"A key is shown once at creation and never again"*, *"Failed webhook deliveries retry with backoff for 24 hours, then park with the payload retained."*** ⛔ **None of it exists, and no module in [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) owns machine credentials.**

> ## ⚡ **It is not a settings section. It is a credential system and an outbound delivery system**, and it arrived disguised as one — which is [D-204](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4's case exactly.

🔴 **And it is already load-bearing**: **[TASK-1407](BACKLOG.md) widens `resolveEntry` to admit a NON-HUMAN principal**, and **this is where non-human principals would come from.** ✅ **[495](architecture/495-principal-and-identity-boundary.md) ratified the principal model, so the two must agree rather than each inventing one.**

**Three candidates, and the choice is architectural:** ⓐ **a new `machine_identity` module** · ⓑ **inside `workspace_tenancy`**, which already owns membership and roles · ⓒ **inside `platform_foundation`**, which owns `infra/` and no runtime surface. ⚠️ **ⓑ is the smallest change and the least honest** — a service principal is not a member.

---

## ⚡ PREPARED 2026-08-13 — the question is unanswerable because it is two questions

🔴 **This item has been open since 2026-08-09 and the reason is in its own sentence:** ***"It is a credential system AND an outbound delivery system."*** ⛔ **Asking *which module owns machine credentials* of a row containing both cannot produce one answer, because the two halves point at different owners.**

### ① API keys — a non-human principal authenticating INBOUND

📁 **[495](architecture/495-principal-and-identity-boundary.md) ratified the model and constrains the owner without naming one:** **`workspace_id` is *"non-nullable for every non-human kind — a machine identity that is not workspace-scoped is a cross-tenant credential"*** · **`owner_user_id` — *"every machine principal is owned by a human"*** · **`acting_for` — *"the field the whole model exists for."***

⚡ **So a machine principal is anchored to a workspace and to a member — the two aggregates [`workspace_tenancy`](../backend/modules/workspace_tenancy/) already owns.** ⚠️ **That is a stronger argument for ⓑ than *"smallest change"*, and it is the one this item did not make.** ⛔ **The counter stands: issuance, rotation, one-time display and per-call logging are a credential lifecycle, not a membership one.**

⛔ **ⓒ is eliminated: `platform_foundation` has no runtime surface, and API keys need endpoints.**

### ② Webhooks — outbound delivery with retry, backoff and parking

⛔ **This half is NOT a credential question at all**, and it is why the row resists a single owner. 📁 **The design: *"failed webhook deliveries retry with backoff for 24 hours, then park with the payload retained"*** — **durable outbound delivery, which is the outbox-and-relay shape the platform already runs.**

⚠️ **And `integrations` is the near-miss worth naming rather than leaving for somebody to propose.** ✅ **It already publishes `Credential`, `ConnectedAccount`, `ConnectionState` and `ExecutionContext`** — ⛔ **but for the OPPOSITE direction: credentials Signora holds to call OUT to a vendor.** 🔴 **An API key is a credential a third party holds to call Signora IN.** 📁 **[§13](../CLAUDE.md) already forbids exactly this conflation — *"a sign-in OAuth token must never be reused as an integration OAuth token"*** — **and putting an inbound machine credential in the module that owns outbound ones is that defect with a new pair of nouns.**

### ⚠️ AND THE CLASSIFICATION IS WRONG

⛔ **This row reads *"RECLASSIFIED to SEQUENCING… never a product decision"*, citing [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7.** 🔴 **[D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) is a dangling reference — cited here and by [C-337](#c-337) and by [ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md)'s status line, and never written.** ✅ **Verified: no `D-232` row exists in the register.**

📁 **And [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s Change Budget puts *a new module or bounded context* at 🔴 — product owner plus an ADR.** ⛔ **So if the answer is ⓐ, this is a product decision and was misclassified as sequencing on the authority of a record that does not exist.**

### ✅ Recommendation — split the row, and only one half needs a ruling

| | |
|---|---|
| **①** | **The credential half needs the ruling** — ⓐ a new bounded context, or ⓑ inside `workspace_tenancy` on 495's anchors. ⛔ **🔴 either way if it is ⓐ** |
| **②** | **The delivery half does not.** ✅ **Durable outbound delivery is platform machinery that already exists, and it is buildable once ① has an owner to authenticate the caller** |

⚡ **This does not release [TASK-1413](BACKLOG.md).** ⛔ **It makes the question answerable in one word instead of unanswerable in three** — and **the split is decomposition of approved scope, never new scope.**

## C-1421 · C-279 prepared — who owns unread state, and whether we own it at all

| | |
|---|---|
| **Opened** | **2026-08-10, Lane C**, preparing [C-279](#c-279) which Lane A raised and correctly refused to decide |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** |
| **Status** | 🟠 **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION` — Lane C, 2026-08-14.** ⚡ **The revisit condition this row set has fired**: *"Revisit when the Notification Center implementation actually reaches the point that needs it."* 📁 **The product owner's implementation-first directive names it directly — *"the architectural ownership question is genuinely blocking TASK-480 and TASK-495"* — and instructs that the smallest decision be raised.** ⛔ **Nothing below is changed and no option is added; the evidence and the recommendation are exactly as prepared.** *(was: ⏸️ **`REVIEW LATER` — product owner, 2026-08-11. [C-279](#c-279) consolidated into this row.** ⛔ **No new bounded context, no unread-state table, no ADR, no `workspace_tenancy` claim.** ✅ **Novu remains the notification infrastructure layer.** ⚡ ***"Do not let an unresolved future notification architecture decision block shell/navigation/common-foundation implementation."***)* |
| 🔴 **THE QUESTION, and it is the whole of what is asked** | > ## **Which module or bounded context owns per-person notification state, including unread/read state?** |
| ⛔ **What is deliberately NOT asked** | **No schema · no subsystem design · no additional features · no ADR text · no vendor question** — 📁 **Novu is already ratified ([ADR-0017](architecture/adr/0017-notifications.md)) and is not in scope here.** ⚡ **Two of the three candidate sources are already closed by rules the repository has** — a workspace-wide domain event cannot carry per-person state, and [§8](../CLAUDE.md) forbids a business module reading `outbox_event` — ✅ **so the per-person record is the only survivor and the only open question is its address** |
| **Module** | **`product_surface`** *(consumer)* — **the owner is the question** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **[TASK-480](BACKLOG.md) only.** ✅ **Lane A moved on, which was right** |

### ✅ What Lane A settled, and it does not need re-deciding

📁 **A domain event cannot carry per-recipient unread state** — one event, many recipients, and [§9](../CLAUDE.md)'s envelope has no per-person field. 📁 **[§8](../CLAUDE.md) forbids a business module querying `outbox_event` outright.** ⚡ **So a per-person unread record is the only survivor of the three candidates, and that reasoning is sound.**

### 🔴 The third option Lane A could not see, because it sits above implementation scope

⛔ **The question was framed as *which module owns the table*. There may be no table.**

📁 **[ADR-0017](architecture/adr/0017-notifications.md) ratifies **Novu** as *"the notification infrastructure layer — a cross-channel notification orchestrator"*.** ⚠️ **It is SILENT on in-app inbox and unread state** — `grep` for *unread · inbox · feed · read state · seen* returns nothing. 🔴 **So the repository has bought a notification vendor and never decided whether its inbox is in scope.**

⚡ **That makes this a [Principle 15](architecture/02-principles.md) question first — *build the advantage, buy the commodity* — and an ownership question only if the answer is *build*.** ⛔ **Per-recipient read state is the most commodity thing a notification vendor sells.**

### The three options, with what each costs

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | **Novu's inbox owns it** | ✅ **No table, no migration, no new bounded context, no RLS surface.** ⛔ **Costs: unread state leaves our database, so it cannot be joined, replayed or audited with our own data, and [§20b](../CLAUDE.md)'s offline story weakens.** ⚠️ **Needs ADR-0017 amended to say the inbox is in scope — it currently says neither** |
| **②** | **`workspace_tenancy` owns it** | ✅ **The table is `(workspace_id, user_id, …)` and that module already owns workspace identity and membership, so the tenancy and the foreign keys are already there.** ⛔ **Costs: unread state is not tenancy. The module's stated context is *"the tenancy root"*, and a notification concern lands in it because the ids are convenient — which is [§4](../CLAUDE.md)'s *never repurpose a term from one module inside another*** |
| **③** | **A new bounded context** | ✅ **Honest about what it is, and [§20a](../CLAUDE.md) does not bar a new MODULE — only platform changes.** ⛔ **Costs: 🔴 a new bounded context is a product-owner + ADR decision, and it is a whole module for one table until the Notification Center is built** |

### ⚡ Recommendation, and it is deliberately conditional

**Rule out ① or adopt it BEFORE choosing between ② and ③.** ⛔ **Choosing an owner for a table we may not need is the expensive order to do this in.**

**If ① is refused, this office recommends ③ over ②** — 📁 **[`Fortune Signora Notification Center.dc.html`](design-snapshot/screens/) is a full screen design, so this is not one table for one badge; it is the first slice of a context that already has an approved surface.** ⚡ **[TASK-495](BACKLOG.md) *Notification delivery through the ratified vendor* is already a row, which means the context exists in the backlog whatever we call it.**


### 🔴 Evidence pass, 2026-08-10 — and it moves the question

**Product owner asked for evidence before ruling. Two of this office's own assumptions did not survive it.**

⛔ **CORRECTION 1.** **I first read [`Fortune Signora Notification Center.dc.html`](../design-snapshot/screens/) and concluded it was *"a preferences screen — no inbox, no feed, no unread count"*.** ⚠️ **I had read 55 lines of a 12-section document.** ✅ **§07 *Notification history & delivery log* and §08 *Inbox, empty, loading & failure* both exist.** **The design specifies an inbox in detail.**

⛔ **CORRECTION 2.** **`grep` for *notification* matched `workspace_tenancy/domain/preferences.py` and `infrastructure/delivery.py`, which looked like existing notification ownership.** ✅ **Opened both: `preferences.py` is theme and density; `delivery.py` is `ConsoleInvitationDelivery`.** ⛔ **`workspace_tenancy` owns NO notification concern today** — a keyword match, which is the instrument [D-220](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §10 forbids relying on.

#### What the finalized design requires — measured, not inferred

📁 **§08 Inbox**: unread count · **Mark all read** · filters `All` · `Direct` · `AI` · **`Held · 4`** · grouping — *"Grouped: 6 more events on Halden Systems"* · empty state — *"You have read everything. 4 items are held until 07:00 and 3 rules are muted"* · ⛔ **a correctness constraint: *"The inbox loads from cache first and reconciles in the background. Unread counts never decrease optimistically."***

📁 **§07 Delivery log**: **last 30 days, every attempt including failures** · columns **When · Notification · Channel · Delivery · Opened · Acted** · **Export** · channel filter.

📁 **App Shell §10**: *"Opening the panel does not mark items read; opening an item does."*

#### 🔴 The discriminator, and it is §07 rather than the inbox

⚡ **The inbox alone is a commodity and a vendor could plausibly own it.** ⛔ **§07 is not**: *Opened* and *Acted* per notification, **exportable, thirty days, including failed attempts** — and 📁 [§17](../../CLAUDE.md) *observability is a product capability*: **a system cannot be improved using information it never recorded.**

⛔ **And the inbox is not generic either**: it groups by **account**, and its empty state joins **held items** to Signora quiet hours and **muted rules** to Signora alert rules. **Three Signora domain concepts inside a feed row.**

#### ⚠️ What this office CANNOT verify, stated rather than assumed

⛔ **Novu appears in ZERO source files** — `grep -rli novu` across `backend/` and `frontend/` returns nothing. **[ADR-0017](architecture/adr/0017-notifications.md) is `Accepted` and nothing is integrated**, so *"what our current integration provides"* is **nothing**, and [TASK-495](BACKLOG.md) is the row that would build it.

🔴 **Novu's actual product capability is NOT verified here.** **No vendor documentation was consulted — this office has no approved documentation path to it in this session.** ⛔ **Every statement about what Novu can do would be recall, not evidence, and [D-220](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §10 forbids exactly that.** ✅ **The matrix column is left UNVERIFIED rather than filled plausibly.**

### ⛔ What this office did not do

**Did not choose. Did not create the module. Did not amend ADR-0017.** 📁 **A new bounded context and a vendor-scope change are both 🔴** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md) Change Budget), **and Lane A was right that this is architectural rather than implementation.**

## C-1420 · TASK-1430's module registry and its ruling name different lanes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Opened** | **2026-08-10, Lane C**, on QE's report that `TASK-1430` is `READY` and appears in no lane queue |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⚡ **an ownership reconciliation, and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) reserves those** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — 2026-08-10, ruled OUTCOME B by the product owner.** ⚡ **The Module cell was wrong; the registry was not. `TASK-1430` is `product_surface`, Lane A, and stays with Lane A** |
| **Module** | **`platform_foundation`** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **[TASK-1430](BACKLOG.md) is invisible to Lane A's poll** |


### 🔴 The conflict, measured rather than recalled

📁 **[TASK-1430](BACKLOG.md)'s Module cell reads `platform_foundation`.**
📁 **[`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) assigns `platform_foundation` to **Lane C** — `current_owner = "Lane C"`, `transition = "settled"`.**
⛔ **The same row says, in terms: *"implemented by LANE A, not by this office"* ([D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4).**

> ⚠️ **The registry says Lane C. The ruling says Lane A. Both cannot be executed.**

### ⚡ Why it surfaced now, and why the obvious fix does not work

**QE reported the row as `READY` and in no queue.** ✅ **Adding it to [`queues/lane-a.toml`](coordination/queues/lane-a.toml) was tried and reverted within minutes**: the generator joins ownership from `modules.toml`, resolved the row to **Lane C**, and overrode the hand-edit.

⛔ **That is the generator behaving correctly** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *no document restates an assignee; ownership is joined at render time*). **A queue file cannot express a ruling that contradicts the registry, and it should not be able to.**

### ⚠️ And the label may itself be the defect

📁 **`modules.toml` describes `platform_foundation` as *"Environment framework, repository tooling, developer commands"*.**
⛔ **TASK-1430 is INBOUND RATE LIMITING in `signora_platform/` — production platform code, not tooling.**

⚡ **So [D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4 may be exactly right and the Module cell simply wrong**, which would make this a one-word correction rather than an ownership question. **Stated as a possibility. Not asserted, and not acted on.**

### ⛔ What this office did not do

**Did not force the queue. Did not re-label the module. Did not re-rule D-232.**

📁 **[D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md): *"Verify first. Change only when evidence proves the current model is incorrect. Never invent a new process merely because an existing process initially appears ambiguous."*** **An ownership change requires its own explicit decision** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), and [C-213](#c-213) is what it costs when one is inferred).

### ✅ The decision needed, and it is one word

| | |
|---|---|
| **①** | **The Module cell is wrong.** Correct it to the module that owns inbound request handling; **[D-232](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4 stands unchanged and Lane A implements** |
| **②** | **The ruling is superseded and Lane C implements it** — in which case [§20a](../CLAUDE.md) applies and the row **already says it needs an ADR** |

⚡ **Until one is chosen the row is invisible to Lane A's poll, and that is the cost being paid** — **the same shape as [C-426](#c-426), one layer down: there the projection was stale, here the projection is correct and the inputs disagree.**

| ⛔ **What this office did NOT do** | **Create a UI because the API exists** ([D-231](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §3) **or delete it because it has no caller** (same). ⚡ **Both were available and both would have been this office deciding a product question by acting** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **No lane is waiting and no row is parked on it** |

### 🔴 The measurement

**Swept all 59 backend routes for a frontend caller. Eight have none.** ✅ **Seven are explained** — four `saved-views` routes have [TASK-452](BACKLOG.md) *"the screens that use it"* `READY`, `accounts-list` has [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md), and `approach` and `decision-package` have rows in validation.

⛔ **One is explained by nothing:**

```
GET /workspaces/{id}/icp-performance
    "Whether each declared criterion actually predicts a win"
    opportunity_engine · shipped by TASK-406 · has an integration test
```

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Frontend callers** | ⛔ **Zero** — checked as a path, a hook name and a camelCase identifier |
| **Backlog rows** | ⛔ **Zero.** No row mentions it, in any state |
| **Screen designs drawing it** | ⛔ **None.** `ICP` appears in `Design Review` and `AI Copilot` only, neither of which is a screen this product builds |

### ⚡ Why this is the INVERSE of [C-1416](#c-1416), and worth its own item

📁 **[C-1416](#c-1416) is four instances of one shape: *the design describes a product further along than this one*.** 🔴 **This is the opposite: the PRODUCT is further along than the design.**

⛔ **It is not the same finding and must not be folded into it.** ⚡ **C-1416's remedy is *ship the designed absent state and wait for the domain*. That remedy is meaningless here** — the domain exists, is tested, and answers a real commercial question. **There is simply no screen asking it.**

### ⛔ What this office deliberately did NOT do

**Create a row.** 📁 **[D-225](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §5 is the precedent and it is exact**: *"If the design specifies the Accounts index: implement it from the design. If the design does not specify it: **do not invent the screen. Raise the exact missing-design question instead.**"*

⚡ **A row here would be inventing scope** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md) — this office *"may not introduce scope the product owner has not approved"*), **and inventing a screen for a capability is a larger invention than inventing a task.**

### ✅ The question, asked once

> ## **`icp-performance` answers *whether each declared ICP criterion actually predicts a win*. Does a customer ever see that, and on which screen?**

**Three outcomes and this office recommends none:**

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **A design names it** | **It becomes a row like any other** |
| ⚠️ **It is a reporting concern** | **It belongs to Reports or the Executive Dashboard, both `planned`, and waits for them** |
| ⛔ **It is premature** | **The capability stands as correct, unreached backend, recorded as such rather than quietly rotting** — 📁 **and [TASK-438](BACKLOG.md)'s `pipeline-health` is the same shape and already known** |

It does not establish authorization semantics the product must adopt.** ⛔ **Had it been canonical, `Team Management` would assign those five.** ✅ **Record the distinction, let implementation continue, introduce no five-role RBAC, redesign no screens** |

### ✅ First — most of [C-277](#c-277) dissolves, and Lane A was measuring its own code rather than the design

Different job, different moment** — a summary where somebody chooses, a comparison where somebody checks |

The design names `Admin · Manager · Rep · Analyst · Guest`.** ⛔ **Not one of the design's five exists.** **It is not a subset — it is a different model** |

> ## ⛔ **So the matrix cannot be rendered truthfully, and that is the whole blocker.** ✅ **Nothing about the design's vocabulary or its form is the problem.**

### 🔴 The pattern, and why it is one question rather than three

| Item | The design assumes | The repository has |
|---|---|---|
| **[C-272](#c-272)** | *"The Executive Dashboard already built"* | ⛔ **No such screen** — the composition exists, the screen does not |
| **[C-1415](#c-1415)** | A workspace has a **region**, an **environment**, a **fiscal calendar** | ⛔ **`WorkspaceResponse` is `id · name · created_at · updated_at`** |
| **[C-277](#c-277)** | **Five roles across seven capabilities in five grades** | ⛔ **Two roles** |

| **[TASK-1420](BACKLOG.md)** *(added 2026-08-10)* | **Entitlement · support tickets · region-scoped status · a docs corpus** | ⛔ **None of the four has a source** |

⚡ **FOURTH INSTANCE, reported by Lane A on the poll after this item was filed.** 🔴 **And it carries the sharpest statement of the risk anybody has made: *"a contractual response time is the worst possible thing to invent."*** ✅ **That is this whole item in one sentence** — the cost of fabricating a missing model is not a wrong pixel, it is a customer believing a commitment the product never made.

⚡ **Four rows, four screens, three days, one shape: the finalized design describes a product further along than this one.** ⛔ **That is not a criticism of the design — a design SHOULD describe the product being built.** ✅ **It is a statement about sequencing, and it will recur on every screen until the domain catches up.**

### ✅ What every lane has already done, correctly and without being told

📁 **Ship the designed absent state and do not fabricate the missing model.** ⚡ **Lane A reached this three times independently** — the rail's routeless entries rendered as locked rather than hidden, the region selector left absent because *"a customer would choose one"*, and this matrix reverted with no residue.

⛔ **The alternative is the failure the Settings screen already names in its own words**: **a control populated with plausible values is worse than an absent one, because a customer will believe it.** 🔴 **A five-column matrix over a two-role product is that failure at its largest — four of five columns would mean nothing, and a customer comparing them would be reading fiction.**

### 🔴 The one question, asked once

> ## **Does the product acquire the design's role model — `Admin · Manager · Rep · Analyst · Guest` across seven capabilities — and if so, when?**

⛔ **This office does not recommend either answer.** ⚡ **It is a product decision about what Signora sells, not a schema question**, and the same is true of a workspace's region, environment and fiscal calendar in [C-1415](#c-1415).

✅ **Until it is answered, nothing is blocked**: the designed absent state is correct, three lanes have already shipped it, and [D-225](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4's principle — *the unresolved design question must not create a functional regression* — already governs the behaviour.

## C-1415 · Two rows hit one gap: a workspace publishes its identity and nothing about its character

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-10 — ⚡ **on Lane A's request to *"see it as a pattern rather than as two separate gaps"*, which is the correct reading** |
| **Owner** | ⚠️ **SPLIT, and the split is the finding** — **the read-shape half is Lane A's own module; the domain half is the product owner's** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** *(half)* · 🔴 **MISSING DOMAIN DECISION** *(half)* |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-10 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ✅ **Both rows ship a designed locked state instead, which the design itself asks for** |

### 🔴 The measurement, from `origin/main`

📁 **`GET /workspaces` — *"List the workspaces the caller belongs to"* — returns `CursorPage[WorkspaceResponse]`, and `WorkspaceResponse` is exactly four fields:**

```
id · name · created_at · updated_at
```

**So the switcher and the Settings identity block both read the same four fields, and neither finds what it needs.**

### ⚡ But the two halves are NOT the same defect, and treating them as one would misroute both

| What is wanted | Modelled? | Class | Whose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The caller's ROLE per workspace** ([C-276](#c-276)) | ✅ **YES** — `MembershipResponse` publishes `role` with `workspace_id`, and `GET /workspaces/{id}/members` returns it | ⚠️ **READ-SHAPE.** ⛔ **The endpoint that lists a caller's workspaces returns the WORKSPACE, not the membership** — so role is reachable only by one call per workspace, which is the N+1 [§14](../CLAUDE.md) forbids | **Lane A** — `workspace_tenancy` is its module, and this is 🟠 inside it |
| **Environment** ([C-276](#c-276)) · **region** · **fiscal calendar** ([TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md)) | ⛔ **NO** — no field, no column, no domain concept | 🔴 **MISSING DOMAIN.** **Nothing to project, because nothing decided a workspace HAS these** | **Product owner** — *does a workspace have a region, an environment, a fiscal calendar?* is a product question, not a schema one |

> ## ⚡ **The pattern is real and the remedy is two remedies.** **One is a read returning the wrong shape and is cheap; three are concepts nobody has decided the product has.**

⛔ **`GET /workspaces` already filters by membership** — it knows the caller's role while assembling the page and discards it. ✅ **That is why the first half is small: the data is present at the moment the response is built.**

### ✅ What both lanes should keep doing meanwhile, and it needs no ruling

📁 **The Settings screen states it in its own words, and the design agrees:** ***"a region selector populated with plausible regions would be the mock business data §20c forbids, and worse than absent: a customer would choose one."*** ⚡ **Locked is shown, not hidden** — the same judgement [D-225](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4 ruled for navigation, and the same one Lane A applied to restricted rail destinations.

⛔ **Neither row is blocked**, and neither should wait on this item.

## C-1414 · The design system's specimens are drawn in sizes its own type system does not define

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-10, on Lane A's report from [TASK-1446](BACKLOG.md) — ⚡ **the lane found two divergent values and recorded them rather than quietly preferring one; measuring the whole section found six** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **derived from the artifacts, NOT escalated.** 📁 **[D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6: *"do not turn an implementation detail into a new Product Owner decision when the existing operating model already answers it"*** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **DESIGN CONFORMANCE** — ⛔ **not a defect in the design and not one in the implementation** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, on measurement** |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing.** ⚡ **Lane A already built to the correct reading before asking** |

### 🔴 The measurement — the whole section, not the two values reported

**§04's `typeRows` names eight roles, each with a token.** **§08 *Headers* draws seven distinct sizes.** ⛔ **Six of the seven match no §04 role:**

| §08 draws | §04 role |
|---|---|
| **30px** | ✅ `Metric` |
| **24 · 16 · 15 · 14.5 · 13 · 11.5px** | ⛔ **none — six of seven** |

### ✅ The rule, and it is a derivation rather than a decision

> ## **§04 is the type authority. §08's raw pixel values are illustrative and are not a second specification.**

⚡ **The reason is in the artifacts and needs no ruling: §04's entries NAME TOKENS — `--text-title`, `--text-label` — and §08's are inline `font-size:` inside a rendered mockup.** ⛔ **A section that names no token cannot be the token authority.** ✅ **Had this been a genuine contradiction between two specifications it would be Design Authority's; it is a specification and a picture of one.**

📁 **[D-138](DECISION_REGISTER.md) makes the snapshot the implementation authority; it does not make every pixel in it a requirement.** ⚡ **A specimen drawn at 24px where the token says 26 is a mockup imprecision, and treating it as a competing value would produce exactly the *"eleven screens, five heading treatments"* fragmentation [D-218](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §9 measured.**

✅ **Lane A reached this reading before asking and built to it** — *"I used the named roles, because §04 is the type authority."* **This item ratifies that reasoning and records the scope, so it is not re-derived per screen.**

### ⚠️ One correction, because the conclusion was right and the evidence was not

📁 **Lane A closed the `--text-label` question citing *"§08's fact strip renders its labels at 12.5px"*.** ⛔ **It renders them at 11.5px** — `{{ f.k }}` at `font-size:11.5px`, with `{{ f.v }}` at 14.5px.

✅ **The conclusion stands and is unaffected**, because it never rested on §08: **§04's `typeRows` carries `['Label', '--text-label', '12.5 / 1.45 / 600', 12.5, 600, …]` verbatim**, which is what this office measured when it answered. ⚡ **Recorded because a right answer resting on a wrong measurement is one refresh away from becoming a wrong answer** — and because Lane A extended this office the same courtesy on [C-270](#c-270--the-count-of-entry-destinations-that-render-nothing-is-eleven-on-record-and-eighteen-at-runtime).

### 🔴 The contradiction, in the row's own words

| The cell | What it says | Written |
|---|---|---|

| ⚡ **Trigger steward** | **Lane C**, and the cell argues the point directly: ⛔ ***"This is not a module assignment and does not become one."*** **The module stays undecided; somebody still watches the trigger** | **[D-135](DECISION_REGISTER.md), 2026-08-06** |

> ## ⚠️ **This is [§2](../CLAUDE.md) — *governance describes reality; it never quietly changes it* — in its documented shape: *if applying the edit would change what somebody does tomorrow, it needed a decision yesterday.***

**And it did change what somebody does tomorrow**, through the instrument rather than the prose: **[`queues/lane-a.toml`](coordination/queues/lane-a.toml) queues `TASK-412` to Lane A**, which is defensible *only* on the Change Budget, while the projection derived `Lane C` from the steward. ⛔ **[B-414](BUGS.md) fixed the tool. ⛔ **This office recommends neither.** ⚡ **The evidence for the second is that D-042 and D-135 both chose it deliberately and twice; the evidence for the first is that [424 §9b](architecture/424-usage-metering-assessment.md) is the preparation and D-187 read it before naming the path.** **Which of those is authoritative is the product owner's, not a derivation.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane C**, 2026-08-09, from the Common Platform Audit — **[498 §2.1](architecture/498-common-platform-audit.md)**, ruled as **[D-218](DECISION_REGISTER.md)** |

| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-09, the requesting lane, on the product owner's ruling.** ⚡ **Raised and answered inside one cycle** |

## ✅ RULED — [D-219](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6, product owner, 2026-08-09

> ## **Utility Panel first. Filter Strip second.**

📁 **The reasoning is the one this office recommended, and it is recorded here in the product owner's own terms:** *"The Utility Panel is a foundational shell capability explicitly referenced by the shell rules and intended to provide contextual information consistently across modules. Therefore the platform should establish it before individual workflows start independently deciding how contextual information should appear."*

⛔ **And the ruling closes the question rather than parking it:** 📁 *"Do not create another Product Owner decision around this unless implementation uncovers a genuine contradiction in the finalized design."*

### ⚡ What discharging it uncovered, which is better than the ruling assumed

🔴 **[TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md) was parked on a claim that measurement contradicts.** ⛔ **Its Status read *"all three tabs are module content and none exists"* — and `AccountHistory` ([`components/timeline/feed.tsx`](../frontend/components/timeline/feed.tsx)) has been rendering on the Account 360 record all along, at `app/(app)/accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx`:492.** ✅ **That IS the Activity tab's content.**

⚡ **So the row did not need its Definition of Done weakened to satisfy the ruling** ([D-219](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7) — **it needed the claim in its own Status cell checked.** ⚠️ **This office wrote that claim and did not check it, which is the same failure as [C-421](#c-421--the-design-authority-cannot-be-reached-by-any-implementation-lane): an absence asserted rather than tested.**

✅ **The real remaining dependency is ordinary and scheduled:** **the panel is tabbed, no shared `Tabs` exists, and [TASK-1448](BACKLOG.md) builds it** — ⚡ **which §11 of the ruling already places ahead of the panel, so the sequencing and the dependency agree without anybody adjusting either.**

⛔ **[TASK-1432](BACKLOG.md)'s prerequisite is genuinely NOT met and is named rather than glossed** ([D-219](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7): **no module reads `lib/shell/scope.ts`.** ✅ **It frees itself the moment one does, and no further ruling is required.**

🔴 **The measurement.** 📁 **[`lib/shell/constitution.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/constitution.ts) declares five `SHELL_REGIONS`; `app-shell.tsx` renders three.** ⛔ **The two absent ones were carved out of [TASK-1408](BACKLOG.md) by [D-215](DECISION_REGISTER.md) — correctly, and recorded honestly — and each was then `SEQUENCED` behind a consumer**: *"behind the first module that reads scope"* and *"behind the content its three tabs name"*.

> ⛔ **`grep` finds no other row in [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md) that mentions a scope consumer, or Insights, or Activity, or Notes.** ⚡ **So both regions are parked behind work that does not exist in the queue at all — which no instrument can distinguish from parked indefinitely.**

✅ **Both rows are right to be parked, and this item is not asking to release them.** **Their own Definitions of Done already require a consumer** — 📁 *"Setting a chip changes what at least one module renders"* · 📁 *"at least one tab renders real module content"* — **so releasing them to `READY` would make them claimable while unfinishable.**

⚠️ **What makes it worth a ruling now rather than later:** 📁 **[D-218](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §9 — *every future workflow inherits these shared platform components***. **Each further workflow built without the utility panel is one more screen that puts its context somewhere else**, and shell rule 08 — 📁 *"Context that describes content goes in the utility panel"* — **is unenforceable until the region exists.**

| The question | |
|---|---|
| ⓐ **Schedule a scope consumer** | **Which module reads `lib/shell/scope.ts` first, and when?** ⚡ **That single row releases [TASK-1432](BACKLOG.md)** |
| ⓑ **Schedule the first utility-panel tab** | **Insights, Activity or Notes — which module owns the first, and when?** ⚡ **That releases [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md)** |
| ⓒ **Accept the wait** | ✅ **A legitimate answer.** ⛔ **But it should be a decision rather than a side effect, and [TASK-1451](BACKLOG.md) then carries the interim cost: `TAB_ORDER` and `scope.ts` name a region the frame does not render** |

> ⚡ **This office's read, and it is a recommendation rather than a ruling.** **ⓑ before ⓐ.** 📁 **The utility panel is named by a shell rule that every subsequent screen is supposed to obey; the filter strip is named by none.** ⛔ **A rule nothing can satisfy is the more expensive of the two to leave open**, because each screen shipped meanwhile makes its own decision about where context goes, and those decisions are what a migration later has to undo.

| `/workspaces` | **404** | ⛔ **09 · 13**, and the fallback of **04 · 23** |

| `/account/deleted` · `/account/suspended` | **404** | ⛔ **01 · 02** |
| `/auth/locked` · `/auth/step-up` | **404** | ⛔ **03 · 05** |
| `/onboarding/:step` | ✅ **307 → `/signin`** | ✅ **18 — the only rule whose destination exists** |
| the intent path | ✅ **307 → `/signin`** | ✅ **06**, ⛔ **and the intent is never captured, so it is never taken** |

### ⚡ Why it is worth a number rather than a shrug

⛔ **The two figures imply different work.** **Eleven of twenty-four reads as a subsystem most of the way there; eighteen of twenty-four reads as a subsystem with two live rules.** ✅ **And the second framing makes [TASK-1438](BACKLOG.md) obviously the highest-leverage row in the set** — 📁 **it alone converts eight rules from 404 to reachable, which no other row comes close to.**

⚠️ **This lane may have the smaller number's basis wrong** — *terminal* has a precise meaning in `rules.ts` (`kind: 'terminal'`, 20 of the 24) and **eleven may have counted something narrower on purpose.** ⛔ **Which is exactly why this is raised rather than corrected.**

## C-271 · Rule 04 asks for behaviour a route-returning function cannot express

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, **inside [TASK-1456](BACKLOG.md)'s audit** |
| **Owner** | **Design Authority** — ⚡ **routed through Lane C** ([D-224](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7) |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⛔ **DESIGN AMBIGUITY** — ⚡ **and a narrow one: twenty-three of the twenty-four rules are unaffected** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10, on analysis.** ⚡ **Reopened first: it had been closed by an editing mistake with no analysis under it** ([B-419](BUGS.md)), **and closing it a second time without doing the work would have been the worse error** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Rule 04 only.** ✅ **[TASK-1456](BACKLOG.md)'s audit completed around it, per [D-224](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §7's *surgically*** |
| ✅ **ANSWERED — most of it dissolves, and no type needs widening** *(Lane C, 2026-08-10)* | 🔴 **Lane A declined to widen `EntryDecision` on an inference, and was right to — but the widening was never needed.** 📁 **`EntryDecision` is `{ route · reason · gate · workspaceId }`, and `reason` is already `SESSION_EXPIRED`.** ⚡ **So the engine CAN identify rule 04's case exactly; what it cannot do is *perform* re-authentication in place — and it is not being asked to** |
| ⚡ **The two halves, and only one of them is the engine's** | **"Re-authenticate IN PLACE. Route, filters and unsaved drafts preserved" is a SCREEN behaviour, not a routing one.** ✅ **The engine's contract is *which decision is this*; the caller's is *what to do about it*.** 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md), the least-powerful-author rule: the engine identifies, the caller acts.** ⛔ **A caller seeing `SESSION_EXPIRED` mounts a re-authentication surface over the live DOM rather than navigating** — **filters and drafts survive because nothing unmounted them**, which is the only way they *could* survive. ✅ **The `route` it also returns is the fallback for a caller that cannot do that, and `intent?.path ?? WORKSPACES` is a correct fallback** |
| 🔴 **What is genuinely open is narrow, and was already raised** | 📁 **`rules.ts`:194 says it in the code**: *"With no intent there is nothing to preserve, and the document does not say where that lands — raised at [C-250](#c-250) rather than invented into a product decision."* ✅ **That is the residual question and it is [C-250](#c-250)'s, already with the product owner as a behaviour a customer sees.** ⛔ **Not duplicated here** — 📁 **[C-1416](#c-1416) is what asking one question three times costs** |
| ⚠️ **So this item needed no Design Authority ruling** | ⛔ **It was routed to Design Authority through this office on the reading that the design asks the ENGINE for something impossible.** ✅ **It does not — it asks the SCREEN.** ⚡ **Twenty-three of twenty-four rules were never affected, and the twenty-fourth is affected only in the half nobody had separated.** 📁 **[D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6: do not manufacture a product decision the artifacts already answer** |

### The question

📁 **Rule 04, `SESSION_EXPIRED`: *"Re-authenticate **in place**. Route, filters and **unsaved drafts** preserved and restored."*** Destination column: *"(intent preserved)"*.

⛔ **Every other rule answers *where does this person go*. This one answers *do not go anywhere* — and it names two kinds of state, filters and unsaved drafts, that no route can carry.**

📁 **The implementation resolves it by picking the readable half**: [`rules.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts):196 returns `intent?.path ?? '/workspaces'`. ✅ **A reasonable reading.** ⛔ **But it makes rule 04 a navigation, which is the one thing the design says it is not** — and the fallback 404s.

> **So: is rule 04 a routing rule at all?** ⓐ **A modal contract the engine only tags**, leaving the current route mounted and the DOM alive · ⓑ **a routing rule whose destination genuinely is the current path**, with draft preservation a separate concern the design mentions in passing · ⓒ **something else.**

⚠️ **The distinction is not cosmetic: ⓐ changes the shape of `EntryDecision`** — a decision that is *"stay here and show a modal"* is not a `{ route, reason }` — **and this lane will not widen a published contract on an inference.**

## C-274 · The switcher's exit and its destination are in different rows, and the destination is blocked

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, **implementing [TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **sequencing between three rows is row scope** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **SEQUENCING** — ⛔ **not a design defect; the design is unambiguous about where the switcher goes** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-10 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **One clause of [TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md)'s `Delivers`, and its `Definition of Done` as written.** ✅ **The other four slots shipped** |

### The conflict, in three lines

📁 **[TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md) `Delivers`**: *"⛔ **The workspace switcher LEAVES the top bar** — see [TASK-1441](BACKLOG.md)."*
📁 **[TASK-1441](BACKLOG.md)** puts it in the rail as its first child — ⛔ **and is `BLOCKED` behind [TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md)**, which is blocked on [C-269](#c-269).
📁 **[TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md) `Definition of Done`**: *"The top bar is the design's five slots **and nothing else**."*

> 🔴 **So the row that removes the control and the row that rehomes it are separated by two blocked rows.** ⛔ **Removing it today does not move it — it deletes it.** ⚡ **`WorkspaceSelector` is the only control a customer has for changing workspace**, and there is no second entrance.

### ✅ What this lane did, and why it is not the DoD being ignored

⛔ **The switcher stays, marked `data-not-a-slot="workspace-switcher"` in the markup and asserted as *not a slot* in `tests/components/top-bar.test.tsx`.** ⚡ **A test states today's truth so the day it changes is loud** — the same device `route-map.test.ts` uses for the absent `/w/` tree.

📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md) ranks the two harms and it is not close**: *a control that does nothing* is the defect the repository keeps finding, **and this control does something.** ⚠️ **Trading a rule violation for a capability loss is the trade this office rejected in [C-269](#c-269)**, on this lane's own evidence — 📁 *"an entry that leads nowhere advertises absence."* ⛔ **A missing switcher is worse than a misplaced one.**

### ⚡ The cheapest resolutions, and none is this lane's to pick

ⓐ **Let [TASK-1441](BACKLOG.md) move it into today's rail** rather than the design's — ⛔ **it is blocked on [TASK-1439](BACKLOG.md) only because the design's landmarks describe the design's rail**, and the control would work in either.
ⓑ **Amend [TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md)'s DoD** to *the design's five slots plus the switcher until [TASK-1441](BACKLOG.md)*, which is what shipped.
ⓒ **Accept the gap** — ⛔ **only if somebody decides a customer may not change workspace for the duration**, which nobody has.
