| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Slot 4 (notifications) and the help half of slot 5.** ✅ **Four slots shipped without them** |

### 🔴 The finding that generalises, and it is the sixth instance

⚠️ **Measured before this row's files existed**: 📁 **all six exports of [`lib/shell/top-bar.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/top-bar.ts) had ZERO production callers** — `TOP_BAR_SLOTS` · `SLOT_SPEC` · `SEARCH_WIDTH` · `statusLabelVisible` · `BADGE_CAP` · `badgeLabel`. ⛔ **The slot law was shipped by [TASK-1408](BACKLOG.md), covered by seven tests, and never consulted by the bar it governs.**

✅ **[TASK-1440](BACKLOG.md) gives `SLOT_SPEC` and `SEARCH_WIDTH` their first callers.** ⛔ **Three still have none, and that is reported rather than fixed by inventing a caller** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md): **a caller written to satisfy a count is the defect the count exists to find.**

> ⚡ **Sixth instance of one pattern**: 📁 the entry engine ([500](architecture/500-authenticated-entry-reconciliation.md)) · `lib/shell/scope.ts` · `command-palette.tsx` ([C-259](#c-259)) · `confidence.tsx` ([C-266](#c-266)) · `drawer.tsx` and `copyable-id.tsx` ([498](architecture/498-common-platform-audit.md) §5.1) · **and this.** ⛔ **[TASK-1451](BACKLOG.md)'s guard walks `components/ui` and would catch none of them.**

### Slot 4 · Notifications — nothing publishes one

📁 **The design wants a 400px popover, grouped by day, three tabs, and a badge that caps at 99+.** ✅ **`badgeLabel` already implements the cap.** ⛔ **Measured: no notification endpoint, no event feed, no unread count anywhere in `lib/api`.**

⚡ **A bell opening an empty 400px panel is precisely what [TASK-1433](BACKLOG.md) is parked for** — 📁 *"an empty panel does not reserve space for a future feature, it takes space from the one the customer is using today."* ✅ **So the slot is absent, and its absence is asserted in the test rather than left to be noticed.**

### Slot 3 · The healthy pill, and a correction to this lane's own first reading

⚠️ **This row's first draft claimed `OfflineStatus` consults `statusLabelVisible`. It does not** — 🔴 **caught by reading the file rather than by inferring the binding from the slot name, which is the third time this lane has made exactly that error.**

✅ **And `OfflineStatus` is right not to call it.** 📁 The helper's entire content is what the GREEN tone does at `<1280px`, and `OfflineStatus` never renders a green tone — 📁 its own note: *"online with an empty queue renders `null`… a pill whose only content is everything is fine is chrome that costs a slot every screen inherits."*

⛔ **So the design's healthy status pill is genuinely absent, and the five subsystems it names — Application, CRM sync, Scoring service, Conversation ingest, Exports — are published by nothing.** ⚡ **`statusLabelVisible` stays uncalled until a source exists.**

### Slot 5 · Help has no destination

📁 **`Fortune Signora Help Center.dc.html` is in the snapshot.** ⛔ **There is no help, docs or support route.** ⚡ **A help control that goes nowhere is [C-269](#c-269) in miniature and gets the same answer: absent, not *coming soon*.**

## C-276 · The switcher cannot show role or environment, and the design gives that a safety reason

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, **implementing [TASK-1441](BACKLOG.md)** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⚡ **which module publishes an environment is row scope, and the answer may be [C-256](#c-256)'s** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ✅ **MISSING IMPLEMENTATION** — ⛔ **the design is complete; the fields are not** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** — raised 2026-08-10 |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **[TASK-1441](BACKLOG.md) shipped the switcher without them** |

### The measurement

📁 **The design's row is *"22px avatar, name, role and environment, right-hand tag"*, grouped by organisation.** ⛔ **Measured: `Workspace` publishes `id` · `name` · `created_at` · `updated_at`. Nothing else.**

| Design | Source |
|---|---|
| Name · avatar | ✅ **`name`, initials derived** |
| Organisation grouping | ⛔ **no parent organisation on the contract** |
| Role per workspace | ⛔ **`useViewerRole` answers for the ACTIVE workspace only** |
| Environment · sandbox | ⛔ **no field** — ⚡ **and [C-256](#c-256) already carries the sandbox banner's half of this** |
| Right-hand tag | ⛔ **it renders the three above** |

### 🔴 Why this one is not cosmetic

📁 **The design states the reason, and it is a safety reason rather than an aesthetic one**: ***"Role and environment on the row prevent the classic mistake of editing production while thinking it is sandbox."***

⛔ **So the switcher this row shipped is exactly the control that warning describes** — **it moves a person between workspaces without telling them what they are entering.** ⚠️ **Today that is survivable because no sandbox exists to be confused with production.** 🔴 **The moment one does, this becomes the defect the design predicted**, and it will not announce itself.

### ⛔ What was deliberately NOT done

**A tag reading *"Prod"* on every row because no field says otherwise.** ⚡ **It would be the product asserting a fact it does not have, about the one thing the design says people get wrong** — 📁 [§2](../CLAUDE.md), and the same reasoning that kept a confidence figure off the signal queue ([C-267](#c-267)).

✅ **A test states the absence** so the day a field arrives is loud, and 📁 **fire-tested**: adding a `Production` label with nothing behind it fails it.

### ⚡ The cheapest first step, and it is one field

⛔ **Not the whole design.** ✅ **`environment` on `Workspace` alone closes the safety half** — grouping and per-workspace role are convenience, and **the mistake the design names is an environment mistake.**

## C-277 · The Settings design asks for a permission matrix this repository reviewed and rejected, with reasons that still hold

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, **implementing [TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **found by building it, and the build is reverted** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⚡ **it is a design-versus-repository conflict before it is an implementation question**, the same shape as [C-272](#c-272) |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **DESIGN CONFLICT** — ⛔ **not a missing implementation**: the thing the design asks for was built, reviewed, and deliberately replaced |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED` — Lane C, 2026-08-10.** 🔴 **TWO OF THIS LANE'S THREE OBJECTIONS DO NOT SURVIVE MEASUREMENT, and both are corrected below rather than defended.** ⚡ **The third holds and is worse than reported.** ⛔ **Re-scoping [TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md) is Product Office's**; nothing here holds up this lane. *(was `OPEN`, raised 2026-08-10)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **[TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md)'s *roles and permissions as an additive matrix*.** ✅ **Nothing else in the row** |

### What the design asks for

📁 **Settings, `permissionRows` and `roleHeads`**: **five roles — Admin · Manager · Rep · Analyst · Guest — across seven capabilities in five grades** (`full · region · own · read · none`), with two rows flagged. 📁 **[TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md)** carries it as *"roles and permissions as an additive matrix"* with an accessibility requirement for a real `<table>`.

### 🔴 What this repository already decided, and it is not a gap — it is a ruling in code

📁 **[`components/team/capabilities.ts`](../frontend/components/team/capabilities.ts) exists, is reviewed, and argues against the matrix by name:**

> ⛔ ***"`policy.csv` holds thirty tuples across twelve resources. A customer does not think in tuples and cannot act on one… which is one sentence, not a matrix."***
>
> ⛔ ***"A tooltip listing `member:add`, `member:remove`, `workspace:update` would be a lie by compression: it looks complete, omits twenty-seven rows, and uses engineering's vocabulary on the one screen where a customer is making a decision about a person."***
>
> ⛔ ***"It is deliberately not generated from the policy… the output would drift into resource names the moment somebody added a resource, and nobody would notice until a customer read it."***

⚡ **And the screen already renders it** — *"What each role can do"*, a `<details>` catalog in the customer's words, **one authoritative copy replacing three that had disagreed.**

### ⚠️ This lane built the matrix before reading that, and the guards caught it

✅ **Reported rather than quietly reverted.** **The matrix was written, mounted, and failed four existing tests** — 📁 `vocabulary.test.tsx`'s *"never uses the platform's vocabulary"* among them, **because the rows rendered `workspace:read` and `member:add` to a customer.**

⛔ **Two independent findings, and the second is the one that matters**: **it would have been a fourth copy of a fact that already has one authoritative representation** — 📁 exactly what `capabilities.ts` was created to end.

✅ **Fully reverted**: the component deleted, the mount removed, and the `ROLE_CAPABILITIES` export it needed in [`lib/state/permissions.ts`](../frontend/lib/state/permissions.ts) taken back out. **2258 tests green, tsc and eslint clean, no residue.**

### The question, and this lane does not answer it

⛔ **[D-154](DECISION_REGISTER.md) says the design wins when an implementation differs from it — *"Always."*** ⚠️ **And [D-217](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6 says existing code is not an argument for keeping it.** 🔴 **Both point at replacing the catalog with the matrix.**

⚡ **But the design's matrix cannot be rendered truthfully here**: **three of its five roles and six of its seven capabilities do not exist**, and rendering four tuples where the policy holds thirty is the *lie by compression* the catalog names.

> **So:** ⓐ **the catalog stands and the design's matrix is a future-state drawing** — the roles it shows are ones Signora does not have yet · ⓑ **the matrix replaces the catalog when the roles exist**, and [TASK-1412](BACKLOG.md)'s clause is premature rather than wrong · ⓒ **a matrix of the REAL two roles now**, ⛔ which this lane believes is the weakest option and says so: **it is the compression `capabilities.ts` rejects, in a table.**

---

### 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-10 — two of the three objections above are wrong, and they are this lane's errors

⚠️ **Left standing above and corrected here, in the order Lane C answered them.** ✅ **Both re-checked against the artifacts directly rather than accepted on report.**

#### ⛔ ① The vocabulary objection was about THIS LANE'S ROWS, not the design

📁 **Settings `permissionRows` is customer language throughout** — ✅ **verified**: *`View own accounts`* / note *"Records where they are owner"* · *`View all accounts`* / *"Across the workspace"* · *`Edit CRM fields`* / *"Write-back to Salesforce"*.

⛔ **The design never asks for tuples.** **`workspace:read` and `member:add` came from the implementation** — mine — **so ADR-0034 and the design are not in conflict. My rows were.** 🔴 **Filing an implementation defect as a design conflict is a worse error than the defect**, because it puts a question to Product Office that the artifacts already answer.

#### ⛔ ② *One sentence, not a matrix* is about a DIFFERENT MOMENT

📁 **`capabilities.ts` argues against a matrix AT A DECISION POINT**, and its own words say which: ***"they are deciding whether a colleague should be able to bring people in."*** ⚡ **That is the invite dialog, the role selector and the roster.**

📁 **The design's matrix is a reference grid on a settings screen.** ✅ **A summary where somebody CHOOSES and a comparison where somebody CHECKS are different jobs, and one does not replace the other.** ⛔ **So it would not have been a fourth copy of one fact** — it would have been a second rendering for a second purpose, which this lane has argued FOR elsewhere (📁 `navigation.tsx`'s *"one list, two renderings"*).

#### ✅ ③ The third objection holds, and it is the whole blocker

⛔ **This lane reported *three of five roles do not exist*. Measured: NOT ONE of the five exists.** 📁 The product has `TeamRole = 'owner' | 'member'`; the design names **Admin · Manager · Rep · Analyst · Guest**. ⚡ **It is not a subset — it is a different model**, so the matrix cannot be rendered truthfully **and nothing about the design's vocabulary or its form is the problem.**

⚠️ **Recorded as [C-1416](#c-1416)'s third instance** — 📁 **C-272 assumed an Executive Dashboard already built, [C-1415](#c-1415) assumed a workspace has region, environment and a fiscal calendar, and this assumes five roles.** **Three rows, three screens, two days, one shape.**

## C-284 · AI Research can be requested for an account and cannot be asked a question

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, from [TASK-1418](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Lane B** — 📁 [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) assigns `ai_research_engine`; ⛔ **not Lane A's to extend** |
| **State** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** |
| **Blocks** | **[TASK-1418](BACKLOG.md)'s central deliverable.** ✅ **Not the row entirely** — what the engine publishes is already surfaced, and this lane continued to the next row rather than idling ([D-229A](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |

**Measured, not assumed.** 📁 **`ai_research_engine/interface/router.py` publishes two endpoints** — `POST …/accounts/{id}/research` and `GET …/accounts/{id}/research`. ⚡ **Research is scoped to an ACCOUNT and takes no other input.**

🔴 **The design's subject is a QUESTION.** 📁 *"Why is EMEA enterprise slipping?"* — **scoped to a segment, a quarter and eleven open renewals**, with the answer becoming a document that carries its sources. ⛔ **Nothing in this product can be asked anything.**

⚠️ **This is not a missing screen; it is a missing capability, and the difference decides what may be built.** ⛔ **A `/research` route with a question box would be [§20c](../CLAUDE.md)'s failure in its worst form** — **not an empty state over an unbuilt list, but a control that invites the product's headline promise and cannot honour it.** 📁 **[TASK-1417](BACKLOG.md) shipped an empty state because a builder had no query engine; a question box with no question-answering is a different thing entirely.**

✅ **What already ships, so this is scoped rather than blocking:** 📁 **`ResearchPanel` surfaces every published feature** — the answer, its findings, the prompt, the model, the evidence digest, and the `requested`/`running` states with polling. **It also already distinguishes a failed read from *nobody has asked*, which is [P-A](DOMAIN_DISCOVERY_REGISTER.md).**

**What is needed, when somebody builds it.** ⚡ **A request that carries a question and a scope**, and an artifact that names the question it answers. ⛔ **The scope is the harder half** — *EMEA · Enterprise · Q3 FY26* is the filter strip's vocabulary ([`lib/shell/scope.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/scope.ts)), **and nothing currently reads it**, which is [TASK-1432](BACKLOG.md)'s own blocker.

## C-283 · A report's narrative has no capability that can write it, and one endpoint is not it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, from [TASK-1417](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Lane B** — 📁 [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml) assigns `ai_platform`'s inference surface; ⛔ **not Lane A's to extend** |
| **State** | 🟡 **`OPEN`** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚡ **The narrative's MERGE rule is built and tested; only its GENERATION waits** |

**Measured, not assumed.** 📁 **`backend/modules/ai_platform/interface/router.py` publishes exactly ONE endpoint** — `GET …/account-narration`, *"what the evidence about this account says, in plain language"*, **scoped to an account.** ⛔ **Nothing in the repository can write commentary over a report's blocks.**

**Why this is a dependency rather than something to build.** 📁 **The design's narrative is *"written from the blocks above, not from a separate prompt — so the prose cannot contradict the charts"*.** ⚡ **That is an inference over a report's own figures**, and [§10](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit: ⛔ **no mock provider, no fabricated inference.** ⚠️ **A narrative block that produced plausible sentences from a template would be indistinguishable from a working one** — **which is the exact failure mode [ADR-0028](architecture/adr/0028-model-runtime-by-environment.md) names for the mock in production.**

**What was built instead, and it is the half that has a law rather than a model.** ✅ **[`lib/reports/narrative.ts`](../frontend/lib/reports/narrative.ts) implements the design's guarantee** — *"edited sentences are preserved through regeneration and marked, so the board sees what a person asserted versus what the model derived"* — **as a pure merge over sentences.** ⚡ **`regenerate` takes the incoming sentences as an argument, calls nothing and knows no model**, ✅ **so the three refusals are tested today**: ⛔ never overwrite a person's sentence · ⛔ never relabel one as generated · ⛔ never delete or move one.

**What is needed, when somebody builds it.** **An inference whose input is a report's blocks and whose output is an ordered list of sentences with stable ids.** 🔴 **The ids are the whole contract** — ⚠️ **a generator that returned prose without them would make the merge above impossible**, because matching on text treats a person's edit as a deletion plus an insertion.

## C-282 · B-219 needs a one-line ruling and has never been routed to anyone who can give it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, on the poll that found it still `OPEN` |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — 📁 **the fix is `next.config`, which [§20c](../CLAUDE.md) and the Change Budget put at 🔴** |
| **State** | ✅ **`RULED` — product owner, 2026-08-11. APPROVED: `distDir`.** ⚡ **Implementation is [TASK-1465](BACKLOG.md), `READY` for Lane A.** ⛔ ***"Do not turn it into a broader build-system redesign."*** **Closes when [B-219](BUGS.md) does** |
| **Blocks** | **Lane C's [TASK-1431](BACKLOG.md)**, which is that lane's only claimable row. ⚠️ **It does not block Lane A** |

**The gap this row exists to close, and it is a process one.** ⛔ **[B-219](BUGS.md) has been `OPEN` since 2026-08-09 with its own status reading *"Not fixed: `next.config` and the runbook are frontend foundation, 🔴 in the Change Budget."*** 🔴 **Nothing carried it any further.** ⚡ **A defect whose fix a lane may not make, with no coordination item, is a defect that can sit forever** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"an item exists only when another module's assignee or the product owner must answer something before implementation can safely continue."* **That was true of B-219 on the day it was filed.**

⚠️ **This lane filed the bug and did not file the item, and that is the miss.** ⛔ **Recording the blocker in the row it blocks is not the same as routing it.**

**The problem.** 📁 **`next dev` and `next build` share one `.next/`.** ⚡ **Completion gate 4 (`next build`) destroys the dev server that gate 5 (the headed journey) runs against**, and ⛔ **the symptom names the wrong subsystem entirely**: every route returns `500`, Playwright fails at *"sign in as the owner"*, and **the diagnosis goes to authentication.** **This lane spent it there — rate limiting, then the Better Auth tables, then which schema they were in.**

**The alternatives, unchanged from the row.**

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | ⚡ **`distDir` for the production build** | ✅ **One line.** **The two stop sharing state and the ordering stops mattering** |
| **②** | **Runbook order** | ⛔ **Weaker — it relies on remembering**, and the whole defect is that nobody remembers |
| **③** | **`make validate` restarts the dev server** | **Most convenient, most machinery** |

**The recommendation, and it is input rather than authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). ✅ **Option ①.** ⚡ **It removes the interaction instead of documenting it**, which is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s preference for a violation that is *unrepresentable* over one that is *discouraged* — **and it is the only one of the three that cannot be forgotten.**

**The implementation impact.** ⛔ **One line in `frontend/next.config.ts` and a sentence in [`RUNNING.md`](RUNNING.md)** — **whose owner is QE.** ⚡ **No product code, no migration, no test change.** ⚠️ **Every lane that runs the Completion gates is exposed to this today**, which is why it is worth a minute rather than a cycle.


## C-281 · Meilisearch is ratified as a vendor and unowned as a module, and a second datastore needs an exception a lane cannot grant

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, evaluating [TASK-496](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — ⚡ **one half is an architecture decision and the other is a Principle 6 exception** |
| **State** | ⏸️ **`REVIEW LATER` — product owner, 2026-08-11. DEFERRED.** ⛔ **No Meilisearch, no second datastore, no ADR, no module, no infrastructure, no Lane A task.** ⚡ **Return it only with a concrete customer-facing workflow and its alternatives** |
| **Blocks** | ⚪ **NO CUSTOMER-FACING WORKFLOW — reclassified REVIEW LATER, Lane C 2026-08-10, on the product owner's own test.** 📁 **They asked: *is Meilisearch actually required for the customer-facing workflow, or merely the currently proposed technical implementation?*** ✅ **Measured, and it is the second.** 📁 **[TASK-496](BACKLOG.md)'s own cells answer it: *"a search read path already works"* ([450](architecture/450-global-search-traceability-audit.md)), and *"this row replaces the INDEX, not the surface, and the surface must not change"* — with **Routes unchanged · APIs unchanged**.** ⛔ **So no customer capability is missing and none is blocked.** ⚡ **Meilisearch has ONE reference in the entire repository — `infra/repository-dashboard.py` — and no adapter, no config, no compose service.** 🔴 **A second datastore still needs an ADR if it is ever adopted, and Principle 6 is untouched by this reclassification.** ✅ **But the product owner's directive is explicit: do not create a Product Owner blocker merely because a vendor was previously ratified.** **Bring it back when a design says what is searched and PostgreSQL is measured insufficient — neither has happened** |

**What is NOT the problem.** ✅ **The vendor is ratified** — 📁 [09-build-vs-buy.md](architecture/09-build-vs-buy.md) — **so this is not a dependency question**, and it is deliberately not filed as one alongside [C-280](#c-280--two-of-task-493s-four-better-auth-plugins-do-not-ship-in-the-installed-version-so-adopting-them-is-a-dependency-decision), which is.

**① The owning module is explicitly undecided.** 📁 **The row's own Module cell**: *"the index adapter's owning module is decided at decomposition, when a design says what is searched."* ⛔ **Building the adapter answers that**, and 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit: *"a dependency on a decision nobody has made is architectural however small the code would be."*

**② A second datastore needs an exception, and stating one is not granting one.** 📁 **[§3](../CLAUDE.md) Principle 6 is a single PostgreSQL database**, and 📁 **[§8](../CLAUDE.md)**: *"Claude must never introduce a second datastore… without an explicit, approved exception."* ⚠️ **The row says the exception *"must be stated in the commit"*.** ⛔ **A lane can state it; only the product owner can approve it** — 📁 [§3](../CLAUDE.md): *"never silently work around a principle because compliance is inconvenient for the task at hand. If a principle appears to block a legitimate need, that is a signal to stop and raise it, not to route around it."*

**The alternatives.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **①** | ✅ **Grant the exception explicitly**, naming Meilisearch as a **derived index rather than a system of record** — ⚡ **which is the distinction Principle 6 actually protects**, and 📁 [§8](../CLAUDE.md) already phrases the danger as *"a cache used as a system of record"* |
| **②** | **Defer, and keep the Postgres search path** — 📁 [450](architecture/450-global-search-traceability-audit.md) measured that it works, and ⛔ **[TASK-481](BACKLOG.md) shipped its surface against it** |

**The recommendation, and it is input rather than authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). ✅ **Option ①, with the exception worded as *derived index, never a system of record*** — ⚡ **because that is what makes it survivable**: the index can be dropped and rebuilt from Postgres at any time, so no customer data lives only there.

🔴 **And the Security Invariant the row itself names is the reason this is worth ruling carefully**: ***"an index is a SECOND place tenant data lives — workspace scoping asserted at query time, not assumed."*** ⚠️ **Meilisearch has no RLS.** ⛔ **Every tenancy guarantee [§11](../CLAUDE.md) makes is a Postgres guarantee**, so the index reproduces none of them and the scoping must be proven in the adapter rather than inherited.


## C-280 · Two of TASK-493's four Better Auth plugins do not ship in the installed version, so adopting them is a dependency decision

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, building [TASK-493](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner + an ADR** — 📁 [§6](../CLAUDE.md): *"never introduce a new framework, library, or major dependency without explicit approval"*, and [§21](../CLAUDE.md) repeats it |
| **State** | ⏸️ **`REVIEW LATER` — product owner, 2026-08-11. DEFERRED.** ⛔ **Do NOT upgrade Better Auth for passkey/SSO now, and do NOT write an ADR.** ✅ **Ship `two-factor` and `multi-session`, which exist in 1.6.25.** ⚡ **[TASK-493](BACKLOG.md) is rescoped: *ship now* vs *deferred*, and the deferral must not block the pipeline** |
| **Blocks** | **Half of [TASK-493](BACKLOG.md).** ✅ **The other half is built and `IN VALIDATION`** |

**The measurement.** 📁 **The row states *"All four ship in Better Auth 1.6.25 and are UNREGISTERED"*.** ⚠️ **Two do and two do not**, and it was checked against `node_modules` rather than against a memory of the vendor's documentation:

| | Ships in 1.6.25? |
|---|---|
| **`two-factor`** | ✅ **Yes** — `better-auth/dist/plugins/two-factor` · **registered by this slice** |
| **`multi-session`** | ✅ **Yes** — `better-auth/dist/plugins/multi-session` · **registered by this slice** |
| **`passkey`** | ⛔ **No.** `require.resolve('better-auth/plugins/passkey')` throws; the name appears nowhere in the package |
| **`sso`** | ⛔ **No.** Same |

**Why a lane cannot simply install them.** 🔴 **Each is a separate package**, so adopting either is **a new dependency** — ⛔ **and the row's own Change Budget is 🟠 one file with 🔴 nothing.** ⚡ **A lane that `npm install`s its way past that has worked around a repository rule**, which [§21](../CLAUDE.md) forbids by name.

**Why it matters beyond the packaging.** ⚠️ **Passkeys and SSO are both authentication mechanisms**, and 📁 [§13](../CLAUDE.md) is emphatic that authentication is **bought, not built**, with Better Auth as the sole Authority. ✅ **Adopting the vendor's own packages is the compliant route** — ⛔ **but it is still an adoption, and [09-build-vs-buy.md](architecture/09-build-vs-buy.md) is where that is recorded.**

**The recommendation, and it is input rather than authority.** ✅ **Adopt both, as vendor packages, under one ADR** — **they are the same decision** (Better Auth ecosystem plugins for capabilities [493](architecture/493-security-platform-architecture.md) already anticipates), **and splitting them would produce two ADRs with one argument.** ⚠️ **SSO additionally interacts with [C-431](#c-431--three-controls-on-the-approved-sign-in-card-have-no-backing-capability)**, whose sign-in card already draws a control with no backing capability.

**The implementation impact once ruled.** ⚡ **Small and additive**: two `npm` dependencies, two lines in the same registry file, and Better Auth's own schema push — ⛔ **no Signora API changes, no Alembic migration** (📁 `0005_auth_schema.py`: *"this migration creates the schema and nothing inside it"* — **Better Auth owns its tables**).

> ⚡ **`tests/unit/auth-plugins.test.ts` asserts the absence rather than only reporting it**, and **it fails in the correct direction**: if a future upgrade ships the two plugins, the resolve-throws assertion breaks and the row becomes buildable. ⛔ **Until then it is what stops a later session quietly adding a dependency to satisfy a row that says all four ship.**


## C-279 · TASK-480's notification badge has three candidate sources, and two are foreclosed by rules the repository already has

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, on [TASK-480](BACKLOG.md)'s own instruction: ⚠️ *"Nothing publishes a notification today. Whether the badge counts a domain event, an outbox row or an unread record is a question for the design, and [D-140](DECISION_REGISTER.md) says ask one precise question rather than make one convenient assumption."* |
| **Owner** | ⛔ **Product owner** — it is a product decision about what a notification *is*, and an architecture decision about which module owns it |
| **State** | ⏸️ **`REVIEW LATER` — product owner, 2026-08-11. CONSOLIDATED INTO [C-1421](#c-1421).** ⛔ **Do not decide it here; the findings stay documented on both** |
| **Blocks** | ⚪ **NOTHING IN THE CURRENT PRIORITY SET — reclassified REVIEW LATER, Lane C 2026-08-10.** ⛔ **It blocks [TASK-480](BACKLOG.md), a notification badge, and nothing else.** ⚡ **The product owner's implementation-first order puts the shell, navigation, common layout and shared components ahead of it, and none of those needs this answer.** 🔴 **So it must not hold the queue**: *"there is an architectural question, therefore implementation is blocked"* is the reasoning the directive forbids. ✅ **The evidence pass stands and is not repeated** — §07 requires an exportable 30-day log with `Opened` and `Acted`, so Signora owns SOME interaction record whatever Novu provides. **Bring it back when the Notification Center is scheduled** |

**The problem.** 📁 **The App Shell §10 design is rich about the SHAPE** — *"a 400px popover, not a page, with three tabs: Needs you, Mentions, All… grouped by day, unread carries a 6px brand dot rather than a coloured row… Agent and AI notifications are marked with the intelligence hue so a generated nudge never reads as a colleague's request"* — ⛔ **and silent about what the badge COUNTS.**

**The affected modules.** `product_surface` (the surface) · a new workspace-scoped read model **whose owning module is not yet decided** · `signora_platform`'s outbox, if option ② were taken.

**The alternatives, and why two are already closed.**

| | Option | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **①** | **A count of domain events** | ⛔ **Closed by the design itself.** ⚡ **The design has *"Mark all read"* and a per-item unread dot**, and **a domain event is workspace-wide with no per-recipient state** — so two people could never have different unread counts, which the design plainly requires |
| **②** | **A count of outbox rows** | ⛔ **Closed by [§8](../CLAUDE.md), absolutely.** 📁 *"`outbox_event` … a business module must never query one — not to check whether an event was relayed, not to inspect a dead letter, not for debugging."* ⚡ **These tables carry no RLS**, so the grant is the only thing separating tenants there |
| **③** | **A per-person unread record** | ✅ **The only option the existing rules leave standing**, and the one the design's *"Mark all read"* and per-person dot imply |

**The recommendation, and it is input rather than authority** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)). ✅ **Option ③**, as a **person-scoped read model** — 📁 the third tenancy class [492](architecture/492-person-scoped-tenancy.md) already ratified and [TASK-470](BACKLOG.md) already built for `person_preferences`, **so it needs no new classification and no new Security Invariant meaning.**

**The trade-off, stated.** ⚠️ **A per-person record means one row per recipient per notification**, which is more rows than a shared event with a read-marker set. ⛔ **The alternative shape — one notification row plus a per-person `read_at` join — is also option ③**, and the ruling need not choose between them; that is an implementation decision inside whichever module owns it.

**The implementation impact.** **One table with its `tenancy_policy.py` registration in the same change** ([§8](../CLAUDE.md)) · **one workspace-scoped read** · **the popover, its three tabs, the four kinds — agent · ai · human · system — and the four states.** ⚡ **None of it is blocked on Novu**: 📁 [TASK-495](BACKLOG.md) owns delivery and [ADR-0017](architecture/adr/0017-notifications.md) is its approval — **this row is what a customer sees, not how it is sent.**

> ⚠️ **Why this is raised rather than assumed, when two options are already closed.** ⛔ **The elimination is strong but it is still a lane's reading**, and 📁 the row itself instructed *ask one precise question*. ✅ **A single ruling unblocks the whole row**, and **the second half is the part a lane genuinely cannot decide**: `product_surface` owns no tables, and the natural owner may be `workspace_tenancy` or a new bounded context — 🔴 **which is an architectural blocker rather than an implementation one** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *two kinds of blocker*: *"a dependency on a decision nobody has made is architectural however small the code would be"*).


## C-278 · The design's single `header[banner]` cannot be expressed while the rail is full-height

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-10, **implementing [TASK-1444](BACKLOG.md)** — ⚡ **found by building it and producing the wrong thing first** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **it is a shell STRUCTURE question, not an accessibility one** |
| **Classification** ([D-208](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §4) | ⚠️ **DESIGN-VERSUS-LAYOUT** — ⛔ **the accessibility rule is satisfiable; the landmark GROUPING is not** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED BY THE DESIGN` — Lane A, 2026-08-10, hours after raising it.** ⛔ **This lane asked a question the artifacts already answer**, which is the error [C-277](#c-277) cost it earlier today, repeated. ⚡ **Found while fire-testing an unrelated guard**, not by re-reading. **No product-owner decision is needed.** *(was `OPEN`)* |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **[TASK-1444](BACKLOG.md) shipped every other landmark and all nine rules** |

### What the design asks for

📁 **App Shell `landmarks`, first entry**: ***"`header[banner]` — Environment and trial banners, then the top bar. First in the DOM, first in tab order."***

⚡ **One `banner` landmark, holding both.**

### 🔴 Why this shell cannot express it

⛔ **The rail is full-height.** The frame is: **banner strip spanning the width → [rail | (top bar, content)]** — so **the top bar sits inside the content column, beside the rail**, while the banners span above both. ⚡ **A single element cannot contain the banners and the top bar without also containing the rail**, which would make the rail part of the banner landmark.

### ⚠️ What this lane built first, and why it was worse than the gap

✅ **Reported rather than quietly reverted.** **A `<header>` was wrapped around the banner strip** — which looked like the fix and **gave the shell TWO `banner` landmarks**, because the top bar's element is already one. 🔴 **A screen-reader user choosing *banner* would have been offered a menu of two**, which is a worse outcome than the missing grouping.

✅ **Reverted.** **The top bar keeps the landmark, the banner strip is a plain region, and a test asserts there is exactly one `<header>`** so a second cannot arrive quietly.

### The question

> ⓐ **The layout changes** — the top bar spans the full width above the rail, which is what the design's landmark order implies and 📁 what its own App Shell drawing shows · ⓑ **the landmark grouping is accepted as unexpressible here** and the design's first entry is read as *banner strip, then top bar, in DOM order* rather than as one element · ⓒ **something else.**

⛔ **This lane does not pick**, because ⓐ is a shell restructure that would touch every screen and is not an accessibility defect — **every one of the nine `a11yRules` is satisfied either way.**

---

### ✅ RESOLVED — the design answers it, and the answer is ⓑ

📁 **App Shell, the reference-viewport paragraph, verbatim:**

> ***"Vertical order is fixed and non-negotiable: environment banner, trial banner, top bar, breadcrumb and filter strip, then the content region. **The rail spans the full height beneath the banners**; the utility panel docks to the right of content, never over it."***

⚡ **That is this shell exactly.** **The rail starts beneath the banners and runs to the bottom**, so the top bar necessarily sits beside it in the content column — ⛔ **which means the design does NOT ask for one element containing banners and top bar.** ✅ **`header[banner]`'s *"environment and trial banners, then the top bar"* describes DOM AND TAB ORDER**, which is what the same entry's next clause says: *"first in the DOM, first in tab order."*

⛔ **So ⓐ — restructuring the shell so the top bar spans above the rail — would have CONTRADICTED the design**, not implemented it. ⚠️ **This lane came close to proposing a restructure of every screen on a misreading of one landmark entry.**

✅ **Nothing changes in the code.** The top bar keeps the `banner` landmark, the banner strip stays a plain region, and the test asserting exactly one `<header>` is now asserting the design's structure rather than a compromise.

⚠️ **The lesson is the one [C-277](#c-277) already taught and this lane did not carry forward**: 📁 [D-228](DECISION_REGISTER.md) §6 — ***do not manufacture a product decision the artifacts already answer.*** **Read the whole design section before raising a structural question about it.**

## C-285 · Three designs publish a shortcut table and three chords carry two meanings

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, implementing [TASK-1445](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **it is a product decision about what a key means, and no lane may pick between two finalized designs** |
| **Status** | ⚠️ **`OPEN`** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ✅ **The keyboard map shipped** by following App Shell and saying so |
| **Becomes blocking when** | 🔴 **Anybody binds `E`, `⏎`, `⌘⏎` or `⌘⇧K`** — the four chords in dispute. **At that moment a lane must choose, and choosing silently is how one design quietly wins** |

### 📁 The disagreement, measured

**Three snapshot documents declare `shortcutGroups`:** `Fortune Signora App Shell.dc.html` §15 · `Fortune Signora Help Center.dc.html` · `Fortune Signora User Profile.dc.html`.

| The command | App Shell | Help Center | User Profile |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ask Signora** | `⌘⇧A` | — | ⛔ **`⌘⏎`** |
| **Switch workspace** | `⌘⇧W` | — | ⛔ **`⌘⇧K`** |
| **Edit cell** | `E` | ⛔ **`⏎`** | ⛔ **`⏎`** |
| **Open record** | `↵` | — | — |
| **Open in panel** | `⌘↵` | — | — |

🔴 **Two of the three are not a naming difference — they are the SAME CHORD meaning two different things.**

- ⛔ **`⌘⏎` is *Ask Signora* in User Profile and *Open in panel* in App Shell.**
- ⛔ **`⏎` is *Edit cell* in Help Center and User Profile, and *Open record* in App Shell.**

⚠️ **A keyboard map cannot render one chord twice with different meanings**, so this is an interaction-design conflict rather than a documentation tidy-up. ⚡ **And a customer who learns `⏎` on one screen and presses it on another gets the other behaviour** — **which is worse than an unbound key, because it does something.**

### ✅ What this lane did, and what it deliberately did not

📁 **[`lib/shell/shortcuts.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/shortcuts.ts) follows App Shell**, on a stated reading: **the shortcut reference is a shell surface and App Shell is the one design whose subject is the shell.** ⛔ **That is a reading, not a ruling**, and it is recorded in the file rather than left to be inferred.

⛔ **`E` and `⏎` are both registered `unbound`** — **nothing was bound to either**, so no code encodes an answer to this question. ✅ **The conflict is visible and costs nothing to resolve later.**

### The question

> **Which table is authoritative where they disagree — App Shell for every surface, or the screen's own design for that screen?** ⚠️ **And if the second, what does a global reference print for a chord whose meaning depends on where you are standing?**

## C-287 · ADR-0408's mechanism and its route scope cannot both be satisfied — the limiter is specified in the tier that cannot see the routes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, on the first hour of [TASK-1430](BACKLOG.md) — ⛔ **before writing any code** |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — 🔴 **an architectural blocker** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)): **no accepted architecture exists for the next step**, and the accepted one contradicts itself |
| **Status** | ✅ **`CLOSED` — Lane A, 2026-08-18.** **Ruled ⓓ by the product owner 2026-08-17 and implemented by Lane C**; closed by the raising lane, as [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) requires |
| **Blocks** | ✅ **Nothing. [TASK-1430](BACKLOG.md) is delivered** — it was never *build a limiter*, and ⑤ is why |

### ✅ ⑦ CLOSED — the ruling, the implementation, and where it actually is

⚡ **Closed on Lane C's report and then verified rather than taken at face value**, because ⑤'s whole lesson is that a confident reading can look in the wrong tier.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Ruled** | **⓭ ⓓ, product owner, 2026-08-17** — two policies, as this row recommended |
| **Implemented** | **Lane C, `2ffcbcb6`** — *"TASK-1430 — inbound rate limiting as two policies, and neither pretends to cover the other tier"* |
| **The line** | 📁 [`frontend/lib/auth/server.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/server.ts):177 — **`rateLimit: { enabled: true, storage: 'database' }`** |
| **The boundary** | 📁 [`docs/architecture/501-rate-limiting-boundary.md`](architecture/501-rate-limiting-boundary.md) — **neither limiter protects both tiers, stated once** |

⚠️ **`'database'` rather than `'secondary-storage'`, and the substitution is sound.** ⛔ **Redis would need a client in the Next.js tier** — a new dependency under the Change Budget ([§6](../CLAUDE.md)). ✅ **The auth pool is already attached and Better Auth migrates its own `rateLimit` table**, so ⑤'s real gap — *"`storage` is unset… in-process counters"* — **closes on infrastructure that already exists.**

🔴 **It is on `lane-c-sync` and NOT on `integration`** — measured after a fetch, not assumed. ⛔ **So the gap ⑤ describes is still live on `integration` today**, and this row is closed against a ruling and an implementation rather than against a promotion. **QE reconciles at the next one.**

⚠️ **This row said `OPEN` and *"blocks TASK-1430 entirely"* for six days after it was answered.** 📁 **That is [C-213](#c-213)'s failure exactly** — *a row that looks unanswered is believed by every lane that passes it* — **and it was mine to close the whole time.** ✅ **Reported by Lane C, who declined to close it themselves because closure is the raising lane's.**

### 🔴 ① The problem

📁 **[ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) is `ACCEPTED` and its two halves are incompatible.**

| The ADR says | Where |
|---|---|
| ✅ **The mechanism**: *"One ASGI middleware in `signora_platform/api/`"* | §4 · §11 · §16, three times |
| ✅ **The routes**: *"`/signin` · `/register` · password-reset request · verification resend"* | §10 |

⛔ **Every one of those four routes is a Better Auth route in Next.js.** ⚡ **An ASGI middleware in the Python tier can never see them.**

📁 **Measured, not assumed:**

- **`frontend/app/(auth)/signin`** and **`frontend/app/(auth)/register`** exist; **`frontend/app/api/auth/[...all]`** is Better Auth's handler.
- **`backend/apps/api/main.py` mounts sixteen routers and not one serves authentication.** A search of every `interface/` layer for `signin|login|register|reset|verif|password` returns **nothing**.
- 📁 **[§13](../CLAUDE.md) and [ADR-0026](architecture/adr/0026-jwt-boundary-architecture.md) make this permanent**: ***"Better Auth runs in Next.js and is the sole Authentication Authority. The Python tier only ever verifies RS256 JWTs"*** — ⛔ **and Claude must never add a login route to the Python tier.**

🔴 **The ADR's own measurement proves the contradiction rather than contradicting it.** 📁 §1: ***"nothing stands between a credential-stuffing script and Better Auth."*** ✅ **True — and Better Auth is in Next.js.**

### ⚠️ Why this is not a cell to correct quietly

⛔ **The ASGI middleware is buildable, and building it would satisfy the exemption while closing none of the gap.** ⚡ **It would guard sixteen business routers that already require a verified RS256 JWT** — **real value, and not the stated one.**

🔴 **And it would make the gap invisible.** 📁 **`infra/production-readiness.py` exists because its own first version reported ✅ on 38 outbound files** ([D-213](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) — ⚠️ **a limiter merged under this ADR would flip that probe to ✅ while `/signin` still accepted unlimited attempts.** ⛔ **That is worse than the gap: it is the gap plus a green light.**

### ⚡ ② Affected modules

**`signora_platform/api/`** *(the named home)* · **the Next.js authentication tier** *(where the routes are)* · **`product_surface`** *(this row's module)* · **[TASK-1431](BACKLOG.md)**'s production-readiness probe, which would report on it.

### ✅ ③ The alternatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **ⓐ** | **The limiter runs in the Next.js tier, where the routes are** | ⛔ **Outside the §20a exemption** — the exemption names `signora_platform/api/`. ⚡ **`frontend/middleware.ts` or Better Auth's own facility.** ⚠️ **Whether this Better Auth version exposes a core `rateLimit` is UNVERIFIED** — 📁 in the installed `better-auth ^1.1.0` tree it appears in **plugin** option shapes (`email-otp`, `magic-link`, `two-factor`, `phone-number`) and **not in `dist/types/`** — ⛔ **so *"Better Auth does it"* must be checked before it is believed** |
| **ⓑ** | **An edge limiter in front of both tiers** | ⚡ **The conventional answer**, and 📁 **deferred with the rest of infrastructure to M14.5** ([§20b](../CLAUDE.md)). ⛔ **Nothing to build today** |
| **ⓒ** | **Build the ASGI middleware as specified, and restate what it protects** | ✅ **Honest and buildable now** — the business API gains a limiter. ⛔ **It does NOT close the credential-stuffing gap**, and the ADR must stop claiming it does |
| **ⓓ** | **Both, as two policies** | 📁 **ADR-0408 §13 already says *"two policies, not one"*.** ✅ **ⓐ for the four named routes, ⓒ for the business API** |

### ⚡ ④ Recommendation

> ✅ **ⓓ, taken in the order ⓐ then ⓒ** — and ⛔ **neither is this lane's to start without a ruling.**

🔴 **ⓐ first, because it is the whole reason the row exists.** 📁 **[§9](../CLAUDE.md) and [§13](../CLAUDE.md) both point the same way**: authentication is **bought, not built**, and ***"Claude must never implement a bespoke auth mechanism, even a small or temporary one."*** ⚡ **A limiter on the authentication endpoints is authentication infrastructure**, so **configuring the vendor's facility beats writing one** — ⚠️ **if the facility exists, which must be verified rather than assumed.**

✅ **ⓒ is worth doing on its own merits and should be re-scoped rather than cancelled** — ⛔ **but its row must say *the business API*, not *`/signin`*.**

### ⚠️ ⑤ Trade-offs

⛔ **ⓐ costs the §20a exemption its subject** — the exemption was granted for a Python middleware and would need re-granting for a different tier. ⚡ **It is also the cheaper build if the vendor already ships it, and the more correct one either way.**

⛔ **ⓒ alone is the dangerous option**, for the reason above: **it satisfies the ADR, the exemption, the row and the probe, and leaves the attack open.**

⚡ **ⓑ is not a competitor** — it is what M14.5 adds on top, and it does not remove the need for a per-identity key that only the application knows.

### 📁 ⑥ Implementation impact

⛔ **Zero code written.** ✅ **Found by reading the ADR against the repository before building**, which is the cheapest place to find it.

⚠️ **[TASK-1430](BACKLOG.md) cannot proceed under its current scope.** ⛔ **This lane will not "just build the ASGI half"** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): ***"'I could just add it' is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision inside a feature slice."***

⚡ **What survives whatever is ruled** is the reuse audit the row asked for: ✅ **`redis>=5.2` is already a dependency**, **`require_redis_url()` already exists**, and **`event_bus/queue.py` is the access pattern** — ⛔ **so no rate-limiting library and no new dependency is needed in the Python tier.** 📁 **The in-process counter is rejected on the ADR's own argument**: it gives an attacker *n* × the budget across *n* replicas and loosens silently as the service scales.

### 🔴 C-287 — MEASURED, 2026-08-11, and the measurement changes the item

⚠️ **Lane C named the question that decides this: *does Better Auth actually ship a limiter, or only plugin option shapes?*** ✅ **Measured, and the answer changes both halves of the row.**

#### ⛔ ① The installed version is not the declared one

📁 **`package.json` declares `better-auth: ^1.1.0`. The installed version is `1.6.25`.** ⚠️ **My first search read the 1.1-era layout and found `rateLimit` only in plugin declarations** — ⛔ **which is why I flagged it as unverified instead of asserting it, and that caution was the right call for the wrong reason.**

#### ✅ ② A core rate limiter exists, and it has every property ADR-0408 requires

📁 **`node_modules/better-auth/dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs`:**

| ADR-0408 requires | Better Auth 1.6.25 |
|---|---|
| **Per-route policy** (§10's four routes, §13's *"two policies, not one"*) | ✅ **`customRules[path]`**, each with its own window and max |
| **A SHARED counter** (§9 — an in-process one gives *n* × budget across *n* replicas) | ✅ **`storage: "secondary-storage"`**, driving `secondaryStorage.get / set / increment` |
| **Configuration rather than code** (§15 — no number in the ADR) | ✅ **`enabled`, `window`, `max`, all options** |

#### 🔴 ③ And it is already enabled in this product

📁 **[`frontend/lib/auth/server.ts`](../frontend/lib/auth/server.ts):147 — `rateLimit: { enabled: true }`**, deliberately, with a comment recording why: **the vendor defaults it to production only, so the throttled screen Workflow 1 built could not be reached at any review.** ✅ **`app/(auth)/signin/throttled.tsx` exists and was built against the real `429` and the real `X-Retry-After`.**

> ⛔ **So ADR-0408 §1 is false.** 📁 It reads *"nothing stands between a credential-stuffing script and Better Auth."* **Something does, it is enabled in every mode, and this product already renders its refusal.**

#### ⚠️ ④ The same probe, the same blind spot, twice

📁 **[D-213](DECISION_REGISTER.md) records the first error: the readiness probe matched `rate.?limit|throttl` and reported ✅ on 38 files that were Signora pacing itself against vendors.** ⚡ **Corrected to inbound-only — and the correction searched `backend/` only.**

🔴 **Authentication does not live in `backend/`.** ⛔ **[§13](../CLAUDE.md) and [ADR-0026](architecture/adr/0026-jwt-boundary-architecture.md) put it in Next.js, permanently** — **so the corrected probe measured the wrong TIER, having first measured the wrong DIRECTION.** ⚠️ **Both readings were confident and neither looked where the routes are.**

#### ✅ ⑤ What the real gap is, and it is smaller and entirely configuration

⛔ **`storage` is unset and no `secondaryStorage` is configured**, so 📁 `create-context.mjs`:174 resolves it to **`"memory"`** — ⚡ **in-process counters, which is exactly what [ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) §9 rejects**: *n* × the budget across *n* replicas, **loosening silently as the service scales.**

⚠️ **And no `customRules` are declared**, so **password-reset request and verification resend get the default policy** rather than the tighter one their mail-amplification shape earns — 📁 the routes §10 calls *"arguably worse"*.

> ✅ **TASK-1430 is not *build a limiter*. It is *the limiter that exists is in-process and unconfigured per route*, and both halves are configuration in the Next.js tier.**

#### ⚡ ⑥ What this does to the recommendation

⛔ **The two-policy split still stands and is now cheaper on both sides.**

**ⓐ** ✅ **Point Better Auth's limiter at shared storage and declare `customRules` for the four routes.** ⛔ **No new dependency, no bespoke mechanism** — 📁 [§13](../CLAUDE.md): *"never implement a bespoke auth mechanism, even a small or temporary one."* ⚡ **This is configuring the vendor, which is what [§9](../CLAUDE.md) buys.**

**ⓒ** ⚠️ **The Python ASGI middleware is still worth building and still must be re-scoped** — **its row must say *the business API*, never `/signin`.**

⛔ **What must NOT happen is unchanged and is now sharper**: **building the ASGI middleware under the current row would leave the in-process auth counter exactly as it is** — ✅ **and the readiness probe, which reads `backend/`, would turn green on the one tier that never had the problem.**

#### 📁 ⑦ What is still the product owner's

⚠️ **[ADR-0408](architecture/adr/0408-inbound-rate-limiting.md) is `ACCEPTED` and its §1 measurement is now known to be wrong.** ⛔ **A lane does not amend an accepted ADR** — **the correction, and whether the §20a exemption still has a subject, are the product owner's.** ✅ **Every number remains configuration and none is proposed here.**

## C-288 · The backlog's READY order and the relayed priority disagree, and six Lane A rows sit above the one being built

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, at the moment of claiming — ⛔ **before any code**, and recorded rather than resolved by choosing |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md): *"a lane never reorders, reprioritizes, removes, or inserts `READY` work without the product owner"* |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **Implementation is proceeding on [TASK-1460](BACKLOG.md)**; this item exists so the choice is visible, not so it is waited on |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **If the ruling goes the other way, one claim commit is abandoned and no code is lost** — which is the whole reason the Task Claim Protocol makes a claim a standalone commit |

### 🔴 The disagreement, measured

📁 **[`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md)'s `READY` section is *"claimable now, in priority order"*, and [§20e](../CLAUDE.md) is explicit that *"the queue order **is** the priority."*** **Read literally, the highest Lane A row is [TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md).**

⚡ **The order the product owner relayed to this lane was different**: 📁 ***"TASK-1461. High priority."*** **and then TASK-1460, TASK-440, TASK-1467.** ⛔ **[TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md) sits BELOW four of those rows in the file** and was nonetheless the stated first priority — **so the file's order and the relayed order were already known to disagree, and the relayed one won.**

| Position in the file | Row |
|---|---|
| 1 | **[TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md)** — Signal Center, eight missing surfaces |
| 2 | **[TASK-1467](BACKLOG.md)** — the three gate screens |
| 3 · 4 | **[TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md)** · **[TASK-1462](BACKLOG.md)** — App Shell sections and values |
| 5 | ✅ **[TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md)** — **built first, on the relayed priority.** `IN VALIDATION` |
| 6 · 7 | **[TASK-1465](BACKLOG.md)** · **[TASK-1466](BACKLOG.md)** |
| 8 | 🔵 **[TASK-1460](BACKLOG.md)** — **claimed now, on the same relayed priority** |

### ⚡ Why this lane took the relayed order rather than the file

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *Continuous execution*, names four things that stop a lane claiming from the top, and the second is *"a higher-priority task has been explicitly assigned by the product owner."*** ✅ **That is what happened for [TASK-1461](BACKLOG.md), and the same instruction named this row next.**

⛔ **But a relayed instruction is not a durable artifact.** ⚠️ **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s own words for exactly this case**: *"if the top item cannot be taken… say so in its backlog note and take the next one. **Skipping quietly is re-prioritizing, and priority is not a lane's to hold.**"* ✅ **So the skip is written into both the claim commit and the row, and this item exists so it is not only in a commit message.**

### ✅ What would resolve it, and it is one sentence either way

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **The relayed order stands** | **Nothing to do.** ⚡ **Ideally [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md)'s `READY` section is re-sorted to match**, so the file stops disagreeing with the instruction and the next lane does not have to ask this question again |
| ⛔ **The file's order stands** | **[TASK-1460](BACKLOG.md)'s claim is returned and [TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md) is claimed instead.** **Cost: one commit** |

> ⚠️ **The general form is worth more than this instance.** ⛔ **A queue whose order is authoritative, and an instruction that overrides it, cannot both be true without the override being written down** — **otherwise every future lane re-derives the same conflict, and the quiet resolution is indistinguishable from a lane choosing its own work.**

## C-289 · Companies renders two of the nine columns the design draws, because the browse read publishes two fields

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, building [TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) — ⛔ **after reading the contract, before drawing a column** |
| **Owner** | **`knowledge_graph`'s current assignee** — joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), ⛔ **not named here** ([C-213](#c-213)) |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **[TASK-440](BACKLOG.md) shipped what the contract publishes**; this item exists so the remaining columns arrive as reads rather than as inventions |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚠️ **It blocks the design's table being *complete*, which is a different claim from the screen being *correct*** |

### 🔴 The measurement

📁 **The design's Companies table draws nine columns**: a selection box, an avatar, the name, and six of score, stage, owner and value.

🔴 **`ListedAccount` publishes two fields — `account` and `kind` — and that is the whole contract.**

| The design draws | Published by `accounts-list`? |
|---|---|
| **Name · identity** | ✅ **Yes** — `account`, the same `AccountIdentity` search and the brief return |
| **Kind** | ✅ **Yes** — and the endpoint says to read it: *"the list answers for companies today and the graph knows more kinds than it can search"* |
| **Score · trend · stage · owner · value · last activity** | ⛔ **No. None of them** |

### ⛔ Why the screen shows two columns rather than nine with dashes

📁 **[§20c](../CLAUDE.md): *"never introduce mock business data — screens without a shipped module behind them ship a designed empty state."*** ⚠️ **An omission is not one.**

🔴 **A column of `—` is worse than no column.** ⚡ **It says Signora looked and found nothing, when the truth is that nothing was ever asked** — and a seller who reads *"score: —"* on eight thousand rows concludes the scoring is broken.

✅ **So the screen names the gap to the reader instead**: *"Score, owner, stage and value are not on this list yet — open an account to see them."* ⚡ **The same treatment the rail gives a destination with no route**, and the same one `freshness.tsx` gives *"last checked"*.

### ⚠️ The owner column is the one that matters most, and it costs a journey step

📁 **[TASK-440](BACKLOG.md)'s own journey is *"a seller opens Companies, **filters to their own book**, searches a company by name, and opens it."***

⛔ **The browse read has no notion of who owns an account**, so **there is nothing to filter on** — ⚡ **and this was already known**: 📁 the previously-built version of this screen recorded it as a decision a later change must not reverse — *"the projection has no notion of who owns an account, so a seller filtered to Mine can be shown a company that is not theirs."*

⚠️ **The attention list DOES have `?owner=`.** ⛔ **Two reads, one with the predicate and one without** — **and the one that browses the whole book is the one that needs it more.**

### ✅ What is asked, and it is one question

> **Should `accounts-list` carry the fields the design's table draws — or does Companies stay a browse surface that hands off to the account for everything else?**

⚡ **Either answer is implementable and neither is this lane's to choose.** ⛔ **What must not happen is the columns arriving by the frontend inventing them**, which is the rule this item exists to keep.

## C-290 · Every `route:` in the entry engine is a promise nothing resolves, and one of them was empty

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, from [B-242](BUGS.md) — ⛔ **found by a reuse audit, not by a gate** |
| **Owner** | **QE** — ⚡ **this asks for a CHECK, and a repository-wide gate is QE's** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *QE creates, maintains, extends and retires repository-wide automated tests*) |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **The one empty promise is fixed**; this item is about the class |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing** |

### 🔴 The finding, in one sentence

> **[`lib/entry/rules.ts`](../frontend/lib/entry/rules.ts) declares where every refused or redirected person lands, and nothing checks that any of those destinations exists.**

⛔ **[B-242](BUGS.md) is what that cost**: rule 05 has routed locked accounts to `/auth/locked` since the engine shipped, **the route did not exist**, and a person who could not sign in met *"that address does not lead anywhere."*

### ⚡ Why every existing gate was blind to it, and each was right to be

| Gate | What it asks | Why it missed this |
|---|---|---|
| **`make reachability`** | *"Does anything LINK to this route?"* | ✅ **Correct to be silent** — **nobody links to their own lockout**, and the route was not there to be reported on |
| **`rules.ts`'s own suite** | *"Does the right rule fire, and does it return the right string?"* | ⚡ **Both true.** ⛔ **The string was never resolved against the route table** |
| **`tsc`** | Types | ⛔ **A route is a `string`** |

> 🔴 **The general form is worth more than the instance: a router tested against its own output is tested against a claim, not against a destination.**

### ✅ What is asked

**A check that every literal route the entry engine can return resolves to a route the application actually serves.** ⚡ **The inputs already exist** — `RULES` is exported and enumerable, and `infra/reachability.py` already walks the route tree for a different question.

⚠️ **Seven destinations are declared today** and this lane has verified only the one it fixed: `/account/deleted` · `/account/suspended` · **`/auth/locked` ✅** · `/auth/step-up` · `/workspaces/none` · and the two `WORKSPACES` constants. ⛔ **This lane did not check the other six**, because **finding a defect outside the row it holds is an obligation to report, never a licence to fix** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md)) — **and six more screens is a commissioning decision, not a slice.**

> ⚡ **[TASK-1423](BACKLOG.md) is already the row for the missing gate screens and is `BLOCKED` on [C-1405](#c-1405) for exactly this reason** — their designs do not exist. **This item is not asking for those screens. It is asking for the check that says which ones are missing**, so the next one is found by a gate rather than by a lane reading a file.

## C-291 · The Saved View store has no frontend consumer, so Signals would be its first — not its second

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, doing [TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md)'s reuse audit — ⛔ **before writing a line, which is what the row instructed** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — 📁 **a scope premise on a row this office prepared**, not a defect and not an architectural blocker |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **Surfaces ② ③ ⑦ are unaffected and proceed** |
| **Blocks** | ⚠️ **Nothing outright.** ⛔ **It re-sizes ① from *reuse* to *first caller*, which is a different piece of work** |

### 🔴 The measurement

📁 **[TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md)'s reuse cell**: ***"[TASK-452](BACKLOG.md) shipped the Saved View store… Signals is another consumer of that same store — ⛔ not a new saved-view mechanism."***

✅ **The instruction is right and this lane will follow it.** ⛔ **The premise behind *another* is not.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The endpoint** | ✅ **Exists** — `GET /workspaces/{id}/saved-views`, `workspace_tenancy` |
| **`lib/views/working-list.ts`** | ✅ **Exists** — builds a declaration, and carries the three refusals |
| **A frontend fetch of it** | ⛔ **NONE.** `grep -rn "saved-views"` over `frontend/**` returns **zero**; so does `SavedView` |
| **A type, a hook, a query key** | ⛔ **None of the three** |

> 🔴 **So the store is shipped, tested, and reachable by nothing.** ⚡ **This is the same pattern this repository has now recorded nine times** — the entry engine, the narrowing law, the top-bar slot set, the command palette, `confidence.tsx`, `drawer.tsx`, the rail's own law, the twelve-column axis, and this. ⛔ **The law shipping first is not the defect; the surface never arriving is.**

### ⚠️ Why the distinction changes the slice rather than only the wording

📁 **[455 §4](architecture/455-context-definitions-r02-r03.md)**: ***"a contract proven by one real caller before six adopt it."*** ⚡ **The FIRST caller pays for proving the contract** — the types, the hooks, the query keys, the persistence path, the failure states, and the first honest answer to *what does a saved view do when the store refuses it*.

⛔ **A row that describes that as *reuse* under-sizes it**, and a lane reading only the reuse cell would plan for an afternoon and find a slice.

⚠️ **`working-list.ts` is the other half of the same finding**: it builds declarations **nothing stores and nothing reads back.** 📁 Its own docstring says *"a saved view outlives the screen that wrote it"* — ⛔ **and today none outlives anything, because none is written.**

### ✅ What is asked

**Confirm the sizing, and say which row carries the store's first frontend caller** — ⚡ **this one, or its own.**

⛔ **This lane is not asking to be released from ①.** **It is asking that the row say what ① is**, so the next lane reading it is not told *reuse* about work that is *first caller*.

> ✅ **Meanwhile ② ③ ⑦ proceed**, and they are genuinely queue-local: filtering by `signal_type`, bulk selection, and the counts header — **none of them touches the store.**
