## C-296 · `statusLabelVisible` cannot be called, because the pill whose label it hides is never rendered

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, implementing [TASK-1474](BACKLOG.md) |
| **Owner** | **Product owner**, via **Lane C** — ⛔ **it needs a source for system status, which is a product decision about what Signora reports on itself** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **The row's other half is DELIVERED.** ⚡ **This half is refused with a measurement rather than deferred with a shrug** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚠️ **It duplicates half of [C-275](#c-275) deliberately** — that item asks for the status SOURCE; this one records that a shipped contract cannot be wired without it |

### 📁 What the row asked for

> **TASK-1474**: *"`statusLabelVisible(tone, width) => tone === 'healthy' ? width >= 1280 : true` … `statusLabelVisible` is called by nothing — the component says so at `:201`. **The real work is the status rule's source**, and the component's note is right that it needs one. **If none exists, implement against the tone the component already renders and say so — check whether `OfflineStatus` already carries a tone before opening a coordination item.**"*

✅ **Checked, exactly as instructed.** ⛔ **And the answer is stronger than *"no tone"*.**

### 🔴 The measurement

📁 **[`offline-status.tsx`](../frontend/components/ui/offline-status.tsx), first line of its render:**

```tsx
if (!offline && queued.length === 0) return null;
```

⚡ **When the system is healthy, the component renders NOTHING** — ⛔ **not a green pill with a hidden label, not a dot: no element at all.**

**⇒ `statusLabelVisible`'s entire content is *when the healthy pill hides its label*, and there is no healthy pill.** ⚠️ **Calling it would be asking a question about an element that does not exist.**

### ⛔ Implementing "against the tone the component already renders" is not available either

⚡ **`OfflineStatus` carries a binary `offline`, not a tone**, and the two states it *does* render are:

| What renders | The design's tone |
|---|---|
| *"You are offline"* | **not healthy** — and `statusLabelVisible` returns `true` for every non-healthy tone at every width |
| *"Sending 3 edits"* | **not healthy**, same |

🔴 **So for both states the component can produce, the rule's answer is `true` — always show the label — which is what it already does.** ⛔ **A call whose result cannot change the output is [§2](../CLAUDE.md)'s Decorative Logic**, and adding one to satisfy a row would be the exact defect this repository names most often.

### ⚠️ The previous lane reached the same conclusion and wrote it in the code

📁 **[`top-bar.tsx`](../frontend/components/shell/top-bar.tsx), slot 3, already says:**

> *"`OfflineStatus` fills this slot and does NOT call `statusLabelVisible` — read, not assumed. And it is correct not to: the helper's whole content is what the GREEN tone does, and `OfflineStatus` never renders a green tone… **the design's healthy pill is genuinely absent, and nothing publishes the state it would show.** The design lists five subsystems — Application, CRM sync, Scoring service, Conversation ingest, Exports — **and none of them is published by any module.** Raised as [C-275](#c-275); `statusLabelVisible` stays uncalled **until there is a source, rather than gaining a caller that invents one**."*

⚡ **That analysis is unchanged and this lane re-measured rather than inheriting it**: `git grep` finds no subsystem status endpoint, and `lib/api/types.ts` publishes no health tone.

### ✅ What would make it buildable, and it is one decision rather than one function

⛔ **Not a caller.** ⚡ **A source**: something that publishes whether Signora's own subsystems are healthy. 📁 **[C-275](#c-275) already holds that request**, and this row is the evidence that a shipped, correct, tested contract has been waiting on it — **which is a better argument for scheduling it than the original absence was.**

⚠️ **And when it arrives, the rule needs no rewriting**: `statusLabelVisible` already carries the design's asymmetry exactly — *"a healthy system may go quiet on a narrow screen; a degraded one may not"* — **so the work is the source and the pill, never the rule.**

## C-295 · Home is now the design's composition, and the composition is empty because no module has shipped a card

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, implementing [TASK-1405](BACKLOG.md)'s route half |
| **Owner** | **Product owner** — ⛔ **a sequencing decision, not an architectural one** |
| **Status** | 🟠 **`OPEN` — the row is DELIVERED as specified and the consequence is reported.** ⚡ **Nothing is blocked; a ruling changes what ships next, not whether this ships** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing** |

### 🔴 What changed, and it is exactly what the row asked for

📁 **The design**: *"Every authenticated person lands on `/w/:workspace/home`. What renders there is resolved from their role, and the resolution is a composition of cards from a shared catalogue."* ✅ **That is now true**: the route resolves a composition and renders the registry.

⚠️ **And the registry is empty.** 📁 [`cards.ts`](../frontend/lib/home/cards.ts) says so in its own words — *"EMPTY, and it is empty on purpose. Measured 2026-08-10: no module publishes a Home card."*

### ⚠️ The consequence, stated plainly

⛔ **`/w/:workspace/home` previously re-exported the attention list** — [TASK-1438](BACKLOG.md) made it so, deliberately, to stop eight of the entry engine's twenty-four rules returning 404, **including rule 24, the default and most common outcome.**

🔴 **So the most common landing destination in the product has gone from *a seller's ranked working list* to *a designed empty state*.** ⚡ **The row anticipated this and sanctioned it** — *"an empty Home is a designed state, not a failure"* — **and it is still a screen a customer would find less useful than the one before it.**

⛔ **The alternative was worse and was refused**: falling back to the attention list when a composition has no cards **would be a second answer to what Home shows**, which is the hybrid [D-229A](DECISION_REGISTER.md) forbids and which [TASK-1438](BACKLOG.md)'s own comment warned against — *"inventing a composition here would be a third answer."*

### ✅ The cheapest way out, and three fifths of it is already built

⚡ **`activation` is the composition every session resolves to today** — `primaryRole` is `null` on every session the platform can produce, so the resolver's fallback is universal. 📁 **Its catalogue entries are:**

| Card | State |
|---|---|
| `connect-a-crm` | ✅ **Built** — §18's checklist step 1, [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) |
| `invite-the-team` | ✅ **Built** — §18's checklist step 3 |
| `connect-calls` | ✅ **Built** — §18's checklist step 2 |
| `what-signora-will-do` | ⛔ Not built |
| `sample-of-one-real-account` | ⛔ Not built |

🔴 **Three of the five already exist as working, tested UI** — reading live connection and roster state — **and they are one component rather than three cards.** ⚡ **Splitting them into three registered cards would make Home useful immediately and would reuse rather than rebuild** ([L-1](../ENGINEERING_LAWS.md)).

⛔ **This lane did NOT do it inside this row.** ⚠️ **[TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) is with QE and unvalidated**, and reworking a slice under validation to serve a different row is how two slices become one unreviewable change. **It is a row, and the product owner decides whether it is the next one.**

### 🔴 The other half, which is a real gap rather than a sequencing choice

⛔ **`CardContract` publishes `id`, `title`, `module` and `requires` — and nothing that renders.** ⚡ **So *"a composition of cards"* had no seam from a card to its content**, and this row added one: **a renderer map owned by Home**, which is where the design's own boundary puts it — 📁 *"Home owns the composition; the module owns the card's content."*

⚠️ **The alternative — a `component` field on the contract — was rejected deliberately**: 📁 the contract's own comment says *"a contract carrying layout, width or position would be the module deciding something Home owns."* **A node handed over by a module is one step from that.**

**⇒ The question for the product owner is only which cards ship first.** ✅ **The mechanism is complete and proven by its own test**: a registered card with no renderer is skipped rather than drawn as an empty title.

## C-294 · A P0 row was handed to this lane as implementation-ready and its own row says BLOCKED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, selecting its next slice |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **a reporting question, not an architectural one** |
| **Status** | 🟢 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **This lane resolved it by the rule and proceeded**; the item exists so the practice is corrected rather than absorbed |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ⚡ **No work waited** |

### 🔴 What happened

**Lane C's poll named [TASK-1473](BACKLOG.md) as *"P0 — implementation-ready"* and described the fix, the working example to copy, and the two-sided assertion the product owner requires.**

⛔ **The row on `integration` reads:**

> ⛔ **`BLOCKED` — awaiting a product/design ruling. NOT `READY`.** 🔴 *"This row previously said `READY` and asserted the implementation was wrong. QE challenged the premise and QE was right."*

⚡ **So the message and the register disagreed, and the register was the more recent truth.**

### ✅ How this lane resolved it, and it needed no ruling

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md) step 3b is exact**: *"If the two disagree, **the backlog wins on state** and the queue wins on ownership — **and report the disagreement**, because one of them is stale."*

⛔ **TASK-1473 was not claimed.** ✅ **This report is the second half of that rule.**

### ⚠️ Why it is worth a row rather than a shrug

🔴 **This is [C-422](#c-422)'s shape one generation on** — *"`TASK-440` was corrected on one day and claimed from the stale state on the next, by a lane that followed every rule."* ⚡ **The correction ran the other way this time**: **the register was right and the message was stale**, and **a lane that trusted the message would have built against a premise QE had already overturned.**

⛔ **The mechanism that saved it is not a lane's diligence.** ✅ **It is that §20e names which artifact wins.** ⚠️ **A cross-session message is not a claimable source and never was** — 📁 *"an implementation lane derives executable work from exactly three things: `origin/integration` · a `READY` task row · certified repository state."*

### ⚡ What would prevent the next one

**A poll that names a row also names its state as the register holds it**, so the two are checkable in the same sentence. ⛔ **Not a new file and not a new process** — 📁 the governance freeze binds, and this is a wording habit rather than a mechanism.

## C-293 · App Shell §18 says a destination that needs data is "marked" and never says what the mark is

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, building [TASK-1463](BACKLOG.md) §18 |
| **Owner** | **Product owner**, via **Lane C** — ⛔ **a design question, not an implementation one** |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **The rest of §18 ships**: the three-step checklist with live counts is delivered |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing today.** ⚠️ **It leaves half of one design section unimplemented, stated rather than silently dropped** |

### 📁 What the design says, in full

> ***"A brand-new workspace shows the full shell with real navigation, not a stripped-down wizard: **destinations that need data are visible but marked**, so the user learns the product's shape while they set it up."***

### 🔴 The measurement

⚡ **That sentence is the only occurrence in the document.** **Measured across the whole App Shell design**: the word *marked* appears twice, once here and once about notifications (*"Agent and AI notifications are **marked** with the intelligence hue"*, §11 — a different subject with a stated mechanism).

⛔ **§18 gives no mechanism.** **There is no rail-entry state in the design's own data** — the navigation entries carry `label`, `icon` and `meta`, and nothing else. ⚠️ **§03 defines the rail's states and *needs data* is not among them.**

### ⛔ Two decisions a lane would have to take, and neither is a lane's

| | |
|---|---|
| **What the mark IS** | A dot · a dimmed label · a tooltip · a count of zero · a badge. ⚡ **Each says something different to a customer** — a dim reads as *disabled*, a dot reads as *new*, and the design system has no token that means *not yet* |
| **WHICH destinations qualify** | ⛔ **There is no published notion of *needs data*.** **Signals, Accounts and Reports plainly do; Settings and Help plainly do not** — **and the boundary is a product judgement, not something derivable from a contract.** ⚠️ **A lane deciding it would encode a product decision inside a feature slice**, which is 📁 [§20e](../CLAUDE.md)'s *"'I could just add it' is how an architectural blocker becomes a silent design decision"* |

### ✅ What shipped instead, so the section is not silently half-done

📁 **The rest of §18 is implemented as written** — `components/shell/activation.tsx`, three steps, live counts, on the workspace's own connections and roster. ⛔ **The rail is untouched**, and this row is why.

### ⚡ What would settle it

**One sentence in the design naming the mark, and one naming the rule.** ⚠️ **Not a lane's proposal to make** — but the cheapest form of the answer is likely *"a destination whose module has no data yet carries a dot"*, with the *needs data* set enumerated rather than derived, exactly as [`rail.ts`](../frontend/lib/shell/rail.ts) enumerates the destinations themselves.

## C-292 · The Signal Center's counts header draws three numbers and the queue publishes one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-11, building [TASK-1468](BACKLOG.md) ⑦ |
| **Owner** | **`signal_engine`'s current assignee** — joined from [`modules.toml`](coordination/modules.toml), ⛔ **not named here** ([C-213](#c-213)) |
| **Status** | 🟡 **`OPEN` — NOT BLOCKING.** ✅ **The one publishable count ships** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing** |

### 🔴 The measurement

📁 **The design's header**: ***"14 need review · 6 assigned to you · 41 this week."***

🔴 **`QueueEntry` publishes six fields** — `signal_id · signal_type · entity_id · rationale · state · resolution`.

| The design draws | Publishable? |
|---|---|
| **`N` need review** | ✅ **Yes** — the open queue's length |
| **`N` assigned to you** | ⛔ **No. There is no assignee on the entry** |
| **`N` this week** | ⛔ **No. There is no timestamp on the entry** |

⚠️ **And the second one has a further wrinkle worth stating**: 📁 `ResolveOutcome` carries `{ kind: 'assigned'; to: string }` — **so the platform can RECORD an assignment and the queue cannot REPORT one.** ⛔ **The fact exists in the write path and not in the read.**

### ⛔ Why one number ships rather than three

📁 **[§20c](../CLAUDE.md): *"never introduce mock business data."*** ⚡ **A count is the single most trusted thing on a triage screen** — **it is what a person decides whether to open the queue at all** — and **a wrong one is worse than a missing one because nothing about it looks wrong.**

✅ **So the strip says `16 need review` and stops**, and a component test and a browser journey both assert that *"assigned to you"* and *"this week"* never appear. ⛔ **A later change filling the design's shape fails rather than shipping.**

### ⚡ Two related absences on the same screen, recorded together

| | |
|---|---|
| 📁 **The design's filter chip is *"Confidence ≥ 3"*** | ⛔ **Confidence is not on the entry.** ✅ **The chips filter by `signal_type`, which is** |
| 📁 **The design lists `Critical` severity** | ⛔ **Not a field the entry carries** — already recorded on the screen by [TASK-439](BACKLOG.md), and unchanged |

### ✅ What is asked

**Whether the triage read should carry an assignee and a raised-at timestamp** — ⚡ **or whether the counts header is a smaller thing than the design draws.**

⛔ **Either answer is implementable.** **What must not happen is the numbers arriving by the frontend counting something it invented.**

## C-1436 · [TASK-495](BACKLOG.md) — is the ratified vendor required for the BELL, and the six cells that said this row had no surface

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-16, on claiming [TASK-495](BACKLOG.md) at `6fd7b7c1`. ⚡ **Two things in one report, and they have one cause** |
| **Owner** | **Lane C** — ⛔ **both halves are this office's: the row is the office's to write, and the question is a read of decisions that already exist** |
| **Status** | ✅ **`ANSWERED`** — 2026-08-16, in [TASK-495](BACKLOG.md)'s own cells. ⛔ **No new decision was taken and none was needed** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing.** ✅ **Lane A built the port, the domain and the outbox wiring while it waited** — **none of which the answer changes** |

### ⚠️ What Lane A found, and it was six cells rather than three

📁 **The row's `Status` — mine, 2026-08-16 — moved the shell bell here from [TASK-480](BACKLOG.md).** ⛔ **The BODY was written when this row was only a vendor adapter, and did not follow:**

| Cell | Said | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Shared layout** | *"n/a — no surface"* | 🔴 **the app shell top bar — every authenticated screen** |
| **Manual review gate** | *"n/a — no surface"* | 🔴 **required, headed** ([D-134](DECISION_REGISTER.md)) |
| **Reusable components** | *"None — no surface"* | ✅ **`badge` · `empty-state` · `skeleton` · `error-state` · `avatar`** |
| **Approved design** | *"n/a — an adapter behind a port"* | 📁 **App Shell Slot 4 — the 400px popover, three tabs, day grouping, 6px dot** |
| **Playwright** | *"none — not a customer journey"* | 🔴 **required** ([§19](../CLAUDE.md)) |
| **Definition of Done** | *"leaves the process through Novu"* | ⚡ **see below** |

🔴 **The fifth is the one that would have cost something.** ⛔ **A lane reading the body would have shipped a bell visible on every screen with no journey and no headed review — and the row would have told it that was correct.**

⚠️ **This is [C-213](#c-213)'s shape inside a single row rather than across two files**, and ⚡ **it is the same defect as the three the office has already recorded this week: a newer authoritative cell, and stale cells nobody re-read.**

### ✅ The answer — the vendor is not this slice, and the row's own `Status` had already said so

📁 **[ADR-0017](architecture/adr/0017-notifications.md)'s subject, in its own Context sentence: *"deliver notifications… across multiple channels (in-app, email, Slack, Teams)"*.**

⚡ **Nothing in this slice leaves the process.** **The bell reads `workspace_tenancy`'s own per-person state** ([D-239](DECISION_REGISTER.md)), **which [TASK-480](BACKLOG.md) already persists on `main`.** ✅ **In-app is a channel Signora owns end to end.**

📁 **What needs a delivery vendor is the *Notification Center* design — measured, not assumed: 7 sections, 4 channels (In-app · Email · Slack · Mobile), digests, quiet hours, and §07 *"Delivery log · every attempt, including the ones that failed"*.** ⛔ **That is Workflow 17's own decomposition and is not this row.**

> ⛔ **An adapter written for a call nobody makes is the speculative abstraction [§6](../CLAUDE.md) forbids.** ✅ **Lane A's instinct — *"I will not adopt the SDK speculatively"* — was right, and the row was what disagreed with it.**

### 🔴 One correction to the proposed shape, and it is the precedent rather than the analogy

✅ **Lane A named `ai_platform`'s registry, and it is the right precedent — it says so in terms:**

> 📁 `ai_platform/infrastructure/composition.py` — ***"An adapter is registered only when its credentials exist."***

⛔ **But the same docstring carries the half that Lane A's wording dropped:**

> 📁 ***"There is deliberately no fallback between them."***

⚠️ **So NOT *"a deterministic default when none is configured"*.** ⚡ **In-app is a distinct CHANNEL, never a substitute for a channel somebody failed to configure.** **A requested channel with no credential must fail legibly**, 📁 **for [§10](../CLAUDE.md)'s stated reason — *"a service running on it is indistinguishable from one that works, which is strictly worse than the outage it would hide"* — and `ai_platform` enforces exactly that by raising rather than degrading.**

✅ **Registered-where-a-credential-exists is right. Falling back is not.** ⛔ **The difference is invisible until the day an email was expected and a bell appeared instead.**

### 📁 Where the answer lives

**[TASK-495](BACKLOG.md)'s `Definition of Done`, `Change Budget`, `Approved design`, `Shared layout`, `Manual review gate`, `Reusable components` and `Testing metadata` cells** — ⛔ **rewritten rather than annotated, because a stale cell beside a correction is still a cell somebody reads.**

## C-1437 · `BACKLOG.md` says QE writes nothing in it, and four of its lifecycle states are QE's alone

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raised by** | **Lane A**, 2026-08-16, setting [TASK-1482](BACKLOG.md) to `IN VALIDATION`. ⚡ **Raised explicitly as *"recorded for the product owner; it blocks nothing"*** — ✅ **which is the correct handling of a governance question found mid-slice** |
| **Owner** | 🔴 **Product owner, and only the product owner.** 📁 **[`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) is theirs** ([§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *Shared files have one owner*) — ⛔ **this office may draft, never rule** |
| **Status** | 🟣 **`READY FOR PRODUCT DECISION`** — ⚡ **no analysis is outstanding; the two sentences are quoted below and they are the whole item** |
| **Blocks** | ⛔ **Nothing, and it has blocked nothing to date.** ⚠️ **What it costs is that both readings are defensible, so two sessions can behave differently and each cite the constitution** |

### 🔴 The two sentences, verbatim

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *Shared files have one owner*, on [`BACKLOG.md`](BACKLOG.md):**

> **"Product owner owns scope and order… A Product Development lane writes preparation rows for its own modules… and its claims. Lane C sets `READY` on approval and `REVISION REQUESTED` on rejection… ⛔ *QE writes nothing.*"**

📁 **[§20e](../CLAUDE.md), *Execution ownership ends at `IN VALIDATION`*, in the lifecycle table:**

> **"`VERIFIED` · `CERTIFIED` · `PROMOTED` · `DONE` — **QE, exclusively.** A feature lane never writes one of these."**

⛔ **Those states live in `BACKLOG.md`.** ⚡ **So QE must write four states into the one file it is told it writes nothing in.**

### ✅ What is NOT in question

⛔ **This is not a defect in either rule, and neither is wrong on its own subject.** **The first governs *scope and order* — who decides what work exists and in what sequence. The second governs *execution state* — who may assert that a thing has passed.** ✅ **Both are correct; the word *"writes"* is doing two jobs.**

⚠️ **And the practice has been unambiguous throughout: QE does set those states, every cycle, and no lane has objected.** ⛔ **The rule is what disagrees with the repository, not the repository with itself** ([§2](../CLAUDE.md)).

### ⚡ The narrowest correction that would close it

**One clause, and this office is proposing rather than making it** — 📁 **[§2](../CLAUDE.md): *governance describes reality; it never quietly changes it*, and a `CLAUDE.md` edit is the product owner's or it is nothing.**

> **"QE writes nothing"** → **"QE writes no scope and no ordering; the four terminal execution states are QE's, per the lifecycle table."**

✅ **That changes what nobody does tomorrow** — ⚡ **which is the test [§2](../CLAUDE.md) gives for whether a governance edit needed a decision first.** ⛔ **It still needs the ruling, because the file is the product owner's.**

### 📁 Why it is worth a row rather than a shrug

**Third governance item this month whose cost is not a blocked slice but a *divided reading***, and the register's own standard is that an item exists when a lane cannot safely proceed without an answer. ⚠️ **A lane CAN proceed here — Lane A did, correctly.** ✅ **The row exists because the next lane may read the other sentence first**, and the two produce opposite behaviour in the same file.
